### WMX-01 — Package code review shows bidirectional control characters as-is, so the code a person reviews can look different from the code that runs (Trojan Source)

**P2** · security · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss` · also reported as WXS-02

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/package-diff-markup.ts:33`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/package-diff-markup.ts:38`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/package-file-reader.ts:69`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/package-file-reader.ts:70`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/08-panels.css:641`
- **What:** fileMarkup writes each diff line as escapeHtml(line.text) inside a .diff-line span, which is display:block and white-space:pre (08-panels.css:641). proposedFileMarkup (the R-017 'Read the whole file' dialog) writes escapeHtml(file.text) into a <pre>. escapeHtml only maps & < > " ', so U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200E/U+200F and U+061C reach the page, and the browser reorders each line by the bidi algorithm. change.path is shown the same way in the summary and the dialog heading. Nothing in src/Nendo.Workbench/src handles bidi characters: a grep for unicode-bidi, dir=, <bdi, 202E or bidi finds nothing, and the host's package code has no check either. ADR-0013 makes this review the gate before view code runs: accepting it is meant to be reading it.
- **Failure:** A package proposal (from an agent at Shape app, an imported .nendoview file, or Save to file from a development folder) adds `const access = "user\u202E \u2066// Check if admin\u2069 \u2066";`. The diff shows `const access = "user"; // Check if admin`, which looks like a closed string followed by a comment, but the source is one string literal. `if (isAdmin) { /* \u202E } \u2066if (isAdmin)\u2069 \u2066 begin admins only */` hides control flow in the same way. A file named `evil\u202Esj.txt` reads as `eviltxt.js`. The person accepts code that behaves differently from what they read, and it then runs wherever its view is shown.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: packageChangesMarkup() from a vite SSR bundle of package-diff-markup.ts, given those two added lines and laid out by headless Edge 155 (scratch page-diff.html, diff.png) -> the third line renders as `+const access = "user"; // Check if admin`. diff.includes('\u202E') -> true.
- **Fix and guard:** In package-diff-markup.ts (lines and change.path) and package-file-reader.ts (text and path), replace every bidi control and invisible format character (U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+2069, and U+FEFF when it is not at the start) with a visible marker, such as <span class="hidden-char" title="U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE">[U+202E]</span>. Add a warning to the file's folded summary and to the proposal's What changes list saying that the file contains hidden bidirectional characters. Guard: a package-diff.test.mjs case asserting that packageChangesMarkup and proposedFileMarkup output for text containing U+202E or U+2066 contains neither raw character and does contain the warning.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ExtensionPackageDiff.cs:117-125 passes each line through unchanged (only a trailing CR is trimmed), package-diff-markup.ts:33 and package-file-reader.ts:69 write it with escapeHtml, which maps only & < > " ', and 08-panels.css:641 lays each line out as a pre block. I rendered a diff-line holding U+202E/U+2066/U+2069 beside a benign line in headless Edge with the real stylesheets: the two lines look identical. ADR-0013 (lines 213-221, 617-624) names this diff the review before code runs, and nothing in the repo handles bidi or format characters. It needs a hostile proposal author and defeats review rather than the sandbox, so P2 rather than higher.
- **Correction:** The path half of the scenario cannot happen: ExtensionPackageModel.ValidPath (src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionPackageModel.cs:336) accepts only ASCII letters, digits and _ - . ~ /, so change.path cannot carry U+202E and 'evil<RLO>sj.txt' is refused before any review. Only the diff line text (package-diff-markup.ts:33) and the whole-file dialog text (package-file-reader.ts:69) are exposed; the fix on change.path and the file path is unnecessary.

<a id="bl-01"></a>

### BL-01 — The Desktop journey tests launch the Debug host under the product AppUserModelID, so every gate run rewrites the owner's real taskbar Jump List and leaves Nendo's notification registration pointing at artifacts/bin

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `baseline` · also reported as TST-03, TGA-02

- **Where:** `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:344`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:345`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopNotifier.cs:46`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:318`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopRuntimeConfiguration.cs:17`
- **What:** RunJourneyAsync starts artifacts/bin/Nendo.Desktop/debug_win-x64/Nendo.Desktop.exe with NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT, NENDO_STARTUP_OPEN and the diagnostics folders, but never sets NENDO_DESKTOP_APP_ID. DesktopShellIdentity.AppUserModelId therefore resolves to DefaultAppUserModelId "Nendo.Desktop", the identity the owner's installed Nendo uses. MainWindow.ApplyFileName -> RefreshJumpList -> DesktopJumpList.Publish writes the custom destination list for that identity with Environment.ProcessPath (the Debug exe), and DesktopNotifier's constructor calls AppNotificationManager.Default.Register("Nendo", icon) with the Debug build's Assets\AppIcon.ico. DesktopRuntimeConfiguration.ResolveAppUserModelId says in its own comment that NENDO_DESKTOP_APP_ID exists so a lane does not write 'entries into the owner's real taskbar menu'; only tools/Review-ShellRuntime.ps1 sets it. The two gate tests ViewsRunInlineIsolatedFromTheWorkbenchAndStopWhenSwitchedOff and AFileOpensOnItsOwnViewAndStudioStaysReachable go through RunJourneyAsync, and tools/Review-DesktopPerformance.ps1, Capture-SiteScreenshots.ps1, Runtime-WorkbenchWindow.ps1, Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1, Review-NeutralityRuntime.ps1, Review-PerformanceMemory.ps1 and Test-ExtensionInstalledJourney.ps1 launch the host without it too.
- **Failure:** The owner runs the gate (or the Desktop test lane) while their installed Nendo is in use. The Debug host opens a temp test file and republishes the 'Nendo.Desktop' Jump List with rows that launch artifacts\bin\...\debug_win-x64\Nendo.Desktop.exe; the owner's taskbar Recent list now shows the test's state until their own Nendo next switches files. The notification identity HKCU\Software\Classes\AppUserModelId\Nendo.Desktop keeps IconUri and the CustomActivator's LocalServer32 pointing at the Debug exe even after the installed Nendo restarts (its Register does not rewrite them), so clicking a Nendo notification while Nendo is closed starts a Debug build of whatever version is in artifacts/ against the owner's real device state, and does nothing at all once artifacts/ is swept as AGENTS.md permits.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: CRC-64 (poly 0x92C64265D32139A4, init all-ones, reflected, uppercase UTF-16LE; checked against Microsoft.Windows.Explorer -> f01b4d95cf55d32a) of 'Nendo.Desktop' -> 2943bb3f738370c0; probe_jumplist.py over %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\CustomDestinations -> '2943bb3f738370c0.customDestinations-ms 2026-10-10 15:42:51 ['debug-exe']' (written during the isolated rerun of the journey test, 15:42:2x-15:43:1x; no reference to Programs\Nendo\Nendo.Desktop.exe). Registry read -> 'IconUri : C:\Users\thoma\Projects\nendo\artifacts\bin\Nendo.Desktop\debug_win-x64\Assets\AppIcon.ico', LocalServer32 -> '"c:\users\thoma\projects\nendo\artifacts\bin\nendo.desktop\debug_win-x64\nendo.desktop.exe" ----AppNotificationActivated:'; key last written 2026-10-10 07:59:42 while the installed Nendo (pid 26128, Programs\Nendo) started at 12:19:19 and did not repair it.
- **Fix and guard:** In RunJourneyAsync (and every runtime lane that starts a host) set NENDO_DESKTOP_APP_ID to a run-unique 'Nendo.Lane.<guid>' identity and delete that identity's AppUserModelId/CLSID keys and customDestinations file afterwards, as Review-ShellRuntime.ps1 already does; consider having the host skip Jump List publishing and notification registration when diagnostics variables (NENDO_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS / NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT) are set without an app id. Guard: in the journey test, record the mtime/hash of %APPDATA%\...\CustomDestinations\2943bb3f738370c0.customDestinations-ms and the values under HKCU\Software\Classes\AppUserModelId\Nendo.Desktop before launch and assert both unchanged after the host exits; falsify by removing the env var and watching the assertion fail.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. RunJourneyAsync (DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:339-346) sets NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT and friends but never NENDO_DESKTOP_APP_ID, so DesktopShellIdentity.ResolveFrom (DesktopShellIdentity.cs:50-53) falls back to DefaultAppUserModelId 'Nendo.Desktop', the identity Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:217-222 registers for the installed app. MainWindow.ApplyFileName -> RefreshJumpList (MainWindow.xaml.cs:75-79, 298-320) then calls DesktopJumpList.Publish(files, identity, Environment.ProcessPath, ...), and DesktopNotifier's constructor (DesktopNotifier.cs:40-46, created at MainWindow.xaml.cs:203) calls manager.Register('Nendo', <Debug AppIcon.ico>). Only tools/Review-ShellRuntime.ps1 sets the override (grep of NENDO_DESKTOP_APP_ID), though DesktopRuntimeConfiguration.cs:14-24 says the override exists precisely to keep lanes out of the owner's taskbar menu. I read the live state: HKCU\Software\Classes\AppUserModelId\Nendo.Desktop has IconUri under artifacts\bin\Nendo.Desktop\debug_win-x64 (setup wrote the installed Assets path), CustomActivator {4833A11A-...} has LocalServer32 pointing at the debug exe, and CustomDestinations\2943bb3f738370c0.customDestinations-ms was written 10-10-2026 15:42:51. No ADR or contract mandates this; it is an unguarded test-isolation gap that damages the owner's installed-app shell registration.
- **Correction:** The 'data-integrity' category overstates it: nothing the owner authored is lost, and the Jump List self-heals the next time the installed Nendo switches files. What persists is the notification registration (icon and activator) pointing at a Debug build under artifacts/. Whether the installed Nendo's own Register would repair that was not established, but the registry state observed today shows it has not. Other lanes (Review-DesktopPerformance.ps1, Capture-SiteScreenshots.ps1 and others) also launch with NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT and no app id, so the fix belongs in the host (skip Jump List and notification registration under NENDO_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS) as much as in each lane.

<a id="esm-01"></a>

### ESM-01 — A link rule declared in the same mutation that creates its table type or an endpoint kind field skips the declaration's data check, so it is accepted over links that already break it

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.LinkRules.cs:387`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.LinkRules.cs:207`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.LinkRules.cs:344`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:179`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:577`, `docs/decisions/0026-allowed-links.md:148`
- **What:** ExecuteDeclareLinkRuleAsync calls RequireAllowedLinksAsync(resolved, LinkScope.All, declaring: true) while the operation executes. That method returns early ('A record type whose table or columns are not there yet holds no records to check') when any of the four physical tables or eight columns is missing. Physical tables and columns are only created afterwards by MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync, which for a DeclareLinkRuleOperation only creates the index (Operations.cs:577-579). The end-of-mutation RequireAllowedLinksAsync(evidence) builds its LinkScope only from create/restore/delete/setField operations, so a DeclareLinkRuleOperation adds nothing and the data is never checked. The delivery note's reason ('a declaration in the mutation that creates its record types has no data to check') is only true when the link type itself is new: an existing link type with records plus a new, empty table type (which allows nothing) or a new sourceKind/targetKind column (all NULL, which matches no row) is skipped.
- **Failure:** Links type holds l1 (actor -> role, kind 'nonsense'). One definition mutation (one MCP add_operations call) creates the Allowed record type with its three fields and declares the rule on Links. It is accepted with zero table rows while l1 remains, contrary to ADR-0026 item 4 ('every link is checked ... validation fails with links-not-allowed'). The file now carries a declared rule its data violates: a new link with the same kinds is refused, a New file of the application is refused, and every later edit of l1's source, target or kind is refused, while nothing ever reported l1.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-linkrule.ps1 against a scratch copy of the built Nendo.Engine.dll on temp files under the scratch folder -> '--- A. The table type created in the SAME mutation as the declaration / ACCEPTED: links.LinkRule declared = True; table rows = 0; link l1 still present = True' then '--- B. ... REFUSED l2: link-not-allowed: Links record l2 is not an allowed link: ...' and the control '--- C. ... REFUSED (control): links-not-allowed: 1 Links record is not an allowed link by Allowed links: l1. Correct those links or add their combinations to Allowed links first; nothing was changed.'
- **Fix and guard:** Run the declaration check after materialization: for every DeclareLinkRuleOperation in the mutation call RequireAllowedLinksAsync(rule, LinkScope.All, transaction, ct, declaring: true) at the end of MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync (both apply paths reach it), or make RequireAllowedLinksAsync(evidence) treat a DeclareLinkRuleOperation as scope.Everything with the declaring refusal; keep the early return only for a link type whose own table is absent. Guard: LinkRuleTests cases that declare with the table type, and separately with a new source-kind field, created in the same mutation over an existing disallowed link and expect links-not-allowed; falsify by removing the post-materialization call.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end and reproduced. ExecuteDeclareLinkRuleAsync runs the declaring check while the operation executes (src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.LinkRules.cs:207). RequireAllowedLinksAsync returns early when any of the four tables or eight columns is missing (LinkRules.cs:386-389). Tables and columns are created only afterwards by MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:538-561), which for a declaration only adds the index (Operations.cs:577-579). The end-of-mutation check on both apply paths (SqliteNendoStore.cs:179 and :411) builds its scope only from create, restore, delete and setField (LinkRules.cs:344-366), so a declaration adds nothing. NendoMutation.Validate (Operations.cs:546) only forbids mixing lanes, and MCP makes one mutation per add_operations call (NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:839-855), so a new table type or endpoint-kind field can share a mutation with the declaration. LinkRuleTests declares only in a mutation of its own. I re-ran the reviewer's probe on a Nendo.Engine.dll built after HEAD (19:43, HEAD 15:04, no src changes in the tree). A was ACCEPTED with 0 table rows and l1 still present. B refused l2 with link-not-allowed. The control C refused with links-not-allowed naming l1. This contradicts ADR-0026 item 4 (docs/decisions/0026-allowed-links.md:89-91). The delivery note at :148 holds only when the link type itself is new. P2 rather than P1: no data is lost, link rules are a rarely declared definition feature, its only adopter (Archi) declares in a separate stage, and the bad state comes out later with l1 named and workarounds available.
- **Correction:** Overstated: 'every later edit of l1's source, target or kind is refused' should be 'every later edit that leaves l1 not allowed is refused'. Clearing its kind, changing it to an allowed combination, or adding the table row still succeeds. 'Nothing ever reported l1' is also too strong. A refused edit of l1 names it, and so does the New-file check (SqliteNendoStore.NewFile.cs:356). Only two variants have an effect: a new table type, and a new endpoint-kind field, whose NULL column matches no row. A new link-side field is NULL, so it leaves links unchecked and does no harm. The fix should also correct the ADR-0026 delivery note at line 148. With the fix, a change set that declares the rule in the mutation that creates the table and seeds rows in a later mutation would be refused, so rows must come first. That matches the control path and Build-Archi's stage order.

<a id="r2ap-04"></a>

### R2AP-04 — A view's records.batch sent again under its writeKey is refused as idempotency-conflict whenever a create leaves recordId out, because the broker mints a new record ID on every send

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `r2-adapter-parity`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:492`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:510`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:311`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:825`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:674`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/nendo-api.ts:516`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/extension-broker.test.mjs:1097`
- **What:** recordWritesParam builds each create with newRecordId(entry), which returns record-<random UUID> when the view gave no recordId (recordId is optional in the method table). batchKey makes the idempotency key view-<package>-<writeKey>, the same on every send. The Engine replays a key only for an identical payload digest (TryResolveReplayAsync), and the record ID is in the payload, so the second send is refused 'The idempotency key was already used with a different mutation payload.'. The contract (custom-views.md:674-681) and nendo-api.ts:521-524 promise that the same batch sent again under the same writeKey 'is kept once and answers as it did'. The R-011 broker test passes an explicit recordId, so it never meets this. Garden avoids it only because it always names record IDs.
- **Failure:** A third-party view calls nendo.records.batch([{op:'create', entityId:'tasks', values:{title:'A'}}], {writeKey:'save-1'}); the answer is lost (host-timeout or disconnected) though the batch committed. Following the documentation it sends the same call again: idempotency-conflict, a code the Workbench classes as a confirmed refusal. The view cannot learn that the first batch landed; if it then retries without the writeKey or with a new one, the task is created twice.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratchpad r2-adapter-parity/probe-broker.mjs (real extension-broker.ts bundled with vite into scratch) -> 'writeKey retry: same idempotencyKey = true view-org.example.glance-save-7f3a', 'first recordId = record-e0fd7d06...', 'second recordId = record-41ad7363...', 'identical payload = false'; then probe-engine.ps1 section 3 with those two IDs under one key -> 'NendoIdempotencyConflictException [] The idempotency key was already used with a different mutation payload.'
- **Fix and guard:** When a writeKey is given, derive a create's missing record ID deterministically from the package, the writeKey and the write's index (as the MCP import derives IDs from its key), or refuse a writeKey batch whose creates lack recordId and say so in the contract. Guard: a broker test sending the same writeKey batch twice with a create without recordId and asserting identical host payloads; falsify by restoring the random ID.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. extension-broker.ts:492 builds each create with newRecordId(entry) (:510), which returns record-<fresh random UUID> when the view gave no recordId, and recordId is optional in the public type (nendo-api.ts:187). batchKey (:311-317) returns the constant view-<package>-<writeKey> on every send. The host passes both through unchanged (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:603-625 -> DesktopSessionController.WriteRecordsAsync:296) and ApplyRecordWritesAsync puts write.RecordId into CreateRecordOperation (NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:124), so the mutation payload digest differs between the two sends. TryResolveReplayAsync (SqliteNendoStore.cs:810-825) then throws NendoIdempotencyConflictException for the reused key, which WorkbenchProtocol.cs:474 returns as idempotency-conflict. That contradicts custom-views.md:674-681 and nendo-api.ts:516-524, which promise that the same batch sent again under the same writeKey is kept once and answered as before. The R-011 test (extension-broker.test.mjs:1097) names recordId explicitly, so it never meets the case. When the first send never committed the second one succeeds, so only the lost-answer case the feature exists for fails.
- **Correction:** No data is lost or duplicated by the refusal itself; a duplicate needs the view to retry without its writeKey afterwards. Built-in views (Garden) name record IDs and are unaffected, and naming a recordId is a one-line workaround, so P2 is the ceiling; category is a broken documented idempotency guarantee rather than data-integrity.

<a id="r2sma-04"></a>

### R2SMA-04 — Recovery export always drops reference fields and calls them 'unsupported or over-limit'

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `r2-safe-mode-and-file-versions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/RecoveryExportModel.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.Engine/RecoveryExportModel.cs:76`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:407`
- **What:** RecoveryCsvWriter.Create keeps only fields whose StorageKind is between Text and Uuid (RecoveryExportModel.cs:32). NendoStorageKind.Reference comes after Uuid, so every relationship column is omitted, the export is marked partial, and the review says '1 unsupported or over-limit field(s) were excluded' (76). A reference value is a plain record-ID string. Since File > Export CSV is disabled whenever the file cannot be edited (WSP-06), this is the only CSV a read-only or recovery session can produce.
- **Failure:** In safe mode a person exports Tasks to get their data out: the CSV has the task titles but not which Project each task belongs to, the dialog forces 'Export partial CSV', and the reason given ('unsupported or over-limit') is wrong. The relationships cannot be recovered from any export Nendo offers in that state.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratch probe3.ps1 export (Tasks with a bound reference 'project' to Projects) -> 'recovery export plan: exported=1/1 partial=True omittedFieldIds=[project]', 'finding csv-omitted-fields: 1 unsupported or over-limit field(s) were excluded...', 'csv: "__nendo_record_id","__nendo_record_version","field/title" / "t1","1","Write the plan"'.
- **Fix and guard:** Include Reference fields as text cells holding the target record ID (optionally a second 'label/<fieldId>' column from ReferenceLabels), and keep only Unsupported and over-limit fields in OmittedFields. Guard: a RecoveryExportTests case with a bound reference that asserts IsPartial is false and the CSV contains the target record ID under field/<referenceFieldId>.
- **Verifier:** RecoveryExportModel.cs:32 keeps only StorageKind from Text to Uuid; the enum (ApplicationModel.cs:7-18) puts Reference after Uuid, so every reference field lands in the omitted list (:35), IsPartial is true (:19) and the finding at :76 reads 'unsupported or over-limit'. NendoWriteCoordinator.RecoveryExport.cs:52 uses this writer for every read-only or recovery export, and File > Export CSV is offered only when capabilities.mutate (file-actions.ts:216), so it is the only CSV in that state. The normal export carries references as stable IDs (csv.md:22, help.ts:69), and nothing in the docs or in RecoveryExportTests (:79 covers only an unknown kind) mandates dropping them. A reference value is a record-ID string, so including it is cheap.
- **Correction:** It is completeness, not integrity: the export is flagged partial, needs explicit confirmation, lists the omitted field IDs, and the file is untouched. The wording 'unsupported or over-limit' is inaccurate for references. Keep P2 because relationships are the one thing a person in this state cannot get out of Nendo.

<a id="tga-04"></a>

### TGA-04 — Review-OutcomeRuntime -Executable on the published payload loses its device-state isolation and leaves the owner's theme on Dark

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `tools-gates`

- **Where:** `tools/Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1:27`, `tools/Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1:3`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopRuntimeConfiguration.cs:66`, `tools/Publish-NendoPayload.ps1:47`, `tools/Review-OutcomeRuntime.mjs:345`, `tools/Review-NeutralityRuntime.ps1:25`
- **What:** The lane isolates the host only through NENDO_DESKTOP_TEST_STATE_ROOT. ResolveDeviceStateRoot reads that variable inside `#if DEBUG` and nowhere else. The parameter comment and docs/architecture.md:1084 name '-Executable for the published payload' as the intended use. Publish-NendoPayload.ps1:47 builds that payload with `-c Release`, where the variable is ignored. The probe clicks `[data-theme-option=light]` and then `dark` three times (lines 287, 315 and 345) and never restores the theme. The last click is Dark, persisted through appearance.set. Review-NeutralityRuntime.ps1:25 relies on the same Debug-only variable and works only because it hard-codes the debug exe.
- **Failure:** `pwsh ./tools/Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1 -Executable artifacts/build/publish/payload/Nendo.Desktop.exe` writes into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nendo. After the run the owner's Nendo opens in Dark rather than following Windows. outcome-workspace.nendo and review-backup.nendo appear in the owner's recent files and Jump List. The lane's report claims an isolated, owned run.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Set NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT (honoured in every configuration) in both Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1 and Review-NeutralityRuntime.ps1, as Capture-SiteScreenshots.ps1 already does. Guard: after the launch, assert that `<evidence>/device-state/appearance.json` exists and that %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nendo\appearance.json is byte-identical to its pre-run copy.
- **Verifier:** Review-OutcomeRuntime.ps1:3-5 offers -Executable for the published payload (docs/architecture.md:1084 repeats it), but :27 isolates only through NENDO_DESKTOP_TEST_STATE_ROOT. DesktopRuntimeConfiguration.cs:66-71 reads that variable only inside #if DEBUG, and Publish-NendoPayload.ps1 publishes -c Release, so the Release host resolves the default %LOCALAPPDATA%\Nendo. Review-OutcomeRuntime.mjs:286-288, 314-316 and 344-346 click light then dark and never restore, and the click persists through appearance.set (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:426). The owner is left on Dark and outcome-workspace.nendo and review-backup.nendo land in recent files. A supported invocation deterministically changes a visible persisted preference, so P2 (a click resets it).
- **Correction:** Capture-SiteScreenshots.ps1:57-58 sets both NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT and NENDO_DESKTOP_TEST_STATE_ROOT, so the fix is to add NENDO_DEVICE_STATE_ROOT. The Review-NeutralityRuntime point is latent only: that script has no -Executable parameter and hard-codes the Debug exe (Review-NeutralityRuntime.ps1:8), where the variable works. The effect is a changed preference and some device-state clutter, not lost authored data.

### UX-01 — Health (nav, Ctrl 6, palette, notification) silently discards unsaved record-form typing that every other route guards

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` (reported P1) · also reported as WCS-04, WSP-04

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:654`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-health.ts:127`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:676`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/draft-guard.ts:31`
- **What:** Every route off a record page calls refuseWhileDirty first: openWorkspaceView (actions.ts:327), openHelp (actions.ts:533), openAgentView (main.ts:659), tabs, rail places. The Health route does not: main.ts:654 wires #nav-health straight to refreshHealth(), and refreshHealth (view-health.ts:127-151) sets state.view = 'health' and calls rerender(); main.render then sets state.openDraft = null and replaces the form. Ctrl 6 presses the same button (runShortcut), the command palette's 'Health' presses it (command-palette.ts:80), and a Windows notification routed to 'health' calls refreshHealth directly (main.ts:676).
- **Failure:** Use > open a record > type into Notes > click Health (or press Ctrl 6). The page switches to File health with no message; going back to Use shows the record with the old Notes. The same typing followed by a click on Data is refused with 'Save your changes or close record details before leaving this screen.'
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=1, typed ' UNSAVED TYPING' into the record inspector, then clicked each route -> 'DATA NAV -> msg: Save your changes or close record details before leaving this screen. \| draft kept: true'; 'HEALTH NAV -> title: File health \| msg: none \| draft kept: false'; 'CTRL+6 -> title: File health \| draft kept: false'.
- **Fix and guard:** Start refreshHealth's navigation path with `if (refuseWhileDirty('opening Health')) return;` (keep the internal health re-reads after a failed write unguarded by splitting the nav handler from the refresh). Guard: a host-behaviour/journey test that dirties a record form, presses #nav-health and Ctrl+6, and asserts the refusal text and that the textarea still holds the typing.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. main.ts:654 wires #nav-health straight to refreshHealth(). refreshHealth (view-health.ts:127-151) has no refuseWhileDirty or recordFormIsDirty check: it sets state.view='health' and calls rerender(). rerender (shell.ts:77) calls render, and render clears state.openDraft (main.ts:117) before renderHealth replaces content.innerHTML (view-health.ts:59). Ctrl 6 goes through runShortcut, which calls target.click() on the same button (main.ts:485-502). The palette's Health entry presses #nav-health (command-palette.ts:78). onNavigate 'health' calls refreshHealth directly (main.ts:676). Every sibling route is guarded: openWorkspaceView (actions.ts:327), openHelp (actions.ts:533) and openAgentView (main.ts:659). The keydown comment at main.ts:460-464 says a key 'is refused wherever the click would be -- ... a page holding unsaved typing'. docs/contracts/semantic-surfaces.md:233-246 says 'another view' must decline in those words, so this breaks the contract. No ADR exempts Health. Priority lowered to P2. Only unsaved typing is lost, never stored data, and saving before you leave avoids it. No AGENTS.md invariant is broken.
- **Correction:** Two more unguarded entry points: the custom-view notice button [data-view-health] (view-frames.ts:523), and the automatic refreshHealth inside refreshAgentStatus (view-agent.ts:657). The automatic one runs only on the Agent page, where no record form is open. Put the guard in the user-initiated callers: the main.ts:654 nav handler, main.ts:676 onNavigate and view-frames.ts:523. Do not put it in refreshHealth itself, or the automatic recovery re-read from view-agent.ts:657 would start showing a refusal. The finding's 'after a failed write' rationale is wrong: no write-failure path calls refreshHealth. recoverAfterWriteFailure (actions.ts:359) re-reads by itself. The issue is already recorded in the untracked root FIXES.md (lines 821-824 and 890-893).

### WDV-02 — Studio grid select editors silently rewrite a stored value that is not in their list, and write null over null

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:625`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:619`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:768`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:718`, `docs/contracts/scalars.md:28`
- **What:** cellEditorParams gives agSelectCellEditor a list that leaves out values the cell can hold: a single choice drops retired options and has '' (not null) for Not set; a rating offers only '' and the scale's steps. AG Grid 36's SelectCellEditor.initialiseEditor sets the editor to values[0] when the current value is not in the list, and stopping the edit commits it. commitGridEdit then writes: '' becomes null for a choice or rating, the first option for a required choice. It never compares the parsed value with the stored one, so null -> '' -> null is sent too. The contract says a rating outside its scale 'is stored, read back exactly ... not refused or clamped', and relationships.md says retired choices stay readable on existing records; rating.ts states 'leaving the control alone never rewrites it'.
- **Failure:** A person double-clicks a Rating cell holding 9 on a 1-5 scale (or a Status cell whose option was retired) to look, then clicks another cell (stopEditingWhenCellsLoseFocus) or presses Enter: the 9 is cleared to Not set (or replaced by 1 when required), the retired status becomes the first option or Not set, and 'Rating saved.' is announced. Opening and leaving an empty optional choice or rating cell writes null over null, so it adds a revision and bumps the record version with no change.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: grid-select-probe.html runs the real AG Grid 36.1.0 bundle in headless Edge with the Studio column shape, opening each editor and stopping without a pick -> onCellValueChanged=[{"col":"rating","oldValue":"9","newValue":""},{"col":"status","oldValue":"legacy","newValue":"open"},{"col":"stage","oldValue":null,"newValue":""}]. commitGridEdit (source) turns each of these into data.setField.
- **Fix and guard:** Always include the cell's current value in the editor's values, labelled by the valueFormatter as '(retired)' or 'outside 1-5', and use null rather than '' for Not set so an empty cell matches. In commitGridEdit, parse the new value and return without writing when sameValue(parsed, storedValue). Guard: the headless AG Grid probe as a Workbench lane, asserting no setField after opening and leaving a cell with a retired, out-of-scale or empty value; falsify by removing the stored value from values.
- **Verifier:** view-data.ts:625 builds a single-choice editor list that drops retired options and uses '' for Not set, and view-data.ts:632 gives a rating only '' plus the scale's steps, while the valueGetter (view-data.ts:581-584) hands the editor the stored lexeme ('9') or null. AG Grid 36.1.0's SelectCellEditor.initialiseEditor (node_modules/ag-grid-community/dist/package/main.esm.mjs, the class at line 41454) calls eEditor.setValue(params.values[0]) when the current value is not in the list. I reproduced it: real AG Grid bundle, headless Edge, editor opened and left by moving focus to another cell. Result: rating 9 -> '', retired 'legacy' -> 'open', null -> ''. An in-scale 3 produced no event. commitGridEdit (view-data.ts:768-801) compares only newValue against oldValue, never the parsed value against the stored one, so these become data.setField writes of null, the first option and null. ExecuteSetFieldAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:457-530) bumps the version with no no-op check, and ValidateChoiceAssignment (SqliteNendoStore.Choices.cs:124) then refuses to put the retired choice back through a normal write. This breaks scalars.md:28-31 and relationships.md:175. It happens only on cells that hold a retired or out-of-scale value, and only when the person leaves without pressing Escape. History undo is available, so P2 fits better than P1.
- **Correction:** Reachability: the default editor-leave path commits, so the probe's explicit api.stopEditing(false) is not needed; moving focus to another cell is enough. A retired choice that was overwritten cannot be put back with an ordinary write (choice-retired, SqliteNendoStore.Choices.cs:126-128); only History undo restores it. That strengthens the fix: always include the stored value in the editor's values. The null-over-null part is the low-impact half: an extra revision and a version bump, no lost value. No Workbench test covers commitGridEdit or cellEditorParams today. Probe: scratchpad/review/verify/workbench-data-views-2/select-verify.html.

### WMX-03 — Record form controls do not round-trip stored text: a single-line input strips line breaks and a textarea drops a leading newline, so editing the field silently rewrites the value

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss` · also reported as WDV-05

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:460`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:434`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:444`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:102`
- **What:** fieldControlMarkup renders every Text field without the longText or markdown presentation as <input type="text" value="${escapeAttribute(value)}">, and an input's value sanitization removes CR and LF. Textareas are written as <textarea ...>${escapeHtml(value)}</textarea>, and the HTML parser drops a single LF directly after a textarea start tag. Multi-line values in a single-line field are legitimate: FieldPresentationOperations allows a field to move from longText back to singleLine because the change 'keeps every value valid', and neither MCP data writes nor CSV import refuse newlines. When the person edits a field, its saved value comes from formValue(field, FormData) (record-form.ts:101-102), so the sanitized control value is what gets written.
- **Failure:** A Text field holding 'Line one\nLine two' (an agent wrote it, or the field was switched from long text to single line) shows as 'Line oneLine two'. Fixing a typo and saving writes 'Line oneLine two', and the line break is gone for good. A long-text value '\nSecond line' opens as 'Second line', and any edit saves it without the leading newline. Typing and then undoing the typing still leaves the page marked dirty, because sameAsStored keeps finding a difference.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: fieldControlMarkup() from a vite SSR bundle of record-markup.ts, parsed by headless Edge (scratch page-form.html) -> input[name=title].value is "line oneline two" for the stored "line one\nline two", and textarea[name=summary].value is "Second line is the first one kept" for the stored "\nSecond line is the first one kept".
- **Fix and guard:** Show a Text value that contains a line break in a textarea, or keep the input read-only with a note and an 'Edit as long text' control. Write a newline immediately after every textarea start tag (`<textarea ...>\n${escapeHtml(value)}`) or set .value after insertion. Guard: a record-markup test asserting that a single-line field holding 'a\nb' produces a control that preserves 'a\nb', and that textarea markup for a value starting with '\n' begins its content with '\n\n'.
- **Verifier:** record-markup.ts:460 renders a plain Text field as <input type="text" value=...>, whose value sanitization strips CR and LF, and record-markup.ts:434 writes <textarea>${value}</textarea>, whose parser drops one leading LF. record-form.ts:97-104 sends a field only when it is in editedFields, and then takes its value from formValue(FormData) (record-form.ts:133-137, parseScalar returns raw for Text), so editing a field that holds 'a\nb' saves 'ab'. Newlines in single-line fields are legal: FieldPresentationOperations.cs:24 allows singleLine from longText as 'keeps every value valid', and I found no newline check in any .cs file, so agent writes and imports can store them. Untouched fields are left alone, which limits the damage to editing that very field. Silent loss of line breaks from stored data, but the previous value stays in History, hence P2 and not higher.

### WSP-02 — Make required fills every missing single-choice value with the first option without asking

**P2** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:381`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:388`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:402`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:447`
- **What:** renderFieldRequirement builds the backfill plan with required: true and draws fieldControlMarkup(plan, null) for each record. For a required single choice, fieldControlMarkup emits <select required> with no empty placeholder (record-markup.ts:447). The browser therefore selects the first option, and the required check passes. form.reportValidity() and formValue then accept that option, and the preview builds data.setField for every listed record. The page says "Enter an explicit value for each record below", and Help says "Nothing is filled automatically" (help.ts:81, help-concepts.ts:73). Each review entry reads only "Set Status for <id>.", without the value.
- **Failure:** A Status choice field has 37 records without a value. The person chooses Make required, then Preview changes without touching a select. The proposal sets Status = "Idea" on all 37 records and makes the field required. Accepting it writes a value nobody chose.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-backfill.mjs (bundles src/record-markup.ts in memory, calls fieldControlMarkup with the plan shape of view-structure.ts:381) -> `required choice backfill -> <label>Status<select name="field.status" required><option value="Idea" >Idea</option><option value="Exploring" >Exploring</option><option value="Done" >Done</option></select></label>`
- **Fix and guard:** In the backfill and reactivation form, draw a required choice with a selected, disabled empty placeholder (<option value="" selected disabled>Choose…</option>) so that `required` fails until a choice is made, for example through an option to fieldControlMarkup. Guard: a record-markup test asserting that a required singleChoice with a null value renders a selected empty option, plus a structure test that previewing an untouched backfill is refused.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. view-structure.ts:381 builds the plan with required:true and fieldControlMarkup(plan, null) at :388. record-markup.ts:447 emits a <select required> with no empty option when field.required (the 'Not set' option is added only when not required). The browser therefore selects the first non-disabled option, so form.reportValidity() (:402) passes untouched and formValue returns that option. :405-408 builds data.setField for every record. The review text carries no value (SemanticDiff.cs:179-181: 'Set <field> for <id>.'). The page says 'Enter an explicit value for each record' (:385) and help-concepts.ts:73 says 'Nothing is filled in automatically', so the guarantee is not enforced for single-choice fields. It is reachable from any Make required or Reactivate on a choice field with up to 50 empty records.
- **Correction:** The Reactivate path (prepareRetirement -> renderFieldRequirement(..., true)) has the same flaw. Mitigation: the first option is visible in each record's select, so a careful reader sees it, but nothing forces a choice.

### ABS-01 — Archi Open imports a truncated .archimate or Exchange file as a smaller, valid-looking model

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:91`, `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:122`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1495`
- **What:** readArchimate and readExchange hand the text straight to archi-online's parseArchimate/parseExchange (archi-online 6205a6a src/model/io/archimate-xml/parse.ts:48-52, exchange-xml/parse.ts:46-50). Those check for <parsererror> only when the document element is not <model>. Chromium's DOMParser does not replace the document on an XML error: it keeps the root and inserts <parsererror> inside it, so a file cut short still has root=model and passes. Measured in headless Edge with a minimal file: 'truncated: root=model guardPasses=true parsererror=1 elements=1' (3 elements in the whole file). With the workbench's own canvas.js: Archisurance saved by exportArchimate and cut before its Relations folder gives 'cut before Relations: opened; {"elements":120,"relationships":0,"views":0,...}; 128 records to write; left out: null'. The whole file opens with 176 relationships and 17 views. An entity-expansion bomb is refused correctly (Chromium gives root=html), so the gap is truncation.
- **Failure:** A person drops an .archimate file that was only partly downloaded or synced (cut after the elements). The dialog says 'Model: 120 elements, 0 relationships, 0 views.' and Open writes that partial model into the new file. Nothing says the file was malformed, and History cannot undo the import.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over CDP, scratch truncated-open.html calling canvas.readModelFile + planImport on exportArchimate(archisurance.json) cut at xml.indexOf('type="relations"') -> 'cut before Relations: opened; {"elements":120,"relationships":0,"views":0,"objects":0,"connections":0,"folders":8}; 128 records to write; left out: null'
- **Fix and guard:** In io.ts, parse once with DOMParser before handing the text over, and throw ArchimateFileError('The file is not well-formed XML (cut short?)') when doc.getElementsByTagName('parsererror').length > 0. Do this in readArchimate and readExchange, and for model.xml in the archive. Guard: a browser-lane case in the Archi gate that drops a truncated Archisurance and expects the dialog to refuse it, with Open disabled. The node lane is not enough, because jsdom reports the error differently.
- **Verifier:** tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:91 hands the text straight to archi-online's parseArchimate, and archi-online src/model/io/archimate-xml/parse.ts:48-52 (and exchange-xml/parse.ts:46-50, reached through parseExchangeDocument at io.ts:122) checks for <parsererror> only when the root is not <model>. I reproduced the Chromium behaviour in the live Chromium 152 tab: a cut archimate document gives 'root=model ns=http://www.archimatetool.com/archimate parsererror=1 elements=2', so the guard is skipped and the partial tree parses. Nothing else validates well-formedness on Open (xsd.js runs only on export, view.js:1573), and readChosen (view.js:1488-1506) shows only counts, so a truncated file imports as a smaller valid model, against the io.ts:115-118 comment that a document it cannot read whole is refused. The counts line is the only cue and the original file is untouched, which keeps this at P2.

### EBH-01 — A trigger condition that cannot be evaluated silently skips its action: BlockedConditions is collected and never reported

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:98`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourExecutionContext.cs:127`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ApplicationModel.cs:307`, `docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md:366`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/BehaviourActionTests.cs:224`
- **What:** RunTriggerAsync catches every NendoCalculationException from EvaluateConditionAsync and appends (TriggerId, Code, Message) to context.BlockedConditions, then returns. BlockedConditions has exactly two references in src/ (its declaration and that Add); nothing reads it. NendoApplyResult carries GeneratedChanges, AssignedValues, RecordVersion and Origin but no blocked-action list, so neither the Workbench, the MCP result nor a receipt learns a rule did not run. A condition has no result declaration (ResultNullable null), so an empty operand is a calculation-missing-input error, not false. The contract says such a condition 'blocks its own action and is reported'; the trigger record's own summary says 'A blocked condition is a visible outcome, not a silent skip'. Test D3_07 asserts the stale total and calls it 'visibly stale' although nothing surfaces.
- **Failure:** Trigger 'Roll up hours' on task with condition `done == true`, where `done` is an optional Boolean bound nullable. A person edits a task whose Done was never set: the condition throws calculation-missing-input, the action that maintains the project's stored total is skipped, the edit commits with a success result, and the project total is now wrong with no notice anywhere. Same for a deleted-record condition (same-record binding reads 'no longer there'), a zero divisor, or a refused value.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe6.ps1 evaluating condition `done == true` (binding done:Boolean nullable, empty, no result declaration) through NendoExpressionAdapter -> THROW NendoCalculationException[calculation-missing-input]: A value this calculation needs is empty. (planner path traced in source: caught at BehaviourPlanner.cs:98, recorded at :103, never read)
- **Fix and guard:** Carry the blocked conditions on NendoApplyResult (trigger ID, display name, code, message), publish them on the MCP write result beside alsoChanged and on the receipt, and show a notice in the Workbench after the save. Guard: extend D3_07 to assert the apply result names the blocked trigger with calculation-divide-by-zero, and an MCP protocol test that the write result carries it.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:98-104 catches every NendoCalculationException from the condition and adds it to context.BlockedConditions. A repo-wide grep finds only the declaration (BehaviourExecutionContext.cs:127) and that one Add. NendoApplyResult (ApplicationModel.cs:307-338) has no blocked list, and both result builders (SqliteNendoStore.cs:224-238 and :469-481) pass only GeneratedChanges and AssignedValues. Nothing in LocalMcp or the Workbench mentions blocked conditions. An empty nullable operand in `done == true` reaches Require at ExpressionAdapter.cs:389, which throws calculation-missing-input. The condition formula declares no result nullability, so the ResultNullable catch at :218 does not apply, and the planner records the trigger as blocked. Accepted ADR-0008 §6 (line 377) says 'Show the blocked trigger in the operation outcome', and §12 (line 495) says successful outcomes 'must also show blocked trigger conditions'. The contract at calculations-and-actions.md:367 says the condition 'is reported'. The code does neither. I lowered the priority to P2 because skipping the action is the behaviour ADR-0008 mandates (§6, and line 599 on optional actions); only the reporting is missing. The typed data is intact, the shipped authoring example's triggers have no conditions (NendoAuthoringExamples.cs:1405), and authors have a workaround: guard the condition with IsEmpty, which the vocabulary documents.
- **Correction:** Add the governing ADR text: ADR-0008 §6 (docs/decisions/0008-general-scripting-and-capability-isolation.md:377) and §12 (:495). It is the stronger authority, and its P3 obligation (:555) asks for 'a visibly blocked trigger condition'. Also note that a Deleted trigger with a same-record condition binding is blocked on every deletion (BehaviourPlanner.cs:125-130), again silently. The guard should add a persisted History entry as well as the apply result and MCP result, because §12 makes History show it too.

<a id="ebh-02"></a>

### EBH-02 — A ceiling reached inside a trigger condition is swallowed as a blocked condition instead of aborting the save

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:98`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:295`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:462`, `docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md:370`
- **What:** The catch at BehaviourPlanner.cs:98 has no filter on Code, so calculation-limit-reached is treated like any undecidable condition. In a chain the BehaviourRecordSource has an observer, so even a plain RelatedAggregate Count skips the uncharged COUNT(*) path (BehaviourSource.cs:295) and reads rows with LIMIT allowance+1; FoldAsync throws LimitReached when the extra row arrives (line 462) without consuming the counters, so the chain continues and commits. The contract lists 'an exhausted budget' among failures that abort everything and says 'If a chain reaches a ceiling, the whole transaction aborts.'
- **Failure:** Trigger on task (Updated) whose condition is `entries < 500`, entries being a RelatedAggregate Count of time entries pointing at the task. A task with 300 entries reads 300 on its record page (read path, COUNT(*)). Editing it: the chain reads 257 rows, throws calculation-limit-reached, the catch records a blocked condition (finding above: never shown), the action does not run and the save commits.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Rethrow when exception.Code == NendoCalculationCodes.LimitReached (catch ... when (exception.Code != LimitReached)), so a ceiling aborts the chain as the contract says. Guard: a BehaviourActionTests case with a condition over RelatedRows+1 members expects calculation-limit-reached, no revision and no receipt.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end in source. BehaviourPlanner.cs:98 catches every NendoCalculationException with no Code filter and records it as a blocked condition, so calculation-limit-reached from BehaviourBudget.Exhausted (BehaviourBudget.cs:94) or from FoldAsync (BehaviourSource.cs:462) is swallowed. In a chain the record source is built with a non-null observe lambda (BehaviourChain.cs:271), so a Count skips the COUNT(*) shortcut at BehaviourSource.cs:295 and reads rows under LIMIT allowance+1. The contract (calculations-and-actions.md:373 and :986) and ADR-0008 section 8 (line 407, 'trigger-chain limit violation cancels the entire transaction') say an exhausted budget or ceiling aborts the whole save, and the only test of a blocked condition (D3_07) uses a divide by zero. BehaviourSource.cs:541 deliberately lets LimitReached propagate for calculated members, which shows the abort is the intended direction. No upstream guard or ADR mandates the swallow. Rare in practice (needs a condition aggregate over more than about 255 rows, or a chain that is out of work units on its last event), but the result is a silently skipped action on a committed save.
- **Correction:** FoldAsync with chargePerRow:true does charge each row, so the related-row counter is left at the ceiling rather than 'not consumed'; the silent skip therefore only survives when nothing later in the same save needs another scan (otherwise the next ReadRecordAsync aborts anyway). Also, calculation-limit-reached is used for non-budget data limits too (HierarchyPath depth at BehaviourSource.cs:437, subtree descendant bound at :382), so a bare 'when Code != LimitReached' filter would turn those into aborts as well; decide whether that is wanted or filter on the budget cases only.

<a id="ebh-03"></a>

### EBH-03 — An action assignment's bindings are never checked against the record type the step evaluates them on

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:454`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:220`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:277`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:319`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:239`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourVocabulary.cs:96`
- **What:** The planner resolves a SetField assignment's bindings with the target record's ID and a CreateRecord assignment's with the event record's ID; ReadFieldAsync then reads binding.EntityId's table by that ID. The vocabulary states this rule ('A SetField assignment's bindings start from the record the step writes; a CreateRecord assignment's from the record that raised the event'), but RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync only checks that each assigned field exists on the step's record type, and RequireBehaviourBindingsResolveAsync only checks that each binding resolves inside its own EntityId. Nothing ties binding.EntityId to the step's record type (a trigger's condition bindings do get that check, in NendoTriggerDefinition.ValidateShape at BehaviourDefinitions.cs:1087), and nothing refuses event-record bindings in a CreateRecord step of a trigger that also runs on Deleted (links get that check at Behaviour.cs:504, bindings do not). Record IDs are caller-chosen and unique only within a type (create_record: 'Stable caller-selected record ID').
- **Failure:** (a) Action: SetField on ReferencedRecord taskProject, assignment projectNote = `title` with a SameRecordField binding starting from task. It installs; every task edit is refused with 'A record this calculation reads is no longer there.' because the task table is read with the project's ID, or, if a task happens to carry the project's record ID (e.g. both '1'), the project silently receives an unrelated task's title. (b) Trigger on Created, Deleted whose CreateRecord step logs the event record's name: installs, and every delete of that type is refused.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe2.ps1 compiling the SetField-on-ReferencedRecord action plus its trigger through CompiledBehaviour.Compile -> COMPILED OK (2 definitions); the storage-level install checks were read and contain no binding-origin check.
- **Fix and guard:** In RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync, require every assignment binding's EntityId to equal the step's evaluation record type (target entity for SetField, trigger.EntityId for CreateRecord), and refuse event-record bindings in a CreateRecord step when the trigger subscribes to Deleted, as action-target-mismatch naming action, step, binding and both record types. Guard: ActionTargetTests installing each mismatched pair expects action-target-mismatch.
- **Verifier:** Traced. The planner resolves a SetField assignment's bindings with the target record's ID (BehaviourPlanner.cs:220 passes entityId/targetRecordId) and a CreateRecord assignment's with raised.Key.RecordId (:277), then BehaviourSource.ReadFieldAsync reads binding.EntityId's table by that ID (:239-248). At install, RequireBehaviourBindingsResolveAsync (Behaviour.cs:343-398) only resolves each binding inside its own EntityId, and RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync (:454-480) only checks that the assigned field exists on the step's record type; NendoActionStep/NendoActionAssignment.Validate (BehaviourDefinitions.cs:571, 636) and CompiledBehaviour.Compile never relate binding.EntityId to the trigger or step. Trigger conditions do get that check (BehaviourDefinitions.cs:1087) and links get the Deleted check (Behaviour.cs:504), so the gap is real. Outcome: a SetField on ReferencedRecord that binds the event record's entity is refused on every save that fires it with 'A record this calculation reads is no longer there' (or silently reads an unrelated same-ID record). The published example (NendoAuthoringExamples.cs:1163) already warns that this 'refuses nothing at install', so it is a known trap, but the contract (calculations-and-actions.md:238-252) presents the pair check as the cure for this class of mistake.
- **Correction:** Scenario (b) should be limited to same-record style bindings: an aggregate binding on a Deleted event legitimately evaluates against staged rows (BehaviourPlanner.cs:125-130 comment), so a blanket refusal of event-record bindings in a CreateRecord step on a Deleted trigger would over-refuse. The requirement for a CreateRecord step is binding.EntityId == trigger.EntityId (not the created type); the evidence sentence about 'the step's record type' is loose for that kind. In SetField the refusal is wrapped with the action and step (BehaviourPlanner.cs:228), so only the CreateRecord path surfaces the bare message.

<a id="ebh-04"></a>

### EBH-04 — An assignment's result type is never compared with the field it writes, and a create step may omit required fields; both install and then fail every save

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/CompiledBehaviour.cs:141`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:463`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:710`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:391`
- **What:** Compile validates each assignment formula and discards the ValidatedExpression, so its ResultType is never used. The pair check only requires the field to exist and be active. `/` always produces Decimal (contract), and ConvertValue for an Integer field calls JsonElement.GetInt64 on the decimal JSON, which throws and becomes 'does not match storage kind'. Text into Date, singleChoice or Reference fields, and Boolean into Integer, are likewise only discovered at save. A CreateRecord step is not checked to cover every required, active field of its record type; the dispatch then refuses 'Required field X needs a value.'. The contract says the pair is resolved against the schema at install so a step does not fail 'at the next save. At that time, the person who saved was not the person who wrote the action.'
- **Failure:** Action 'Average hours' sets the Integer field taskAverage = `total / count`. It installs; every save that raises the trigger is refused with 'Value for field taskAverage does not match storage kind Integer.' (even when the quotient is whole). A kickoff CreateRecord step on task without the required taskTitle installs; every project create is refused.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe2.ps1 compiling an action assigning `a / 2` (Decimal) to an Integer field -> COMPILED OK (2 definitions); install-time pair check read in source.
- **Fix and guard:** In the pair check compare the assignment's validated ResultType with BehaviourScalarOf(field.StorageKind) (allow Integer->Decimal and Date->Text), refuse Reference/DateTime/Uuid targets with the 'use a link' remedy, and for CreateRecord require every required active field to be assigned or linked. Keep the validated assignment from Compile so its type is available. Guard: one refusal test per mismatch, each expecting action-target-mismatch.
- **Verifier:** Traced. CompiledBehaviour.cs:141 calls adapter.Validate for each assignment and discards the ValidatedExpression, so ResultType is never compared. RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync (Behaviour.cs:463-476) checks only that the field exists and is active; it does not look at storage kind or required fields. At run time a mismatch is only found by ConvertValue (Operations.cs:710-745: GetInt64 on a fractional JSON number or GetBoolean mismatch becomes 'does not match storage kind'), and a create step that omits a required active field fails at Operations.cs:391 with 'Required field X needs a value.'. Test D3_17 (BehaviourActionTests.cs:517-535) itself documents that a Text-into-Integer action installs ('Nothing at install time compares the assignment's type to the field's storage kind') and is refused only at save, and no test covers an install-time refusal. The failure is fail-closed (typed refusal, nothing written), but it blocks every edit that fires the trigger until the action is repaired, and ADR-0008 section 6 says a definition that cannot work should be refused before acceptance.
- **Correction:** 'even when the quotient is whole' is overstated: decimal division of whole inputs keeps scale 0 (10/5 serialises as 2, which GetInt64 accepts, and SameScalar treats an equal stored value as a no-op), so the Integer-field failure is for non-whole or scaled results. The proposed fix is too strict as written: Text results may legitimately fill Date, DateTime, Uuid and singleChoice fields when the text is well formed (ConvertValue accepts strings for them), so only clearly impossible pairs (for example Boolean or Text into Integer/Decimal/Boolean, Decimal into Integer) can be refused statically; and 'every required active field must be assigned or linked' must exempt fields that AssignSequencesAsync fills (Operations.cs:370 runs before the required check at :391).

### EBH-06 — Two calculations may share one derived field ID (and schema.addField may reuse one), which crashes surface compilation with a duplicate-key exception

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:331`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourValidation.cs:117`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:843`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:294`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:120`
- **What:** Install only checks a calculation's FieldId against the stored fields of its own record type. NendoBehaviourGraph.ValidateCandidate and CompiledBehaviour.Compile never compare calculations' FieldIds with each other or with other record types' fields, although field IDs are documented as unique file-wide. ExecuteAddFieldMetadataAsync never checks calculated field IDs, so a stored field can later take a derived field's ID. DerivedFieldsOf (surface compile) and the read-only query path both build entity.DerivedFields.ToDictionary(field => field.FieldId), which throws ArgumentException on a duplicate.
- **Failure:** An agent installs calc A and calc B, both with fieldId taskScore on task. Studio's record view shows only the first (resultFor looks up by fieldId). Any proposal or render that compiles a custom surface over task throws 'An item with the same key has already been added' and reaches clients as an internal error, as does a read-only snapshot query over task. Separately, schema.addField taskScore after calc A leaves a stored and a calculated field with one ID, which bindings and the write path then resolve inconsistently.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe4.ps1 compiling two calculations with fieldId taskScore on task -> COMPILED OK (2 definitions); install and addField checks read in source.
- **Fix and guard:** Refuse in ValidateCandidate any two calculations with the same FieldId, and at install any calculation FieldId equal to a stored field ID anywhere in the file; refuse schema.addField of an ID a calculation uses. Guard: BehaviourDefinitionTests for both orders, and a surface-compile test over an entity that would have had a duplicate.
- **Verifier:** Traced. Install checks a calculation's FieldId only against the stored fields of its own record type (Behaviour.cs:331-340). NendoBehaviourGraph.ValidateCandidate (BehaviourValidation.cs:117-192), NendoCalculationDefinition.ValidateShape (BehaviourDefinitions.cs:835-850) and CompiledBehaviour.Compile never compare calculations' FieldIds with each other, and ExecuteAddFieldMetadataAsync (Operations.cs:117-165) never consults calculated field IDs (its only guard is the __nendo_field primary key). ReadDerivedFieldsAsync (Behaviour.cs:128-151) then returns both calculations for the entity, and several readers do ToDictionary(field => field.FieldId): NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:844, NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:294 and :332, and SqliteNendoStore.CalculatedQueries.cs:22. No test covers duplicate calculation field IDs. Reachable by an agent copying a calculation and keeping its fieldId; ArgumentException is not a NendoException, so it surfaces as an internal error.
- **Correction:** The blast radius is larger than stated: DerivedFieldsOfAsync (CalculatedQueries.cs:20-22) is used by the store's record query and aggregate paths (ReadQueries.cs:146 and :472), so every record query over the affected record type throws, not only surface compilation and the read-only snapshot query. Mitigating: it needs an authoring mistake (two definitions sharing a fieldId) and the definitions can be repaired through another reviewed change set, so P2 rather than P1.

### EBH-09 — Installed behaviour is checked against the schema only at install; later schema edits silently break it

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRequirements.cs:17`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:163`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:170`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:593`
- **What:** RequireBehaviourBindingsResolveAsync and RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync run only from ExecuteSetBehaviourDefinitionAsync. ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync reads no behaviour, so a field can become optional under a Sum (which install refuses over an optional field 'because such a sum promises a total that the first empty value breaks'), or under a nullable:false binding, and a field can become required under a CreateRecord step that does not assign it. ValidateRetiredBehaviourAsync checks bindings, step targets and assignments, but not a create step's links (link.FieldId and a ReferencedRecord link's referenceFieldId), which the 2026-10-10 links amendment added.
- **Failure:** (a) project.totalHours sums task.hours (required at install). schema.setFieldRequired(hours, false) commits; the first task saved without hours turns the total into 'Cannot calculate' and refuses every save whose action uses it. (b) Requiring taskNote after a kickoff create step was installed refuses every project create. (c) Retiring taskProject, used only as a kickoff step's link, commits; the next project create is refused with field-retired.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Run behaviour revalidation over the final candidate after schema.setFieldRequired, schema.setFieldPresentation and retirement (bindings, all trigger/action pairs, links and link targets, relevant fields), refusing with retired-binding or a new binding-optional code that names the definition. Guard: one test per schema edit expecting the refusal, and one where the same proposal also rewires the behaviour and is accepted.
- **Verifier:** RequireBehaviourBindingsResolveAsync and RequireActionTargetsResolveAsync are called only from ExecuteSetBehaviourDefinitionAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:170,180; grep shows no other caller). ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync (FieldRequirements.cs:17-46) reads no behaviour, so (a) a required field under an installed Sum can become optional although install refuses exactly that (RequireMemberField -> RequireScalarField, Behaviour.cs:562-597; contract calculations-and-actions.md:167-170), and FoldAsync then throws calculation-missing-input on the first null member (BehaviourSource.cs:~485); (b) making a field required under a CreateRecord step that does not assign it fails every create ('Required field X needs a value', Operations.cs:391-396). (c) ValidateRetiredBehaviourAsync (Retirement.cs:163-195) loops step.Assignments and step targets but never step.Links, and a link value is put in the create's Values (BehaviourPlanner.cs:285-289), which Operations.cs:365 refuses with field-retired for a retired field, so retiring a link-only reference commits and breaks the next trigger run. No test (FieldRequirementTests, FieldRequirementProtocolTests) touches behaviour, and no ADR makes this a trade-off: ADR-0008 line 375 only accepts value-caused errors, and the contract lists retirement as checked 'from the other side' but names only retirement. Failure is loud and fail-closed, with a workaround (restore the old requirement, or rewire in the same proposal).
- **Correction:** None of substance. Note (a) and (b) are schema.setFieldRequired only; schema.setFieldPresentation is cited in the fix but its effect on behaviour was not traced. The 'Cannot calculate' wording in (a) is the calculation-missing-input path.

### ESM-03 — A filterClause's valueKind is never checked against its field or operator, so today on a Boolean or Integer, now on a Date, or null with eq compiles and then every read of the surface is refused

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:703`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:721`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.Extensions.cs:123`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:662`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-window.ts:68`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:696`, `src/Nendo.Engine/RecordQuerySemantics.cs:37`
- **What:** ValidateFilterClause only checks that valueKind is one of literal/today/now/null, and requires a value only for literal. It never asks whether today fits a Date or DateTime field, whether now fits a DateTime, or whether null makes sense with a comparing operator; ValidateFilters for custom views has the same gap. A commandStep does make those checks (NUI287). At read time resolveClauseValue turns today into 'yyyy-MM-dd' (or a local instant for dateTime), now into an ISO timestamp, and null into no value at all; the host then refuses: ConvertValue throws 'does not match storage kind Integer/Boolean' or 'must use the yyyy-MM-dd date format', and RecordQuerySemantics.Validate throws 'Use isNull or isNotNull to query missing values.' A stray value beside today/now is also accepted and silently ignored.
- **Failure:** An agent authors a list 'Overdue' with filterClause {fieldId: due, operator: lt, valueKind: now} on a Date field, or 'Done today' with {fieldId: done (Boolean), operator: eq, valueKind: today}, or {operator: eq, valueKind: null}. The proposal validates and is accepted; from then on the list, its tiles and drills read 'Unavailable' on every load (record-window.ts's own comment describes this exact symptom for an unresolved clause), and nothing in the review warned.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-compile2.ps1 (NendoSemanticCompiler.Compile on the built DLL) -> 'A1. filterClause Done eq valueKind today (a Boolean compared with a date) / valid=True', 'A2. filterClause Due lt valueKind now (a Date compared with a timestamp) / valid=True', 'A3. filterClause Points gt valueKind today / valid=True', 'A4. filterClause Due eq valueKind null (no value) / valid=True', 'A5. ... valueKind today WITH a stray value / valid=True'. The read-time refusals are by source (ConvertValue, RecordQuerySemantics.Validate).
- **Fix and guard:** In ValidateFilterClause (and ValidateFilters) apply the commandStep rule: today only on Date or DateTime, now only on DateTime, null never on a filter (point at isNull/isNotNull instead), and refuse a value with any non-literal valueKind (as NUI289 does for a command step). Use a new code or extend NUI274. Guard: compile tests for each pairing expecting the refusal; falsify by removing the kind check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ValidateFilterClause (NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:683-731) only checks valueKind is in the closed set and requires a value for literal; for today/now/null it never compares the kind with the field's storage kind (ValidateCommandStep does at :662-669, NUI287/288/289) and a stray value beside a non-literal kind is not refused. Nothing else checks it (valueKind appears nowhere else in the Engine compiler). At read time record-window.ts:68-77/107 resolves today to yyyy-MM-dd (or an offset timestamp for dateTime), now to an ISO instant and null to no value; the host then refuses in ValidateRecordQuery -> ConvertValue (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:696-736: GetBoolean/GetInt64 on a string throws, Date requires yyyy-MM-dd) or RecordQuerySemantics.Validate:37-38 ('Use isNull or isNotNull'). A proposal preview only compiles, it never runs the queries, so the review cannot catch it. Impact is one screen reading Unavailable until a new proposal fixes it, not data loss.
- **Correction:** The view-side ValidateFilters (Extensions.cs:109-129) has the same gap, as stated. Priority P2 is borderline P3 because the definition only breaks the one screen and is fixable by another proposal.
