### ESM-04 — Undoing a ui.setProperty revision from History has no definition-revision guard, so it can restore a property that no longer compiles, every custom screen disappears, and the undo cannot itself be undone

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:505`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:164`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:116`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:184`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:333`
- **What:** Every other single-operation definition inverse (retirement, behaviour, link rule, presentation ...) carries the applied definition revision as its expected revision, so it only runs while nothing has changed since. CreateSetUiPropertyInverseAsync checks only that the property still holds the value the revision wrote, and emits a SetUiPropertyOperation, which has no revision check. The compensation is applied directly (no proposal, so no preview compile), and ValidateRetiredBindingsAsync only inspects the entityId, fieldId, groupByFieldId and cardFieldIds properties, not orderByFieldId, dateFieldId, endDateFieldId, titleFieldId, subtitleFieldId, accentFieldId, rowByFieldId, columnByFieldId, rankByFieldId, viaFieldId, targetEntityId or visibleWhen. The contract says every compile error suppresses all custom plans, and a compensation revision of non-record operations 'cannot itself be compensated'.
- **Failure:** R1 orders a list by Old sort, R2 re-orders it by New sort, R3 retires Old sort (nothing binds it, so it is accepted). The person presses Undo on R2 in History: it is accepted, the list is ordered by a retired field again, the whole definition fails NUI278, every list, board, page and front page of the file falls back to Studio, and Undo on that compensation is refused. The only way back is to author a proposal. The same happens for a visibleWhen or a filter pointed back at a calculation that a later revision removed.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-undo-property.ps1 (NendoWriteCoordinator on a temp .nendo in the scratch folder) -> 'R3: Old sort retired, which nothing binds now. / surfaces compile: valid=True applications=1 / --- Undo R2 from History / ACCEPTED: compensation revision-9ac6... / surfaces compile: valid=False applications=0 / NUI278 [list.root/orderByFieldId] The ordering field does not exist or is retired. / --- Undo the undo / REFUSED: NendoCompensationNotSupportedException: A compensation revision cannot itself be compensated.'
- **Fix and guard:** Refuse the ui.setProperty inverse when the definition revision has moved since the revision (as the other definition inverses do), or compile the candidate surface definition inside the compensation transaction and refuse a compensation that turns a valid definition invalid; widen ValidateRetiredBindingsAsync to every field- and entity-naming property. Guard: an Engine test reproducing the probe that expects the compensation to be refused; falsify by removing the guard.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. History's Compensate button (view-history.ts:20, canCompensate) calls CompensateRevisionAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:321-376), which applies the mutation directly with no preview compile. For a single-operation ui.setProperty revision CreateSetUiPropertyInverseAsync (Compensation.cs:505-568) checks only that the property still holds the value the revision wrote, then emits a SetUiPropertyOperation, which carries no expected definition revision (Operations.cs:309-345). Every other definition inverse reads appliedDefinitionRevision from its evidence (Retirement.cs:192, Choices.cs:146, LinkRules.cs:279 and the others grepped) and so refuses once the definition has moved. The only post-check is ValidateRetiredBindingsAsync (SqliteNendoStore.cs:184), which looks at entityId, fieldId, groupByFieldId and cardFieldIds only (Retirement.cs:116), so orderByFieldId, dateFieldId, visibleWhen and the rest slip through. The undo of the compensation is then refused by Compensation.cs:164-168. ADR-0006 line 70 says an inverse is offered only when preconditions prove it safe, which this inverse does not. Consequence is a suppressed set of custom screens (contract: every error suppresses all custom plans), with Studio still reachable and a proposal as the way back; no data is lost.
- **Correction:** Reaches only a single-operation ui.setProperty revision (a multi-operation revision is refused earlier at Compensation.cs:196-202), so the scenario needs the edit to have been its own revision. The UI button is labelled Compensate, not Undo.

### ESM-05 — Literal values in filter clauses and command steps are checked for JSON type only: a Date, DateTime or UUID in the wrong format, or a retired choice, compiles and is then refused on every read or every run

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:734`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:658`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:724`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Choices.cs:124`
- **What:** ValidateLiteral accepts any JSON string for Date, DateTime, Uuid, Text and Reference fields. Storage's ConvertValue requires yyyy-MM-dd for a Date, an ISO timestamp with an explicit zone for a DateTime and a hyphenated UUID, and refuses otherwise. A commandStep literal on a single-choice field is checked against field.Options (NUI286), which still lists retired options (ChoiceMetadataIsValid requires Choices.Count == Options.Count), while ValidateChoiceAssignment refuses a retired choice on every write.
- **Failure:** A list filtered on Due eq '2026/10/31' or '31-10-2026', or a view filtered on a UUID field with a shortened ID, validates and is accepted, then fails 'Value for field due must use the yyyy-MM-dd date format.' on every read. A 'Mark done' command whose step sets Stage to the option a later proposal retired keeps compiling and appearing as a button, and every press is refused 'This choice is retired. Select an available choice.'
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-compile2.ps1 -> 'B1. filterClause literal 'next week' on a Date, and 'abc' on a Uuid / valid=True'; 'C1. commandStep literal sets Stage to the RETIRED choice 'done' / valid=True'; 'C2. commandStep literal sets Due to 'tomorrow' / valid=True'. The run-time refusals are by source.
- **Fix and guard:** Make ValidateLiteral apply the same format rules ConvertValue applies (DateOnly.TryParseExact yyyy-MM-dd, the timestamp pattern, Guid 'D'), and make NUI286 check against the field's active choices (Choices where !Retired). Guard: compile tests for each malformed literal and for a retired choice expecting NUI277/NUI286; falsify by restoring the string-only check.
- **Verifier:** Traced. ValidateLiteral (NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:734-753) accepts any JSON string for Date, DateTime, Uuid, Text and Reference, while ConvertValue (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:725-736) requires yyyy-MM-dd, an ISO timestamp with explicit zone and a hyphenated UUID, and is applied to every filter value at read time (ReadQueries.cs:518-520, HierarchyReads.cs:37), so a malformed filter literal refuses every read of that screen. A bare date such as 2026-10-01 on a DateTime field is a likely authoring slip and is refused the same way. For commands, NUI286 (:658-660) checks field.Options, and Options still lists retired choices (SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:32 passes field.Options; retirement only flips __nendo_choice.retired, Choices.cs:90-96), while ValidateChoiceAssignment (Choices.cs:124-129) refuses a retired choice on every write; ValidateRetiredBindingsAsync does not look at a step's value, so retiring the choice is accepted. The literal in a commandStep is likewise only type-checked.
- **Correction:** Filter literals on a retired choice are legitimate (finding old records), so the retired-choice half applies to commandStep literals only, which is how the finding words it. Impact is a broken screen or an always-refused button, fixable by a new proposal.

### ESM-09 — A wrongly typed integer in a canonical payload escapes the shape check as InvalidOperationException or OverflowException and reaches the agent as NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:386`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:395`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:122`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:426`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:926`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:87`
- **What:** Integer() and Long() call JsonElement.TryGetInt32/TryGetInt64 without checking ValueKind; both throw InvalidOperationException for a string, null, boolean, object or array. setFieldSequence's width uses checked((int)width), which throws OverflowException. RequireCompilable only catches NendoValidationException or ArgumentException, and NendoToolErrors.Translate maps anything else to NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR and writes a device failure report. Only a fractional number gets the intended 'requires an integer' refusal.
- **Failure:** An agent sends ui.addNode with "position":"1", data.setField with "expectedRecordVersion":null, a rating addField with "max":"5", data.createRecord expectedTargetVersions {"a":"2"}, schema.renameEntity with "expectedDefinitionRevision":"3" or setFieldSequence with width 99999999999. Instead of a refusal naming the operation and property, add_operations fails with 'The local Nendo request failed (InvalidOperationException; failure ...)', and a failure record is written for a client typo.

- **Fix and guard:** In Integer and Long require value.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Number before TryGet*, and range-check width before the cast, throwing NendoValidationException with the property name. Guard: a canonical-compiler test table of non-number values for every integer property asserting NendoValidationException naming the property; falsify by removing the ValueKind check.
- **Verifier:** CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:384-399 Integer()/Long() call JsonElement.TryGetInt32/TryGetInt64 with no ValueKind check; I ran the API in pwsh 7.6.6 and it throws InvalidOperationException for a String and for Null (it does not return false). Line 122 does checked((int)width), which overflows. No earlier guard exists: NendoToolBoundary.cs:114-118 treats an operation payload as Open and defers to the engine, and NendoAgentAuthoringService.RequireCompilable (:926) catches only NendoValidationException or ArgumentException. NendoToolErrors.Translate (:87) then returns NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR and writes a failure report. The draft is not corrupted because RequireCompilable runs before AddRange. The defect is real but the effect is a retry with an unactionable message, so P2.

### ESM-10 — schema.addField accepts longText or singleLine on any storage kind, and the presentation can never be corrected afterwards

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:180`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:203`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:120`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldPresentation.cs:19`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:433`
- **What:** AddFieldOperation.ValidatePresentation ties singleChoice, markdown and rating to their storage kind and date to Date, but has no rule for longText or singleLine, and ExecuteAddFieldMetadataAsync stores whatever passed. ExecuteSetFieldPresentationAsync refuses any field whose storage is not Text ('is not a text field shown as a single line, long text or Markdown, so its presentation cannot change'), so the bad presentation is permanent. fieldControlMarkup draws presentation longText as a textarea before it looks at the storage kind.
- **Failure:** schema.addField with storageKind Integer, Boolean or Date and presentation longText is accepted; the record form shows a four-row textarea for a whole number, a yes/no or a date in place of the number input, checkbox or date picker, and neither Studio nor setFieldPresentation can change it. An Integer created with presentation singleLine can never be made unique (FieldRules requires an Integer's presentation to be null). Only retiring the field and adding a new one recovers.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-check.ps1 -> 'ACCEPTED schema.addField {..."storageKind":"Integer","required":false,"presentation":"longText"}', 'ACCEPTED ... "storageKind":"Boolean" ... "presentation":"singleLine"', 'ACCEPTED ... "storageKind":"Reference" ... "presentation":"longText"'; storage and renderer by source.

- **Verifier:** AddFieldOperation.ValidatePresentation (Operations.cs:172-213) ties singleChoice, markdown, date and rating to a storage kind but has no rule for singleLine or longText. SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:120-157 stores whatever passed. ExecuteSetFieldPresentationAsync (FieldPresentation.cs:19-21) refuses any non-Text field, so the presentation cannot be corrected. record-markup.ts:433 draws a textarea for presentation longText before it looks at the storage kind. FieldRules.cs:58-60 CanBeUnique requires an Integer's presentation to be null, so Integer plus singleLine can never be made unique. No test accepts such a combination, and NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:48 lists the presentations without tying them to a storage kind. Reachable only through an agent mistake, but the result is permanent.
- **Correction:** The recovery is costlier than the finding says. RequireUniqueDisplayNameAsync (Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Evolution.cs:22-35) scans retired fields too, so the author must rename the field, retire it, add a new one under the old name and move the data. The suggested fix (refuse longText and singleLine unless StorageKind is Text) is right, and it should reuse SetFieldPresentationOperation.TextPresentations.

### ESM-12 — ui.addNode declares Reversible and ui.moveNode ReversibleWithRetainedState, but compensation implements neither, so the review labels changes reversible that History cannot reverse

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:288`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:373`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:222`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:312`, `src/Nendo.Engine/FieldPresentationOperations.cs:35`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldPresentation.cs:57`
- **What:** The single-operation compensation switch has no 'ui.addNode' or 'ui.moveNode' case (default: 'Compensation is not implemented for ...'), and CreateCausalInverses refuses any non-record operation in a multi-operation revision. ui.moveNode already retains previousParentNodeId and previousPosition, so an inverse is available but unused. The review renders each semantic diff line with reversibilityLabel, which prints 'Reversible' for an added node. ADR-0006 driver 4 requires reversibility claims to match available inverse evidence. Related: schema.setFieldPresentation declares Reversible although its inverse depends on retained evidence (previousPresentation) and writes 'singleLine' where the field had null.
- **Failure:** A person accepts 'Add the record list "Open deals".' labelled Reversible, or a section move labelled 'Compensatable with retained state', and History later refuses with 'Compensation is not implemented for ui.addNode' or '... ui.moveNode'.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Implement the inverses (ui.removeNode for an added node with no later children, ui.moveNode back to the retained parent and position) or declare both IrreversibleDeclared until they exist; declare setFieldPresentation ReversibleWithRetainedState and restore a null presentation exactly. Guard: a test that applies one instance of every NendoOperation subtype and asserts that each non-IrreversibleDeclared class produces a compensation mutation; falsify by removing a case.
- **Verifier:** Operations.cs:288 declares ui.addNode Reversible and :373 declares ui.moveNode ReversibleWithRetainedState. The single-operation switch in Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:222-310 has no case for either (default 'Compensation is not implemented for ...'), and CreateCausalInverses (:312-340) refuses any non-record operation. ui.moveNode retains previousParentNodeId and previousPosition (Operations.cs:316), so an inverse is available but unused. format.ts:90 prints 'Reversible' and 'Compensatable with retained state' for these, and help-concepts.ts:170 says 'a screen node added' is Reversible. ReadQueries.cs:538-541 comments that a ui.moveNode 'is ReversibleWithRetainedState yet has no inverse', which is the same mismatch. ADR-0006 driver 4 requires the claims to match the inverse evidence.
- **Correction:** The failure scenario is wrong about when History refuses. SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:538-580 computes canRequestCompensation from the implemented operation types, and ui.addNode and ui.moveNode are not in that list, so History never offers Compensate for them and no click is refused. The real defect is only that the review, History's per-operation lines and help-concepts.ts:170 overstate reversibility. The suggested fix 'declare both IrreversibleDeclared' is not viable: ADR-0023 says the class is part of every stored operation's canonical form, so a change breaks stored digests. The correct fix is to implement the inverses (or correct the label and help text). The setFieldPresentation sub-point is a minor nit, since null versus 'singleLine' is the same presentation.

<a id="ess-01"></a>

### ESS-01 — Definition operations read or rebuild a record table as if a field added earlier in the same mutation already had a column, and fail with a raw SqliteException

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-storage-schema`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Hierarchy.cs:184`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Hierarchy.cs:188`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:100`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRequirements.cs:44`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:79`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:61`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:554`
- **What:** ExecuteAddFieldMetadataAsync inserts the __nendo_field row immediately, but the column is added only by MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync after every operation of the mutation (Operations.cs:554-564). GetEntityMappingAsync re-reads __nendo_field, so later operations in the same mutation see the new field. RequireTreeAsync guards only on TableExistsAsync (Hierarchy.cs:184, comment: 'A record type created in the same mutation has no table yet') and then runs SELECT __nendo_record_id, "<parent column>" (line 188). RebuildRequiredConstraintsAsync (called from ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync line 44-45 and ExecuteSetRetiredAsync line 79-80) builds its column list from entity.Fields and copies with INSERT INTO temp (...) SELECT ... FROM table (Retirement.cs:97-100) without ColumnExistsAsync. ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync checks materialization only for its own field (lines 29-32), never for siblings. The entity-retirement incoming-reference probe (Retirement.cs:59-62) has the same gap for a reference added and configured in the mutation. Every other reader in scope (EnsureUniqueIndexAsync, RequireNoCollisionsAsync, NextFromDataAsync, IndexRowsAsync, ExecuteConfigureReferenceAsync) does check ColumnExistsAsync.
- **Failure:** One proposal mutation on an existing record type 'capabilities': schema.addField(parent, Reference, optional), schema.configureReference(parent -> capabilities), schema.declareHierarchy(capabilities, parent). DeclareHierarchy reaches RequireTreeAsync, the table exists, the parent column does not: SQLite Error 1 'no such column: "parent"'. Likewise [schema.addField(notes), schema.setFieldRequired(title, true)] or [schema.addField(notes), schema.setRetired(requiredField, true)] on an existing type fails in the rebuild's INSERT...SELECT. The exception is not a NendoException, so proposal validation drops the proposal and rethrows (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:153-165): the author sees an internal error instead of a diagnostic, and the natural one-mutation change set ('add a Parent field and make it the hierarchy') cannot be validated at all; splitting it into two mutations is the only workaround and nothing says so.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_tree_unmaterialized.py against the e_sqlite3.dll that Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 10.0.11 ships (SQLitePCLRaw 2.1.12, SQLite 3.53.3), replaying RequireTreeAsync's SQL -> RequireTreeAsync: (1, 'no such column: "parent" - should this be a string literal in single-quotes?'). Executed: python -I probe_e_sqlite3_dqs.py with the same DLL, replaying RebuildRequiredConstraintsAsync's copy for a mapping that lists a pending column -> rebuild copy: (1, 'no such column: "notes" - should this be a string literal in single-quotes?'). The probes replay the Engine's SQL in scratch; the Engine itself was not run.
- **Fix and guard:** In RebuildRequiredConstraintsAsync build the temp table and the copy from fields whose column exists (ColumnExistsAsync), leaving pending columns to MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync's ADD COLUMN, which appends them in the same field order. In RequireTreeAsync return early when the parent column does not exist yet (a just-added column holds no values). Apply the same guard to the entity-retirement probe. Guard: Engine tests that apply one mutation [addField(parent), configureReference, declareHierarchy] and one [addField(notes), setFieldRequired(title,true)] to an existing populated record type and assert the commit succeeds (and the tree/NOT NULL hold); falsify by removing the column check and quote the SqliteException 'no such column'.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ExecuteAddFieldMetadataAsync (Operations.cs:151-169) inserts the __nendo_field row at once, but the column is added only by MaterializeSchemaChangesAsync after all operations (Operations.cs:554-564, SqliteNendoStore.cs:154-177), and GetEntityMappingAsync (Operations.cs:654-679) lists every __nendo_field row. RequireTreeAsync (Hierarchy.cs:184-188) guards only TableExistsAsync, so for an existing table it selects a parent column that does not exist yet. RebuildRequiredConstraintsAsync (Retirement.cs:96-100) puts every entity.Fields column into the INSERT..SELECT with no ColumnExistsAsync, and is reached from ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync (FieldRequirements.cs:44-45) and ExecuteSetRetiredAsync (Retirement.cs:79-80). Its materialization check covers only its own field (FieldRequirements.cs:29-32). Nothing upstream stops the mix: NendoMutation.Validate (Operations.cs:531-557) only forbids mixing lanes, and the authoring text explicitly invites configureReference in the same mutation as addField (NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:56). I ran the reviewer's probe_e_sqlite3_dqs.py against the Engine's e_sqlite3 2.1.12 DLL: the copy fails with 'no such column: "notes" - should this be a string literal in single-quotes?', so DQS is off and the failure is real. SqliteException is not a NendoException, so ApplyChangeSetAsync does not record it, and proposal validation drops the proposal and rethrows (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:~153-165). Existing tests build the hierarchy only on a new entity, where TableExistsAsync returns early (HierarchyProtocolTests.cs:21-28, ReviewStorageRegressionTests.cs:17-33). No data is lost, the transaction rolls back, and splitting into two mutations works around it, so P2.
- **Correction:** The entity-retirement probe (Retirement.cs:59-62) needs an unusual combination (a reference added and bound in the mutation that retires its target), so it is much less likely than the hierarchy and required/retired rebuild cases. The Engine itself was not run; the SQL probe and the code trace stand in for it.

### ESS-02 — Undoing a deletion is refused whenever the same revision also wrote a record the deleted record references (a delete-triggered action updating its parent, or a batch that edits the target after the delete)

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `engine-storage-schema`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Deletion.cs:68`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Deletion.cs:115`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.References.cs:150`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:377`
- **What:** ExecuteDeleteRecordAsync records each reference target's version in target_versions_json while the operation executes (Deletion.cs:68-71), before RunBehaviourChainAsync runs the mutation's automatic actions. A Deleted trigger whose step targets NendoActionTarget.Referenced(...) writes the parent from the before-state (BehaviourPlanner.cs:162-181, 235-240), advancing its version in the same revision. CreateCausalInverses reverses operations in reverse order (Compensation.cs:351), so the generated SetField inverse runs first and leaves the parent at v+2; then RestoreDeletedRecordOperation (line 377-382) is built with no planned target versions, unlike the SetField branch, which substitutes versions[targetKey] for a target the revision itself wrote (lines 390-405, the R-015 fix for moves). ExecuteRestoreDeletedRecordAsync only adjusts a target that was itself deleted and restored (Deletion.cs:115-117), then ValidateReferenceValueAsync compares the current version with the recorded one (References.cs:150-151). The behaviour compensation fixture already has such a trigger (BehaviourCompensationTests.cs:270-281: Created\|Updated\|Deleted, writes projects.total) but no test deletes and undoes.
- **Failure:** Projects keep a 'Finished' count with an action triggered on task Created/Updated/Deleted. The person deletes a finished task t2 (project p1 at version 5; the action writes total, p1 -> 6). Immediately choosing Undo in History: the total inverse puts p1 at 7, the restore expects 5, and the whole compensation is refused as target-version-conflict 'The selected target changed. Select it again before saving.' The deletion is declared ReversibleWithRetainedState, yet it can never be undone, and the record ID stays reserved, so the person cannot even re-create t2 under its ID. The same happens for a batch [data.deleteRecord(t2), data.setField(p1.name)].
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** When CreateCausalInverses emits a RestoreDeletedRecordOperation, give it the version each of the record's reference targets will hold when it runs, computed from the revision's own evidence exactly as the SetField branch does (versions[targetKey] for a target the revision touched, carried versions otherwise), and have ExecuteRestoreDeletedRecordAsync use those in place of target_versions_json for those targets; the restore stays built from history, never from client input. Also give the restore's refusal its own wording ('X changed after this record was deleted') instead of the picker message. Guard: in BehaviourCompensationTests, delete a finished task under the fixture's Deleted trigger, compensate, and assert the task is back at deletedVersion+1 and the total restored; falsify by dropping the override and quote the target-version-conflict.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ExecuteDeleteRecordAsync stores target_versions_json from the pre-chain state (Deletion.cs:68-71, 85) and the delete's evidence keeps deletedVersion (Deletion.cs:93). A Deleted trigger whose step targets Referenced(...) resolves its targets from raised.Before and writes the parent (BehaviourPlanner.cs Targets, ~lines 150-167), which appends a SetField to the same revision after the delete. CreateCausalInverses reverses in reverse order (Compensation.cs:351), so the parent's SetField inverse runs first and leaves the parent at v+2. The RestoreDeletedRecordOperation is then built from deletedVersion alone (Compensation.cs:377-382), unlike the SetField branch, which swaps in versions[targetKey] for a target the revision wrote (Compensation.cs:396-405). ExecuteRestoreDeletedRecordAsync adjusts only a target that was itself deleted and restored (Deletion.cs:115-117), then ExecuteCreateRecordAsync(restoring: true) still calls ValidateReferenceValueAsync (Operations.cs:373-379), which compares the parent's current version to the recorded one and throws target-version-conflict (References.cs:150-151). The compensation is refused whole. The ID stays reserved (Operations.cs:354), so there is no way to bring the record back under its ID. No test deletes under a Deleted trigger and then compensates (BehaviourActionTests.cs:152 deletes but never undoes; BehaviourCompensationTests.cs has no delete case). The refusal is clean, so there is no corruption. Delete is declared ReversibleWithRetainedState, and rollup actions on Deleted are the standard use of the feature, so it is a material defect with no workaround for that record.
- **Correction:** The trigger has to change the parent's value, otherwise the planner skips the write ('already what it should be', BehaviourPlanner.cs RunStepAsync). In the BehaviourCompensationTests fixture, deleting an undone task leaves the count unchanged and does not hit this; deleting a done task does. The batch variant [deleteRecord(t2), setField(p1.x)] is reached the same way.

### GGV-05 — Dependency graph hides the arrowhead of every link whose target is not to the right of its source, so its direction cannot be read

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:97`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:95`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:101`
- **What:** Except for a same-row link pointing left, every link is drawn from the source's right edge to the target's left edge (to.x, to.y+33). When the target is in the same column or a column to the left on another row, the curve's last control point lies to the right of to.x, so the path arrives moving left and the marker's body sits inside the target's rectangle. Edges are appended before the nodes, so the node's filled rect paints over the arrowhead.
- **Failure:** In a grid of five records (three on the first row, two below) a link n0->n3 (straight down) and n2->n4 (down and left) show as plain lines with no arrowhead: the person cannot tell whether Node 0 blocks Node 3 or Node 3 blocks Node 0, which is what a dependency graph is for. With the grid placement this affects roughly every link that goes down or left.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-arrows.mjs -> [{"edge":"n0->n3","tip":[30,273],"body":[38,270],"bodyUnderTarget":true},{"edge":"n2->n4","tip":[260,273],"body":[269,272],"bodyUnderTarget":true},{"edge":"n0->n4",...,"bodyUnderTarget":false}]; screenshot dependency-graph-arrows.png shows the first two links without arrowheads.
- **Fix and guard:** Pick the target's attachment side from the relative position (top edge when the target is lower, right edge when it is left, as Systems Lens does with its return legs), or draw edges above the nodes, ending at the box boundary. Guard: Review-NendoGraph asserts, for every edge, that getPointAtLength(length - 9) lies outside its target node's box; falsify with the current path.
- **Verifier:** graph.js:97 draws every non-same-row link from (from.x+190, from.y+33) to (to.x, to.y+33) with the last control point at ((from.x+190+to.x)/2, to.y+33-bend). When to.x <= from.x the path therefore arrives at the target's left edge travelling left, from inside the target's own x-range. The marker (index.html:8: refX 9, stroke 1.7, so about 10.7 units of body trail the path end) lies inside the 190x66 rect, and edges are appended before nodes (graph.js:98-99 then :122) while .node rect has an opaque fill (graph.css:7), so the node paints over the arrowhead and the last stretch of the line. The grid placement at :83-84 puts columns 230 apart, so any link to the same or an earlier column is affected. I viewed dependency-graph-arrows.png: n0->n3 and n2->n4 have no arrowhead, n0->n4 has one. The package advertises 'directed edges' (nendo-package.json) and no gate checks arrowheads.
- **Correction:** The direction is still available in text: the selection line and text view give incoming and outgoing counts and names, which is the workaround. The package ships in extensions/ as a documented example, but the planner uses Work dependencies (ELK, orthogonal routes) and not this view, so reach is mainly authors who copy the example.

<a id="mtd-01"></a>

### MTD-01 — Import resolves every reference target version once, before the first batch, so a later batch fails when an earlier batch's automatic action moves a referenced record

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:149`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:217`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:255`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Csv.cs:185`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:178`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.References.cs:150`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:170`
- **What:** ImportCsvAsync calls DecodeCsvRowsAsync once for offset 0 and count = Rows.Count, which caches one version per target (targets dictionary) and gives a row created earlier in the same import version 1 (CsvCodeResolver.Resolve returns (planned, 1)). ImportRecordsAsync likewise maps every JSON record through toEntry before CommitAsync runs. CommitAsync then commits batch after batch with those versions. The store checks each target's version for exact equality (target-version-conflict), and automatic actions run after the authored operations of each mutation (RunBehaviourChainAsync after the operation loop), so a commit of batch 1 can advance a record that batch 2's rows still expect at its old version. The native importer prepares one batch at a time (PrepareCsvBatchAsync decodes its own window), so it does not have this problem.
- **Failure:** Task has a reference to Project and an automatic action 'when a Task is created, set its Project's lastActivity'. An agent imports 120 tasks that all name project p1 (by record ID, or by code with matchFieldId). All rows are resolved at p1 version 5. Batch 1 (50 rows) commits and the action moves p1 to version 55. Batch 2 is refused with target-version-conflict, the call answers NENDO_IMPORT_PARTIAL committed=50. The documented recovery, an identical retry, replays batch 1, re-resolves batch 2 and commits it, then fails on batch 3: each retry advances one batch, so a 500-row import needs ten calls. The same happens without any reference to another type when an action writes back to a parent row of the same import: children in a later batch expect the parent at version 1.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Decode and resolve one batch at a time immediately before it is committed (DecodeCsvRowsAsync(offset = batchStart, count = BatchSize) after the previous batch commits; call toEntry per batch for JSON), keeping the receipt-recorded versions for batches that already committed. Guard: a LocalMcp import test with an automatic action on create that sets a field on the referenced record, 120 rows naming one target, asserting a single import_records call commits all 120 and Remaining is 0; falsify by restoring the up-front decode and watching it answer NENDO_IMPORT_PARTIAL.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoImportService.cs:149-158 decodes all rows once (offset 0, count = Rows.Count), and NendoApplicationService.Csv.cs:185-214 caches one target version per (entity, record); CsvCodeResolver likewise returns version 1 for a row of the same import. CommitAsync (:255-283) then commits batch by batch with those versions, and the JSON path maps every record through toEntry before CommitAsync (:217-222). The store compares exactly (SqliteNendoStore.References.cs:150, target-version-conflict). Within one mutation, all create operations are validated first (SqliteNendoStore.cs:154-161) and RunBehaviourChainAsync runs after them (:170-172), and an action step with a ReferencedRecord target writes the referenced record via SetFieldOperation (SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:172-241), bumping its version. So batch 1 commits and batch 2 is refused, giving NENDO_IMPORT_PARTIAL. The native importer decodes per batch (PrepareCsvBatchAsync), so it is unaffected. The existing test comment (ImportExportProtocolTests.cs:243-244) assumes no refusal can stop a CSV import between batches, and no test covers an action. Needs an action writing a referenced record plus more than 50 rows, with a workaround (<=50 rows per call), hence P2.
- **Correction:** The v5 to v55 detail holds only if the action writes a different value for each created task. A single bump (for example set Project.status to Active) is enough to fail batch 2. The retry-advances-one-batch claim holds only for an action whose value changes on every batch; a one-time bump lets the first retry finish.

<a id="r2aav-01"></a>

### R2AAV-01 — A reusable function's declared resultType is never checked against its body; callers are typed by the body, so the published signature is decorative

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adr-and-vision-conformance`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/CompiledBehaviour.cs:76`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:178`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/CompiledBehaviour.cs:106`, `docs/design/adr-0008-semantics.md:21`, `docs/decisions/0008-general-scripting-and-capability-isolation.md:315`
- **What:** CompiledBehaviour.Compile validates each NendoFunctionDefinition through adapter.Validate (lines 76-90) and stores the ValidatedExpression, but never compares function.ResultType with the analyzed expression.ResultType. The comparison exists only for calculations (lines 106-111). NendoBehaviourAnalyzer.ApplicationCall then returns target.ResultType (line 178), which is the analyzed body type, not the declared one. adr-0008-semantics.md says 'Reusable functions declare typed parameters and a result; recursive definitions and mismatched types refuse validation', and ADR-0008 section 3 makes the declared result type part of the stored function. The declared resultType is still what the body codec stores, what describe and the review show, and what an agent reads.
- **Failure:** An agent installs function fn.label declared resultType Integer with body Concat('n','o'). It installs. A calculation declared Text that calls label(x) also installs, although the function says Integer. A calculation declared Integer that calls it is refused with "'calc.i' declares integer but its formula produces text", which blames the calculation for a type the function's published signature contradicts. The same happens when a function declared Decimal has an Integer body: callers compute in Int64 and can overflow where the declared Decimal would not.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: function-type-probe.ps1 (reflection over the built Nendo.Engine.dll, CompiledBehaviour.Compile) -> '1. function declared integer, body text : COMPILED: fn.label analyzed=Text'; '2. function declared integer, body p / 2 (decimal) : COMPILED: fn.half analyzed=Decimal'; '3. calculation declared text = label(x) : COMPILED'; '4. calculation declared integer = label(x) : REFUSED [NendoValidationException] 'calc.i' declares integer but its formula produces text.'
- **Fix and guard:** In the function loop of CompiledBehaviour.Compile, refuse when the analyzed type differs from function.ResultType (allowing only Integer body for a Decimal declaration, and then widen at the call), with a message that names the function. Have ApplicationCall return the declared type. Guard: a BehaviourCalculationTests case that installs a function declared Integer with a Text body and expects a refusal naming the function, falsified by removing the new check.
- **Verifier:** CompiledBehaviour.cs:76-90 validates each function body through adapter.Validate and stores the ValidatedExpression without comparing function.ResultType to the analyzed type; the only such comparison is for calculations at :106-111. BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:178 returns target.ResultType, which is the analyzed body type (ExpressionAdapter.cs:147-149), not the declared one. No other check exists: NendoFunctionDefinition is referenced only by the codec, SemanticDiff, BehaviourValidation.cs:129 (count only) and CompiledBehaviour. The reviewer's reflection probe reproduces it (probe-function-type.log: declared Integer with Text body compiles; a calculation declared Integer calling it is refused blaming the calculation). The design intent is stated at adr-0008-semantics.md:21-22 and ADR-0008:315.
- **Correction:** The current contract's Validation list (calculations-and-actions.md:286-301) does not list function result-type mismatch; the promise lives in the historical design note adr-0008-semantics.md:21-22 and in ADR-0008 s3 (declared result types stored), so say 'design intent' rather than 'contract violation'. Evaluation stays consistent with the static (body) type, so no wrong value is produced; the harm is a false published signature, a misattributed refusal, and the Int64-vs-Decimal overflow edge. P2 is held only because it is a missing install-time type check in the closed validation model; it could equally be rated P3.

<a id="r2ap-01"></a>

### R2AP-01 — MCP undo_revision answers every compensation refusal (already undone, keep mark changed, not a record revision, irreversible) as NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR, where the view and History get compensation-not-supported with its sentence

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adapter-parity`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:87`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:136`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:169`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:52`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:490`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:410`, `docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:359`
- **What:** The Engine refuses a compensation it will not make with NendoCompensationNotSupportedException (a NendoException that is neither a precondition nor a validation): 'This revision already has a compensation revision.', 'A view undoes record changes only, and this revision changes more than records.', 'Whether record X is kept in new files changed after the selected revision...', '... declares itself irreversible ...', '... retained no prior value ...'. WorkbenchProtocol.HandleAsync maps that type to code compensation-not-supported with the Engine's sentence, and custom-views.md:749-751 promises views exactly that code. NendoToolErrors.Translate has no arm for the type, so it falls to the default arm: NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR naming only the exception type, and NendoAgentFailures.Report files it as a host failure in the device's failure record. mcp-interface.md:359 says a definition revision and an irreversible operation 'are refused by the Engine as for a view'. UndoRevisionToolTests line 77 only asserts the text contains 'NENDO_', so it passes on NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR.
- **Failure:** An agent undoes its own set_field (undo_revision, key u1), loses the answer and retries with a new key, or the person has already compensated that revision in History: the call returns 'NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: The local Nendo request failed (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure 2713ab84).' instead of saying the revision is already undone, so the agent reports a Nendo crash and the person's failure record gains an entry for an ordinary refusal. The same happens for an agent undoing a revision whose keep mark changed since, or a definition revision of its own.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratchpad r2-adapter-parity/probe-engine.ps1 (real Nendo.Engine and Nendo.LocalMcp DLLs from artifacts/bin, a fresh file in scratch) -> 'undo #2 (key u2) -> NendoCompensationNotSupportedException [] This revision already has a compensation revision.' / 'MCP tool text: NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: The local Nendo request failed (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure 2713ab84).' and for a definition revision 'A view undoes record changes only, and this revision changes more than records.' -> 'NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: ... (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure a5ed067b).'
- **Fix and guard:** Add a NendoCompensationNotSupportedException arm to NendoToolErrors.Translate (and NendoMcpErrors) yielding NENDO_COMPENSATION_NOT_SUPPORTED with the Engine sentence (the templates carry only record IDs, operation types and counts), and reword the caller-facing sentences so they do not say 'view' (see the revision-not-yours finding). Guard: in UndoRevisionToolTests assert the exact code NENDO_COMPENSATION_NOT_SUPPORTED for a second undo with a new key and for a definition revision, and that no NendoAgentFailure was recorded; falsify by deleting the arm.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs throws NendoCompensationNotSupportedException (a plain NendoException) at :52, :71, :116, :120, :138, :166, :171, :218, :247 for already-compensated, keep mark changed, definition revision, irreversible. UndoRecordWritesAsync (NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:203) and NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:338 let it propagate, and NendoDataMutationService.AdmitAsync/WithConsentAsync catch only NendoPreconditionException. NendoToolCall.RunAsync then calls NendoToolErrors.Translate, whose switch (NendoToolErrors.cs:32-90) has no arm for this type, so it falls to the default at :87 NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR and NendoAgentFailures.Report files a host failure. WorkbenchProtocol.cs:490 maps the same type to compensation-not-supported with the Engine sentence, and custom-views.md:750 promises it. UndoRevisionToolTests.cs:77 asserts only 'NENDO_', so it passes on the internal error. The retry-with-a-new-key scenario (already compensated) is a plausible agent path; same-key retry replays fine.
- **Correction:** mcp-interface.md:359 (cited) says only that these refusals are 'refused by the Engine as for a view' and names no code, so the contract is silent rather than contradicted; the defect is the internal-error classification and the spurious device failure record. NendoMcpErrors (resource path) is irrelevant to this tool path.

<a id="r2lat-01"></a>

### R2LAT-01 — Screens left open past midnight keep yesterday's 'today': lists, tiles, charts and the Garden agenda re-read only on a file change, while the calendar's today ring moves

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:429`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:416`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:479`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-use.ts:60`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/reads.ts:284`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-window.ts:111`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-markup.ts:176`, `extensions/garden/agenda.js:124`
- **What:** A clause with valueKind today is resolved when a query is built (record-window.ts clauseFilters/resolveClauseValue use new Date() at call time), and a trend or activity range is resolved by the Engine against DateTime.Now each time it is read. But every Workbench read is cached by changeSequence alone: readIsPending (plan-selection.ts:429-434) re-reads a tile or chart only when known.changeSequence differs, view-use.ts:60-62 says 'A window loaded earlier in this revision is still the answer, so returning to a surface does not re-read it', and loadAccumulatedPage (reads.ts:284) treats a calendar/timeline window as fresh while the change sequence is unchanged. Nothing schedules a redraw at the civil day change (no midnight timer, no visibilitychange, the only setInterval in main.ts:770 is the Agent poll). The calendar's today highlight, by contrast, is recomputed on every render (surface-markup.ts:176-180 todayCivil()). record-window.ts:62-66 itself states that 'a view left open past midnight must not keep asking for yesterday', and DateBuckets.cs says a range is 'resolved against today each time it is read'. The Garden Agenda groups tasks into Overdue/Today/This week with today() at load (agenda.js:124) and reloads only on 'changes' and 'context' events.
- **Failure:** Nendo is tray-resident and stays open overnight (the close button hides it). A screen 'Due today' (filterClause dueDate eq today) still lists yesterday's tasks the next morning; an 'Overdue' tile (dueDate lt today) omits every task that became overdue at midnight; a 'last 30 days' trend still ends yesterday; the Garden Agenda still shows yesterday's tasks under Today. The calendar beside them highlights the new day, so the two disagree on screen. Choosing the screen again in the rail does not help (view-use.ts:62); only an unrelated write that bumps the change sequence corrects it, so on a day nobody writes it never does.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Make the civil day part of every read's freshness: store the resolved civil date (yyyy-MM-dd from the same clock resolveClauseValue uses) beside changeSequence in surfaceWindows, accumulatedWindows, summaryCounts and chartStates, and treat a different day as pending in readIsPending, view-use.ts:62 and loadAccumulatedPage; arm a timer for the next local midnight (re-armed on visibilitychange/resume) that calls rerender. Views get a 'day' event or re-read on the same tick. Guard: a unit test of readIsPending/loadAccumulatedPage with an injected clock that crosses midnight at an unchanged change sequence expects a re-read, and a CDP gate step that overrides Date to 23:59:58, opens a screen with a today clause, advances past midnight and asserts the list and tile were read again with the new date; falsify by removing the day from the key.
- **Verifier:** Traced in source. `today` is resolved with `new Date()` when a query is built (record-window.ts:68-84, clauseFilters), but every Workbench read is gated on changeSequence alone: readIsPending (plan-selection.ts:429-434) re-reads a tile or chart only when known.changeSequence differs, view-use.ts:62 and surface-markup.ts:88 treat a surface window at the current sequence as the answer, and loadAccumulatedPage (reads.ts:276-278) does the same for calendar/timeline pages. main.ts has no midnight timer, no focus/visibilitychange listener (grep finds none), and its only setInterval (main.ts:770) polls Agent status; the Desktop raises fileChanged only from FileCommitted (MainWindow.xaml.cs:225). Meanwhile todayCivil() (plan-selection.ts:133) is recomputed per render, so the calendar ring moves and the lists do not. Garden agenda.js:124 resolves today() only in load(), which runs on 'changes'/'context' events. The app is tray-resident by default (DesktopShellStore.cs:26), so leaving it open overnight is the normal case. Workaround exists (any write, or a back/forward navigation), so P2 rather than higher.
- **Correction:** The recovery paths are slightly wider than the finding says: navigateToPlace (navigation-actions.ts:300) calls refreshDerived with navigation:true, which re-reads the selected surface under a fresh query, so back/forward or a place restore refreshes the open list (tiles and charts still wait for a sequence change). The Garden agenda is only stale while its frame stays alive; a freshly mounted view calls load() and gets the new day. Fix direction is sound: put the resolved civil date beside changeSequence in the freshness test and arm a next-midnight timer.

### R2RM-01 — nendo.data.undo_revision reports every Engine refusal of an undo as NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR, because NendoCompensationNotSupportedException has no translation

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-reversibility-matrix`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:87`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ApplicationModel.cs:466`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:138`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:171`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:98`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataTools.cs:260`, `docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:359`
- **What:** NendoToolErrors.Translate (line 32) has cases for McpException, authority, authoring, import-partial, idempotency, recovery, cancellation, NendoPreconditionException, NendoCalculationException, NendoValidationException and ArgumentException. NendoCompensationNotSupportedException derives straight from NendoException (ApplicationModel.cs:466), so it reaches the `_ =>` arm (line 87), which returns NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR and calls NendoAgentFailures.Report, which writes a device failure record with a stack trace while a tool scope is active. CreateCompensationMutationAsync throws exactly this type for the ordinary refusals the tool description and mcp-interface.md:359 call Engine refusals: a revision already compensated (Compensation.cs:138), 'A view undoes record changes only, and this revision changes more than records.' (:171, the definition-revision case), a keep mark changed since (:52), an irreversible operation (:218, :309), more than 12,800 operations (:301), and a compensation of non-record changes (:166). Two undo-specific precondition codes are also withheld, because they are missing from DiagnosablePreconditions (line 98 onward): deletion-state-conflict (Deletion.cs:106) and field-not-retired (FieldRequirements.cs:55) reach the agent as 'The semantic precondition was not met.' The one refusal that passes through, revision-not-yours, tells the agent 'This revision was not written by this view's package, so the view cannot undo it.' Probe output (reflection on copies of the built Nendo.LocalMcp.dll of 2026-10-10 15:35, newer than the last change to NendoToolErrors.cs and ApplicationModel.cs; no tool scope, so nothing was reported): "NendoCompensationNotSupportedException('This revision already has a compensation revision.') -> NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: The local Nendo request failed (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure 686d7af1)." and the same for the other three messages; "NendoPreconditionException(revision-not-yours) -> NENDO_REVISION_NOT_YOURS: This revision was not written by this view's package, so the view cannot undo it."
- **Failure:** An agent at Edit data calls nendo.data.undo_revision on its own batch after the person has already compensated it in History, or on the definition revision its accepted proposal made. It receives 'NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: The local Nendo request failed (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure 686d7af1).' It cannot tell a refusal from a host crash and has no reason to act on. Each time, the person's device failure log, which is kept for real faults (F-181), gains an entry for a normal refusal. An agent that retries with a new key gets the same internal error again.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh probe-mcp-translate.ps1 (reflection on copies of artifacts/bin/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/debug assemblies in the scratch folder) -> "NendoCompensationNotSupportedException('This revision already has a compensation revision.') -> NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR: The local Nendo request failed (NendoCompensationNotSupportedException; failure 686d7af1)."
- **Fix and guard:** Add `NendoCompensationNotSupportedException => Error("NENDO_COMPENSATION_NOT_SUPPORTED", exception.Message)`; its messages are constants that name revision and record IDs and operation types. List the code in mcp-interface.md, and add deletion-state-conflict and field-not-retired to DiagnosablePreconditions. Word the caller-specific refusals for whoever called ('was not written by this session', 'undo_revision reverses record changes only'). Guard: a NendoToolErrors test asserting the code and message and that NendoAgentFailures receives nothing, plus an MCP tool test that undoes one revision twice under different keys and expects NENDO_COMPENSATION_NOT_SUPPORTED. Falsify by removing the case.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoToolErrors.Translate (src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:32-90) has no arm for NendoCompensationNotSupportedException, which derives straight from NendoException (src/Nendo.Engine/ApplicationModel.cs:466), so it falls to the `_ =>` arm at :87 and becomes NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR plus NendoAgentFailures.Report (a device failure record while the tool scope from NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:470 is active). UndoRevisionAsync (NendoDataMutationService.cs:410-440) goes through AdmitAsync -> NendoToolCall.RunAsync (NendoToolCall.cs:34-37) and nothing in between catches or maps it. CreateCompensationMutationAsync throws that type for ordinary refusals: already compensated under a different key (Compensation.cs:136-139), a definition revision when a caller is set (:169-173), a keep mark changed (:52), irreversible operation (:309), over 12,800 operations (:301). The only MCP test that hits one of these (UndoRevisionToolTests.cs:72-77) asserts just Contains("NENDO_"), which NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR satisfies, so nothing guards it. mcp-interface.md:359 calls these 'refused by the Engine' without naming a code, and :623 reserves NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR for unexpected failures. The extra claim holds too: deletion-state-conflict (Deletion.cs:106) and field-not-retired (FieldRequirements.cs:55) are missing from DiagnosablePreconditions (NendoToolErrors.cs:98-122), so they arrive as 'The semantic precondition was not met.'. Reachable by an agent that undoes the same revision twice or undoes a definition revision. The agent cannot tell a refusal from a host fault, and the person's failure log gains an entry. No data loss, so P2.
- **Correction:** None of substance. The 'reproduction' probe was not re-run. The code path above is enough to establish it.

### UIS-04 — Escape inside the Filter menu, the View picker or a form field also triggers the page's first Close, shutting the record and discarding unsaved typing

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data` · also reported as WCS-05

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:540`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:38`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-use.ts:200`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:178`
- **What:** The document Escape listener (main.ts:540-553) clicks content.querySelector('[data-dismiss]:not(:disabled)') unless defaultPrevented. It ignores where focus is. The Filter menu's and View picker's own Escape handlers (quick-filter.ts:38, view-use.ts:200) close their menu but neither calls preventDefault or stopPropagation. The reference picker does call both (reference-controls.ts:71), which shows the intended pattern. The dismiss is #close-inspector, which calls closeInspector (record-form.ts:178-183) without refuseWhileDirty.
- **Failure:** With a record open, a person opens Filter and presses Escape to back out. The record inspector closes and the Filter menu stays open. The redraw reopens it because openSurfaceId is still set. Escape in the View picker closes both. With unsaved typing in the inspector, the typing is thrown away with no message, whereas every other exit is refused with 'Save your changes or close record details…'. Escape pressed in a text field, for example to dismiss autofill, does the same.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p23-hold.mjs -> 'after Escape in the Filter menu: filter open = true , inspector open = false'; 'after Escape in the View picker: picker open = false , inspector open = false'. p24-dirty.mjs -> typed 'Thomas and Ada' then Escape -> {inspector:false, owner:null, message:null}.
- **Fix and guard:** Call event.preventDefault() and event.stopPropagation() in both menu Escape handlers. In main.ts, skip the dismiss when the event target is inside an open details element or the header, and route a dismiss over a dirty draft through refuseWhileDirty or a discard confirmation. Guard: a gate step that opens a record, opens Filter, presses Escape, and asserts .record-inspector still exists and the menu is closed.
- **Verifier:** Traced. The document Escape listener (main.ts:540-553) returns only for defaultPrevented, an open dialog or the File menu, then clicks the first content [data-dismiss]:not(:disabled), which with a record open is #close-inspector (page-markup.ts:224). The Filter menu's handler (quick-filter.ts:37-39) and the View picker's (view-use.ts:199-201) set open=false and refocus the summary but call neither preventDefault nor stopPropagation, so the same keydown bubbles on to the document and closes the inspector (closeInspector, record-form.ts:178-183, plain leaveRecordContext + rerender). The code base's own pattern for a menu that must stand alone is preventDefault + stopPropagation (reference-controls.ts:72, view-menu.ts:111-114), so this is an omission, not a design choice. The 'Filter stays open' half also follows: menu.open=false only queues a toggle event, so the synchronous rerender still sees openSurfaceId set (quick-filter.ts:15,27,34) and draws the menu open. The data-loss reach is limited: needs a dirty draft, an open Filter or View picker and Escape. P2.
- **Correction:** Partly overstated: closing a dirty record through the Close button or Cancel also discards the draft with no refusal, and main.ts:522-525 says Escape deliberately does 'exactly what that visible Back/Cancel button does'; draft-guard.ts:32 even tells the person to 'close record details' to drop the draft. So Escape in a plain form field closing the record is documented behaviour, not a defect. The real defect is Escape inside the Filter menu and View picker also running the page-level dismiss. The guard and fix for that part stand.

### UIS-09 — placeKey leaves out fileView, so moving between a record type's screen and the file's own views (or between two views) overwrites the current trail entry

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data` · also reported as WCS-09

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-trail.ts:89`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-actions.ts:44`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/rail-places.ts:63`
- **What:** Place carries fileView (navigation-trail.ts:43), but placeKey (89-109) compares view, applicationEntityId, studioEntityId, showOverview, surfaceId and the rest, never fileView. placeOfNendo records applicationEntityId and surfaceId from activePlan() (navigation-actions.ts:44-46), which falls back to the selected or first type even while a file view is shown (plan-selection.ts:58-60). openPlace sets showOverview=false for both views and types (rail-places.ts:63-72). A type board and a file view therefore have equal keys, and record() replaces the current entry instead of pushing a new one.
- **Failure:** In a file with views such as Garden and Codemap, a person goes from the Work board to Garden to Codemap through the navigation. Back goes to whatever came before the Work board, or is disabled, because each move overwrote the last. The trail cannot step between two of the file's views or back from a view to the board it was opened from.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p10-trail.mjs (navigation-trail.ts bundled with vite, three places differing only in fileView) -> 'placeKey equal for two file views: true'; 'trail after Work board -> Garden view -> Codemap view: {"length":1,"cursor":0,"titles":["Codemap(view.codemap)"]}'; 'canGoBack: false'.
- **Fix and guard:** Add place.fileView to the placeKey array. Guard: a node-lane test in the navigation-trail suite that records a type place and then a file-view place and asserts canGoBack() is true. Falsify it by removing fileView from the key.
- **Verifier:** Place declares fileView (navigation-trail.ts:43) and placeOfNendo fills it (navigation-actions.ts:54), but placeKey (navigation-trail.ts:89-109) omits it, and record() overwrites the current entry whenever keys match (navigation-trail.ts:~187-192). activePlan() falls back to the selected or first type (plan-selection.ts:~58-60), so on a file view applicationEntityId and surfaceId equal the type board's. Both rail-places.ts:openPlace and showFileView set showOverview=false and call leaveRecordContext. recordPlace is called once per draw (main.ts:127). The only other discriminator is viewPlaces, which keeps entries only for views that call ui.setPlace; in the shipped packages that is Archi and Garden only when a note or diagram is open (extensions/garden/workspace.js:412), while bcm-atlas, gantt, swarm, systems-lens and the others never call it. The test helper place() in scripts/navigation-trail.test.mjs has no fileView, so nothing guards the key. Board to view to view therefore collapses into one entry and Back skips the board.
- **Correction:** Reachability is narrower than the finding says: it needs a file view that has not declared a ui.setPlace place (Garden before a note is open, any package without setPlace). A view that has declared a place yields a different key through viewPlaces, which is why G39 in docs/contracts/custom-views.md passes.

### UX-02 — Data grid shows a refused edit as if it were saved (confirmed rejection keeps the rejected value in the cell)

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` (reported P1) · also reported as WDV-07

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:614`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:794`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:85`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/write-failure.ts:37`
- **What:** The column valueSetter writes the new value into the row data before anything is sent (view-data.ts:614-618). commitGridEdit sends data.setField through runMutation; on a confirmed rejection (validation, record-version-conflict, calculation-refused and the rest of pending-mutations.ts:19-32) decideWriteFailure answers 'retain-draft', so runMutation neither re-reads nor re-renders (actions.ts:85-88). That rule exists for a record form whose draft lives in the DOM; in the grid it leaves the refused value drawn in the cell, with the old version number, and the error is cleared by the next key press (shell.ts:545). Studio contract §11: 'Invalid or conflicting edits are never presented as committed'; §5 asks for explicit validation-failed and conflicted states.
- **Failure:** An agent edits a row while the person has Data open, or an automatic action refuses the save. The person edits a cell in that row and presses Enter: the message slot says the save was refused, but the cell keeps the typed value. After the next key press the message is gone and the grid still shows the refused value; every later edit on that row is refused again because the row's recordVersion was never refreshed.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=tree, Data > Table, edited Order of row 0 from 2048 to 77 and pressed Enter (the preview host refuses it) -> 'msg: Order must be a number.' and 'cell after: 77 \| version 1' (screenshot 20-grid-rejected.png). The refusal reason is preview-only; the retain-draft path it exercises is the real one.
- **Fix and guard:** In commitGridEdit, on any failure restore the row: call event.node.setDataValue(colId, event.oldValue) (or rebuild the grid from recordWindows) and mark the cell as refused (cellClass plus an aria description) until the next successful read. Guard: a grids/host-behaviour test that makes the preview host refuse a setField and asserts the cell text equals the stored value afterwards.
- **Verifier:** The core path holds. The column valueSetter writes the typed value into the grid row copy (view-data.ts:614-618, the copy made at view-data.ts:553). commitGridEdit then sends data.setField through runMutation (view-data.ts:797-804). On a confirmed rejection, decideWriteFailure answers retain-draft (write-failure.ts:37-39, pending-mutations.ts:19-32), so runMutation only calls showError and neither re-reads nor rerenders (actions.ts:80-89). The cell keeps the refused value. A real host reaches this path too: an automatic action that fails while computing its write, or a Refuse() outcome, aborts the edit, and the Workbench gets a calculation-* code (calculations-and-actions.md:366-378, 871), which is in the confirmed set. commitGridEdit does restore the grid for its own refusals (blank required, parse failure: recoverAfterWriteFailure at view-data.ts:788-794) but not for the host's. So studio.md:77 (explicit validation-failed state) and the studio.md:286 criterion are not met. The impact is overstated, so I lowered it to P2. The alert stays in the DOM until the next redraw: the keydown listener only nulls state.lastOutcome (shell.ts:545-551). That same redraw rebuilds the grid from the stored windows. No data is lost.
- **Correction:** Two parts of the failure scenario are wrong. (1) 'Every later edit on that row is refused again because recordVersion was never refreshed' is false. For refusals that leave the file unchanged (validation, calculation-*, link-not-allowed), the row's version is still the current one. For a version conflict caused by another writer, onFileChanged plus the followTheFile chase (main.ts:708-724, 747-753) re-reads and rerenders once holdingThePage lifts. (2) 'After the next key press the message is gone' is also false. A key press clears only state.lastOutcome; the slot text stays visible until the next redraw, and that redraw also brings back the stored cell value. What is left of the defect: the cell has no refused state, and it shows the refused value next to an alert at the top of the pane until something redraws. The suggested fix event.node.setDataValue(colId, oldValue) would fire onCellValueChanged again (view-data.ts:689). commitGridEdit does not filter by event.source, so the fix would send a second setField. Rebuild the grid instead (recoverAfterWriteFailure or rerender, as the client-side refusal branches already do), or ignore non-'edit' sources. The reviewer's reproduction relies on a preview-only refusal (host-preview.ts:1186-1187, a type mismatch the real host would not raise), but the retain-draft path it exercises is the real one.

### WAU-01 — Closing the conversation's tab leaves the agent running once Back, or the trail's 50-place bound, has dropped the conversation from that tab (ACP-06 fix incomplete)

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-trail.ts:200`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-trail.ts:202`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:104`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/workspace-tabs.ts:94`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/tab-set.ts:76`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:141`
- **What:** onTabClosed (view-agent-chat.ts:103-116) ends the agent only when the closed tab's trail still contains an agentChat place and tabsHolding('agentChat') is 0. Ownership is inferred from what the trail holds (trailHolds, tab-set.ts:76). The trail does not keep that record. Trail.record drops every place ahead of the cursor when the person goes somewhere new from part-way back (navigation-trail.ts:200), and it drops the oldest places beyond trailCeiling = 50 (navigation-trail.ts:202). The conversation tab [Agent, conversation] then Back then Data becomes [Agent, Data]. No tab holds the conversation, so closing that tab, Ctrl+W or a middle click ends nothing. The fix's guards cover only the forward journey, conversation then Data (Gate-AgentChat.mjs:165-172, navigation-trail.test.mjs:324). The Launch tab then tells the person to 'Close {name}'s tab to launch another' (view-agent.ts:141), about a tab that no longer exists.
- **Failure:** Launch Copilot at Shape app or Unattended. In its tab, press Back (Alt+Left) to the Agent page, click Data, then close the tab. The agent program keeps running unconfined with its own tools and keeps its MCP access, although Help says 'Closing the tab ends the agent.' The same happens after 50 more moves in the conversation's tab.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node trail-probe.mjs (bundles navigation-trail.ts and tab-set.ts in memory) -> {"journey":"conversation -> Data (the gate covers this)","holds":true} {"journey":"conversation -> Back to Agent -> Data","places":["agent","data"],"holds":false} {"journey":"conversation -> 50 more places","holds":false}
- **Fix and guard:** Give the conversation an explicit owner instead of inferring one from the trail. Keep the id of the tab that opened (or last showed) the conversation in view-agent-chat.ts, and end the agent when that tab closes. Alternatively, make Trail.record and the ceiling never drop an agentChat place. Guard: extend navigation-trail.test.mjs with record(agent), record(chat), stepBack(), record(data) and with the 50-place case. Add the Back, Data, close journey to Gate-AgentChat.mjs, asserting that 'ended with its tab' is said and agentSession.list.running is null. Falsify by restoring the trail-content check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. onTabClosed (view-agent-chat.ts:103-104) ends the agent only if the closed tab's trail still contains an agentChat place. openTabOn creates the tab as [Agent, agentChat] (workspace-tabs.ts:160-166, newTab copies the Agent place, then rerender records the chat). Trail.record (navigation-trail.ts:200) does places.slice(0, cursor + 1) before pushing, so Back to Agent and then Data leaves [Agent, Data]. The conversation is gone from every trail, tabsHolding('agentChat') is 0 and the closed trail has no agentChat place, so nothing calls agentSession.end. The ceiling slice at :202 does the same after 50 further places. The ACP-06 fix only covers the forward journey conversation -> Data. docs/contracts/launched-agents.md:229-231 and ADR-0030 'Lifetime' say closing the tab ends the agent and that a tab that went on to another page still holds the conversation; the trail does not keep that promise. view-agent.ts:141 then tells the person to 'Close X's tab' about a tab that no longer exists. A workaround exists (Open conversation on the Agent page opens a new tab, closing it ends the agent; so does Off), which keeps this at P2.

### WDV-03 — Drilling into a trend or activity-grid bucket sends gte/lte, which the record query refuses

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:191`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/panels.ts:365`, `src/Nendo.Engine/RecordQuerySemantics.cs:28`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/over-time.test.mjs:46`
- **What:** bucketDrillFilters returns {operator:'gte'} and {operator:'lte'}. drillInto stores them as the drill, and loadSurfaceWindow sends them to data.queryRecords unchanged. RecordQuerySemantics.Validate accepts only eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge, contains, isNull, isNotNull and descendantOf, and throws 'The record filter is invalid.' record-window.ts:38 (queryOperatorFor) exists precisely because the record query spells these le/ge. over-time.test.mjs asserts the wrong spelling, so the suite locks the defect in.
- **Failure:** On a list with a 'Created by month' trend, the person clicks the February column (or a day square of an activity grid): the drill pill appears and the list shows the read error 'The record filter is invalid.' instead of February's records. Every bucket drill fails.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs (vite SSR bundle of charts.ts) -> "Trend bucket drill filters: [{"fieldId":"due","operator":"gte","value":"2026-02-01"},{"fieldId":"due","operator":"lte","value":"2026-02-28"}]" and "operators the Engine record query accepts: gte=false lte=false" (accepted set copied from RecordQuerySemantics.cs:28).
- **Fix and guard:** Emit 'ge' and 'le' (or pass both through queryOperatorFor) and correct over-time.test.mjs. Guard: a host-level test, like WorkbenchQuickFilterTests, that sends bucketDrillFilters' output to data.queryRecords and expects the bucket's records; falsify by restoring gte.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. charts.ts:191-192 emits operators 'gte'/'lte'; panels.ts:362-368 stores them verbatim as the drill; plan-selection.ts:374-378 effectiveSurfaceQuery returns drill.filters unchanged; reads.ts:57-61 loadSurfaceWindow sends them to data.queryRecords via record-window.ts windowRequest (no queryOperatorFor). Desktop passes the payload straight to NendoWriteCoordinator.QueryRecordsAsync (ReadQueries.cs:321), whose RecordQuerySemantics.Validate (RecordQuerySemantics.cs:27-29) accepts only eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/contains/isNull/isNotNull/descendantOf and throws 'The record filter is invalid.' No operator aliasing exists on the Desktop path (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:413 deserializes directly). queryOperatorFor (record-window.ts:38) exists precisely because the contract spells these gte/lte, and bucketDrillFilters bypasses it. over-time.test.mjs:46-49 asserts the wrong spelling. The gate step that clicks a trend column (tools/Gate-AgentAuthoring.mjs:2792-2796) only asserts the drill pill text, not that records came back, so it cannot catch this. The list shows the read error for every trend/activity-grid bucket drill.
- **Correction:** Also note why nothing noticed: Gate-AgentAuthoring.mjs:2797-2798 explicitly says it does not assert a record count. Priority stays P2 (a whole drill feature fails, error is visible, user can filter manually).
