### WDV-04 — Matrix cell drill on a Boolean axis sends 'true'/'false' strings, which the host refuses; axis clauses on Booleans are ignored

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:257`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-use.ts:314`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:712`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-model.ts:218`
- **What:** A matrix may cross a Boolean field: axisOptions gives it lanes ['false','true'], and laneOf and groupLabel handle it. wireMatrix reads the lane from data-matrix-row as a string, and cellDrillFilters emits {operator:'eq', value:'true'}. The host's ValidateRecordQuery runs ConvertValue, whose Boolean branch calls value.GetBoolean() on a JSON string and rethrows 'Value for field X does not match storage kind Boolean.' drillFilter for breakdown charts converts the key to a boolean; the matrix path does not. reachableGroups also skips any clause whose value is not a string, so a matrix declaring 'urgent eq true' still draws an always-empty 'No' lane.
- **Failure:** A matrix of Tasks by Urgent (Boolean) x Status: clicking the '4 with Yes and Open' cell opens the list with the read error instead of the four tasks.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs -> "Matrix cell drill on a Boolean axis (row \"true\"): [{\"fieldId\":\"urgent\",\"operator\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"true\"},...]" against "breakdown drill on the same Boolean group: {\"fieldId\":\"urgent\",\"operator\":\"eq\",\"value\":true}". Host refusal: source (Operations.cs:712, 739-742).
- **Fix and guard:** Pass the axis fields to cellDrillFilters and convert lanes of a Boolean field to true/false, as drillFilter does. In reachableGroups, compare String(value) for boolean clause values. Guard: a unit test for cellDrillFilters with a Boolean axis, plus a host test that runs the produced filters; falsify by reverting the conversion.
- **Verifier:** Boolean matrix axes are supported by design (NendoSemanticCompiler.Summaries.cs:261, SemanticVocabulary.cs:477, site docs screens.md:92). surface-model.ts:260-265 axisOptions gives ['false','true']; surface-markup.ts:485 writes the lane string into data-matrix-row; view-use.ts:314-317 reads it back as a string and drillIntoCell -> cellDrillFilters (charts.ts:257-258) emits {operator:'eq', value:'true'} with no field type conversion (the breakdown path, charts.ts:505, converts with isBooleanField). The host's ValidateRecordQuery (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:518-520) runs ConvertValue, whose Boolean branch (Operations.cs:712) calls value.GetBoolean() on a JSON string; InvalidOperationException is rethrown at Operations.cs:739-742 as 'does not match storage kind Boolean'. Desktop's WorkbenchScalarJsonConverter does not coerce strings. So the drill from any cell on a Boolean axis shows the read error. Secondary claim also holds: the compiler requires a Boolean filter literal to be a JSON boolean (ComposableSurfaces.cs:742), so reachableGroups (surface-model.ts:218) skips it and an always-empty lane stays. grids.test.mjs:35-37 tests only the lanes, not the drill.
- **Correction:** Reach is limited to matrices with a Boolean axis, so P2 is borderline P3; kept at P2 because it is a documented configuration whose drill is entirely broken.

### WDV-09 — Studio's outline offers Move up/down and outdent moves the Engine refuses for a hierarchy without an order field

**P2** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:212`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:234`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:47`
- **What:** moveInOutline and syncMoveButtons call moveTarget(outline, focus, direction) without its 'ordered' argument, so it defaults to true and produces a beforeRecordId for up, down and outdent. The Use outline passes config.ordered (outline-surface.ts:161). Studio opens any record type with entity.hierarchy as an outline, including one whose orderFieldId is null. The Engine refuses a move with beforeRecordId on such a hierarchy as hierarchy-order-not-declared.
- **Failure:** A record type with a declared parent but no order field: in Studio the Move up and Move down buttons are enabled for any record with a sibling, and Alt+Shift+Up is accepted, but every attempt fails with the host refusal. Outdenting a record whose parent has a following sibling fails the same way.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs (outline-model.ts) -> "moveTarget(b, \"up\") -> {\"parentRecordId\":null,\"beforeRecordId\":\"a\"}" and "moveTarget(b, \"up\", ordered=false) -> null". Engine refusal: source.
- **Fix and guard:** Pass ordered = entity.hierarchy?.orderFieldId != null to moveTarget in moveInOutline and syncMoveButtons. Guard: a studio-outline test with an unordered hierarchy asserting the up/down buttons are disabled and outdent sends beforeRecordId null; falsify by dropping the argument.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. view-data.ts:212 and :234 call moveTarget(outline, focus, direction) without the 'ordered' argument, so outline-model.ts:87 defaults ordered=true and returns a beforeRecordId for up, down and outdent-with-following-parent-sibling. layoutOf (view-data.ts:177-179) opens any entity with a hierarchy as an outline, and outlineToolbarMarkup (view-data.ts:238-244) always draws all four buttons. ADR-0019 / relationships.md:35 make orderFieldId optional (HierarchyOperations.cs:37 maps blank to null), and NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:47-49 throws hierarchy-order-not-declared when BeforeRecordId is set with no order field. The Use outline already does this right (outline-surface.ts:161, outline-surface-markup.ts:98-101) and semantic-surfaces.md:537-538 says only Outdent, Indent and drop are offered without an order field, so Studio diverges from the contract. No data loss, the refusal is explicit, and only unordered hierarchies are affected, hence P2 not higher.

### ABS-07 — One malformed Bendpoints or Legend text breaks the whole Archi workbench (canvas, Analysis, editor, validator, exports)

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `tools/archi/canvas/mirror.ts:136`, `tools/archi/canvas/mirror.ts:152`, `extensions/archi/view.js:408`, `extensions/archi/view.js:452`
- **What:** buildMirror runs JSON.parse on ar.item.bendpoints and ar.item.legend with no guard. Both are ordinary long-text fields, shown on the Diagram item screen (tools/archi-definition.mjs:502), so a person can edit them on the record page and an agent can write them over MCP. buildMirror backs renderDiagram, analysedMirror (Analysis in the properties pane of every concept), the editor, the validator, Visualiser, image export and Save as .archimate or Exchange. Measured with canvas.js: one connection's bendpoints set to '[{"x": 1' gives 'buildMirror threw: SyntaxError Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 8' and 'exportArchimate threw: ...'. The message names no record.
- **Failure:** Someone edits the Bendpoints of one connection on its record page and leaves invalid JSON. From then on, opening any view or selecting any concept throws inside render(): the properties pane keeps the previous record's fields and the diagram never draws. Save as .archimate fails too. The person gets a JSON parse error with no record ID and no way to the faulty record from the workbench.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-mirror.mjs (canvas.buildMirror on archisurance.json with one bendpoints text broken) -> 'mirror ok: views 17 connections 199' then 'buildMirror threw: SyntaxError Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 8 (line 1 column 9)' and 'exportArchimate threw: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 8 (line 1 column 9)'
- **Fix and guard:** Parse with a guard in mirror.ts. A bad bendpoints value gives [] and a bad legend gives no legendOptions. Record the item ID in a list that the validator (integrity pass) and the status line report ('Connection <id> has unreadable bendpoints'). Guard: a mirror test that feeds a malformed bendpoints and legend and expects buildMirror to succeed and report both IDs.
- **Verifier:** tools/archi/canvas/mirror.ts:136 and :152 call JSON.parse on ar.item.bendpoints and ar.item.legend with no try/catch. Bendpoints is a long-text field bound on the authored record page (tools/archi-definition.mjs:243, :502), so it is editable in Studio and over MCP, and nothing validates it. buildMirror then runs for the whole file: extensions/archi/view.js:408 (any view opened), :452 via renderAnalysis at :582 (selecting any concept), :1103/:1209/:1555/:1570 (editor, validator, exports). render() at :1670-1680 has no guard, so the SyntaxError escapes readAll and only surfaces as 'The model could not be read. <JSON message>' with no record named. Studio remains the way to repair it, so this is a robustness gap, not data loss.
- **Correction:** Only Bendpoints is on the authored record page; Legend options (tools/archi-definition.mjs:249) is a long-text field but is not bound there, so it is reachable only through Studio's generic editing or an agent. Bendpoints is the realistic trigger.

<a id="dae-04"></a>

### DAE-04 — A JSON-RPC error with a non-integer code faults the read loop, and the faulted loop then makes disposal throw, so closing the file leaves the MCP listener running

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AcpConnection.cs:216`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AcpConnection.cs:281`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:248`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:164`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:428`
- **What:** Dispatch reads an error's code with c.TryGetInt32 without checking its kind (line 216). The throw escapes Dispatch and ReadLoopAsync, whose catches cover only OperationCanceledException, IOException and ObjectDisposedException, so the finally closes the connection with the default reason "The agent closed its output." and the _reader task is left faulted. AcpConnection.DisposeAsync awaits _reader.WaitAsync(5 s) catching only TimeoutException (line 281), so it rethrows. EndLaunchedAgentCoreAsync calls agent.DisposeAsync() outside its try (line 248), and CloseAgentFileSessionCoreAsync runs it before StopAgentAccessCoreAsync and the proposal cleanup (DesktopAgentAccess.cs:428-431); LaunchAgentAsync disposes the previous conversation the same way after setting _launched to null (line 164).
- **Failure:** An agent answers one of Nendo's requests with {"error":{"code":"internal","message":"boom"}} (or code null). The conversation ends saying the agent closed its output, which it did not. When the person then closes or switches the file, CloseAsync throws InvalidOperationException: the MCP host for the closed file is never disposed and keeps its port and discovery entry, the next open of that file falls back to another port while configured clients reach the dead listener, and agent proposals are not closed. New session on that conversation fails the same way and the old transcript is gone.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: malformed-probe.ps1 steps 3 and 4 -> "3. an error answer with code \"internal\": connection closed=True; reason=The agent closed its output.; state=ready; working=True" and "4. DisposeAsync after the text code: threw InvalidOperationException: The requested operation requires an element of type 'Number', but the target element has type 'String'." The controller chain from DisposeAsync to the skipped StopAgentAccessCoreAsync is from source.
- **Fix and guard:** Read the code only when it is a Number (else -32603), wrap Dispatch so no exception ends the loop, make AcpConnection.DisposeAsync swallow a faulted reader, and dispose in EndLaunchedAgentCoreAsync and LaunchAgentAsync inside a catch so StopAgentAccessCoreAsync always runs. Guard: a fake agent that answers with a text code, then CloseAsync must complete and the controller's agent host must be disposed (its port free); falsify by removing the kind check and the catch.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. AcpConnection.cs:216 does c.TryGetInt32 on an error's code without a kind check, which throws for a String/null; Dispatch (line ~190) has no catch around that branch and ReadLoopAsync (line ~125-150) catches only OperationCanceled, IOException and ObjectDisposedException, so the finally closes with the default reason and the _reader task faults. DisposeAsync (line 281) awaits _reader.WaitAsync(5 s) catching only TimeoutException, so it rethrows the stored InvalidOperationException. DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:248 awaits agent.DisposeAsync() (DesktopLaunchedAgent.DisposeAsync -> _conversation.DisposeAsync -> _connection.DisposeAsync) outside its try, and DesktopAgentAccess.cs:428-431 runs it first in CloseAgentFileSessionCoreAsync, so StopAgentAccessCoreAsync (host.DisposeAsync, lease/authority invalidation) and _agentProposals.CloseFileSessionAsync are skipped; DesktopSessionController.cs:490-498 only resets state in its finally and lets the exception out. RestoreAgentModeAsync (DesktopAgentAccess.cs:148) also returns early while _agentHost is non-null. The trigger is an agent that answers with a non-integer error code, which is uncommon, but the skipped close-time cleanup (ADR-0009: file close invalidates old authority) is more than cosmetic.
- **Correction:** None to the locations or chain. Trigger likelihood is low (a protocol-violating agent, for example one that forwards a Node error code string), which keeps this at P2 rather than higher; any other exception escaping Dispatch would produce the same faulted reader.

<a id="esq-03"></a>

### ESQ-03 — Undoing a record revision that carries a keep mark commits the undo, then throws InvalidOperationException

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-service-queries`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:203`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:214`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:220`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:361`
- **What:** UndoRecordWritesAsync first calls _coordinator.CompensateRevisionAsync, which applies and commits the compensation. Only then does it walk mutation.Operations, with a switch that knows SetField, BackfillRetiredField, RestoreDeletedRecord and DeleteRecord. Any other type hits throw new InvalidOperationException($"A view's undo planned {operation.OperationType}."). The planner for record compensations emits a SetRecordKeptInNewFilesOperation for every data.setKeptInNewFiles in the revision (Compensation.cs:361-366). IsRecordChange admits such revisions, and History's eligibility SQL offers undo for them. CreateRecord(s)Async and ApplyRecordWritesAsync put keep marks in the same revision as the create (ADR-0022). Both callers reach this path: NendoDataMutationService.UndoRevisionAsync (nendo.data.undo_revision) and the Desktop view undo.
- **Failure:** An agent builds a skeleton with nendo.data.apply_writes keptInNewFiles:true, or with nendo.data.set_kept_in_new_files, then calls nendo.data.undo_revision. 1. The records are deleted and the revision commits. 2. The tool answers with an internal error: 'A view's undo planned data.setKeptInNewFiles.' 3. An exact retry replays the receipt and throws again. 4. A retry with a new key is refused with 'This revision already has a compensation revision.' The agent cannot learn that its undo succeeded. A redo of such an undo fails the same way.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Handle SetRecordKeptInNewFilesOperation in the switch. It moves no version, so add the record once with its planned version, or with null if it has none. Also validate the planned operation types before CompensateRevisionAsync applies anything, or make the default branch a no-op, so a planning gap can never surface after commit. Guards in RecordWritesUndoTests, each returning its records without throwing: - a create with KeptInNewFiles, then UndoRecordWritesAsync, then Redo; - SetRecordsKeptInNewFilesAsync, then undo.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ApplyRecordWritesAsync adds a SetRecordKeptInNewFilesOperation beside the create (NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:155-156), and the host skill tells agents to do this (NendoHostSkill.cs:155). SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:24 admits data.setKeptInNewFiles as a record change, and CreateCausalInverses emits a SetRecordKeptInNewFilesOperation for it (lines 361-367). UndoRecordWritesAsync calls _coordinator.CompensateRevisionAsync (Batch.cs:203), which applies and commits the compensation (NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:345-364). Only afterwards does the switch at Batch.cs:214-221 see that operation; it has no case for it and the default throws InvalidOperationException. An exact retry rebuilds the same mutation (exactReplay) and throws again, and a retry under a new key is refused by Compensation.cs:136-140. The switch also runs before the IsIdempotentReplay return, so the replay throws too. Both callers reach it: nendo.data.undo_revision (NendoDataMutationService.cs:422) and the Desktop view undo. No test covers it: RecordWritesUndoTests and UndoRevisionToolTests have no keep-mark case. The data is consistent, because the undo is committed, but the caller gets an internal error for an undo that succeeded.
- **Correction:** None to the locations. Impact is an error response after a successful commit, with no data loss, so P2 stands. The fix should add a SetRecordKeptInNewFilesOperation case that moves no version, and avoid throwing after commit.

<a id="mtd-02"></a>

### MTD-02 — A JSON import that names targets in references cannot be retried: committed batches are rebuilt with the targets' current versions and refused as NENDO_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:612`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:217`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:264`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:274`
- **What:** ImportAsync passes record => ToEntryAsync(entityId, record, ct) to ImportRecordsAsync. ToEntryAsync resolves every references entry to the target's version now (ResolveReferencesAsync sets targets[fieldId] = found.RecordVersion). Unlike create_record, create_records, update_record and apply_writes, which pass the result through CommittedTargetVersionsAsync and Recorded (F-258), and unlike the CSV path, which reads committedVersions per batch from the receipts (R-006), the JSON import path never substitutes the versions its committed batches recorded. CommitAsync then resubmits batch 0 under its original key with a different expectedTargetVersions payload, and the Engine refuses a used key with a different payload.
- **Failure:** An agent imports 120 JSON records whose references name project p1 by record ID. Batch 1 commits; batch 2 fails (or the response is lost). Between the attempts p1 is edited by the person, or by the action in the finding above. The agent follows the description and retries the identical call with the same idempotencyKey: batch 0 is rebuilt with p1's new version, the Engine sees a different payload, and the call answers NENDO_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT with committed=0 reported nowhere. The key is now unusable; a new key derives new record IDs and duplicates the 50 committed records.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Before CommitAsync, read each batch's receipt (as ReadCommittedTargetVersionsAsync does for CSV) and replace the versions of fields named in references with the ones the committed revision recorded, using the existing Recorded helper per record. Guard: a JSON import test that commits batch 1, fails batch 2 through the BeforeBatch hook, edits the referenced target, retries the identical call and asserts it completes with batch 1 replayed; falsify by removing the substitution and quoting the NENDO_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT text.
- **Verifier:** Traced. NendoDataMutationService.cs:609-612 passes record => ToEntryAsync(...) to ImportRecordsAsync (NendoImportService.cs:217-222), and ToEntryAsync (:131-138) resolves each references entry to the target's current version (ResolveReferencesAsync :215-216). Unlike CreateRecordAsync (:81-88), CreateRecordsAsync (:108-114), UpdateRecordAsync (:322-326) and apply_writes, the JSON import never runs CommittedTargetVersionsAsync/Recorded, and ImportRecordsAsync has no receipt reading, whereas the CSV path does (NendoImportService.cs:147-148, :169-177). CreateRecordOperation.WritePayload writes expectedTargetVersions into the canonical payload (Operations.cs:460-466), and TryResolveReplayAsync throws NendoIdempotencyConflictException when the payload digest differs (SqliteNendoStore.cs:825-829). CommitAsync only wraps failures in NendoImportPartialException when committed > 0 (:273), so a batch-0 conflict surfaces as a bare NENDO_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Tests cover the retry after a target move for CSV (ImportExportProtocolTests.cs:184, :223) and for create/update/apply_writes (BatchWriteToolTests.cs:238), but not for a JSON import. The F-258 comment says 'as the import's does', which holds only for CSV. Reachable after a lost response or partial failure plus an edit to the target, including the edit finding 1's action makes. A workaround exists (get_receipt by the same key, then import the rest under a new key), so P2.
- **Correction:** The new-key consequence is misstated. A JSON import carries caller-supplied recordIds (ToEntryAsync :134-137), not seed-derived IDs, so a new key would be refused as an existing record rather than duplicate the 50 committed records. Only CSV derives IDs from the key.

<a id="tbi-02"></a>

### TBI-02 — A missing owned file is reported as 'Payload differs' and blocks repair, upgrade and uninstall, leaving no recovery path

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:105`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:594`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:616`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:153`
- **What:** Assert-Bytes throws the same 'Payload differs; retained for recovery' for an owned path that is absent ('-not (Test-Path ...)') as for one whose bytes changed. It runs on the installed tree before every Install (616), including the identical-payload repair path, and before every Uninstall (594, and again inside Remove-Owned at 153). A missing file carries no external edit to protect, yet it vetoes every operation.
- **Failure:** Defender quarantines one DLL of the unsigned payload, or a person deletes a file. Rerunning the same Nendo-Setup.exe, the obvious repair, fails. A newer installer fails. Uninstall from Apps & features fails. Each failure shows the NSIS 'Close Nendo and check the setup details' box.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: setup-missing-file-probe.ps1 case A (installed lib\core.dll deleted from a synthetic install root; Windows PowerShell 5.1) -> setup.log: 'Setup failed: Payload differs; retained for recovery: ...\A\Nendo\lib\core.dll' three times, for Install of the same payload, Install of the next payload, and Uninstall.
- **Fix and guard:** Split absent from changed in Assert-Bytes. An absent owned file is restored by Install (repair) and skipped by Uninstall. Refuse only when bytes exist and differ. Guard: a Test-NendoSetup.ps1 case that deletes one owned file, reruns the same payload (expect exit 0 and the file back with its manifest hash), deletes it again and runs Uninstall (expect exit 0).
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. Assert-Bytes (Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:102-107) throws the identical 'Payload differs; retained for recovery' when the file is absent (Test-Path -PathType Leaf false) as when its hash differs. It runs on the installed tree at 616 for every Install, including the identical-payload path (617-631 is only reached after it), and at 594 and again inside Remove-Owned:153 for Uninstall. With one owned file missing, a rerun of the same installer, a newer installer and Uninstall each throw before changing anything. Recover mode (Restore-Pending) needs a journal and does nothing here. Deleting nendo-install.json does not help either, because the existing files then hit 'Unowned file collision' at 637. The only way out is deleting Programs\Nendo and the HKCU Uninstall key by hand. No ADR or contract mandates refusing on absence (grep of docs/ finds none); the guard is there to avoid overwriting an external edit, and a missing file carries none. The trigger (a file removed by antivirus or cleanup) is an ordinary external event, and the reviewer's synthetic probe reproduced it.
- **Correction:** Low likelihood: no 'Payload differs' failure appears in the owner's %TEMP%\Nendo-Setup.log. Keep P2 only because the blast radius is every operation with a manual-cleanup workaround; P3 is defensible. NSIS shows 'Close Nendo' for it, which misleads.

### TST-01 — The default gate's extension-view journey reads and overwrites the real Windows clipboard, and fails about one run in three when the clipboard is busy or the session is locked

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `dotnet-tests-quality` · also reported as BL-02

- **Where:** `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:311`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:377`, `tools/Review-ExtensionViews.mjs:182`, `tools/Review-ExtensionViews.mjs:201`, `tools/Review-ExtensionViews.mjs:843`, `tools/Test-Production.ps1:88`
- **What:** ViewsRunInlineIsolatedFromTheWorkbenchAndStopWhenSwitchedOff carries [TestCategory("ExtensionRuntime")] but nothing filters that category: Test-Production.ps1 runs `dotnet test Nendo.slnx` with no filter or runsettings. RunJourneyAsync starts Review-ExtensionViews.mjs, and its G36 step makes a view write PNGs to the system clipboard. It then reads them back through readWindowsClipboard(), a one-shot `[Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetDataObject()` in powershell.exe with no retry. The test asserts the script's exit code is 0. The TRX history under tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/TestResults has 45 runs since 2026-10-01. This test failed in 13 of them and passed in 28. Every failure is the clipboard: twelve end in `Windows clipboard probe failed: Exception calling "GetDataObject" ... "Requested Clipboard operation did not succeed." ... FullyQualifiedErrorId : ExternalException`, and one (2026-10-03) ends in `A picture drawn from SVG did not reach the Windows clipboard intact: null`. The latest gate run (2026-10-10 14:54) failed this way, and it was the only Desktop failure in that run.
- **Failure:** The owner runs Test-Production while another program holds the clipboard open (a clipboard manager, Office, a remote-desktop client) or while the workstation is locked. OpenClipboard fails, the probe throws, node exits 1, and the whole gate goes red although nothing in Nendo is wrong. Even on a run that passes, whatever the owner had copied is silently replaced by the probe's red-square PNG and a 730x1240 drawing.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python trxfail.py over tests/*/TestResults since 2026-10-01 (read-only TRX parse) -> "13 fail / 28 pass FLAKY ViewsRunInlineIsolatedFromTheWorkbenchAndStopWhenSwitchedOff". Per run, the last error line is "+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : ExternalException" for 12 runs and "Error: A picture drawn from SVG did not reach the Windows clipboard intact: null" for 2026-10-03_11_20_52.
- **Fix and guard:** Move G36 out of the default lane. The script could skip it unless NENDO_RUN_CLIPBOARD=1, with the C# test reporting Inconclusive for that part, as the Soak and Inspector lanes do. If it stays in the default lane, retry OpenClipboard and GetDataObject with backoff (for example 20 x 100 ms), save the owner's clipboard before G36 and restore it afterwards, and detect a locked session (LogonUI running) to report Inconclusive instead of failing. Guard: start a helper that holds OpenClipboard for 3 s during the G36 window and check that the journey still passes or reports Inconclusive, never Failed. Also check after the run that the clipboard holds the sentinel text written before it.
- **Verifier:** Traced and re-measured. tools/Test-Production.ps1:88 runs `dotnet test Nendo.slnx` with no filter or runsettings (no ExtensionRuntime filter anywhere in tools/*.ps1, csproj or props), so DesktopExtensionViewJourneyTests.cs:311 runs in every gate. Review-ExtensionViews.mjs:817-859 (G36) makes a view write PNGs to the system clipboard, then calls readWindowsClipboard() (line 182), a one-shot powershell.exe `[Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetDataObject()` with no retry. I re-parsed tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/TestResults/*.trx since 2026-10-01: 13 fail / 28 pass for this test. Twelve failures are the `Requested Clipboard operation did not succeed` GetDataObject error and one (2026-10-03) is `A picture drawn from SVG did not reach the Windows clipboard intact: null`. The 2026-10-10_14_54_46 run fails the same way. The owner's memory note (nendo-locked-workstation-clipboard-test) records the same failure under a locked session, so this is a known environment dependence with no code-side mitigation and no documented acceptance in docs/. tools/clipboard-probe.test.mjs covers only the error-reporting path, not retry or skip.
- **Correction:** The dominant cause is probably a locked workstation (LogonUI), which refuses every clipboard read, rather than another program holding the clipboard. Retry with backoff would therefore not help in that case; the effective fix is to detect the locked session and report Inconclusive, or to move G36 behind an opt-in switch. The overwritten user clipboard is inherent to the G36 measurement and is the lesser concern. Priority stays P2: roughly a third of gate runs fail falsely, and a rerun on an unlocked desktop is the workaround.

<a id="tst-02"></a>

### TST-02 — Concurrent test suites still lose MCP handshakes and child-process starts under the full gate (F-134 recurs); the Desktop suite also has half the timeout and no thread-pool sizing

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `dotnet-tests-quality`

- **Where:** `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/ProtocolResourceTests.cs:292`, `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/LatestProtocolTests.cs:94`, `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/TestHostThreads.cs:22`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopAgentSettingsTests.cs:249`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionWriterAgentRaceTests.cs:102`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopReplacementTests.cs:270`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/TestWaits.cs:21`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/MSTestSettings.cs:1`
- **What:** All three projects declare [assembly: Parallelize(Scope = MethodLevel)] with the default worker count, one per processor. `dotnet test Nendo.slnx` (VSTest runner, per global.json) starts the three test hosts at the same moment: in the 2026-10-10 14:54 TRX files the Engine, LocalMcp and Desktop runs all begin within one second. Many tests start their own Kestrel host, pwsh children, Node agents or a WebView2 host. TestHostThreads raises the minimum thread-pool size in the LocalMcp process only. ProtocolResourceTests.ConnectAsync allows 10 s for initialization, and LatestProtocolTests.Client sets HttpClient.Timeout to 10 s. The Desktop tests' own MCP clients (AcquireLeaseAsync, ConnectAsync) allow 5 s for InitializationTimeout and ConnectionTimeout, and the Desktop process gets no pool sizing. TRX history: the 2026-10-05 06:09 LocalMcp run had 9 failures and the 2026-10-10 07:01 run had 18, almost all `McpException: The server does not support the requested protocol version '2026-07-28'` (a lost handshake) or `TaskCanceledException ... HttpClient.Timeout`. In the same windows, DesktopAgentSettingsTests.ASettingsRequestAdmittedBeforeSwitch... and ARefusedExpiry... failed with `TimeoutException: Initialization timed out` (3 runs each). The Engine process tests also failed at 07:01 with `Waited 60 s for the child's first line`.
- **Failure:** Something else is busy, such as a second worktree's build or an indexer, during a full gate run. Dozens of handshakes at once outrun the 10 s (LocalMcp) or 5 s (Desktop) bound, and between 2 and 18 unrelated tests fail with a misleading "protocol version" message. The run has to be repeated, and a real regression in the same area is hard to tell from noise.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python trxruns.py over tests/*/TestResults since 2026-09-27 -> LocalMcp "2026-10-05_06_09_10 total=220 failed=9" and "2026-10-10_07_01_12 total=246 failed=18"; Desktop "2026-10-10_07_02_35 total=415 failed=2"; Engine "2026-10-10_07_01_20 total=1114 failed=2". trxfail.py names the messages: "The server does not support the requested protocol versi...", "Initialization timed out", "Waited 60 s for the child's first line".
- **Fix and guard:** Bound the concurrency instead of stretching timeouts. In Test-Production, run the three test projects one after another (one `dotnet test` per project, or `-m:1`), and cap MSTest workers in each MSTestSettings.cs (for example Workers = Environment.ProcessorCount / 2). Move TestHostThreads, or an equivalent [AssemblyInitialize], into the Desktop project too. Raise the Desktop clients' InitializationTimeout to the LocalMcp value through one shared helper instead of four copies. Guard: a repeat lane (`Test-Production -Repeat 5`) that fails if any run has a handshake-timeout failure, plus a per-run summary that counts HANDSHAKE > 1 s lines from ConnectAsync.
- **Verifier:** The TRX history supports the claim, and the code matches it. All three projects declare `Parallelize(Scope = MethodLevel)` (MSTestSettings.cs:1). The 2026-10-10_14_54 TRX files for Engine, LocalMcp and Desktop start within one second of each other (14:54:45, 14:54:45, 14:54:46), so the three hosts do run together under the VSTest runner. SetMinThreads appears only in tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/TestHostThreads.cs:26. Client bounds: LocalMcp ProtocolResourceTests.cs:315 InitializationTimeout 10 s and LatestProtocolTests.cs:94 HttpClient.Timeout 10 s; Desktop DesktopAgentSettingsTests.cs:254-259, DesktopExtensionWriterAgentRaceTests.cs:108-113 and DesktopReplacementTests.cs:276-281 use 5 s. I re-parsed the TRX files: LocalMcp 2026-10-05_06_09_10 had 9 failures (7 `does not support the requested protocol version`, 2 HttpClient.Timeout); 2026-10-10_07_01_12 had 18 (16 protocol version, 1 Initialization timed out, 1 HttpClient.Timeout). Desktop 2026-10-05_06_09_32 and 2026-10-10_07_02_35 each had 2 `Initialization timed out` failures, and Engine 2026-10-10_07_01_20 had 2 `first line` waits. TestHostThreads.cs documents F-134 as fixed by sizing the harness, so these are recurrences.
- **Correction:** Qualify the rate. Handshake failures hit 4 of 101 LocalMcp runs and 4 of 101 Desktop runs since 2026-09-27, always in early-morning runs where something else was loading the machine. The 2026-10-10 07:01 LocalMcp run took about 11 minutes against about 2 minutes for the clean 14:54 run. So the three concurrent hosts amplify an external load spike rather than failing on their own. The listed fix of running the three projects one after another and capping MSTest workers is still the sound remedy. Ordinary gate runs are not affected.

<a id="wxs-04"></a>

### WXS-04 — A view can keep the Workbench busy by repeating ui.openScreen, and while it does Nendo silently drops the person's navigation and kill-switch clicks

**P2** · reliability · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:658`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-ui.ts:124`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:325`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-packages.ts:329`
- **What:** ui.openRecord, ui.openScreen and ui.openStudio are `local()` entries with no rate limit. ui.toast, ui.setToolbar, ui.showMenu, ui.setPlace and the keys all have one. openScreenFromView sets `state.actionInFlight = true` and keeps it across `await refreshDerived()`. Opening the view's own screen keeps its frame, because the mountKey does not change and wireViewFrames adopts the frame, so the view keeps running and can ask again at once. While actionInFlight is true, openWorkspaceView returns without a word (`if (state.actionInFlight) return;`). That is how Studio > Surfaces > Custom views and openCustomViews are reached. setViewSwitch, the kill switch itself, also returns without a word.
- **Failure:** A hostile or broken view loops `nendo.ui.openScreen(nendo.context.viewId)` with up to eight requests in flight. The ones that arrive while an open runs get `busy` and are sent again. The Workbench is busy almost all the time. Each open forces state.view back to Use on the view's screen. The person's clicks on Studio, Surfaces or the Run custom views switch land while actionInFlight is true and do nothing, with no message. ADR-0013's decision driver 6 says a person can always turn views off, and 'Restart without custom views' is only offered in the recovery view after a failure.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Bound the navigation methods per connection, for example one a second as for toasts. Answer an open of the screen or record already shown as done without redrawing. Refuse navigation from a mount that is not on screen (see the parked-view finding). Make the kill switch preempt instead of dropping the click: setViewSwitch should apply while a view-started action is in flight, or queue and say so. Guard: an extension-broker.test.mjs case asserting that a second ui.openScreen within a second is refused `busy` without calling deps.ui.openScreen, and a view-packages test asserting setViewSwitch still applies while actionInFlight is set by a view-started navigation.
- **Verifier:** Traced from source: ui.openRecord/openScreen/openStudio are plain local() entries with no withinRate (extension-broker.ts:655-658, unlike toast/setToolbar/showMenu/setPlace at 659-707); the contract's Limits table (custom-views.md:1090-1104) lists no limit for them. openScreenFromView (extension-ui.ts:124-150) holds state.actionInFlight=true across await refreshDerived() and then rerender()s; the view's own frame is kept (mountKey, wireViewFrames adopt), so it can immediately ask again. While actionInFlight is true openWorkspaceView (actions.ts:325) and setViewSwitch (view-packages.ts:329) return without a word, and setBusy(true) (shell.ts:440-449) disables the [data-action] controls too; a full rerender every open also replaces the DOM under a press. So a looping or buggy view can make the kill-switch clicks and Studio navigation mostly fail. Not reproduced in a real WebView2. ADR-0013 driver 6 ('a person can always turn views off') and 'the kill switches are the whole control' (line 633) make this more than cosmetic, but safe mode, Restart without custom views and quitting remain, and the ADR already accepts view-caused renderer DoS (Negative consequences), so P2 stands only as friction with a workaround.
- **Correction:** Reproduction was source-only; the 'almost always busy' claim rests on timing (an open takes a host round trip plus a full rerender; the gap before the view's next request is one message round trip). Workaround exists: safe mode, Restart without custom views, or closing the file; no data is at risk.

### CSS-04 — Under forced colors (Windows contrast themes), the selected navigation item, the rating, the selected record-page tab, view switcher segment, theme toggle and @ menu option, and the focused treegrid row can't be told apart

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:175`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:183`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:514`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:423`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:447`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/14-refinements-controls.css:716`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:58`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:573`
- **What:** These states are drawn only with background colour, box-shadow or a coloured pseudo-element. Forced colors replaces all three: backgrounds become Canvas and box-shadow becomes none. Covered here: the NavigationView selection, which is a fill plus a `::before` pill (21:175-194); the rating radios (`appearance: none`, checked = cobalt fill, 14:716-735) and the rating dots (09:58-69); the selected record-page tab (09:573-578); the pressed view switcher segment (08:534-539); the pressed theme and shortcut toggles (21:447-448); the @ menu's aria-selected option (22:1102-1109); the treegrid row, which sets `outline: none` and shows focus as a td fill plus an inset shadow (09:1281-1283); and today's calendar cell (09:381-383). The one forced-colors fallback for the nav and the theme control (10-forms.css:514-521, border CanvasText) is cancelled by higher-specificity Mica rules: `.rail .nav-item.is-selected:not(.nav-section) { border: 0 }` (21:177) and `.status-bar .theme-control { border: 0 }` (21:423-428). Text fields set `outline: 0` (10-forms.css:12) and show focus only as a border hue.
- **Failure:** A person using a Windows contrast theme (Aquatic, Desert, or High Contrast Black or White) opens a record. They can't see which rating value is chosen, which tab is open, which navigation place they're on, or which theme is active. Arrowing through the outline treegrid or the @ menu gives no visible focus. Nendo is Windows-only, so this is that platform's accessibility mode.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-states.cjs and probe-focus.cjs with Emulation.setEmulatedMedia forced-colors: active. Checked and unchecked rating radios both computed bg rgb(255,255,255) with border rgb(0,0,0). The filled and empty rating dots computed identical. The selected nav item had border none and pill-bg rgb(255,255,255). The selected and unselected tablist tabs both had shadow none. The focused outline row had td-bg rgba(255,255,255) and td-shadow none. The focused input showed outline none, with the border going from rgb(0,0,0) to rgb(55,0,110). Screenshot forced-form.png shows the three severity pills and the dots identical.
- **Fix and guard:** Add an `@media (forced-colors: active)` block that gives each state a forced-colors-safe mark: `outline: 2px solid Highlight` or `border-color: Highlight` for the selected nav item, tab, segment, toggle and mention option; `forced-color-adjust: none` or `background: Highlight` for the checked rating radio and filled dots; and `outline: 2px solid Highlight` for `.outline-row:focus-visible`. Write them with selectors at least as specific as the 21-native rules they compete with. For text fields, replace `outline: 0` with `outline: 2px solid transparent`, which becomes visible in forced colors. Guard: a CDP lane with forced-colors emulation that asserts that a selected and an unselected instance of each control differ in computed outline or border style, colour or width.
- **Verifier:** No @media (forced-colors: active) block covers these states. The only ones in the slices are 04-shell:138, 10-forms:514, 11:182, 12:281, 16:286, 18:201, 22:379 and 22:1180, none for the listed controls. The one nav/theme fallback (10-forms.css:514-521) is beaten by .rail .nav-item.is-selected:not(.nav-section) { border: 0 } (21-native.css:175-178) and .status-bar .theme-control { border: 0 } (21:423). The states are drawn only with background, inset box-shadow or a coloured ::before (09:58-69, 09:573-578, 08:534-539, 14:716-735, 21:447-448, 22:1102-1109, 09:1281-1283, 09:381-383), all of which forced colors flattens. I re-ran headless Edge with forced-colors emulation: checked and unchecked rating radios, filled and empty dots, selected and unselected tab and theme button all compute the same border and the same Canvas or transparent background and box-shadow none; the selected nav-place pill ::before becomes Canvas white; the focused .outline-row keeps outline-style none (only the outline colour changes). studio.md:86 and :253 list high-contrast presentation as a goal and nothing defers it, so this is not a documented trade-off. Real, scoped to Windows contrast themes.
- **Correction:** Text-field focus is weak but not invisible: with focus emulation on, #probe-input border goes from rgb(0,0,0) to Highlight rgb(55,0,110), so that sub-claim is a minor aside, not an indistinguishable state. Button focus (button:focus-visible, 03-base.css:68) is fine under forced colors. Selected tab keeps a 600 vs 670 font-weight difference, which is a very weak cue.

### GGV-01 — Gantt bars, milestones and the selected row vanish in Windows contrast themes (forced colours)

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/gantt/gantt.css:37`, `extensions/gantt/gantt.css:39`, `extensions/gantt/gantt.css:32`, `extensions/gantt/gantt.css:38`
- **What:** Every mark the chart draws is an HTML span painted only by background-color (.bar{background:var(--cobalt)}, .milestone{background:var(--cobalt)}, .row[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--cobalt-soft)}). In forced-colours mode Chromium replaces background-color with the Canvas system colour, so the marks take the page's background. The kit's installFocusRing covers forced colours only for the focus outline, and the authoring guide claims high contrast reaches a view through the forced-colors media query.
- **Failure:** A person running a Windows contrast theme opens a screen with the Gantt: every track is empty (only the labels and an axis line remain), milestones and the selected record are invisible, so the chart carries no information.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-gantt.mjs in headless msedge with forcedColors:'active' -> forced colours: {"forced":true,"bar":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","main":"rgb(255, 255, 255)","body":"rgb(255, 255, 255)"}; screenshot gantt-forced.png shows twelve labelled rows with blank tracks.
- **Fix and guard:** Add an @media (forced-colors: active) block: .bar,.milestone{forced-color-adjust:none;background:CanvasText} .row[aria-pressed=true] .bar,.row[aria-pressed=true] .milestone{background:Highlight} .row[aria-pressed=true]{outline:2px solid Highlight}, or draw the marks with borders, which forced colours keep. Guard: in Review-Gantt open the chart with forcedColors 'active' and assert the bar's computed background differs from main's and its rect has non-zero area; falsify by deleting the block.
- **Verifier:** extensions/gantt/gantt.css:37-40 paints .bar and .milestone (and the selected row at :32) with background-color only, with no border, outline, forced-color-adjust or @media (forced-colors) rule anywhere in the extension (grep: the only forced-colors rule is the kit's focus ring, tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:34). docs/custom-view-authoring.md:449-452 says high contrast reaches a view through the forced-colors media query, so the page is in scope for it, and the Workbench's own CSS has forced-colors blocks. Chromium replaces background-color with Canvas there, so marks take the track colour. I viewed the reviewer's gantt-forced.png: twelve labelled rows with blank tracks. No accepted ADR mandates this.
- **Correction:** The defect is real but narrow: it needs a Windows contrast theme. P2 stays because the chart carries no information there and the fix is a few CSS lines.

### GGV-03 — A re-read drops keyboard focus to the document in all four views, and the Gantt's one tab stop resets to the first row

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/gantt/gantt.js:51`, `extensions/gantt/gantt.js:128`, `tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:52`, `tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:109`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:79`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:301`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:454`
- **What:** Each view rebuilds its rows or nodes from scratch on every read (element('rows').replaceChildren(), drawing.replaceChildren(), layer.replaceChildren()) and never puts focus back. The Gantt then calls keys.refresh(); the kit's refresh() re-settles on current(), which picks the first item whose tabIndex is 0 - every freshly created <button> - so the roving stop moves to the first row even though the selection (aria-pressed) is kept.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user arrows to the 15th Gantt row (or tabs to a node in a graph), presses Enter to open it beside the view and edits it; the commit triggers a re-read, the focused element is removed, focus falls to <body>, and the next Tab starts again at the first row or node of a possibly long list.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-gantt.mjs (Tab, ArrowDown x3, emit changes) -> focus before re-read: {"id":"t3","stops":["t3"]} after: {"id":"BODY","stops":["t0"],"reads":2}; probe-graphs.mjs -> dependency-graph / systems-lens / work-dependencies: focused element after re-read = BODY.
- **Fix and guard:** Before redrawing, note whether focus is inside the drawing and the focused item's data-id; after redrawing, focus the item with that id ({preventScroll:true}) or the nearest survivor. In the kit, let refresh() keep the stop by an identity (refresh(keyOf) or a data-id comparison) instead of element identity. Guard: Review lanes focus row/node 3, emit changes, and assert document.activeElement.dataset.id is unchanged and exactly that item has tabIndex 0; falsify by removing the restore.
- **Verifier:** Every re-read rebuilds the drawing with replaceChildren (gantt.js:51, graph.js:79, lens.js:301, work-dependencies/view.js:454), which removes a focused element and drops focus to the document, and none of the four restores it. In the Gantt, keys.refresh() (gantt.js:128) calls the kit's refresh() (nendo-view-kit.js:109), which settles on current() (:52); current() returns the first item with tabIndex 0, and every freshly created <button> has tabIndex 0, so the roving stop resets to the first row while aria-pressed is kept. The Gantt gate only checks the one-stop invariant after arrow keys (Gate-Gantt.mjs:118-130), not across a re-read. The changes event fires on any commit (contract line 1068), so an agent write is enough.
- **Correction:** The scenario is slightly off: while the person edits the record beside the view, focus is in the other frame, so the view's activeElement is lost silently and the cost shows when they return and Tab restarts at the first row or node. A commit made while they arrow through the view (an agent write, or Work dependencies' own command at view.js:601) drops focus at once. The defect itself stands.

### GGV-04 — Systems Lens text view rebuilds itself on every selection, so activating a component from it by keyboard loses focus

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:223`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:252`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:239`
- **What:** A text-view button's click calls select() -> highlight() -> paint(), and paint() ends with textView(verdict), which calls list.replaceChildren() and creates every button again. The button the person just pressed is destroyed. paint() also runs for Focus and Take out, rebuilding the list each time. The Dependency graph and Work dependencies only update aria-pressed in place and keep focus.
- **Failure:** A screen-reader or keyboard user works in the text alternative (the view's accessibility path), moves to 'Coolant pump A' and presses Enter: the component opens, focus jumps to <body>, and they must Tab back from the top through every control to the list and find their place again - after every single selection.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-graphs.mjs (Text view, focus button n4, press Enter) -> systems-lens: after Enter in the text view, focus is on BODY; dependency-graph: BUTTON:n4; work-dependencies: BUTTON:n4.
- **Fix and guard:** Build the text list in render() only, and in paint() update aria-pressed and the verdict paragraphs of the existing rows; or, if the list must be rebuilt, refocus the button with the same data-id. Guard: Review-SystemsLens focuses a text-view button, presses Enter and asserts document.activeElement.dataset.id; falsify by restoring the rebuild.
- **Verifier:** A text-view button's click calls select() (lens.js:242) then highlight() (:239), which calls paint(); paint() ends with textView(verdict) (:223), and textView() starts with list.replaceChildren() and builds every button again (:252-277). The button that was pressed is destroyed inside its own click handler, so focus drops to the document. The Dependency graph's highlight() only updates aria-pressed in place (graph.js:50) and Work dependencies' paint() does the same (view.js:537), so the contrast is accurate. The text view is the stated accessibility alternative, and the SVG nodes stay focusable, so there is a path that keeps focus.
- **Correction:** Take Out and Focus buttons are in the header, so rebuilding the list does not affect them directly. The defect is selection from the text list.

### UIK-03 — Conversation tab drops keyboard focus to <body> after Send, Stop, answering a permission request, Launch and New session

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard` · also reported as WAU-02, WAU-08

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:427`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:471`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:295`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:166`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:140`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:249`
- **What:** patchChat swaps the round button by setting `sendButton.hidden = composer.canStop` and `stopButton.hidden = !composer.canStop`, which removes the focused button from the page. An answered permission is redrawn as `<p class="chat-answered">` with no controls, so focusedControl(held) finds no counterpart and the replaced Allow button takes focus with it. launchAgent and newSession rebuild the page through openTabOn -> renderAgentChat (content.innerHTML), and nothing then focuses #agent-prompt.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user Tabs to Send and presses Enter: focus goes to <body>. They press Enter on Stop: <body> again. They answer 'Allow' on a permission request: <body>, and they have to find the message box again. A screen reader's cursor jumps to the top of the window after each of these.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p04 and p06 in headless Edge (real CDP key events) -> "focus right after Launch: body"; "focus after Send button: body send hidden: true"; "focus after Stop: body stop hidden: true"; "focus after answering: body".
- **Fix and guard:** In patchChat, when document.activeElement is the button about to be hidden, focus its counterpart (Send<->Stop) or the textarea. After an answer, focus #agent-prompt, or give the answered line tabindex=-1 and focus it. After a launch or New session, focus #agent-prompt once it is enabled. Guard: a headless journey asserting activeElement.id is 'stop-agent' or 'agent-prompt' after Enter on #send-prompt, 'agent-prompt' after Enter on Allow, and 'agent-prompt' after Launch.
- **Verifier:** patchChat sets sendButton.hidden = composer.canStop and stopButton.hidden = !composer.canStop (view-agent-chat.ts:426-430); .chat-round[hidden] is display:none (22-agent-chat.css:1017), and composerState.canStop is chat.working (agent-chat-model.ts:168). Pressing Send makes the agent work, so the focused Send is hidden; pressing Stop ends the turn, so the focused Stop is hidden. Either way focus goes to <body>. For permissions, the Allow click goes through act -> patchChat; the answered item is a control-less <p class=chat-answered> (agent-chat-model.ts:295-297), so focusedControl(held) finds no [data-option-id] counterpart and focus is not restored (view-agent-chat.ts:466-472). launchAgent (view-agent-chat.ts:140-153) ends in openTabOn -> rerender -> renderAgentChat, which builds the page with content.innerHTML and never focuses #agent-prompt (grep: no .focus() on it anywhere). ACP-05 only covers fold toggles and options of a redrawn item, so this is a gap in intended behaviour.
- **Correction:** Narrow the Send and Stop cases: pressing Enter inside the textarea (the main send path) and Esc there keep focus, because the textarea stays enabled while working. Only Tab-to-Send, Tab-to-Stop, the permission answer buttons, Launch and New session lose focus. Not run against a screen reader.

### UIK-04 — Opening or leaving the agent proposal review, accepting it, and opening or closing a record all leave focus on <body>

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard` · also reported as UIS-07

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:622`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:222`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:369`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:572`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:614`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-use.ts:248`
- **What:** The dismiss-return logic records `button.id` only (`dismissReturnId = button.id === '' ? null : button.id`). The agent's 'Review changes' button ([data-review-agent-proposal]) and the Use record rows ([data-record-id]) have no id, so Back or Escape restores nothing. Opening the review (reviewAgentProposal -> state.view='agentProposal'), accepting (resolveAgentProposal -> state.view='agent') and opening a record (card click -> rerender) all replace the clicked control, and nothing focuses the new surface. Add has an id and comes back correctly, which shows the gap is the id-only lookup.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user presses Enter on 'Review changes' and focus is on <body>, with the review content far down the Tab order. Escape returns to the Agent page with focus on <body> instead of the button. Accepting leaves focus on <body>. In Use, Enter on a record opens the inspector with focus on <body>, so reaching it means tabbing through the rest of the list. Escape closes it and leaves focus on <body>.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p07 and p16 in headless Edge -> "on review page, focus: body"; "after Escape back to Agent, focus: body"; "after Accept, focus: body \| outcome: status ... Refine Idea workflow accepted."; "after opening a record: focus body ... inspector: true"; "after Escape: focus body \| inspector: false"; control case "after Escape from Add: focus button#new-record.primary-button".
- **Fix and guard:** Record a selector for the control that opened a surface, not only its id: reuse the data-attribute approach of view-agent.ts focusedControl, such as [data-review-agent-proposal=…] or [data-record-id=…]. When a review or the inspector opens, focus its heading (tabindex=-1) or its Back/Close button. After Accept, focus the outcome slot or the Activity tab. Guard: a journey asserting activeElement is inside .agent-proposal-page after Enter on Review changes, and matches the originating [data-review-agent-proposal] or [data-record-id] after Escape.
- **Verifier:** main.ts:622-633 records only button.id (dismissReturnId = button.id === '' ? null : button.id) and restores it with document.getElementById. The Review changes button is rendered with data-review-agent-proposal and no id (view-agent.ts:~240), and every record row/card is a <button data-record-id> with no id (surface-markup.ts:171, 240, 510; record-markup.ts:86), so Escape (main.ts:541-551 clicks the [data-dismiss] control) or Back restores nothing. Opening the review (view-agent.ts:563-578), accepting (resolveAgentProposal, view-agent.ts:614-618, state.view='agent' then rerender) and opening a record (view-use.ts:248-257, rerender) all replace content.innerHTML, and no shared focus restore exists in shell.rerender or view-use.ts (grep: only the surface picker is refocused). Controls with an id such as #new-record do round-trip, which shows the id-only lookup is the gap. Nothing moves focus to the newly opened review or inspector either.
- **Correction:** The comment at main.ts:619-621 states the intent (hand focus back), so this is a hole in an existing mechanism rather than a new feature. Reproductions were headless Edge, same Chromium engine as WebView2.

### UIK-05 — The chat's role=log re-announces whole items: each streamed chunk re-inserts the full message, and the empty state is re-inserted on every read

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard` · also reported as WAU-04

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:259`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:476`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:487`
- **What:** #chat-thread is role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions". patchChat redraws any item whose markup changed with `held.replaceWith(next)`, which is a removal plus an addition. The streaming agent message, the steps line ('· 1 step', '· 2 steps', done) and the answered permission are therefore new additions each time, carrying their full text. With no items, patchChat sets `thread.innerHTML = <div class="chat-empty">…` on every patch, even when the text is identical.
- **Failure:** A screen-reader user asks the agent something. The reply arrives in chunks, and each chunk is announced as a new log entry with the whole message so far ('I proposed a Task record type', then 'I proposed a Task record type with a title and a due date.', then again with 'Review it…'). A real agent streams far more chunks than this preview. While idle, changing Mode re-announces 'GitHub Copilot CLI is ready…' twice.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p06 with a MutationObserver on #chat-thread -> "insertions during the streamed reply: 11859 chat-answered ... / 12163 chat-agent markdown-body :: I proposed a Task record type / 12457 chat-agent markdown-body :: I proposed a Task record type with a title and a due date. / 12762 chat-agent markdown-body :: ... Review it o"; steps re-inserted 4 times in one turn; "insertions after option change: 6212 chat-empty :: GitHub Copilot CLI is ready... / 6216 chat-empty :: GitHub Copilot CLI is ready...".
- **Fix and guard:** Keep one element per item and update it in place: replace the markdown body's children or textContent rather than the item element, and give a streaming item aria-busy="true" until the turn ends. Write chat-empty only when its text changes. Guard: in the headless lane, count .chat-agent additions during a 3-chunk reply (expect 1) and chat-empty insertions after an option change (expect 0).
- **Verifier:** #chat-thread is role=log aria-live=polite aria-relevant=additions (view-agent-chat.ts:259). In patchChat a changed item is redrawn with held.replaceWith(next) (view-agent-chat.ts:476-484), which is a removal plus a new node carrying the whole text. itemMarkup (agent-chat-model.ts:259-262) renders the agent message from entry.text, and mergeChat (agent-chat-model.ts:75-80) overwrites the entry by id with a higher revision, so every streamed chunk changes the markup and replaces the whole .chat-agent element; the steps line changes the same way (stepsSummary). With no items, patchChat sets thread.innerHTML to the chat-empty block unconditionally on every call (view-agent-chat.ts:486-490, no comparison with `drawn`). Nothing is preview-specific: the same path runs for a real ACP agent. The announcement itself depends on the screen reader; the review measured insertions, not NVDA or JAWS output.
- **Correction:** The re-insertion of an answered permission as one new line is arguably wanted, so the defect is streaming agent text, the steps line and the empty state. The streaming fix should update the existing element in place (or set aria-busy) rather than replace it; the empty-state fix should compare text before writing.

<a id="uis-05"></a>

### UIS-05 — The sticky Save bar in the record inspector covers the control that keyboard focus moves to (focus obscured)

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/14-refinements-controls.css:93`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:158`
- **What:** .record-inspector .form-actions is position:sticky; bottom:0 (14-refinements-controls.css:93-101). The header is sticky at the top (82-87). .record-inspector, the scroller, declares no scroll-padding (09-surfaces.css:158-163), and no stylesheet anywhere sets scroll-padding or scroll-margin. When focus moves to a control below the fold, the browser scrolls it only to the scroller's bottom edge, which is behind the bar.
- **Failure:** At 1024x768, open a Decision and press Tab down the form. The State select receives focus but all 30px of it sit under 'Delete record… / Save changes'. Someone using the keyboard cannot see the field they are on (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11). This happens in every fixture and at every size tested.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p34-obscured.mjs -> '1024 decision hidden under the Save bar: field.decision.state 30/30px'; '1024 idea … field.idea.nextAction 30/30px'; '1024 tree … field.capability.owner 30/30px'; '1440 decision … field.decision.reviewDate 30/30px'; '800 idea … field.idea.createdDate 30/30px'. Screenshot obscured-decision-1024.png
- **Fix and guard:** Set scroll-padding-block on .record-inspector to at least the header height (52px or more) at the top and the form-actions height at the bottom, or call scrollIntoView with a margin from a focusin handler. Guard: p34-style gate check asserting zero overlap between document.activeElement and .form-actions for every Tab stop in the form.
- **Verifier:** Read the CSS and searched for any mitigation. 14-refinements-controls.css:93-101 makes .record-inspector .form-actions position:sticky; bottom:0 with an opaque background, and :82-87 makes the inspector header sticky at the top. The scroller is .record-inspector (09-surfaces.css:158-163, overflow:auto), and no scroll-padding or scroll-margin appears anywhere under src/ (grep for scroll-padding\|scroll-margin\|scrollIntoView finds only 'nearest' scrolls of menus, messages and revealField, record-form.ts:339). Chromium's focus-scroll test uses the scroller's padding box and ignores sticky overlays, so a control that tabbing brings into the bottom ~60px of the scroller counts as already visible and is left under the bar. Sequential Tab through a form that overflows therefore lands the next field under the bar, which matches the reviewer's measured 30/30px overlaps. That is a real WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 failure on the main record edit path for keyboard users. Workaround is wheel-scrolling or Tab once more, so P2.
- **Correction:** Mechanism detail: the field is hidden because it is inside the scroller's visible box but under the sticky bar (so the browser does not scroll), not because it is scrolled to the bottom edge from far away. The sticky header at the top has the same exposure on Shift+Tab. The fix (scroll-padding-block on .record-inspector) is right.

<a id="uis-06"></a>

### UIS-06 — Choice chips for options without a tone fail WCAG AA contrast for about half of all derived hues in Light

**P2** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/tones.ts:40`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:122`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:135`
- **What:** choiceStyle gives an untoned option --status-color: hsl(hue 58% 49%) (tones.ts:40). .card-chip draws 0.75rem / weight 680 text in color-mix(status 78%, ink) on color-mix(status 14%, surface-raised) (13-refinements-pages.css:122-133). Dark mixes 55% with white on 22% (135-138). Named tones pass. Derived hues, the default for every option nobody coloured, often do not.
- **Failure:** On the Idea board fixture, the 'Medium' Energy chip is 3.22:1 in Light, and the dark 'High' chip is 4.27:1 at 10.5px. Measured with the page's own CSS over all 360 derived hues, 183 fail 4.5:1 in Light (minimum 2.56:1 at hue 60, yellow) and 62 fail in Dark (minimum 4.13:1). Any board, gallery or record header whose choice field has no tones shows status text below AA.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p27-chips.mjs -> light {tones all 4.74-6.23, derived:{fails:183, of:360, min:2.56, minHue:60}}; dark {tones 5.28-5.76, derived:{fails:62, of:360, min:4.13, minHue:240}}; tour.json card-chip 'Medium' 3.22 (light), 'High' 4.27 (dark).
- **Fix and guard:** Derive the chip's text colour from luminance instead of a fixed 78% mix: mix towards ink until the contrast reaches 4.5:1, or clamp the derived hue's lightness per theme (for example 35% in Light, 70% in Dark). Guard: a node test over hues 0-359 that resolves the mix and asserts at least 4.5:1 in both themes.
- **Verifier:** Recomputed by hand from the code. tones.ts:36-41 gives an untoned option --status-color: hsl(<derivedHue> 58% 49%), and choiceStyle is what feeds .card-chip (record-markup.ts:83). 13-refinements-pages.css:127-130 sets chip text to color-mix(status 78%, ink) on color-mix(status 14%, surface-raised) at 0.75rem/680. With the Light tokens (--ink #1b1b1b, --surface-raised #fff, 02-tokens.css:20,22) at hue 60 (about rgb 197,197,52) the text mixes to about rgb 160,160,47 (L about 0.326) on about rgb 247,247,227 (L about 0.919), which is 2.58:1; the reviewer measured 2.56. So untoned yellow-green options fail AA by a wide margin, and many other hues fail too. The derived-hue fallback itself is what the ADR-0004 tone amendment describes (tones.ts:1-7), but nothing there or in docs/contracts mandates the chip's text colour, and no gate measures contrast (grep over tools/ and docs/ finds none). Named tones pass, and giving an option a tone is a workaround, so this is a real but bounded accessibility defect: P2, low end.
- **Correction:** The Dark failures are marginal (reviewer's minimum 4.13:1), so the weight of the finding is the Light theme. The fix belongs in the chip CSS (13-refinements-pages.css:127-138) rather than in derivedHue, which must stay stable per value.

### ABS-05 — Archi toolbar declaration exceeds Nendo's 16 KiB once a model has about 33 element specializations; the fallback toolbar has no Edit, Commit, Discard, Undo or zoom

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `extensions/archi/view.js:771`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1926`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1935`, `extensions/archi/view.js:817`, `extensions/archi/view.js:881`, `extensions/archi/index.html:5`
- **What:** declareToolbar puts up to 40 specializedItems (each with a label and a detail line) into the New menu. It also adds specializationFilter, a select of up to 63 options with record-ID values. Nendo refuses any declaration over extensionLimits.toolbarBytes (16 KiB, view-toolbar-model.ts:246). The refusal goes to leaveNativeChrome, which sets nativeChrome=false for the rest of the visit and shows #own-toolbar. That toolbar holds no Edit toggle, Commit, Discard, Undo/Redo, Arrange or zoom. Measured by evaluating view.js's own declareToolbar, editingMenus, specializedItems and specializationFilter against a stub model with realistic names, while editing a view: '30 specializations: 15590 bytes', '40 specializations: 18623 bytes > 16 KiB, refused'. With no view open: '63 specializations: 17750 bytes > 16 KiB, refused'.
- **Failure:** In a repository with 35 element specializations, a person opens a view and presses Edit, and the declaration grows past 16 KiB. The workbench drops Nendo's row and says 'Nendo could not show the workbench's controls'. The waiting edits can now be neither committed nor discarded from any control, and they stay in localStorage.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-archi-toolbar.mjs (evaluates the declareToolbar source from extensions/archi/view.js) -> ' 0 specializations: 6390 bytes ... 30 specializations: 15590 bytes / 40 specializations: 18623 bytes > 16 KiB, refused / 63 specializations: 21320 bytes > 16 KiB, refused'
- **Fix and guard:** Keep the declaration within 16 KiB. Drop the detail line from specialized items, or cap them by measured bytes rather than by count (40). Move the specialization filter to a search or a shorter list. Measure JSON byte length before sending, and trim the optional parts first. Never fall back to a toolbar that lacks Commit and Discard while edits wait; add them to #own-toolbar. Guard: a view.test.mjs case that builds declareToolbar with 63 specializations of 80-character names while editing, and asserts the JSON is at most 16384 bytes.
- **Verifier:** Host limit: readToolbar refuses a declaration over extensionLimits.toolbarBytes = 16 KiB of JSON of {items, add} (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-toolbar-model.ts:244-246, extension-api/protocol.ts:60). I evaluated view.js's own declareToolbar, editingMenus, specializedItems and specializationFilter (extensions/archi/view.js:755-880, 1927-1950) against a stub model in node (probe-toolbar-v1.mjs): editing with 0 specializations is 6,391 bytes, 30 gives 15,745, 33 gives 16,666 (refused), 40 gives 18,817; with no view open 63 gives 17,998 (refused). The setToolbar rejection reaches leaveNativeChrome (:881-886), which sets nativeChrome=false for the visit and shows #own-toolbar, and extensions/archi/index.html:5-23 holds no Edit, Commit, Discard, Undo, Redo or zoom, and no keys are delivered. Pressing Edit therefore strands the waiting edits (kept in localStorage and restored into the same overflowing editor on return). The caps (40 items, 63 options) count entries, not bytes. The trigger needs roughly 31 or more element specializations, uncommon but ordinary for a large repository.
- **Correction:** Threshold with 42-character names and 38-character record IDs is about 31-32 specializations while editing (the finding says about 33); names near the 80-character cap hit it sooner. Otherwise as stated.
