### CSS-01 — At windows of 840px wide or less and 600px tall or less, the navigation shrinks to a clipped 56x48 box with blank buttons, and the command box sits under the window's caption buttons

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/12-agent-activity.css:296`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/12-agent-activity.css:297`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/12-agent-activity.css:304`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:499`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:503`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:506`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/20-title-bar.css:517`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/20-title-bar.css:528`
- **What:** The compact block in 12 (`@media (max-width: 840px) and (max-height: 600px)`) still gives `.app-shell` a 56px column and a single row (line 297). It also hides the labels with a clip (line 304). 21-native's `@media (max-width: 840px)` block comes later in the cascade and has the same specificity. It turns `.rail` into a 48px-tall horizontal bar with `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none` (506-515) and hides `.rail .nav-symbol` (503-504), but it never resets `.app-shell`. That leaves the top bar squeezed into the 56px side column. Every Studio item ends up with neither an icon nor a label. The title-bar reservation fails too. 20-title-bar's branch for this size (`(min-width: 841px), (max-height: 600px)`) reserves `--title-bar-right` on `.workspace-header`, but `html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header` (21-native.css:344) outranks it. Its other branch (`min-height: 601px`) reserves on the rail and doesn't apply here. mica-direction.md:115 says that below 841px the navigation is the bar across the top. The host's minimum window is 1024x720 physical pixels (Nendo.Desktop/DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:10-11). That is 819x576 CSS px at 125% and 683x480 at 150%. The first-launch default of 1600x960 is 800x480 at 200%.
- **Failure:** On a laptop at 125% or 150% scale, a person resizes Nendo to its minimum size or snaps it to half the screen. The left edge shows only an 'F' from the clipped File menu. Data, Structure, Surfaces, History, Health, Agent and Help can't be seen or clicked. The command box is the last control on the address row, and Windows draws Close and Maximise over it. On a 4K display at 200%, this is the first-launch layout.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over a static copy of index.html with the concatenated stylesheet (probe-layout.cjs, probe-states.cjs) -> at 800x560 the probe reported shellCols "56px 744px", rail [0,0,56,48], railScrollW 306, and 'nav-data:20x32@114,8 sym=none labW=1' (the same for every Studio item). With data-title-bar=window and --title-bar-right 138px it reported 'controls under caption buttons (x>662, y<48): palette-open[744-780]'. Screenshot layout-800x560.png shows no navigation.
- **Fix and guard:** In the 21-native `@media (max-width: 840px)` block, restate `.app-shell { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr); }`. Delete the shell and rail rules of 12's compact block (lines 297-314), or the whole block. Change 20-title-bar's media queries to `(min-width: 841px)` and `(max-width: 840px)` so the rail reserves the caption width at every narrow height. Guard: a CDP browser lane at 800x560 and 683x480. It asserts that every displayed `.rail .nav-item` is at least 24px wide, fully inside the rail's visible rect, and shows a symbol or label. With --title-bar-right set, it also asserts that no button or summary in the top 48px crosses into [innerWidth - right, innerWidth].
- **Verifier:** I traced the cascade at <=840px wide and <=600px tall (import order in src/styles.css:12-33). 12-agent-activity.css:297 sets .app-shell to `56px minmax(0,1fr)` with one row. Nothing later resets it: 21-native.css:453 only applies at min-width 841, and 15-rail-collapse.css only under min-width 841. 21-native.css:499-514 then makes .rail a 48px-tall row with overflow-x:auto and scrollbar-width:none, inside that 56px column. 21-native.css:502-503 hides `.rail .nav-symbol`, which beats 12's display:inline because it has the same specificity and comes later. 12-agent-activity.css:304 clips the labels, and 21-native.css:156-163 never resets position, width or clip-path. The result: every primary and Studio item is a blank button that is padding only. On the title bar, `:root[data-title-bar=window] .workspace-header` (0,3,0) at 20-title-bar.css:16-23 loses to `html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header` (0,3,1) at 21-native.css:344. The rail reservation at 20-title-bar.css:27-31 needs min-height 601, so nothing keeps the caption-button width free. That leaves the 36px palette-trigger under Windows' buttons. The regime is reachable. DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:8-11 sizes the window in physical pixels, and WebView2 uses RasterizationScale with no ZoomFactor override. So the 1024x720 minimum is 819x576 CSS px at 125%. The 1600x960 first-launch default is 800x480 at 200% and 640x384 at 250%. I'm lowering it to P2. There are workarounds: maximise or enlarge the window, Ctrl 1-7, F1 and Ctrl K (mica-direction.md keyboard section). It only bites at small or high-DPI window sizes.
- **Correction:** The 20-title-bar.css line numbers are wrong. The file has 44 lines, and the two media blocks are at 20-title-bar.css:16-23 and 27-31, not 517/528 (those look like lines in a concatenated stylesheet). The nav-symbol hide is at 21-native.css:502-503 and the rail rule at 505-514. Two more points belong in the evidence. First, the label clip survives because 21-native.css:156-163 restyles `.rail .nav-item > span:not(.nav-symbol)` without resetting position, width, height or clip-path. Second, 20-title-bar.css:12-15 still says 'the rail runs down the side' in a window <=840 wide and <=600 tall, which 21-native.css:496-499 no longer honours. That comment is stale and should be fixed with the media queries. The failure scenario should add that clicking the palette trigger there lands on a caption button (Close or Maximise), and that Ctrl K and Ctrl 1-7 stay usable.

### DSH-01 — Startup opens (double-click, Jump List, Explorer New, New file's own window) end on the generic 'Studio recovery' panel for a synced-folder file or a known-instance copy, where the interactive open would ask

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:451`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:481`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:198`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:204`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:126`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopLocationPolicy.cs:90`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopNewFilePresentation.cs:49`
- **What:** InitializeStartupSessionAsync calls _session.OpenAsync / CreateAsync / CreateFromSavePickerAsync with no FileRequestScope bound. OpenCandidateCoreAsync(readOnly:false) calls RequireWritableLocation, which throws NendoPreconditionException('unsupported-sync-location') because HasLocationAcknowledgement has neither _currentWritableLocationAcknowledged nor a scope; it also throws DesktopFileCollisionException when CheckAsync finds a known original with the same instance. CreateCoreAsync does the same RequireWritableLocation. The catch at line 481 discards the exception and shows the fixed sentence 'The requested file could not be opened. Use Open file or backup to inspect it and choose recovery actions.'; RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync then says 'No file is open.' The interactive path (OpenNativeAssessmentAsync) handles both cases with a dialog offering Continue anyway / Open read-only / Open original. DesktopNewFilePresentation.OpenInItsOwnWindow launches a second process with the path, so a location the person acknowledged in the first process is refused again in the second.
- **Failure:** Windows 11 with OneDrive backing up Documents (the OOBE default): DesktopLocationPolicy.ForDevice adds %OneDrive%, so every .nendo under C:\Users\x\OneDrive\Documents that is double-clicked, picked from the taskbar Jump List, or made with Explorer New lands on 'Studio recovery' with no file open and no mention of the location. Same for File > New file into such a folder: the person clicks 'Continue anyway', the file is created, and the window that opens for it shows the recovery panel. Double-clicking an Explorer copy of a file previously opened writable shows the same panel instead of the collision choice.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Treat a startup request like a dropped file: start the Workbench with no file and run the interactive OpenNativeFileAsync(path) / create flow for the startup path (location dialog, collision dialog, read-only fallback), or at minimum show the refusal's own message and offer 'Open read-only' on the panel. Guard: a Desktop test that starts a MainPage-equivalent startup with a DesktopLocationPolicy whose root covers the path and asserts the panel text carries warning.Message and an Open read-only action (or that the location dialog is requested); and one with a seeded history collision.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. MainPage.xaml.cs:451-484 calls _session.OpenAsync/CreateAsync/CreateFromSavePickerAsync with no FileRequestScope (only BindReadProjection). OpenCandidateCoreAsync (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:198) and CreateCoreAsync (DesktopSessionController.cs:126) call RequireWritableLocation; HasLocationAcknowledgement (DesktopLocationPolicy.cs:86-88) is false with no scope and _currentWritableLocationAcknowledged unset, so a path under %OneDrive%/Dropbox/Google Drive (ForDevice adds them, lines 24-33) throws NendoPreconditionException. DesktopFileCollisionException (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:12, a NendoException) is thrown at 204-208 for a known-instance copy. Both are swallowed by the catch at MainPage.xaml.cs:481, which shows only the fixed sentence 'The requested file could not be opened...'. The interactive path (MainPage.FileActions.cs:181-236) asks the collision and 'Unsupported writable location' questions instead. The New-file route is real: NewNativeFileAsync (FileActions.cs:282) launches DesktopNewFilePresentation.OpenInItsOwnWindow(destination), whose new process goes through the same startup Open with no acknowledgement. No test in tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests covers a startup open in a policy root. Workaround exists (Open file or backup on the panel re-runs the interactive flow), so P2 stands.
- **Correction:** None to locations. The 'Studio recovery' panel does offer 'Open file or backup', which is the workaround; the defect is the dropped location/collision question and the generic message at startup.

### ESM-11 — No canonical operation removes a UI property, so an optional property once set cannot be cleared, refusals tell authors to remove it, and undoing its introduction is refused

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:185`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:253`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:347`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.Bindings.cs:194`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:834`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:515`
- **What:** The UI operations are ui.addNode, ui.setProperty, ui.moveNode and ui.removeNode. ExecuteSetUiPropertyAsync upserts value_json, so a null value is stored as JSON null and read back as a present property; the optional-property validators all refuse null (NUI312 opens, NUI330 visibleWhen, NUI340/341/342 header roles, NUI372 endDateFieldId, NUI278/279 ordering, NUI296 scope, NUI433/434 outline, NUI396/421 limit). Hints say 'or remove subtitleFieldId', 'Remove opens from this section', 'Remove visibleWhen', 'Remove fieldId' and 'Remove entityId', which no operation can do. CreateSetUiPropertyInverseAsync refuses 'A UI property with no retained prior value cannot be compensated' because there is no inverse to emit, although ui.setProperty declares ReversibleWithRetainedState.
- **Failure:** An author who gave a record page with thirty bindings a subtitle, a visibleWhen, an opens, a sort or a scope and wants it gone must remove the whole node subtree and rebuild it; setting the property to null fails validation; History cannot undo the revision that introduced the property; and the file keeps the capability rung the property raised (for example opens raises 1.28).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-compile.ps1 case 4 -> 'NUI312 [page.sec/opens] 'null' is not a way a section can start.' / 'NUI330 [page.sec/visibleWhen] 'null' is not a calculated field of this record type.' / 'NUI341 [page.root/subtitleFieldId] The page subtitle must name a field. \| hint: Set the fieldId of an active field, or remove subtitleFieldId.'
- **Fix and guard:** Add ui.removeProperty {surfaceId, nodeId, propertyName} (definition lane, ReversibleWithRetainedState, evidence = previous value) through Operations.cs, the canonical compiler, storage, SemanticDiff and compensation, and use it as the inverse of a setProperty whose previousValuePresent is false; or define a JSON null value as deletion in storage. Guard: tests that clear subtitleFieldId and compile valid, and that compensating a first-time setProperty succeeds; falsify by removing the delete.
- **Verifier:** The only UI operations are ui.addNode, ui.setProperty, ui.moveNode and ui.removeNode. Operations.cs:333 is setProperty, and Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:253-260 upserts value_json, so a JSON null is stored as a present property. Read.cs:347-355 reads it back as present. Bindings.cs:190-200 tests ContainsKey(subtitleFieldId), gets a null field and raises NUI341 with the hint 'or remove subtitleFieldId'. Bindings.cs:105-110 (endDateFieldId) and ComposableSurfaces.cs:834 (opens, NUI313) give the same 'remove' advice, and I found no DELETE of a UI property and no ui.removeProperty anywhere in src or docs. Compensation.cs:512-516 refuses a setProperty that had no prior value. The gap is real, but a node can be removed and re-added, so P2.
- **Correction:** ADR-0004 (line 1682) lists the canonical UI operations with 'such as', so a new ui.removeProperty is not barred by the ADR. Some properties have a default value to reset to (opens to 'open', limit, scope), so the stuck cases are the ones with no default: visibleWhen, subtitleFieldId, accentFieldId, endDateFieldId and the ordering properties. SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:545-548 already stops History offering Compensate for a first-time property, so the undo refusal shows up as a missing button rather than an error. SemanticDiff.cs already narrates a null description as clearing it, which is a precedent for the 'null means delete' fix.

### ESM-14 — Several review lines do not say what they act on: retire, rename, retired-field backfill, choice metadata and node removal

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:128`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:136`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:137`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:127`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:130`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:169`
- **What:** setRetired renders 'Retire field; retain stored data.' or 'Retire record type; ...' with no name; renameEntity and renameField render 'Rename record type to X.' and 'Rename field to X.' without the current name or record type (Resolve has already overwritten the old name); backfillRetiredField renders 'Fill the explicitly selected retained field value.'; setChoiceMetadata never names the field; removeUiNode says 'Remove the tab group "X" from its surface.' without saying its sections and bindings go with it. - **Failure:** In a file with Notes on both Task and Client, a proposal that retires Client's Notes and renames Task's Notes reads 'Retire field; retain stored data.' and 'Rename field to Comments.'; the person cannot tell at the accept gate which field is retired or renamed.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-diff.ps1 case 4 -> '[setRetired] Retire field; retain stored data.' / '[renameField] Rename field to Comments.' / '[setRetired] Retire record type; retain stored data.' / '[setChoiceMetadata] Name choice Closed, mark it available and give it no colour; preserve its stored ID.'
- **Fix and guard:** Name the subject with FieldName and EntityName read from the active definition ('Retire Notes on Client; keep its stored data.', 'Rename Notes on Task to Comments.', 'Fill Notes on record ...', 'Rename Stage's option done to Closed'), and state how many nodes a removal takes with it. Guard: SemanticDiff tests asserting the field and record type names appear; falsify by reverting one summary.

Neighbouring lines such as setFieldRequired (:126) and configureReference already name fields and record types through FieldName and EntityName, so the information is at hand. view-proposal.ts:27 and view-agent.ts:359 render only entry.summary and reversibilityLabel, never SemanticIds, so a proposal that retires or renames several same-named fields cannot be told apart at the accept gate. Retiring hides data from the app, so this is more than polish.
- **Correction:** The removeUiNode sub-point is weak: :169 already names the node through NodeDescription (SemanticDiffSummaryTests.cs:704 shows 'Remove the record list "Open work"...'). Only the cascade to child sections and bindings is unstated. The rest of the finding stands. The fix needs the old display name captured from the active snapshot in Resolve before the rename overwrites it.

### GDN-02 — The wheel over the Overview's graph and a note's local graph zooms the drawing instead of scrolling the page

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/graph.js:64`, `extensions/garden/garden.css:235`, `extensions/garden/garden.css:264`, `extensions/garden/garden.css:466`
- **What:** createGraph() installs d3.zoom with its default filter (graph.js:64-71), which takes every wheel event and calls preventDefault until the scale extent [0.1, 8] is reached; the same drawing is the local graph inside the scrolling #note (full page width, clamp(360px, 60vh, 680px) tall, css:235) and the Overview's hero graph (at least 64vh tall in a scrolling body, css:466). .graph-host also sets touch-action: none (css:264), so a swipe over it does not scroll either.
- **Failure:** Reading a note with its local graph open, the person scrolls back up with the pointer over the graph: the page stays put and the graph zooms in 3.5 times (and stops refitting itself, since `arranged` is now true). On the Overview, the screen the file opens on, scrolling down to the pinned cards with the pointer over the graph zooms the graph out instead.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge, fixture broker (probe-browser.js step C): three wheel-up ticks over the local graph of Start here -> {"graphBox":{"w":1104,"h":540},"scrollTopBefore":438,"scrollTopAfter":438,"transformBefore":"translate(-8.99,1.04) scale(1)","transformAfter":"translate(-31.32,178.39) scale(3.48)"}
- **Fix and guard:** Give the inline drawings (compact and the Overview) a zoom.filter that zooms on the wheel only with Ctrl (or a pinch, or after the person clicks into the graph) and lets a plain wheel scroll the page; keep the full-screen Graph screen as it is; set touch-action: pan-y on inline hosts. Guard: a lane step that wheels over the local graph and the Overview graph and asserts the scroll container moved and the viewport transform did not.
- **Verifier:** extensions/garden/graph.js:64-71 builds d3.zoom().scaleExtent([0.1,8]) with no .filter, so d3's default wheel handler calls preventDefault whenever the scale would change; createGraph is the same code for the Graph screen (graphscreen.js:55), the Overview hero (home.js:83) and the compact local graph (workspace.js:670). garden.css:264 sets touch-action:none on .graph-host, and the hosts are tall (css:235 clamp(360px,60vh,680px); css:466 min-height clamp(380px,64vh,640px)) inside scrolling containers. Documented wheel-zoom (help/05-the-graph.md, garden.md:101, Gate-Garden.mjs:601) is described for the Graph screen only; the local graph is described as 'stretched, not zoomed' (graph.js:8, garden.md), so zooming it by wheel is an unintended side effect. The reviewer's executed probe (scrollTop 438 -> 438, scale 1 -> 3.48) matches the code.
- **Correction:** Fix scope: only the inline drawings (compact and the Overview) need a Ctrl/pinch-gated zoom.filter and touch-action:pan-y; the Graph screen's plain-wheel zoom is documented behaviour and the gate asserts it, so it must stay. Priority kept at P2 as a high-frequency friction on the landing screen with an obvious workaround (move the pointer off the graph); no data impact.

### GGV-02 — Dependency graph, Systems Lens and Work dependencies throw away the person's pan and zoom on every re-read

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:124`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:379`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:734`
- **What:** render() (graph, lens) and relayout() (work-dependencies) always end in fit(); refit();, so every `changes` event, which arrives for any commit to the file, recomputes scale and offset from the whole drawing. ui.openRecord opens the record beside the view, which keeps running, so editing the record the view just opened is itself a re-read; in Work dependencies running a record command from the view schedules one too.
- **Failure:** A person zooms into one corner of a 200-item plan, selects an item (it opens beside the graph), changes its status or runs Start work from the view: a quarter of a second later the graph snaps back to the fitted whole-plan view at an unreadable scale, and they have to find and zoom into their place again after every edit.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-graphs.mjs (three zoom-in clicks, then window.__emit('changes')) -> dependency-graph: transform zoomed=translate(-324.9 -146.3) scale(1.281) \| after a changes event=translate(43 27.8) scale(0.656); systems-lens: scale(0.4796) -> scale(0.2455); work-dependencies: scale(1.396) -> scale(0.715).
- **Fix and guard:** Fit only on the first render and when the person asks (Fit, Ctrl 0, a resize before they have moved); on a re-read keep scale and offset, and in Work dependencies, whose ELK layout can move items, keep the selected or focused item at the same screen position. Guard: in each Review lane zoom in, emit changes, and assert #drawing's transform is unchanged; falsify by restoring the unconditional fit().
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. graph.js:124 (render ends textView(); fit(); refit();), lens.js:379 (paint(); fit(); refit();) and work-dependencies/view.js:734 (relayout ends fit(); refit();) recompute scale and offset unconditionally. Every file commit raises a changes event (docs/contracts/custom-views.md:1068, 'when anything commits to the open file'), which schedule() turns into read() then render(), and in Work dependencies act() also calls schedule() at view.js:601. ui.openRecord opens the record beside a view that keeps running (custom-view-authoring.md:456-458), so editing it re-reads the view. No README or ADR documents a re-fit on re-read as intended; the fit-on-render comments are about the first open. The reviewer's probe numbers are consistent with the code.
- **Correction:** Work dependencies re-layouts with ELK on re-read, so some re-fit is defensible there, but keeping scale and offset unless the extent changes is still the better behaviour. Priority is a P2/P3 borderline: friction with an easy workaround, but it hits every edit and every agent write.

### MAA-05 — ui.moveNode without parentNodeId moves the node to the root instead of keeping its parent

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `mcp-authoring-agent`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:113`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:191`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.Anchors.cs:147`
- **What:** The published table lists parentNodeId as optional on ui.moveNode. Its summary reads 'Move a node to another parent or place on the same surface: position as on ui.addNode'. The Engine binds it with OptionalString, so an omitted key is null, and MoveUiNodeOperation treats null as 'make it a root' (SemanticDiff.MoveSummary renders 'Move X to position N of its surface'). The anchor tracker does the same (Place sets ParentNodeId = Text(payload,'parentNodeId')). Nothing says that omitting the key reparents the node.
- **Failure:** An agent reorders a field binding inside a list with ui.moveNode {surfaceId:'taskAll', nodeId:'taskAllTitle', position:3}, leaving the parent unchanged. Validation fails on a root-kind diagnostic about a fieldBinding that cannot be a root, which the agent did not intend. For a kind that may also be a root, such as a recordCommand nested in a record page, the change validates and silently pulls the button out of the page into a standalone root.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** At the MCP boundary, fill an omitted parentNodeId on ui.moveNode with the node's current parent, from the same definition snapshot the anchor resolver reads. Keep an explicit null as 'move to the root', and say so in the operation summary. Guard: a test that moves a child by position with no parentNodeId and requires its parent to be unchanged in nendo://application/surfaces after acceptance.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:113-114 lists parentNodeId as optional on ui.moveNode with no statement of what omission means. CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:191-196 binds it with OptionalString, MoveUiNodeOperation (Operations.cs:347-362) normalises null to no parent, and ExecuteMoveUiNodeAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:290-325) runs UPDATE ... SET parent_node_id = @parentNodeId with DBNull, so an omitted key reparents the node to the root. The anchor tracker does the same (Anchors.cs:147), and no MCP-boundary code fills the current parent (anchors set it from the anchor, but a plain position move does not). A kind that cannot be a root is refused by NUI012 'cannot be a surface root' (NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:329); a root-capable kind such as a section is moved out of its page or tab group, which the diff states (SemanticDiff.cs:902-910: 'no longer a tab'). At Unattended the agent can accept its own proposal with no one reading that line. No document defines this semantics (semantic-surfaces.md:1283-1290 only covers anchors).
- **Correction:** P2 rather than higher: validation catches leaf kinds, a person reviews the move at lower levels, and sending parentNodeId is a one-key workaround. The fix is as proposed (fill the node's current parent from the definition snapshot when the key is absent; keep an explicit null as 'make it a root') or, at minimum, state in the ui.moveNode summary that an omitted parentNodeId means root.

### R2LAT-05 — Decimal entry refuses the comma that the Danish, German and French numpad and the decimal touch keypad type, although the Studio contract promises a locale-aware numeric editor; Integer fields offer a decimal keypad they then refuse

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/scalars.ts:24`, `docs/contracts/studio.md:142`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:460`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:792`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:489`
- **What:** parseScalar accepts a decimal only as /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ (scalars.ts:24) and refuses anything else with 'Enter a decimal using a dot, without separators or an exponent.' The record form, the Studio grid (view-data.ts:792) and the Studio filter Value box (view-data.ts:489) all go through it. docs/contracts/studio.md:142 maps integer/decimal to a 'locale-aware numeric editor', so the code violates the contract that governs Studio. On Danish, German, French and most continental layouts the numpad's decimal key types ',', and record-markup.ts:460 gives Decimal inputs inputmode="decimal", whose touch keypad also offers the locale's ',' as its only separator, so a number entered with either keypad is always refused. record-markup.ts:460 gives Integer fields inputmode="decimal" too, so a touch keyboard offers a separator that an Integer then refuses ('Enter a whole number without separators.').
- **Failure:** The owner types 12,5 on the numpad into a Decimal field or the Studio grid and gets a refusal. The value has to be retyped with the main keyboard's '.', on every entry. On a Windows tablet, an Integer field shows a decimal keypad.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-scalars.mjs on the bundled scalars.ts -> Decimal "12.5" -> {"$nendoNumber":"12.5"}; Decimal "12,5" -> refused: Enter a decimal using a dot, without separators or an exponent.
- **Fix and guard:** Accept a single ',' as the decimal separator when the text has no '.' and the comma is not followed by exactly three digits (or when the WebView2 locale's decimal separator is ','), and normalise it to '.' before building the exact lexeme. Keep refusing grouping. Give Integer fields inputmode="numeric". Guard: scalars.test cases '12,5' -> 12.5, '1,234' still refused for Decimal and '1.5' refused for Integer, plus a record-markup test asserting inputmode="numeric" on an Integer input.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. parseScalar('Decimal') accepts only /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ and otherwise throws 'Enter a decimal using a dot, without separators or an exponent.' (scalars.ts:24); the only Decimal test case in scalars.test.mjs covers dot input and overflow, none a comma. The record form (record-form.ts:136), the Studio grid cell commit (view-data.ts:792) and the Studio filter Value box (view-data.ts:489) all go through parseScalar, so '12,5' is refused in every Studio entry path. docs/contracts/studio.md:142 promises a 'locale-aware numeric editor' for integer/decimal, which the code does not provide, and scalars.md says nothing that mandates dot-only entry from the person (the dot is the wire lexeme, not the typed form). record-markup.ts:459-460 gives Integer and Decimal alike inputmode="decimal", so an Integer field offers a decimal keypad and then refuses a separator. On a Danish or German layout the numpad decimal key types ',', and the owner is Danish, so this is a recurring entry refusal. The error text names the workaround (type a dot on the main keyboard), which keeps it at P2 rather than higher.
- **Correction:** The touch-keypad separator claim for inputmode="decimal" is platform-dependent and unverified in the Windows host; the numpad comma on Danish/German/French layouts is the solid half of the scenario. The Integer inputmode="numeric" point is a trivial, correct side fix.

### R2RM-02 — History offers Compensate on every past definition change, but the Engine reverses one only while it is the file's latest definition revision; the others are refused with the agent-facing 'Use expectedDefinitionRevision' text

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `r2-reversibility-matrix`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:553`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:529`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Evolution.cs:11`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Evolution.cs:66`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Retirement.cs:192`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Behaviour.cs:297`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:185`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionCompensation.cs:23`
- **What:** Every single-operation definition inverse except ui.setProperty and the package operations takes the evidence's appliedDefinitionRevision as its expected revision: retirement (Retirement.cs:192), rename (Evolution.cs:66), choice metadata, required, behaviour (Behaviour.cs:297), purpose, look, new-file label, kept default, hierarchy, link rule, unique, presentation and sequence. Each Execute* refuses when manifest.DefinitionRevision differs, with DefinitionVersionConflict (Evolution.cs:11): 'This operation expected definition revision {expected}; the file is at {actual}. Use expectedDefinitionRevision {actual} for this operation. Within one change set the definition revision increases by one for each definition-lane mutation that precedes it. Review a fresh proposal.' The Workbench shows the message as it is (format.ts messageFor). The custom-view removal inverse refuses the same way (ExtensionCompensation.cs:23). The guard itself is deliberate: Behaviour.cs:280-286 says 'a later definition change therefore conflicts loudly', and relationships.md:217 says a type's keep default is 'reversed from History while it is the latest definition change'. The defects are the offer and the refusal text. History's eligibility SQL says in its own comment (ReadQueries.cs:545-552) that the flag must match what CreateCompensationMutationAsync actually reverses, because 'A class-based flag offered a Compensate button the engine refused'. It reads ui.setProperty's evidence for exactly that reason. Yet it never compares r.definition_revision_after with the manifest it has already read at :529, so it offers every one of these revisions. A compensation is itself a Definition-lane revision (SqliteNendoStore.cs:185 adds one), so after the latest change is undone the one before it is refused as well. application.buildSearchIndex is also Definition lane (Search.cs:23, as ADR-0028 requires), so pressing Build search index blocks every earlier definition undo. Probe: History's eligibility SQL, copied verbatim from the source at HEAD and run on an in-memory SQLite DB with five hand-made revisions and manifest definition revision 9, printed "R3-retire-field lane=Definition defAfter=8 canRequestCompensation=1 <- Engine inverse expects definition revision 8; file is at 9" and "R1-rename-field lane=Definition defAfter=6 canRequestCompensation=1 <- Engine inverse expects definition revision 6; file is at 9".
- **Failure:** The person renames field Status to State in Studio (R1, definition revision 6), then retires an unused field (R2, revision 7). The rename was a mistake. History shows Compensate on R1, and pressing it shows 'This operation expected definition revision 6; the file is at 7. Use expectedDefinitionRevision 7 for this operation... Review a fresh proposal.' The person can do nothing with that sentence. Undoing in last-first order fails too: Compensate on R2 succeeds and moves the file to revision 8, R1 is still refused, and R2's compensation cannot itself be compensated. A search-index build in between has the same effect. The only remedy is to author the old state again by hand, and History never says so.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_history_flag.py (eligibility SQL extracted from SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs, in-memory SQLite, manifest definition revision 9) -> "R1-rename-field lane=Definition defAfter=6 canRequestCompensation=1 <- Engine inverse expects definition revision 6; file is at 9"; the Engine refusal is traced from source (Evolution.cs:11-19 and 66).
- **Fix and guard:** In the eligibility SQL, for single-operation Definition-lane revisions of the guarded types, also require r.definition_revision_after = the manifest's definition revision (already read at :529). In the compensation path, catch definition-version-conflict and say something a person can act on: 'Only the latest structure change can be compensated; <description> was changed after it.' If walk-back is wanted, replace the whole-revision guard with a subject guard, as ui.setProperty and the package inverses already have: the field is still retired, the name is still the applied name, the definition body is still the one installed. Guard: a flag test that, for every eligible definition type, applies a later definition revision and asserts CanRequestCompensation equals the compensation outcome. Falsify by removing the new condition.
- **Verifier:** Traced. The History eligibility SQL (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:553-583) offers any single-operation revision whose type is in the list (schema.setRetired, renameEntity/renameField, setChoiceMetadata, behaviour.*, etc.) and never compares r.definition_revision_after with the manifest it already read at :529. The inverses carry appliedDefinitionRevision as the expected revision (Evolution.cs:66-69, Retirement.cs:192), and each Execute* throws DefinitionVersionConflict when manifest.DefinitionRevision differs (Evolution.cs:41-42 and the other sites). A compensation is itself a Definition-lane revision (SqliteNendoStore.cs:185 adds 1), and application.buildSearchIndex is Definition lane (Search.cs:23), so only the very latest definition change can ever be compensated. The refusal is tested as intended (SchemaRenameTests.cs:44, ChoiceEvolutionTests.cs:57) but no test checks the History flag against it. The message reaches the person unchanged (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:455-457, actions.ts runMutation -> messageFor) as 'Use expectedDefinitionRevision N ... Review a fresh proposal.', which is agent-facing text. The ReadQueries.cs:545-552 comment shows the flag is meant to match what the Engine reverses, and Help (help-concepts.ts:177) says Compensate is offered 'when the class and the current state allow it'. The Help line is the strongest point against the code. Mitigations: the latest-only guard is deliberate and documented (relationships.md:217, NewFileTests.cs:104), nothing is written, and the button carries the hedge 'Current state is checked when requested' (view-history.ts:20). So this is a UX mismatch, not a safety defect. P2 is defensible because the button is dead for most definition entries on the History page, and the workaround is to re-author by hand.
- **Correction:** Priority could reasonably be P3 given the documented latest-only rule and the 'checked when requested' hedge. The proposed fix (a definition_revision_after = manifest condition in the SQL, plus a person-readable refusal) is sound.

### R2SMA-08 — Double-clicking a file Nendo would open read-only (marked read-only, needing recovery or an upgrade) ends on the generic recovery panel with no file open

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `r2-safe-mode-and-file-versions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:476`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:483`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:155`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:223`
- **What:** InitializeStartupSessionAsync calls _session.OpenAsync(path), which always opens writable (DesktopSessionController.cs:155). For any file whose inspection forbids writing (file-read-only, invalid-surface, upgrade-required, surface-version-mismatch, replacement-pending...) OpenCoreAsync throws NendoFileOpenException (Open.cs:223-226), and the startup catch shows 'The requested file could not be opened. Use Open file or backup to inspect it and choose recovery actions.' with the inspection's reason discarded and RecoverySession 'No file is open', so Upgrade, Export readable data and Inspect again are disabled. The interactive open (OpenNativeAssessmentAsync) offers 'Inspect read-only' for the same file. DSH-01 is the same startup path for synced-folder and known-instance files; this is every file in a read-only or safe-mode state.
- **Failure:** A person double-clicks an older file that needs an upgrade, or a file copied from a read-only share: Nendo starts on 'Studio recovery' saying the file could not be opened, without the reason, and they must find the same file again with 'Open file or backup' before the Upgrade button becomes available.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** At startup, assess the file first and open read-only when the inspection grants ReadData but not write authority (the same rule OpenNativeAssessmentAsync applies), showing the findings; keep the recovery panel for Rejected files and put the first finding's message in RecoveryReason. Guard: a Desktop test that starts the page path (or DesktopSessionController's startup entry) with a read-only-attribute fixture and asserts a readOnly session with the file-read-only finding.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. MainPage.xaml.cs:476 calls _session.OpenAsync(path) for the default startup mode; DesktopSessionController.cs:155 hard-codes readOnly:false. For a file whose inspection forbids writing (Inspection.cs:368-371 file-read-only, :361 upgrade-required, any other finding sets recovery at :560 so CanAcquireWriteAuthority is false at :567) NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:223-226 throws NendoFileOpenException. The catch at MainPage.xaml.cs:481-484 discards it and shows the fixed sentence; RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync then reads an empty session (DesktopRecoveryPresentation.cs:9 'No file is open') so Upgrade/Export/Inspect stay disabled (FileActions.cs:83-86). The interactive path OpenNativeAssessmentAsync (FileActions.cs:195-213) offers 'Inspect read-only' for the same file. App.xaml.cs:29 only hands off files another window owns. No test covers a startup open of such a file. Workaround exists (Open file or backup), same as the already-recorded DSH-01, so P2 is consistent.
- **Correction:** Locations and evidence are accurate. This is the same startup catch and the same fix as DSH-01 (FIXES.md, which already proposes running the interactive open flow with its read-only fallback for the startup path); the new part is only the extra triggers (file-read-only, upgrade-required, recovery findings). Fix both together. Scope note: not every recovery-required file reaches this path with a useful read-only open, but any file with ReadData true does at the interactive path.

### TBI-03 — Upgrading over Nendo running in the tray (the default close action) fails after extraction with a generic 'Close Nendo' box and quits, so the installer must be rerun; the owner's setup log holds 10 such refusals

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:508`, `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:81`, `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:127`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopShellStore.cs:26`
- **What:** CloseAction defaults to 'tray', so clicking X leaves Nendo.Desktop running. The NSIS section extracts the whole payload, writes the uninstaller and only then runs setup. Assert-Closed throws 'Close Nendo before installing or uninstalling, then run setup again.' The installer shows MB_OK 'Nendo could not be installed. Close Nendo and check the setup details.' and then Quit. There is no running-instance check in .onInit, no Retry, and no mention of the notification area. The same fixed text is shown for every setup failure, including 'Payload differs', 'Insufficient staging space', 'Previous payload contains unrecognized files' and 'Another Nendo setup is running'.
- **Failure:** A person closes the Nendo window, runs the new installer, waits through extraction, and is told to close Nendo, which they believe they did. They must find the tray icon, quit, and start the installer again from scratch.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: grep 'Setup failed: Close Nendo' %TEMP%\Nendo-Setup.log -> 10 matches. Each is followed by a fresh run, e.g. '2026-09-26 10:11:48 Setup failed: Close Nendo before installing or uninstalling, then run setup again.' then '2026-09-26 10:12:05 Checking the new files.', and '2026-10-06 04:25:24 Setup failed: Close Nendo ...' then '2026-10-06 04:25:37 Checking the new files.'
- **Fix and guard:** In .onInit, detect a Nendo.Desktop process under $INSTDIR before extracting and loop on MB_RETRYCANCEL with text naming the tray icon's Quit command. Better still, ask the running instance to exit. Make setup's refusal say that Nendo is still running in the notification area. Show setup's own failure sentence instead of the fixed 'Close Nendo' text. Guard: a setup test asserting the refusal text names the notification area. The NSIS loop is coverable only by the clean-user lane.
- **Verifier:** DesktopShellStore.cs:26 defaults CloseAction to 'tray', and site getting-started.md:74 documents that closing the window leaves Nendo in the notification area. Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:38-50 .onInit has no running-instance check, and the Install section extracts the whole payload (60-67) before calling setup. Assert-Closed (Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:508-516, called at 568) then throws, and the NSIS box at Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:83 is the same fixed 'Close Nendo and check the setup details' text for every failure, with no Retry and no mention of the tray. The owner's %TEMP%\Nendo-Setup.log shows 8 'Setup failed: Close Nendo before installing...' lines (26 Sep to 9 Oct), each followed within seconds to minutes by a fresh 'Checking the new files.' run. No doc tells a person to Exit Nendo from the tray before upgrading. The refusal is a safe interlock, so this is UX friction with a workaround (Exit Nendo, rerun).
- **Correction:** The log has 8 'Setup failed: Close Nendo' refusals, not 10: the reviewer's 10 counts 'Close Nendo' and includes two lines (8-9) of a raw PowerShell error dump. The setup details list does print the specific sentence ('Close Nendo before installing or uninstalling, then run setup again.') via nsExec::ExecToLog, so the user is not wholly uninformed; the gap is the missing tray hint and the check after extraction. P3 is defensible.

### UIK-01 — Agent page's 3-second poll rebuilds the whole page even when nothing changed: selections are wiped, alerts re-inserted, and dialog and error focus lost

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard` · also reported as WAU-07

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:770`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:795`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:245`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:98`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:153`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:447`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/confirm-dialog.ts:8`
- **What:** The interval in main.ts runs `refreshAgentStatus().then(rerender)` every 3 s whenever view==='agent', nothing is in flight and focus is not inside .agent-connection/.agent-launch. Nothing compares the new status with the one on screen, so renderAgent always replaces content.innerHTML. rerender then calls restoreOutcome (shell.ts:98-113), which draws the retained outcome into the brand-new .message-slot with role alert or status. focusedControl (view-agent.ts:153-164) restores focus only for controls inside content, and not for the focused error slot, which has no id. setAgentMode (view-agent.ts:447-453) awaits confirmUnattended before it sets actionInFlight, so the poll keeps rebuilding the page under the open modal. When the native dialog closes, it tries to give focus back to a rung the poll has already replaced.
- **Failure:** (1) On Connect, a person drag-selects the address `http://127.0.0.1:41763/mcp` (or the server name) to paste it into a client config. Within 3 s the selection is gone. (2) An error or an outcome such as 'Refine Idea workflow accepted.' is re-inserted as a new role=alert or role=status element every 3 s, so a screen reader repeats it until the person presses a key. An outcome repeats until the next action. (3) After showError focuses the message slot, the next poll drops focus to <body>. (4) A keyboard user who reads the Unattended dialog for more than 3 s, then cancels or confirms, lands on <body>.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over CDP against http://127.0.0.1:5173/?preview=1 (p25, p03, p19, p21) -> "whole-page rebuilds in 9.2 s with an unchanged status: 3"; "selected: http://127.0.0.1:41763/mcp" then "selection lost after ms: 2951"; "role=alert slots inserted in 9.5 s with nobody touching the page: 4612 role=alert hidden=false :: Agent access could not be changed. / 7616 role=alert ... / 10617 role=alert ..."; "focus after showError: div.message-slot" -> "focus after one poll: body"; "button still in page after 4 s with the dialog open: false", "Cancel after 4 s -> focus: body", "Confirm after 4 s -> mode unattended focus: body".
- **Fix and guard:** Redraw only when the status (and Launch's facts) differ from what was last drawn, for example by comparing a JSON digest. Hold the poll while a dialog is open (the interactionInProgress() dialog test) and while a non-collapsed selection lies inside #studio-content. In restoreOutcome, keep the existing slot node when its message is unchanged. Guard: in the agent headless lane, (a) count .agent-page insertions over 9 s with a fixed status and expect 0; (b) select #agent-endpoint, wait 3.5 s and expect the same selection text; (c) open the Unattended dialog, wait 4 s, press Escape and expect activeElement to be [data-agent-mode="unattended"].
- **Verifier:** main.ts:769-797 runs refreshAgentStatus().then(rerender) every 3 s while view==='agent', holding only for actionInFlight or focus inside .agent-connection/.agent-launch; nothing compares the new status with what is drawn, so renderAgent (view-agent.ts:245 onward) always does content.innerHTML = ..., which destroys any selection and the .message-slot. rerender then calls restoreOutcome (shell.ts:98-106), which re-draws the retained outcome into the new slot with role alert/status and unhides it (shell.ts:109-113). focusedControl (view-agent.ts:153-164) cannot restore focus that sat on the slot (no id) or on the dialog. setAgentMode awaits confirmUnattended (view-agent.ts:447) before setting actionInFlight and the poll has no dialog[open] check, so the rung that opened the modal is replaced; confirm-dialog.ts:8-21 then has no live opener to return focus to. shell.ts:373 interactionInProgress already holds on dialog[open] but this poll does not use it, and its own doc comment says the rule applied to the Agent page poll, so the code has drifted from the stated rule. A page rebuild every 3 s is a known, commented design, but its side effects are not a recorded trade-off.
- **Correction:** Scope scenario (1): the poll is already held while focus is on a control inside the Connect or Launch panels (main.ts:771), so a selection is lost only once the press on the text has moved focus to <body>. Scenario (2): an error is cleared by the next pointerdown or keydown (shell.ts:545-551), so its repeat lasts only until the person touches the page; a 'done' outcome stays until the next action or view change. The AT repetition rests on DOM insertions, not an NVDA or JAWS run.

### UIK-07 — Use screen Filter: the first arrow key in a Filter select applies that value, closes the menu, re-reads the screen and drops focus

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:40`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:49`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/quick-filter.ts:60`
- **What:** Each [data-quick-filter] select applies the pick on 'change', sets openSurfaceId = null, and reopen() re-reads the window and rerenders. The menu is drawn closed and the select is gone. An arrow key on a closed select fires change on Windows.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user opens Filter on 'All ideas', Tabs to Status and presses ArrowDown to look at the choices. 'Status: Idea' is applied at once, the menu closes, focus goes to <body>, and the list shows an empty 'No Idea records yet'. Each further look means reopening the menu.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p12 in headless Edge -> "filter open: true", "focus: select AnyIdeaExploringTryingPausedDoneNot set", then "value before \"\" \| after ArrowDown: menu open: false \| focus: body"; screenshot 16-filter-after-arrow.png shows the pill 'Showing Status: Idea'.
- **Fix and guard:** Apply the pick on Enter or blur, or keep the menu open and put focus back on the same select after the reread. Guard: a journey pressing ArrowDown on [data-quick-filter] that expects the details still open, activeElement still the select, and no reread until Enter.
- **Verifier:** quick-filter.ts:40-51 applies the pick on every select 'change', sets openSurfaceId = null and calls reopen(), which rerenders the whole Use page (shell.ts rerender -> renderer). Nothing in quick-filter.ts or view-use.ts restores focus to the Filter summary (the only focus code in view-use.ts is the surface picker at lines 200-209), so focus drops to <body>. Chromium on Windows (WebView2) fires change on the first ArrowUp/ArrowDown of a closed select, so a keyboard user browsing the options applies the first one, loses the menu and focus. No ADR or contract mandates it; the 'menu closes after a pick' comment is about mouse picks. Falls short of P1 because the filter is a reversible view narrowing and Alt+Down or type-ahead gives a commit-free path.
- **Correction:** Focus loss happens after any Filter pick, mouse or keyboard (Tab then restarts from the document start), not only after an arrow key; the fix should restore focus to the Filter summary after reopen() as well as stop committing on arrows.

### UIS-03 — The redraw hold ignores the breadcrumb pickers, so an automatic redraw closes the open View picker or record-type list under the pointer

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data` · also reported as WCS-13

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:373`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:423`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/place-pickers.ts:44`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-use.ts:167`
- **What:** Since W-092 the View picker (details.surface-picker) and the record-type select live in #place-pickers, in the header and outside #studio-content. interactionInProgress() looks only for content.querySelector('details[open]…'), and treats a focused select as interaction only if content contains it (shell.ts:380-385). The pointerdown/keydown/focusin quiet-window listeners are attached to content only (shell.ts:423-433). So holdingThePage() is false while a picker is open. Every redraw then runs drawPlacePickers, which replaces slot.innerHTML (place-pickers.ts:44) with markup that is never open.
- **Failure:** On a Use board, a person opens the View picker. An agent writes through MCP, or a tile, relation or overview chase lands. followTheFile or the chase calls rerender, the picker snaps shut, and the click lands on the surface underneath. A native record-type select whose list is open is replaced the same way. The shell's own comment names this failure mode, 'the picker closes under the pointer and the click lands on nothing'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p23-hold.mjs -> 'view picker open: true', 'interactionInProgress with the view picker open: false', 'holdingThePage with the view picker open: false', 'view picker open after an automatic redraw: false'; same probe with the Filter menu (inside content) -> 'interactionInProgress: true'.
- **Fix and guard:** Make the hold look at #place-pickers too. Check document.querySelector('#place-pickers details[open]') and a focused control inside #place-pickers, and register the quiet-window listeners on the header as well as on content. Guard: a node or gate test that opens .surface-picker and asserts interactionInProgress() is true. Falsify it by removing the new selector.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. shell.ts:151 defines content as #studio-content; index.html:97 puts #place-pickers in the header, outside it. interactionInProgress (shell.ts:373-386) checks content.querySelector('details[open]...') and content.contains(focused), and the pointerdown/keydown/focusin/scroll quiet-window listeners are attached to content only (shell.ts:423-433), so an open View picker (details.surface-picker, surface-markup.ts:64) or record-type select never counts as a hold. holdingThePage (draft-guard.ts:47-48) is that plus draft state. The automatic redraws all gate on it: followTheFile (main.ts:708-724, triggered by client.onFileChanged, i.e. an agent write), surfaceChase and relationChase (view-use.ts:270-276). Their rerender calls renderUse, which calls drawPlacePickers (view-use.ts:167, place-pickers.ts:44) and does slot.innerHTML = markup; surfaceSelectorMarkup emits no open attribute and no module state remembers the picker as open (unlike openSurfaceId for Filter, quick-filter.ts:15), so the picker snaps shut. scroll-restore.test.mjs:26 even says the redraw 'has already closed' the picker options. The shell's own comment (shell.ts:361-368) names this failure mode. Impact is a picker that closes under the pointer when an agent writes or a tile read lands, with a re-open workaround, so P2 not P1.

### UIT-02 — Accepting a Structure proposal moves the person to Use, with no visible confirmation

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio` · also reported as UX-05

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:72`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:78`
- **What:** promoteProposal sets `state.view = fromView \|\| codeOnly ? state.proposalReturnView : state.proposal.previewApplications?.length ? 'use' : 'data'`. Any file with screens has previewApplications, so every Structure proposal lands on Use. The outcome then goes only to `announce()` (a visually hidden live region) unless a refresh notice or a landed view exists; showOutcome is not called.
- **Failure:** Structure -> Add field 'Effort points' -> Preview field -> Accept changes. The window jumps to Use 'All ideas', where the new field is on no screen, and nothing visible says the field was added. The person has to return to Structure to check whether it worked.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p05-accept.mjs (1440x900) -> after accept {"view":"All ideas","announcement":"Add Effort points field accepted."}; only element with the text is span.visually-hidden; screenshot ac-after-accept-1440-light.png shows no message
- **Fix and guard:** Return to `state.proposalReturnView` for Studio-prepared proposals (Structure, Surfaces, Data) and call showOutcome(outcome) as the landed-view path does. Guard: an SSR or gate check that after accepting from Structure the view is 'structure' and a visible outcome element contains '<title> accepted.'
- **Verifier:** view-proposal.ts:72 sets state.view = fromView\|\|codeOnly ? proposalReturnView : previewApplications?.length ? 'use' : 'data'. A Studio-prepared Add field proposal (view-structure.ts:209, return view 'structure') in any file with screens has previewApplications from the validated clone (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:136), so it lands on Use. The success path then calls only announce(outcome) (:79); showOutcome runs only when a landed view exists (:81, set by landAddedView) and refreshAfterOutcome returns null on success (actions.ts:96-104). announce writes to a visually hidden live region (shell.ts:588), and tools/Review-OutcomeRuntime.mjs:176 itself notes 'The announcement is a live region nobody sees'. The reviewer's screenshot ac-after-accept-1440-light.png shows All ideas with no message and the new field on no screen.
- **Correction:** The 'use' landing dates from the first public release (git log -L72) and was written for Start application recipes; nothing in the code or contracts says it is intended for field, rename or retire proposals. The fix is as given: return to proposalReturnView for Studio-prepared proposals and call showOutcome. Reproduced on the preview host, but the host-side inputs (previewApplications, no visible outcome) are identical in the real host.

### UIT-05 — Review lines for retiring and renaming don't say which field or record type they change

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:128`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:136`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:137`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:127`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:27`
- **What:** SetRetiredOperation reads "Retire field; retain stored data." or "Retire record type; …" without a name. RenameFieldOperation reads "Rename field to {new}." and RenameEntityOperation "Rename record type to {new}.", neither naming the old name. BackfillRetiredFieldOperation reads "Fill the explicitly selected retained field value." The surrounding code (FieldSummary's comment, setFieldRequired) shows that naming the field is the norm. view-proposal.ts renders these strings verbatim as 'What changes'.
- **Failure:** A custom view (ADR-0013 Phase 3) or an agent prepares 'Tidy the Idea type' with two schema.setRetired operations and one schema.renameField. The review reads 'Retire field; retain stored data.' twice and 'Rename field to Details.'. The person cannot tell which fields are retired or which one is renamed before accepting. Only Studio's own single-operation proposals are saved by their titles.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Use FieldName and EntityName in these summaries, for example "Retire Energy on Idea; its stored values stay." and "Rename Notes on Idea to Details." (take the old name from DiffNames before the change set renames it). Guard: SemanticDiffTests asserting that each summary contains the field's or type's current display name.
- **Verifier:** SemanticDiff.cs:128 prints 'Retire field; retain stored data.' / 'Retire record type; ...' with no name, :136-137 print 'Rename record type to X.' / 'Rename field to X.' without the old name or owning type, and :127 is a static sentence. Neighbouring lines (:126 setFieldRequired, :132 configureReference, :181 setField) name fields through FieldName/EntityName, so the data is at hand. view-proposal.ts:27 and view-agent.ts:359 render only entry.summary and the reversibility, never the SemanticIds the entry carries, so an agent proposal that retires two fields and renames one is three unnamed lines at the accept gate. Retiring hides data from the app, so a review that cannot say which field is a real review-quality gap. Studio's own single-operation proposals are partly rescued by their title, as the finding says.
- **Correction:** Fix detail: Resolve (SemanticDiff.cs:431-433) overwrites the active file's display name with the renamed one before summaries are built, so the old name is not in DiffNames as the finding suggests. Capture it in Resolve before the overwrite (or read it from the active snapshot), while Retire and Reactivate can already use FieldName/EntityName. No existing test pins these strings (grep found none), so changing them is safe.

### UX-03 — Every Data-grid save rebuilds the grid: keyboard focus drops to <body>, horizontal scroll returns to 0, and nothing visible says it saved

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` · also reported as WDV-06

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:794`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:77`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:115`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:74`
- **What:** commitGridEdit -> runMutation -> rerender() (actions.ts:77) -> main.render -> destroyGrid() (main.ts:115) and mountRecordGrid anew. Nothing restores the focused cell (headerFocusAfterDraw only covers headers, outlineFocus only the outline), and shell.ts:74's scrollPositions list has no AG Grid viewport, so .ag-center-cols-viewport and the body viewport start at 0. The success text '<Field> saved.' goes only to the hidden live region (actions.ts:78). Studio contract §5 requires keyboard focus, navigation, edit, commit and cancel behaviour and an explicit committed state.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user in Studio > Data presses Enter on Title, types, presses Enter: focus is on <body>, so ArrowDown does nothing and they must click back into the grid for every cell. A person editing a column scrolled to the right (Next action) sees the grid jump back to the left edge after each save, hiding the cell they just edited.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=1, Data -> keyboard edit of row 0 Title -> 'focused after: BODY row=-', 'after ArrowDown focus: BODY row=-', 'message slot: hidden', 'announcement: Title saved.'; scrolled the grid to scrollLeft 511, edited Next action -> 'scrollLeft after 0' (screenshot 10-after-scrolled-edit.png).
- **Fix and guard:** After a successful grid commit, update the row in place (gridApi.applyTransaction / setDataValue with the returned version) instead of a full rerender, or capture the focused cell and the viewport scroll before rerender and restore them with setFocusedCell/ensureColumnVisible after mountRecordGrid; flash a per-cell 'Saved' state. Guard: a browser lane that commits two cells in a row by keyboard and asserts document.activeElement is the next cell and the viewport scrollLeft is unchanged.

The only focus restoration in mountRecordGrid is headerFocusAfterDraw and the outline's setFocusedCell (view-data.ts:728-738), neither used by the flat table, and rerender()'s scrollPositions() (shell.ts:74-76) lists the content pane and surface scrollers but no AG Grid viewport, so the grid's own horizontal scroll resets. The success text goes only to announce() (actions.ts:78). Keyboard focus drops to <body> after every cell commit and a horizontally scrolled grid jumps to the left edge; docs/contracts/studio.md:78 asks for keyboard focus/commit behaviour. No ADR mandates the rebuild. Friction with a workaround (click back into the grid), so P2 not P1.
- **Correction:** Vertical scroll is preserved (the content pane is in scrollPositions), so only focus and the grid's horizontal scroll are lost. The 'nothing visible says it saved' part duplicates finding 4. The runMutation call is at view-data.ts:794, not the commitGridEdit line 768 only.

### UX-07 — History cannot tell a person what a change was: entries name no record or field, and 29 of 40 operation types show as raw identifiers

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` · also reported as WMX-12, UIT-07

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/history-markup.ts:10`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/format.ts:99`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-history.ts:20`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.cs:439`
- **What:** A record save's History title is the Engine's fixed 'Edit record fields' (NendoApplicationService.cs:439), a delete is 'Delete <Type>' (:373). 'View changes' draws operationDetailsMarkup, which shows only operationLabel(operationType) and the reversibility class and ignores canonicalJson, the payload that names the record and field (history-markup.ts:10). operationLabel maps 11 of the Engine's 40 operation types; the rest fall through to the identifier (format.ts:99-114). Help tells the person 'To restore a deleted record, open History. Find its Delete entry and click Compensate' (help.ts:85).
- **Failure:** After deleting three Ideas in a day, History shows three identical 'Delete Idea' entries whose details read 'Delete record · Compensatable with retained state': nothing says which one held 'Pocket field notes'. Renaming a field shows 'schema.renameField · Not compensatable'; a calculation change shows 'behaviour.setDefinition'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: bundled format.ts in node -> 'unlabelled 29 of 40 : application.buildSearchIndex, application.setLook, application.setPurpose, behaviour.removeDefinition, behaviour.setDefinition, data.backfillRetiredField, data.convertLegacyReference, data.moveRecord, extension.putFile, ... schema.renameField, schema.setFieldRequired, schema.setRetired, ui.moveNode, ui.removeNode'; History in headless Edge shows 'Edit record fields' with detail 'Set field · Compensatable with retained state'.
- **Fix and guard:** Label every operation type in operationLabel (plain words: 'Rename field', 'Make field required', 'Move record'), and in operationDetailsMarkup parse canonicalJson to name the field (from state.session.entities) and the record (label field read as holderNamed does), e.g. 'Set Notes on “A quieter weekly review”'. Guard: format.test.mjs iterating the Engine's operation-type list and failing on any label equal to its identifier; history-markup.test.mjs asserting a setField detail names its field.
- **Verifier:** Traced. A record save is submitted with the fixed description 'Edit record fields' (NendoApplicationService.cs:439) and a delete as $"Delete {entity.DisplayName}" (:373); view-history.ts:20 draws revision.description plus an operation count, and 'View changes' goes through operationDetailsMarkup (history-markup.ts:10), which prints only operationLabel(operationType) and reversibilityLabel and never reads the operation payload. operationLabel (format.ts:99-114) maps 11 types and returns the raw identifier for the rest; the Engine defines many more, e.g. schema.renameField (SchemaEvolutionOperations.cs:26), schema.setFieldRequired (FieldRequirementOperations.cs:13), ui.moveNode (Operations.cs:371), behaviour.setDefinition (BehaviourOperations.cs:36). So three deleted records produce three identical entries, and the Help recipe 'find its Delete entry and click Compensate' (help.ts:85) cannot say which. The roadmap lists no such limitation and no ADR/contract mandates it. History is the only path to compensate, so this materially limits it; the timestamp and origin are a workaround, hence P2.
- **Correction:** I confirmed the 11-label mapping and the existence of unlabelled types but did not count the Engine's operation types, so treat '29 of 40' as unverified. The record IDs and field names exist in the stored operation payload, so the fix (parse the payload in operationDetailsMarkup) is feasible as described.

### UX-12 — Escape, the inspector's × and 'Back to Data' close a record page with unsaved typing without asking; the refusal text even recommends it

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:540`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:40`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/draft-guard.ts:33`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/page-markup.ts:224`
- **What:** main.ts:540-553 turns Escape anywhere (also from inside a text field) into a click on the first [data-dismiss], which on a record page is the × (page-markup.ts:224, view-use.ts:135, :175) or 'Back to Data' (record-markup.ts:533); record-form.ts:40 wires those to close(), which re-renders and drops state.openDraft with no check of recordFormIsDirty. Every guarded move says 'Save your changes or close record details before …' (draft-guard.ts:33), offering 'close' as the alternative to saving without saying it discards.
- **Failure:** A person types two paragraphs into Notes and presses Escape to dismiss the browser's autocomplete or out of habit: the record page closes and the paragraphs are gone, with no prompt and nothing to undo.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=1, typed into the inspector's Notes then pressed Escape -> 'ESCAPE -> inspector open: false \| msg: none \| dialog: false'.
- **Fix and guard:** When recordFormIsDirty(), make close/Escape open confirmDialog('Discard your changes?', confirmLabel 'Discard', cancel keeps editing) and reword the refusal to 'Save or discard your changes before …'. Guard: a host-behaviour test that dirties the form, dispatches Escape and asserts a dialog is open and the textarea keeps its value.
- **Verifier:** main.ts:540-553: the Escape handler returns only for an open dialog or the file menu, does not look at the focused element, and clicks the first enabled [data-dismiss]. On a record page that is the inspector close button (page-markup.ts:224, view-use.ts:135,175) or 'Back to Data' (record-markup.ts:533). record-form.ts:40 wires #close-inspector/#cancel-create straight to the close callback; closeInspector (record-form.ts:178) and the Data callbacks (view-data.ts:517,526) call rerender() with no recordFormIsDirty() check, and main.ts:117 then sets state.openDraft = null. grep finds no discard confirmation anywhere for a dirty record form. draft-guard.ts:33 does say 'Save your changes or close record details before ...', offering close as the way out without saying it discards. Unsaved typed text is lost silently.
- **Correction:** Mitigating context: main.ts:521-525 states Escape deliberately mirrors the visible Back/Cancel button, and draft-guard.ts treats an explicit close as the discard route, so this is an acknowledged design, not an oversight; it is still a missing confirmation. The loss is unsaved typing only (nothing persisted), hence P2 not higher. Not re-run: the 'Executed' Edge reproduction.

### WDV-08 — After a record-version conflict, a record form with unsaved typing can never be saved; the only way out discards the typing

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views` · also reported as UX-11

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:127`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:170`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:85`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/draft-guard.ts:47`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:723`
- **What:** saveRecordChanges always sends the record.version captured when the form was drawn. On record-version-conflict (a confirmed rejection), runMutation keeps the draft and shows the host's text: 'Record <id> is version 7, not 6.' Nothing re-reads the record or offers a rebase. The file-follow chase and the relation chase wait on holdingThePage, which is true while recordFormIsDirty(), so the page is never refreshed under the draft. Every other move is refused by refuseWhileDirty; closing the record (closeInspector) is not, and silently drops the typing.
- **Failure:** The person is typing notes into a task while an agent or an automatic action updates the same task. Save fails with 'Record t-12 is version 7, not 6.' Every retry fails the same way, and the screen never catches up. To recover they must copy their text out, close the record, which loses the typing, reopen it and type again.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In saveRecordChanges, on record-version-conflict, re-read the record by ID, rebase the edited fields onto the new version and say which fields changed underneath, or offer 'Reload this record, keeping my changes'. Guard: a node test with a stand-in host that refuses the first data.setFields with record-version-conflict and asserts that the next save carries the new expectedRecordVersion and the draft's values; falsify by removing the rebase.
- **Verifier:** Traced. record-form.ts:127 saveRecordChanges sends expectedRecordVersion: record.version (line 170) where record is the object closed over when the form was wired (wireRecordForm line 33/97), so it never changes. The Engine throws record-version-conflict with 'Record X is version N, not M.' (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:491-496). That code is in the confirmed-rejection set (pending-mutations.ts:19-20), so runMutation keeps the draft (actions.ts:85-89) and shows the host's sentence; there is no restate callback, re-read or rebase on this path (unlike the board's target-version-conflict handler, view-use.ts:412-419). The `.then` at record-form.ts:128 clears editedFields only when nothing was sent, so the form stays dirty. draft-guard.ts:47-49 holdingThePage includes recordFormIsDirty(), and main.ts:719-723 passes it to the file-follow chase, so the page never catches up under the draft; every other move is refused by refuseWhileDirty (draft-guard.ts:30-34), while closeInspector (record-form.ts:178-183) calls leaveRecordContext and rerender with no dirty check, dropping the typing. So Save fails identically on every retry and the only exits are copying the text out or discarding it.
- **Correction:** The retain-draft behaviour is deliberate (write-failure.ts:25-39, write-failure.test.mjs:21-25), but its rationale there, 'the file did not move', does not hold for a version conflict, where another writer moved it; no accepted ADR or contract requires leaving the form without a recovery path. Realistic trigger is an agent or other MCP client writing the same record while the form is dirty. A workaround exists (copy the typing, close, reopen), hence P2.

### WMX-04 — Related lists show stored choice IDs and raw target record IDs instead of their labels

**P2** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:262`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:209`
- **What:** relatedListMarkup builds each row's text as valueDisplay(related.values[fieldId]) for every binding that is not calculated. It never calls choiceDisplay or reads related.referenceLabels, although RecordSnapshot carries referenceLabels. Every other surface goes through recordFieldDisplay (record-markup.ts:29-39), which resolves both choices and references.
- **Failure:** A Project page has a related list of Tasks bound to Status (single choice) and Owner (reference). The rows show 'in_progress' and the owner's raw record ID, where the Tasks list shows 'In progress' and 'Ada Lovelace'. After a choice label is renamed in Edit choices, the rows keep showing the old text, because a choice created in Studio uses its original text as its ID. When the first binding is a choice or a reference, the row's accessible name ('Open ...') uses the same raw text.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Compute each row's text with recordFieldDisplay(recordPlanOf(related), fieldId, relatedDerived), which already handles choices, references and calculations. Guard: move the computation into an exported relatedRowDisplays() and test that a related item with a choice ID and a referenceLabels entry yields the display names and neither ID.
- **Verifier:** record-markup.ts:259-263 builds each related row from valueDisplay(related.values[fieldId]) for every non-calculated binding, with no choiceDisplay and no referenceLabels. The compiler lets a related list bind any non-retired field of the related type (NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:444-450), and the Engine returns referenceLabels on the same query that feeds the related window (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:428-451, reads.ts:185). recordFieldDisplay (record-markup.ts:29-39), used by cards and lists, resolves both, so a choice ID such as 'in_progress' or a target record ID shows in a related row while the Tasks list shows the label. No test covers a choice or reference in a related row (record-markup.test.mjs:117-139, related-actions.test.mjs). Visible wrong display on a core record-page surface, reachable only when a relation binds a choice or reference field; the row's Open link is the workaround.
- **Correction:** The 'choice created in Studio uses its original text as its ID' remark is secondary and I did not trace it; the agent-authored ID case ('in_progress') and the reference case are enough on their own. The reproduction field says 'Source', which is accurate.
