### ABS-08 — In-place label editors are white on white in the dark theme (Archi box rename, Swarm decision and start/end labels)

**P2** · ui · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `extensions/archi/editor.css:683`, `extensions/archi/view.css:17`, `extensions/swarm/view.css:3`, `extensions/swarm/view.css:36`
- **What:** Archi's .direct-edit (archi-online's in-place textarea for renaming a box on the view) sets background: #fff and no colour. view.css gives form controls color: inherit, and body takes var(--ink), which is #ffffff in the dark tokens (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/02-tokens.css:66). In Swarm, bpmn-js styles the direct-editing box of an external label (gateways and events, i.e. Decision, Start and End) inline with backgroundColor #ffffff and no colour. Swarm's view.css sets nothing for .djs-direct-editing-*, so the text inherits var(--nendo-ink). Measured with the real stylesheets and the dark ink token: 'archi .direct-edit: color rgb(255, 255, 255) on background rgb(255, 255, 255)' and 'swarm label editor: color rgb(255, 255, 255) on background rgb(255, 255, 255)'.
- **Failure:** In the dark theme, double-clicking a box in the Archi editor (or pressing F2 on it), or double-clicking a Swarm decision's label, opens a white box in which the typed text is invisible.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over CDP, scratch dark-edit.html loading extensions/archi/view.css + editor.css and extensions/swarm/view.css with the dark tokens applied -> 'archi .direct-edit: color rgb(255, 255, 255) on background rgb(255, 255, 255)' / 'swarm label editor: color rgb(255, 255, 255) on background rgb(255, 255, 255)'
- **Fix and guard:** Archi: give .direct-edit an explicit dark text colour to match its white paper (color: #1b1b1b, as the figures draw on white in both themes), or use var(--surface) and var(--ink) together. Swarm: add '.djs-direct-editing-parent { color: var(--nendo-ink); background: var(--nendo-surface) !important; }' (or black text on its white box). Guard: a gate step in both themes that opens each editor and asserts computed colour and background differ (contrast at least 4.5).
- **Verifier:** Archi: the box-rename control is a bare textarea.direct-edit (canvas.js bundle, no inline colour). extensions/archi/editor.css:683-696 gives it background:#fff and no colour. extensions/archi/view.css:17 sets textarea{color:inherit}, and body takes var(--ink) (view.css:16), which is #ffffff in the dark tokens (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/02-tokens.css:66). .view-editor (editor.css:566) and its ancestors set no colour, so typed text is white on white. Swarm: the vendored bpmn-js LabelEditingProvider sets backgroundColor:#ffffff for external labels (isLabelExternal covers Event and Gateway, i.e. Start/End/Decision), the contenteditable inherits colour, extensions/swarm/vendor/diagram-js.css has no direct-editing rule, and view.css:3 gives body var(--nendo-ink). No test touches either editor in dark. Light theme is unaffected and Archi can still rename through the tree or properties pane, hence P2 rather than higher.

**P2** · ui · Confirmed · area `site`

- **What:** Markdown tables render as bare <table> children of .prose (no wrapper). Prose.astro:36 only lifts max-width (.prose table { max-width: none }) and .docs-body (Doc.astro:137) has min-width:0 but no overflow handling, so a table wider than its column overflows into the next grid track and the page. The Agents resource table's code cells hold URI templates such as nendo://application/entity/{entityId}/aggregate{?aggregate,fieldId,groupBy,rowBy,columnBy,dateFieldId,bucket,range,filter} with no break opportunity after the commas. Measured after fonts loaded: 1440 {"tocLeft":1095,"bodyRight":1061,"tableRight":1366,"overlap":true}; 1920 agents table right 1606 vs tocLeft 1335; 1280 /docs/agents sw 1286 vw 1265; 1024 sw 1237 vw 1009; 800 sw 979 vw 785; 375: /docs/agents sw 980, /docs/files-and-data sw 530 (Action and State tables), /docs/concepts sw 444, /docs/getting-started sw 415, /docs/screens sw 397 (all vw 375). Screenshot agents-resources-1440.png shows the 'What it returns' column text drawn under the TOC links.
- **Failure:** A reader opens Agents > Reading the file on a 1440x900 laptop: the second column of the resource table is overprinted by the sticky On-this-page list and cannot be read. On a 375px phone, Files and data > Copies cuts off the History and 'Use it to' columns and the whole page pans sideways.

- **Fix and guard:** Wrap every rendered markdown table in a scroll container (a small rehype plugin in astro.config.mjs markdown.rehypePlugins that wraps <table> in <div class="table-scroll">, which Prose.astro:41 already styles), and let code inside table cells break (.prose td code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }). Guard: a geometry check in Gate-SiteSearch.mjs (or a sibling lane) that, for every guide at 1440/1024/375, asserts document.scrollWidth <= clientWidth and that no .docs-body table/pre right edge exceeds .docs-toc left.
- **Verifier:** Prose.astro:36-52 only lifts max-width for markdown tables (no .table-scroll wrapper is generated; astro.config.mjs:12-17 has no rehype plugin) and Doc.astro:137 .docs-body has min-width:0 but no overflow rule, so a table wider than its grid track spills out. Reproduced against the built dist/ served locally: at 1440 the Agents resource table right edge is 1365 vs .docs-toc left 1094, 49 table text rects fall inside the transparent sticky TOC column (Doc.astro:82-89); at 375 scrollWidth/clientWidth is 979/360 (agents), 529/360 (files-and-data), 444 (concepts), 414 (getting-started), 397 (screens).

### UIS-01 — The tab strip has no overflow handling: past about seven tabs the active tab and the + button are drawn outside the window

**P2** · ui · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data` · also reported as CSS-06

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:218`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:232`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/workspace-tabs.ts:117`
- **What:** .tab-strip is display:flex with overflow visible (21-native.css:218-228). Each .tab is flex 0 1 236px with min-width 96px (232-244). drawTabs (workspace-tabs.ts:117-128) appends every tab and then #tab-new, and nothing scrolls the strip, wraps it, or brings the active tab into view. The ancestor clips what spills over, so the document does not scroll either.
- **Failure:** At 1024x768, open 11 tabs with Ctrl+T. Tabs 8 to 11 and the + button sit at x 988 to 1422 in a 1024px window. The newly opened tab is the active one and cannot be seen or clicked, + cannot be reached with the mouse, and every visible label is cut to 'D…'. In the Desktop host the overflow also runs under Windows' caption buttons, because --title-bar-right is only padding.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p21-tabs.mjs (Ctrl+T x10 at 1024x768) -> strip {sw:1142, cw:744, overflowX:'visible'}, tabs [[288,384],...,[988,1084],[1088,1184],[1188,1284],[1288,1384]], plus [1390,1422], innerWidth 1024, activeIdx 10; label sw 119 / cw 20. Screenshot tabs-10-1024.png
- **Fix and guard:** Make the strip scroll horizontally with overflow-x:auto and the tab buttons as flex:none past their minimum, or add an overflow menu like Explorer's. Call scrollIntoView({inline:'nearest'}) on the active tab in drawTabs, and keep #tab-new outside the scroller so it stays reachable. Guard: a gate check that opens 12 tabs at 1024px and asserts the active tab's rect and #tab-new's rect lie within innerWidth minus --title-bar-right.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end in CSS and TS. 21-native.css:218-228 makes .tab-strip a flex row with no overflow rule (visible), and .tab is flex 0 1 236px with min-width 96px (232-244), so tabs stop shrinking at 96px and spill past the strip. workspace-tabs.ts:117-128 appends every tab plus #tab-new and nothing scrolls, wraps or caps (newTab at 138-154 has no limit). body is overflow:hidden (03-base.css:13), so the spill is clipped, not scrolled; .tab-new is flex:none and sits after the last tab, so it goes off-screen too. The newly opened tab is the active one, so Ctrl+T past ~7 tabs at 1024px lands on an invisible tab. Workaround exists (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab, Delete on a focused tab), and the tab strip is hidden at <=840px (21-native.css:500), so it only bites at wider windows with many tabs: P2 not higher.
- **Correction:** Detail only: the Desktop host reserves --title-bar-right as right padding on the strip (21-native.css:227), so the overflow runs through that padding and under the caption buttons, as the finding says. FIXES.md CSS-06 already records the same defect.

### UIS-02 — In a narrow window (840px or less) the File menu opens clipped to the 48px top bar, so its actions cannot be seen or used

- **What:** At max-width 840px the rail becomes the top bar: height 48px with overflow-x:auto and scrollbar-width:none (21-native.css:506-515). A non-visible overflow-x makes overflow-y auto as well, so the rail clips its descendants vertically. Alt+F moves keyboard focus to 'About this file', which is scrolled to y=-3 and clipped. Open file, Close file, backup, restore and CSV actions are unreachable by pointer; only the Ctrl+K palette still lists them.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p29-popovers.mjs at 800x700 -> file panel rect {l:42,t:40,r:382,b:590}, clip {by:'aside#app-rail', anc:[0,0,800,48]} (light and dark). p30-rail.mjs at 800 -> Alt+F focus 'button#about-file' rect [51,-3,312,55] clipped by aside#app-rail [0,0,800,48]. Screenshot pop-file-800-light.png
- **Fix and guard:** Take the panel out of the scrolling rail. Either render it position:fixed, anchored to the summary's rect, or move overflow-x:auto from .rail to an inner wrapper around the nav sections only, so .brand is not inside a clipping box. Guard: at 800x700, open #file-menu and assert that clippedByAncestor(#file-actions) is null and that its rect height is over 200px.
- **Verifier:** Traced in CSS and DOM. At max-width 840px 21-native.css:506-515 makes .rail a 48px-high row with overflow-x:auto; a non-visible overflow-x forces overflow-y to auto, so the rail clips descendants. index.html:16-26 nests aside#app-rail > .brand > details#file-menu > #file-actions. 01-file-menu.css:6 and :12 make .file-menu position:relative and the panel position:absolute, so the panel's containing block is inside the rail and the rail's overflow clips it (21-native.css:86-90 only repositions it, no position:fixed). No other rule moves it. Reachable in the product, not only in the preview: DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:10 sets the minimum window width to 1024 physical px, which is about 819 CSS px at 125% scaling and 683 at 150%, so a minimum-width window on a common high-DPI laptop gets this layout. Workaround: Ctrl+K palette lists the file actions (command-palette.ts:111), or widen the window. P2.
- **Correction:** The 'reachable in the Desktop host' point is an addition: the 1024-physical-pixel window minimum becomes <=840 CSS px at 125% display scaling or more. No change to locations or fix.

### DSH-04 — Heavy picker-free methods (history.fold, data.buildSearchIndex, data.writeRecords, data.undoRecordWrites, data.searchRecords) run their synchronous SQLite work on the UI thread

**P2** · performance · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchCancellation.cs:33`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:293`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:398`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:420`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:424`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileReplacement.cs:28`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:191`
- **What:** Only methods in WorkbenchMethods.OffUiThread are handed to Task.Run; everything else runs HandleAsync on the UI thread. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's async calls complete synchronously and the Engine has no Task.Run, so the SQL runs on whatever thread awaits it. data.writeRecords and data.undoRecordWrites go through MutateAsync with calculations and automatic actions, exactly like data.setFields, which is offloaded. history.fold does a full BackupDatabase copy plus VACUUM (SqliteNendoStore.Backup.cs:171, HistoryFold.cs:294); data.buildSearchIndex rebuilds the FTS index. None touches a picker or XAML. The Workbench's 15 s timeout applies to these methods (only file.* and extension.* are exempt).
- **Failure:** On a large file, History > Fold freezes the native window (title bar, resize, tray menu; Windows marks it Not Responding) for the whole backup+VACUUM; after 15 s the Workbench rejects with host-timeout 'The Desktop host did not respond' while the fold continues, and the late response is dropped, inviting a retry. A custom view's batch write with automatic actions, or typing in Ctrl K search, stalls the window the same way.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I scratchpad/review/desktop-shell/offui_probe.py -> 'methods in the HandleAsync switch: 62 / in OffUiThread: 47 / switch methods that run on the UI thread: ... DataBuildSearchIndex = data.buildSearchIndex, DataSearchRecords = data.searchRecords, DataUndoRecordWrites = data.undoRecordWrites, DataWriteRecords = data.writeRecords, ... HistoryFold = history.fold, HistoryFoldPreview = history.foldPreview, ...' (also agent.* and extension.state.*).
- **Fix and guard:** Add DataWriteRecords, DataUndoRecordWrites, DataSearchRecords, DataBuildSearchIndex, HistoryFoldPreview, HistoryFold, AgentGetStatus/SetMode/RevokeEditing/GetProposal/SetSettings and ExtensionStateRead/Set to OffUiThread, and give history.fold/data.buildSearchIndex no Workbench timeout (or a long one). Guard: a test that asserts every switch method not in an explicit 'needs the UI thread' list (pickers, title bar, appearance, downloads, diagnostics, file actions, extension import/export/develop link) is in OffUiThread, so a new method cannot silently land on the UI thread.
- **Verifier:** Traced. MainPage.xaml.cs:293 hands only WorkbenchMethods.OffUiThread members (WorkbenchCancellation.cs:33-82) to Task.Run. data.writeRecords, data.undoRecordWrites (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:398-399), data.searchRecords, data.buildSearchIndex (:420-421), history.foldPreview and history.fold (:424-425) are absent from that set, while data.setField(s), data.createRecord and data.moveRecord, which use the same MutateAsync path, are in it. src/Nendo.Engine has no Task.Run/Yield (grep), and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite async calls complete synchronously, so the SQL runs on the UI thread. history.fold (DesktopFileReplacement.cs:28-44) does a backup copy, the fold transaction and a VACUUM (ADR-0021 item 6), for files that have reached the operation-row bound. host-desktop.ts:191-197 exempts only session.*File, file.* and extension.* from the 15 s timeout, so a long fold would show host-timeout while the window is frozen. Not an ADR-mandated trade-off: the allowlist comment says an omitted method is 'merely slower', which is accepted for light methods but not for these. I read the probe output as consistent with the switch.
- **Correction:** The Ctrl K data.searchRecords example is overstated (a bounded 1-100 record read); the real weight is history.fold, data.buildSearchIndex and batch data.writeRecords/undoRecordWrites. Severity depends on file size; P2 is on the high side but defensible for a user-initiated fold on a large history.

### PERF-01 — History fold deletes revisions through an unindexed ON DELETE CASCADE into __nendo_idempotency, so folding a file grown by single edits is quadratic: minutes at 10k-20k revisions, about an hour near the 99k row ceiling

**P2** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.HistoryFold.cs:249`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:685`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:918`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.NewFile.cs:386`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:55`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/HistoryFoldTests.cs:24`
- **What:** CurrentSchemaSql declares __nendo_idempotency with PRIMARY KEY (idempotency_scope, idempotency_key) and FOREIGN KEY (revision_id) REFERENCES __nendo_revision(revision_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, and no index whose first column is revision_id (SqliteNendoStore.cs:685-692). AppendRevisionAsync inserts exactly one idempotency row per revision (SqliteNendoStore.cs:918-930), so a file grown by Studio cell edits or MCP set_field calls has about one idempotency row per revision. WriteHistoryFoldAsync runs `DELETE FROM __nendo_revision WHERE change_sequence > 0 AND change_sequence <= $last` (HistoryFold.cs:249) with foreign_keys=ON (ApplyAndVerifyProfileAsync); SQLite resolves the cascade for every deleted revision with a linear scan of the unindexed child table, so the statement costs folded revisions x idempotency rows. TransformIntoNewFileAsync (New file, ADR-0022) folds every revision with HistoryFoldPolicy.KeepNone through the same WriteHistoryFoldAsync (NewFile.cs:386-394). The ADR-0021 lane writes 200-record x 5-field batches (about 1,000 operations per revision, about 100 revisions, HistoryFoldTests.cs:24-41), so it holds about 100 idempotency rows and cannot see the cost. The fold runs under the coordinator gate and is followed by VACUUM and a full InspectAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:55-73).
- **Failure:** A planner used daily through Studio edits reaches History's 80% warning (about 79,000 operation rows, about 79,000 revisions and idempotency rows). The person clicks Fold older history: the DELETE alone extrapolates to roughly an hour (180 s at 20,000 revisions, growing faster than quadratically), holding the coordinator and request gates; history.fold runs on the UI thread (already DSH-04) and the Workbench reports host-timeout after 15 s (WCS-21). If the person ends Nendo, the transaction rolls back and the file stays at the write ceiling refusing writes with write-ceiling-rows; the other remedy the refusal names, a new file, folds its stage with the same statement.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_fold_cascade.py 5000 10000 20000 (shipped DDL, foreign_keys=ON, one operation and one idempotency row per revision, keep 1,000) -> "revisions= 5000 folded= 4000 shipped DDL: 11069.7 ms with index on idempotency(revision_id): 335.1 ms"; "revisions= 10000 folded= 9000 shipped DDL: 33981.0 ms with index on idempotency(revision_id): 367.1 ms"; "revisions= 20000 folded= 19000 shipped DDL: 179510.8 ms with index on idempotency(revision_id): 1000.4 ms". Deleting the folded idempotency rows first without an index (probe_fold_prefix.py) is still "revisions= 20000 idempotency-first then revision delete: 16034.9 ms".
- **Fix and guard:** Create `__nendo_idempotency(revision_id)` as an index rung of the protected layout (it changes ProtectedSchemaSignatureAsync, so it goes on the ladder with its own ADR-0021 note), created by EnsureHistoryFoldLayoutAsync inside the fold transaction before the DELETE so existing files gain it on their first fold, and by NewFile's transform on its stage. Guard: an Engine test that builds 10,000 single-operation revisions through ApplyAsync (one idempotency row each) and asserts the fold completes within a fixed bound and that EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for `SELECT 1 FROM __nendo_idempotency WHERE revision_id = ?` reports a SEARCH; falsify by dropping the index and quoting the timeout.
- **Verifier:** The code does what the finding says. __nendo_idempotency has PK (idempotency_scope, idempotency_key) and FK revision_id -> __nendo_revision ON DELETE CASCADE, and nothing in src/ indexes revision_id (SqliteNendoStore.cs:685-692; the only CREATE INDEX statements are ui_node_surface, field/link rules and entity indexes). foreign_keys=ON is required by ApplyAndVerifyProfileAsync (SqliteNendoStore.cs:582-596). AppendRevisionAsync writes one idempotency row per revision unconditionally (SqliteNendoStore.cs:918-930). WriteHistoryFoldAsync deletes the folded prefix in one statement (SqliteNendoStore.HistoryFold.cs:249), and TransformIntoNewFileAsync reaches the same statement with KeepNone (NewFile.cs:386-394). __nendo_operation and __nendo_attribution are fine because their PKs lead with revision_id. HistoryFoldTests.cs:24-41 writes 1,000-operation batches, about 100 revisions, so the lane cannot see the cost. I reproduced it independently with the shipped DDL in Python sqlite 3.50.4, one operation and one idempotency row per revision, keeping 1,000. Shipped DDL: 3,000 revisions took 478.5 ms, 6,000 took 5,203.6 ms, 12,000 took 24,018.3 ms. With an index on idempotency(revision_id): 34.6, 144.1 and 536.0 ms. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows 'SCAN __nendo_idempotency' without the index and 'SEARCH ... USING COVERING INDEX' with it. history.fold is also not exempt from the Workbench's 15 s RPC timeout (host-desktop.ts:191-196), and the fold holds the request and coordinator gates throughout (DesktopSessionController.cs:574-590, NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:31-85). I lowered the priority to P2. The fold is a rare, owner-started action. It is atomic and backed up, so there is no loss or corruption, and it does finish if the person waits. That makes it severe friction in the remedy for the write ceiling, not a defect in a common workflow.
- **Correction:** The magnitude depends on the machine. My extrapolation from the measured per-row rate (about 0.34 us per child row scanned at 12k revisions) puts a fold of about 78k single-operation revisions at roughly 15-20 minutes, not about an hour. A planner averaging two operations per revision would have about 40k revisions at the 80% warning, which is roughly 4-5 minutes. Either way it is minutes under the gates, and longer than the Workbench's 15 s timeout. Deleting the idempotency rows first does not remove the cost. The later revision DELETE still scans the remaining child rows for each parent row, and PRAGMA foreign_keys cannot be switched off inside the fold transaction. So the index rung the finding proposes is the right fix.

### WST-03 — The refusal-code tests pin hand-copied lists, so a definitive Engine refusal the Workbench never classified (value-not-unique, kept-in-new-files-unchanged) wedges the save journal with every test green

**P2** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/write-failure.test.mjs:186`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/host-behavior.test.mjs:45`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/host-behavior.test.mjs:143`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:19`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:209`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.NewFile.cs:139`
- **What:** write-failure.test.mjs keeps its own 'confirmed' array, a partial copy of pending-mutations.ts's rejected set that already omits the hierarchy, link and calculation codes. It only asserts that the codes it lists are retained. host-behavior.test.mjs enumerates 4 reference codes and 7 hierarchy codes by hand. No test derives the codes from the Engine, so a NendoPreconditionException a journaled write can raise falls through to 'unsettled' unnoticed. Two concrete misses: value-not-unique (ADR-0020, raised in the write's own transaction from data.setFields/createRecord) and kept-in-new-files-unchanged (raised for the per-record op behind data.setKeptInNewFiles, which isJournaledMutation lists). The product consequence for value-not-unique is reported as WCS-01. This finding is the missing guard, and the second code it lets through.
- **Failure:** Studio's grid is stale after an agent set a record's In-new-files mark. The person picks the same mark, and the Engine refuses with kept-in-new-files-unchanged without changing anything. The journal keeps the entry 'pending'. Every later save in the file is then refused with 'A previous save is still unconfirmed', and decideWriteFailure discards the view.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probes/kept-refusal-probe.mjs (real src/host.ts and src/write-failure.ts, test fixture) -> 'refusal code: kept-in-new-files-unchanged \| decideWriteFailure -> refresh-view' / 'journal entries left in localStorage: 1 \| receipt lookups made: 1' / 'next save (a different value): refused: A previous save is still unconfirmed. Check or retry that saved request first. \| mutations sent: 1'. Same result for value-not-unique via unique-refusal-probe.mjs. Engine precondition codes not in rejected (grep of new NendoPreconditionException over src/Nendo.Engine, 144 codes) include value-not-unique and kept-in-new-files-unchanged.
- **Fix and guard:** Add the definitive data-write codes to rejected. Replace the copied lists with a test that extracts every `new NendoPreconditionException("code"` from src/Nendo.Engine and requires each to be in pending-mutations' rejected set or in an explicit, commented 'not a journaled-write refusal' list. The test then fails the day a new refusal code is added unclassified. Falsify the guard by deleting 'record-version-conflict' from rejected.
- **Verifier:** pending-mutations.ts:19-29 'rejected' lacks value-not-unique and kept-in-new-files-unchanged. The Engine raises both inside a journaled write's transaction (SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:209; NewFile.cs:139 for SetRecordKeptInNewFiles behind data.setKeptInNewFiles, which is in the journaled 'methods' set at pending-mutations.ts:18). WorkbenchProtocol.cs:455-457 passes the Engine code through to the page (actions.ts:40 already reads error.code === 'value-not-unique'). In sendPending (pending-mutations.ts:~130-145) an unlisted code is not removed: lookup() finds no receipt, the error is rethrown and the entry stays 'pending'. submit() then refuses every later save with 'A previous save is still unconfirmed' (pending-mutations.ts:~93), and 'Check or retry save' only replays the same refused request. decideWriteFailure also returns refresh-view for it. The tests copy the lists by hand (write-failure.test.mjs:13, host-behavior.test.mjs:45 and :143) and nothing derives codes from the Engine, so the gap passes green. I read the reviewer's kept-refusal-probe.mjs against the real host.ts and it matches the code path.
- **Correction:** The write-failure.test.mjs location is line 13 (the 'confirmed' array), not 186. kept-in-new-files-unchanged needs a stale grid (the follow-the-file redraw normally refreshes it quickly), so value-not-unique, the ADR-0020 unique-field duplicate, is the realistic trigger. That product consequence is outside this finding (WCS-01); here the finding is the missing guard.

### WST-02 — The Workbench bundle and the installer ship AG Grid Community, ag-stack, ag-charts-types (MIT) and Lucide icon paths (ISC) without any licence notice

**P2** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/vite.config.ts:4`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/LICENSE.lucide.txt:1`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/icons.ts:1`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Nendo.Desktop.csproj:62`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/package-lock.json:1`
- **What:** package-lock.json lists three production packages, ag-grid-community 36.1.0, ag-stack 36.1.0 and ag-charts-types 14.1.0, all with license MIT. icons.ts draws paths from Lucide 1.48.0 (ISC), and LICENSE.lucide.txt sits at the project root, outside public/, so vite never copies it into dist. The minified bundle carries no licence banner, because AG Grid's ESM has none to preserve. Nendo.Desktop.csproj copies dist/**/* into Workbench/, and nothing in Publish-NendoPayload.ps1 or Build-NendoInstaller.ps1 adds a notice. The extension packages already ship vendor/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt for their own vendored code. The Workbench has no equivalent.
- **Failure:** Every Nendo installation redistributes AG Grid's MIT code (inside index-*.js, 1.4 MB) and Lucide's ISC artwork. Both licences require their copyright and permission notice in all copies, and no copy carries one. The public repository therefore distributes a binary that is out of licence compliance.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: grep -o -i '@license\|MIT License\|Copyright' over src/Nendo.Workbench/dist/assets/index-*.js -> no output; find artifacts/build/publish/payload -iname '*licen*' -o -iname '*notice*' -> no output; package-lock production entries -> 'ag-charts-types 14.1.0 MIT', 'ag-grid-community 36.1.0 MIT', 'ag-stack 36.1.0 MIT'
- **Fix and guard:** Generate dist/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt at build time from the lockfile's production packages (each node_modules/<pkg>/LICENSE*) plus LICENSE.lucide.txt. A small vite plugin emitting an asset, like viewApiReferenceFile, would do it. Add a verify:dependencies check that every production package in package-lock.json and the Lucide notice appear in that file. Add a Test-NendoInstaller assertion that payload/Workbench/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt exists.
- **Verifier:** package-lock.json production entries are ag-charts-types 14.1.0, ag-grid-community 36.1.0 and ag-stack 36.1.0, all MIT. The built bundle src/Nendo.Workbench/dist/assets/index-*.js holds no copyright, MIT or @license text (only an ag-grid.com URL). vite.config.ts sets no legal-comment handling and emits no notice asset. Nendo.Desktop.csproj:61-66 copies dist/**/* into Workbench/ and nothing else, so LICENSE.lucide.txt, which sits beside package.json and not in public/, is never shipped. icons.ts:1-3 says the icon paths come from Lucide (ISC). No tool script (Build-NendoInstaller, Publish-NendoPayload, Test-NendoInstaller) mentions a licence or notice, and the extensions do ship vendor/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (garden, swarm), so the Workbench is the exception. No ADR or contract mandates omitting it; ADR-0015 only requires a permissive licence. MIT and ISC both require the notice in copies, so it is a real redistribution gap, although it has no runtime effect.
- **Correction:** The Desktop csproj include is at lines 61-66, not 62 only. Not even Nendo's own LICENSE is shipped in the payload, so the fix could emit one combined notices file.

### DOC-01 — Authoring guide tells a view to resend a write after `disconnected`, omits writeKey, host-timeout and written-not-read

**P2** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `docs-drift`

- **Where:** `docs/custom-view-authoring.md:773`, `docs/custom-view-authoring.md:648`, `docs/custom-view-authoring.md:1054`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/nendo-api.ts:293`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/reference.ts:396`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:306`
- **What:** The guide's refusal table says `disconnected` \| 'Nendo reconnected the view while the request waited. Send it again' (line 773), and the table has no `host-timeout` or `written-not-read` rows. The 'Several writes at once' section (648-667) never mentions the `writeKey` option, and the 'cannot' table says a view cannot 'Choose the idempotency key' (1054). Since review R-011 (2026-10-06) the code says the opposite: api.js rejects with 'A read can be sent again; a write may have been kept, so read before writing again, or send a batch again under its writeKey' (nendo-api.ts:293), reference.ts:396-397 says the same for disconnected and host-timeout, and the broker writes a batch under `view-<package>-<writeKey>` (extension-broker.ts:306-312). custom-views.md:674-682, 1123-1125 and 2030-2035 record that disconnected/host-timeout 'no longer say to send a write again'.
- **Failure:** A view author follows the guide: a `records.create` or a `records.batch` without writeKey times out or is disconnected after the host committed it; the author's retry logic 'sends it again' and the file gets a second copy of the created records (each call carries a fresh idempotency key).
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In custom-view-authoring.md, replace the `disconnected` row with the contract's wording (read first, or resend a batch under the same writeKey), add `host-timeout` and `written-not-read` rows, document `{ writeKey }` in the records.batch section, and reword the 'cannot choose the idempotency key' row to say the key is namespaced by the package. Guard: extend scripts/view-api-reference.test.mjs (or a docs check) to assert every refusal code in reference.ts appears in the guide's refusal table.
- **Verifier:** docs/custom-view-authoring.md:773 still says of `disconnected` 'Send it again' and has no host-timeout or written-not-read row; the only mention of writeKey-style keys is :1054 'Choose the idempotency key' as something a view cannot do (grep for writeKey, host-timeout, written-not-read in the guide returns nothing). The code says the opposite: nendo-api.ts:293 ('a write may have been kept, so read before writing again, or send a batch again under its writeKey'), reference.ts:396-398, and extension-broker.ts:306-312 (batchKey writes under view-<package>-<writeKey>, a fresh randomUUID key otherwise). The contract already has it right (custom-views.md:622, 674-682, 1123-1125), so this is the author-facing guide lagging the contract. Without a writeKey every call carries a fresh key, so a literal 'send it again' after a timed-out or disconnected write can duplicate created records. It is the most consequential of the doc drifts because the stale text is an instruction rather than an omission, but the runtime error message gives the correct advice at the moment of failure, so P2 rather than higher.
- **Correction:** Also stale: the :1054 'cannot choose the idempotency key' row (a view can now choose a package-namespaced key via writeKey on records.batch); the 'Several writes at once' section (648-667) never documents `{ writeKey }`. The suggested guard (assert every refusal code in reference.ts appears in the guide's table) is sound.

### UX-09 — Help tells the person custom views cannot change records and files never carry scripts, contradicting the custom-views guide and the code

**P2** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` · also reported as WSP-07

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help-concepts.ts:186`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help-concepts.ts:89`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help.ts:53`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:581`
- **What:** 'What Nendo deliberately leaves out' says a custom view 'reads records through Nendo’s typed services and, in this version, cannot change them' and 'There are no plug-ins or scripts in a file' (help-concepts.ts:186). 'Screens are definitions, not code' says 'The file never contains HTML, styling, scripts or SQL, so a screen can never run anything on your computer' (help-concepts.ts:89). 'Find your way around' says a view 'can also change records and run a record’s commands ... Nendo asks nothing first' (help.ts:53), and the broker routes a view's writes to data.writeRecords (extension-broker.ts:581).
- **Failure:** A person deciding whether to keep Run custom views on for a file they received reads 'Boundaries, stated as boundaries' and concludes a view cannot alter their data, when it can write records without asking.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Rewrite help-concepts.ts:186 and :89 to state that a file may carry custom-view code that runs in its own frame and can change records and run commands, each change in History under its package; check site/ guides for the same sentence. Guard: help.test.mjs asserting no topic contains 'cannot change them' while the broker exposes data.writeRecords.
- **Verifier:** help-concepts.ts:186 (topic 'limits', 'Boundaries, stated as boundaries') says a custom view 'reads records ... and, in this version, cannot change them' and 'There are no plug-ins or scripts in a file'. The code and the sibling Help text say the opposite: help.ts:53 states a view 'can also change records and run a record's commands ... Nendo asks nothing first', and extension-broker.ts:581 routes records.batch to data.writeRecords (contract custom-views.md:618-622 lists records.create/update/batch). help-concepts.ts:169/180 even mention changes 'a custom view' makes in History. No other copy of the stale sentence exists (grep over site/ and src), and no test pins it. Stale safety wording on the page that people read when deciding whether to run a received file's views, so more than cosmetic drift.
- **Correction:** The line 186 defect is the solid one. Line 89 is weaker: that sentence is in the 'Screens are definitions, not code' topic and is true of a screen definition; only its file-level phrasing 'The file never contains HTML, styling, scripts or SQL' is false once custom views exist, and the next sentence in 'limits' does warn that the file's code runs and can reach the network and clipboard. Fix line 186 first (drop 'in this version, cannot change them', say views can write records and run commands, each change visible in History); reword line 89 to 'a screen definition never contains...'. Cited line help.ts:53 is the correct statement, not part of the defect.

### DAE-02 — A view's geolocation request gets WebView2's own prompt with the grant kept in the profile, so one Allow covers every view of every file

**P2** · security · Plausible · area `desktop-agents-extensions` (reported P1)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frame-markup.ts:21`, `docs/decisions/0013-custom-views-with-code-in-the-file.md:355`
- **What:** OnViewPermissionRequested sets args.Handled = true and returns at once for every kind other than ClipboardRead and MultipleAutomaticDownloads, leaving State at Default and SavesInProfile at its default (true); only the two allowed kinds get SavesInProfile = false. Every view frame carries allow="... geolocation" (frameAllow), so navigator.geolocation in any view raises a request that ends in WebView2's own prompt. prototypes/iframe-views/FINDINGS.md S10 measured that a view's permission request carries the Workbench's origin (https://app.nendo.local/) and that a grant kept with the default SavesInProfile applied to a second view origin without any event. ADR-0013 says of exactly this path: "anything else gets WebView2's default prompt, and no grant is saved, where it would cover every view." The code does nothing to keep it from being saved.
- **Failure:** The person's own map view asks for their location; WebView2's prompt names the Workbench's origin, so it reads as Nendo asking, and they click Allow. The decision is kept in the profile for the Workbench origin. Weeks later they open a file someone sent them; its view calls navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition, no prompt appears, and it posts their location to its server.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Answer every other kind on the frame with SavesInProfile = false and State = Deny (or show Nendo's own prompt that names the view and the file, then set Allow or Deny with SavesInProfile = false); drop geolocation from frameAllow if no prompt is built. Guard in the extension-view journey: a view requests geolocation, the default is answered Allow once, then a second view origin's navigator.permissions.query({name:'geolocation'}) must still read prompt or denied; falsify by restoring the early return.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:99-101 sets Handled = true and returns for every kind except ClipboardRead and MultipleAutomaticDownloads. State stays Default, so WebView2 shows its own prompt, and the Workbench's Deny handler at :107 never runs. view-frame-markup.ts:21 delegates geolocation to every view frame, and no Permissions-Policy header exists anywhere in src. ADR-0013:355-358 and docs/contracts/custom-views.md:496-500 both promise that no answer is saved in the profile. Nothing in the code makes that true for these kinds, and no test covers them. All windows share one default WebView2 profile (MainPage.xaml.cs:159 calls EnsureCoreWebView2Async with no options), and S10 measured that a saved grant is keyed to app.nendo.local and reaches a second view origin without an event. What I could not establish is the remaining link: whether an Allow clicked in WebView2's default prompt for a delegated geolocation request is saved. S10 measured a grant the host set for clipboard-read, not a decision made in the default prompt. I ran no probe: the workstation is locked (LogonUI running), and the prompt needs a click. Downgraded to P2 because it needs a view the person has already allowed to read their location, which is not a common workflow, and clicking Block avoids it. It breaks an accepted ADR's stated guarantee but not an AGENTS.md invariant.
- **Correction:** The evidence blames SavesInProfile being left at its default. Per the WebView2 SDK docs (Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.xml, 1.0.3719.77), SavesInProfile governs 'the permission state set from the PermissionRequested event', meaning a state the host sets. Here State is left Default, so the user's choice in WebView2's default prompt is what would be saved, and setting SavesInProfile = false alone, with State still Default, may not prevent that. S10 (prototypes/iframe-views/FINDINGS.md:33) measured a host-set clipboard-read Allow, not geolocation through the default prompt, so it supports the cross-view reach, not the persistence of a prompt decision. The fix as proposed is right: either answer every other kind with an explicit State and SavesInProfile = false (Deny, or Nendo's own prompt that names the view and file), or drop geolocation from frameAllow and from the contract table at docs/contracts/custom-views.md:342, together with the assertion in src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/view-frames.test.mjs:28.

<a id="esc-01"></a>

### ESC-01 — A crash during a write leaves a hot -journal, and every later open refuses the file for good, telling the person to close a writer that does not exist

**P2** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-storage-core`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:250`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:252`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:203`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:180`
- **What:** InspectAsync returns Unreadable("operational-sidecars", "This file has an unfinished or unsupported storage operation. Close its writer before inspecting it.", recovery: true) whenever <file>-journal exists. That result has NendoFileCapabilities.None, so ReadData is false. The check runs before SQLite opens the file, so a DELETE-mode hot journal is never rolled back. ReadDeclaredIdentityAsync (line 203) and RequireUnchangedPhysicalFile (line 180) refuse the same way. In a DELETE-mode write, ApplyAsync and ApplyChangeSetAsync create the journal at the first dirtied page and SQLite deletes it only when COMMIT finishes. No code in src/ handles the operational-sidecars code: grep finds no recovery or rollback flow, and no Workbench or Desktop text either. tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/FileInspectionTests.cs:172 pins the refusal with a 4-byte junk journal. No test kills a process in the middle of a transaction and then reopens the file.
- **Failure:** Nendo is killed during a write: a power cut, Task Manager, a crash, or a forced Windows Update reboot during a 200-record import, a package put or a fold. A cache spill or a COMMIT in progress has already written new pages to the main file. On the next open the file is Rejected or RecoveryRequired with no readable data, and the message says to close a writer that does not exist. The obvious workarounds are to delete the -journal, or to copy or back up only the .nendo file. Either one turns an exactly recoverable file into a torn one: some rows carry the uncommitted transaction and others do not. The manifest, revisions and record versions then disagree, and PRAGMA integrity_check still reports ok, so Nendo's own inspection cannot tell. Without a raw SQLite tool the person cannot reach their data.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python probe_storage.py (probe 3, a scratch SQLite file in DELETE mode, cache_size=8, child os._exit(9) inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE) -> "child exit code 9; -journal exists: True; size 4351520" / "main file header bytes 18/19 (1/1 = rollback journal): 1/1" / "main file read WITHOUT its journal: integrity_check=[('ok',)] distinct values=(2,)" / "after an ordinary SQLite open rolled the journal back: integrity_check=('ok',) distinct values=(1,); -journal exists: False"
- **Fix and guard:** Treat a lone -journal on a rollback-mode file (header bytes 18/19 == 1, no -wal or -shm, no live write owner) as an interrupted write rather than an unknown operational set. Under the instance and write-ownership leases, first copy both files byte for byte into a host-owned stage. Then open a ReadWrite connection with the bounded profile and let SQLite play the journal back, for example with BEGIN IMMEDIATE; ROLLBACK. Confirm the journal is gone, then run the ordinary full InspectAsync. Until that exists, change the message so it warns never to delete or separate the -journal. Guard: an Engine process test that blocks a child inside ApplyAsync after its statements and before COMMIT, with a cache small enough to spill, kills it, asserts that the -journal exists, then asserts the recovery step restores the pre-write manifest and records. Falsify the guard by removing the playback step and quoting the operational-sidecars failure. Keep UnqualifiedOperationalSetIsNotOpenedOrRepaired for -wal and -shm.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed: Inspection.cs:252-254 returns Unreadable("operational-sidecars") on any -journal before SQLite opens the file, and :180 and :203 refuse the same way. Nothing in src/ rolls a journal back or deletes a stale one (grep of -journal finds only refusals and DeletePartialCreation for a failed create), and no test kills a writer between its first dirtied page and COMMIT (the kill tests in ProposalOutcomeProcessTests.cs:27 and RestoreInterruptionTests.cs:58 kill after commit or during restore staging). I did not reproduce the Nendo side; the reviewer's Python probe shows only SQLite behaviour. It is also a pinned, documented fail-closed policy rather than an oversight: FileInspectionTests.cs:172-190 is named UnqualifiedOperationalSetIsNotOpenedOrRepaired and covers -journal, -wal and -shm alike, ADR-0012 rejects guessed repair, ADR-0011:100 and roadmap.md:45 leave physical power loss unqualified, and site/src/content/docs/files-and-data.md:141 tells people a file with an unfinished storage operation stays unreadable until the other program closes it (which assumes a live writer). Reachability needs a kill or crash inside a write transaction, a window of milliseconds to seconds, so it is real but rare. The gap is that a crashed writer is the one case where no live writer exists, and the message is wrong for it.
- **Correction:** Keep this PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED. (1) The scenario depends on the process dying while the transaction is open; the journal exists from the first dirtied page until COMMIT. The main file changes only on a cache spill or at commit, so the torn-file risk after a deleted journal exists only if the kill came after one of those. (2) The fix is a new repair action, which ADR-0012 currently rejects and ADR-0011 does not cover, so it needs an ADR amendment before any code. The cheap part, stating in the message that the journal must not be deleted or separated from the file, needs none. (3) The workaround is a Nendo-made backup copy, so the data is reachable apart from the last interrupted write.

<a id="dsh-05"></a>

### DSH-05 — titleBarChanged never fires on a display-scale change at standard scales, so passthrough regions stay in the old monitor's physical pixels after the window moves between 100% and 150%/200% screens

**P2** · ui · Plausible · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:59`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:52`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:74`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/title-bar.ts:49`
- **What:** RefreshTitleBar (raised on XamlRoot.Changed, i.e. on a RasterizationScale change) compares DescribeTitleBar() = (Height/scale, LeftInset/scale, RightInset/scale) with the previous record and returns when equal. The tall bar is 48 x scale physical with 144 x scale for the caption buttons (architecture.md:567), so at 125/150/175/200% the DIP answer is the same 48/0/144 and no event is raised. SetTitleBarControls converts the page's CSS boxes to physical pixels with the scale at the time of the call, and the Workbench only re-sends when onTitleBarChanged fires (it sets sent = null there) or its CSS boxes change (sameBoxes), which a pure DPI change does not cause.
- **Failure:** Laptop at 150% plus an external monitor at 100%: drag the Nendo window from the monitor to the laptop. A tab at CSS x 300-400 stays passed through at physical 300-400 while it is now drawn at 450-600; clicking it starts a window drag or a double-click maximises, and File menu/tab clicks miss until something else changes the bar's layout.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Keep the last scale in MainWindow and raise TitleBarChanged when the scale changes even if the DIP view is equal (or keep the last CSS rects and re-apply them with the new scale on XamlRoot.Changed). Guard: a pure change-detection helper (previousBar, previousScale, bar, scale) -> bool with a test for 1.0 -> 2.0 at identical DIP values; falsify by dropping the scale term.
- **Verifier:** MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:52-65: DescribeTitleBar returns (Height/scale, LeftInset/scale, RightInset/scale) and RefreshTitleBar returns early when the record equals the previous one. AppWindowTitleBar.Height/insets are physical pixels (48 x scale, 144 x scale per architecture.md:545-570), so at standard exact-multiple scales (1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0) the DIP value stays (48, 0, 144) and TitleBarChanged is never raised on XamlRoot.Changed or AppWindow.Changed. title-bar.ts:49-54 sets sent=null and re-sends only in onTitleBarChanged; otherwise report() (:123-129) skips when sameBoxes (exact CSS-pixel equality, title-bar-model.ts:76-79), and a monitor change normally keeps the CSS viewport size. SetTitleBarControls (MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:74-81) converts to physical pixels with the scale at call time, so the stored passthrough rects go stale. No test or doc covers a scale change (DesktopTitleBarTests only uses 48/0/144). Not reproduced at runtime, so reachability depends on Windows keeping the old pixel rects and not re-measuring, hence PLAUSIBLE; the next layout change that alters a box does heal it, which is the workaround.
- **Correction:** The event does still fire at non-integral scales (e.g. 1.33) where rounding changes the DIP values; the defect is limited to scales where 48/144 x scale are exact. Fix as described (track the last scale).

<a id="dae-05"></a>

### DAE-05 — Handle redaction misses the agent's own prose, which the contract says it covers

**P3** · security · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:712`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:721`, `docs/contracts/launched-agents.md:154`
- **What:** The Handle regex requires a ':' or '=' between the key and the value: ((?:resume[_ ]?)?application[_ ]?handle\\?["'`*]{0,2}\s*[:=]\s*...). Any other wording passes through Redact unchanged, and so does a bare 64-hex handle or one named by another key (application-handle, handle). The contract (line 154) says the value is hidden whether "quoted or in the agent's own words". The handle is minted by the in-process MCP host (NendoLeaseTools: 32 random bytes as lowercase hex), so the host could hide it by value.
- **Failure:** Asked what it holds, the agent replies "Your applicationHandle is 3f9a..." or lays the grant out as a Markdown table. The full handle is drawn in the conversation tab, where the ADR says it must never appear, and stays readable on screen or in a screen share for as long as the transcript lives.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh -File scratchpad/review/desktop-agents-extensions/conversation-probe.ps1 with a synthetic handle -> "e5 order=5 kind=agent text=\"Your applicationHandle is feedfacefeedface...\"", "e6 order=6 kind=thought text=\"\| applicationHandle \| feedface...feedface \|\"", "entries that show the synthetic handle: 2".
- **Fix and guard:** Redact by value: have the host expose the handles it minted for this file (or match any 64-lowercase-hex run that equals one) and replace them wherever they occur, keeping the key-based pattern for the cut-off streaming case. Guard: extend AHandleTheAgentRepeatsIsHiddenInEveryPartOfTheTranscript with "is", table and bare-value forms; falsify with the current regex.
- **Verifier:** AgentConversation.cs:712-714: the Handle regex needs [:=] right after 'application handle' plus optional quotes/spaces, so 'Your applicationHandle is feed...', a Markdown table row '\| applicationHandle \| feed... \|' and a bare 64-hex value pass Redact unchanged; Redact is the only redaction (AcpConnection.cs:218 and AgentConversation View()/Read also call it, nothing redacts by value). docs/contracts/launched-agents.md:154 does say 'quoted or in the agent's own words', and ADR-0009 (Authority section) says the UI exposes only pseudonyms, so the contract wording is not met for prose forms. But the code comment (lines 703-707) and test AHandleTheAgentRepeatsIsHiddenInEveryPartOfTheTranscript scope 'own words' to key:value forms, so this is a best-effort gap rather than a regression of ACP-08, and the exposure is narrow: the agent must write its own private handle in prose (the lease tool tells it to keep it private), it is shown only to the local person who owns the file and can revoke the lease, and the agent already holds the capability. No boundary is crossed.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: defence-in-depth on a local screen. Either narrow the contract sentence to 'key: value forms' or add by-value redaction (the host knows the 32-byte hex handle it minted); the reviewer's fix is sound.

### EXT-02 — A put that changes only a file's media type is reviewed as "Keep ... as it is" and left out of packageChanges, yet changes how the file is served

**P3** · security · Confirmed · area `engine-extensions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionPackageDiff.cs:39`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:360`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:321`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:139`
- **What:** ExtensionPackageDiff.ComputeAsync skips a touched file when `before?.Sha256 == after?.Sha256`, so packageChanges omits it even though NendoExtensionFileChange carries MediaTypeBefore/MediaTypeAfter. SemanticDiff.Put compares only Sha256 and says "Keep {path} in {title} as it is; the content sent is identical." ExecutePutExtensionFileAsync still runs `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET media_type = excluded.media_type`, and the Desktop serves the stored media type. The import change set itself proposes such puts, because it re-puts a file whose stored media type differs from MediaTypeFor(path).
- **Failure:** A package's index.html was put over MCP with mediaType text/plain, or app.js with application/octet-stream, so it is inert. Re-importing the folder, or an agent's proposal, puts identical bytes with text/html or text/javascript. The review's Code section shows nothing for that file and its sentence says it is kept as it is. After acceptance, the browser runs it as HTML or script at the view's origin. The reverse also holds: a proposal that silently retypes app.js to text/plain breaks the view while the review says nothing changed. This defeats ADR-0013's only control, which is that a person reads the change before it reaches the file.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe3.ps1, NendoExtensionArchives.ChangeSet(folder with index.html, current snapshot holding the same bytes as text/plain) -> 'op: extension.putFile path=index.html mediaType=text/html sha256 same=True expected=True'. ComputeAsync line 39 and SemanticDiff.Put line 360 then treat it as unchanged (Source).
- **Fix and guard:** In ComputeAsync, continue only when both the sha and the media type are equal, and report a type-only change (for example change "retyped", or "replaced" with both media types and no hunks). In SemanticDiff.Put, say "Serve {path} as {new type} instead of {old type}" when only the type differs. Guard: a proposal test with a same-content, different-type put that asserts packageChanges holds the file with MediaTypeBefore != MediaTypeAfter and that the sentence names both types.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. ExtensionArchive.cs:139-142 deliberately emits a put when the stored media type differs from MediaTypeFor(path), even for identical bytes (the contract says so at custom-views.md:1344). ExtensionPackageDiff.cs:39 then skips the file because only Sha256 is compared, so packageChanges omits it. SemanticDiff.cs:360-361 says 'Keep {path} ... as it is; the content sent is identical.' (a sentence custom-views.md:172 mandates for the identical case). Meanwhile SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:321 rewrites media_type and ExtensionAssetServer.cs:99 serves the stored type, so the review hides a real change in how the file is served. custom-views.md:192-195 says packageChanges lists each changed file with its media types before and after, so this is a gap. The impact is smaller than 'security P2': SemanticDiff.cs:296 still emits the extensionCode 'This code runs...' line for any put, including this one. The earlier Add review already showed the type ('Add path (media type, size)'). IsTextual (ExtensionPackageModel.cs:379) is false for application/javascript, so code typed that way is already not line-diffed, which means the retype adds little over what a proposer can already do in one step.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3, category review accuracy rather than a bypass of ADR-0013's control. The review still shows the extensionCode warning for the put, and the previous Add showed the media type. The fix (compare media type too in ComputeAsync, say 'Serve X as T instead of U' in PackageState.Put) is right, but the contract's line 172 sentence and the packageChanges rule at lines 192-195 need updating in the same change.

<a id="mhs-06"></a>

### MHS-06 — The MCP web host takes Kestrel endpoints from ambient configuration (process environment, appsettings.json in the current directory), so its binding is not loopback-only

**P3** · security · Confirmed · area `mcp-host-security` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:354`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:367`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:615`
- **What:** BuildAndStartAsync uses WebApplication.CreateBuilder with no ContentRootPath and the default configuration sources. Those include unprefixed environment variables and appsettings.json from Directory.GetCurrentDirectory(). Kestrel's configuration loader binds any Kestrel:Endpoints it finds in addition to the code's Listen(IPAddress.Loopback, port). The same sources can also set AllowedHosts. Nothing in src sets the current directory (there is no SetCurrentDirectory or ContentRootPath), and the payload ships no appsettings.json. ADR-0009 says the server is 'bound only to IPv4 loopback'.
- **Failure:** A developer opens a .nendo file from an ASP.NET project folder, or from an extracted folder that also holds an appsettings.json with "Kestrel":{"Endpoints":{"Http":{"Url":"http://0.0.0.0:5000"}}}, and turns agent access on. The MCP host now also listens on every interface. The middleware's loopback check refuses /mcp from the LAN, but the /MCP bypass above does not. If that port is in use, both the fixed-port attempt and the ephemeral fallback fail with AddressInUse, and agent access cannot start, with an error about ports that names nothing. An extra 127.0.0.1 endpoint makes the `.Single(address.Host == 127.0.0.1)` at line 617 throw.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-ambient-config.ps1, which builds the host as BuildAndStartAsync does (Args=[], Production, ConfigureKestrel Listen(Loopback,0)). With Kestrel__Endpoints__Extra__Url=http://[::1]:0 in the process environment: `bound: http://127.0.0.1:51717` / `bound: http://[::1]:51718`. With the current directory holding an appsettings.json that declares the same endpoint: `contentRoot=...\cwd-with-appsettings` / `bound: http://127.0.0.1:51719` / `bound: http://[::1]:51720`.
- **Fix and guard:** Build the host from an empty configuration: WebApplication.CreateEmptyBuilder plus UseKestrelCore and routing, or clear builder.Configuration.Sources, set ContentRootPath to AppContext.BaseDirectory, and do not let Kestrel load a configuration section. Guard: a test that starts the host in a child process with Kestrel__Endpoints__X__Url set and a current directory holding appsettings.json, and asserts that IServerAddressesFeature.Addresses is exactly one 127.0.0.1 address.
- **Verifier:** Traced and reproduced. NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:354-359 calls WebApplication.CreateBuilder with no ContentRootPath and default configuration sources, and nothing in src sets the current directory or clears sources (grep for SetCurrentDirectory, ContentRootPath, CreateEmptyBuilder, Configuration.Sources found none; no appsettings in the repo). Kestrel loads its Kestrel:Endpoints section additively to the code's Listen(IPAddress.Loopback, port) (lines 367-376). I re-ran the reviewer's probe-ambient-config.ps1 (env variant, same builder arguments as the host): it bound http://127.0.0.1:60926 and http://[::1]:60927. The host's own check at line 615-617 (.Single on 127.0.0.1) would then throw if a second 127.0.0.1 endpoint is configured, and ADR-0009:249-254 ('bound only to IPv4 loopback ... never fatal') no longer holds. The defect is a genuine hardening gap, but it needs a hostile or unusual environment (Kestrel__ variables, or an appsettings.json in the process's current directory, which Explorer typically sets to the opened file's folder).
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The LAN-exposure scenario is blocked by the middleware's own remote-address check (NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:34-38 refuses any non-127.0.0.1 peer on /mcp), so an extra listener is reachable only together with finding 1's path-case bypass; on its own the impact is a startup failure (AddressInUse on both attempts, or the Single() throw) and an ADR wording deviation. The fix (CreateEmptyBuilder, or clear Configuration.Sources and set ContentRootPath to AppContext.BaseDirectory) is sound.

<a id="r2sp-05"></a>

### R2SP-05 — Turning agent access Off is remembered only after the listener's cleanup succeeds; a cleanup throw (for example a discovery entry another process is reading) leaves the old level to come back on the next open

**P3** · security · Confirmed · area `r2-several-processes` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:275`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:405`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:691`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:711`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:151`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:228`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:146`
- **What:** SetAgentModeAsync("off"), which the tray's 'Turn agent access off' also calls, runs StopAgentAccessCoreAsync and only then RememberAgentModeAsync. StopAgentAccessCoreAsync awaits host.DisposeAsync(), which collects every cleanup failure and then throws IOException('Agent access stopped, but its local cleanup did not finish.'). NendoDiscoveryStore.DeleteIfPresent lets anything but not-found escape. Other Nendo processes read entries with File.ReadAllText, which opens with FileShare.Read and so denies delete. They do this in ReadValidEntry, from CleanupStaleEntries on every host start and from ReadLiveEntries behind the instances resource. AnnounceAgentIdle is skipped as well.
- **Failure:** Window A (Planner, Unattended) is told 'Off' at the moment window B starts its listener, or an agent in B reads nendo://application/instances. A's entry delete fails with a sharing violation. DisposeAsync throws, and the Off request returns file-io ('The file action could not be confirmed…') although the listener did stop. The dead endpoint stays advertised under a live PID. agent-modes.json still holds 'unattended', so the next open of Planner (RestoreAgentModeAsync) starts an Unattended listener the person had switched off. The race window is short, but any other DisposeAsync failure (lease revoke, draft discard) has the same effect.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-delete.ps1 (File.Delete on an entry another handle holds with FileShare.Read, as ReadValidEntry does) -> 'delete while a reader holds the entry -> IOException: The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process.' and 'entry still present afterwards: True'
- **Fix and guard:** Forget the remembered level before the stop, or in a finally around it, so Off always sticks. Read discovery entries with FileShare.ReadWrite \| FileShare.Delete. Treat a sharing violation on the delete as retry-then-ignore rather than a failure of the whole stop. Guard: a test holds a FileShare.Read handle on the host's discovery entry during SetAgentModeAsync("off"), then asserts no exception and that DesktopAgentModeStore.Recall returns null.
- **Verifier:** Traced. DesktopAgentAccess.cs:274-279: for Off, `await StopAgentAccessCoreAsync();` then `await RememberAgentModeAsync(...)` with no try/finally, so an exception from Stop skips the Remember that forgets the level. StopAgentAccessCoreAsync (405-421) clears _agentHost/_agentMode first, then awaits host.DisposeAsync(), and AnnounceAgentIdle (420) is skipped on a throw. NendoLocalMcpHost.DisposeAsync (673-723) gathers cleanup failures and ends with `throw new IOException(...)`. NendoDiscoveryStore.DeleteIfPresent (NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:151-166) swallows only not-found, and ReadValidEntry (228-240) uses File.ReadAllText (FileShare.Read, which denies delete); it runs from ReadLiveEntries (instances resource) and CleanupStaleEntries (every host start), so a sharing violation is possible. DesktopSessionSignals.cs:129 shows the tray calls the same SetAgentModeAsync. RestoreAgentModeAsync (130-146) then recalls the unforgotten level on the next open and restarts the listener. The reviewer's probe reproduced the delete refusal. Mitigations: the window is milliseconds, the person sees a file-io error at the time, and a second Off (host already null) forgets the level, so this is a narrow race with a visible symptom.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: a very short race (or another DisposeAsync failure) with an error shown, and a repeat Off clears it. The structural flaw (remembered level cleared only if the stop fully succeeds) is real and the suggested fix (forget before or in a finally; read discovery entries with FileShare.Delete) is sound.

<a id="wxs-08"></a>

### WXS-08 — The broker runs a view's handed-back keys and draws its menus whether or not the view has focus, so Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Back and menus that take focus can arrive with no key pressed

**P3** · security · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:389`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:876`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:430`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-menu.ts:129`
- **What:** handKey accepts any `{t:'key', keys}` that is a host key or a declared key, up to eight a second. keyFromView runs host keys through hostKeyRunner (tabs, Back and Forward, the palette, the rail) without checking that the frame has focus. The contract describes these as keys 'pressed inside the view'. showMenuFor likewise draws a menu without checking focus or a recent pointer event, and showViewMenu focuses its first item, so a menu can take focus from a Nendo field.
- **Failure:** While the person types in a Nendo record form, a buggy or hostile view posts `{t:'key', keys:'Ctrl+W'}` and the active tab closes, or posts `Alt+ArrowLeft` and the page goes back. Or it calls ui.showMenu, the menu takes focus, and the person's next Space picks its first item, sending the view a command they never chose.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Require `document.activeElement === mount.frame` in keyFromView before running a handed-back key, and in showMenuFor before drawing; drop the key or answer null otherwise. A key or right-click really pressed inside the view always leaves the iframe element as the parent's activeElement. Guard: view-frames tests that a key from an unfocused mount does not reach hostKeyRunner and that showMenu from an unfocused mount draws nothing. Falsify them by removing the check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end: a view posts {t:'key',keys:'Ctrl+W'} on its own port; handKey (extension-broker.ts:876-881) checks only deps.running(), that the key is in hostKeys or declared, and the 8/s rate; keyFromView (view-frames.ts:389-393) then calls hostKeyRunner, which main.ts:507-516 maps to runShortcut (closeTab, newTab, cycleTab, palette, route buttons) or goBack/goForward. Nothing checks that the frame has focus. showMenuFor (view-frames.ts:430-445) likewise draws the menu and showViewMenu focuses its first item (view-menu.ts:128). The contract (custom-views.md:590) and ADR-0013 (~line 510) describe the key as one pressed inside the view, but the broker cannot tell. Impact is small: the dirty-form guards still apply to tab and route changes (workspace-tabs.ts closeTab -> refuseWhileDirty), and ADR-0013 line 267 already lets a view navigate the Workbench via ui.openScreen/openRecord/openStudio without any gesture; the only new reach is tab close/open, palette and Back/Forward, so P3.
- **Correction:** The keyFromView half of the fix (require document.activeElement === mount.frame) is sound, because a key pressed in the cross-origin frame leaves the iframe element as the parent's activeElement. Applying the same check to showMenuFor would break the legitimate case where a view opens a menu in answer to a `command` event from a palette entry or declared key, when the Workbench, not the frame, has focus (ADR-0013 Menus bullet; contract 915). For menus, a rate limit or requiring a recent pointer event inside the frame is safer. Also, the failure scenario's 'Back' needs fileDetails closed and no dialog open (main.ts:509-511).

<a id="abs-02"></a>

### ABS-02 — Archi Open silently drops Sketch and Canvas views; the dialog's 'Left out' line does not mention them

**P3** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:98`, `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:141`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1499`
- **What:** archi-online's parser skips archimate:SketchModel and canvas:CanvasModel elements without saying so (parse.ts:294, 'Silently skip SketchModel / CanvasModel'). leftOutOf counts only image objects, connections to images and pictures, and leftOutSentence returns null when there are none. The design doc says these views are out of scope (docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:125). But README.md:181-183 says the dialog 'says what the file holds and what is left out', and the person is never told that they are lost. Measured: Archisurance plus one SketchModel with a sticky and one CanvasModel gives 'with a sketch and a canvas view: opened; {..."views":17...}; 778 records to write; left out: null'. The counts are identical to the file without them.
- **Failure:** A team moves an Archi model with whiteboard Sketch views into Nendo. Open reports nothing left out. Save as .archimate later writes a model without the sketches, so the work is lost if the original is retired.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over CDP, scratch truncated-open.html, exportArchimate(archisurance.json) with a SketchModel and a CanvasModel inserted after the diagrams folder tag -> 'opened; ... 778 records to write; left out: null'
- **Fix and guard:** In readArchimate, count folder children whose xsi:type is archimate:SketchModel or canvas:CanvasModel, with a DOMParser pass or a regex over the XML. Add them to LeftOut (sketchViews, canvasViews) and to leftOutSentence. Guard: an io.test.mjs case that reads a file with one of each and expects leftOutSentence to name both.
- **Verifier:** archi-online parse.ts:294 skips SketchModel/CanvasModel folder children silently ('Silently skip SketchModel / CanvasModel and unknown types'). leftOutOf (io.ts:98-113) counts only image objects, their connections and pictures, and leftOutSentence (io.ts:141-150) returns null when none, so the Open dialog (view.js:1497-1500) says nothing about sketches or canvases. The scope itself is deliberate: docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:71 and :125 say 'Sketch and Canvas views \| Out, as in archi-online', and extensions/archi/README.md:181-185 defines 'left out' as images only. What is real is the silence, not the omission. The loss lands only in the copy in Nendo (the source file is not modified), so this is a disclosure gap, not P2 data loss.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The omission is documented scope (design doc :71, :125); only the missing mention in the dialog is the defect. The README does not claim sketches are reported.

### ABS-04 — Archi delete of more than 200 records is several revisions: a refusal part way is reported as 'refused', it cannot be undone, and Undo then takes back the gesture before it

**P3** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/archi/view.js:142`, `extensions/archi/view.js:170`, `extensions/archi/view.js:742`, `extensions/archi/view.js:733`
- **What:** The confirm-delete close handler calls write(() => M.deletePlan(...).writes, label) with atomic=false. writeNow therefore sends records.batch in slices of 200, each its own revision. If a later slice throws, outcome is '<label> was refused: ...' although the earlier slices are kept. On success it pushes an undo step only when revisions.length === 1, but it leaves saved.undo as it was. undoName() and Ctrl+Z then name and run the previous gesture. Deleting one view easily crosses 200 writes: deletePlan takes every diagram object, connection and property of the view (summary.items).
- **Failure:** A person moves element X (step 'Move X'), then deletes a large view of 150 boxes and 120 connections (271 writes, 2 revisions). Ctrl+Z, meant to bring the view back, runs 'Undo Move X' instead. X jumps back and the view stays deleted. If the second batch is refused, for example because someone else edited one of the records, half the view's objects are gone while the status line says 'Delete View was refused'.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Send a delete atomically (write(..., { atomic: true })): a plan over 200 writes is refused before anything is written, as Commit and the tools already are. Alternatively, warn in the confirm dialog that it cannot be undone. Either way, clear saved.undo (or push a barrier) when a gesture succeeds but cannot be undone. Report partial success the way openChosen does. Guard: a view.test.mjs case with a fixture broker. Delete a view whose plan has 201 writes and assert one of two outcomes: nothing is written and the refusal is shown, or the Undo button no longer names the earlier gesture.
- **Verifier:** Traced in extensions/archi/view.js: the confirm-delete handler calls write() with atomic=false (:742, :122), writeNow slices into 200-write batches (:143-153), and only pushes an undo step when revisions.length === 1 (:170), leaving saved.undo untouched. undoName() (:220-223) and the toolbar Undo (:792) then name and run the previous gesture, so Ctrl+Z after a >200-write delete undoes an earlier 'Move X'. deletePlan (model.js:266-312) collects every item, connection and property pointing at the doomed view or folder, so a large view or folder crosses 200. The other halves are documented: view.js:106-112 says a gesture over 200 writes is 'not undoable here', and docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:155-157 says deleting a large folder 'still go[es] in batches of 200'. Deletes go in dependency order, so a part-way refusal leaves a consistent but incomplete delete, and it needs a concurrent edit to occur. The missing undo barrier is the one unconsidered consequence; Undo is version-checked and labelled, so it is surprising, not destructive.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. Non-undoability and part-way batches are documented (view.js:106-112, design doc :155-157). The real defect is that saved.undo is not cleared or fenced after a non-undoable success. 'Easily crosses 200' overstates it for single views (typical views hold tens of objects), though a large folder delete crosses it routinely. The part-way refusal needs a stale version, i.e. a concurrent write.

### ABS-09 — Capability Atlas editor silently sets an empty Lifecycle to the first choice whenever any field is saved

**P3** · data-integrity · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:962`, `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:987`
- **What:** edit() fills the lifecycle select with empty=null, so it has no empty option, and its current value is binding.value(record,'lifecycle') ?? binding.choices.lifecycle?.[0]?.id. save() writes every bound choice part from the form: values[field] = form.elements[part].value.trim() \|\| null. For an existing capability whose lifecycle is null, the select shows the first non-retired choice, and saving writes it. cap.lifecycle is not required (tools/bcm-atlas/definition.mjs:16), so capabilities made on Nendo's own record page, by CSV import or by an agent can have none. README.md:111 promises the first choice only for a new capability.
- **Failure:** A capability created in Studio without a lifecycle is opened in the Atlas editor to fix a typo in its definition. Save also sets Lifecycle = Proposed. History shows the change attributed to the package, and the badge and lifecycle-based screens now treat it as Proposed.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Default to the first choice only when record is null (a new capability). For an existing record, add an empty option, '—' or 'Not set', and keep null. Better still, write only fields the person changed, compared with the record's values. Guard: a model or editor case in tools/bcm-atlas (or the Atlas gate's second fixture) that edits a capability with a null lifecycle, changes only the name, and asserts the update's values carry no lifecycle field.
- **Verifier:** extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:962 fills the lifecycle select with empty=null and current = binding.value(record,'lifecycle') ?? choices.lifecycle[0].id, so an existing capability whose lifecycle is null shows the first choice. save() (:987-989) writes every bound choice part from the form, so Save writes that first choice. cap.lifecycle is not required (tools/bcm-atlas/definition.mjs:16) and README.md:111 promises the first choice only for a new capability. Real, but limited: the form visibly shows the value, only capabilities with no lifecycle (for example from a CSV import without that column; Northstar seeds all of them) are affected, and the consequence is a badge and a single field value, so P3 not P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The trigger is a capability with a null lifecycle that is edited through the Atlas editor; the shipped seeds always set lifecycle, so it needs imported or hand-made data.
