### GDN-05 — A checkbox in a numbered list is drawn as a live tick box that saves nothing

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/render.mjs:44`, `extensions/garden/render.mjs:49`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:24`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:542`, `extensions/garden/parse.mjs:11`
- **What:** render() treats any list item, bullet or numbered (render.mjs:44), whose text starts with [ ] as a task and, in the reading view, gives it an enabled checkbox with data-line (49-52). parse()'s CHECKBOX (parse.mjs:11) and toggleTask()'s TASK_LINE (workspace.js:24) accept only - * + bullets, so toggleTask returns at line 542 without changing the body or saving.
- **Failure:** A note says '1. [ ] Call Sam'. While reading, the person ticks the box: it shows ticked, nothing is written, no task record exists, and the next redraw unticks it.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-parse.mjs -> parse tasks of "1. [ ] Call Sam": [] while render(…, {interactive:true}) gives <input type="checkbox" data-line="0" …>; headless Edge (probe-browser.js step B) -> {"checked":true,"dirty":false,"bodyHasX":false,"status":""}, records.batch requests: 0
- **Fix and guard:** Make render agree with parse: draw a task box only for a bullet item (a numbered '[ ]' stays text), or extend CHECKBOX, TASK_LINE and the skill to numbered items together. Guard: a render.test asserting '1. [ ] x' renders no interactive box (or a parse/sync test that it is a task and a tick writes it).
- **Verifier:** render.mjs:44-52 treats any bullet or numbered item whose text starts with [ ]/[x] as a task and, when interactive, emits an enabled checkbox with data-line; workspace.js:24 TASK_LINE and parse.mjs:11 CHECKBOX accept only [-*+] bullets, so toggleTask (workspace.js:541-543) returns at the TASK_LINE test without changing the body or saving, and parse() finds no task. I re-ran the probe: parse tasks of '1. [ ] Call Sam' is [] while render(interactive) yields an enabled <input type=checkbox data-line=0>. No render/parse test covers a numbered item (render.test.mjs:13 only checks a plain <ol>), and help/02-writing.md does not promise numbered tasks. A visible but dead control in a rare notation: P3.
- **Correction:** Either fix is fine (draw a box only for bullet items, or extend CHECKBOX/TASK_LINE/SKILL.md to numbered items). Minor extra mismatch: render accepts an empty task text (`(.*)`) where parse requires `(.+?)`.

### GDN-07 — The renderer drops the # of '# Learning C#' and shows a placeholder for a link whose words are code

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/render.mjs:39`, `extensions/garden/render.mjs:81`, `extensions/garden/render.mjs:92`
- **What:** The heading pattern /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$/ (39) strips a closing run of # even when no space precedes it. Code spans are held as \u0000N\u0000 placeholders before LINK runs (81); the link's words are escaped with the placeholder inside, and the final one-pass replace (92) does not expand placeholders nested in a held anchor.
- **Failure:** A note headed '# Learning C#' reads 'Learning C'. 'Run [`npm ci`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/ci) first.' shows a link whose text is two replacement characters around a 0. Both appear in the reading view, the preview, the hover card and the task strip.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-render2.mjs -> "# Learning C#" => "<h1>Learning C</h1>"; "Run [`npm ci`](…) first." => "<p>Run <a href=…>\u00000\u0000</a> first.</p>"
- **Fix and guard:** Strip a closing hash run only after whitespace (\s+#+\s*$); expand placeholders until none remain (or render a link's words through the code-span pass first). Guard: render.test cases for both shapes.
- **Verifier:** Both defects reproduced by importing extensions/garden/render.mjs in node: '# Learning C#' => <h1>Learning C</h1> (heading regex at render.mjs:39, lazy (.+?) then \s*#*, strips a closing # with no preceding space, which CommonMark does not do), and 'Run [`npm ci`](https://...) first.' => <a ...>\u00000\u0000</a>. inline() holds the code span as a placeholder (render.mjs:69), LINK wraps the still-placeholder label into a second held anchor (81), and the single-pass replace at 92 never re-expands a placeholder nested inside a held value. Reachable in the reading view, preview, hover card and task strip, and [`code`](url) links are common Markdown. Cosmetic, nothing is lost from the stored body, hence P3.
- **Correction:** A browser's HTML parser ignores U+0000 in body text, so the link shows the text '0' rather than two replacement characters around a 0; the substance (the code words are lost) stands.

### GGV-07 — Work dependencies re-enables command buttons with the version it read before the command, so a second command is refused as a conflict nobody caused

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:593`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:600`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:567`
- **What:** act() awaits nendo.commands.run(command.id, node.record) and discards its answer (the record as it now stands). finally sets acting = false and calls showActions(), which re-enables every button on the same stale node.record, then schedule() reads again only 250 ms later plus the loadGraph and layout time. spent() is also judged on the stale values, so the command just applied is not greyed.
- **Failure:** A person presses Start work and then, as soon as the line says it is done, Send to review: the second run is sent at version 1, the host refuses it as record-version-conflict, and the view says 'Item 1 changed since this view read it, so nothing was done' - though the only change was their own. Start work also stays pressable until the re-read lands.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-workdeps2.mjs (second button clicked in-page the moment the first outcome appears) -> after Start work answered: ["start:enabled","review:enabled"]; outcome "Item 1 changed since this view read it, so nothing was done. Reading it again."; run calls [["run","start","n1",1],["run","review","n1",1]].
- **Fix and guard:** Replace node.record in all.nodes and shown.nodes with the record commands.run returns (values and version) before re-enabling, or keep the buttons disabled until the scheduled read has completed. Guard: Review-WorkDependencies presses a second command immediately after the first resolves and asserts it is sent with version 2 and succeeds; falsify by restoring the discarded answer.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end: nendo-api.ts:157-163 counts every edge whose ends are not both among the filtered nodes in hiddenEdges, and no extension reads it (grep finds hiddenEdges only in docs, nendo-api.ts, protocol.ts, reference.ts and the api test). work-dependencies/view.js:685 counts items with no drawn incoming link as unblocked and view.js:648 says 'nothing is blocking it'; systems-lens/lens.js:314 seeds (incoming.length===0) and summarize() at :280-293 call them declared sources. custom-view-authoring.md:304-306 tells a view to 'Say so, rather than draw a graph that looks complete', so the gap is real. Reach is narrower than presented: authoredFilters (nendo-api.ts:343-349) only restricts nodes when the view's definition carries filterClause children, and the shipped Planner Dependencies view has none (tools/planner-definition.mjs:686-691), where hiddenEdges can only count link records with a null end, which block nothing. The view never gates commands on blockers, so the harm is misleading text, not data loss.
- **Correction:** Only views whose definition adds filters (or have links with a null end) are affected; the default Planner view is not. Priority P3, not P2. The Dependency graph variant is just an uncounted-links summary, the least severe of the three.

### MAA-06 — The proposal preview's shape ignores the surface's own eq/ne clauses, so the review states the wrong grid or board size

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-authoring-agent` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentProposals.cs:687`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentProposals.cs:727`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-model.ts:209`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringExamples.cs:567`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:416`
- **What:** ShapeOf counts every option (GroupCount: Options.Count), or every target record for a reference board (target.Records.Count). The renderer draws a lane only when the surface's own filterClause children allow it: reachableGroups removes an option named by ne and keeps only one named by eq, on both matrix axes and on board columns. ShapeOf reads no filterClause, and it does not apply boards.maximumReferenceColumns, above which a reference board draws no columns at all. The person's Agent view renders this string as the surface's shape during review (view-agent.ts:416), and the code's own comment says 'a guessed size is worse in a review than none'.
- **Failure:** The published example a-matrix-and-a-ranking crosses dealStage (4 options) with dealSize (3) and adds dealGridOpen 'dealStage ne Lost'. Its note says 'this grid is three stages wide, not four'. The preview states '4 rows by 3 columns, 12 cells' while the matrix draws 3 by 3, 9 cells. A board with 'status ne Done' over four options previews as '4 columns' and draws 3.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Apply the reachableGroups rule in ShapeOf: drop ne values, keep only an eq value, on each axis and on board columns, and for a reference board above maximumReferenceColumns state that it would draw none. Guard: add an ne clause on an axis field to ASurfaceWhoseSizeCannotBeGuessedStatesItInThePreview (AuthoringErgonomicsTests.cs:198) and assert '3 rows by 2 columns, 6 cells'.
- **Verifier:** ShapeOf (NendoAgentProposals.cs:687-712) counts options via GroupCount (727-732, field.Options.Count, Boolean 2) and never reads the node's filterClause children. The renderer does: surface-model.ts reachableGroups (209-223) drops a value named by ne and keeps only one named by eq, for board columns (boardViewOf, 190) and both matrix axes (matrixViewOf, 251-252); the contract and the published example say the same (NendoAuthoringExamples.cs:567-570: 'this grid is three stages wide, not four'). So the example's dealStage ne Lost yields '4 rows by 3 columns, 12 cells' in the review (view-agent.ts:416 prints surface.shape) while the grid draws 3 by 3. The code's own comment (722-726) says a count is stated only where exact. No test covers an ne/eq clause: the fixture ShapeProbeSurfaceOperations (CrmAuthoringFixture.cs:227-245) has no filterClause and AuthoringErgonomicsTests.cs:232-244 asserts only unfiltered shapes.
- **Correction:** The reference-board ceiling part is partly mitigated: SemanticDiff.cs:945 already says a reference board draws nothing above MaximumReferenceBoardColumns (24), so the review still carries that fact in the diff line, though ShapeOf's 'N of them' is silent about it. Priority is P3: a reviewer sees an overstated cell or column count in a summary line; the file itself is unaffected.

### MAA-10 — Required payload keys are published but not enforced, so leaving out setLook's letter or setPurpose's purpose silently resets it

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-authoring-agent`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:1213`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:99`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:93`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:135`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:9`
- **What:** ValidateOperation refuses unknown keys but never checks that the table's RequiredPayload keys are present. application.setLook lists tone and letter as required, application.setPurpose lists purpose, and application.setNewFileLabel lists label. The Engine binds each with OptionalString, so a missing key becomes null, and null means 'return to the default' (SetApplicationLookOperation) or 'clear' (purpose and label). The class comment calls the table 'both the published description and the enforced allowlist'.
- **Failure:** An agent recolours the file with application.setLook {tone:'teal'}. The add is accepted, and on acceptance the letter the person chose earlier silently reverts to the default from the file name. An application.setPurpose sent as {} clears the purpose.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In ValidateOperation, refuse a payload missing any RequiredPayload key, naming the key and saying that null is how to clear it. Guard: an InputSchemaContractTests/AuthoringErgonomicsTests case sending setLook without letter that expects NENDO_INVALID_REQUEST naming 'letter'.
- **Verifier:** Traced. ValidateOperation (NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:1213-1226) checks only unknown keys against AllowedPayloads, never RequiredPayload. The remaining gate, RequireCompilable -> NendoCanonicalOperations.Check, binds application.setLook with OptionalString(tone)/OptionalString(letter) (CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:135-137), setPurpose with OptionalString(purpose) (:147-148) and setNewFileLabel with OptionalString(label) (:144-145). OptionalString returns null for an absent key (:346-349). The operations treat null as 'default' or 'clear' (ApplicationLook.cs:93-99, 'A null part returns to the default'). So setLook {tone:'teal'} is accepted and resets the letter, and setPurpose {} clears the purpose, although NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:95,101,107 publish those keys as required. NullableBoolean (:374-379) shows the Engine can demand an explicit null elsewhere. Mitigation: the proposal summary carries LookBefore/LookAfter and PurposeBefore/PurposeAfter, so the person sees the change at review; at Unattended the agent accepts its own call. Low-impact consistency gap, P3.
- **Correction:** The same gap covers schema.setFieldSequence (prefix and width listed as required at NendoAuthoringOperations.cs:82 but bound with OptionalString/OptionalLong at CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:121-123, so omitting both removes the sequence). The fix should treat the whole set of OptionalString-bound required keys, not three.

### MAA-11 — A chunked package file whose first part carries sha256 fails at validate, because the join keeps that hash beside the whole file

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-authoring-agent`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:1069`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:1030`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:303`
- **What:** RequireAppendTargets refuses sha256 only on an append chunk. The first putFile of a file may carry text or base64 plus sha256, which the Engine treats as a check against the bytes sent (Checked), so add accepts it when the hash matches that first part. JoinChunks rebuilds the first put by removing only text, base64 and append, then writes base64 of the joined bytes. sha256 stays, so the joined operation fails Checked with 'extension.putFile sha256 does not match the bytes sent for {path}' at validate.
- **Failure:** An agent sends a 300 KiB view.js as a first putFile of text plus sha256 of that 96 KiB part, accepted at add, followed by two append chunks. validate answers NENDO_INVALID_REQUEST with a hash mismatch for bytes the agent never sent together, and no operation is named.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In JoinChunks, drop sha256 (and byteLength) from the first put when chunks join it, or refuse sha256 on any put that a later chunk extends, at the add that sends the chunk. Guard: an ExtensionPackageProtocolTests case with sha256 on the first part of a chunked file, requiring validate to be previewable or the add to be refused by name.
- **Verifier:** Traced. At add, RequireAppendTargets (NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:1030-1038) refuses sha256 only on an append chunk, and RequireCompilable calls NendoCanonicalOperations.Check on the first put alone, where ExtensionPutFile's Checked (CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:269-297) passes because the hash matches that part's bytes. At validate, Compile (:838) calls JoinChunks, which rebuilds the first put dropping only text/base64/append (:1071-1073) and writes base64 of the joined bytes, leaving sha256 in place. The Engine binding then finds base64 plus sha256 and Checked throws 'extension.putFile sha256 does not match the bytes sent for {path}' (:292-295). Defect is real in the join, and it fails closed (a refusal, no corruption). The trigger is atypical: sha256 beside text/base64 is an Engine-side check that the putFile summary does not advertise, and no existing test sends it, so P3.
- **Correction:** The refusal does name the file path (not 'no operation is named'), though not the mutation ordinal. The cause is not visible from that text, since the agent hashed what it sent.

### MTD-03 — references by matchFieldId do not follow the CSV matchFieldId rule they claim to: integer codes are always refused, text codes match case-sensitively, and a JSON import cannot name its own rows

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:207`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:255`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:612`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringContracts.cs:31`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:710`, `src/Nendo.Engine/RecordQuerySemantics.cs:54`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:122`
- **What:** ResolveReferencesAsync looks a code up with Filters = [eq, JsonSerializer.SerializeToElement(reference.Value)], and NendoReferenceInput.Value is a string. For a unique Integer field (ADR-0020 allows 'a single-line Text field or a plain Integer field' to be unique) the filter value goes through ConvertValue, where GetInt64 on a JSON string throws and is refused as 'Value for field X does not match storage kind Integer'. For a Text field, RecordQuerySemantics.Compare uses StringComparer.Ordinal, while the unique index is COLLATE NOCASE and the CSV resolver indexes codes with OrdinalIgnoreCase; the in-batch Holds() is Ordinal too. A JSON import maps every record with ToEntryAsync and no earlier rows, so a reference to another row of the same import is looked up in the store and not found. NendoRecordInput.References' description says 'The rule CSV import's matchFieldId follows', and the CSV rule resolves integer codes, ignores case and resolves the import's own rows.
- **Failure:** (1) Project has a unique Integer field projectNo = 42. create_record for a Task with references {project: {matchFieldId: projectNo, value: '42'}} is refused NENDO_INVALID_REQUEST 'Value for field projectNo does not match storage kind Integer'; there is no way to send the value as a number because value must be a string. (2) Project code 'PRJ-1'; references value 'prj-1' answers NENDO_TARGET_NOT_FOUND 'No Project record holds prj-1 in code', although uniqueness treats the two as equal and a CSV import with the same cell resolves it. (3) A JSON import of a folder tree whose children name their parent by code via references fails with target-not-found, while the same rows as CSV import parents first.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Resolve a matchFieldId through one shared resolver with the CSV path: convert the text to the match field's storage kind (parse Integer, refuse a non-integer by name), compare Text case-insensitively as the unique index does, and for a JSON import index the import's own rows as CsvCodeResolver does. Guard: data-tool tests for an integer code, a differently cased text code (create_record, apply_writes in-batch, JSON import) and a JSON import tree; falsify by reverting each branch.
- **Verifier:** All three divergences trace through. (1) ResolveReferencesAsync builds Filters=[eq, SerializeToElement(reference.Value)] (NendoDataMutationService.cs:207-210) and Value is a string (NendoAuthoringContracts.cs:48). QueryRecordsAsync runs ValidateRecordQuery, which calls ConvertValue on the match field (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:518-520). For an Integer field ConvertValue does value.GetInt64() on a JSON string (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:710), which throws InvalidOperationException and is rewritten as 'does not match storage kind Integer' (:739-743). A unique Integer field is allowed (docs/contracts/relationships.md:84), and the CSV resolver handles it via RecordQuerySemantics.Text (CsvReferenceCodes.cs:132). (2) The filter predicate is RecordQuerySemantics.Matches, which compares Text with StringComparer.Ordinal (SqliteNendoStore.HierarchyReads.cs:33-35, RecordQuerySemantics.cs:54). The unique index is COLLATE NOCASE (FieldRules.cs:90), the CSV resolver uses OrdinalIgnoreCase (CsvReferenceCodes.cs:124,139), and ADR-0020's W-075 amendment says codes are compared 'without regard to case'. (3) ToEntryAsync is called with no earlier rows in ImportRecordsAsync (NendoImportService.cs:218-221) and CreateRecordsAsync (NendoDataMutationService.cs:113); only apply_writes passes `earlier`. docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md and the references description say the CSV rule is 'now one rule for both formats', so the code contradicts the contract. Downgraded to P3 because every case is a loud, named refusal (no silent wrong write) with a workaround: look up the record ID by a read and pass recordId, or pass the parent's ID in values with expectedTargetVersions {field: 1} for a same-import parent. It also needs an unusual schema (unique Integer match field) or a case mismatch.
- **Correction:** The case-sensitive comparison is also mirrored in the in-batch Holds() on purpose ('as the screens' eq filter would compare it'). It is still a divergence from the ADR-0020 amendment. The own-rows limitation applies equally to create_records, not only to a JSON import. Integer matching works in-batch (Holds accepts Number tokens) but not against the store.

### MTD-12 — The CSV import path skips limits.recordValueBytes and recordValuesBytes, which every other agent write enforces

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoImportService.cs:164`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:757`
- **What:** ReadValue and ReadValueMap refuse a value over 32 KiB and a record over 64 KiB for create, update, apply_writes and JSON import. ImportCsvAsync builds NendoCreateRecordEntry from DecodeCsvRowsAsync's values directly, so a cell up to the CSV profile's 64 Ki characters is written unchecked. The vocabulary publishes the value bound as 'The most one submitted field value may hold'.
- **Failure:** The same 40 KB note is refused as NENDO_VALUE_TOO_LARGE when imported with format json and accepted with format csv; an agent told the bound is 32 KiB cannot predict which import succeeds, and the published limit is not a limit.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Apply the same StoredBytes checks to each decoded CSV row before the first batch, naming row and field; or document the bound as JSON-only. Guard: an import test with a 40 KB cell in each format asserting identical outcomes.
- **Verifier:** Traced. The 32 KiB value and 64 KiB value-map caps are enforced only in the adapter's ReadValue/ReadValueMap (src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:718-772), which create, update, apply_writes and the JSON import reach via ToEntryAsync (line 136). ImportCsvAsync builds NendoCreateRecordEntry straight from DecodeCsvRowsAsync's row.Values (NendoImportService.cs:164-178) and never calls them. The Engine has no value-size bound of its own (grep of src/Nendo.Engine finds none; SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs only converts the value), NendoCsvProfile.Decode returns the cell unchanged for Text (CsvProfile.cs:131), and the only CSV bound is 65,536 characters per cell (CsvProfile.cs:53,101), so a 40 KB cell is written. The published statement, docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:212-217 and SemanticVocabulary.cs:1021-1029, is 'inside a record write, one value holds at most limits.recordValueBytes', with no CSV exemption, and the csv.md contract only names the 64 Ki-character cell limit for the native importer. The 256 KiB request body bounds the damage, so this is an inconsistency, not a safety hole. P3.
- **Correction:** Note the Engine stores any size, so the cap is purely an adapter rule; an exact-parity fix would need to count UTF-8 bytes per decoded cell and per row (cells over 32 KiB bytes can occur well below the 64 Ki-character cell limit when non-ASCII).

<a id="mtd-13"></a>

### MTD-13 — An empty recordId= or filter= on the records read returns an unrelated page instead of being refused by name

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoResourceProjection.cs:240`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoResourceProjection.cs:306`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoResourceQuery.cs:16`
- **What:** NendoResourceQuery keeps every empty value except cursor so 'the read [can] refuse by name'. GetRecordsAsync then maps a blank recordId to null and ParseFiltersAsync returns no filters for a blank filter, so both silently widen the read to the whole type, while an empty sort= is refused.
- **Failure:** An agent builds nendo://application/entity/task/records?recordId={id} with an empty id and takes items[0] with its recordVersion as 'the record'; it then edits the first task in ID order. The same happens with an empty filter that should have narrowed the read.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Refuse a present-but-blank recordId and filter ('recordId names one record'), matching sort. Guard: resource tests for ?recordId= and ?filter= asserting NENDO_INVALID_REQUEST.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoResourceQuery.Canonicalize (NendoResourceQuery.cs:63-65) drops only an empty cursor, so ?recordId= reaches GetRecordsAsync as an empty string; NendoResourceProjection.cs:240 maps it to RecordId=null and ParseFiltersAsync (:306) returns [] for a blank filter, so both read the whole type. Line 230 (`sort is not null` then RequireAsync("")) does refuse an empty sort, so the inconsistency is real. No test pins the widening (tests only use non-empty recordId). Weakened by the fact that blank-as-omitted is the project's convention for fields, desc and newestFirst (docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:286 'Omitted or empty, the record is whole'; NendoResourceProjection.cs:234), and the response is a multi-record page with nextCursor rather than one record, so only a client that already built a bad URI is hit.
- **Correction:** Low-impact footgun, not a regression: the NendoResourceQuery comment ('every other empty value stays a value, for the read to refuse by name') describes canonicalization, and the blank-to-null mapping at :240 is deliberate coding that matches the documented blank-equals-omitted convention for other parameters. The empty-sort refusal at :230 is probably an accident of RequireAsync rather than a designed rule, since :241 also maps blank sort to null. Fix stays as proposed (refuse a present-but-blank recordId, and probably filter).

### R2AAV-02 — A choice that mixes a whole number and a decimal is typed Decimal but evaluated in Int64, so it overflows where decimal arithmetic would answer

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adr-and-vision-conformance`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourVisitor.cs:98`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:129`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/ExpressionAdapter.cs:240`, `docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md:842`
- **What:** The analyzer types `c ? <Integer> : <Decimal>` as Decimal (BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:129). BehaviourEvaluationVisitor.Visit(TernaryExpression) returns the selected branch's raw value (lines 98-110), a boxed long when the Integer branch is taken. The enclosing `+ - * %` then runs EvaluationHelper on long and long with OverflowProtection. The only widening is in Calculate (ExpressionAdapter.cs:240-242), and it applies to the root result, not to an operand. The contract says `+ - * %` produce 'decimal if either side is', and the side is statically decimal.
- **Failure:** A calculation `(useOverride ? units : 0.5) * 2` with units = 9223372036854775807 reports calculation-overflow, although its static type is Decimal and the decimal result 18446744073709551614 is in range. The same applies to `-(c ? x : 0.5)` at Int64.MinValue and `(c ? x : y) + 1` with y a Decimal field.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: formula-probe.ps1 cases5.json -> '(true ? x : 0.5) * 2 => static=Decimal EVAL-ERROR [NendoCalculationException calculation-overflow]' (x=9223372036854775807), while 'x * 2' with x a Decimal 9223372036854775807 => 'static=Decimal value=Decimal 18446744073709551614'; '-(true ? x : 0.5) => static=Decimal EVAL-ERROR ... calculation-overflow' (x=Int64.MinValue).
- **Fix and guard:** Have the analyzer record, by reference, each TernaryExpression it types Decimal from mixed numeric branches, carry that set on ValidatedExpression, and widen a long branch result to decimal in Visit(TernaryExpression) for those nodes. Guard: a BehaviourScalarTests case `(true ? x : 0.5) * 2` at Int64.MaxValue expecting Decimal 18446744073709551614, falsified by removing the widening.
- **Verifier:** BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:129 types a choice with Integer and Decimal outcomes as Decimal, but BehaviourVisitor.cs:98-110 returns the taken branch's raw value (a boxed long for the Integer branch), so the enclosing operator in ExpressionAdapter.EvaluateBinary (:347-350) runs EvaluationHelper on long operands under OverflowProtection. The only widening is at the root (ExpressionAdapter.cs:240-242). I re-ran the probe against the built Engine: '(true ? x : 0.5) * 2' with x=Int64.Max gives static=Decimal and EVAL-ERROR calculation-overflow, while 'x * 2' with x a Decimal gives 18446744073709551614. This contradicts calculations-and-actions.md:842 ('decimal if either side is').
- **Correction:** Reachability is limited to Integer values within a factor of two of the Int64 limits (or exactly Int64.Max/Min for + and -), so it is a boundary-exactness defect, not a common-path one; P3 is right. No existing test covers a mixed-type choice at the Int64 boundary.

<a id="r2aav-06"></a>

### R2AAV-06 — acrossSubtree related aggregates never enforce ADR-0019's 10,000-descendant bound: the LIMIT counts only the related rows, so a 20,000-record subtree is answered

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adr-and-vision-conformance`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:371`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:359`, `docs/decisions/0019-hierarchies-in-the-schema.md:152`, `docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md:144`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/HierarchyTests.cs:503`
- **What:** SubtreeAggregateAsync builds one recursive CTE `sub` over the descendants. For a SubtreeAggregate the LIMIT @limit (10,001) applies to the descendants themselves (line 361). For RelatedAggregate with acrossSubtree it applies to the related rows `r` (line 371), so the CTE walks every descendant without any bound. ADR-0019 point 7 says both forms 'are bounded at 10,000 descendants and refuse past it by name', and design driver 3 says 'A deep or wide tree is refused by name, not answered slowly'. The tree read and descendantOf refuse past 10,000 records. PastTheDescendantBoundEveryReadRefusesRatherThanAnswerInPart covers SubtreeAggregate, the tree read and descendantOf, never acrossSubtree. The bound also counts the wrong quantity the other way: a node with 5 descendants and 10,001 links is refused as 'More than 10000 records ... across the hierarchy'. With includeSelf (line 359), a node with exactly 10,000 descendants is refused because the record itself is counted.
- **Failure:** A capability root with 20,000 descendants and three linked applications: 'applications supporting this capability or anything under it' (acrossSubtree Count) answers 3 after walking all 20,000. The same root's 'capabilities inside' (SubtreeAggregate Count) is an error, and its tree read and descendantOf filter are refused. One file gives two answers about whether this subtree is too wide.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python subtree_bound_probe.py (replays the SQL of SubtreeAggregateAsync lines 345-371 on an in-memory SQLite table with the production index shape) -> 'descendants under root: 20000'; 'acrossSubtree rows read: 3 (refused only if > 10000) -> ANSWERED in 16.8 ms'; 'SubtreeAggregate rows read: 10001 -> REFUSED'
- **Fix and guard:** Bound the descendant walk itself for both forms: count `sub` with LIMIT 10,001 (as HierarchyReads does) and refuse past 10,000 before folding. Keep the related-row bound for acrossSubtree as a separate, named refusal, and exclude the record itself from the descendant count under includeSelf. Guard: add acrossSubtree Count and Sum to PastTheDescendantBoundEveryReadRefusesRatherThanAnswerInPart over 10,001 descendants with one link, expecting an error, falsified by removing the new count.
- **Verifier:** SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:353-372: for SubtreeAggregate the LIMIT @limit (bound+1 = 10,001) applies to the descendant rows themselves, so FoldAsync (:457-463) throws LimitReached at row 10,001; for RelatedAggregate with acrossSubtree the same LIMIT applies to the related rows 'r' and the descendants appear only in an IN (SELECT id FROM sub ...) subquery, so no descendant count is taken. ADR-0019 point 7 (:151-153) says both forms are 'bounded at 10,000 descendants and refuse past it by name'. HierarchyTests.cs:503-526 covers SubtreeAggregate Count, the tree read and descendantOf past the bound but never acrossSubtree. I re-ran the reviewer's SQLite replay: 20,000 descendants with 3 links gives ANSWERED (3 rows) for acrossSubtree and REFUSED for SubtreeAggregate.
- **Correction:** Two overstatements. (1) The CTE walk is not an unbounded-work differential: SQLite materialises 'sub' fully for the IN in both forms before LIMIT trips, so both walk all 20,000 descendants; the real difference is only refuse versus answer. The answer is exact, never partial, so no wrong value results. (2) calculations-and-actions.md:144-146 says 'the hierarchy's own limit of 10,000 records' and the error text says 'More than N records contribute ... across the hierarchy', which fits bounding the contributing related rows, so the '5 descendants and 10,001 links is refused' and includeSelf-off-by-one points are consistent with the shipped message; only ADR-0019's 'descendants' wording is contradicted. Keep P3 (spec drift plus a missing guard, no data risk).

<a id="r2aav-07"></a>

### R2AAV-07 — A ranking decides ties by JavaScript numbers, so two different exact values share a rank numeral

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adr-and-vision-conformance`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:270`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:302`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-overview.ts:152`, `docs/decisions/0004-versioned-semantic-ui-contract.md:1012`, `docs/contracts/scalars.md:25`
- **What:** rankedRowsMarkup maps each row through rankValue, which does Number(lexeme) on the exact $nendoNumber lexeme (charts.ts:302-308). rankNumerals then gives equal numerals to adjacent values that compare === as doubles (charts.ts:270-279). ADR-0004 S6 says 'Equal numbers share a numeral', and the scalar contract keeps Integer and Decimal values exact. Integers past 2^53, or decimals that differ beyond about 17 significant digits, become the same double. The host's sort orders them correctly, and the numerals then contradict that order.
- **Failure:** A top-ten by Value lists 9007199254740993 above 9007199254740992 (the host's exact order) and labels both '1', reading as a tie. The same happens with decimals 0.30000000000000000001 and 0.3. A screen reader hears 'ranked 1' for both.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node bundle-charts.mjs (vite SSR bundle of src/charts.ts into the scratch folder) -> 'rankValue of ["9007199254740993","9007199254740992","0.30000000000000000001","0.3"] -> [9007199254740992,9007199254740992,0.3,0.3]'; 'rankNumerals([9007199254740993, 9007199254740992]) -> [1,1]'; 'rankNumerals([0.30000000000000000001, 0.3]) -> [1,1]'
- **Fix and guard:** Compare the exact lexemes for ties (normalise sign, leading and trailing zeros, then compare strings, or use a BigInt and scale comparison), and keep Number only for the bar width. Guard: a charts test where rankNumerals over the lexemes 9007199254740993 and 9007199254740992 gives [1,2], falsified by restoring the Number comparison.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. view-overview.ts:151-152 calls rankValue on each record's rank field, and charts.ts:302-308 turns the exact $nendoNumber lexeme into a JS double with Number(lexeme). rankNumerals (charts.ts:270-279) then gives equal numerals when value === previous. Two distinct Int64 values such as 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993 become the same double, so adjacent rows get the same numeral and the aria-label says 'ranked 1' for both. The window order comes from the host's orderByFieldId read, and SQLite compares Int64 exactly. The tests (grids.test.mjs:95-98, 114-119) only use small numbers. ADR-0004 line 1012 says 'Equal numbers share a numeral', so two different numbers sharing one contradicts it. Only the rank numeral is wrong: the exact amount still shows beside each row. It needs a rank field with values past 2^53 or decimals that differ beyond about 17 significant digits, which is rare. scalars.md:26-27 bans JS numbers only in the edit and transport paths, so it is not the contract being broken, only ADR-0004's tie rule.
- **Correction:** The decimal half of the scenario is unproven. Whether the host orders near-equal Decimal values exactly depends on the typed decimal sorting scalars.md:55 requires, and I did not trace it. The Integer case alone establishes the defect. Priority P3, or lower given how unlikely the values are.

<a id="r2ap-03"></a>

### R2AP-03 — Value-size limits exist only in the MCP adapter: the person's forms, the Studio grid, the native CSV import and every custom-view write store values an agent may not write back

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adapter-parity` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:14`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:757`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticVocabulary.cs:1014`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:696`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:246`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:780`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:208`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:83`
- **What:** limits.recordValueBytes (32 KiB) and limits.recordValuesBytes (64 KiB) are enforced in NendoDataMutationService.ReadValue/ReadValueMap and nowhere else. NendoApplicationService and the store's ConvertValue accept any text length. The Desktop bridge only caps the whole message at 262,144 characters and clones values unchecked; the broker's valuesParam checks kinds, not size; the Studio grid's large-text editor allows 1,000,000 characters; the native CSV batch allows 64 Ki characters per cell. So the same Engine operation is refused through MCP and accepted through the other two adapters. Not MTD-12 (the MCP CSV path skipping the MCP limits); this is the Desktop and view paths having none, which makes values agents cannot round-trip.
- **Failure:** A person writes a 40,000-character Markdown note in Studio, or the Garden view saves a long note body. An agent reads the record, appends one sentence and calls update_record with the body: NENDO_VALUE_TOO_LARGE. An agent that exports records and re-imports them as JSON, or copies a record with apply_writes, is refused for values the file already holds.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratchpad r2-adapter-parity/probe-engine.ps1 -> 'Engine SetField 40,000-character notes (Desktop and view path) -> OK' and 'MCP adapter ReadValue on the same 40,000-character value -> [value-too-large] The value of field.idea.notes is 40000 bytes, and a value may hold at most 32768 (limits.recordValueBytes ...)'. The Desktop and broker paths add no size check (source).
- **Fix and guard:** Enforce the value bounds once, in NendoApplicationService (create, create many, set field, set fields, record writes, CSV decode) with the same value-too-large / values-too-large codes, so every adapter refuses identically and the MCP adapter stops being the only gate; or raise the MCP limit to what the Engine stores. Guard: one Engine test writing a 40,000-byte value through SetFieldsAsync and ApplyRecordWritesAsync expecting value-too-large, plus a Desktop bridge test for data.setFields and a broker test for records.update expecting the same code.
- **Verifier:** The 32 KiB per-value and 64 KiB per-write caps are enforced only in NendoDataMutationService.ReadValue/ReadValueMap (:718-772; limits at :14-16 and SemanticVocabulary.cs:1014-1015). The Engine's ConvertValue (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:~696-740) converts a Text value of any length, and nothing in NendoApplicationService checks size. The Desktop bridge only caps the whole message at 262,144 characters (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:246,288) and ClonedValues (:780) clones unchecked; the Studio large-text editor allows 1,000,000 characters (view-data.ts:83) and the native CSV cell cap is 64 Ki characters (CsvProfile.cs:53). So a 40,000-character note the person or Garden saves is stored, and an agent's update_record that sends it back gets NENDO_VALUE_TOO_LARGE. Real parity gap, but the agent cap is a published, clearly worded bound on agent input (mcp-interface.md:212-217; the 256 KiB body cap bounds it anyway), the refusal names the field, cap and size, and only values over 32 KiB are affected, so it is friction rather than a broken invariant.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3. The ADRs do not mandate or discuss the 32 KiB cap, so it is not a documented trade-off, but the same finding family was rated P3 for the CSV path (MTD-12 in FIXES.md). The Desktop path is effectively bounded at about 256 K characters per message, not unbounded, so 'stores values an agent may not write back' is accurate only above 32 KiB and below that ceiling.

<a id="r2ap-06"></a>

### R2AP-06 — An agent's redo is recorded in History as 'Undo …', identical to the undo it reverses, while a view's redo of the same chain is 'Redo …'

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-adapter-parity`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataMutationService.cs:423`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:183`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:262`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDataTools.cs:260`
- **What:** The compensation's History name is caller.Label ?? (caller.Redo ? 'Redo ' : 'Undo ') + StepName(description, isCompensation), and StepName strips a leading 'Undo '/'Redo ' from a compensation's description. The broker's records.redo sends redo: true; NendoDataMutationService.UndoRevisionAsync always sends Redo: false, though the tool says 'a compensation can itself be undone, which is redo'. So undoing 'Undo Edit Idea Title' through MCP is named 'Undo ' + 'Edit Idea Title'.
- **Failure:** An agent edits a title, undoes it, then redoes it (undo_revision on the undo's revision). History shows two consecutive entries both called 'Undo Edit Idea Title' by the same agent, so the person cannot tell from History whether the edit is currently in place.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratchpad r2-adapter-parity/probe-engine.ps1 section 6 -> "agent write: 'Edit Idea Title' \| agent undo: 'Undo Edit Idea Title' \| agent redo: 'Undo Edit Idea Title'" and "view write: 'Edit Idea Title' \| view undo: 'Undo Edit Idea Title' \| view redo: 'Redo Edit Idea Title'"
- **Fix and guard:** Name the step by what it reverses rather than by the caller's flag: a compensation of an 'Undo …' step is 'Redo …' and of a 'Redo …' step 'Undo …' (or have the MCP adapter set Redo when the target revision is an undo, without the view's not-an-undo restriction). Guard: UndoRevisionToolTests asserts the redo's History description starts with 'Redo '.
- **Verifier:** NendoDataMutationService.UndoRevisionAsync always sends Redo: false (NendoDataMutationService.cs:423), though the tool says an undo can itself be undone as a redo (NendoDataTools.cs:260). The Engine allows that call, since only Redo:true on a non-compensation is refused (Compensation.cs:110), and names the step caller.Label ?? (caller.Redo ? 'Redo ' : 'Undo ') + StepName(description, isCompensation) (:183-185). StepName (:262-265) strips the leading 'Undo ' from the undo's description, so an agent's redo of 'Undo Edit Idea Title' is again 'Undo Edit Idea Title', while a view's redo is 'Redo Edit Idea Title' (asserted for views at DesktopExtensionWriterTests.cs:140 and RecordWritesUndoTests.cs:43; nothing asserts the agent's redo name, and UndoRevisionToolTests.cs:93 only checks the version). Two consecutive identical History entries result. Cosmetic: the data and the compensation link are correct, and the agent can pass a label.
- **Correction:** Polish-level P3. The tool's label parameter says an omitted label is 'Undo and the revision's description', so the wording is partly documented; the defect is that the redo is not named for what it does.

### R2LAT-02 — Search cannot find words in Thai, Chinese or Japanese text: unicode61 never segments them, and shreds Thai at every vowel sign; Turkish ı never matches I

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Search.cs:26`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Search.cs:120`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Search.cs:327`
- **What:** The index is FTS5 with tokenize = 'unicode61 remove_diacritics 2' (Search.cs store line 26), used for writable files and, through SearchSnapshotAsync, for read-only files. unicode61 splits only on Unicode separators and punctuation: a run of CJK characters is one token, and Thai vowel signs and tone marks (category Mn) are treated as separators, so Thai text is cut into meaningless fragments. ADR-0028's first driver is 'Search must find a word in any text field' and it records no language limitation. SearchTerms.Parse also drops any token where no UTF-16 code unit is IsLetterOrDigit (Search.cs:120), which silently drops a term made only of astral-plane letters. Turkish dotless ı is not folded to i while I is folded to i, so Turkish lowercase spelling never matches a capitalised word.
- **Failure:** A note 'ฉันชอบกินข้าวผัดที่ร้านนี้' is not found by searching 'ข้าวผัด' (fried rice), while unrelated fragments such as 'ร้าน' match by accident; a Japanese note '東京都に住んでいます' is found by '東京' (prefix of the whole run) but not by '住んで'; a Chinese note '北京大学的学生' is not found by '学生'. This affects Ctrl K, Studio search, the @ menu, Garden Find and nendo search over MCP. A Turkish user searching 'ığdır' does not find 'Iğdır'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python fts_probe.py / fts_vocab.py in the scratch folder against SQLite 3.50.4 FTS5 with the same tokenizer string -> '"ข้าวผัด"' -> [], '"住んで"*' -> [], '"学生"*' -> [], '"東京"*' -> [2], '"ıgdır"' -> []; fts5vocab tokens for the Thai row: ['ฉ', 'ดท', 'นข', 'นชอบก', 'ร', 'านน', 'าวผ'], for CJK: ['北京大学的学生', '東京都に住んでいます'], for 'Iğdır': ['igdır']
- **Fix and guard:** Index scripts without word separators so a word inside a run can match: add a second FTS5 column or table with tokenize='trigram' (SQLite 3.34+, in e_sqlite3) and route a term containing Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Han, Hiragana, Katakana or Hangul characters to it, or pre-segment those runs into character bigrams on both the indexed text and the query. Normalise ı/İ for the fold or document it. Count letters by Rune, not char, in SearchTerms.Parse. Record the limitation in ADR-0028 and queries.md until fixed. Guard: SearchIndexTests cases for a Thai, a Japanese and a Chinese word in the middle of a sentence (each must be found, and a fragment such as 'ร้าน' must not match 'ข้าวผัด'), falsified against the current tokenizer.
- **Verifier:** Reproduced the tokenizer behaviour myself (python sqlite 3.50.4, fts5 `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, prefix='2 3', in verify/r2-locale-and-time-1/fts_probe_v1.py): '"ข้าวผัด"' -> [], '"住んで"*' -> [], '"学生"*' -> [], '"東京"*' -> [2]; fts5vocab shows the Thai row shredded into ['ฉ','ดท','นข','นชอบก','ร','านน','าวผ'] and the CJK rows kept as one token each; 'Iğdır' indexes as 'igdır' so a typed 'ığdır' misses it. The tokenizer string is exactly what the Engine creates (SqliteNendoStore.Search.cs:26), and SearchTerms.Parse adds no segmentation (Search.cs:120-135 only splits on whitespace/quotes). So a word inside a Thai/Chinese/Japanese sentence is not findable. However, the tokenizer is chosen by accepted ADR-0028 (Decision section, 'unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'), and the product has no localisation goal in vision/roadmap (English UI, Danish owner), so this is an unrecorded limitation of a deliberate choice, not an implementation bug. ADR-0028 driver 1 ('find a word in any text field') is silently unmet for non-segmenting scripts, and nothing records it, which AGENTS.md says to do. P3, not P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The remedy within current authority is to record the limitation (ADR-0028 negative consequences / roadmap / queries.md); switching to trigram or bigram indexing changes the protected layout and needs a new ADR. The Turkish dotless-i point and the astral-plane-only-term drop (char.IsLetterOrDigit on a lone surrogate) are real but marginal and should not carry the priority.

### R2LAT-08 — Fold dates disagree: the fold dialog and History show the local date, the checkpoint text shows the UTC date, and the 'history was folded on' refusal uses the regional calendar (Buddhist, Hijri or Persian year)

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:96`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.HistoryFold.cs:191`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.HistoryFold.cs:130`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.NewFile.cs:390`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:463`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-history.ts:47`
- **What:** Revision timestamps are stored in UTC (SqliteNendoStore.cs:1084), and the checkpoint description is written with {plan.FirstAt:yyyy-MM-dd} to {plan.LastAt:yyyy-MM-dd} under InvariantCulture (HistoryFold.cs:191-192; NewFile.cs:390-392), which prints UTC dates. The confirm dialog prints the same instants with new Date(value).toLocaleDateString() (actions.ts:463), and History's 'last folded on' does the same (view-history.ts:47), which are local dates. The compensation refusal interpolates {fold.FoldedAt:yyyy-MM-dd} without InvariantCulture (Compensation.cs:96), so the 'yyyy' uses the CurrentCulture calendar. HistoryFold.cs:130 formats the 'nothing to fold' reason with {fresh:N0} under CurrentCulture, which the Workbench shows verbatim.
- **Failure:** The newest folded change was saved at 00:30 on 12 October in Copenhagen: the dialog says the fold covers changes 'to 12.10.2026', and the checkpoint entry in History then says 'to 2026-10-11'. In Apia, every change before 13:00 is dated a day earlier in the checkpoint. On a machine with Thai, Saudi or Persian regional format, Compensate on a folded revision says 'Its older history was folded on 2569-10-11', '1448-04-30' or '1405-07-19', and the reason line reads '1٬234 changes' with an Arabic thousands separator.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh, formatting DateTimeOffset 2026-10-11T10:00Z with '{0:yyyy-MM-dd}' under CurrentCulture -> th-TH: calendar=ThaiBuddhistCalendar -> folded on 2569-10-11; ar-SA: calendar=UmAlQuraCalendar -> folded on 1448-04-30; fa-IR: calendar=PersianCalendar -> folded on 1405-07-19; (1234567).ToString('N0') under ar-SA -> 1٬234٬567
- **Fix and guard:** Format Compensation.cs:96 and HistoryFold.cs:130 with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture (string.Create as the other fold texts do), and pick one civil zone for fold dates: either write the dates the person sees (local) into the checkpoint text, or make the Workbench show the stored UTC date with a 'UTC' label. Guard: an Engine test that runs the refusal under CultureInfo th-TH and asserts 2026, and a Workbench test that the dialog's dates equal the checkpoint's for an instant just after local midnight.
- **Verifier:** surface-preview.ts:86 calls sampleBucketed(node, app.records, new Date()), and charts.ts:470-479 resolves the bounds with getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate. The Engine resolves the same words against the local date (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193 with DateBuckets.Resolve, DateBuckets.cs:54-62). Near local midnight the two dates differ; at 00:30 on 1 Nov in Copenhagen, local is 1 Nov and UTC is 31 Oct (node probe). The leap-day claim I reproduced: preview lastTwelveMonths on 2028-02-29 starts 2027-03-02 (Date.UTC(2027,1,30) rolls over), while .NET DateOnly(2028,2,29).AddYears(-1).AddDays(1) is 2027-03-01 and spans 366 days (pwsh probe). The test (over-time.test.mjs:171-180) passes a fixed UTC midnight, so it never exercises either difference. This affects only the proposal preview's bucket bounds, so P3.

### R2LAT-09 — Help search depends on letter case under a Turkish or Azerbaijani display language: toLocaleLowerCase turns 'I' into dotless 'ı', so 'Import' finds 2 topics instead of 8 and 'inspect' misses the topics that only say 'Inspect'

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help.ts:37`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-help.ts:50`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-help.ts:41`
- **What:** helpSearchText lowercases the whole topic text with toLocaleLowerCase() (help.ts:34-38) and the query is lowercased the same way (view-help.ts:50); the match is a plain includes (view-help.ts:41). Both use the WebView2 default locale, which is the Windows display language. In tr and az, 'I' lowercases to 'ı' (U+0131) and only 'İ' to 'i', so the English help text's capitalised words ('Import and export CSV', 'Inspect', 'If') become 'ımport', 'ınspect', 'ıf'. A query typed in lower case never matches those, and a capitalised query matches only the capital-I occurrences. The search-text.ts fold used for record search lowercases with the locale-independent toLowerCase, so only Help is affected.
- **Failure:** A person whose Windows display language is Turkish opens Help and types 'Import' (as the File menu spells it): 2 topics are listed instead of the 8 an English system lists. Typing 'inspect' lists 5 of the 7 topics, because the two that say only 'Inspect' (capital I) are now 'ınspect'. Typing 'Inspect' lists 3. No spelling finds all of them.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: help-turkish.mjs and help-turkish2.mjs over CDP against the shared preview (Emulation.setLocaleOverride, Input.insertText into #help-search) -> en-US: 'import' 8 topics, 'Import' 8, 'inspect' 7; tr-TR: 'import' 8, 'Import' 2 ('Import and export CSV \| The MCP surface: every resource and tool'), 'inspect' 5, 'Inspect' 3. help-turkish3.mjs: inside the search box's input handler under tr-TR, 'Import'.trim().toLocaleLowerCase() -> 'ımport' (code points 131 6d 70 6f 72 74).
- **Fix and guard:** Fold both sides with a locale-independent fold: toLowerCase(), or foldText from search-text.ts (NFD, marks removed, toLowerCase), which also lets 'cafe' find 'café'. Guard: a help.test case that runs the Help filter over a topic containing 'Inspect' and 'Import' with the queries 'inspect', 'Inspect', 'INSPECT' and 'İnspect' and expects a match for each; falsify by substituting toLocaleLowerCase('tr') and watch the lower-case query fail.
- **Verifier:** Compensation.cs:96 interpolates {fold.FoldedAt:yyyy-MM-dd} in a plain $"" string, so it uses CurrentCulture. HistoryFold.cs:130 formats {fresh:N0} the same way, and the Workbench shows that reason verbatim (view-history.ts, preview.reason). No code sets a default culture (grep finds only test code). A pwsh probe of DateTimeOffset 2026-10-11T10:00Z with yyyy-MM-dd gives th-TH 2569-10-11, ar-SA 1448-04-30 and fa-IR 1405-07-19, and N0 under ar-SA gives an Arabic thousands separator. The UTC-versus-local mismatch is also in the code: the checkpoint text prints plan.FirstAt/LastAt, which are parsed UTC DateTimeOffsets (SqliteNendoStore.cs:1084-1088, HistoryFold.cs:191-192, NewFile.cs:390-392), while actions.ts:463 and view-history.ts:47 show new Date(value).toLocaleDateString(), a local date. No ADR or contract mandates either form. It is cosmetic and occurs only near midnight or with a non-Gregorian regional format, so P3.

### R2RM-04 — The fill revision the Reactivate form writes can never be compensated, yet History offers Compensate: a backfill's inverse requires the field to be retired, and the null it puts back is refused on a required field

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-reversibility-matrix`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:405`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:412`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:356`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:408`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRequirements.cs:55`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:469`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRequirements.cs:25`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:588`
- **What:** prepareRetirement sends Reactivate for a required field to renderFieldRequirement(entity, fieldId, true) (view-structure.ts:356-357). That form lists the records whose value is null (isNull filter, :377-378) and builds one proposal of two mutations. The first is 'Fill missing X values': data.backfillRetiredField operations, each with null as the previous value (:405, :411). The second is 'Reactivate X': schema.setRetired false (:412-415). After acceptance, History offers Compensate on the fill revision (record branch of the eligibility SQL, ReadQueries.cs:588-591). CreateCausalInverses answers a backfill with another backfill carrying the previous value, null (Compensation.cs:406-410). ExecuteBackfillRetiredFieldAsync refuses while the field is active: 'This repair operation requires a retired field.' (FieldRequirements.cs:55). Suppose the person first compensates 'Reactivate X' so the field is retired again. ExecuteSetFieldAsync then refuses the null because the field is still required, a check made before retirement is considered: 'Required field {fieldId} cannot be null.' (Operations.cs:469-471). A retired field cannot be made optional either, because setFieldRequired calls RequireActive (FieldRequirements.cs:25). So the revision becomes reversible only after three further definition changes: Make optional, Retire, then Compensate. The only test of this inverse (FieldRequirementTests.cs:121) compensates a backfill of an optional, still-retired field with a non-null previous value, which is the one shape this flow never produces. The same refusal meets an agent's backfill of an optional retired field once the field is reactivated, although putting the value back would then be an ordinary edit. Through MCP the refusal arrives as NENDO_FIELD_NOT_RETIRED with 'The semantic precondition was not met.'
- **Failure:** Field Owner on Task is required and was retired, and 30 Tasks were created since without it. The person chooses Reactivate in Structure, fills 30 owners and accepts. They notice they picked the wrong owners and press Compensate on 'Fill missing Owner values': 'This repair operation requires a retired field.' They compensate 'Reactivate Owner', which is the latest definition change, and press Compensate on the fill again: 'Required field owner cannot be null.' History offers the button in both states. The 30 values can be taken back only by making Owner optional, retiring it and compensating, or by editing each record.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** When a backfill's field is no longer retired, reverse it as a plain data.setField: let ExecuteBackfillRetiredFieldAsync accept an active field when it runs as a compensation's inverse (compensationOfRevisionId is set), as it already lets a retired field through. For a required field whose previous value is null, either do not offer Compensate (the same rule in the eligibility SQL) or refuse with a reason a person can act on: 'Owner is required, so the values filled to reactivate it stay. Make it optional first.' Guard: an Engine test of the Reactivate flow's two mutations, with the fill compensated after reactivation, asserting the chosen outcome, and a flag test that History does not offer what the Engine always refuses. Falsify by restoring the field-not-retired check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. Reactivating a required retired field opens renderFieldRequirement (view-structure.ts:355-358, 370-422), which builds two mutations: data.backfillRetiredField fills (:405, :411) and then schema.setRetired false (:412-415). The fill revision passes History's record-change eligibility (ReadQueries.cs:588-591 lists data.backfillRetiredField). CreateCausalInverses answers a backfill with another BackfillRetiredFieldOperation carrying previous = null (Compensation.cs:408-409). ExecuteBackfillRetiredFieldAsync refuses an active field with field-not-retired (FieldRequirements.cs:54-55). If Reactivate is compensated first, ExecuteSetFieldAsync refuses the null on a still-required field before it considers retirement (Operations.cs:469-473). A retired field cannot be made optional either, since ExecuteSetFieldRequiredAsync calls RequireActive (FieldRequirements.cs:25 -> Retirement.cs:29-33). The only inverse test (FieldRequirementTests.cs:100-125) uses an optional, still-retired field with a non-null previous value, so this flow is untested. The class is declared RWRS while the inverse is unreachable in the state the flow itself produces. It is an edge case that needs the person to want the fill undone after reactivating. Nothing is written on refusal, and the values can be re-edited, so P3.
- **Correction:** Minor: the 'three further definition changes' count is Make optional, Retire, then Compensate. That is accurate. The optional-field agent case (backfill compensated after reactivation) holds but is rare.

### R2SP-02 — Device-wide agent connection settings are read once per window, so a lease-expiry or fixed-port choice made in one window is not applied to listeners another window starts later

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-several-processes` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:104`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:80`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentSettingsStore.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:451`
- **What:** Settings() is `_agentSettings ??= new DesktopAgentSettingsStore(_deviceStateRoot)`, which keeps one instance for the controller's whole life (the window's life, across file sessions). The constructor is the only read of agent-settings.json. CurrentHostOptions builds every listener's PreferredPort and LeaseTtl from that cached instance (lines 80-81). OffStatus and ReadAgentStatusCoreAsync report it to the Agent page (lines 451-455 and 492-499). Save merges with the latest document (DesktopAgentSettingsStore.cs:77-89), so the cache is refreshed only when this window itself saves.
- **Failure:** Windows A (BCM.nendo) and B (Planner.nendo) are both open. In A the person turns on 'Lease expiry' (60 s) to harden agent access, or turns Fixed port off. Later, in B, they switch agent access on. B's listener starts with LeaseTtl null and the old fixed port, so the hardening the person just chose does not apply. B's Agent page also still shows Lease expiry off. This lasts until B saves a connection setting itself or the window is restarted.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Read the 4 KB settings document again for every host start and status read, for example by building a fresh DesktopAgentSettingsStore in Settings() and keeping only the pending-edit flags across reads. Guard: a test with two controllers on one device-state root saves LeaseExpiry=true through one, starts a host through the other, and asserts the second host's LeaseTtl and reported LeaseExpiry.
- **Verifier:** Traced. DesktopAgentAccess.cs:104-105 caches `_agentSettings ??= new DesktopAgentSettingsStore(...)`; grep shows no other assignment, so the only read of agent-settings.json is the store constructor (DesktopAgentSettingsStore.cs:32-52). CurrentHostOptions (line 80-81) builds PreferredPort and LeaseTtl from the cache, FilePortAsync/PortPreferenceAsync (193-206) and the status reads (451-499) do too. Each file is its own process (ADR-0002, architecture.md 'Several files at once'), so another window's Save is never seen until this process saves itself (Save re-reads only to merge, lines 77-89). The Agent page opens/polls status through Settings(), so a window that has shown the page holds the old values; RestoreAgentModeAsync at file open also populates the cache. The Save comment ('its unchanged controls may already be stale') shows the authors knew pages go stale but nothing refreshes the read side. No ADR or contract requires the cached behaviour. Impact: a device-wide hardening choice (lease expiry, fixed port off) is not applied to a listener another already-open window starts later, until that window restarts; defaults are the relaxed single-user ones by ADR-0009, so this is a low-severity inconsistency.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: cross-window staleness of an optional hardening setting; the person sees the old value on the page and can re-save. Precondition is that the second window already read the settings (Agent page opened or an access level restored) before the first window saved.

<a id="r2sp-03"></a>

### R2SP-03 — Files of the same application (New file, Duplicate) share one kept agent port, and giving one of them another port moves the other one too

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `r2-several-processes` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentPortStore.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentPortStore.cs:54`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:227`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopAgentAccess.cs:202`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:232`
- **What:** DesktopAgentPortStore keys each entry by application ID alone. Claim returns kept.Port to any file of that application. ADR-0022 (New file) and ADR-0010 (Duplicate) both keep the application ID and give the copy a new instance ID. The second file's bind therefore falls back to a temporary port (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:592-609). Peek still shows the shared kept port in that file's 'Port for this file' field. Set (called from SetAgentSettingsAsync, line 227) rewrites the one shared entry, so it moves the sibling's port as well. The name label flips to whichever file claimed last.
- **Failure:** Reading 2026.nendo was made with File → New file from Reading 2025.nendo. With agent access on in both, 2025 holds 41764 and 2026 silently listens on a temporary port. 2026's page says 'Port 41764 was in use'. The person sets 2026 to 41770. The application's entry is now 41770, so 2025's next start also asks for 41770, and the agent client registered for 2026 at 41770 reaches 2025 whenever 2025 opens first. The agent then writes to the wrong year's file. Two files of one application can never keep separate fixed ports, against the store's own promise that each file can be registered once under a name of its own.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Key ports by application and instance, which is what the mode store's documentation intends, and fall back to the application-only entry once for migration. Guard: a DesktopAgentPortStore test claims for (app, instance A) and (app, instance B), asserts two different ports, and asserts that Set for one leaves the other unchanged.
- **Verifier:** Traced. DesktopAgentPortStore keys Claim/Peek/Set by applicationId alone (DesktopAgentPortStore.cs:32-71). ADR-0010 line 53 and its ADR-0022 amendment (lines 62-64 and ADR-0022:185) say Duplicate and New keep the application ID and take a new instance ID, so siblings share one entry. MainPage.FileActions.cs:281-283 shows New file opens the result in its own window while the source stays open, so two sibling files with agent access on is a normal flow. The second Claim returns the kept port; NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:592-609 then fails to bind it and falls back to a temporary port. Set (line 54-71) skips the same-application entry in its collision check and overwrites the one shared record, so choosing a port for one sibling moves the other. The mode store was later keyed with the instance ID (DesktopAgentModeStore.cs docs) but the port store was not. Caveat: ADR-0009's 2026-09-28 amendment (lines 79-88) literally says ports are 'filed under its application ID' and only considers a Fork, so the fix needs an ADR amendment (owner pre-accepts these), but the shared-port outcome contradicts that amendment's own aim that each file be registerable once under its own name. Sibling of the known DSH-10.
- **Correction:** Priority P3 (matches DSH-10 for the mode store): needs two same-application files both with agent access on, and the failure mode is a temporary port plus a confusing port field; the 'agent writes to the wrong year's file' step also requires the person to register both clients and open them in a particular order. The fix must amend ADR-0009 (key by application and instance) rather than only the code.

### UIT-03 — Studio Surfaces marks every root 'Healthy' and drops compiler warnings, including a custom view whose package is missing

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio` (reported P2) · also reported as WSP-26, UX-17

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-surfaces.ts:170`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-surfaces.ts:29`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.Extensions.cs:66`
- **What:** surfaceCard always emits `<span class="health-chip healthy">Healthy</span>`. diagnosticsMarkup is used only when there is no valid plan. A view naming a package the file lacks compiles valid with warning NUI452, and the custom-views contract says it 'shows the missing notice' in Use. Studio, the destination for 'validation/disable/restore' (studio.md section 2), shows neither the warning nor the state. The Custom views panel lists only packages the file carries, so the orphan view appears nowhere.
- **Failure:** A file carries the screen 'Links' (extensionGraphSurface, packageId org.example.link-graph), but the package is not in the file, or the person has switched custom views off. Surfaces lists 'Links · Custom graph · runs org.example.link-graph · Healthy' while Use shows 'Link graph is not in this file'. The person sees no problem in the one place meant to show it.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p19-off.mjs (preview carries only Board glance and the skill package) -> cards: "Links \| Custom graph · runs org.example.link-graph \| Healthy"; after turning Run custom views off (aria-pressed=false) the cards still read "Glance ... \| Healthy" and "Links ... \| Healthy"
- **Fix and guard:** Pass the compile diagnostics with severity Warning, keyed by semanticId, into treeSurfaceCard, and render a warning chip with the message. For extension roots, also use extensions.packages and extensions.run to say Missing package or Off. Guard: an SSR test of renderSurfaces with a valid compilation carrying an NUI452 warning, asserting that the card does not read Healthy and shows the message.
- **Verifier:** view-surfaces.ts:170 hard-codes the 'Healthy' chip in surfaceCard for every card, and diagnosticsMarkup (:174) is reached only when there is no valid plan and no file views (:29). A valid compile that carries warnings is never shown: NUI452 for a view whose package is not in the file is Severity.Warning (NendoSemanticCompiler.Extensions.cs:66), compiles valid, and the Workbench reads no warning severity anywhere in Studio. It is reachable through Studio's own flow, since removing a package leaves the views that name it (the Remove review says so). So Surfaces lists 'runs org.example.link-graph · Healthy' while Use shows the missing notice.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3. custom-views.md:1555 and Extensions.cs:6-9 make NUI452 a warning that 'the view says ... where it is shown', and Use carries the missing notice with an Add package step (custom-views.md:1299), so the problem is surfaced and fixable elsewhere. The 'switch off' half of the scenario is weak: the Custom views switches sit on the same Surfaces page and the Health card names Off, and Healthy there only means the definition compiles. The only warnings that exist are NUI452 and the NDATA010-012 record warnings, so 'drops compiler warnings' really means NUI452.

### UIT-04 — Review and History show reversibility classes that History never offers to compensate

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:27`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/history-markup.ts:10`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:545`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Operations.cs:288`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help-concepts.ts:169`
- **What:** Each review line and each History operation prints reversibilityLabel(entry.reversibility). ui.addNode declares Reversible (Operations.cs:288), and Help defines Reversible as 'Nendo can produce the exact inverse: a screen node added'. History's eligibility SQL offers Compensate only for single-operation revisions of a fixed list (ui.addNode is not on it), package-only batches and data batches. Its own comment says 'A ui.moveNode or general ui.removeNode is ReversibleWithRetainedState yet has no inverse'. Studio's Add view proposal is one ui.addNode plus several ui.setProperty, so it is never offered.
- **Failure:** The person uses Surfaces -> Custom views -> Add view…, reads 'Reversible' or 'Compensatable with retained state' beside the change, and accepts. History then shows 'No compensation offered' for that revision. Studio has no remove-view control, so the change the review called reversible cannot be undone from Studio at all.
- **Reproduction:** Source (preview history hard-codes canRequestCompensation:false, so the offer cannot be shown live). Executed: p14-history.mjs -> History detail "Set surface property · Compensatable with retained state" beside "No compensation offered" on the same revision
- **Fix and guard:** Expose the same eligibility the store computes on the proposal preview (for example canCompensateAfterAccept) and show it in the review, rather than the class alone. In History, show the class only where Compensate is offered, or say 'no inverse in History' next to it. Either add ui.addNode-only revisions to the eligible set, or stop labelling them Reversible in Help. Guard: an Engine test asserting that a revision whose operations all read Reversible or ReversibleWithRetainedState is either CanRequestCompensation or flagged in the preview.
- **Verifier:** The facts hold. addViewProposal (custom-view-recipe.ts:179-181) builds one mutation of ui.addNode (Reversible, Operations.cs:288) plus several ui.setProperty (ReversibleWithRetainedState). The review prints reversibilityLabel per entry (view-proposal.ts:27). SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:545-591 offers Compensate only for a single supported type, a package-only batch or an all-data batch, and CreateCompensationMutationAsync would refuse a multi-operation UI revision (Compensation.cs:218-224, 'covers record changes'). History therefore shows 'No compensation offered' (view-history.ts:24) for that revision, and the Workbench has no ui.removeNode control. help-concepts.ts:169 defines Reversible with 'a screen node added' as the example, so the label and the offer disagree.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3. The divergence between declared class and offered compensation is deliberate and documented: the SQL comment at ReadQueries.cs:536-543 says eligibility follows implemented operation types 'not the reversibility class', ADR-0006 says 'Nendo offers an inverse only when preconditions and retained state prove that it is safe' and 'Compensation ... is not universal', and History renders 'No compensation offered' beside the class. What remains is a wording and honesty gap on the consent screen and in Help (the class reads as a promise of undo), not a defect in the compensation engine. Fix by wording or Help rather than by widening eligibility.
