### WCS-10 — A tab switch whose restore fails after settle() has begun puts the old tab and trail back while the screen shows the new tab's place

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/tab-set.ts:31`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-actions.ts:195`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-actions.ts:256`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/navigation-actions.ts:236`
- **What:** switchTab loads the arriving trail and calls show() = revisitCurrent(); on false it restores set.active and both trails (review R-002). revisitCurrent returns false when settleRestoring catches a failure from settle(), but settle() has already set state.view, selectedEntityId, selectedApplicationEntity, showOverview, fileView, drills, quick filters, studio queries, tabs and selectedRecordId synchronously before `await refreshDerived(...)`, and settleRestoring's finally calls rerender() with that state. So the tab strip, heading and Back describe the old tab while the content shows the target place, and the next render records the target place into the old tab's trail, cutting off its forward entries.
- **Failure:** While an agent writes continuously, the person clicks their History tab from a Use tab. refreshDerived gives up with 'view-changed'. The error appears, the Use tab stays highlighted, but History is drawn; their next click records History as a step of the Use tab and Forward on that tab is lost.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Snapshot the renderer state settle() writes and restore it (and redraw) when settle fails inside a tab switch, or have switchTab only commit after settle succeeds. Guard: tab-set test where show() mutates state then returns false, asserting state.view and the drawn place match the restored active tab.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. tab-set.ts:30-36 loads the arriving trail, calls show() (revisitCurrent), and on false restores set.active and both trails. revisitCurrent (navigation-actions.ts:189-196) -> settleRestoring (224-244): settle() (256-337) assigns state.view, selectedEntityId, selectedApplicationEntity, showOverview, fileView, helpTopicId, tabs, selectedRecordId before 'await refreshDerived', so when refreshDerived throws (view-changed after three moved reads, actions.ts:261, or any host error) the catch records the failure, the finally calls rerender() with the mutated state, and false is returned. switchTab then puts the old tab and trail back, so the content shows the target place while the tab strip (activateTab -> refreshChrome) and Back/Forward describe the old tab, and the next render records the target place into the old tab's trail (navigationTrail.record slices off forward entries). tab-set tests only cover show() returning false without mutating state.
- **Correction:** The heading is drawn from state (currentHeading), so it follows the target place with the content, not the old tab; only the tab strip, Back/Forward labels and the trail describe the old tab. Trigger is rare (refreshDerived failing mid-switch), so P3 not P2. The Back/Forward path is consistent because travel steps the trail before settle; only the tab switch and close-tab paths roll back.

### WCS-18 — A navigation that fails leaves state.view on the new screen while the old screen stays drawn

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:338`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:342`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:660`
- **What:** openWorkspaceView sets state.view = target before awaiting refreshDerived; its catch only calls showError, with no rerender. openAgentView sets state.view = 'agent' and renders only in the success branch of refreshAgentStatus(). showError records lastOutcome under the new view name while writing into the old page.
- **Failure:** Clicking Structure fails with 'view-changed'. The Data page stays drawn with the error, the rail still highlights Data, but state.view is 'structure', so the next automatic redraw suddenly swaps to Structure and the error disappears with it.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Restore the previous view on failure, or rerender in the catch so screen and state agree. Guard: unit test with a failing refreshDerived asserting state.view is unchanged.
- **Verifier:** openWorkspaceView assigns state.view = target (actions.ts:338) before awaiting refreshDerived (:340), and its catch only calls showError (:342-343) with no rerender and no restore of the view. showError (shell.ts:527-535) writes into the message slot of the page still on screen and does not call the chrome. The rail highlight, which is set only in updateChrome via render(), therefore stays on the old view while state.view names the new one. openAgentView (main.ts:658-663) has the same shape: state.view = 'agent', and render only in .then(render). refreshDerived can throw 'view-changed' after attempt 2 (actions.ts:261) or a host error. By contrast, Back/Forward's settleRestoring rerenders in its finally (navigation-actions.ts:229-251), so the failure path here is the odd one out. Error-path-only divergence, so P3.
- **Correction:** The error does not disappear on the next redraw. showError stores lastOutcome with view = state.view, which is already the new view, so restoreOutcome (shell.ts:98-106) redraws the message on the new page. The real symptom is the old page drawn under a rail highlight and state that disagree, until some redraw (file-change nudge, tile refresh) swaps the page. Fix is unchanged: restore the previous state.view in the catch, or rerender.

### WDV-13 — Rating values outside the scale are shown through a JavaScript number, so large stored integers display wrongly

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/rating.ts:32`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/rating.ts:60`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/rating.ts:95`, `docs/contracts/scalars.md:26`
- **What:** ratingValue converts the exact lexeme with Number(lexeme). The out-of-scale branches print String(rating), and ratingControlMarkup's note says 'Stored as N'. The contract says numbers must never pass through a JavaScript number in the Workbench, and that a value outside the scale is 'read back exactly'.
- **Failure:** A rating field holds 9223372036854775807, written by an agent or an import. The cell, list and record page show '9223372036854776000 outside 1-5', and the form says 'Stored as 9223372036854776000', which is not the stored number.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs -> ratingValue -> 9223372036854776000; ratingMarkup -> <span class="rating is-outside">9223372036854776000<span class="rating-issue">outside 1–5</span></span>
- **Fix and guard:** Keep the lexeme for display, and compare against the scale with BigInt, or with Number only when Number.isSafeInteger. Guard: an assertion in rating.test.mjs that the Int64 max lexeme is displayed verbatim; falsify by restoring Number().
- **Verifier:** rating.ts:32 converts the exact lexeme with Number(lexeme) and :60 / :95 print String(rating) for an out-of-scale value. I ran node on the Int64 max lexeme: Number gives 9223372036854776000 and Number.isSafeInteger is false, so the cell, list and record page (rating.ts callers at record-markup.ts:54, :451 and view-data.ts:608) show a number that is not the stored one. docs/contracts/scalars.md:25-32 says a value outside the scale is 'read back exactly' and numbers must never pass through a JavaScript number in the Workbench, and rating.ts:4-7 promises it is 'shown as itself'. In-scale values are unaffected and display only is wrong (no write path is changed), and it needs an agent- or import-written value beyond 2^53 in a Rating field, so P3.
- **Correction:** The contract's JavaScript-number ban is worded for the edit and transport paths; this is the display path, so the stronger citation is the 'read back exactly' sentence.

### WDV-15 — A breakdown whose groups total zero or less says 'No records' although records exist

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/chart-kit.ts:89`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:353`
- **What:** breakdownSegments maps each lexeme through proportionOf, which returns 0 for any non-positive number, and drops contributingRecords. proportionBar then decides emptiness by total === 0 and draws 'No records' with aria-label 'No records', while the legend lists the real totals.
- **Failure:** A 'Balance by status' breakdown (sum of a Decimal) whose groups total -120.50 and -30 over five records draws an empty track labelled 'No records', directly above a legend that reads Open -120.50 and Done -30. A screen reader hears 'No records'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs with breakdownSegments({groups:[{key:'open',valueLexeme:'-120.50',contributingRecords:3},{key:'done',valueLexeme:'-30',contributingRecords:2}]}) -> track says "No records": true \| legend still lists: true
- **Fix and guard:** Carry contributingRecords into the segments and say 'No records' only when no group has any. When totals are zero or negative, state that a proportion of these totals cannot be drawn and keep the table. Guard: a chart-kit test for zero and negative totals; falsify by restoring the total === 0 check.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. charts.ts:353-361 maps each group's valueLexeme through proportionOf (chart-kit.ts:54-58), which returns 0 for any non-positive number; chart-kit.ts:86-90 then sums amounts and draws the 'No records' track with aria-label 'No records' when total === 0, while the legend at :97-98 still prints each group's real lexeme. A breakdownChart may use sum/min/max over Integer/Decimal (semantic-surfaces.md:755, ADR-0004 S1), so all-negative (or exactly zero) group totals are reachable, and chart-kit.test.mjs:63-69 only pins proportionOf, not the label. The contract line 'A zero total is an empty track that says so' (semantic-surfaces.md:849) was written for counts and does not address negative sums; ADR-0004:1005-1010 shows the ranked list handles the same case by drawing no bars but stating every number. Cosmetic/accessibility wording defect with the numbers still shown, hence P3.
- **Correction:** Same wrong label also appears when totals are exactly zero (e.g. sums of 0, or only zero/negative groups), not just negative ones; mixed-sign totals silently draw only the positive groups. Neither changes the verdict.

### WDV-21 — A filter clause with valueKind 'null' and a comparing operator is sent with no value, so the screen's read is refused

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-window.ts:68`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-window.ts:121`
- **What:** The value kinds a filter clause may declare are literal, today, now and null (custom-views.md:1479; SemanticVocabulary.ValueKinds), and ValidateFilterClause does not refuse 'null' with eq or ne. resolveClauseValue handles only today and now, and returns properties.value (undefined) for 'null'. clauseFilters then sends {operator:'eq'} with no value, and RecordQuerySemantics.Validate refuses 'Use isNull or isNotNull to query missing values.'
- **Failure:** An agent authors a board clause {fieldId:'owner', operator:'eq', valueKind:'null'}. The proposal compiles and is accepted, and the board then shows its read error permanently.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In clauseFilters, map valueKind 'null' with eq to isNull and with ne to isNotNull (or have the compiler refuse other operators). Guard: a record-window.test case for both mappings; falsify by removing them.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end by reading. NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:703-731 (ValidateFilterClause) accepts valueKind 'null' (it is in NendoSemanticVocabulary.ValueKinds, SemanticVocabulary.cs:338) with eq/ne: it is not presenceOnly, the NUI276 'no value' check fires only for valueKind == literal, and no literal check runs. record-window.ts:68-77 (resolveClauseValue) handles only today/now and returns the undefined value for 'null'; clauseFilters (record-window.ts:119-121) then builds {operator:'eq'} with no value, and RecordQuerySemantics.cs:37-38 refuses it with 'Use isNull or isNotNull to query missing values.' The block comment at record-window.ts:45-55 names this exact failure class. No test covers a null filter clause (record-window.test.mjs has only today/now/literal). It stays P3: it needs an author to write a meaningless eq+null combination, and the outcome is a visible, fail-closed read error rather than wrong or lost data.
- **Correction:** The root cause is the compiler, not the Workbench: 'null' is a command-step word ('Closed value vocabulary, shared with a command step', SemanticVocabulary.cs:337) that no contract gives a meaning on a filterClause (custom-views.md:1475-1480 only says isNull/isNotNull take no value). The same compile-time gap is reported on the Engine side as ESM-03. So the preferred fix is to refuse valueKind 'null' on a filterClause in ValidateFilterClause (and ValidateFilters, NendoSemanticCompiler.Extensions.cs:123-127), pointing at isNull/isNotNull. The finding's Workbench alternative of mapping eq+null to isNull and ne+null to isNotNull would invent filter semantics that no contract states. The guard should be a compile test, not a record-window test.

### WDV-22 — A required field revealed in a closed tab opens without reading that tab's relations and totals

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:329`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:265`
- **What:** revealField calls activateTab(plan, null, ...), and activateTab returns before loadRelatedWindows, refreshVisibleTiles and patchReadOnlyPanels when record is null. The record is known in wireRecordForm but not passed through. Nothing redraws after the 'X is required.' error, so the relation chase does not run.
- **Failure:** Saving an existing record with a required field empty on the Contacts tab opens that tab, but its related list and totals stay unread (shown as loading) until something else redraws the page.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Pass the record to revealField and on to activateTab. Guard: a record-form test asserting a relation read after a reveal; falsify by passing null again.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. record-form.ts:109-112 finds a required field whose value is null or '' and calls revealField(page, ...) without the record. revealField (record-form.ts:324-329) calls activateTab(plan, null, ...), which returns at record-form.ts:265 ('if (record === null) return') before loadRelatedWindows, refreshVisibleTiles and patchReadOnlyPanels. Related lists and totals are read lazily per open tab (plan-selection.ts:284-298 visibleNodes, reads.ts:177-189), and an unread one draws 'Loading...' (record-markup.ts:249). showError (shell.ts:527) redraws nothing, so it stays so. The fold branch of the same function does read, because its toggle handler is given the record (record-form.ts:196-213), so the two reveal paths disagree. Reachability is narrow, which keeps it P3. Nendo's own editors cannot empty a required field in a tab the person has not opened (the person opening the tab already read it; the Studio grid refuses a blank required cell), and setFieldRequired checks existing rows. But the Engine refuses only null for a required field (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:391-397, 469) and scalars.md:22 keeps null and empty text distinct, so an agent or CSV import can store '' in a required Text field; the form treats '' as missing (record-form.ts:109), so any save of that record is refused and sends the person to an unvisited tab whose relations read 'Loading...'.
- **Correction:** The scenario as worded ('saving an existing record with a required field empty on the Contacts tab') is only reachable when that field is stored as '' by an agent or import, since Nendo's own editors cannot produce an empty required value in an unvisited tab. The effect is a related list or totals that read 'Loading...' (or show a stale revision) in the revealed tab until the person fixes the field and saves, which redraws the page. The proposed fix is sound: pass the record through revealField into activateTab. The guard's falsification step is right. A tab click on a create form (record null) correctly reads nothing, so only the existing-record case is affected.

### WMX-07 — Emphasis regexes run over the link and image markup inserted just before them, so tooltips show literal tags and an unbalanced <strong> or <em> turns the rest of the record form bold

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:106`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:108`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:442`
- **What:** inline() first inserts <span class="markdown-link" title="$2">, then runs the strong, em and del regexes over the whole string, title attribute included. A delimiter in the URL pairs with one in the text, so one of the inserted tags lands inside the attribute (where it shows as text in the tooltip) and its partner is left open. The record page builds the markdown body inside the same innerHTML as the rest of the form, and the HTML parser reopens an unclosed formatting element in every following block.
- **Failure:** The value `**Bold [link](https://x.y/a**b) rest` produces <p><strong>Bold <span class="markdown-link" title="https://x.y/a</strong>b">. The tooltip reads 'https://x.y/a</strong>b', and every later field label, the Not set checkbox and the Save button render bold. `[docs](https://example.com/_next/a_b_)` shows the tooltip 'https://example.com/<em>next/a_b</em>', and `[x](https://a/~~b~~)` shows '<del>' in its tooltip.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: fieldControlMarkup() for a markdown field holding that value, parsed by headless Edge -> 6 <strong> elements in the form, #after paragraph font-weight 700, and the Save button inside a <strong>. The markdownMarkup probe gives url_underscore_title -> title="https://example.com/<em>next/a_b</em>".
- **Fix and guard:** Take links and images out before formatting, as code spans already are: split on the link pattern, format only the surrounding text and the link text, and leave the URL alone. Guard: markdown.test.mjs asserting that these three inputs give balanced tags (as many <strong> as </strong>) and titles with no '<'.
- **Verifier:** src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:105-111: inline() escapes, inserts <span class="markdown-link" title="$2">, then runs the strong/em/del regexes over the whole string, title attribute included. I ran a copy of markdown.ts under node 25: '**Bold [link](https://x.y/a**b) rest' gives <p><strong>Bold <span class="markdown-link" title="https://x.y/a</strong>b">link</span> rest</p> (unbalanced <strong>, which the HTML parser reopens in later blocks of the same innerHTML at record-markup.ts:442); '[docs](https://example.com/_next/a_b_)' and '[x](https://a/~~b~~)' put <em>/<del> literally in the tooltip. No ADR or contract mandates this. It cannot become script (the inserted tags carry no quotes) and the bold spill needs an odd delimiter inside a URL, so P3.
- **Correction:** A more common trigger than the ones listed: '[__init__.py](pkg/__init__.py)' gives title="pkg/<strong>init</strong>.py" (balanced, so only the tooltip is wrong). The form-wide bold spill needs an unpaired ** / __ / ~~ / _ inside a URL, which is rare.

### WMX-08 — Markdown subset mis-renders common text: '# Learn C#' loses its '#', two-space line breaks never work in paragraphs, backslash escapes are ignored, and '**a **b' becomes italic with stray asterisks

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:32`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:79`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:112`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:108`
- **What:** The heading regex's `\s*#*\s*$` strips trailing '#' characters even with no space before them; CommonMark requires one. Paragraph lines are trim()med before they are joined (line 79), so the ` {2,}\n` -> <br> rule (line 112) can never match inside a paragraph and is dead code there. Backslash escapes such as \* and \_ get no handling. When the strong regex fails, the em regex pairs the stray asterisks.
- **Failure:** An agent heading '## Using C#' renders as 'Using C', and '## Fix issue #' as 'Fix issue'. A note that uses two-space line breaks for an address renders on one line. 'Price 5\*3 and \*not em\*' shows the backslashes and an italic run.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: markdownMarkup probe -> heading_csharp "<h3>Learn C</h3>"; hard_break_paragraph "<p>line one line two</p>"; escaped_star "<p>Price is 5\\<em>3 and \\</em>not em\\*</p>"; '**a **b' -> "<p><em>*a *</em>b</p>".
- **Fix and guard:** Strip a closing heading sequence only when whitespace precedes it. Use trimStart() when collecting paragraph lines, so trailing double spaces survive to the <br> rule. Escape backslash-escaped ASCII punctuation out of the text before formatting. Guard: a markdown.test.mjs case for each input.
- **Verifier:** Reproduced with a copy of src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts under node 25. markdown.ts:32: the heading regex `\s*#*\s*$` strips a trailing '#' with no space before it, so '## Learn C#' gives <h4>Learn C</h4> (CommonMark keeps it). markdown.ts:79 trims each paragraph line, so the ` {2,}\n` -> <br> rule at line 112 never fires in a paragraph ('line one \nline two' gives <p>line one line two</p>); it works only in list items. There is no backslash-escape handling: 'Price 5\*3 and \*not em\*' gives <p>Price 5\<em>3 and \</em>not em\*</p>. '**a **b' gives <em>*a *</em>b. All are real, small rendering errors in a deliberately minimal subset (markdown.ts:7-11) and no contract mandates them, so P3.
- **Correction:** The example '## Fix issue #' is not a defect: CommonMark also treats a trailing ' #' preceded by a space as a closing sequence, so 'Fix issue' is correct. Only a '#' with no space before it ('C#', 'F#') is wrong. Hard-break and backslash-escape support are feature gaps in the subset rather than regressions, and the doc comment never promises them.

### WSP-15 — Compensate is offered for revisions already compensated on a newer History page

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-history.ts:20`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/format.ts:95`
- **What:** canCompensate checks only state.history, the current page of 50. The host's canRequestCompensation ignores existing compensations, and the engine refuses a second one with "This revision already has a compensation revision." (SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:139). History is newest first, so a compensation always sits on the same page as its target or an earlier one.
- **Failure:** Page 2 offers Compensate on a revision compensated last week. Clicking it ends in an error.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Have the host mark a revision that already has a compensation in QueryHistoryAsync (EXISTS on compensation_of_revision_id), or include that fact in the page. Guard: an engine test that a compensated revision's CanRequestCompensation is false.
- **Verifier:** format.ts:95-96 canCompensate looks for a compensating revision only in the history array passed in, which is state.history, the current page of 50 (view-history.ts:20). The host flag in SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:553-592 has no EXISTS on compensation_of_revision_id for the non-redo branch, so it is true for an already-compensated revision. History defaults to newest first (ReadQueries.cs:202 NewestFirst = true), so a compensation sits on the same or an earlier page than its target; when it is on an earlier page, the target's page offers Compensate and SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:131-140 refuses with 'This revision already has a compensation revision.' Reach needs the pair to straddle a page boundary (more than 50 later revisions, or a boundary split), and the refusal is an error message with no data effect, so P3.
- **Correction:** The finding's page-2 scenario is accurate. Note the host flag deliberately stays true for record-change compensations so redo works (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:585-591), so the fix must exclude only the case where the revision itself already has a compensation, not all compensation targets.

### WST-05 — agent-working.test asserts the text of a condition that can never be true, and the real pill shows 'is working' for 1.2 s after a 5 ms read has already ended

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/agent-working.test.mjs:48`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:324`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:320`
- **What:** The test 'nothing appears for work that finished inside the wait' only regex-matches the line `if (!agentWork.busy && Date.now() - lastAgentWorkAt >= agentIdleMs) return;`. That check runs in a timer set busyBarDelayMs (700 ms) after the first busy signal, and lastAgentWorkAt is never earlier than that signal. Date.now() - lastAgentWorkAt is therefore at most 700 and never reaches agentIdleMs (1200), so the early return is dead code. The pill is shown for any work, however short, and then hidden 1200 ms later. setAgentWork's doc comment says 'a stale "still writing" is the one wrong thing this can say'.
- **Failure:** An agent makes one 5 ms read and goes idle. 700 ms later the status bar says 'Codex is working', and it stays up until 1.9 s, after the agent has stopped. An agent polling every couple of seconds makes the pill blink on and off for the whole session, which is the flicker the delay was meant to prevent.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node agent-pill-probe.mjs (real shell.ts setAgentWork, fake clock) -> 't=+5ms agent idle again; pill hidden=true' / 't=+700ms pill hidden=false text="" title="Codex · nendo.read.resource. End it under Agent → Revoke edit access."' / 't=+1900ms pill hidden=true'
- **Fix and guard:** In the timer, return when !agentWork.busy, meaning the work already ended inside the wait. Keep the 1200 ms idle window only for hiding a pill that is already shown. Replace the regex with a behavioural test that bundles shell.ts with a fake clock, as the probe does, and asserts that a 5 ms burst never shows the pill and a 27-call burst does.
- **Verifier:** shell.ts:316-324: the appear timer is set busyBarDelayMs (700) after the first busy signal, and lastAgentWorkAt (set at shell.ts:~296 on every busy signal) is never earlier than that signal. At firing, Date.now() - lastAgentWorkAt is therefore at most about 700 and cannot reach agentIdleMs (1200), so `!agentWork.busy && ... >= agentIdleMs` is dead code. A single short read followed by idle still shows the pill at +700 ms and hideTheAgentPillSoon() takes it down 1.2 s later. That contradicts the in-code comment 'Nothing appears for work that is already over'. agent-working.test.mjs:48-53 only regex-matches that line, so it passes whatever the behaviour is. Source and test both read as claimed.
- **Correction:** Cosmetic only: an indicator of the agent's presence that lingers for about 1.2 s. The proposed fix of returning on !agentWork.busy would also hide the pill for a burst of 27 sub-700 ms calls that ends before the timer fires, which the file's own comment wants shown, so the intended rule needs choosing before fixing.

### WST-08 — Studio's search text is remembered per entity ID across files, so opening another file re-runs the previous file's search automatically

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/studio-search.ts:17`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/studio-search.ts:23`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/studio-search.ts:88`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/file-follow.test.mjs:246`
- **What:** `const searchTexts = new Map<string, string>()` is a module-level map keyed by entityId. It is not created with fileScopedMap/fileScopedClearable, unlike studioQueries and every other per-file Studio cache in app-state.ts, so clearFileScoped() never empties it. studioSearchFieldMarkup pre-fills the box from it, and wireStudioSearch runs `if (input.value.trim().length > 0) schedule(true)`, which sends data.searchRecords at once. studio-search.ts has no test, and file-follow.test.mjs only checks six registered caches, so an unregistered module-level cache passes.
- **Failure:** The person searches 'invoice' in Tasks in Work.nendo, then opens Home.nendo, which also has a record type with the entityId 'tasks'. Opening Data → Tasks shows 'invoice' in the box and runs that search against the new file, listing results nobody asked for.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Create it with fileScopedClearable(new Map()). Add a guard test that scans src/*.ts for module-level `new Map(`/`new Set(` not wrapped in fileScopedMap/fileScopedSet/fileScopedClearable, with a named allow-list for device-wide or constant tables. The test should fail today on searchTexts.
- **Verifier:** studio-search.ts:17 is a plain module-level Map keyed by entityId, never registered with fileScopedClearable (only grep hit for searchTexts is lines 17/23/74), so clearFileScoped() (app-state.ts:284, called from resetFileView actions.ts:143 on every fileSessionId change) cannot empty it. studioSearchFieldMarkup (line 23) pre-fills the box from it and wireStudioSearch line 88 runs schedule(true), sending data.searchRecords against the newly opened file. The sibling filter state, studioQueries (view-data.ts:453), is file-scoped, and app-state.ts:246-255 states the rule that this kind of cache must register itself because 'a node ID that another file could also carry'. Entity IDs do collide across files: ADR-0022 new files and packages/recipes carry the same schema (e.g. 'entity.idea', idea-garden-recipe.ts:21). Effect is small (a stale pre-filled search and, if the new file has no index, a build-index prompt), hence P3.
- **Correction:** Location file-follow.test.mjs:246 does not exist: the file is 55 lines and its cache-clearing test is at lines 42-54 (it checks six hand-named caches, which is the point). Studio-created record types get random UUID entity IDs (studio.ts:45), so the collision needs files of one application lineage (new-file copies, recipes, packages), not arbitrary files.

### WXS-12 — Package IDs the Engine accepts (`org.my--view`, `org.view-`) are refused by the host's actor check and by the Add view form

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/custom-view-recipe.ts:113`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:531`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionPackageModel.cs:312`
- **What:** ValidPackageId accepts any dotted ID whose segments start with a letter and hold letters, digits and '-', so doubled and trailing hyphens are allowed. The host's actor pattern and refusalFor both use `^[a-z0-9]+(?:[.-][a-z0-9]+)*$`, which refuses `--` and a trailing '-' (and accepts a segment that starts with a digit, which the Engine refuses).
- **Failure:** A person imports a package with ID `org.view-`. Import and review accept it, and its views run. But every write, state change or proposal it makes is refused with `actor-not-allowed`, and Studio's Add view form says 'Choose a package this file carries.' about the very package the card shows.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe.mjs recipe -> E.id {"id":"org.my--view","engineAccepts":true,"hostActorAccepts":false,"addViewForm":"Choose a package this file carries."} / E.id {"id":"org.view-","engineAccepts":true,"hostActorAccepts":false,"addViewForm":"Choose a package this file carries."}. Also node probe-recipe.mjs -> org.example-.map Engine valid: true form says: Choose a package this file carries. / 1org.map Engine valid: false form says: (accepted)
- **Fix and guard:** Use one definition everywhere. Either tighten ValidPackageId to the actor pattern, with a migration note for existing files, or widen the actor regex and refusalFor to the Engine's rule. Guard: a shared table of IDs run against the Engine, the host actor check and refusalFor, asserting that all three agree.
- **Verifier:** The Engine's rule (ExtensionPackageModel.cs:312-316, same as the contract at custom-views.md:133) accepts any dotted ID whose segments start with a-z and hold a-z, 0-9 and '-', so org.view- and org.my--view import. The host's actor check (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:531) and refusalFor (custom-view-recipe.ts:113) both use ^[a-z0-9]+(?:[.-][a-z0-9]+)*$, which needs an alphanumeric after every '-' or '.', so a trailing or doubled hyphen fails. Every record write, state read/write and proposal a view of such a package makes carries actor extension:<package> (extension-broker.ts stateWrite and others), so ExtensionWriter refuses it with actor-not-allowed; its views still run and read, since reads carry no actor, and the origin slug collapses hyphens (ExtensionOrigins.cs) so nothing else blocks them. The Add view form also answers 'Choose a package this file carries.' for it. So the host is stricter than the contract. Needs an ID with a doubled or trailing hyphen, which is rare, so P3.
- **Correction:** The extra remark that the host regex accepts a segment starting with a digit is true but harmless, since the Engine refuses such an ID at import and it never reaches a file. Loosening the host regex to the Engine's rule is the smaller change; tightening ValidPackageId would need a migration for files that already carry such an ID.

### WXS-15 — ui.setPlace answers success while the Workbench keeps nothing, and the next redraw hands the view an older place, so it jumps back

**P3** · correctness · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:700`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:702`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:296`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:275`
- **What:** setViewPlace returns false and keeps nothing when the view is not on the page (`mount.placeholder === null \|\| !mount.placeholder.isConnected`, which is the case for a view held for its review) or when there is no trail entry. The broker ignores that answer, sets `connection.placeJson` to the place the view declared, and answers the view with ok/null. On the next draw, wireViewFrames calls `broker.place(mount, placeOf(mount))` with the place the Workbench actually kept. That differs from placeJson, so the broker posts it to the view as a `place` event.
- **Failure:** A workbench view (such as Archi, which declares its open view as a step) prepares a proposal, and the review opens with the view parked. When the acceptance's `changes` event arrives, the view opens the new diagram and declares the place with `replace: true`. That call is answered as done but kept nowhere. When the person comes back to the screen, the view is handed its old place and jumps back to the diagram it showed before.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-broker-misc.mjs (2), with deps.ui.setPlace answering false -> setPlace answer while the Workbench kept nothing: {"t":"res","id":1,"ok":true,"r":null} / then the next redraw hands the view: {"t":"evt","n":"place","d":{"view":"old"}}
- **Fix and guard:** Record placeJson only when deps.ui.setPlace answered true. Otherwise refuse with a code such as `not-on-screen`, so the view declares its place again once it is shown. Guard: an extension-broker.test.mjs case where ui.setPlace answers false, asserting that the request is refused and that a following place(mount, old) posts nothing the view had not been told.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. extension-broker.ts:700-702 ignores the boolean from deps.ui.setPlace (declared at :62 to answer whether anything changed) and always sets connection.placeJson and answers null. view-frames.ts:296-298 setViewPlace returns false when the placeholder is not connected or there is no trail entry. A view held for review is parked with its old placeholder detached (view-frames.ts:187-205, heldForReview). The broker's changes() event (view-frames.ts:143, extension-broker.ts:937-946) reaches connections regardless of placement, so a held view can declare a place. On the next wireViewFrames, line 275 calls broker.place(mount, placeOf(mount)). placeOf returns the older kept place, which differs from placeJson, so extension-broker.ts:968-975 posts a 'place' event with the old value. That contradicts the contract line 965, 'The view is never handed back the place it declared itself'. The reviewer's probe uses the real broker, and I confirmed its setPlace stub matches the real setViewPlace semantics. Impact is a view jumping back to its previous place after a review, so P3.
- **Correction:** The probe stubs deps.ui.setPlace to false. In the product that answer needs the mount to be held for review, or no trail entry to exist, which is a narrow window.

Each replay assigns model, sim and replayMode in one synchronous segment on finishing, so the last to finish wins and its notice is the one shown. The first to finish also runs finally { loading = false } at :258 while the other still runs. Matches the finding; effect is cosmetic and transient, so P3.

### EXT-09 — A state key's version restarts at 1 after it is forgotten, including when History restores it, so a stale expectedVersion is accepted

**P3** · concurrency · Confirmed · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:507`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:646`
- **What:** The upsert writes `version = (previous?.Version ?? 0) + 1`. After a deletion, previous is null and the version is 1 again. The inverse of a Forget is SetExtensionStateOperation(value, ExpectAbsent), and applying it also lands at version 1. Versions are the only conflict check (contract: 'A stale one is refused with state-version-conflict').
- **Failure:** View X reads key 'layout' as A at v1. A second frame of the same package, using shared state, sets B (v2) and forgets the key. The person compensates the Forget in History, which restores B at v1. X writes C with expectedVersion 1, which is accepted and overwrites B, a value X never saw. That is the ABA overwrite the version check exists to prevent.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Make versions monotonic per (package, view, key) across deletions: keep a tombstone row (value null, version n), or take the next version from a per-package counter. Guard: an Engine test of set, forget, compensate the forget, then a write with the pre-delete version that expects `state-version-conflict`.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end in SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs. The forget path DELETEs the row (about lines 509-515). The next write reads previous=null from ReadStateRowAsync and upserts version=(previous?.Version ?? 0)+1, which is 1 (lines 524-531). The conflict check at lines 505-507 compares previous?.Version ?? 0 with expectedVersion, so a writer that read v1 before the forget passes if anyone has re-set the key to v1. This needs no History: forget by one frame followed by a re-set by another is enough. CreateExtensionInverse (case extension.setState, about lines 630-641) turns a Forget's compensation into a set with expected=ExpectAbsent, and applying it also lands at v1, which is the finding's variant. docs/contracts/custom-views.md:811-813 promises that a stale expectedVersion is refused, and the compensation promise ('refuses when the key has been written again since') is defeated the same way. ABA on the version is real. Impact is small: no shipped view passes expectedVersion (grep of extensions/ finds none), and it needs two frames of one package or a History compensation between a read and a write.
- **Correction:** The History scenario is only one variant. The plain form needs no compensation: frame A reads v1, frame B forgets the key and sets it again (v1), and frame A's write with expectedVersion 1 is accepted. Compensations of ordinary sets have the same weakness, because their expected version is previousVersion+1. The line references are fine (507 is the conflict check, 646 is the inverse builder).

### R2SP-07 — Device-state documents are replaced by moving a stage over them, which fails whenever another process has the document open; readers never take the lock, so concurrent reads silently drop or session-only writes

**P3** · concurrency · Confirmed · area `r2-several-processes`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopStateFile.cs:8`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopStateFile.cs:33`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopStateFile.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopExtensionSettingsStore.cs:55`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.cs:107`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileHistory.cs:163`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileHistory.cs:186`
- **What:** DesktopStateFile's doc says that 'a reader opens it shared with that move', and OpenForRead uses FileShare.Read \| FileShare.Delete. On this machine, however, File.Move(stage, path, overwrite: true) is refused with access denied while any handle is open on the destination, with or without FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Readers run outside DesktopDeviceStateLock. DesktopExtensionSettingsStore polls every 250 ms in every window. DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.IsGranted and RevocationGeneration read on every authority check. The Agent page's 3 s poll calls DesktopAgentPortStore.Peek and DesktopAgentModeStore.Recall. DesktopFileHistory.LoadAsync opens with FileShare.Read, while RememberCoreAsync moves the document over while holding only .recent-access. TryReplace and RememberCoreAsync swallow the failure and return false.
- **Failure:** With three windows open, the person turns 'Custom views off' for the device in window A while B and C poll extension-settings.json. Roughly one save in 400 fails. A then says the setting 'applies for this session, but could not be saved for the next launch', and B and C keep running views, because the file never changed. A remembered agent level, a kept port or a recent-file entry is lost the same way with no message at all.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-move.ps1 (.NET 10.0.12, Windows 10.0.26300) -> 'reader share=Read -> move failed: UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path is denied.' and 'reader share=Read, Delete -> move failed: UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path is denied.'; probe-rate.ps1 (three processes reading every 250 ms as DesktopStateFile.OpenForRead does, one writer using Replace's stage+move) -> 'writer replaced the document 826 times; 2 replacements failed with access denied'
- **Fix and guard:** Retry the move a few times on access denied or a sharing violation (it clears within a millisecond), or have readers take the document's named lock. Correct the DesktopStateFile comment. Say in the extension-settings notice that other open windows did not receive the change. Guard: turn probe-rate into a test (a background reader loop plus 500 Replace calls, asserting zero failures).
- **Verifier:** Reproduced here (probe in verify/r2-several-processes-7): File.Move(stage, path, overwrite:true) over a document that another handle has open fails with UnauthorizedAccessException even when that handle was opened FileShare.Read\|Delete, so the DesktopStateFile.cs:10 comment ('a reader opens it shared with that move') is false on this machine. Readers run outside DesktopDeviceStateLock (DesktopStateFile.cs:68-98, DesktopExtensionSettingsStore.cs:50-60 polls every 250 ms per window), Replace has no retry (DesktopStateFile.cs:33) and TryReplace (:50-61) and DesktopFileHistory.RememberCoreAsync (:186) swallow the failure, so a recent-file/port/level/window-place write is lost silently, while the extension-settings and approval stores report a session-only notice (DesktopExtensionSettingsStore.cs:277-281, DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.cs:162-170). Real but rare and recoverable, hence P3.
- **Correction:** The 'one save in 400' rate was measured with PowerShell readers that hold the handle for milliseconds; the host's readers hold it for tens of microseconds, so the real rate is lower (still non-zero, and it scales with the number of open windows). Also note DesktopFileHistory.LoadAsync (:163) opens FileShare.Read without Delete, which blocks the move for the whole async JSON read, so the recent-files document is the most exposed one. The reviewer's fix (retry the move a few times) is sound.

### WCS-07 — When following the file fails once, the screen stays on old data for good: the session is advanced without the derived state, and later nudges are ignored

**P3** · concurrency · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:708`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:751`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:257`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/read-chase.ts:116`
- **What:** followTheFile's pass assigns state.session from session.getSnapshot and then awaits refreshDerived(); refreshDerived's retry path also assigns state.session = refreshed before recursing and throws 'view-changed' on the third mismatch. The chase's failure callback only calls showError; the stillBehind re-entry lives in the redraw callback, which a failed pass never calls, and nudges that arrived while the pass was in flight were dropped by `if (inFlight) return`. onFileChanged then ignores any nudge whose changeSequence is <= state.session.manifest.changeSequence, which the failed pass already advanced, so state.compilation, recordWindows and the surface page stay at the older revision until the person navigates. showError also moves focus to the message slot (focusWithoutInteraction) even though this is a background refresh.
- **Failure:** An agent writes a burst of records while the person watches a board. Three consecutive refreshes see the file move and the pass fails with 'The file is changing. Refresh the view when the current changes finish.'; the agent's last write was already in the snapshot that pass read. The board never shows the last writes or a field the agent added, the sentence offers no Refresh control, focus jumps to it, and further fileChanged events for those sequences are ignored.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-journal-chase.mjs (real read-chase.ts and file-follow.ts, the main.ts follow wiring re-created) -> "nudge 12 -> chased" / "nudge 14 (while pass in flight) -> chased busy= true" / "{ passes: 1, redraws: 0, failures: 1, sessionSeq: 14, followTarget: 14, stillBehind: false }" / "later nudge 14 -> ignored ; derived state was never rebuilt for 14"
- **Fix and guard:** Keep a separate 'derived at' sequence set only when refreshDerived commits, compare nudges and stillBehind against it, re-arm the follow from the failure callback (the chase already bounds it to one pass a second), and report a background follow failure without stealing focus. Guard: read-chase/file-follow node test where the pass rejects after advancing the session and a later nudge at that sequence still schedules a pass.
- **Verifier:** Traced. The follow pass (main.ts:708-725) assigns state.session from session.getSnapshot and then awaits refreshDerived. refreshDerived also assigns state.session = refreshed on its retry path (actions.ts:262-266) and throws 'view-changed' on the third mismatch (:261). In read-chase.ts the failure branch (:116-122) sets allowedAt and calls only failed(), which here is showError (main.ts:718). The stillBehind re-entry exists only in the redraw callback (main.ts:716), which a failed pass never reaches, and a nudge that arrives while a pass is running returns at 'if (inFlight) return' (read-chase.ts:90). The host nudges once per commit with no heartbeat (MainPage.xaml.cs:73, MainWindow.xaml.cs:225). So after a failed pass nothing re-arms until some later commit or a navigation, and onFileChanged ignores nudges at or below the session's sequence (main.ts:751). showError also focuses the message slot (shell.ts:527-535) although this is a background refresh. The other chases (view-use.ts:271, 274) are re-armed by every render, which main.ts's follow is not. The error sentence has no Refresh control.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: the screen is stale only until the next commit by anyone or any navigation (a nudge after the failure starts a new pass), and writes made from the stale view are protected by expectedRecordVersion. The stated example is slightly off for a view-changed failure: that error means the file moved after the snapshot, so the last write is not in the snapshot the pass read, and the final nudge was swallowed while the pass was in flight. The sequence-ignored variant fits a failure of another kind after the snapshot was adopted (a read error or host-timeout in semantic.compile or data.queryRecords). Either way the missing piece is the same: a failed pass must re-arm the follow. The reviewer's probe re-created main.ts's wiring rather than running it; I confirmed the wiring against the source.

### WCS-11 — Opening Help resets the topic the person picked while Help was loading, and its late redraw lands on whatever page is on screen

**P3** · concurrency · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:545`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-help.ts:56`
- **What:** openHelp('') draws Help first, then awaits session.getSnapshot, refreshDerived (a full semantic.compile) and help.readPages. Topic buttons stay clickable meanwhile and set state.helpTopicId. After the awaits, `if (topicId === '' && state.view === 'help') state.helpTopicId = ''` and rerender() send renderHelp back to the file's first page or Start. The final rerender() is unconditional: actionInFlight is already false while help.readPages is awaited, so the person can have moved to another screen, and rerender -> main.render sets state.openDraft = null and replaces the content.
- **Failure:** The person opens Help on a large file and immediately clicks 'Connect with MCP'; a second later the article jumps back to the file's own first page. If help.readPages is slow (queued behind other host work), a person who has already left Help for a record page and started typing has the form redrawn from stored values when the late answer lands.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Remember the topic the first draw chose and only reset when state.helpTopicId still equals it; skip the final rerender unless state.view is still 'help' and nothing is held (holdingThePage()). Guard: unit test of openHelp with a delayed client that changes helpTopicId, and one that moves state.view, mid-flight.
- **Verifier:** actions.ts:532-547: openHelp('') draws Help (line 535), then awaits getSnapshot+refreshDerived (compile) and help.readPages, then at line 545 resets state.helpTopicId = '' if topicId === '' and view is still 'help', and calls rerender() unconditionally. Help topic buttons are data-help-topic (view-help.ts:28,54-61), which setBusy's selector (shell.ts:440: [data-action], [data-file-action], .studio-content inputs) does not disable, so a topic clicked while the refresh runs is overwritten and renderHelp (view-help.ts:17) falls back to the file's first page or Start. The final rerender() runs after actionInFlight is already false, so it redraws whatever view is current.
- **Correction:** The first half (clicked topic reset) has a real window, the length of the snapshot+compile on a large file. The second half (late redraw onto another page, destroying a draft) only spans help.readPages, a small local read, and during refreshDerived most rail routes refuse on actionInFlight, so it is largely theoretical. P3 is right.

### DAE-03 — A number that arrives as another JSON kind throws out of the handshake or a permission request, leaving the conversation stuck at Starting or Waiting for you

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:145`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:686`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:164`
- **What:** JsonElement.TryGetInt32 throws InvalidOperationException when the element is not a Number. StartAsync calls v.TryGetInt32 on protocolVersion without checking its kind (line 145) and catches only OperationCanceledException, AcpConnectionClosedException and AcpRemoteException (lines 164-176), so a string version faults the Started task with the state left at starting, no notice, and the 90-second handshake timeout no longer applies. CallDetails calls line.TryGetInt32 on a location's line (line 686), which ACP allows to be null; the throw happens inside AskPersonAsync's lock after Add("permission") has already put the entry in the transcript but before Options are set and before the entry is registered in _permissions, so the agent is answered -32603 and a permission entry with options null and answer null stays.
- **Failure:** (1) A person adds their own command and it turns out to speak MCP rather than ACP (both start with initialize); it answers protocolVersion "2025-06-18". The tab says Starting forever, no sentence says why, another launch is refused as agent-already-running, and only End gets them out. (2) An agent asks permission for an edit with locations [{path, line: null}]: its tool call fails with "Nendo could not answer.", and the tab shows a permission card with no buttons and the state Waiting for you (waitingForYou is true for any permission entry with answer null) for the rest of the conversation; Answer is refused as agent-question-gone and Stop does not clear it.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh -File scratchpad/review/desktop-agents-extensions/malformed-probe.ps1 against the shipped AgentConversation -> "1. initialize answered with protocolVersion \"2025-06-18\": state=starting; handshake task status=Faulted; exception=InvalidOperationException; notice=" and "2. permission with location line null: agent was answered={\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":\"p1\",\"error\":{\"code\":-32603,\"message\":\"Nendo could not answer.\"}}; permission entries in transcript=1; its options=null; its answer=null", "answering it: The agent is no longer waiting for that answer.", "after Stop: answer=null (still waiting)".
- **Fix and guard:** Check ValueKind == Number before every TryGetInt32/TryGetInt64 on agent-supplied JSON (a small helper), treat any other kind as absent (version 0, no line), build the permission entry fully before Add, and have StartAsync end the conversation with a sentence on any unexpected exception. Guard in DesktopLaunchedAgentTests with the fake agent: initialize answered with a string protocolVersion must end with a notice naming the version, and a permission request with line null must show its options and be answerable; falsify by restoring the unchecked TryGetInt32.
- **Verifier:** Traced in source. AgentConversation.cs:145 calls v.TryGetInt32 on protocolVersion with no ValueKind check; JsonElement.TryGetInt32 throws InvalidOperationException for a String. StartAsync (lines 164-176) catches only OperationCanceled, AcpConnectionClosed and AcpRemote, and DesktopLaunchedAgent.cs:78 assigns the task to Started, which nothing awaits (grep shows only the assignment), so the fault is never observed and the state stays starting; WatchAsync only wakes on process exit/Closed/Ended. AgentConversation.cs:686 does the same on a location's line (null is legal in ACP), inside AskPersonAsync's lock after Add("permission") (line ~455) and before Options are set (line ~463) and before _permissions registration; AcpConnection.AnswerAsync (line ~236) turns it into -32603, leaving a permission entry with Answer null, which waitingForYou (agent-chat-model.ts:94) counts. Both defects are real, but I downgrade to P3: the first needs a non-ACP program answering initialize with a string version (a custom command pointed at an MCP server), the second needs an agent that sends line:null rather than omitting it, which the mainstream ACP adapters I know of do not; End clears both.
- **Correction:** Priority P3 rather than P2 (trigger needs a protocol-violating or non-ACP program; End is a workaround). Evidence is accurate. Note the stale permission entry's Revision is set by Add() without a Touch(), so it may only appear in the tab on the next change.

### EBH-13 — The body codec accepts numeric enum text, and an undefined binding kind or aggregate escapes as InvalidOperationException

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourBodyCodec.cs:438`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourBodyCodec.cs:277`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourDefinitions.cs:182`
- **What:** Enum<TValue> uses Enum.TryParse, which accepts any integer string and returns undefined values. NendoBindingShape.For then calls All.First(...), which throws InvalidOperationException for a kind or aggregate outside the table. The MCP boundary maps an unrecognised exception to NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR. Numeric aliases such as "0" are silently accepted as SameRecordField/Integer.
- **Failure:** An agent sends a binding with "kind": "9" or "aggregate": "5": instead of a refusal naming the binding and the allowed kinds it gets NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR (InvalidOperationException; Sequence contains no matching element).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe2.ps1 NendoBehaviourCodec.Read of an authored calculation with binding kind "9" -> THROW System.InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no matching element; aggregate "5" -> same; kind "0" -> accepted as SameRecordField.
- **Fix and guard:** Refuse text that is numeric or not Enum.IsDefined in Enum<TValue>, with the existing 'Use one of' remedy. Guard: codec tests for "9" and "0".
- **Verifier:** BehaviourBodyCodec.Enum<TValue> (BehaviourBodyCodec.cs:438-446) uses Enum.TryParse(text, ignoreCase: false, ...), which returns true for numeric text and an undefined member, so "kind":"9" passes. Bindings() then calls NendoBindingShape.For(kind, aggregate) (:277), which is All.First(...) over the closed table (BehaviourDefinitions.cs:182) and throws InvalidOperationException. The authored path NendoAgentAuthoringService.RequireCompilable catches only NendoValidationException or ArgumentException (:926), and both NendoToolErrors and NendoMcpErrors map any other exception to NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR (NendoToolErrors.cs:84-89, NendoMcpErrors.cs:43-47). The sibling BehaviourKind parser in CanonicalChangeSetRequest.cs:309-312 already guards with Enum.IsDefined, so the codec is the gap. "0" is accepted as the first enum member (SameRecordField, Count). Only a malformed request triggers it, and agents send names, so impact is a misleading error code on bad input.
- **Correction:** None. Remedy should also make Enum<TValue> reject numeric text, not only undefined values, so that "0" stops aliasing.

### ECO-03 — BeginProposalAsync leaves a half-registered proposal (and a full clone in %TEMP%) when the refusal diagnosis is cancelled or the final persist fails

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:147`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:356`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:167`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:44`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:179`
- **What:** The proposal is added to _proposals at line 56. Only the sibling catch at lines 153-166 removes it, and that handler does not cover exceptions thrown from inside the catch (NendoException) block at lines 145-152. DiagnoseRefusalAsync catches NendoException, IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException but not OperationCanceledException (lines 350-361), so a cancelled pass-clone backup escapes with the proposal still registered in state Validating. The final ProposalWorkspace.PersistAsync(context, cancellationToken) at line 167 sits outside every handler, so a cancellation or IO error there leaves a Previewable proposal whose ID was never returned. The workspace directory is also created (line 44) before CaptureTouchedRecords/SemanticDiff.From (lines 54-55), which can throw record-not-found, and that directory is never removed. The comment at lines 154-162 states that a half-registered proposal must not linger.
- **Failure:** An agent's validate of a refused change set is cancelled by the client while the extra refusal clones run. The coordinator keeps a 'Validating' proposal and its proposal.nendo, a full copy of the file, until the file closes. Restore then reports one more pending proposal than the person can see. For a custom view, a cancel during the last persist leaves a Previewable proposal the view never received. Every later proposal from that view is refused with 'proposal-waiting' (DesktopSessionController.Extensions.cs:179-183).
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Wrap everything after registration, including DiagnoseRefusalAsync and the final persist, in one try whose non-Nendo handler removes the proposal and TryDeletes the workspace. Alternatively, register only after the final persist succeeds, and persist with CancellationToken.None. Capture the touched records before ProposalWorkspace.Create. Guard: an Engine test that cancels the token during the refusal diagnosis and during the final persist, through seams. It asserts ListProposalsAsync is empty and the proposal root holds no proposal-* directory.
- **Verifier:** Traced in NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs: the proposal is registered at line 56 and only the sibling handler at 153-166 removes it. An exception thrown from inside the `catch (NendoException)` block (145-152) is not seen by that sibling handler, and DiagnoseRefusalAsync's catches (350, 356-361) cover NendoException/IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException but not OperationCanceledException, while BackupToAsync/OpenAsync/ApplyChangeSetAsync at 335-346 take the caller's token. A cancelled validate of a refused change set therefore leaves a Validating context in _proposals plus a full proposal.nendo clone in %TEMP%. The only caller on the agent path (NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:327-373) cleans up through draft.Preview, which is still null because PrepareProposalAsync never returned, so nothing rejects it. The final PersistAsync at line 167 is likewise outside every handler, and the 153-166 comment says a half-registered proposal must not linger. Impact is small: the leak is bounded to the file session (cleaned by CleanupAbandoned on dispose), the proposal is visible in ListProposalsAsync and can be rejected, and the trigger needs a cancellation or IO error in a narrow window.
- **Correction:** The Create-before-CaptureTouchedRecords workspace directory at line 44 is not a lasting leak: Outcomes.cs:51/78 and dispose sweep abandoned workspaces through CleanupAbandoned. 'proposal-waiting' for a view only applies to the final-persist case (state already Previewable), and the person can reject that proposal, so it is not stuck.

- **Verifier:** Traced in NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs: `context.State = Applying` and `await ProposalWorkspace.PersistAsync(context, cancellationToken)` at lines 198-199 sit before the try at 201, and the reset to Previewable at 245 covers only exceptions from store.ApplyChangeSetAsync. PersistAsync is five File.WriteAllTextAsync calls with the caller's token (ProposalWorkspace.cs:111-135), so a cancellation or IO error there leaves State=Applying with nothing committed. Every retry then returns 'Only a previewable proposal can be applied.' at line 87, and nothing else resets the state (the only other use of Applying is a display string, NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:684). By contrast FinishCommittedProposalAsync treats the same write as best effort. The impact is bounded: RejectProposalAsync works in any state, so the person or agent rejects and validates again, and the trigger needs a cancellation or IO fault in a very small window before a normal commit.

<a id="eco-09"></a>

### ECO-09 — A failed restore or upgrade from a read-only session keeps the instance lease and write-owner sidecar it acquired

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Restore.cs:99`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Upgrade.cs:56`
- **What:** When _instanceOwnership is null, RestoreAsync and UpgradeAsync acquire InstanceOwnershipLease and WriteOwnershipLease into the coordinator's fields (Restore.cs:99-104; Upgrade.cs:56-61), then call ExecuteReplacementCoreAsync. A failure before retirement (restore-stage-invalid, a full volume while staging, the source changing) returns without releasing them, and the session stays a read-only inspection holding write authority until it is closed.
- **Failure:** The person inspects a recovery file read-only and tries Restore, and staging fails. They then open the same file for editing in another window and get 'This application instance is already open for editing in another Nendo session', although no session is editing it.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Track whether this call acquired the leases, and dispose them in a finally when !_replacementRetired. Guard: an Engine test where BeforeRestoreValidation throws on a read-only coordinator, followed by OpenAsync from a second coordinator, which must succeed.
- **Verifier:** RestoreAsync (Restore.cs:99-104) and UpgradeAsync (Upgrade.cs:56-61) assign InstanceOwnershipLease and WriteOwnershipLease to the coordinator's fields when _instanceOwnership is null (a read-only/recovery session), then call ExecuteReplacementCoreAsync. Any throw before _replacementRetired (stage invalid, disk full, cancellation, current-backup invalid) leaves RestoreAsync through the NendoRecoveryRequiredException catch and the gate-release finally, which release no lease. Desktop's ReplaceFileAsync (DesktopFileReplacement.cs:~95-103) only detaches when Health == Closed, which is not true before retirement, so the read-only session stays open. The leases are released only in DisposeAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:~383-410). InstanceOwnershipLease is a Global named kernel event (InstanceOwnership.cs:29-39), so another window or process opening the same instance for editing gets 'instance-in-use'. The session's Capabilities stay read-only, so it holds write exclusion without writing.
- **Correction:** Narrow in practice: it needs a read-only or recovery session, a restore or upgrade that fails after the lease step but before retirement, and a second window that wants write access while the first stays open. A retry of the same restore in the same session is fine, since the held leases are reused. Priority P3 stands.

<a id="esc-06"></a>

### ESC-06 — SQLITE_BUSY from a write or read transaction reaches adapters as a raw SqliteException, not the typed busy outcome ADR-0011 requires

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-storage-core`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:112`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:246`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:333`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:521`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:137`
- **What:** ADR-0011 says "Busy outcomes remain bounded typed service errors". ApplyAsync and ApplyChangeSetAsync start with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and end with transaction.Commit(). In DELETE mode, COMMIT needs an EXCLUSIVE lock. The bounded queries open deferred read transactions. None of these maps SqliteErrorCode 5 or 6. Only VerifyBackupAuthorityAsync (Backup.cs:27) and InspectAsync (Inspection.cs:577) translate busy into a typed code (backup-source-busy, file-busy). Nothing in NendoWriteCoordinator or the adapters catches SqliteException, and NendoToolErrors.Translate turns it into NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR.
- **Failure:** A SQLite-aware reader outside Nendo holds a shared lock on the open .nendo file for more than 2 s, such as DB Browser for SQLite or a sqlite3 shell left in a read transaction. Every save then fails after the 2,000 ms timeout. The person or agent sees an internal error rather than "the file is busy, retry". The retry advice the backup path already gives is missing.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Catch SqliteException with code 5 or 6 around BeginTransaction and Commit in ApplyAsync and ApplyChangeSetAsync, after the rollback, and in the read entry points. Rethrow it as a NendoPreconditionException("file-busy", …). Guard: a test that holds BEGIN; SELECT 1 on a second connection to the same file and asserts ApplyAsync throws NendoPreconditionException with code file-busy, and that the file is unchanged.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. SqliteNendoStore.cs:112 opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE and :246 commits; the catch at :252-262 only rolls back and rethrows. NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:267-295 catches only NendoRecoveryRequiredException. The only SqliteException 5-or-6 handlers in src are Backup.cs:27 and Inspection.cs:577, and NendoToolErrors.cs:85-89 maps anything else to NENDO_INTERNAL_ERROR. SQLite behaviour is that a DELETE-mode COMMIT needs EXCLUSIVE and fails with SQLITE_BUSY once the 2,000 ms busy timeout passes while another connection holds a read lock; BackupTests.cs:466-487 demonstrates the same lock from the other side (error code 5). ADR-0011:58-59 says busy outcomes stay bounded typed service errors, and the write path gives the bound but not the type. The trigger needs a reader outside Nendo holding a read transaction past 2 s (Nendo's own connections are serialized by the coordinator gate), which is uncommon, so P3.
- **Correction:** BEGIN IMMEDIATE itself does not fail against readers, because RESERVED coexists with SHARED. It fails only against an external writer. The reader-caused failure comes at COMMIT (:246), or earlier on a cache spill that needs EXCLUSIVE. The finding's fix location (catch around Commit and BeginTransaction) is right, but the BeginTransaction half applies only to writers.

<a id="esm-08"></a>

### ESM-08 — Surface nesting depth is unbounded and unvalidated: a record page nested 29 sections deep makes Compile throw JsonException, and a front page nested about 1,000 sections deep overflows the stack and kills the host

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:914`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticModel.cs:170`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:175`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:531`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:108`, `src/Nendo.Engine/SemanticVocabulary.cs:297`
- **What:** section admits section, and the compiler states depth is 'bounded by which kinds may contain which, not by a constant', so nothing limits it. WithComposableDigest serializes each application plan with NendoRenderPlanJson.Options, which keeps System.Text.Json's default MaxDepth of 64; each node level costs two JSON levels, so a deeper record page throws JsonException ('A possible object cycle was detected ... maximum allowed depth of 64') out of Compile. The front page has no digest, so its CompileOverviewNode/CompileOverviewChild recursion continues until the thread's stack is exhausted. Proposal preparation compiles the clone in the host process; a JsonException escapes as a non-Nendo exception, and a stack overflow cannot be caught at all.
- **Failure:** An agent (or a generator with a recursion bug) authors a record page 29 sections deep: validation fails with an internal error rather than a diagnostic. On a file whose front page already nests about 900 sections (built over several accepted proposals, each within the 512-operation ceiling), the next validate that adds a further level crashes the Nendo process, taking the open planner, every agent connection and any unsaved typing with it.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-depth.ps1 (Compile on the built DLL, thread-pool thread) -> 'depth=28 mode=pool -> valid=True diagnostics=0' then 'depth=29 ... Exception calling "OnPool" ... "A possible object cycle was detected. This can either be due to a cycle or if the object depth is larger than the maximum allowed depth of 64."'; overview mode -> 'depth=920 mode=overview_pool -> valid=True' and 'exit=-1073741571 depth=1000 :: Stack overflow.'
- **Fix and guard:** Publish a maximum node depth in the vocabulary (well under the digest limit, e.g. 16) and refuse deeper trees in ValidateComposableTree with a new NUI code before any recursion; make the digest serializer's MaxDepth follow from it. Guard: compile tests at the limit (valid) and one past it (the new code, no exception), plus a 1,000-deep front page that returns the diagnostic; falsify by removing the check.
- **Verifier:** The record-page half is traced: section admits section (SemanticVocabulary.cs:297-300), no depth limit exists in ValidateComposableTree (:293-361) or in ExecuteAddUiNodeAsync (Operations.cs:194-225), and WithComposableDigest (ComposableSurfaces.cs:914-918) serializes the plan with NendoRenderPlanJson.Options, which sets no MaxDepth, so System.Text.Json's default of 64 applies and each node level adds two JSON levels. Compile has no try/catch (NendoSemanticCompiler.cs:10-18), and BeginProposalAsync rethrows a non-Nendo exception raw (Proposals.cs:153-166), so a deep enough record page, reachable in one change set (about 60 canonical operations), fails validation with an internal error instead of a diagnostic. The front-page half is real by reading (CompileOverviewNode/CompileOverviewChild recurse with no digest, :175-247), but a single change set is capped at 128 submitted operations (NendoAuthoringLimits.OperationsPerChangeSet), so at most about 128 nested sections, far below the roughly 900 needed; reaching it takes about eight separately accepted proposals, each of which must itself compile, which an Unattended agent could do but a normal flow would not.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3: the JsonException is only a poor error for an absurd nesting, and the stack overflow needs hundreds of nested front-page sections built across many accepted proposals (a stack overflow during preview happens before acceptance, so the crashing state is never committed). The exact depth threshold (the finding says 29 sections) was not re-measured here; by counting it is in the low 30s, which does not change the verdict.

<a id="ext-05"></a>

### EXT-05 — Corrupt, encrypted or unsupported-compression zip entries escape ReadZip as raw exceptions and reach the Workbench as `internal`

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:101`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:106`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:80`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:506`
- **What:** ReadZip turns InvalidDataException into NendoValidationException only around the ZipArchive constructor. entry.Open() and Read() throw InvalidDataException for BZip2, LZMA or PPMd entries, encrypted entries, and corrupt deflate data or CRCs. Those propagate unchanged, and WorkbenchProtocol's final `catch (Exception)` answers 'internal: The host could not complete the Workbench request.'
- **Failure:** A person imports a package that 7-Zip compressed with BZip2, or a truncated download. Instead of being told the zip cannot be read, they get a generic host failure with no file named. The contract says a package that cannot be carried is refused by name.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe5.ps1 (stored zip with index.html's method patched to 12) -> 'bzip2 entry -> System.IO.InvalidDataException: The archive entry was compressed using BZip2 and is not supported. (is NendoException: False)'
- **Fix and guard:** Wrap the manifest and file reads in ReadZip in `catch (Exception e) when (e is InvalidDataException or NotSupportedException)` and rethrow NendoValidationException("{relative} in the zip cannot be read: ..."). Guard: a ReadZip test with a method-12 entry and one with a corrupted deflate stream, both expecting NendoValidationException that names the entry.
- **Verifier:** ExtensionArchive.cs:79-80 converts InvalidDataException only around the ZipArchive constructor. entry.Open() and the reads in ReadBounded (lines 101 and 106) are unguarded, and .NET throws InvalidDataException for unsupported compression methods such as BZip2, for encrypted entries, and for corrupt deflate streams. InvalidDataException is not a NendoException, JsonException, IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException. The import path (WorkbenchProtocol.Extensions.cs:103) is a bare Task.Run(Read) with no catch, so the exception reaches the final catch at WorkbenchProtocol.cs:506 and the person sees 'internal: The host could not complete the Workbench request.' No other InvalidDataException handling exists in src/ (grep). The contract promises a package that cannot be carried is refused by name. It is a rare input (BZip2/encrypted/truncated zip) with a safe failure (nothing proposed) and an easy workaround, so P3.
- **Correction:** None. The wrap should also cover NotSupportedException, as proposed.

### GDN-17 — Failed reads in Today and after a save have no catch, so the view stays silent

**P3** · reliability · Confirmed · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/workspace.js:1040`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:969`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:1174`
- **What:** daily() awaits records.get for the Template note without a catch (1040), and send()'s read-back after a save that raced typing awaits records.get outside any catch (969); both are reached from the command listener (1174) or the guide, which do not catch, so a refusal becomes an unhandled rejection.
- **Failure:** Today is pressed while the file is busy or the template read times out: no new note, no problem line, nothing. A save whose read-back fails is kept but the view does not move onto the saved version and says nothing.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Catch both reads and show the problem with Retry, as open() and loadIndex() do. Guard: a gate step with broker.fail('records.get') before Today asserting a problem line.
- **Verifier:** daily() (workspace.js:1034-1042) awaits nendo.records.get for the Template note with no try/catch, unlike open() (:365-368), which catches and shows the problem. Every caller drops the rejection: command() has no catch (:1132-1137) and the 'command' listener ignores its promise (:1174); the guide handler is an async listener with no catch (:1244-1252); takeRequest() calls it (:1299) from begin() (:1328), so a Today request handed over from the Overview that meets a failed read rejects begin() itself, skipping storeDrafts, the 'kept from before' status and the unanswered-save problem at :1333-1335. The seeded garden does carry a Template note (tools/garden/definition.mjs:506), so the read happens on the normal Today path. Result is a silent no-op, as claimed; the trigger is a failing single-record read, so rare.
