### R2LAT-10 — Six first-party views and the authoring guide mark their English text as the person's language (<html lang> set to context.locale), so screen readers speak each view with a Danish, Thai or Arabic voice

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/garden.js:28`, `extensions/gantt/gantt.js:317`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:294`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:613`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:994`, `extensions/archi/view.js:2275`, `docs/custom-view-authoring.md:154`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:103`
- **What:** The view context's locale is navigator.language (view-frames.ts:103). Nendo sets no WebView2 language option, so this is the Windows display language. Each of these views then runs document.documentElement.lang = context.locale, but every string it draws is English: 'Show all', 'Overdue', 'tasks done', 'No record selected', the Gantt's empty-state sentences. The Workbench page around the frames is lang="en" (src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:2). The attribute is used as a carrier for date formatting: gantt.js:34 and garden/tasks.mjs:63 read documentElement.lang as the toLocaleDateString locale. The custom-view authoring guide's example (docs/custom-view-authoring.md:154) teaches the same line, so third-party views copy it. WCAG 3.1.1 requires the declared language to be the language of the text.
- **Failure:** On Windows with a Danish display language, NVDA (automatic language switching is on by default) and Narrator switch to the Danish voice inside every custom view frame. 'Show all', 'Overdue', 'No date' and the Gantt row labels are spoken with Danish phonetics, while the Workbench chrome around them is read in English. With a Thai or Arabic display language, a Thai or Arabic voice reads the English words, and some synthesizers spell them letter by letter.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Leave <html lang="en"> (the language the view is written in) and keep context.locale in a variable for the formatters; set lang to the person's locale only on elements that hold the person's own text, such as the Garden note editor, if that is wanted. Change docs/custom-view-authoring.md:154 to match. Guard: a Review-ExtensionViews step that loads each first-party view with context.locale set to 'da-DK' and asserts document.documentElement.lang === 'en' while the Gantt axis still formats Danish month names; falsify by restoring the current line in one view.
- **Verifier:** help.ts:34-38 builds the topic text with toLocaleLowerCase() and view-help.ts:50 lowercases the query the same way. The match is a plain includes (view-help.ts:41), and the help text is English. Nothing in src/ sets a WebView2 language or ICU locale (grep for CoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions, --lang and .Language finds none). Under a tr or az default locale 'Import'.toLocaleLowerCase('tr') returns 'ımport', and I confirmed in node that it does not include 'import'. The search therefore loses every capital-I word for a Turkish display-language user, while search-text.ts uses the locale-independent toLowerCase. help.test.mjs runs in the default en locale, so it never exercises this. The WebView2 default locale under a Turkish Windows display language was not reproduced here; the reviewer's CDP override stands in for it. Only Help search is affected and it has a workaround (type capitals as İ), so P3.

### SITE-06 — Text and control contrast below WCAG AA: code on the violet panel 3.88:1, the green 'reversible' label 3.82:1, violet eyebrows on dark panels 4.40:1, search field border 1.43:1

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/src/pages/index.astro:353`, `site/src/pages/index.astro:448`, `site/src/pages/index.astro:438`, `site/src/styles/global.css:138`, `site/src/styles/tokens.css:70`, `site/src/pages/concept.astro:197`, `site/src/components/DocsSearch.astro:25`
- **What:** Computed from rendered colours (alpha blended): Light home '.panel-violet code' rgb(255,255,255) on 143,107,229 = 3.88:1 at 15.3px (index.astro:353-357 puts white on rgba(255,255,255,0.16) over --violet-slab); '.proposal-rev strong' rgb(31,138,76) on 237,239,251 = 3.82:1 at 14.4px and '.op-sign' 3.83:1 (--healthy #1f8a4c on --canvas / --healthy-soft). Dark: '.eyebrow' and '.axiom-number' rgb(154,115,240) (--violet #9a73f0, tokens.css:70) on the panel surface 28,33,80 = 4.40:1 at 15.2px and 13.1px, on the home 'The problem' panel, concept 'How it could fail' and the axiom numbers, status 'The biggest risk'. The search input's only boundary is --line-strong #c3c9e6 on the rail's #edeffb = 1.43:1 (1.64:1 on white; dark 1.97:1), under the 3:1 non-text minimum.
- **Failure:** A low-vision reader in Light cannot reliably read the inline '.nendo' code on the home page's violet 'The idea' panel or the 'reversible' verdict in the proposal demo; in Dark every eyebrow on a raised panel is under 4.5:1.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: CDP contrast.mjs over 11 pages in both themes -> 'light / code. rgb(255, 255, 255) on 143,107,229,1 ratio 3.88', 'strong. rgb(31, 138, 76) on 237,239,251,1 ratio 3.82', 'dark /concept span.axiom-number rgb(154, 115, 240) on 28,33,80,1 ratio 4.40'; node contrast calc -> 'light input border line-strong on canvas 1.43 on white 1.64'
- **Fix and guard:** Give .panel-violet code a darker fill (for example color-mix of --violet-slab with black) instead of a white tint; darken light --healthy to about #17733f; lighten dark --violet to about #a888f5 or use --ink for eyebrows on raised panels; give the search input a border that reaches 3:1. Guard: keep contrast.mjs as a lane over every page in both themes, failing below 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for control boundaries.
- **Verifier:** Recomputed the WCAG ratios from tokens.css and the CSS: white on rgba(255,255,255,0.16) over --violet-slab #7a4fe0 (index.astro:353-357) is 3.88:1; --healthy #1f8a4c on --canvas #edeffb (index.astro:448, .proposal-rev sits in the .proposal tray with background var(--canvas)) is 3.82:1; dark --violet #9a73f0 on --surface-raised #1c2150 (the .panel behind .eyebrow, global.css:138, and .axiom-number, concept.astro:197) is 4.40:1; --line-strong #c3c9e6 on canvas is 1.43:1 (1.64 on white; dark #3a4190 on #121634 is 1.97). All below 4.5:1 for 13-15px text or 3:1 for the input boundary (DocsSearch.astro:25). Genuine but marginal AA misses, not a blocker.
- **Correction:** .op-sign (index.astro:438) is an aria-hidden decorative '+' glyph, so it is weaker evidence than the 'reversible' label and the code/eyebrow cases. The search-field border claim rests on a strict reading of WCAG 1.4.11 (the white fill against the canvas is also faint).

### SITE-07 — Keyboard focus ring is cobalt on the violet panel: 1.11:1 in Light, 2.42:1 in Dark

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/src/styles/global.css:51`, `site/src/pages/index.astro:345`
- **What:** global.css:51 draws every :focus-visible outline in --cobalt. The home page's 'The idea' panel (index.astro:345-351) is --violet-slab, and its 'How it works' link is reached by keyboard (15th Tab stop). Outline rgb(36,88,230) on panel rgb(122,79,224) = 1.11:1 in Light; dark #6f98ff on #6441c9 = 2.42:1. Screenshot focus-violet-light.png shows a blue ring barely separable from the violet.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user tabbing down the home page loses track of focus on the violet panel's link, because the ring is nearly the same luminance as the panel (WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.7).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: CDP focus2.mjs -> 'focused in violet panel: How it works after 15 tabs', '{"outline":"rgb(36, 88, 230) solid","offset":"2px","panelBg":"rgb(122, 79, 224)"}'; contrast calc -> 'light focus cobalt on violet-slab 1.11', 'dark focus cobalt on violet-slab 2.42'
- **Fix and guard:** Override the ring inside .panel-violet (outline-color: var(--on-violet)), or use a two-tone ring (outline plus box-shadow in --canvas) everywhere. Guard: a focus probe that tabs through each page and asserts the outline colour against the nearest opaque background is at least 3:1.
- **Verifier:** global.css:51 draws every :focus-visible outline as 2px solid var(--cobalt) with no override anywhere in site/src (grep for outline/:focus finds only that rule). index.astro:345-351 gives .panel-violet the --violet-slab background and its only link 'How it works' inherits that ring. I recomputed contrast from tokens.css: cobalt #2458e6 on #7a4fe0 = 1.11:1 (Light) and #6f98ff on #6441c9 = 2.42:1 (Dark), both under the 3:1 non-text minimum, and the link has no other focus cue. CSS is deterministic so this holds without a browser. Accessibility polish on a site outside the product boundary (ADR-0018), hence P3.

### SITE-08 — Docs search is not announced or navigable as a combobox, and Escape wipes the query and drops focus to the page body

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/src/components/DocsSearch.astro:9`, `site/src/components/DocsSearch.astro:16`, `site/src/components/DocsSearch.astro:137`
- **What:** The input (DocsSearch.astro:9-15) has no role=combobox, aria-controls, aria-expanded or aria-describedby, and the results container (line 16) has no role, label or aria-live, so a screen reader hears nothing when results arrive or when 'Nothing matched.' replaces them. ArrowDown does nothing. The keydown handler (line 137-139) calls input.blur() on Escape, and Chromium's native Escape on type=search also clears the value. Probe attributes: {"role":null,"live":null,"inputAttrs":"id,type,placeholder,autocomplete,data-pagefind-base,..."}.
- **Failure:** A screen-reader user types 'lease' in the rail search: four results appear silently; pressing ArrowDown stays in the field. Pressing Escape to close the panel erases 'lease' and moves focus to <body>, so the query must be typed again.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: CDP search.mjs and esc.mjs -> 'after ArrowDown active: INPUT docs-search-input'; 'before {"value":"lease","hidden":false,"results":4}' then 'after Escape {"value":"","hidden":true,"active":"BODY"}'
- **Fix and guard:** Give the input role=combobox, aria-expanded tied to results.hidden and aria-controls the results list (role=listbox or a list with an aria-live=polite count line such as '4 guides match'); move focus into the results on ArrowDown; on Escape preventDefault, close the panel and keep focus and the value in the field. Guard: extend docs-search.test.mjs to assert aria-expanded toggles and the value survives Escape, and Gate-SiteSearch.mjs to press Escape and read input.value and document.activeElement.
- **Verifier:** DocsSearch.astro:9-17 has an input with no role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls or aria-describedby, and the results div has no role, label or aria-live, so arriving results and 'Nothing matched.' are not announced (WCAG 4.1.3). The only keydown handler (line 137-139) handles Escape and nothing else, so ArrowDown does nothing. Escape calls dismiss() and an explicit input.blur(), so focus drops to body. The query wipe comes from Chromium's native Escape-clears behaviour on type=search, and the code does not prevent it. Neither scripts/docs-search.test.mjs nor tools/Gate-SiteSearch.mjs asserts any aria state. Real but minor accessibility gap on the public site, P3.
- **Correction:** The focus drop is deliberate (explicit input.blur()) and the value clearing is browser-native for type=search rather than application code, so the fix has to preventDefault on Escape and drop the blur, not only add ARIA.

### SITE-10 — Autoplaying motion that never stops: the looping brand video has no controls and the hero mark breathes forever, unless the OS asks for reduced motion

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `site`

Guard: a probe asserting the video exposes a pause control and that no animation-iteration-count is infinite on the page without one.
- **Verifier:** index.astro:211-219 renders the brand video with muted, loop, playsinline and autoplay, and no controls. The inline script (222-235) adds controls and pauses it only under prefers-reduced-motion. I loaded the built page in the browser pane and read controls false, loop true, autoplay true, paused false, buffered 0-10.005 s. BrandMark.astro:32-35 runs brand-mark-breathe 6s infinite on the hero mark, with the same reduced-motion-only exit (global.css:236). Both start automatically, last over 5 s and sit beside text with no pause mechanism for other readers, which fails WCAG 2.2.2 (Level A). I recomputed it: #005fb8 at 22% over white is about (199,220,239), 1.41:1 against white, matching the reported 1.4. The @ option (22-agent-chat.css:1103-1108) is a #f3f3f4 fill plus a 1px inset cobalt-45% ring, which comes to about 2.28:1 against the white panel, matching 2.27. The switch off track is var(--line-strong) #d1d1d1 on a white card (11-agent-access.css:553-573), about 1.5:1, with a #ffffff knob. All three fall under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11; the composer's :focus-within ring is already on while the selects are focused, so it does not mark which one is. The toggle button itself does have a full-contrast :focus-visible outline (11-agent-access.css:532). No ADR mandates this. It is polish, not a blocker.
- **Correction:** The switch item is a state-indicator contrast issue, not a focus indicator; the button's own focus ring is fine. Otherwise accurate.

<a id="uik-10"></a>

### UIK-10 — The @ menu is not exposed as a popup: the message box is a plain textbox with no expanded or haspopup state, so opening the list is not announced

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:271`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-mention.ts:111`
- **What:** The textarea carries aria-autocomplete, aria-controls and aria-expanded. aria-expanded is not supported on the textbox role, so Chrome drops it, and there is no aria-haspopup. drawMenu only toggles those attributes and announces nothing. The command palette's input, by contrast, exposes combobox, hasPopup and expanded.
- **Failure:** A screen-reader user types '@'. A listbox of record types, views and proposals opens over the box, but nothing says a list appeared or how many choices it holds. Arrows silently change aria-activedescendant on a control the reader treats as a plain multiline edit.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p15 Accessibility.getPartialAXTree -> chat: "textbox \"Message to the agent\" [...[\"autocomplete\",\"list\"],[\"activedescendant\",[\"mention-option-1\"]],[\"controls\",\"chat-mention\"]...]" (no expanded, no hasPopup); palette: "combobox \"Command\" [...[\"hasPopup\",\"listbox\"],[\"expanded\",true],[\"activedescendant\",[\"command-option-1\"]]...]".
- **Fix and guard:** Add aria-haspopup="listbox" to the textarea (supported on textbox). Announce through #announcement when the menu opens ('6 choices; up and down to choose') and when the active option changes, and drop the unsupported aria-expanded. Guard: an AX assertion that the textarea exposes hasPopup=listbox, plus a check of the announcement text after typing '@'.
- **Verifier:** view-agent-chat.ts:271 puts aria-autocomplete, aria-controls and aria-expanded on a plain <textarea>, which has the textbox role; aria-expanded is not a supported attribute for textbox in ARIA 1.2, and there is no aria-haspopup. agent-mention.ts:111-129 (drawMenu) only toggles those attributes and aria-activedescendant. Neither drawMenu nor follow() calls announce() when the list opens or on a count (announce is used only after a choice, line 231). The textarea is therefore exposed without any popup or expanded state, while the command palette input is a combobox. No test or doc asserts the textarea's popup semantics. It is a real semantics gap, but screen-reader polish.
- **Correction:** 'Arrows silently change aria-activedescendant' is overstated: aria-activedescendant is supported on textbox and Chromium screen readers normally announce the new active option. What is missing is the announcement that a list opened and how many choices it holds. The fix (aria-haspopup="listbox" plus an announce on open) stands. The effect on actual screen-reader output was not measured, only the AX tree.

<a id="uik-11"></a>

### UIK-11 — ARIA roles misreport two controls: the title-bar tablist contains close and New tab buttons, and the access ladder is five toggle buttons that cannot be un-pressed

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard` · also reported as WCS-23, UIS-22

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:85`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/workspace-tabs.ts:117`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:252`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:448`
- **What:** #tab-strip is role=tablist, but drawTabs fills it with div wrappers that hold a role=tab button and a close button, followed by #tab-new. Every tab is a Tab stop although the arrow keys also move between them. The ladder renders five buttons with aria-pressed, one of them pressed. setAgentMode returns early when the pressed one is pressed again, so it is a single-choice group presented as independent toggles.
- **Failure:** A screen reader in the tab strip meets 'Close Agent access' and 'New tab' buttons inside a tab list, so the tab count and position it reports are wrong. On the ladder it hears 'Shape app, toggle button, pressed'. Pressing it does nothing, although a toggle promises to turn off.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p14 Accessibility.getFullAXTree -> under the tablist: "tab \| Agent access", "button \| Close Agent access", "tab \| GitHub Copilot CLI", "button \| Close GitHub Copilot CLI", "button \| New tab"; ladder: "group \| Agent access level" with "button \| Shape app Propose structure and surfaces \| {'pressed': 'true'}".
- **Fix and guard:** Keep only role=tab children in the tablist: put the close and New tab buttons outside it (or give the wrappers role=presentation with the close buttons outside the tab sequence) and use a roving tabindex. Render the ladder as role=radiogroup with role=radio and aria-checked. Guard: AX-tree assertions that every tablist child is a tab and that the ladder exposes radios.
- **Verifier:** index.html:82 declares #tab-strip as role=tablist, and workspace-tabs.ts:117-128 fills it with role-less div wrappers holding a role=tab button, a close button and then the #tab-new button, so the tablist contains non-tab buttons; none of the tab-main buttons has a roving tabindex, so each tab and each close button is a Tab stop. view-agent.ts:252-253 renders the five access levels as aria-pressed buttons in a role=group, and view-agent.ts:448 returns early when the pressed level is pressed again, so the group is single-choice and cannot be un-pressed. Both are always rendered, so reachability is certain. The impact is conformance and polish, with no change to what the controls do. The tab strip mirrors a deliberate design (mica-direction.md:95-97: arrows move between tabs, Delete closes), and aria-pressed segmented buttons are a common, accepted pattern, so the ladder half is closer to a preference than a violation.
- **Correction:** 'The tab count and position it reports are wrong' is unproven and probably false: Chromium counts role=tab siblings only, ignoring the generic wrappers. The real problems are the non-tab children in the tablist and the extra Tab stops. Treat the ladder item as optional (radiogroup is a refinement, not a fault). Priority P3.

<a id="uik-14"></a>

### UIK-14 — The Studio Data grid takes one Tab stop per cell, so leaving it by keyboard costs rows × columns presses

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:657`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:711`
- **What:** The grid options set no tabToNextCell, so AG Grid's default applies: Tab moves cell by cell through every row (ensureDomOrder, suppressColumnVirtualisation) before focus leaves the grid. The arrow keys already move between cells.
- **Failure:** On a page of 100 records with 9 columns, a keyboard user who wants the controls after the grid, such as the status line's theme buttons, has to press Tab about 900 times, or go round through the document start with Shift+Tab.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p02 tab walk on Data (2 records) -> Tab stops 33–50 are the 18 grid cells ("div.ag-cell-value.ag-cell… \| A quieter weekly review \| …" through "… \| 1 \| 1350,363,90,40") before the theme buttons.
- **Fix and guard:** Set `tabToNextCell: () => false` (or return null) so that Tab leaves the grid and the arrow keys move between cells, as the grid pattern expects. Guard: a journey that focuses the first cell, presses Tab once and expects focus outside .ag-root-wrapper.
- **Verifier:** view-data.ts:656-716 builds the GridOptions with no tabToNextCell, and AG Grid 36.1.0's default (node_modules/ag-grid-community/dist/package/main.cjs.js:32984-33100, onTabKeyDown/findNextCellToFocusOn) moves Tab cell to cell and row to row, only handing focus to the browser when there is no next cell. The reviewer's recorded p02 tab walk (tabwalk-data-light.json) shows 9 header cells and then every body cell as separate Tab stops before the status-line theme buttons. No contract or ADR mandates this: docs/contracts/studio.md section 5 only asks for keyboard navigation/edit/commit, and there is no F6 or skip mechanism in shortcuts.ts. It is the library default rather than a coding slip and there is a workaround (Shift+Tab from the start, arrows inside the grid), so P3 accessibility friction.
- **Correction:** The proposed fix `tabToNextCell: () => false` would regress data entry: in AG Grid, returning false while editing (main.cjs.js:33056-33062, editSvc.moveToNextCell at :44230-44245) stops editing and drops Tab-to-next-editable-cell. It must be conditional, e.g. `params => params.editing ? params.nextCellPosition : false`, and the guard must also cover Tab inside an editor. Header cells also count as Tab stops (9 more), and ensureDomOrder/suppressColumnVirtualisation are not what creates the stops (the numbering '33-50' is 0-based in the probe output).

<a id="uik-15"></a>

### UIK-15 — The Agent page restores focus on 'Open conversation' to the copy in the hidden Activity panel, dropping focus

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-agent-keyboard`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:162`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:226`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-launch-model.ts:142`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:335`
- **What:** focusedControl maps any focused [data-open-agent-chat] to the selector '[data-open-agent-chat]'. While an agent runs, there are two such buttons, one in the Activity panel's presence aside and one on the Launch tile. querySelector returns the Activity one, which is hidden when Launch is the selected tab, so focus() fails.
- **Failure:** On Launch with an agent running, a keyboard user is on the tile's 'Open conversation' when any redraw happens, such as the copy line expiring 8 s after a Copy or a hide/show. Focus goes to <body>.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p24 -> "Open conversation buttons: agent-panel-activity (hidden), agent-panel-launch"; "focus before: button.secondary-button Open conversation"; "focus after the copy line went: body".
- **Fix and guard:** Scope the restore selector to the visible panel (`.agent-panel:not([hidden]) [data-open-agent-chat]`), or give each button a distinct key. Guard: the p24 sequence as a journey step, expecting focus on the Launch tile's button.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. view-agent.ts:162 maps any focused [data-open-agent-chat] to the bare selector, and the redraw restores with content.querySelector(refocus)?.focus() (view-agent.ts:335). While an agent runs, the Activity panel's presence aside (view-agent.ts:226) and the Launch tile (agent-launch-model.ts:142/154) each render that button; the Activity panel comes first in DOM order (view-agent.ts:~257-258) and `.agent-panel[hidden]{display:none}` (11-agent-access.css:197), so with Launch selected querySelector returns the hidden copy, focus() is a no-op, and focus stays on body after innerHTML replaced the old node. The redraw trigger exists: the copy line's 8 s timer calls rerender() (view-agent.ts:86-91). The reviewer's p24 probe ran this sequence and recorded body as the focus after.
- **Correction:** The trigger is narrower than 'any redraw': the 3 s status poll skips redrawing while focus is inside .agent-launch (main.ts:772), so with focus on the Launch tile the real trigger is the copy-feedback expiry (a Copy click, then Tab to Open conversation, then 8 s) or another action's rerender, not the poll. 'hide/show' does not apply since focus would be on the Hide/Show button, which has its own key. Fix as proposed (scope to .agent-panel:not([hidden])) is sound, or iterate querySelectorAll and focus the first visible match.

### UIS-12 — Form controls are named without their field: every optional field's checkbox is 'Not set' and every reference button is 'Choose record'

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:432`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/reference-controls.ts:13`
- **What:** textControl wraps the null toggle in <label class="checkbox-field">…Not set</label> with no reference to the field (record-markup.ts:432). referenceControl renders <button class="reference-choose">Choose record</button> and labels the field with a plain span, not a label (reference-controls.ts:9-13).
- **Failure:** On the Decision form a screen reader hears 'Not set, checkbox' twice, for Context and for Owner, with nothing to tell them apart. A record page with two references has two identical 'Choose record' buttons.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p28-names.mjs (Chromium AX tree) -> Not set checkboxes: [{role:'checkbox', name:'Not set'}]; Choose record buttons: [{role:'button', name:'Choose record'}].
- **Fix and guard:** Add aria-label="<Field> not set" to the checkbox, and aria-label="Choose <Field>" or aria-describedby pointing at the field label on the reference buttons. Guard: an SSR-bundle test on fieldControlMarkup and referenceControl asserting that the field name appears in the accessible name.
- **Verifier:** record-markup.ts textControl (~line 432) emits <div class=scalar-field>...<label class=checkbox-field><input type=checkbox name=__unset:... data-null-field>Not set</label></div>, so every optional text field's null toggle has the accessible name 'Not set' with no field name, no aria-label and no aria-describedby, and the wrapper div has no group role. referenceControl (reference-controls.ts:7-13) labels the field with <span class=field-label>, not a <label>, and its buttons are the literal text 'Choose record' and 'Clear', again with no field name; only the hidden picker section carries aria-label 'Choose <Field>' (reference-controls.ts:15). So two optional text fields or two references on one form give identical control names. No ADR or contract requires this wording. It is an accessibility polish gap (WCAG 2.4.6, 3.3.2), not a functional break.

### UIS-13 — Type-tile letters are below 4.5:1 in Light in the rail, the tab and the address field, although the stylesheet says they read in both themes

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:562`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:570`
- **What:** .type-tile draws its 10px/700 letters in the tone itself, on color-mix(tone 16%, transparent) (21-native.css:562-576). The comment says the tone 'colours the letters, so it reads in both themes'. On the selected rail row and the active tab the tinted tile sits on a further tint, which lowers the contrast again.
- **Failure:** In Light, 'De' (orange) on the selected rail row measures 2.8:1, and the amber tile in the rail measures 2.71:1. All eight tones fail in the rail (2.71 to 3.74:1), in the tab (3.22 to 4.45:1), and in the address field for six tones (3.37 to 4.33:1).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p27-chips.mjs -> light tiles {address:{red:4, orange:3.49, amber:3.37, green:3.56, teal:3.72, blue:4.33, violet:4.66, grey:4.07}, rail-selected:{red:3.21, orange:2.8, amber:2.71, green:2.87, teal:3, blue:3.48, violet:3.74, grey:3.28}, tab-active:{… amber:3.22 … violet:4.45}}.
- **Fix and guard:** Darken the letters in Light, for example color-mix(in srgb, var(--tile) 70%, var(--ink)), or tint the tile less. Guard: a node or gate check of every tone on the three hosts asserting at least 4.5:1.
- **Verifier:** 21-native.css:562-576 draws the tile letters in var(--tile) on color-mix(tile 16%, transparent), and 02-tokens.css:35-42 gives the Light tones. I recomputed WCAG contrast with a script: on white the address-field figures match the reviewer exactly (red 4.00, orange 3.49, amber 3.37, green 3.56, teal 3.72, blue 4.33, violet 4.66, grey 4.07), and on the mica ground they are lower still (amber 3.01). typeGlyph is used in the rail (rail-places.ts:30), the tab (workspace-tabs.ts:58) and the address row (main.ts:312). So the numbers are real.
- **Correction:** Severity stays P3: the tile is aria-hidden (type-icons.ts:87) and only repeats the type name printed beside it, and docs/design/mica-direction.md:60-63 deliberately lists the 10px tile letters among the small labels. That makes it a decorative glyph, so 'fails WCAG AA' overstates it; the point holds only as 'weaker than the other text'. FIXES.md already carries this as UIS-13.

### UIS-15 — Alt+F does nothing visible when the rail is folded: it opens a File menu that is display:none and leaves focus on the body

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-shell-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:494`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:474`
- **What:** runShortcut('file') sets fileDetails.open = true and focuses its first enabled button (main.ts:494-498). It does not check whether the menu is shown. When folded, :root[data-rail="collapsed"] .brand .file-menu { display: none } (21-native.css:474).
- **Failure:** With the navigation folded (Ctrl+B), the documented Alt+F shortcut opens nothing and focus stays on BODY. The menu's open state is left true underneath, and nothing tells the person they must unfold the rail first.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p31-fold.mjs -> 'rail now: collapsed'; 'Alt+F folded -> {"el":"","w":1440,"h":900,"visible":true,"menuOpen":true,"menuDisplay":"none"}'.
- **Fix and guard:** When the File menu is not rendered (offsetParent === null), unfold the rail first or open the palette filtered to File, as other shortcuts check target.offsetParent. Guard: a gate step that folds the rail, presses Alt+F, and asserts the focused element is visible inside #file-actions.
- **Verifier:** main.ts:494-498 handles 'file' before the offsetParent guard at main.ts:499-501: it sets fileDetails.open = true and focuses the first enabled button in #file-actions. index.html:23 makes #file-menu the .file-menu element, and 21-native.css:474 hides it with display:none when the rail is collapsed (min-width 841px block). focus() on a button inside a display:none ancestor does nothing, so the key shows nothing and the open flag stays true. shortcuts.ts:38 and :90 confirm Alt+F is a documented shortcut.
- **Correction:** There is a second effect the finding does not name. While the hidden details is open, the Escape handler (main.ts:543-548) spends its next press closing the invisible menu, and the Alt+Left/Right handler (main.ts:533) returns early. Unfolding the rail later also shows the File menu already open. Ctrl+K still lists the File commands, so a workaround exists. P3 is right.

### UIT-14 — After 'Add view…' focus lands on a Title field below the visible area

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-packages.ts:200`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-packages.ts:212`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:405`
- **What:** Add view… calls redrawForm('add-view-title'), which calls focusWithoutInteraction, and that focuses with `{ preventScroll: true }`. The form is appended under the package's uses list, so the focused input is often outside the #studio-content scroller.
- **Failure:** At 800x700, keyboard Enter on 'Add view…': focus moves to #add-view-title at y 730–760, while the scroller ends at 672 behind the status line. A keyboard user types into a field they cannot see, and a mouse user sees nothing open apart from a sliver of 'What to add'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p10-focusvis.mjs (800x700 dark) -> {"active":"add-view-title","rect":[730.4,760.4],"scroller":"studio-content","scrollerRect":[96,672],"visibleInScroller":false}
- **Fix and guard:** When opening the form, scroll it into view (scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})) before focusing. Keep preventScroll only for redraws caused by a change inside the form. Guard: the same geometry assertion in the custom-views lane at 800x700.
- **Verifier:** view-packages.ts:206-213 sets draft and calls redrawForm('add-view-title'), which runs rerender() (shell.ts:77-90 only restores prior scrollTop values) and then focusWithoutInteraction (shell.ts:404-408), which focuses with preventScroll:true. The form is rendered in the package card body below packageUsesMarkup (view-packages.ts:33), and no scrollIntoView is called for it anywhere (only view-packages.ts:27 for the whole panel). So on a short viewport the focused Title input is outside the scroller. The reviewer's screenshot fv-addview-keyboard-800-dark.png shows only the top of 'What to add' above the status line at 800x700. Real, but window-height dependent and a scroll recovers it, so P3.
- **Correction:** Does not occur when the card sits high enough in the viewport (e.g. 1440x900 with a few uses); the same preventScroll applies to redraws from the kind/entity selects, which are correct to keep.

### WDV-17 — The reference picker drops keyboard focus on every page change

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/reference-controls.ts:49`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/reference-controls.ts:74`
- **What:** load() starts by disabling both Previous and Next. When Next was pressed from the keyboard, the focused button becomes disabled, Chromium's focus fixup moves focus to the body, and nothing restores it after the page arrives. The panel's Escape handler is on the panel, so Escape then no longer closes the picker either.
- **Failure:** A keyboard user presses Next in 'Choose record'. Focus jumps to the top of the document, so they must Tab all the way back into the picker for each page, and Escape no longer cancels it.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Mark the pager busy with aria-disabled rather than disabled while loading, or put focus back on the pressed button, or on the first result, when the page arrives. Guard: a gate step that pages the picker by keyboard and asserts document.activeElement stays inside the picker; falsify by restoring the disable.
- **Verifier:** reference-controls.ts:47-49 load() synchronously sets previous.disabled and next.disabled = true; :73-74 route the Previous/Next clicks through it; :60 re-enables them after the read but nothing restores focus (only hide() at :38 calls choose.focus()); the Escape handler is bound to the panel (:72), so with focus on body it no longer fires. I reproduced the platform behaviour in headless Edge (Chromium, as WebView2): probe verify/workbench-data-views-15/focus-probe.html focuses a button, disables it, and activeElement goes from 'next' to BODY and stays on BODY after it is re-enabled. Reachable whenever the target type has more than 25 records and the person pages by keyboard. Keyboard-focus loss, not data loss, hence P3.

### WST-13 — index.html names generic elements with aria-label, which assistive technology ignores, so 'Studio sections', 'File actions' and 'Session status' are never announced

**P3** · accessibility · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:44`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:25`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:18`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:126`
- **What:** <div class="studio-nav" aria-label="Studio sections">, <div id="file-actions" … aria-label="File actions"> and <div class="brand" aria-label="Nendo"> have no role. <footer id="session-status" aria-label="Session status"> sits inside <main>, so it has the generic role, not contentinfo. ARIA 1.2 prohibits naming the generic role, and screen readers drop the name. No script adds a role at runtime (file-actions.ts only fills #file-actions).
- **Failure:** A screen-reader user moving through the rail hears the six Studio buttons with no group name, and the status bar with no name. The labels the markup intends never reach them.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Give the containers a role that takes a name: role="group" for studio-nav and brand, role="group" or a menu pattern for #file-actions. Make the status footer a role="region" or move it out of <main>. Add a check to an existing markup test that every aria-label in index.html sits on an element with an explicit role or a naming-capable tag.
- **Verifier:** index.html:18 (div.brand), :25 (div#file-actions) and :44 (div.studio-nav) carry aria-label but no role, and :126 is a footer nested in main (opens :80, closes :156), which HTML-AAM maps to generic rather than contentinfo. ARIA 1.2 prohibits naming the generic role, and Chromium does not expose a name there. I grepped src/*.ts for runtime role assignment: only command-palette, main.ts:204 (#file-notice), shell.ts:111 and view-frames.ts:607 set roles, and file-actions.ts:200-225 only fills #file-actions with buttons, so nothing repairs these four. No ADR or contract mandates the markup and no test inspects it. The defect is real but small: every control inside is individually named, so only the group and region names are lost.
- **Correction:** All four cited index.html lines are accurate. Impact is cosmetic accessibility polish. The brand label is also redundant with its visible 'Nendo' text and the empty-alt image, and #file-actions sits inside a details disclosure whose summary is already named 'File'. The simplest fix for the status footer is to drop the label or make it role=region.

### ABS-14 — Capability Atlas map keys fire while typing: Alt+Shift+arrows in the editor move the capability, and F2 leaves a stray rename box

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1379`, `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1393`
- **What:** The document-level keydown handler checks only renaming, mode, selected and the modifiers. It never checks whether the event target is an input, textarea or select, or whether the #editor dialog is open. Keydown in the modal editor's fields bubbles to document. Alt+Shift+ArrowUp there runs moveCard (a records.move write), and F2 runs startRename. startRename appends a rename input behind the modal, which cannot take focus, so blur never fires. renaming stays set, which turns off F2 and the move keys until the person finds and leaves that box.
- **Failure:** A person editing a capability's definition presses Alt+Shift+Up, a Windows layout or IME habit. The capability moves among its siblings, as a write in History, while the dialog is still open.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Return early when event.target.closest('input, textarea, select, [contenteditable]') or $('editor').open. Guard: an Atlas gate step that types Alt+Shift+ArrowUp and F2 inside the editor's description field and asserts no records.move was sent and no .cap-rename exists.
- **Verifier:** extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1379-1397 is a document-level keydown handler that checks only renaming, mode, selected and the modifiers; it never looks at event.target or whether #editor is open. The editor is a modal dialog (:971 showModal) whose keydown events bubble to document. Alt+Shift+Arrow therefore reaches moveCard (a records.move, :1392) and F2 reaches startRename (:1395). The map's own handler at :1185 does guard with event.target !== map, which shows the guard was intended for the document one too. startRename appends the input to #drawing (:1337), which is inert behind the modal, so focus() does nothing, blur never fires and renaming stays set (:1385 then early-returns, disabling F2 and the move keys) until the box is found. The gestures are rare while typing, hence P3.

### ABS-16 — Capability Atlas drops out of Nendo's toolbar for the session once 'Change since' has more than 64 assessment dates

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1442`, `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1470`, `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1474`
- **What:** With colour 'change', declareToolbar adds a select whose options are every distinct assessment date (binding.assessmentDates()). Nendo refuses a select of more than 64 options, and a declaration past a bound is refused whole. The refusal calls leaveNativeChrome, which sets nativeChrome=false permanently and shows 'Nendo could not show the Atlas's controls...'. Assessments recorded on individual days reach 64 distinct dates quickly.
- **Failure:** A file has assessments on 70 different days. Choosing Colour: Change since replaces Nendo's toolbar with the Atlas's own for the rest of the visit, with a technical message.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Offer at most 64 dates, the most recent or one per month or quarter, or use a search or date field. Do not leave native chrome over an optional control: declare again without it. Guard: a fixture with 70 assessment dates that asserts the declaration is accepted (at most 64 options).
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:1442-1443 declares a select holding every date from binding.assessmentDates() when colour === 'change'. model.js:176-188,202 makes that the Set of all distinct assessment dates. The host caps a select at 64 (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/protocol.ts:57 selectOptions: 64), and view-toolbar-model.ts:75-77 list() throws invalid-params when longer, refusing the whole declaration. view.js:1470 catches it and calls leaveNativeChrome (:1474-1481), which sets nativeChrome = false for good and shows the technical message. Reachable with real data: tools/bcm-atlas/assessments.mjs:37 migrated() dates each assessment by the capability's own cap.reviewed, so a file whose capabilities carry per-capability review dates easily has more than 64 distinct dates. The Northstar fixture has two dates, which is why the gate does not see it. Impact is limited because the Atlas has its own toolbar as the designed fallback.
- **Correction:** The trigger is more likely via migrated per-capability 'Last reviewed' dates than via assessments recorded day by day.

The Archi workbench slices its labels to 80 and its options to 63 for this reason (view.js:1938-1939).

The host rebuilds it in src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-toolbar-model.ts:87-91 (label longer than extensionLimits.labelCharacters=80 throws invalid-params) and :75-78/:191 (more than selectOptions=64 throws), and extension-broker.ts:681 propagates the rejection before anything is drawn. toolbar() ends in .catch(problem) (view.mjs:25) and Swarm's index.html has no Play, Reset or Save buttons of its own, so the claim holds. sw.species.name has no length bound in tools/swarm/definition.mjs:7, so an 81-character name typed in Studio reaches it. ### ABS-21 — Swarm lists saved experiments in random order: newest-first by reversing record-ID order does not work with generated IDs

- **What:** saveExperiment calls records.create without a recordId, so the broker makes `record-<uuid>` (extension-broker.ts:511). queryAll returns records in record-ID order. renderExperiments shows [...records.experiments].reverse(), which is random rather than newest first.
- **Failure:** A person saves a run and finds it somewhere in the middle of the list rather than at the top.
- **Reproduction:** Source

### ABS-22 — Archi restores edits kept in the browser into whichever view the person edits next, not the view they were made on

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm`

- **Where:** `extensions/archi/view.js:1003`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1731`, `extensions/archi/view.js:974`
- **What:** keepEdits stores { viewId, writes }. applyPlace uses viewId to reopen the editor only on that view. renderEditor applies readEdits().writes whatever view is being opened and says '<n> edits were waiting to be committed, and are here again.' keepEdits then overwrites viewId with the current view.
- **Failure:** A person closes Nendo with 5 waiting edits on view A. The next day, with no place to restore, they open view B and press Edit. The editor says 5 edits are 'here again', but none show on B. Leaving Edit is refused until they commit or discard edits they cannot see.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** When the kept viewId differs from the view being edited, open the kept view first, or name it in the status ('5 edits wait on <view A>'). Guard: a view.test.mjs case with kept edits for view A that opens view B and asserts the editor shows A or names it.
- **Verifier:** Traced in extensions/archi/view.js. keepEdits (:971-976) stores viewId of the current editor; readEdits (:964-969) returns the writes whatever view is open. applyPlace (:1731) turns editing on only when readEdits().viewId equals the restored view. The docs say kept places are this session's and forgotten with the file (docs/contracts/custom-views.md:957-961), so after reopening the file there is no place and the tree opens with nothing in the editor. Opening another view B and pressing Edit reaches renderEditor (:998-1024): it applies saved writes to the mirror and says '<n> edits were waiting ... and are here again', pending becomes n via editsChanged, and keepEdits then overwrites viewId with B. toggleEditing(false) (:1051-1055) refuses until commit or discard. The writes belong to view A's items, so nothing shows on B. Reachable; Discard and Commit are both available, so the harm is confusion, not loss.
- **Correction:** Slight overstatement: the editor holds one file-wide edit set by design, so edits made on view A also stay invisible on B in a single session when the person selects B while editing; that is documented behaviour, and the only real gap is the missing hint of which view the edits are on after a reopen. Commit would write view A's changes while B is shown, which the finding does not mention.

### CSS-02 — The recovery layout keeps two columns at every width, so the File status findings squeeze to a 19px column in a narrow window

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/14-refinements-controls.css:49`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/01-file-menu.css:79`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/12-agent-activity.css:330`
- **What:** 01-file-menu.css:79 makes `.recovery-layout` a single column at `max-width: 900px`. 14-refinements-controls.css:49-52 restates `.recovery-layout { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 0.95fr) minmax(320px, 1fr) }` later in the cascade, outside any media query, with the same specificity. So the narrow-window rule and the compact rule at 12:330 never apply. The actions column always keeps 320px, and the findings column gets whatever is left. The recovery path must stay reachable (AGENTS.md architecture invariants), and this is the Health page a damaged file opens on (view-health.ts:66).
- **Failure:** A file fails its integrity check, and the person reads Health in a narrow window. At 546px wide the findings column is 129px. At 400px it is 19px wide and 2041px tall, so the explanation of what went wrong is unreadable beside the 320px action column.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-layout.cjs -> recoveryCols "129.188px 320px" at 546x574, "209px 320px" at 600x800, and "19px 320px" at 400x700, where findings measured [18,569,46,2041].
- **Fix and guard:** Move the 14:49-52 grid-template-columns into an `@media (min-width: 901px)` block, or restate the single column in a media query after it. Delete the dead 12:330 rule. Guard: a browser-lane assertion that `.recovery-layout` has exactly one column track at a 700px and a 400px viewport.
- **Verifier:** 14-refinements-controls.css:49-52 restates .recovery-layout grid-template-columns (minmax(0,.95fr) minmax(320px,1fr)) outside any media query, same specificity and later in the import order than 01-file-menu.css:79 (<=900px single column) and 12-agent-activity.css:330 (compact two equal columns), so both never win. view-health.ts:66-74 emits this layout on the Health page. I re-ran headless Edge over the concatenated slices: findings text column is 225px at 683x720, 77px at 512x360, 146px at 585x411 while the actions column stays 320px. Real cascade bug, but it only bites below roughly 700 CSS px; the host minimum window is 1024x720 physical (DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:10-11), so it needs 175-200% scaling at minimum width or a deliberately narrow window. The text stays reachable by wrapping/scrolling, so this is polish rather than a P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The 19px/400px case is below the host minimum at every common scale (needs about 250%). Realistic reach: 585px wide (175%) gives a 146px text column, 512px (200%) gives 77px; at 683px (150%) it is about 225-239px and readable.

### CSS-19 — Below about 550px the top-bar navigation scrolls sideways with its scrollbar hidden, so Agent and Help are off-screen with no cue

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:513`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:529`
- **What:** In the narrow layout, `.rail` is a row with `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none`, and `.rail-foot { margin-left: auto }` pushes Agent and Help to the far end. Once the row is wider than the window, the end of the bar is out of view and nothing on screen shows it scrolls. A vertical mouse wheel doesn't scroll it.
- **Failure:** At the supported 320-500px widths (body min-width 320px, 03-base.css:12), the bar is 550px wide. Health is partly visible, and Agent and Help are hidden to the right. A mouse user can't reach them without Shift+wheel.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-layout.cjs -> at 400x700 'rail [0,0,400,48] railOverflowX "auto" railScrollW 550'.
- **Fix and guard:** Show a thin scrollbar or fade edges, or move Studio's pages into an overflow menu below a width threshold. Guard: assert #nav-agent and #nav-help intersect the viewport at 400px.
- **Verifier:** Traced and reproduced. 21-native.css:499-531 (max-width 840px) makes `.rail` a 48px row with `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none` (:513-514), and `.rail-foot { margin-left: auto }` (:529) pushes Agent and Help to the end. I ran a probe from the verify folder against the reviewer's page with the real stylesheet. Without the host attributes the rail's scrollWidth is 550. At 500x700 #nav-agent spans 468..504 and #nav-help 506..542, so Help is wholly outside the 500px viewport and Agent partly. At 400x700 both are off-screen. Nothing shows the bar scrolls: no scrollbar, no fade. A vertical wheel does not scroll an overflow-x container that has no vertical overflow, so Shift+wheel, a horizontal gesture or Tab focus is needed. Workarounds exist and stay reachable at those widths, which is why it is not P2: Ctrl 7 for Agent, F1 for Help, Ctrl K, and widening the window. Narrow widths happen at 175% or higher scaling with a window near the 1024px minimum, or a snapped half-screen on a laptop, and are not the normal case. Polish-level discoverability friction, P3.
- **Correction:** The Desktop host makes the narrow-window case worse than stated. With data-title-bar=window and --title-bar-right 138px (set by hand in my probe; 20-title-bar.css:27-30 adds `padding-right: calc(14px + var(--title-bar-right))` when height is over 600px), the rail's scrollWidth is 694 and the overflow starts below about 694 CSS px, not 550. At 585px wide, Agent (468..504) and Help (506..542) at scroll 0 sit under the Windows caption buttons, which cover roughly 447..585. 'Supported 320-500px widths' is mostly hypothetical: the 1024px physical minimum is 512 CSS px only at 200% scaling (410 at 250%). The 03-base.css min-width is at line 10, not 12. The :513 citation is right; the :529 citation is the `.rail-foot { margin-left: auto }` line.

### DAE-10 — Sign-in can be started twice: the buttons stay live and the host sends a second authenticate and a second session/new

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:226`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:216`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:334`
- **What:** AuthenticateAsync checks only that the state is signIn and sets a notice; it never marks a sign-in as running, so each call sends authenticate and then OpenSessionAsync, which overwrites _sessionId and the options. The tab keeps the sign-in buttons enabled while the state stays signIn, and OnNotification ignores the sessionId of updates, so both sessions write into one transcript.
- **Failure:** The browser takes a few seconds to open, the person clicks Sign in again (or picks the other method): the agent runs two sign-in flows and opens two sessions, each connecting to the file's MCP address, and the conversation follows whichever answered last.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: conversation-probe2.ps1 step 3 -> "sign-in conversation state: signIn" and "requests the agent received after two presses: authenticate, authenticate".
- **Fix and guard:** Keep a signing-in flag under the lock, refuse a second AuthenticateAsync while one runs (agent-signing-in), clear it when it ends; disable the buttons while the notice says it is waiting; drop updates whose sessionId is not the current one. Guard: DesktopLaunchedAgentTests calls authenticate twice and asserts the fake agent saw one authenticate; falsify by removing the flag.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. AgentConversation.AuthenticateAsync (AgentConversation.cs:226-239) and the controller guard (DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:216) only test that the state is still signIn; the state stays signIn until OpenSessionAsync sets ready (line 201), so a second call passes and SignInAsync (241-264) sends another authenticate and another session/new that overwrites _sessionId. The Workbench keeps the buttons live while chat.state is signIn (view-agent-chat.ts:445-449) and its act() has no in-flight guard (381-395). OnNotification (479-515) never reads sessionId, so both sessions would write into one transcript. The docs and tests (DesktopLaunchedAgentTests.cs:420-429) cover a single press only. Real double-submit, but it needs a second click during the sign-in wait and agents may tolerate it, so P3.

### DAE-12 — PATH and the environment are this process's snapshot from when Nendo started, so a newly installed agent stays 'not installed' and agents miss new variables

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopAgentCatalog.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentProcess.cs:19`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-launch-model.ts:135`
- **What:** DesktopAgentCatalog.List reads Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH") from Nendo's own process, and AgentProcess.Start inherits the process environment unchanged. Nendo keeps running in the tray across windows, so this is the environment Explorer gave it at start. The Launch tile tells the person to run the install command in a terminal "then open this page again".
- **Failure:** The person installs Node.js (which adds C:\Program Files\nodejs and %APPDATA%\npm to PATH) and runs npm install -g @github/copilot as told; on returning, the tile still says not installed, and stays so until Nendo is quit from the tray. An API key set afterwards in Windows' environment settings (GEMINI_API_KEY, for example) never reaches the launched agent, which then asks to sign in.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Build the PATH (and the agent's environment block) from the current user and machine environment in the registry (HKCU\Environment and HKLM\...\Session Manager\Environment, expanding REG_EXPAND_SZ), as Explorer does, each time the catalogue is listed and an agent starts. Guard: a catalogue test with an injected environment reader that adds a folder after construction must find the program on the next list; falsify by reading the process variable.
- **Verifier:** DesktopAgentCatalog.List and Custom read Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PATH") from Nendo's own process (DesktopAgentCatalog.cs:97, 141), and AgentProcess.Start (AgentProcess.cs:67-95) sets no environment, so the agent inherits that process block. A Windows process environment is a snapshot from process start, and a repository grep finds nothing that refreshes it (no WM_SETTINGCHANGE handling, no registry environment read). architecture.md:441-455 says the process stays resident in the tray by default after the window closes, so the snapshot can be old. The tile text says to install and "then open this page again" (agent-launch-model.ts:135). Reachable only when a new PATH folder or variable appears after Nendo started, for example Node.js installed or an API key set in that time. The usual case, with %APPDATA%\npm already on PATH, works because the shim is looked up on every list. A restart from the tray is the workaround, so P3.
- **Correction:** The Node.js-first-install and newly-set-variable scenarios are the only ones affected. An agent installed into a PATH folder that was already present is found on the next list.

### DAE-14 — When Nendo itself closes the connection, the notice blames the agent and drops the reason

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopLaunchedAgent.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AcpConnection.cs:132`
- **What:** WatchAsync, woken by _conversation.Closed, waits two seconds and then writes "<agent> stopped (exit code N)." or "<agent> stopped answering." with the stderr tail; it never reads _conversation.Closed.Result. AcpConnection sets that reason to "The agent sent a message larger than Nendo accepts." when it ends the connection over a line past 8 MiB, after which EndAsync kills the program.
- **Failure:** An agent returns one very large tool result in a single message. Nendo closes the connection and ends the program, and the tab says the agent "stopped answering", so the person blames the agent and relaunches into the same failure instead of learning that Nendo refused the message size.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: conversation-probe2.ps1 step 2 -> "after an oversize line: state=ready; Closed says: The agent sent a message larger than Nendo accepts." (the reason exists; the WatchAsync notice that discards it is from source).
- **Fix and guard:** When Closed completes first and the program is still running, use Closed.Result in the notice (and end the conversation with it). Guard: a DesktopLaunchedAgentTests case with the fake agent printing a line over MaximumLineBytes asserts the notice names the size; falsify by restoring the generic sentence.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. AcpConnection.ReadLoopAsync sets reason "The agent sent a message larger than Nendo accepts." and returns (AcpConnection.cs:132-143), completing Closed with it (158) and faulting pending requests with AcpConnectionClosedException. Nothing carries it to the person after the handshake: RunTurnAsync swallows that exception without a notice (AgentConversation.cs:328), and only StartAsync uses exception.Message (169-172). DesktopLaunchedAgent.WatchAsync (DesktopLaunchedAgent.cs:88-104) wakes on Closed, waits 2 s for the process to exit, never reads Closed.Result, and writes "<agent> stopped (exit code N)." or "<agent> stopped answering." plus the stderr tail, then ends the program through EndAsync. The program is still running in this case, so the notice reads "stopped answering" and the Nendo-side size limit is lost. No test mentions the limit. The trigger is a single message over 8 MiB, which is rare, and the effect is a misleading sentence, so P3.

### DSH-06 — Opening another file closes the current one before assessing the new one, so Cancel or a refusal leaves no file open and discards pending agent proposals; picking the already-open file closes and reopens it

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:160`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:181`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:207`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:221`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:696`
- **What:** OpenNativeFileAsync / OpenRecentNativeFileAsync ask 'Open another file? ... pending proposals are discarded', call _session.CloseAsync() (CloseAgentFileSessionCoreAsync ends the launched agent, stops agent access, closes the proposal store), and only then AssessOpenAsync, because EnsureAvailableForOpen refuses an assessment while a file is open. OpenNativeAssessmentAsync then shows a second dialog whose Cancel (line 207) or 'Choose another file' (line 221) returns with nothing opened; an assessment that throws (unreadable file) also leaves nothing open. There is no check that the chosen path is _session.CurrentFilePath (DesktopWindowHandoff.OwnerOf ignores this process).
- **Failure:** With an agent's proposals waiting, the person drops or picks another .nendo, clicks Continue, then sees it is in a synced folder and clicks 'Choose another file' (or Cancel on 'Open / Open read-only'): the window now has no file, the agent was ended and its proposals discarded, and nothing was opened. Dropping the file that is already open runs the same close-and-reopen and discards the proposals for no change.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Let PrepareOpenCoreAsync/AssessOpenAsync run while a file is open (it touches only the candidate), show the assessment and location dialogs first, and close the current file only after the final choice; return early when the path equals CurrentFilePath. Guard: a controller test that AssessOpenAsync succeeds with a file open and that the current file is still open after a cancelled assessment.
- **Verifier:** Traced. MainPage.FileActions.cs:160-173 and :181-191: with a file open, the 'Open another file?' confirm is followed by _session.CloseAsync() and only then AssessOpenAsync, because AssessOpenAsync/OpenAssessedAsync call EnsureAvailableForOpen (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:81, DesktopSessionController.cs:696-705), which throws file-already-open while _coordinator is set. OpenNativeAssessmentAsync (:195-236) returns with nothing open on Cancel (:207) or 'Choose another file' (:221), and an assessment that throws leaves nothing open. DesktopWindowHandoff.OwnerOf (DesktopWindowHandoff.cs:80) returns null for this process's own sidecar, so choosing the file already open here runs the same close and reopen. Not mandated by an ADR or contract. It is a UX dead end rather than data loss: the first dialog states the current file will close, agent access stops and pending proposals are discarded, so the discard is disclosed and consented to, and Open file remains available.
- **Correction:** The loss of proposals is disclosed by the first dialog, so the defect is the dead end after the later cancel or refusal and the pointless close and reopen of the already-open file. P3 (minor UX with a trivial workaround), not P2.

### DSH-15 — Browser accelerator keys stay enabled on the Workbench document: F5/Ctrl+R reload it and drop unsaved typing, Ctrl+P/Ctrl+F open browser UI

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:191`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/draft-guard.ts:25`
- **What:** StartWorkbenchAsync sets AreHostObjectsAllowed, IsStatusBarEnabled, IsWebMessageEnabled and IsZoomControlEnabled but leaves AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled at true and adds no AcceleratorKeyPressed filter. The Workbench keeps an open record form's edits only in the DOM (draft-guard.ts: 'the draft lives in the DOM it replaces') and has no reload guard.
- **Failure:** A person presses F5 expecting a data refresh while editing a record: the WebView reloads app.nendo.local, the edited fields are gone without a prompt, and Ctrl+P opens Chromium's print preview of the app chrome.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Handle CoreWebView2Controller AcceleratorKeyPressed (or set AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled=false when the focused frame is the Workbench) to swallow reload, print, find, history and devtools shortcuts for the Workbench document while leaving views alone. Guard: a journey that sends F5 and asserts the document's start timestamp is unchanged.
- **Verifier:** MainPage.xaml.cs:192-195 sets four CoreWebView2 settings and leaves AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled at its default of true. A grep of src/ finds no AcceleratorKeyPressed handler, and Workbench src has no F5, Ctrl+R or beforeunload handling. The open record form's edits live only in state.openDraft in the DOM (draft-guard.ts:4-27), so a main-frame reload drops them without a prompt. WebView2 documents F5/Ctrl+R reload, Ctrl+P print and Ctrl+F find as accelerators controlled by that setting. The contract's 'browser is open' text (docs/contracts/custom-views.md:480-493, ADR-0013:345) covers custom views and their DevTools, and ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:29-31 only enables menus and DevTools; no accepted ADR mandates reload for the Workbench document.
- **Correction:** Setting AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled=false would also remove F12, Ctrl+Shift+I and the other shortcuts, so a custom-view author would lose the DevTools shortcut. Right-click Inspect, which the docs name, remains. The fix needs an AcceleratorKeyPressed filter rather than the blanket flag.

<a id="dsh-20"></a>

### DSH-20 — History fold always fails for a file in a synced folder the person accepted, because the backup path beside it is a new, unacknowledged path

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileReplacement.cs:31`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileReplacement.cs:41`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopLocationPolicy.cs:86`
- **What:** FoldHistoryAsync passes RequireWritableLocation(path) for the acknowledged open file, then PrepareBackupAsync(destination) calls RequireWritableLocation(destination) for '<name> before folding <stamp>.nendo' in the same folder. HasLocationAcknowledgement matches only _currentPath or paths in the request scope, and the Workbench's history.fold has no way to acknowledge a destination.
- **Failure:** A file in OneDrive opened with 'Continue anyway': History > Fold answers with the unsupported-sync-location message ('Choose another location or inspect read-only') and nothing the person can choose makes the fold run.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Treat the fold's own backup beside an acknowledged file as covered (add destination to the scope's AcknowledgedLocations when path was acknowledged), or let the fold return a location question the Workbench can confirm. Guard: controller test with a policy root covering the folder and an acknowledged current path asserting FoldHistoryAsync reaches the Engine.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. A writable open in a synced folder sets _currentWritableLocationAcknowledged (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:228). FoldHistoryAsync passes RequireWritableLocation(path) (DesktopFileReplacement.cs:31) but only adds that one path to the request scope, then builds the backup in the same folder (:35-40) and calls PrepareBackupAsync(destination), whose lambda runs RequireWritableLocation(destination) (:15). Inspect(destination) matches the same sync root (DesktopLocationPolicy.cs:36-42), and HasLocationAcknowledgement (:86-88) is true only for _currentPath or paths in the scope's AcknowledgedLocations, so it throws unsupported-sync-location. The Workbench's history.fold sends {} (actions.ts:423, WorkbenchProtocol.cs:425), so no destination acknowledgement can be supplied; no Desktop test covers FoldHistoryAsync. DesktopLocationTests.cs:42-46 makes 'accepted source location is not a blanket grant for other outputs' deliberate, but that policy does not mandate a dead end: the other flows (backup, copy, export) all go through a native destination prompt that calls AcknowledgeDestinationLocationAsync, and the fold has none. Workaround exists (move the file out of the synced folder), and synced writable use is unsupported anyway (architecture.md:228), hence P3.
- **Correction:** Add that the 'no blanket grant' rule (DesktopLocationTests.cs:42-46) is deliberate, so the fix should be either to add the host-chosen backup path to the scope when the file's own location was acknowledged, or to let fold return a location question the Workbench can confirm; not to loosen RequireWritableLocation generally.

### EBH-05 — Refusals of generated writes are not attributed to the action, step and field outside SetField formula evaluation

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:218`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:239`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:277`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:298`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:352`, `docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md:376`
- **What:** Only EvaluateAssignmentAsync inside a SetField step is wrapped (lines 218-231) to rename the failure 'The automatic action ... could not write ... (step ...)'. ExecuteAsync's dispatch refusals (NendoValidationException / NendoPreconditionException: storage-kind mismatch, required field, choice, reference target, delete blocked by references, record-id-reserved), CreateRecord assignment evaluation (line 277, no try), and SpendChange's limit refusal all propagate unchanged. The contract says 'The refusal names the action, the step and the field that it could not write, and states that nothing changed.'
- **Failure:** A person creates a project; a kickoff CreateRecord step misses a required field, so the save is refused with 'Required field taskTitle needs a value.', naming a field that is not on the project form and no rule. An agent gets NENDO_VALIDATION about a field it never sent. A DeleteRecord step blocked by references reports a reference refusal about a record the person did not delete.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Wrap each step's evaluation, budget charge and dispatch in one catch over NendoException that rethrows the same code and exception kind with 'The automatic action <name> could not <create/set/delete> <field> (step <id>): <message> The save was refused, so nothing changed.'. Guard: tests for a CreateRecord missing a required field and a storage-kind mismatch assert the message names the action and step.
- **Verifier:** Traced. Only EvaluateAssignmentAsync inside the SetField step is wrapped into 'The automatic action ... could not write ... (step ...)' (BehaviourPlanner.cs:217-231). The CreateRecord assignment evaluation (:274-278) has no try, and ExecuteAsync (:352-361) lets dispatch refusals (NendoValidationException/NendoPreconditionException such as required field, storage kind, choice, reference target, blocked delete) and SpendChange's limit refusal (BehaviourBudget.cs:87) propagate unchanged; nothing upstream rewraps them (SqliteNendoStore.cs has no catch around the chain, WorkbenchProtocol.cs:459 and the MCP error mappers pass the message through). The contract (calculations-and-actions.md:376-378) says the refusal names the action, the step and the field, so the text is incomplete for these paths and no test asserts the wording. Re-rated P3: every path still fails closed with a typed code and a message that normally names the offending field, nothing is corrupted, and most of these paths only arise from definitions that findings 3 and 4 would catch at install, so this is diagnostic-quality and contract drift rather than a material defect.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The refusals do name the field (for example 'Required field taskTitle needs a value.'); what is missing is the action, the step and the 'nothing changed' sentence. The proposed fix must rethrow the same exception type and code so the Workbench and MCP mappings (validation, precondition, calculation) keep working.

### EBH-15 — Formula refusals name neither the formula nor the position, although the parser reports the position

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/ExpressionAdapter.cs:124`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/ExpressionAdapter.cs:132`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:92`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/CompiledBehaviour.cs:141`
- **What:** Validate replaces every parser failure with 'This formula could not be read. Check its syntax.' and drops expression.Error, which carries NCalc's position. Analyzer and adapter messages ('x' is not one of the values this formula declares, Both outcomes of a choice must be the same kind) never include the FormulaId, although Compile passes one ("{action}:{step}:{field}", "{trigger}:condition").
- **Failure:** An action with six assignments, one missing a closing parenthesis, is refused with 'This formula could not be read. Check its syntax.' and nothing says which assignment or where.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe5.ps1 NCalc parse of `price * (qty + ` -> 'Parenthesis not closed. at position (1:13)', of `a.b` -> 'Invalid token in expression at position (1:2)'; adapter message (ExpressionAdapter.cs:133) is the fixed sentence.
- **Fix and guard:** Prefix validation refusals with the formula's owner (calculation ID, action/step/field, trigger condition) and append the parser's position text. Guard: a definition test asserting the refusal names the assignment and a position.
- **Verifier:** ExpressionAdapter.cs:124-133 turns every NCalc parse failure into the fixed sentence 'This formula could not be read. Check its syntax.' and drops expression.Error, although probe5.log shows NCalc reports e.g. 'Parenthesis not closed. at position (1:13)'. BehaviourAnalyzer.cs:92 and its other refusals, and CompiledBehaviour.cs:112-141, build the FormulaId ('{action}:{step}:{field}', '{trigger}:condition') but Validate/Analyze never put it in a message. Unclosed parentheses are not caught by BehaviourPreflight either, which only handles quotes and nesting. Neither ADR-0008 nor the contract mandates the fixed text; the contract's 'no expression internals' line (calculations-and-actions.md:942) concerns runtime outcome messages and a position is not an internal. No test pins the sentence. A real authoring friction with a small fix, so P3.
- **Correction:** The finding overstates 'names neither the formula': the failing operation is located by the proposal diagnostic (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs Locate sets OperationId; the MCP add_operations path prefixes 'Mutation N, operation M (behaviour.setDefinition id)'), so a calculation, function or trigger is identifiable. What is missing is the step/assignment inside a multi-assignment action and the position within the formula.

### EBH-16 — Binding, parameter and alias IDs may contain '-', '.' or start with a digit, yet a formula cannot name them without undocumented [brackets]

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourValidation.cs:19`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourDefinitions.cs:376`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/ExpressionAdapter.cs:141`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Behaviour/BehaviourVocabulary.cs:168`
- **What:** Binding aliases, parameters and call aliases go through RequireIdentifier, which allows hyphen, dot and a leading digit. The expression grammar reads unit-price as subtraction and a.b as a syntax error; only [unit-price] works, and neither the vocabulary nor the contract mentions bracket syntax.
- **Failure:** An author binds 'unit-price' and writes `quantity * unit-price`: refused with ''unit' is not one of the values this formula declares.'; a binding 'line.total' gives 'This formula could not be read.'
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe1.ps1 `unit-price` -> THROW NendoValidationException: 'unit' is not one of the values this formula declares.; `a.b` -> 'This formula could not be read. Check its syntax.'; `[unit-price]` -> Integer 3.
- **Fix and guard:** Restrict formula-visible names to [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* at shape validation, with a refusal that says so; or publish the [name] form in the vocabulary operators and in the refusal. Guard: shape-validation test.
- **Verifier:** BehaviourValidation.cs:19-35 RequireIdentifier allows letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', with no restriction on the first character. It is applied to binding aliases (BehaviourDefinitions.cs:376), expression parameters (ExpressionAdapter.cs:141) and call aliases. A formula reads each of these through NCalc's identifier grammar, so 'unit-price' is subtraction and 'a.b' a syntax error; probe1.log shows the refusals and that only '[unit-price]' evaluates. A grep of docs/contracts/calculations-and-actions.md, ADR-0008, the vocabulary and the skills finds no mention of bracket syntax, and the contract (line 100) only states the stable-ID alphabet. The refusal is loud, not silent, and the bracket form is a workaround, so P3.
- **Correction:** Add a worse variant: if bindings 'a', 'b' and 'a-b' all exist, 'a-b' in a formula compiles as a minus b with no refusal, so the author gets a different number than they meant. The fix should tighten the alias shape or publish the [name] form.
