### UX-04 — Successful actions are announced only to screen readers: saves, adds, deletes, commands, undo, accepting or rejecting a proposal and the fold's backup location leave nothing on screen

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics` (reported P2) · also reported as UIS-08

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:78`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:79`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:101`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:634`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:428`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-health.ts:169`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:555`
- **What:** shell.ts:553-561 records that announce() 'writes into a visually hidden region, so an outcome went to a screen reader and to nobody else', which is why showOutcome exists. runMutation still ends with announce(success) (actions.ts:78), so 'Record saved.', 'Record added.', '<Field> saved.', '<Command> completed.', 'Compensation added to history.' and 'Record deleted. Open History to review or restore it.' are never drawn. promoteProposal uses showOutcome only when a view landed (view-proposal.ts:79-82); rejectProposal and an agent proposal's Reject only announce (view-proposal.ts:101, view-agent.ts:634); foldHistory's 'The full history is in <backup>, beside the file.' is announced only (actions.ts:428); approving automatic actions and revoking edit access likewise (view-health.ts:169, view-agent.ts:555).
- **Failure:** Structure > Show as Markdown > Accept changes: the review closes and the person lands on Use with no sentence saying anything was accepted. After 'Back up and fold', the only place the backup's file name is ever written is the hidden live region, so a sighted person never learns where the full history went. After Delete record, the instruction to restore from History is never shown.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=1 -> after a record form Save: 'after save msg: none \| announce: Record saved.'; after accepting 'Show Notes as Markdown': 'VIEW2 message slot: hidden', 'VIEW2 announcement: Show Notes as Markdown accepted.'; after rejecting the agent proposal: 'visible msg: none \| announce: The proposal was rejected.'
- **Fix and guard:** Route the success string of runMutation, promoteProposal, rejectProposal, resolveAgentProposal(false), foldHistory, setBehaviourApproval and revokeAgentEditing through showOutcome (which also announces); give the delete outcome an action button that opens History on the entry (OutcomeNotice.action already exists). Guard: a host-behaviour test per path asserting .message-slot is visible with the outcome text after the action.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed: runMutation ends in announce(success) only (actions.ts:78), promoteProposal announces and calls showOutcome only when a view landed (view-proposal.ts:79-82), rejectProposal announces only (view-proposal.ts:101), the agent-proposal reject path falls to announce (view-agent.ts:634; the applied-accept branch at :633 does use showOutcome), foldHistory announces only (actions.ts:428), setBehaviourApproval and revokeAgentEditing announce only (view-health.ts:169, view-agent.ts:555). shell.ts:553-561 itself says announce() reaches only a screen reader, and showOutcome exists for that; record-form.ts:160-165 uses it for 'No changes to save.'. So the gap is a real, inconsistent application of the project's own rule. But in most paths the screen visibly changes (form re-renders, record leaves the list, Agent page shows 'None waiting', Accept lands on another page), nothing is lost, and no contract requires a visible toast. The sharpest instances are the fold's backup file name and the delete 'restore from History' hint, which are informational. Polish-level, so P3 rather than P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. Also the 'status line' has no saved indicator (the 'Saved locally' pill in index.html:139 is hidden while health is normal), so nothing else compensates, but the visible state change in each flow makes the omission low impact.

- **Fix and guard:** Swap the Value input for a control matched to the field: Yes/No select for Boolean, the option list (labels, sending IDs) for a choice, the reference picker (reference-controls.ts) for a reference; at minimum accept Yes/No in parseScalar for the filter and make the message name the accepted words. Guard: scalars/format test that parseScalar('Boolean','Yes') succeeds or that the message names what is accepted; a grids test that the Value control for a choice field is a select of labels.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. studioQueryMarkup draws a plain text Value input for every field kind (view-data.ts:460-462); wireStudioQuery sets the Boolean placeholder 'true or false' (:481) and on submit calls parseScalar(storageLabel(kind), value) (:489), which for Boolean accepts only 'true'/'false' and otherwise throws 'Choose Yes, No or Not set.' (scalars.ts:12-15, shown by showError at :492). So typing 'Yes' or 'No' as the message asks repeats the error. A single-choice field is a Text scalar compared with the stored option ID while cells show choiceDisplay (format.ts:41-45), and renaming a choice keeps its ID (help.ts:84), so filtering by the new label returns nothing; a Reference passes through parseScalar as a raw record ID. docs/contracts/studio.md:81 asks for 'field-aware sort and filter operations'. However this is Studio's admin/inspection filter where stored values are the documented model (studio.md:145: single choice is 'allowed stable option IDs'), the placeholder names the accepted Boolean words, and the Use surfaces have their own quick filter. Friction with an obvious workaround, so P3.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The choice-label mismatch only appears after a choice is renamed (option IDs equal the typed labels until then). The misleading error text for Boolean is the cleanest defect: either accept Yes/No in the filter path or change the message to name 'true' and 'false'.

So it is genuine inconsistency, not a deliberate trade-off.

Use list rows end in '<small>v${record.version}</small>' (surface-markup.ts:171,240,510), board/gallery cards in '<footer><small>v${record.version}</small></footer>' (record-markup.ts:86, styled visible in 09-surfaces.css:131-148), and the Use inspector ends 'Record version ${record.version}' (page-markup.ts:224). The version is the optimistic-concurrency counter, +1 per field written (SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:506; Help says each command step advances it by one), so a Use-screen 'v7' is not meaningful to a person. ### UX-24 — Reject on a proposal review is one click beside Accept, with no confirmation, and discards an agent's work for good

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `ux-heuristics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:361`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:370`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:31`
- **What:** Both review pages put Reject immediately left of Accept changes (view-agent.ts:361, view-proposal.ts:31) and wire it straight to proposal.reject (view-agent.ts:370 -> resolveAgentProposal(false); view-proposal.ts:38 -> rejectProposal). A rejected proposal cannot be reopened; the agent has to rebuild it. Accepting Unattended has a confirmation (confirmUnattended), rejecting has none, and the outcome is only announced (see the visibility finding).
- **Failure:** A person reviewing an agent's 100-operation proposal with new code clicks Reject instead of Accept: the Agent page returns with 'None waiting' and no message.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge on ?preview=1, Agent > Review changes > #reject-agent-proposal -> 'AFTER REJECT title: Agent access \| visible msg: none \| announce: The proposal was rejected. \| pending: ... None waiting'.
- **Fix and guard:** Ask 'Reject this proposal? The agent would have to prepare it again.' via confirmDialog for proposals not prepared by Studio's own one-click actions, and show the outcome with showOutcome. Guard: a host-behaviour test asserting a dialog opens on Reject and the proposal stays pending on Cancel.
- **Verifier:** view-agent.ts:361-371 and view-proposal.ts:29-38 wire #reject-agent-proposal and #reject-proposal straight to proposal.reject with no dialog, while the Unattended switch does use confirmUnattended (view-agent.ts:433,453). Engine side, NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:40-65 RejectProposalAsync sets state Rejected, persists, then ProposalWorkspace.Delete(context) and _proposals.Remove(proposalId), so a rejected proposal is gone and an agent has to prepare it again. No ADR or contract mandates an unconfirmed reject (ADR-0025:71 is about a read-only card, not this page). The cost of a mis-click is only the agent's rework; the active file is untouched ('Your active file is unchanged until you accept', view-agent.ts:354), hence P3.
- **Correction:** The 'no message' part of the scenario is a separate announce-only issue: resolveAgentProposal ends with announce(outcomeMessage) for a reject (view-agent.ts:633), not showOutcome. Any confirmation should skip Studio's own one-click proposals, and the gate journeys tools/Journey-Drag.mjs:109, Journey-Pilot.mjs:109, Review-NeutralityRuntime.mjs:132/308/344 and Review-OutcomeRuntime.mjs:185 click the Reject buttons directly and would need to accept the dialog.

### WAU-03 — A thing that cannot be pointed at (a ninth item, or no room left) is refused only to screen readers, while its @name is still written into the message (ACP-10 fix incomplete)

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-mention.ts:210`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-mention.ts:216`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-mention.ts:228`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:588`
- **What:** choose() writes '@{label} ' into the textarea and dispatches input (agent-mention.ts:210-214) before it checks the limit or the budget. Two refusals follow: 'A message points at 8 things at most.' (216), and withAttachment's 'X does not fit ... Stop pointing at Y, which says the most, to make room.' (227-228). Both go only to announce(), which writes into #announcement, a visually hidden live region (index.html:181, shell.ts:588-591). No chip is drawn and nothing visible changes. The ACP-10 fix says the tab names the item that says the most so it can be taken back, but only screen-reader users hear that sentence.
- **Failure:** A sighted person points at six large record types, then chooses a seventh. '@Projects ' appears in their sentence just as the others did, no chip appears, and no message is shown. They send 'Add a field to @Projects'. The agent gets the words but none of Projects' IDs or fields, which is the stall W-200 was built to prevent, and the person never learns which chip to remove.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Check the limit and withAttachment before writing the @name, or remove the written name when the item is refused. Show the refusal visibly beside the chips (an inline note in #chat-attachments, or showError) as well as announcing it. Guard: a Gate-AgentChat.mjs journey attaches items until one is refused, then asserts a visible note that names the largest item and no '@name' added to the textarea. Falsify by reverting to the announcement alone.
- **Verifier:** Traced in agent-mention.ts. choose() writes '@label ' into the textarea and dispatches input (:210-214) before any check. The ninth-item refusal (:216) and withAttachment's budget refusal (:227-228, message built at agent-context-model.ts:309-313) go only to announce(). announce() writes the text into #announcement, which is class visually-hidden role=status (index.html:181, shell.ts:588-591). No chip is drawn and nothing else shows the refusal, so a sighted person sees the @name in their sentence and no explanation. The contract line 'the tab says which item says the most, to take back' (launched-agents.md:176-179) is met only for screen readers. The trigger is uncommon (eight chips, or several maximum-size descriptions exceeding the 32,000-character total), and the agent still has MCP read access to find the type, so the harm is a silent refusal rather than lost work. P3 rather than P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3: reaching the limit takes eight chips or about 32,000 characters of descriptions, and the agent can still read the type through its MCP address. The failing behaviour (silent, invisible refusal with the @name left in the text) is as described.

<a id="wau-10"></a>

### WAU-10 — Send and Launch have no in-flight guard, and Enter during a turn is ignored without a word

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:368`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:167`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:316`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:162`
- **What:** send() reads the box, awaits act(), and clears the box only afterwards. canSend stays true until the host's answer is merged, so a second Enter sends the same text again; the host refuses it as agent-working, which is shown as an error although the first send went through. launchAgent checks state.actionInFlight but never sets it, and the Launch button (data-launch-agent) stays enabled during the request. A double click therefore sends two agentSession.launch requests; the second is refused as agent-already-running, and its error is shown in the new tab. While the agent works, Enter returns early because canSend is false (agent-chat-model.ts:162) and nothing is said. The placeholder that explains this is hidden as soon as the box has text.
- **Failure:** A person double-clicks Launch, and the fresh conversation opens with 'An agent is already running' as an error. A person who types their next instruction while the agent works and presses Enter sees nothing happen, and cannot tell whether it was sent.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Hold a sending flag and a launching flag, and disable Send and the Launch button until the request settles. When Enter is pressed during a turn, say briefly (visibly and announced) that the message waits until the agent finishes, or queue it. Guard: a gate step presses Enter twice quickly and asserts one prompt entry and no error; another double-clicks Launch and asserts one launch.
- **Verifier:** launchAgent checks state.actionInFlight but never sets it and calls no setBusy (view-agent-chat.ts:167-185), and nothing disables the Launch button (agent-launch-model.ts:141), so a double click sends two agentSession.launch requests. The second queues on the Desktop _gate and then hits 'agent-already-running' (DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:156-158), which showError draws on whatever page is current. send() reads the box and clears it only after act() returns (view-agent-chat.ts:368-378), and canSend stays true until the merge, so a second Enter in that window re-sends and the host refuses it with 'agent-working' (AgentConversation.cs:287-288) even though the first prompt went through. During a turn, Enter returns silently at the canSend check (agent-chat-model.ts:162; view-agent-chat.ts:370), and the placeholder only shows while the box is empty. All traced in source; the race window is short, so impact is cosmetic.

### WAU-12 — The permission card omits the tool's kind, and a request cancelled by Stop, End or the program exiting reads 'you chose Cancelled'

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:306`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:296`
- **What:** The head that permissionMarkup draws is '{agent} asks: {title}' plus the origin tag (306). entry.toolKind is never drawn on the card, although the steps list shows it as Read, Edit, Delete or Run (toolKinds, 202-205), and the title is the agent's own free text of up to 500 characters. The person has no way to answer a request with Cancel. When Stop, End, the file closing or the connection ending cancels a request, the host records Answer = 'Cancelled' (AgentConversation.cs:467), and the answered line renders it as 'you chose Cancelled' (296).
- **Failure:** An agent asks 'Update records' for a tool whose kind is delete, and the card gives no Delete cue before Allow once. After the program crashes mid-question, the thread says the person chose Cancelled, which they never did.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Show the kind on the card beside the title ('Delete · Nendo'). Render a request answered with no option as cancelled without attributing it to the person ('cancelled when the turn stopped'). Guard: agent-chat.test.mjs asserts that a permission with toolKind delete renders 'Delete', and that an answer of 'Cancelled' does not render 'you chose'.
- **Verifier:** The 'you chose Cancelled' half is traced end to end. Stop, End and the connection ending answer every open request with null (AgentConversation.cs:350, 388), HandlePermission then stores entry.Answer = 'Cancelled' (467), and permissionMarkup renders any non-null answer as '{title} · you chose {answer}' (agent-chat-model.ts:296). A request the program's exit or a file close cancelled therefore reads as the person's choice. The contract (launched-agents.md:204) only says it is answered as cancelled, so the wording is a UI slip. The card head draws only the agent's title and origin tag, with no toolKind (agent-chat-model.ts:306), while the steps list does show it (286).
- **Correction:** The missing kind cue is an enhancement, not a defect. Nothing in ADR-0030 or the contract requires it, the kind is itself agent-supplied text, and 'Show what it does' already exposes the details. The confirmed defect is the misattributed 'you chose Cancelled' wording, which is cosmetic.

### WCS-08 — Error texts tell the person to 'Refresh the view' but offer no control; the refresh they will reach for (F5/Ctrl+R) reloads the renderer and drops drafts, tabs and the trail

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state` (reported P2) · also reported as UX-23

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:251`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:178`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:261`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:467`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:192`
- **What:** 'The file changed while this action was running. Refresh the view.', 'The file is changing. Refresh the view when the current changes finish.' and the host's 'This action belongs to a file session that has closed. Refresh the view before continuing.' are shown through showError, which has no button (only showRetainedNotice carries 'Refresh view'). The host never sets CoreWebView2Settings.AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled (default true) and the Workbench neither intercepts F5/Ctrl+R in its keydown handler nor registers beforeunload, so F5 reloads the whole Workbench: the DOM-only record draft, every workspace tab and the navigation trail are discarded.
- **Failure:** A save reports 'The file changed while this action was running. Refresh the view.' The person presses F5, as the sentence suggests. The window reloads to the start screen of the file; the record they were editing, its unsaved values, the four tabs they had open and Back/Forward are all gone.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Give these refusals a real 'Refresh view' action (showRetainedNotice with reloadReadWindows) or reword them to name a control that exists; in main.ts map F5/Ctrl+R to that refresh with preventDefault (or set AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled=false in the host and add a beforeunload guard while recordFormIsDirty()). Guard: gate step pressing F5 with a dirty form asserts the page did not reload and the draft remains.
- **Verifier:** The three sentences are shown through showError (shell.ts:527-535), which draws no button; only showRetainedNotice (shell.ts:578) carries 'Refresh view'. host-desktop.ts:178/251 and actions.ts:261 are the cited texts. Nothing handles F5/Ctrl+R: the only Workbench keydown handlers are main.ts:467/530/540 and none match F5, there is no beforeunload, and MainPage.xaml.cs:192-195 sets only AreHostObjectsAllowed, IsStatusBarEnabled, IsWebMessageEnabled and IsZoomControlEnabled, so AreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled keeps its WebView2 default (true) and F5 reloads the page, dropping the DOM-only draft, tabs (workspace-tabs.ts module state) and the trail. The triggers are rare races, so this is wording friction plus an unguarded browser default, not a P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. Mitigations the finding omits: on the stale-file-session path runMutation already runs recoverAfterWriteFailure (actions.ts:85-86), which re-reads the session and redraws or retains the draft read-only before the sentence is shown, and any rail click re-reads the snapshot (openWorkspaceView, actions.ts:334), so a real refresh is one click away. The unsaved-save journal survives a reload (localStorage), so only drafts, tabs and the trail are lost. F5 reload behaviour is from the WebView2 documented default; I did not run the app.

### WCS-12 — Ctrl+/ (show or hide shortcuts) cannot be pressed on keyboards where '/' needs Shift, such as Danish and German

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shortcuts.ts:78`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/protocol.ts:156`
- **What:** matchShortcut requires !event.shiftKey for every Ctrl shortcut, and on Danish/German/Nordic layouts '/' is Shift+7, so the event is key '/', ctrlKey, shiftKey. chordOf for custom views deliberately drops Shift for symbols ('which symbols need Shift depends on the keyboard'), so the same keys work inside a view and not in the Workbench. The status bar advertises 'Ctrl / hide shortcuts'.
- **Failure:** On a Danish keyboard the person presses Ctrl+Shift+7 (Ctrl+/) as the status bar says; nothing happens unless focus is inside a custom view.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-shortcuts.mjs -> "main document matchShortcut(Ctrl+Shift+7 \"/\") = null" / "inside a custom view chordOf -> Ctrl+/ -> shortcutForKeys = hints"
- **Fix and guard:** In matchShortcut ignore Shift for single-character symbol keys, as chordOf does. Guard: shortcuts.test.mjs case for { key: '/', ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true }.
- **Verifier:** shortcuts.ts:78 requires !event.shiftKey for every Ctrl shortcut, and line 81 maps key '/' to 'hints'. On Danish, German and Nordic layouts '/' is Shift+7, so Ctrl+Shift+7 arrives as key '/', ctrlKey, shiftKey and matchShortcut returns null; main.ts:467-478 then falls to chordOf (extension-api/protocol.ts:144-158), which drops Shift for symbols, finds no view-declared 'Ctrl+/' and does nothing. Inside a custom view the same keys work because api.js hands 'Ctrl+/' back (shortcutForKeys, shortcuts.ts:56-58). shortcuts.test.mjs:32-41 has no '/' with Shift case, so this is not a deliberate choice; the comment at shortcuts.ts:73 is about letters.
- **Correction:** Minor scope: only Ctrl+/ is affected (digits, letters and Tab have no shifted form), and the same toggle is reachable from the status-bar button (#shortcuts-toggle, main.ts:431,451) and the palette, so P3. KeyboardEvent.key for Ctrl+Shift+7 being '/' is Chromium's documented behaviour (Ctrl is not applied to the character); I did not run it.

### WCS-15 — The command palette keeps showing record hits for the previous text, and Enter opens one

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/command-palette.ts:202`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/command-palette.ts:214`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/command-palette.ts:286`
- **What:** filter() re-ranks commands and schedules a search 150 ms later, but leaves `records` from the earlier text in place (cleared only below two characters). active resets to 0, so when no command matches the new text, Enter runs records[0] from the old query.
- **Failure:** The person types 'inv', sees 'Invoice 12', keeps typing 'invoice 99' and presses Enter quickly; 'Invoice 12' opens.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Clear or mark records stale when the text changes, and do not run a record entry until the search for the current text has answered. Guard: palette unit test with a delayed search asserting Enter before the answer runs nothing from the old text.
- **Verifier:** command-palette.ts:201-206 filter() re-ranks, sets active = 0, schedules the search and draws, but leaves `records` from the earlier answer in place. scheduleSearch() (:211-216) clears them only when the text is under searchMinimum (2) or there is no file. searchRecords() replaces them only after the 150 ms pause plus the host round trip. In that window the stale hits are still listed. When no command matches the new text, ranked is empty, so Enter -> runAt(0) (:286-296) resolves records[0 - ranked.length] and runs the old hit's openRecordFromView. The module comment ('only the answer to the latest text is shown') covers dropping late answers, not stale display. No test or ADR-0028 text mandates keeping stale hits. Navigation only, no write, and it needs a fast Enter, hence P3.

### WCS-17 — Ctrl+click or middle-click on a rail route opens a new tab even when the route then refuses, leaving a duplicate tab selected

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/workspace-tabs.ts:243`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/workspace-tabs.ts:249`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:325`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:414`
- **What:** wireOpenInNewTab registers a capture-phase click listener on #app-rail that calls newTab(false) for any Ctrl+click on an enabled .nav-item/.nav-place before the route's own handler runs, and the auxclick listener calls newTab(false) and then route.click(). newTab copies the current place into the new tab, makes it active and redraws the strip. The route handlers decline afterwards in ordinary states: openWorkspaceView returns silently on state.actionInFlight and refuses with refuseWhileDirty; openHelp, openAgentView and rail-places openPlace refuse while dirty. Nothing removes the tab that was made for the refused move.
- **Failure:** With unsaved typing on a record page, the person Ctrl+clicks History in the rail to look at it in another tab. The sentence 'Save your changes or close record details before leaving this screen.' appears, yet a second tab with the same record page is now open and selected, and the draft now sits in the new tab while the original tab holds the same place. The same happens silently when the click lands while a save or read is in flight.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Decide the refusal before creating the tab: check state.actionInFlight and recordFormIsDirty() (refuseWhileDirty) in wireOpenInNewTab, or have the route report whether it moved and close the new tab (closeTabAt) when it did not. Guard: a workspace-tabs test that a Ctrl+click on a route with a dirty openDraft leaves set.tabs.length unchanged.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. wireOpenInNewTab (workspace-tabs.ts:243-250) adds a capture-phase click listener on #app-rail that calls newTab(false) for any Ctrl+click on an enabled .nav-item/.nav-place, before the route's own handler runs and without checking state.actionInFlight or recordFormIsDirty(). newTab (:150-163) saves the current trail, inserts a tab, makes it active and loads a trail holding only the current place. The route handler then declines: openWorkspaceView returns on actionInFlight or refuseWhileDirty (actions.ts:325-327), openPlace does the same (rail-places.ts:58), as do openHelp (actions.ts:533) and openAgentView (main.ts:661). Nothing closes the tab already made, and the middle-click path (:253-259) makes the tab first too. A second tab on the same place is left selected, next to the 'Save your changes or close record details before ...' sentence. No test covers it; mica-direction.md:98 only says Ctrl-click opens a new tab. Harmless duplicate (closable, no data loss), so P3.
- **Correction:** State.openDraft is not tab-scoped, so the draft does not 'move' to the new tab. Both tabs show the same place and the draft stays on screen. A plain Ctrl+T on a dirty page also makes a duplicate by design (newTab says 'Nothing redraws'), so the defect is only that a refused open still leaves a tab behind.

### WCS-20 — While a save is unconfirmed, the read-only sweep disables Revoke edit access, the control the busy bar and agent pill send the person to

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:162`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:185`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:228`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:356`
- **What:** render() disables every '[data-action]' when awaitingSave; #revoke-agent carries data-action and is not exempted (only #approve-behaviour/#revoke-behaviour and [data-agent-chat] are). A person's save usually goes unconfirmed because an agent holds the gate past the 15 s timeout, which is when the pill says 'End it under Agent -> Revoke edit access.'
- **Failure:** An agent's long write makes the person's save time out; they go to Agent to revoke the agent as the status bar says, and Revoke edit access is greyed out until a retry succeeds, which waits on the same agent.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Exempt #revoke-agent (and other agent-control actions that are not edits to the file) from the pending-save sweep. Guard: render test with a pending mutation asserting #revoke-agent is enabled.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. main.ts:161-171 disables every control matching alwaysAvailable (main.ts:185-186) when renderPendingMutation() returns true (pending-mutations journal entry in state 'pending'); that selector exempts #approve-behaviour and #revoke-behaviour but not #revoke-agent, which view-agent.ts:228 renders with data-action and outside any [data-agent-chat] wrapper (the only other exemptions at main.ts:167-169). The entry stays 'pending' for every code outside the rejected set (pending-mutations.ts:19-33,129-139), so host-timeout (host-desktop.ts:191-196) and cancelled (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:494-497) both lock the file, and the Agent page poll (main.ts:770-798) re-renders through the same sweep. shell.ts:356-357 and 472-473 tell the person that Agent -> Revoke edit access is how to stop the agent, so the sweep disables the very control those texts name. No test or doc pins this (grep of tools/ and Workbench scripts finds no #revoke-agent use). It is friction, not data loss: File-menu actions are exempt, and Check or retry save unlocks once the agent's write ends, so P3 stands.
- **Correction:** 'Usually' is overstated, since a host-timeout needs one agent write longer than 15 s. The more direct route is pressing Stop on the 'X is writing to this file...' busy bar (finding 22), which also leaves the save pending. The gap is wider than stated: setBusy (shell.ts:440-451) disables [data-action] including #revoke-agent for the whole time the save is in flight, so the control is unavailable before the timeout as well as after it.

### WCS-22 — Stopping a slow save leaves it pending, and the only way to unlock editing resends the save the person stopped

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:482`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:133`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:217`
- **What:** Stop calls cancelInFlight; the host answers the save with code 'cancelled', which is not a confirmed rejection, so the entry stays pending and every control is disabled. The notice offers only 'Check or retry save', which replays the payload when no receipt exists. There is no discard path.
- **Failure:** The person presses Stop on a save they no longer want; editing is locked until they press 'Check or retry save', which writes the change they stopped.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Treat a host-confirmed cancellation as settled when the host guarantees nothing committed, or add 'Discard this unsent change' once a receipt lookup confirms nothing landed. Guard: journal test for code 'cancelled' with a null receipt.
- **Verifier:** Traced. shell.ts:482-494 Stop calls client.cancelInFlight (host-desktop.ts:147-159), which sends request.cancel for each pending request. The host maps the resulting OperationCanceledException to code 'cancelled' (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:494-497). That code is not in the rejected set (pending-mutations.ts:19-33), so sendPending (pending-mutations.ts:123-141) does a receipt lookup, finds none, and rethrows with the entry still 'pending'. The next render() sweeps every control disabled and shows the notice (main.ts:161-224). The only button is retryPendingSave (actions.ts:480-516), which calls journal.retry with allowReplay=true: lookup returns null, then sendPending resends the original payload (pending-mutations.ts:99-107). The journal has no discard method and the notice offers none, so the stopped change is written the moment the person unlocks editing. No test covers 'cancelled' in the journal (grep of scripts/ and tools/).
- **Correction:** This follows the documented fail-safe in docs/contracts/operation-outcomes.md:51-59: an unresolved save blocks new keys and is resolved only by an explicit Check or retry. It is also reasonable for the host not to promise 'nothing landed' on cancel, since a cancel can arrive mid-commit. So the defect is a missing 'Discard this unsent change' affordance after a receipt lookup returns null, not a misclassified code. Stop is only offered for a save that has been slow for 700 ms, so impact is limited to a locked page and one forced resend, which is not data loss. P3.

### WDV-10 — A record form value that does not parse is reported without its field name, and the field is not revealed

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-form.ts:101`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/scalars.ts:18`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/scalars.ts:24`
- **What:** The submit handler parses every field inside a single try, and catches with showError(messageFor(error)). The messages from parseScalar name no field ('Enter a whole number without separators.'), and unlike the required-field branch nothing calls revealField. Numeric fields are type=text inputs, and tabbed pages are novalidate, so the browser does not point at the field either.
- **Failure:** A record page has eight numeric fields across three tabs. The person types '1,000' into Budget on the Finance tab and saves from the Overview tab. They read 'Enter a whole number without separators.' with no idea which field it means, and its tab stays closed.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pure-probe.mjs -> parseScalar("Integer", "1,000") throws "Enter a whole number without separators."; parseScalar("Decimal", "1,5") throws "Enter a decimal using a dot, without separators or an exponent." The submit path that drops the field: source.
- **Fix and guard:** Parse field by field, prefix the message with the field's displayName and call revealField(page, field.semanticId) (and focus it on untabbed forms), as the required check does. Guard: a record-form test that submits an unparseable value in a closed tab and asserts the message names the field and the tab opens; falsify by restoring the single catch.
- **Verifier:** record-form.ts:100-104 parses every edited field inside one try and catches with showError(messageFor(error)); scalars.ts:15,18,20,24,28 throw messages that name no field (e.g. 'Enter a whole number without separators.'). Unlike the required branch at record-form.ts:111-114 nothing calls revealField. Numeric fields are plain type=text inputs (record-markup.ts:460, no pattern/setCustomValidity anywhere in src), and tabbed pages are novalidate (record-markup.ts:470-476), so the browser does not point at the field either. The defect is real but it is a message-quality/UX gap: only fields the person edited can fail, the message says what to type, and they can find the field they just typed into, so P3 rather than P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: no data is lost or misdirected; the friction is locating the field on a multi-tab page.

### WMX-06 — Nested Markdown lists in agent replies and AI-written notes are flattened or merged into their parent item

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:49`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:57`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:86`
- **What:** listItem accepts at most three leading spaces. A child line indented by four spaces is therefore not an item, and line 57 appends it to the parent's text joined by a space. A child indented by two spaces becomes a sibling. A bullet under a numbered item fails next.ordered === item.ordered, which ends the ordered list. No nested list is ever emitted. W-173's stated purpose and the agent tab (agent-chat-model.ts:264) both render AI-written Markdown, where nested lists are routine.
- **Failure:** '- Parent\n - child one\n - child two' renders as one bullet, 'Parent - child one - child two'. '1. Step one\n - detail a\n - detail b\n2. Step two' renders as three separate lists, so the details lose their parent step.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: markdownMarkup() from a vite SSR bundle -> nested_list_4sp gives "<ul><li>Parent - child one - child two</li><li>Next</li></ul>"; ordered_with_nested_bullets gives "<ol><li>Step one</li></ol><ul><li>detail a</li><li>detail b</li></ul><ol start=\"2\"><li>Step two</li></ol>".
- **Fix and guard:** Track indentation, and emit a nested <ul> or <ol> inside the parent <li> when a list line is indented at least to the parent's content column (two or more spaces for a bullet, the marker's width for a number). Guard: markdown.test.mjs cases for both inputs, asserting <li>Parent<ul><li>child one</li>...</ul></li> and a single <ol> that contains the nested <ul>.
- **Verifier:** markdown.ts:85-89 accepts at most three leading spaces on a list line, markdown.ts:57 folds a deeper-indented line into the previous item's text, and nothing emits a nested list. I ran the real file under node 25: '- Parent\n - child one\n - child two\n- Next' gives <ul><li>Parent - child one - child two</li><li>Next</li></ul>, and '1. Step one\n - detail a\n - detail b\n2. Step two' gives <ol>, <ul>, <ol start="2"> as three separate lists, matching the report. agent-chat-model.ts:264 and record-markup.ts:442 both use it for AI-written text. No ADR or contract promises nested lists: the markdown.ts:4-12 header and markdown.test.mjs list the supported subset without them. The text stays readable and nothing is lost, so this is a rendering gap in a documented subset, P3.
- **Correction:** It is a limitation of an explicitly partial subset, not a regression. Two-space nesting renders as flat sibling items rather than merging into the parent.

### WMX-17 — Studio's Surfaces catalogue describes a matrix screen by its raw kind 'matrixSurface' and files it under the generic 'Surfaces' kind

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-surfaces.ts:136`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-surfaces.ts:161`
- **What:** treeSurfaceCard has a case for each root kind except matrixSurface, so a matrix falls to default and parts.push(root.kind) writes 'matrixSurface' as the card's description. cardKindFor has no matrix case either and returns 'Surfaces', which gives the card the generic icon. surface-model.ts already has kindLabel('matrixSurface') === 'Matrix'.

### WSP-19 — A Studio change the host refuses lands on a dead review, and Back throws away what was typed

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:562`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:28`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:36`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:209`
- **What:** On a validation refusal, proposal.prepareChangeSet returns an Invalid proposal with diagnostics and empty PreviewApplications (catch block in NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs); it does not throw. The dialog is replaced by the review ("Cannot apply", "No healthy preview is available"). Back goes to proposalReturnView ('structure'), not to the dialog, and leaves the invalid proposal in the host unless the person presses Reject.
- **Failure:** The person adds a field whose name the host refuses, or hits any other validation refusal. The review shows the diagnostic, Back shows Structure, and the name, type and choices have to be entered again.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** When the preview is not previewable, reject it in prepareApplication and keep the dialog, showing the diagnostics in its message slot. Guard: a test with a stub client returning an Invalid state, asserting that state.view is unchanged and proposal.reject was called.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:~150 catches NendoException from the clone apply, sets State = Invalid with diagnostics and empty PreviewApplications, and returns it rather than throwing. For example RequireUniqueDisplayNameAsync (SqliteNendoStore.Evolution.cs:34) refuses a duplicate rename with label-conflict, so a Rename or Add field to an existing name is reachable. actions.ts:556-566 prepareApplication has no previewable check: it stores the proposal and sets state.view = 'proposal'. view-proposal.ts:24-28 renders 'Cannot apply', 'No healthy preview is available', the diagnostic, and Accept disabled. Back (view-proposal.ts:36) sets state.proposal = null and view = proposalReturnView ('structure') without calling proposal.reject, so the Invalid context stays in the coordinator's _proposals, and the add-field/rename dialog (renderAddField/renderRenameSchema) is rebuilt from scratch, losing the typed name, type and choices. Impact is retyping one small form, so P3.
- **Correction:** The review is not entirely dead: it does show the host's diagnostic message and hint, which is the engine's designed refusal path. The cost is that Back lands on Structure rather than the dialog and does not reject the Invalid proposal. Validation errors that throw before the gate (changeSet.Validate) stay in the dialog and are not affected.

- **What:** renameSchemaProposal titles a rename "Rename to X", and the engine's diff says "Rename field to X.". Neither names the field, its record type or the old name. renderFieldRequirement keeps the title "Make X required" or "Reactivate X" for a batch proposal that, when nextCursor is set, carries only fill operations. Every "What changes" entry gets the ＋ mark, including retirements, removals and deletions.

The reachable defects are the misleading accepted announcement and the unnamed rename diff.

### WST-01 — A Help article jumps back to the top on every file-change redraw, and the scroll-restore guard reads only 2 of the 22 stylesheets

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/scroll-restore.test.mjs:21`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:74`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:430`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-help.ts:27`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/05-help.css:25`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:708`
- **What:** scroll-restore.test.mjs builds its list of scrollers from ['08-panels.css', '09-surfaces.css'] only. shell.ts scrollPositions() restores content plus '.use-surface, .card-stack, .outline-surface-frame, .record-inspector, .quick-filter-panel'. Help owns its own scroll regions: .studio-content.is-help has overflow hidden, and .help-article and .help-index have overflow-y auto (05-help.css:12,25). On a fileChanged event, followTheFile (main.ts:708-724) calls rerender(), which runs renderHelp(). renderHelp rebuilds content.innerHTML, so the new .help-article starts at scrollTop 0 and nothing restores it. The hold that should defer the redraw does not see the reading either. shell.ts:430 registers content.addEventListener('scroll', ...) without capture, and element scroll events do not bubble. Scrolling inside .help-article, .record-inspector or .card-stack therefore never updates lastInteractionAt.
- **Failure:** The person opens Help -> Agent access and scrolls halfway down the article while an agent writes to the file (an Unattended build sends dozens of fileChanged events). Each chase pass redraws Help, at most once a second, and the article snaps back to the top every time. This is the same once-a-second scroll-to-top defect the guard's own comment describes for .record-inspector.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probes/scroll-restore-all.mjs (the test's own scrollingClasses rule run over every stylesheet) -> 'NOT SCANNED 05-help.css: help-index, help-article, help-topics', 'NOT SCANNED 07-studio.css: studio-content, studio-search-results', 'NOT SCANNED 12-agent-activity.css: reference-results, package-file-text, preview-content', 'NOT SCANNED 22-agent-chat.css: chat-scroll, chat-plain, chat-mention' (plus popups: file-menu-panel, command-palette-list, view-menu, primary-nav)
- **Fix and guard:** Add .help-article and .help-index to scrollPositions(), or have renderHelp keep both scrollTops across a redraw of the same topic. Register the scroll listener with { capture: true, passive: true } so a scroll inside any scroller counts as reading. Change the guard to read every file in src/styles/, and give the popups and self-managed scrollers (chat-scroll, command-palette-list, view-menu, file-menu-panel, primary-nav, chat-mention) a named EXEMPT reason. Falsify the guard by removing .record-inspector from the selector and confirming it fails, then confirm it fails today on help-article.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. main.ts:703-724 followTheFile calls rerender() on every fileChanged, and main.ts:137-138 sends the Help view to renderHelp(), which rebuilds content.innerHTML (view-help.ts:27-45), so the new .help-article (overflow-y:auto, 05-help.css:25) starts at scrollTop 0. shell.ts:67-76 scrollPositions() restores only content plus .use-surface, .card-stack, .outline-surface-frame, .record-inspector and .quick-filter-panel, and content itself has overflow:hidden in Help (05-help.css:9). The hold does not see the reading either: shell.ts:430 registers the scroll listener without capture and scroll does not bubble, and the other three listeners are pointerdown, keydown and focusin, so a wheel reader inside .help-article leaves interactionInProgress() false. The guard reads only 08-panels.css and 09-surfaces.css (scroll-restore.test.mjs:21) out of the 22 files in src/styles, so it cannot see 05-help.css. Reachability needs an external writer (own writes return early at main.ts:~795) while the person reads Help, which is narrow, so P3 rather than P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: the redraw needs an agent or other client committing while Help is open, and it clears when the writes stop. The reproduction is a source trace plus the reviewer's scan of the guard's selector rule, not a live UI run.

### WST-07 — Agent activity labels the main write tools 'Changed workspace data' or 'Agent activity', and the test meant to stop that uses a stale tool list and an assertion that cannot fail for mutations

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/format.test.mjs:109`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/format.ts:164`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/format.ts:195`
- **What:** activityLabel's table has no entry for nendo.data.apply_writes, nendo.data.update_record, nendo.data.undo_revision or nendo.change_set.revalidate. These are tools the host declares (help.test.mjs expectedTools) and that NendoHostSkill tells agents to use. The data tools are logged with category 'mutation' (NendoDataTools.cs:352), which falls back to 'Changed workspace data'. revalidate is 'authoring', which falls back to 'Agent activity'. format.test.mjs:110 hard-codes 22 tool names without those four, and only asserts `!== 'Agent activity'`, which the 'mutation' fallback always satisfies.
- **Failure:** An agent applies a batch with nendo.data.apply_writes or undoes one with nendo.data.undo_revision. The Agent page's activity feed reads 'Changed workspace data' for both, so the person cannot tell a write from an undo. A revalidated proposal reads only 'Agent activity'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probes/activity-labels.mjs (real src/format.ts) -> 'mutation nendo.data.apply_writes "Changed workspace data"', 'mutation nendo.data.update_record "Changed workspace data"', 'mutation nendo.data.undo_revision "Changed workspace data"', 'authoring nendo.change_set.revalidate "Agent activity"'
- **Fix and guard:** Add labels for the four tools, for example 'Wrote records as one revision', 'Edited a record', 'Undid its own change' and 'Revalidated an app proposal'. In format.test.mjs, iterate the tool names from help.ts agentSurface instead of a copied array, and assert that the label is neither fallback ('Agent activity' nor 'Changed workspace data'). Falsify by deleting one label.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. format.ts:164-194 has no label for nendo.data.apply_writes, nendo.data.update_record, nendo.data.undo_revision or nendo.change_set.revalidate. NendoDataTools.cs:352 records every data tool (including these three, lines 195/231/253) under category 'mutation' with the tool name, and NendoAuthoringTools.cs:217 records revalidate as 'authoring'. The fallback at format.ts:195 then yields 'Changed workspace data' / 'Agent activity', and view-agent.ts:349 renders only that label plus client and a short revision id, so a batch write, a single-record update and an undo read the same. The comment at format.ts:162 says every tool is labelled, so this is an oversight, not a choice. It is cosmetic (activity-feed wording), hence P3.
- **Correction:** The test critique is slightly off: format.test.mjs:111 loops over six categories including 'tool' and 'authoring', so its assertion does fail for any name on its list that lacks a label. The real test defect is only that the hard-coded list (line 110) is stale and omits the four tools (and set_kept_in_new_files); the 'cannot fail for mutations' wording applies only to the 'mutation' category. The fix (add four labels, derive the list from help-agents.ts or the host's tools) is right.

### WST-10 — In dark mode every window paints light first: index.html hard-codes data-theme="light" and the theme is applied only after the 1.4 MB module has run

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:2`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/02-tokens.css:10`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:369`
- **What:** The document starts as `<html data-theme="light" data-theme-preference="system">`. 02-tokens.css defines light tokens on :root and dark ones only on :root[data-theme="dark"], and no stylesheet has a prefers-color-scheme rule. The stylesheet is render-blocking, while the module script is deferred, and applyTheme(readPreference()) runs only inside initialise(), after the whole bundle (index-*.js, 1,434,994 bytes) is parsed and evaluated. The Desktop gives the WebView a transparent DefaultBackgroundColor (MainPage.xaml.cs:152), so the light canvas is what shows.
- **Failure:** With Windows in dark mode, or the Dark override, opening a window, a new window or a renderer restart flashes the light canvas and light rail before the page turns dark. AGENTS.md requires the effective theme to apply to the app frame.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Add `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root[data-theme-preference="system"]:not([data-theme="light"]) { …dark tokens… } }`. Alternatively, load a tiny same-origin theme-boot.js synchronously in <head> (allowed by script-src 'self') that applies the stored preference before first paint. Guard it with a headless-Edge check under prefers-color-scheme: dark that the first frame's body background equals --canvas dark.
- **Verifier:** index.html:2 hard-codes data-theme="light"; 02-tokens.css puts light tokens on :root and dark only on :root[data-theme="dark"] (line 58); no stylesheet has a prefers-color-scheme rule; applyTheme runs from initialise() (main.ts:369) inside the deferred module. MainPage.xaml.cs:152 makes the WebView transparent and nothing hides it until the page is ready. Reproduced with the shipped dist/ in headless Edge 154 (same Chromium as WebView2) under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, using Page.startScreencast (probe: scratchpad/review/verify/workbench-scripts-tests-7/theme-screencast-probe.mjs), 3 runs: frame 0 is the dark about:blank (18,18,18), frame 1 is a composited LIGHT page (canvas 249,249,250 and root 238,241,246), frame 2 onward is dark (30,32,36 and 39,40,41). So a light frame is shown before the theme is applied, every time.
- **Correction:** Magnitude is small: the light frame lasted 1 to 2 frames (about 10 to 34 ms between screencast timestamps), measured in headless Edge rather than inside WebView2 itself. Real but a brief flicker, so P3. The suggested fix (a prefers-color-scheme rule under data-theme-preference=system, or a synchronous same-origin theme-boot.js) would remove it.

### WXS-06 — A navigation or proposal a view starts by itself, while the person has unsaved typing, moves focus out of the field they are typing in

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-ui.ts:24`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-ui.ts:35`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/draft-guard.ts:32`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:532`
- **What:** refuseNow is used by openRecordFromView, openScreenFromView and openStudioFromView, and inside the try of openProposalFromView. It calls refuseWhileDirty. While a record form is dirty, that calls `showError('Save your changes or close record details before opening a record from a custom view.')`. showError runs `focusWithoutInteraction(slot)` and `scrollIntoView`. ui.openRecord, ui.openScreen, ui.openStudio, proposals.prepare and proposals.open have no rate limit and need no action from the person.
- **Failure:** A view creates a record and calls nendo.ui.openRecord when the write answers, or prepares a proposal in reaction to a `changes` event. Meanwhile the person has started typing in a record form. The refusal moves focus from their field to the message slot, their next keystrokes go nowhere, and the sentence blames them for an action they never took. A view that repeats the call can keep the form unusable.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Give the paths a view starts a refusal that does not touch the page. A variant of refuseWhileDirty that only reports whether the form is dirty lets the broker answer `not-allowed` to the view and leaves showError and focus alone. Keep the visible refusal for the person's own clicks. Guard: an extension-ui test with a dirty form, asserting that ui.openRecord rejects with not-allowed and document.activeElement is unchanged.
- **Verifier:** extension-ui.ts:24-29 refuseNow calls refuseWhileDirty, which (draft-guard.ts:32-36) runs showError before refuseNow throws; showError (shell.ts:527-535) calls focusWithoutInteraction(slot), which does call element.focus() (shell.ts:402-406; it only keeps the move out of the interaction timer), and scrollIntoView. openRecordFromView, openScreenFromView and openStudioFromView call refuseNow first; openProposalFromView (extension-ui.ts:35-41) catches the throw but showError has already run. The three navigation methods have no rate limit (extension-broker.ts:655-658), so a view that calls them on its own (for example from a changes event) while a record form is dirty pulls focus off the person's field with a sentence about an action they did not take. Fine when the person clicked in the view; only the self-initiated call is wrong. It needs a buggy or hostile view and costs a focus move, so P3.
- **Correction:** Only affects self-initiated view calls; a person's own click inside the view legitimately gets this refusal. The rest of the finding (proposals.prepare/open also unrated) is accurate: no rate limit on those paths either.

### WXS-13 — Studio's package card says 'Not shown anywhere yet' for a package that only an extensionView (a screen of the file) shows

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/custom-view-recipe.ts:195`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-packages.ts:127`
- **What:** viewsOfPackage keeps only nodes whose kind is one of viewKinds (extensionRecordsSurface, extensionGraphSurface, extensionRecordPanel). An `extensionView` root carries `packageId` (ADR-0013, W-106) but is dropped, so packageUsesMarkup prints 'Not shown anywhere yet. Add a view to put it on a screen or a record page.' with no Open button.
- **Failure:** A file's workbench is an extensionView (the Archi workbench pattern), possibly the screen the file opens on. Studio > Surfaces > Custom views tells the person the package is shown nowhere. Answering that question is what the list is for (C-189), and the answer suggests removing the package is safe.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe.mjs recipe -> G.uses [] for one root {kind:'extensionView', properties:{packageId:'org.example.archi', title:'Archi workbench'}}
- **Fix and guard:** Include `extensionView` in viewsOfPackage as a use worded 'a screen of the file', with an Open button that goes through the file-view path (`state.fileView`). Guard: a custom-view-recipe.test.mjs case asserting that an extensionView root is listed.
- **Verifier:** viewsOfPackage (custom-view-recipe.ts:193-208) keeps only nodes whose kind is in viewKinds (custom-view-recipe.ts:20-24: extensionRecordsSurface, extensionGraphSurface, extensionRecordPanel), so an extensionView root (required packageId, contract custom-views.md:1442) yields no use. packageUsesMarkup (view-packages.ts:125-128) is rendered for every package card (view-packages.ts:30-34) and then prints 'Not shown anywhere yet. Add a view to put it on a screen or a record page.' with no Open button. Studio's Screens of the file list (view-surfaces.ts:56-61, contract line 385) does show the same view as 'runs <packageId>', so the two parts of the same Surfaces page contradict each other. The helper predates W-106 (its tests, custom-view-recipe.test.mjs:114-116, cover only the three kinds) and the Add view form cannot create an extensionView, so this reads as an omission, not a choice. It is a wording and discoverability error on a read-only card, so P3.
- **Correction:** The Open button for an extensionView must go through the file-view path (showFileView / state.fileView in file-view-model.ts), not the data-view-open handler that takes an entity. The reviewer's remark that the card 'suggests removing the package is safe' is an inference; removal still goes through a reviewed proposal.

### WXS-14 — In a file with no authored record page, the Add view form's panel choice asks the person to choose a record type the form does not offer

**P3** · ux · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-packages.ts:139`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/custom-view-recipe.ts:115`
- **What:** initialDraft('panel') takes `pageChoices(...)[0]`. With no recordForm or detailSurface root it sets entityId to ''. refusalFor checks the record type before the page and returns 'Choose a record type that exists.', but the panel form draws only an empty 'Record page' select and no record-type control.
- **Failure:** A person picks 'A panel on a record page' in a file whose record pages are not authored as nodes. Preview stays disabled, the sentence points at a control that is not on the form, and nothing says a record page has to exist first.

- **Fix and guard:** In refusalFor, check the page first for a panel, and say 'This file has no record page to put a panel on yet.' when pageChoices is empty. Or leave the panel kind out when there are no pages. Guard: a custom-view-recipe.test.mjs case with no pages asserting that refusal.

The message is misleading but the effect is limited to a disabled Preview button in a file that has no record page; no data is touched.

### CSS-05 — Below 651px the address row stacks into three rows, with a full-width Back/Forward bar and a breadcrumb that doesn't stretch

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design` (reported P2) · also reported as UIS-16

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:367`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:374`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:380`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:385`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:344`
- **What:** The pre-Mica `@media (max-width: 650px)` block sets `.workspace-header { flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start }`, `.header-controls { flex-direction: column; width: 100% }`, `.theme-control, .history-control { width: 100% }` and `... button { flex: 1 }`. 21-native.css:344 uses the specificity bump `html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header` to restate the address row, but it resets only justify-content, gap, min-height, padding, border and background. Flex-direction, align-items and the history-control width still come from 10. mica-direction.md describes the address row as one row: Back and Forward, the breadcrumb, then the command box.
- **Failure:** In a window 600px wide, the address row grows to 120px. A full-width strip holds two stretched Back/Forward buttons. The breadcrumb sits on its own line at its content width (166px), so a long record type or view name truncates with room to spare. The command box gets a third line. That is 120px of chrome on the screen with the least height to spare.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-layout.cjs -> at 600x800 the probe reported header [0,48,600,120] with headerDir "column", history [16,58,564,32], identity [20,94,166,32] and palette [24,130,36,32]. Screenshot layout-600x800.png shows the stack.
- **Fix and guard:** Delete the `.workspace-header`, `.header-controls`, `.theme-control, .history-control` and button `flex: 1` rules from 10-forms.css:366-388, because 21-native owns these. Replace the `html:root` bump with a plain `.workspace-layer > .workspace-header` rule once the conflict is gone. Guard: a browser-lane assertion that `.workspace-header` is one row (height at most 52px, flex-direction row) at 600px and 400px widths.
- **Verifier:** 10-forms.css:366-388 (@media max-width: 650px) sets .workspace-header flex-direction column and .header-controls/.history-control width 100%. 21-native.css:344 (html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header) resets only justify-content, gap, min-height, padding, border and background, so flex-direction and the 100%-width rules survive. 12-agent-activity.css:308 restores row, but only inside the compact (max-width 840 and max-height 600) block. I re-ran headless Edge: 650x800, 600x601 and 600x700 give a 120px column header; 651x800, 600x560 and 512x480 give a 48px row. Real cascade leftover, but it needs width <=650 and height >600. The host minimum is 1024 physical px (DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:10-11), so that is reachable only at 175%+ scaling in a tall narrow window; at 100-150% the minimum window is already wider than 650 CSS px.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The stack does not appear in short windows: at height <=600 the compact rule at 12:308 forces a row, so the 'screen with the least height to spare' scenario does not apply. It is limited to width <=650 and height >600.

### CSS-07 — The recovery-panel heading rules target h3, but the Health page emits h2, so the compact grid misplaces the heading and the headings render at the browser default size

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/12-agent-activity.css:335`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:552`
- **What:** view-health.ts:66 and :74 emit `<h2>File status</h2>` and `<h2>Recovery actions</h2>`. The rules meant for them are `.recovery-action-list h3 { grid-column: 1 / -1 }` (12:335, in the compact two-column action grid) and `.recovery-findings h3, .recovery-action-list h3 { font-size: 1.05rem }` (13:552). Neither matches. Only `.recovery-layout h2 { margin }` (01:70) applies, so the headings use the user-agent h2 size.
- **Failure:** In the compact layout, 'Recovery actions' fills the first grid cell and 'Inspect Data' sits beside it rather than under it. At every other size, both recovery headings render at about 21px, larger than any other card heading in Studio (0.95-1.05rem).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-layout.cjs screenshots -> layout-800x560.png shows 'Recovery actions' in column 1 beside 'Inspect Data'. tabs-12.png (1280x800) shows 'File status' and 'Recovery actions' at the large default h2 size.
- **Fix and guard:** Change both selectors to h2, or make the markup emit h3 consistently. Guard: assert the computed font-size of `.recovery-action-list > h2` equals 1.05rem, and in the compact layout assert its grid-column-end is -1.
- **Verifier:** view-health.ts:66 and :74 emit <h2>File status</h2> and <h2>Recovery actions</h2>. The rules written for them target h3: .recovery-action-list h3 { grid-column: 1 / -1 } (12-agent-activity.css:335) and .recovery-action-list h3 { font-size: 1.05rem } (13-refinements-pages.css:552). The Recovery actions section contains no h3, so those selectors match nothing. No global h2 rule exists (02-tokens.css:13 sets 14px root; UA 1.5em gives about 21px). In the compact layout, 12:334 makes .recovery-action-list a two-column grid, so the h2 occupies the first cell beside Inspect Data; the reviewer's layout-800x560.png shows it and I viewed it. Cosmetic.
- **Correction:** The h3 half is only partly dead: .recovery-findings h3 (13:552) does match the 'Automatic actions' h3 emitted by behaviourApprovalMarkup (view-health.ts:40) inside the findings card; only the .recovery-action-list h3 selectors are dead. 'Larger than any other card heading in Studio' is overstated (.record-form-card h2 is 1.45rem, .help-article h2 1.9rem); it is larger than the Health page's other card headings (0.95-1.05rem).

### CSS-08 — Wide windows 720px tall or less get a 12px empty band under the status line

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:470`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:213`
- **What:** 10-forms.css:470-473 adds `.workspace { padding-bottom: 12px }` at `max-height: 720px`, a leftover of the pre-Mica floating card. 21-native restates `.workspace` (grid rows, background) without padding. It only zeroes padding below 841px wide (line 501). So in the wide layout the status line no longer reaches the window's bottom edge.
- **Failure:** On a maximised 1366x768 screen at 100%, or a 1920x1080 screen at 150%, the viewport is 720px tall or less. The status line floats 12px above the bottom of the window, with a strip of Mica ground below it.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-layout.cjs -> at 1000x700 the status bar measured [280,660,720,28], ending at y=688 of 700. At 1280x800 it measured [280,772,1000,28], ending at 800.
- **Fix and guard:** Delete the `.workspace` padding rule from 10-forms.css:470-473 (the `.status-bar` and `.workspace-header` rules beside it are already dead). Guard: assert status-bar bottom == innerHeight at 1280x700.
- **Verifier:** 10-forms.css:470-473 is a top-level `@media (max-height: 720px) { .workspace { padding-bottom: 12px } }`. 06-status.css:4-10 sets `.workspace { padding: 0 }` earlier; 21-native.css:213 restates `.workspace` (rows, background) with no padding; the only later padding reset is 21-native.css:501, inside `@media (max-width: 840px)`. The status bar is the last grid row inside `.workspace` (index.html:123-124, 21-native.css:413-421, transparent background), so at 841px+ wide and 720px tall or less it ends 12px above the window edge, while at taller heights it ends at the edge. The sibling `.status-bar` (min-height 24px, padding-top) and `.workspace-header` (min-height 82px) rules in that block are overridden by 21-native, so this padding is the one stale pre-Mica remnant that still applies. The review's screenshot layout-1000x700.png shows it. It is purely cosmetic: the band is ground-coloured and nothing is clipped.
- **Correction:** None to the location or mechanism. The impact is cosmetic only, a 12px inconsistency in status-line placement that appears only on short windows.

### CSS-10 — In Dark, cards cast a white glow because --shadow-card and --shadow-raised mix --ink

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:23`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:24`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:140`
- **What:** `--shadow-card` and `--shadow-raised` are declared on :root as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) N%, transparent)`. In Dark, `--ink` is #ffffff, so every `.record-card` (13:140) and its hover state (13:142) gets a light halo rather than a shadow. mica-direction.md says dark is designed, not inverted. The theme's own `--shadow` uses black in Dark.
- **Failure:** On a Dark board or gallery, each card's 8-24px blur reads as a faint white bloom around it, and hovering brightens it. Light-mode shadows have turned into glows.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-dark.cjs -> 'dark card shadow=color(srgb 1 1 1 / 0.06) 0px 1px 2px 0px, color(srgb 1 1 1 / 0.04) 0px 8px 24px 0px'.
- **Fix and guard:** Define both shadow tokens per theme in 02-tokens.css, with black in Dark as `--shadow` does, or derive them from a dedicated shadow colour token. Guard: assert in the theme lane that the record card's box-shadow colour channels are below 0.2 in Dark.
- **Verifier:** 13-refinements-pages.css:23-24 declare `--shadow-card` and `--shadow-raised` on plain `:root` as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) N%, transparent)`. Custom-property var() resolves on the declaring element, and `:root[data-theme="dark"]` (02-tokens.css:66) sets `--ink: #ffffff` on that same element, so in Dark both tokens compute to white at 4-7% alpha. They are used only by `.record-card` and its hover (13:140-142). The theme's own `--shadow` (02-tokens.css:76) uses black in Dark, and nothing overrides the card tokens per theme. So Dark cards get a faint white halo where the Light shadow was meant. The effect is real but very faint (4-6% alpha), and some dark UIs use a light lift on purpose, so it is cosmetic.
- **Correction:** None. At 4-7% alpha the halo is subtle, which supports P3 rather than anything higher.

### CSS-11 — Failed summary totals read an undefined --danger-text and fall back to the muted colour

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:219`
- **What:** `.summary-failed { color: var(--danger-text, var(--muted)); }` reads a custom property no slice declares (the static probe found it used once and declared nowhere). chart-kit.ts:74 and record-markup.ts:282 render 'Unavailable' with this class. The fallback makes a failed total the same grey as its context line, while the equivalent failed calculation (`.derived-field[data-state=error]`) uses `--danger`.
- **Failure:** A count or chart total fails to compute. 'Unavailable' renders in muted grey, the same as an empty or context value, so it doesn't read as a failure.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-static.cjs -> '--danger-text 09-surfaces.css:220 (fallback)' under 'used but never declared'. probe-states.cjs -> 'summary-failed=rgb(197, 197, 197) (--danger #f37b72, --muted #c5c5c5)'.
- **Fix and guard:** Use `var(--danger)` directly, or declare `--danger-text` in both themes. Guard: a static lint that fails when a `var(--x)` in the stylesheet names a property no slice declares and no source sets inline. The allow-list covers --status-color, --group-count, --span, --matrix-columns, --outline-depth, --chart-zero and --title-bar-*.
- **Verifier:** 09-surfaces.css:219-222 is `.summary-failed { color: var(--danger-text, var(--muted)); font-size: 1rem }`. `--danger-text` is declared nowhere: grep over src/Nendo.Workbench and docs finds only this one use, and `git log -S` shows it dates from the initial release. So the fallback always applies and a failed total renders in `--muted`. chart-kit.ts:74 and record-markup.ts:282 emit this class for 'Unavailable'. `.summary-value` (09:197) sets no colour, so the failed value is the small muted text that the dangling token was meant to colour. `--danger` exists in both themes (02-tokens.css:70 area). The cause is real: an orphaned token reference. The consequence is only cosmetic, because the word 'Unavailable', the context message and the Retry button still say it failed.
- **Correction:** The impact is cosmetic. The wording 'doesn't read as a failure' overstates it, since the text states the failure and a Retry button follows. The fix is `var(--danger)` or declaring the token.

### CSS-13 — On Structure, field rows overflow their card at viewport widths of about 841-985px and 651-700px

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/08-panels.css:122`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:439`
- **What:** `.field-row` needs at least 644px: `minmax(250px, 1.6fr) repeat(3, minmax(100px, 0.65fr))` plus 54px of gaps and 40px of padding. The two-column fallback switches on the viewport (`max-width: 650px`), but the space available is the viewport minus the 280px rail and 56px of page padding. So between those widths the rows overflow the card's right border, and at 900px the content pane scrolls horizontally.
- **Failure:** A window half-snapped on a 1920px screen at 100% is 960px wide. The Requirement column on Structure pokes 22px past the card's border. At 900px the whole page gains a horizontal scrollbar.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-field.cjs -> '960 card 309-932 row 310-954 row.scrollWidth=644' and '900 ... content scrollW=673 clientW=619'.
- **Fix and guard:** Use `minmax(0, 1.6fr) repeat(3, minmax(0, 0.65fr))` with overflow-wrap, or a container query on `.definition-card` instead of the viewport query. Guard: assert the row's right edge is at or left of the card's at 900, 960 and 680px.
- **Verifier:** 08-panels.css:120-128: `.field-row` is a grid of `minmax(250px, 1.6fr) repeat(3, minmax(100px, 0.65fr))` with 18px gaps and 20px side padding. Its minimum content width is 250+300+54+40 = 644px. The only narrow fallback is `@media (max-width: 650px) { .field-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr } }` (10-forms.css:439), and it keys on the viewport. The space the card gets is the viewport minus the 280px rail (21-native.css:453, 841px+) minus `.studio-page` padding 28px each side (07-studio.css:500-504), or minus only the padding when the rail is the top bar below 841px. So rows overflow between about 841 and 980px and between about 651 and 700px. `.definition-card` (08:56-62) has no overflow rule and no later rule restates `.field-row` columns (grep: 08, 10, 13, 14 only), so the last column pokes past the card border and `.studio-content` (07:142-146, overflow auto) scrolls horizontally. Arithmetic agrees with the review's measurements (960: row 644 wide against a card about 623 wide). Reachable by a half-snap of a 1920px screen at 100% scale or any window in that range; the page stays usable by scrolling or widening.
- **Correction:** None to the arithmetic or ranges. Scale factors of 125% and above shift common half-snap widths below 841px, where the card is wide enough, so this affects the 100% and 841-980px cases most.

### CSS-14 — The 'Ctrl K' key cap in the command box sits off-centre because 21-native switches it to inline-block

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:459`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/16-command-palette.css:97`
- **What:** `kbd` is drawn as an 18px `inline-flex` box with `align-items: center` and `line-height: 1` (16:97-114). The wide-window rule `.palette-trigger kbd { display: inline-block }` (21:459), written to undo the 1100px hide, drops the flex centring. The text then sits at the top of the cap.
- **Failure:** On every window 841px wide or more, 'Ctrl K' in the address row's command box is pinned to the top of its key cap, with 0px above and 6px below. Every other key cap is centred.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-field.cjs -> 'kbd: display=block ... gapTop=0.0 gapBottom=6.0'. The palette foot's inline-flex kbd measured 'gapTop=2.8 gapBottom=3.3'.
- **Fix and guard:** Use `display: inline-flex` at 21-native.css:459. Guard: assert in the browser lane that the top and bottom text gaps in `.palette-trigger kbd` differ by at most 1px.
- **Verifier:** I traced and reproduced it. Base `kbd, .kbd-hint` in 16-command-palette.css:6-24 is `display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 18px; line-height: 1`. 21-native.css:459, inside `@media (min-width: 841px)`, adds `.palette-trigger kbd { display: inline-block }`. It has higher specificity than the base rule and comes later, so it wins. The parent `.palette-trigger` is a flex container, so the kbd is blockified to `block`, the flex centring is lost, and the text sits at the top of the cap. index.html:105 renders it as `<kbd aria-hidden>Ctrl K</kbd>`. No other rule restyles it (grep shows only 16:88 and 21:459). I ran a probe from the verify folder against the reviewer's page, which uses the real concatenated stylesheet, at 1280 wide: computed display=block, box h=18, font-size and line-height 10.5px, text range gapTop=0.0 and gapBottom=6.0. The kbd is visible at 841px and wider (display=block at 841, 'none' at 840). The glyphs sit about 2-3px above centre in an 18px cap. It is a real cosmetic defect on the default wide layout and nothing more, hence P3.
- **Correction:** Line numbers: the base kbd rule is 16-command-palette.css:6-24, not 97-114. The 21-native.css:459 citation is correct. The 1100px hide it undoes is 16-command-palette.css:85-89. The one-word fix (inline-flex) is right.
