### CSS-15 — The @ menu has a fixed 340px max-height, so at short wide windows its top is clipped above the content pane, heading included

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:1062`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:1069`
- **What:** `.chat-mention` opens upward from the composer (`bottom: calc(100% + 6px)`) with `max-height: 340px`. Its ancestors `.studio-content.is-fill`, `.workbench` and `.workspace-layer` all clip (`overflow: hidden`). Nothing caps the height at the space above the composer, so on a short pane part of the menu box sits above the pane top. The menu's own scroll can't bring that part back.
- **Failure:** In a 1024x600 window (wide layout), typing @ with a long list cuts off the top 15px of the menu, including the 'Records' heading. ArrowUp can select an option no one can see.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-chat.cjs (mock from view-agent-chat.ts markup, 14 options) -> '1024x600 pane top=96 menu top=81 h=340 clipped=15px; head visible=false'. At 1280x720 it measured 'clipped=0px'.
- **Fix and guard:** Bound it to the room above, for example `max-height: min(340px, calc(100cqh - …))` using a size container on `.agent-chat`, or have view-agent-chat.ts set the max-height from the composer's offsetTop. Guard: in a 1024x600 lane, assert the menu's top edge is at or below the content pane's top.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed and I reproduced it. 22-agent-chat.css:1062-1076 puts `.chat-mention` at `bottom: calc(100% + 6px)` of `.chat-composer` with a fixed `max-height: 340px`, and nothing bounds it by the room above. view-agent-chat.ts:279 puts it inside the composer form. agent-mention.ts sets no max-height, and its only scrollIntoView is the menu's own `block: nearest` (:127). `.studio-content.is-fill` (22:214), `.workbench` (07:139) and `.workspace-layer` (21:329) all clip with overflow hidden, so the part of the menu above the pane top is invisible and unreachable. contextChoices (agent-context-model.ts:74) offers up to 3+6+6+5+6+4 options, and about 18 with no query, so the 340px cap is routinely reached. I reran the reviewer's mock from the verify folder: 1280x800 menu top 293 and 1280x720 top 201, both clipped 0px. 819x576 is narrow layout with pane top 48, clipped 0px. 1024x600 has pane top 96, menu top 81, clipped 15px, heading not visible. The menu top works out to about viewport-height minus 524px at a wide layout, so clipping starts at roughly 615px of CSS height. It is real but narrow: it needs a wide layout (over 840px) with under about 615px of CSS height, and menu content taller than the room. At 100% scaling the 1024x720 minimum window never reaches it. It appears at 125% scaling or higher with a shrunk window, or on a user-resized short window. It is cosmetic and keyboard-visible only for the top rows, so P3.
- **Correction:** Reachability is narrower than the failure scenario suggests: the 1024x720 physical minimum window (DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:10-11) gives 819x576 CSS at 125%, which is the narrow layout and is not clipped. Clipping needs a wide layout with under about 615 CSS px of height. The mock's dock is slightly shorter than the real one (three chips, an options row, two-part under line), so the real threshold is somewhat higher. 'ArrowUp can select an option no one can see' holds only for the top row or two. Line numbers 1062 and 1069 are right.

### CSS-17 — Agent-page and conversation styles bypass the Mica radius scale and the shared tokens

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design` · also reported as UIK-13

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/11-agent-access.css:56`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:330`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:754`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:1073`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/11-agent-access.css:66`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/11-agent-access.css:150`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/01-file-menu.css:22`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/16-command-palette.css:139`
- **What:** mica-direction.md fixes 4px controls and 8px panels and cards (`--radius-control`, `--radius-panel`). Several surfaces hard-code other radii instead: the agent tabs at 10px (11:56) and the tab icon at 8px (11:110); the chat bubble, permission card, sign-in card and More panel at 10px (22:330, 589, 664, 976); the composer and @ menu at 12px (22:754, 772, 1073); and the attachments and mention icons at 6px (22:810, 1116). `.agent-tab:hover` uses a literal `rgba(20, 23, 28, 0.08)` shadow, invisible in Dark (11:66). Mono stacks are typed out instead of `var(--mono)` (11:150, 08:637, 10:577, 10:639). The modal scrims disagree: the file dialogs use a navy `rgb(10 20 40 / 45%)` (01:22, 12:350), while the command palette uses a canvas wash plus a literal black shadow (16:139 and its ::backdrop).
- **Failure:** The Agent page and the conversation look like a different design system, with rounder 10-12px cards beside 8px cards elsewhere. Opening the command palette washes the window light, while About and Delete darken it. The two kinds of modal read as two applications, which is exactly what the comment at 01-file-menu.css:19-20 warns against.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-static.cjs colour-literal listing (11:66, 01:22, 12:350, 16:139) plus source reading of the radius literals.
- **Fix and guard:** Replace the radius literals with `var(--radius-panel)` and `var(--radius-control)` (or add a documented token if the owner wants 12px for the composer), use `var(--mono)`, use `var(--shadow)` for hover, and pick one scrim token for every ::backdrop. Guard: a stylesheet lint that rejects `border-radius` literals other than 50%, 999px, 2px and 3px outside 02-tokens and 21-native :root, and colour literals outside :root.
- **Verifier:** The facts check out in the code. mica-direction.md says 'Radii are --radius-control (4px) and --radius-panel (8px)'. 21-native.css:17-19 defines the tokens. Hard-coded radii: `.agent-tab` 10px (11-agent-access.css:56); `.chat-you`, `.chat-permission`, `.chat-sign-in` and `.chat-more-panel` 10px (22:330, 589, 664, 976); `.chat-composer` and its textarea 12px (22:754, 772); `.chat-mention` 12px (22:1073); `.chat-attachment` and `.mention-icon` 6px (22:810, 1116). `.agent-tab:hover` uses `rgba(20, 23, 28, 0.08)` (11:66). Cascadia stacks are typed out in 11:150, 08:637, 10:577 and 10:639. The modal scrims disagree: `rgb(10 20 40 / 45%)` at 01:22 and 12:350, against `color-mix(in srgb, var(--canvas) 55%, transparent)` plus a literal black shadow at 16:139-144. AGENTS.md says colours come from the tokens and never from a literal, and the Mica doc has no entry for a 10-12px conversation radius. That makes this an unrecorded divergence rather than a documented trade-off. It is cosmetic consistency drift, P3. The radii came from owner-picked canvases (Agent tab and composer), so how much of this is a defect is partly a design call.
- **Correction:** Overstated or off in places: (a) the tab icon at 8px (11:110) is exactly --radius-panel, so it is on-scale, not a deviation; (b) the comment at 01-file-menu.css:19-20 is about two modal panels disagreeing about their border, not about scrims, so 'exactly what the comment warns against' stretches it; (c) the Dark invisibility of the agent-tab hover shadow is moot because the hover also changes border-colour; (d) the 12px composer, the 10px cards and the lighter palette scrim trace to owner-chosen canvases, so the right fix is to tokenise or record the divergence in mica-direction.md, not necessarily to flatten them to 8px; (e) other colour literals outside :root exist too (07:268, 08:97, 11:358, 11:569-570, 22:1029 and similar), so the proposed lint would need an allow-list. The wording 'a different design system' is an overreach.

### DSH-11 — Native recovery-panel actions never update the window caption, icon, Jump List, placement or tray tooltip after opening, closing or replacing a file

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:104`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:306`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:61`
- **What:** Only DeliverResponse calls App.CurrentWindow.ApplyFileName, with the comment 'Every open, create, close and replacement answers through here'. RunNativeFileActionAsync (Open file or backup, Close file, Restore, Upgrade, Inspect again, Review recovery) changes the session directly and its finally only calls RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync.
- **Failure:** From the recovery panel the person opens B.nendo (or closes A): the title, taskbar and Alt+Tab still read 'Nendo - A.nendo' with A's badge icon, _placementFile stays A (B's window place is saved under A), and the Jump List is not refreshed, until a Workbench response arrives after Restart view.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Call App.CurrentWindow?.ApplyFileName(_session.CurrentFileName, _session.CurrentLook) at the end of RunNativeFileActionAsync (and after the startup open). Guard: a window-level test or journey that closes the file from the recovery panel and asserts the caption is 'Nendo'.
- **Verifier:** App.CurrentWindow.ApplyFileName has exactly one production call site, DeliverResponse in MainPage.xaml.cs:308, which runs only for Workbench bridge responses. The recovery-panel actions (RecoveryOpen_Click, RecoveryClose_Click and the rest, via RunNativeFileActionAsync, MainPage.FileActions.cs:104-136) change the session directly, and their finally block calls only RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync (lines 74-100), which sets panel text and button states. Nothing else calls ApplyFileName (grep), so the caption, icon, Jump List, _placementFile and tray tooltip keep the previous file's values until the Workbench restarts and answers a request.
- **Correction:** It is limited to the interval between a recovery-panel action and the next Restart view, and the finding says so. Cosmetic, so P3.

### DSH-13 — Restoring the window from the tray puts the badge back but not the taskbar progress, so a running agent shows no indicator until its next call

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:391`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:258`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopTaskbarStatus.cs:129`
- **What:** RestoreTaskbarState calls _taskbar.Forget() (which sets _busy = false because the new button has no progress) and RefreshShellState(), which re-applies only the overlay. SetTaskbarBusy is not called, although _fileActionBusy/_agentBusy may still be true.
- **Failure:** An agent is mid-call while the window is hidden; the person restores it from the tray: the badge returns but the indeterminate progress the code adds for exactly this case is missing until the agent's next start/finish.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In RestoreTaskbarState also call _taskbar?.SetBusy(_fileActionBusy \|\| _agentBusy). Guard: a test with a fake taskbar asserting SetBusy(true) after Forget when agent busy.
- **Verifier:** MainWindow.xaml.cs:391-395 RestoreTaskbarState calls _taskbar.Forget() then RefreshShellState(); Forget (DesktopTaskbarStatus.cs:129-133) sets _busy=false and RefreshShellState (MainWindow.xaml.cs:281-287) only calls _taskbar.Apply(badge). Nothing re-sends SetBusy(_fileActionBusy \|\| _agentBusy); SetTaskbarBusy (line 258) runs only from FileActionRunning and AgentWorkChanged. RestoreFromTray (line 416) and the TaskbarCreated callback (line 198) both go through it. The class's own comment says a re-shown window gets a bare button with no progress, so an agent still busy at restore shows no indicator until its next start/finish event. Cosmetic and short-lived.

### DSH-14 — Window default and minimum sizes are physical pixels, so on high-DPI screens the first window is half-size and can shrink below the layout's minimum

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:8`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:41`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:21`
- **What:** DefaultWidth 1600 x DefaultHeight 960 and MinimumWidth 1024 x MinimumHeight 720 are passed to AppWindow.MoveAndResize and OverlappedPresenter.PreferredMinimumWidth/Height, which take physical pixels, against DisplayArea.WorkArea (physical). No RasterizationScale or monitor DPI is applied.
- **Failure:** First launch on a 4K laptop at 200%: the window opens at 800 x 480 effective pixels (below the 600-high narrow-layout threshold, so the wide layout is squeezed), and the minimum lets it shrink to 512 x 360; at 250% it opens at 640 x 384.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Scale the constants by the target display's scale (GetDpiForMonitor for the DisplayArea, or XamlRoot.RasterizationScale after load) before clamping to the work area. Guard: unit-test FitTo/MinimumFor with a scale parameter (2.0 -> 3200 x 1920 clamped).
- **Verifier:** DesktopWindowPolicy.cs:8-11 holds literal 1600x960 and 1024x720; FitTo/MinimumFor (lines 41-55) clamp them against DisplayArea.WorkArea, which is physical pixels, and Apply passes the result to AppWindow.MoveAndResize and OverlappedPresenter.PreferredMinimumWidth/Height (lines 23-27). No scale is applied anywhere. The repo's own MainWindow.TitleBar.cs:111-121 ResizeClient multiplies DIPs by RasterizationScale before calling the same AppWindow/presenter APIs, which treats them as physical. At 200% the default window is 800x480 DIP and the minimum 512x360 DIP. tests/DesktopShellContractTests.cs:15 pins the unscaled 1600x960. No ADR or doc mandates this.
- **Correction:** Reach is narrower than stated: DesktopWindowStore.Load (DesktopWindowStore.cs:31) falls back to the last saved device window, so the unscaled default applies only on a device with no saved window state (first launch). The too-small minimum applies on every launch at high DPI. Polish-level.

### GGV-17 — A graph of one record is drawn off-centre

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:83`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:85`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:508`
- **What:** The Dependency graph sizes the drawing from columns = ceil(sqrt(n*1.5)), which is 2 for one node, so width is 490 while the node occupies x 30..220, and fit() centres the 490-wide box. Work dependencies pads extent to at least 320x200 anchored at the drawing's top-left, so a lone item sits up and left of centre.
- **Failure:** A view with a single record shows it pushed toward the left of the canvas rather than in the middle, which reads as a layout glitch.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-graphs.mjs (800x600, one node) -> dependency-graph: {"canvasCentreX":400,"nodeCentreX":257,...}; work-dependencies: {"canvasCentreX":400,"nodeCentreX":353,"canvasCentreY":384,"nodeCentreY":309}.
- **Fix and guard:** Use min(columns, nodes.length) for the width; in Work dependencies grow the minimum extent symmetrically around the content. Guard: lane asserting a lone node's centre is within a few pixels of the canvas centre.
- **Verifier:** Dependency graph: graph.js:83 gives columns = ceil(sqrt(1*1.5)) = 2 for one node and :85 sets width = max(260, 2*230+30) = 490, while the node sits at x 30..220 (:84); fit() (:25-32) centres the 490-wide box, so the node centre lands about 120 drawing units left of the canvas centre (about 143 px at 800 wide, scale capped at 1.2). The file's own comment at graph.js:35-36 says the graph 'always opens centred in view'. Work dependencies: a lone item is unlinked, goes to the shelf (view.js:395-420) so placed.width is NODE_WIDTH, and view.js:508 pads extent to at least 320x200 anchored at the top-left, so fit() (:608-617) centres the padded box, not the item. The maths matches the reviewer's probe. Cosmetic and only for a one-record view.
- **Correction:** Cosmetic only; a single-record graph has no links to read, so P3 is right. In Work dependencies a lone unlinked item is placed by shelve(), not by the layered layout.

### MAA-16 — The proposal summary leaves out file-scoped custom views (extensionView), so a proposal that adds one is reviewed as adding no screen

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `mcp-authoring-agent`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentProposals.cs:624`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:136`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ProposalModel.cs:96`
- **What:** Summarize builds Surfaces from PreviewApplications plus PreviewOverview. The compiler puts file-scoped extensionView roots in NendoMcpSurfaces.Views, outside the applications, and the proposal context copies only Applications and Overview, so nothing carries views. The comment at 620-623 describes this exact gap for the front page: 'a proposal that adds one is reviewed as adding no screen at all'.
- **Failure:** A proposal adds an extensionView with opensFile true, so the file will open on that view. Its preview summary lists no surface, and the person's Agent view review shows no screen for it, though the diff names the node.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Carry the compiled Views on NendoProposalPreview and list them in Summarize with entityId null. Guard: a preview test adding an extensionView that requires it in preview.surfaces.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. extensionView is a file-scoped root: NendoSemanticCompiler.ComposableSurfaces.cs:29 splits fileScoped roots, :70 CompileFileViews, and :109 returns them only in Compilation.Views. The proposal context copies only boundedPreview.Applications and .Overview (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:136-137; ProposalModel.cs:96 and ProposalWorkspace.cs:61 carry no views), and NendoAgentProposals.Summarize (:624-628) builds Surfaces from applications plus PreviewOverview. A proposal that adds only an extensionView therefore previews with zero surfaces. The Workbench review then shows 'Screens 0' and 'This proposal changes structure and data only. Review it in Studio after accepting.' (view-agent.ts:398,407). The comment at NendoAgentProposals.cs:620-623 names the same gap for the front page as a defect.
- **Correction:** The review is not blind. The semantic diff names the view (Nendo.Engine/SemanticDiff.cs:844, 'Add a custom view as a screen of the file ... runs its package's code'), and PackageChanges lists the package code lines. The gap is the 'what the file would hold' summary and its 'structure and data only' sentence, which is wrong for such a proposal. P3.

- **What:** Where a line ends with a word and the next line starts with <code>, <strong> or <a> (or the element ends a line and text continues on the next), the built HTML has no whitespace between them. Eve'; grep -> 'It refuses <code data-astro-cid-ikooipj4>avg</code></strong>and says why'

The source lines (for example index.astro:246-247, concept.astro:73) do have a newline between the word and the inline element, so the loss is introduced at build time. **P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `site`

Guard: the nojs probe as a lane asserting one visible image per figure and the dark canvas under a dark preference.

So with scripts blocked every figure shows both captures stacked (built dist: index 10 pairs, how-it-works 3, use 3) and a dark-preferring reader gets the light page. tokens.css:5 and Base are not 'always stamps' without JS. It is a cosmetic scrollbar flash lasting about a third of a second, and only with classic scrollbars.
- **Correction:** The overflow lasts about 170-500 ms of the animation, not 'the first 900ms', and the mark is at scale 1.07 only around the 55% keyframe. The range is roughly 861px to 1150px, not just 1024. Overlay-scrollbar platforms show no visible bar.

### UIT-11 — Every Help article starts with a stray '/' after its location line

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `ui-live-studio`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-help.ts:29`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/06-status.css:154`
- **What:** The article header uses `<p class="location">`. The global `.location::after { content: "/" }` rule, meant for the old workspace breadcrumb, applies to it, while 21-native.css only restyles `.workspace-identity .location`.
- **Failure:** Every Help topic shows 'About this app · Board glance /' or 'Getting started /' above its title, a separator with nothing after it, in both themes and at every width.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: p02-tour.mjs -> t-help-1024-dark.png and t-help-800-light.png show "About this app · Board glance /"
- **Fix and guard:** Give the article line its own class (for example help-location), or scope the ::after rule to .workspace-identity. Guard: a computed-style assertion in the help gate that getComputedStyle(article .location, '::after').content is 'none'.
- **Verifier:** The mechanics are as claimed. view-proposal.ts:36 sets state.proposal = null and returns to proposalReturnView without proposal.reject. The host keeps the proposal and its clone: PrepareProposalAsync adds it to _proposals (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:56) with RetainUntilExplicitCleanup (ProposalWorkspace.cs:76), and the Outcomes.cs:51 cleanup spares every key in _proposals, so it lingers until the file closes or reopens (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:49/403); there is no cap. No Studio list reaches Workbench-prepared proposals (the Agent page lists NendoAgentProposals only). navigation-actions.ts:120 judges the trail place by state.proposal?.proposalId alone, so trail Back says 'no longer waiting'. Low impact: the wording is accurate from the person's side, since the review is dismissed and unreachable; the real defect is an un-rejected clone left behind, against ADR-0007's 'explicit cleanup' model, with re-preparing leaving another clone.
- **Correction:** The sentence is not the main defect; the substantive issue is that in-page Back leaves a validated proposal and a full-file clone in the host. The simplest fix is to reject on Back (or say 'discarded'), not to re-open it. Severity stays P3: no data loss, bounded by file close, one clone per Preview.

### WCS-24 — 'Restart query' disappears on the next redraw while the sentence that names it is put back

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-core-state`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/actions.ts:166`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/shell.ts:98`
- **What:** handlePageFailure writes 'The file changed. These results are from the earlier query. Restart to see the current records.' through showError (retained in lastOutcome) and appends a 'Restart query' button to the slot by hand. restoreOutcome redraws only the sentence after any redraw, without the button.
- **Failure:** On Data, paging fails with stale-cursor; an agent write then redraws the page; the sentence still tells the person to restart, but the button is gone (and the redraw already shows current records).
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Carry the restart as the outcome's action (OutcomeNotice.action) so restoreOutcome redraws it, and drop the notice when a refresh has replaced the results. Guard: unit test that rerender after handlePageFailure still shows #restart-record-query or no stale sentence.
- **Verifier:** Traced. handlePageFailure (actions.ts:163-183) on a stale-cursor in the data view calls showError(...), which stores lastOutcome as { view, message, tone } with no action (shell.ts:527-535), then appends the 'Restart query' button into the live slot by hand (actions.ts:167-181). Any later rerender() calls the renderer and then restoreOutcome (shell.ts:77-106). The view's rebuilt markup has a hidden .message-slot (view-data.ts:353,391), and drawOutcome redraws only the sentence plus outcome.action/refresh buttons. Neither exists for this notice, so the button is gone while the sentence stays. The redraw is likely, not hypothetical. loadRecordWindow throws stale-cursor because the session is behind the file (reads.ts:44-46), so the follow chase (main.ts:708-754) is already due to redraw the screen (rerender at main.ts:715), and that redraw also reloads the first page of current records. The only other thing that clears the sentence is the person's next press outside the slot (shell.ts:545-551). No test covers #restart-record-query (grep). Cosmetic and short-lived, so P3.
- **Correction:** Fix by routing the button through OutcomeNotice.action. That is how the Show in folder button survives redraws (main.ts:736-742, shell.ts:114-123). If the notice stays, it should also be dropped once a refresh has replaced the results, since the sentence is then false.

### WDV-19 — Proposal preview draws a Boolean matrix as an empty grid and shows Boolean values as true/false

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-preview.ts:450`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-preview.ts:29`
- **What:** matrixMarkup takes its lanes from rowField.options and columnField.options only, so a Boolean axis, which has no options, yields no rows or columns. The live matrix uses axisOptions, which gives ['false','true'], and also applies reachableGroups, which the preview skips. text() prints booleans as 'true' and 'false', where every live screen shows Yes and No.
- **Failure:** A reviewer previews a proposal adding 'Tasks by Urgent x Status' and sees a corner with no cells, so cannot judge the screen they are asked to accept. Card values read 'true' and 'false'.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Build the preview's lanes with matrixViewOf (axisOptions plus reachableGroups) and label them with groupLabel; format booleans as Yes and No in text(). Guard: a surface-preview test with a Boolean axis asserting two lanes; falsify by restoring options-only lanes.
- **Verifier:** The contract allows a Boolean matrix axis (semantic-surfaces.md:896) and the live view handles it via axisOptions, which supplies ['false','true'] only when a field has no options (surface-model.ts:260-265). surface-preview.ts:450-451 instead reads rowField.options / columnField.options directly, and a Boolean field carries none (charts.ts:415 special-cases Booleans for the same reason), so the header and body at :455-465 are empty and the reviewer sees a bare corner. The preview also skips reachableGroups (surface-model.ts:209), and text() (surface-preview.ts:29) stringifies a Boolean as 'true'/'false' where live screens show Yes/No (format.ts:26). No preview test covers a Boolean axis (grids.test.mjs:36 covers only matrixViewOf). The proposal preview is the screen a person reviews before accepting, so this is a real product surface, but limited to Boolean axes and cosmetic labels.

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:106`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/13-refinements-pages.css:122`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/09-surfaces.css:851`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/14-refinements-controls.css:934`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-markup.ts:86`
- **What:** recordCardMarkup puts the heading in <strong>, the values in .card-values spans and choice values in .card-chip. .record-card > strong and .card-values > span set neither overflow-wrap nor min-width, and .card-chip sets white-space: nowrap. .related-rows .related-row and .drill-pill set neither. overflow-wrap: anywhere appears only on .matrix-cell .record-card strong (09-surfaces.css:1157) and .preview-content .record-card (12-agent-activity.css:366): the matrix and the proposal preview were fixed, and the board, the gallery, related rows and the pill were not.

Let .card-chip truncate (max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis) with the full value in its title. Guard: a stylesheet test such as css-custom-properties.test.mjs asserting that these selectors carry overflow-wrap or min-width, plus a measured layout case with a long value asserting that card scrollWidth <= clientWidth.

I rebuilt a three-column board from the real stylesheets in headless Edge with a 240-character unbroken URL as title and value: the card clientWidth is 253px and scrollWidth 1730px, the <strong> is 1718px wide and ends at x=1760 while the card ends at 284 and the column at 297, and card and column both compute overflow visible, so the text spills across the neighbouring columns. The related-row and pill rules have the same missing properties. Layout damage only, no data effect, and the person can open the record to read it, so P3 rather than P2.
- **Correction:** I measured the board card only. The related-row and drill-pill widths were not re-measured, though their rules (09-surfaces.css:851-864, 14-refinements-controls.css:934-945) carry no wrapping either.

### WMX-16 — First-letter glyphs split surrogate pairs, drawing a broken character for names that start with an emoji or an astral-plane letter

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-structure.ts:35`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/type-icons.ts:72`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/type-icons.ts:73`
- **What:** Structure's entity icon is displayName.slice(0, 1).toUpperCase(), and tileLetters indexes words[0][0] and words[1][0]. Both work in UTF-16 code units, so they cut a surrogate pair in half.
- **Failure:** A record type named '🚀 Launches' shows a replacement character in Structure's title tile. A type named '𠮷野家 orders' shows a broken first letter in the navigation tile, the tab and the address.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-glyph.mjs -> the view-structure expression on "🚀 Launches" gives "\ud83d" (isWellFormed false); tileLetters("𠮷野家 orders") gives "\ud842O" (isWellFormed false).
- **Fix and guard:** Take whole code points or graphemes (Array.from(word)[0], or Intl.Segmenter) and skip characters that are not letters. Guard: a type-icons test asserting that tileLetters output and the Structure initial are well-formed for emoji-led and astral-plane names.
- **Verifier:** Reproduced with node: view-structure.ts:35 uses entity.displayName.slice(0, 1).toUpperCase(); for '🚀 Launches' that yields '\ud83d' (isWellFormed false). Display names allow any characters up to 200 UTF-16 units (SqliteNendoStore.Evolution.cs:25), so an emoji-led record type name is reachable. type-icons.ts:72 indexes words[0][0] and words[1][0]; for '𠮷野家 orders' tileLetters returns '\ud842O' (isWellFormed false). A single-word astral name works only by accident because [1] is the low surrogate. Cosmetic: one broken glyph in a tile.
- **Correction:** The emoji example only hurts Structure's title tile. In tileLetters the split regex /[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u treats an emoji as a separator, so '🚀 Launches' gives 'La' there (well-formed). tileLetters breaks only for names whose first word starts with an astral-plane letter (e.g. CJK Extension B) followed by a second word, which is rare.

### WSP-09 — The Studio filter status reads "[object Object]" for a number filter, and stored IDs for choice and reference filters

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/studio-columns.ts:116`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-data.ts:489`
- **What:** view-data builds filter values with parseScalar, which returns {$nendoNumber: '5'} for Integer and Decimal. queryStatusText prints String(filter.value).
- **Failure:** Filtering Count by "is greater than 5" shows "Only where Count is greater than [object Object] · across every record of this type". A choice filter shows the option's stored ID, and a reference filter shows a record ID (Studio contract section 2: no foreign-key values).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-pure.mjs (bundles src/studio-columns.ts and src/scalars.ts in memory) -> `status for Count > 5 -> Only where Count is greater than [object Object] · across every record of this type`
- **Fix and guard:** Format values with exactNumberText for numbers, choiceDisplay for choices and the reference label where it is known. Guard: a studio-columns.test.mjs case with a $nendoNumber value asserting "greater than 5".
- **Verifier:** view-data.ts:488-489 builds the filter value with parseScalar(storageLabel(kind), text); scalars.ts:17-29 returns {$nendoNumber: ...} for Integer and Decimal. studio-columns.ts:116 then prints String(filter.value), which is "[object Object]" for that object, and view-data.ts:464 puts the result in the query status line. The only existing test (studio-columns.test.mjs:69-77) uses a text filter, so nothing catches it. Any numeric field filtered with a comparison reaches this on the common Studio Data screen. Cosmetic status text only; the query itself is sent correctly.
- **Correction:** Only the number case is a real defect. For a choice or reference field the Value box is free text (view-data.ts:462) and parseScalar returns the text as typed, so the status just echoes what the person typed (the stored ID); that part of the finding is not a bug in the status formatter.

### WXS-07 — A view parked during the review of its own proposal can still draw Nendo's menu at the window's top-left corner over the review, and can move the person out of the review

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:432`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:202`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-ui.ts:102`
- **What:** While a view's own proposal is reviewed, releaseViewFrames keeps the view running in the hidden `#view-frame-parking` container (heldForReview). showMenuFor refuses only when `!frame.isConnected` or a dialog is open, and a parked frame is connected. Its getBoundingClientRect is all zeros because an ancestor has display:none, so the point clamps to (0,0). showViewMenu then draws the menu fixed at the window's top-left (clamped to 8 px) and focuses its first item. ui.openRecord, ui.openScreen and ui.openStudio check only actionInFlight and the dirty form, so a parked view can also replace `state.view` while the person reads the review.
- **Failure:** A view calls proposals.prepare and the review opens over it. The view, still running, then calls ui.showMenu from a timer or a stale contextmenu handler. A menu in Nendo's style with the view's labels appears over the title band at the top-left of the review and takes focus, so Enter or Space picks its first item. Or the view calls ui.openScreen, and the review the person was reading disappears.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Treat a parked or held mount as not on screen. In showMenuFor, require `mount.placeholder?.isConnected` and a frame outside the parking lot, and answer null otherwise. Have the navigation methods refuse with `not-allowed` while `heldForReview.has(mount.key)` and state.view is 'proposal'. Guard: a view-frames test that parks a mount for review and asserts that showMenu answers null and draws no `.view-menu`, and that ui.openScreen leaves state.view at 'proposal'.
- **Verifier:** Traced: releaseViewFrames (view-frames.ts:~185-192) keeps a mount in heldForReview alive while state.view==='proposal', and parkViewFrames moves its frame into the hidden #view-frame-parking container (hidden=true, so display:none) where it stays connected and running; the broker keeps its connection (mounts() lists any mount with a frame, view-frames.ts:118/extension-broker.ts:885). showMenuFor (view-frames.ts:430-441) refuses only on !frame.isConnected or an open dialog, so a parked frame passes; getBoundingClientRect under a display:none ancestor is all zeros, so x=y=0, and showViewMenu (view-menu.ts:64-105) draws a fixed menu at the clamped top-left and focuses its first item. ui.openScreen/openRecord/openStudio check only actionInFlight and the dirty form (extension-ui.ts:24-29), so a parked view can also replace state.view and remove the review the person is reading. It needs a buggy or hostile view that keeps calling after proposals.prepare; the menu items only send a command back to the view and cannot accept the proposal, so impact is confusion and focus theft, hence P3. Not rendered in a real WebView2.
- **Correction:** Menu selection only returns an id to the view (it cannot accept or reject the proposal), and the menu is dismissed by Escape, Tab, a press elsewhere, blur, scroll or resize (view-menu.ts:~100-135), so the harm is limited to a spurious menu and, via ui.openScreen, losing the review screen (the proposal remains and proposals.open can reopen it). Source-traced only.

### WXS-17 — When views come on while the page is held, a record panel starts its frame beside the stale 'Custom views are off' notice

**P3** · ui · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:256`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frames.ts:520`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-settings.ts:23`
- **What:** showNotice sets `stage.innerHTML` to the notice and adds `is-notice` to the stage. In wireViewFrames the 'run' branch never clears either: it creates the mount, sets the height and starts or adopts the frame, and start() only prepends the iframe. A normal render draws a fresh placeholder, but refreshExtensionSettings' held path (record form dirty, menu open or recent interaction) re-wires the existing DOM with park, wire and release.
- **Failure:** A person is typing in a record form whose page has a custom-view panel showing 'Custom views are off on this device. Turn them on under Studio > Surfaces > Custom views.' In another Nendo window they turn Run custom views on. The host's extensionSettingsChanged reaches this window, which takes the held path. The panel's frame starts at the top of a 360 px stage that still holds the off notice and its Open Custom views button, styled as a centred notice grid.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In wireViewFrames' run branch, when the stage has `is-notice`, remove the class and the notice children before adopting or starting the frame. Guard: a view-frames test that wires a placeholder with views off, switches the session to run and wires again without redrawing, asserting that no `.view-notice` remains and the stage has no `is-notice`.
- **Verifier:** Traced in source. view-frames.ts:518-521 showNotice adds 'is-notice' to the stage and replaces its innerHTML. The 'run' path in wireViewFrames (:256-278) never removes the class or the notice children, and start() (:464-484) only does stage.prepend(frame). A normal render draws a fresh placeholder, but extension-settings.ts:23-30 takes the held path when holdingThePage() is true (draft-guard.ts:47-49: dirty record form, retained draft or interaction in progress). That path only re-runs parkViewFrames, wireViewFrames and releaseViewFrames on the same DOM. extensionSettingsChanged reaches it through host-desktop.ts:379 and main.ts:756. 09-surfaces.css:726-733 styles the stage as a notice grid, so the frame lands beside the stale notice. The effect is cosmetic and clears on the next full render once the form is saved or closed. It needs a second window or a toggle from another place, plus a dirty form.

### DSH-12 — Recovery panel and native actions read the full record snapshot on the UI thread

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:78`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:112`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:236`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:642`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:426`
- **What:** ReadViewCoreAsync uses GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync only when _boundedReadProjection is set, which only HandleAsync and startup do. RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync (from ShowRecovery and after every recovery action), RunNativeFileActionAsync's binding read, BackupNativeFileAsync/CopyNativeFileAsync/SaveNativeDiagnosticsAsync call _session.GetViewAsync() unbound, i.e. GetSnapshotAsync with every record, to read a file name, capabilities or the entity count.
- **Failure:** The renderer dies on a large healthy file (often from memory pressure); ShowRecovery immediately materialises every record on the UI thread to set six button states, and each backup/diagnostics click from the panel does it again.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Wrap the recovery panel's reads in _session.BindReadProjection(true) (as InitializeStartupSessionAsync does). Guard: a controller test that GetViewAsync under the recovery helper returns Records.Count == 0 for a file with records.
- **Verifier:** ShowRecovery (MainPage.xaml.cs:416, on the UI thread) calls RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync, which awaits _session.GetViewAsync() with no BindReadProjection (MainPage.FileActions.cs:78). _boundedReadProjection is an AsyncLocal that defaults to false (DesktopRequestBinding.cs:8), so ReadViewCoreAsync takes GetSnapshotAsync (DesktopSessionController.cs:642-644), which reads every record via SqliteNendoStore.GetSessionSnapshotAsync with includeRecords true (SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:11, 36). The Engine has no Task.Run and the SQLite async calls complete synchronously, so this runs on the UI thread. The panel only uses Entities.Count, capabilities and findings (DesktopRecoveryPresentation.Describe and RefreshNativeRecoveryAsync), which the definition snapshot also carries (ReadQueries.cs:17, includeRecords false). The same unbound read happens in RunNativeFileActionAsync (line 112) and in Backup, Copy and Diagnostics (lines 236, 246, 321). InitializeStartupSessionAsync (MainPage.xaml.cs:464) already binds the bounded projection for this reason.
- **Correction:** The cost scales with record count and was not measured, so this is a modest performance issue, P3. A read-only session returns a cached snapshot (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:197), so only writable sessions pay each time.

### DSH-17 — DescribeShellState, documented as I/O-free for window procedures, reads behaviour-grants.json and can block on a lock held across a 5 s cross-process mutex wait; it runs after every bridge response

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionSignals.cs:92`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.cs:107`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.cs:148`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:88`
- **What:** DescribeShellState says 'no snapshot, no I/O, no await' but reads coordinator.BehaviourTrust, which calls DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.IsGranted -> lock(_sync){ Read() } -> ReadBytes + JSON parse of up to 256 KB. Change() holds the same _sync while DesktopDeviceStateLock.EnterRequired waits up to 5 s and writes through to disk; the Unattended consent delegate calls Approve on the agent thread. DeliverResponse -> ApplyFileName -> RefreshShellState calls DescribeShellState on the UI thread after every response, including frequent window.setTitleBarControls replies.
- **Failure:** For a file with automatic actions every bridge response costs a disk read and parse on the UI thread; while another Nendo process holds the grants mutex and this process's agent is approving at Unattended, the tray menu, tooltip refresh and response delivery block for seconds.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Cache the trust answer per file session (refresh it on approve/revoke, definition change and the store's revocation generation) and read the cache in DescribeShellState; never take _sync from the UI thread. Guard: a test that DescribeShellState returns while another thread holds the store's lock.
- **Verifier:** Traced: DeliverResponse (MainPage.xaml.cs:308) -> MainWindow.ApplyFileName (xaml.cs:88) -> RefreshShellState -> DescribeShellState (DesktopSessionSignals.cs:84-123). It reads coordinator.BehaviourTrust, which for a file with a behaviour requirement calls _behaviourAuthority.IsGranted (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:147-148), i.e. DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.IsGranted (lines 107-115): lock(_sync){ Read() } with a file read and JSON parse every time. Change() (lines 142-163) holds the same _sync across DesktopDeviceStateLock.EnterRequired, which waits up to 5 s (DesktopDeviceStateLock.cs:25). So the 'no snapshot, no I/O, no await' summary at DesktopSessionSignals.cs:75-83 is false for files with automatic actions, and DescribeTray and Notify take the same path on the UI thread.
- **Correction:** Impact is overstated. Only files with automatic actions pay; the read is a small local file (cap 256 KB). A multi-second UI stall needs another Nendo process to hold the grants mutex that long, while holds are normally one short write. The per-check read is deliberate (DesktopBehaviourGrantStore.cs:55-57), so the defect is the UI-thread caller and the false comment, not the store. No deadlock cycle exists.

### DSH-22 — Opening a recent file fully inspects it twice before the open, the first time only to learn its path

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:129`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileHistory.cs:111`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.FileActions.cs:183`
- **What:** OpenRecentNativeFileAsync calls ResolveRecentPathAsync for the handoff check, which calls DesktopFileHistory.ResolveAsync -> NendoWriteCoordinator.ObserveAsync (full inspection: integrity, classification, digest) and keeps only .Path; AssessRecentAsync then calls ResolveAsync again, observing the file a second time.
- **Failure:** Opening a large file from the recent list pays two full inspections (seconds each on a big file) before the dialog appears; the startup-timing work elsewhere shows each inspection is the dominant open cost.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Give DesktopFileHistory a path-only lookup for the handoff check (no observation), keeping the observing ResolveAsync for the assessment. Guard: a test counting ObserveAsync calls per recent open (expect one).
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. The Workbench's open-recent action reaches OpenRecentNativeFileAsync (MainPage.FileActions.cs:48, 181-191). It first calls _session.ResolveRecentPathAsync (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:129-136), which calls DesktopFileHistory.ResolveAsync (DesktopFileHistory.cs:106-115) -> NendoWriteCoordinator.ObserveAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:16-31), a full SqliteNendoStore.InspectAsync (PRAGMA integrity_check at SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:188, plus ReadContentDigestAsync at :571), and keeps only .Path. It then calls AssessRecentAsync (DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:138-148), which calls ResolveAsync again, repeating the same observation before the dialog. ObserveAsync is static with no cache, and nothing in the code or docs presents the double observation as a deliberate trade-off. Impact is time on every recent-file open, proportional to file size (the first observation is outside the gate but still on the path to the dialog); a small file costs little, hence P3.
- **Correction:** Seconds per inspection on a big file is an estimate not shown in code; the claim that inspection dominates open cost is consistent with DesktopFileLifecycle.cs:54-61 ('a full inspection') and IdentifyAsync's doc (Open.cs:33-37). Note OpenAssessedAsync -> the coordinator open later re-checks the pinned observation too, so the total is more than two touches of the file, but the two before the dialog are the avoidable ones.

### EBH-21 — Event derivation charges the related-row ceiling for every touched record, including record types no trigger watches

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:44`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:412`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourChain.cs:256`
- **What:** Once a file has any trigger, RunAsync derives an event for every record the mutation names; DeriveAsync calls ReadRecordAsync, which spends one related-row scan of the chain's 256, whether or not any trigger subscribes to that record type.
- **Failure:** A file has one trigger on project. An agent's change set mutation creates 300 contact records (no trigger on contact): the preview is refused with 'This calculation reached the related record limit for a single save. Simplify the formula or narrow what it reads.' A 200-write batch leaves 56 rows for the project trigger's Sum over 60 tasks and is refused too.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Skip records of types no trigger subscribes to before reading them, and charge initial event derivation to work rather than the related-row ceiling. Guard: write-route test creating RelatedRows+1 untriggered records in a file with a trigger elsewhere.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourChain.cs:125-149 captures every record any operation touches once the file has a behaviour table (no filter by trigger subscription); ExecuteBehaviourChainAsync only gates on 'any trigger' (line 256); BehaviourPlanner.RunAsync (line 44) calls DeriveAsync for every captured key, and DeriveAsync -> ReadRecordAsync (line 412-423) calls context.Budget.SpendScan() for any record type that has stored fields, watched or not. The only exemption is a type with no stored fields, so the charge against the 256 related-row ceiling is real and shared with later aggregate reads. Nothing in the contract (Limits table, line 980) requires charging untriggered types. The effect is small: it only matters when a single mutation touches a lot of records.
- **Correction:** The headline example (300 contact records) cannot occur: one mutation is bounded by MaximumRecordWrites = 200 (NendoApplicationService.Batch.cs:58, 84-87) and OperationsPerChangeSet = 128 (SemanticVocabulary.cs:985); create_records is capped at 50. The reachable case is a batch of up to 200 writes, such as 199 untriggered contact writes plus one task edit whose trigger sums 60 tasks (56 rows left), which is then refused. A workaround is to split the batch. Priority stays P3.

### ESC-09 — An open that confirms an observation scans the file's integrity three times on one connection, and the counter records only one of the scans

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `engine-storage-core`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:759`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Authority.cs:36`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:187`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:245`
- **What:** OpenAsync runs ValidateAsync, which runs PRAGMA quick_check over the whole file. The first GetAuthoritySnapshotAsync runs ReadAuthoritySnapshotAsync, which calls GetStorageHealthAsync with verifyIntegrity true. That runs PRAGMA integrity_check and throws unless it is ok. The confirming (W-026) open path then calls PassesIntegrityCheckAsync, a third full scan on the same connection with no commit in between. PassesIntegrityCheckAsync bypasses GetStorageHealthAsync, so IntegrityCheckCount (ReadDiagnostics.IntegrityChecks) records one scan where three ran.
- **Failure:** Opening a large file from the recent list, the path built to be the cheap open, pays for quick_check plus two integrity_checks. The instrumentation that tests and benchmarks rely on hides the extra scans.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python probe_integrity_cost.py (synthetic 107,663,360-byte DELETE-mode file, warm cache) -> "PRAGMA quick_check: ok in 0.15 s" / "PRAGMA integrity_check: ok in 0.20 s" / "PRAGMA integrity_check: ok in 0.21 s"
- **Fix and guard:** Drop the confirming-path PassesIntegrityCheckAsync, because the cold authority read has just run integrity_check on this connection and refused anything but ok. Drop or skip ValidateAsync's quick_check when an authority read will follow. If a scan is kept, route it through GetStorageHealthAsync so it is counted. Guard: an AuthorityCacheTests case asserting ReadDiagnostics.IntegrityChecks == 1 after an observed open, with PassesIntegrityCheckAsync incrementing the counter.
- **Verifier:** Traced the confirming open statically. SqliteNendoStore.OpenAsync -> ValidateAsync runs PRAGMA quick_check (SqliteNendoStore.cs:70/89, :760). NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:242 -> GetAuthoritySnapshotAsync -> ReadAuthoritySnapshotAsync (cache is null, so a cold read) -> GetStorageHealthAsync with verifyIntegrity defaulting to true (Authority.cs:36, Read.cs:86-101) runs integrity_check and throws unless 'ok' (Authority.cs:37-38). Open.cs:245 then runs PassesIntegrityCheckAsync (Inspection.cs:187-189), a third full scan with no commit in between, and it skips IntegrityCheckCount (Read.cs:100), so the counter reads 1 where 2 integrity_checks ran. The redundancy is real, but small: the file is capped at 256 MiB (Inspection.cs:39), the reviewer's probe measured about 0.2 s per scan on 107 MB, and the repeats run on a warm cache. W-026 (commit c286522) added the explicit check without noting the authority read already does it.
- **Correction:** Not a correctness issue, and the contract does list the explicit check (reads-and-authority.md:104-106 'SQLite's integrity_check runs on the writable connection'), so the fix must also reword that paragraph to say the cold authority read supplies it; nothing in ObservedOpenTests pins the extra scan. The fix 'drop ValidateAsync's quick_check' is less safe than dropping PassesIntegrityCheckAsync, because ValidateAsync also guards the non-observed and inspection stores (Inspection.cs:387) where no authority read follows. Treat it as a perf and maintainability nit.

### ESQ-04 — Every command button reads and projects every record in the file just to find the command

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `engine-service-queries` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.cs:450`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.cs:205`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:41`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:264`
- **What:** ExecuteCommandAsync calls CompileSemanticUiAsync, which calls _coordinator.GetSnapshotAsync. That is GetSessionSnapshotAsync with includeRecords: true. ReadRecordsAsync then reads every row of every record type, labels references, and runs calculations over all of them, and ProjectRecords projects them. FindComposableCommand and ExecuteComposableCommandAsync use only plan.Surfaces and plan.Entity.Fields, which are definition data. A definition-only compile, CompileSemanticDefinitionAsync, already exists. AuthorityCacheTests:75 states the rule 'Ordinary reads and writes must not run full projections'.
- **Failure:** In a planner-sized file (thousands of records with calculated fields), each click on a record command such as 'Mark done' does a full-file read plus calculations before writing one record. This holds in the Workbench and through nendo.data.execute_command. Latency grows with the whole file rather than the record, and FullRecordReadCount rises by one per click.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Find the command with CompileSemanticDefinitionAsync, or a cached definition compile, instead of CompileSemanticUiAsync. Guard: an AuthorityCacheTests-style test asserting that coordinator.ReadDiagnostics.FullRecordReads is unchanged across ExecuteCommandAsync.
- **Verifier:** Traced. ExecuteCommandAsync (NendoApplicationService.cs:450) calls CompileSemanticUiAsync, which calls _coordinator.GetSnapshotAsync (line 205). That reaches store.GetSessionSnapshotAsync with includeRecords true (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:202, SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:41,264-300), which increments FullRecordReadCount, reads every row of every type, labels references and runs calculations. ProjectRecords then projects them. FindComposableCommand and ExecuteComposableCommandAsync (lines 475-526) use only plan.Surfaces and plan.Entity.Fields, which come from the cached definition compile (the compile runs on 'snapshot with { Records = [] }', lines 222-232). Record-level diagnostics are warnings, so IsValid cannot differ. CompileSemanticDefinitionAsync (line 209) already exists, and DesktopSessionController.cs:373-377 uses it for a definition-only compile. So the full read per command is avoidable and AuthorityCacheTests.cs:75 states the opposite rule for ordinary reads. This is only an efficiency defect: the result is identical, nothing is measured, and a file's Workbench refresh already reads fully.
- **Correction:** Downgrade P2 to P3. It is wasted work and not wrong behaviour; no latency was measured, and the cost grows with file size only. The fix is as proposed (definition-only compile for the lookup).

### EXT-12 — Each "Read the whole file" window reopens and quick_checks the whole proposal clone while holding the write gate

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Extensions.cs:43`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Extensions.cs:54`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:759`
- **What:** ReadProposalPackageFileAsync takes `_gate` and then calls SqliteNendoStore.OpenAsync(clonePath) for every window of at most 256 KiB. OpenAsync re-applies the connection profile and runs ValidateAsync, which includes `PRAGMA quick_check` over the entire clone, and then reads the whole file's bytes to return one slice.
- **Failure:** A reviewer opens Read the whole file on a 4 MiB bundle in a large file. That is 16 windows, each a full open, quick_check and whole-file read of the clone. All writes (record saves, view writes) wait behind the gate for the duration.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Read the file from the clone once per (proposal, digest, path) and cache the bytes, or keep a read-only clone store open for the proposal's lifetime without re-validating. Do the clone I/O outside `_gate` once the proposal state and digest are checked. Guard: a test that counts clone opens across the windows of a 4 MiB file and expects 1.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. package-file-reader.ts:28-37 loops one proposal.readPackageFile request per 256 KiB window. Each goes through WorkbenchProtocol.cs:407 -> DesktopSessionController.cs:428-431 (QueryAsync, which holds the Desktop request gate) -> NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadProposalPackageFileAsync (Extensions.cs:43-62), which holds _gate. It then calls SqliteNendoStore.OpenAsync(clonePath) (SqliteNendoStore.cs:80-97), which applies the profile and runs ValidateAsync, whose PRAGMA quick_check scans the whole clone (about line 759). ReadExtensionFileAsync then loads the file's whole blob to return one slice. Nothing is cached across windows, so a file of N windows pays N full opens and quick_checks under the gates. Impact is bounded: it only happens when a person asks to read a file, most package files fit in one or two windows, and the gate is released between windows. The cost scales with clone size and was not measured. It is a performance inefficiency with a modest stall, not a correctness problem.
- **Correction:** Add that the Desktop request gate (QueryAsync) is held as well as the coordinator _gate, so every Workbench request waits during each window, not only writes. Only files of 3.75 MiB or more reach 16 windows. The cost per window was not measured; I read the quick_check cost from the code, not from a timing.
