### MHS-08 — The oversized-body envelope scan runs outside the request gate and re-parses its carry, so its cost is quadratic in the length of one token

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `mcp-host-security`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:62`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:358`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:370`
- **What:** A request whose Content-Length is between 256 KiB and 16 MiB is scanned before gate.EnterAsync, so neither the 16-in-flight bound nor the timeout applies. EnvelopeScanner.Feed builds `[.. _carry, .. piece]` and re-reads it from the start whenever a token spans pieces, so a long string value before the id is copied and rescanned on every 16 KiB piece. The class comment says only a cut token is carried, but here the cut token is the whole body.
- **Failure:** A client sends a 15 MiB string value ahead of its id. That one request costs about 3.5 s of CPU and up to roughly 30 MiB of churn before its 413. Twenty such requests in parallel are not throttled by the gate, which exists to bound exactly this, and they starve the host's other requests.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-envelope.ps1 (EnvelopeScanner.ScanAsync by reflection, a string of N MiB before the id) -> ` 1 MiB: 50 ms`, ` 4 MiB: 343 ms`, ` 8 MiB: 1.549 ms`, `15 MiB: 3.562 ms`.
- **Fix and guard:** Stop carrying a string token once it passes a small bound: track that the reader is inside a string, discard its bytes and resume after the closing quote. Alternatively, scan only the first and last few KiB. Take a gate place before scanning. Guard: a unit test asserting that a 15 MiB string before the id scans in under 200 ms, and a perimeter test asserting that oversized requests count against requestsInFlight.
- **Verifier:** Traced and reproduced. The oversized-Content-Length scan (NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:62-69) runs before gate.EnterAsync (line 76), so neither the in-flight bound nor the timeout applies. EnvelopeScanner.Feed (355-371) rebuilds '[.. _carry, .. piece]' and re-parses from the start of a cut token on every 16 KiB piece, so one long string value before the id costs quadratic time; Kestrel sets no tighter body limit here (only AddServerHeader and Listen at NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:367-376). I re-ran the reviewer's probe-envelope.ps1 against the HEAD DLL copy: 1 MiB 300 ms, 4 MiB 1,888 ms, 8 MiB 8,245 ms, 15 MiB 31,304 ms, strongly superlinear. It is reachable only from a loopback client that passed the Host and Origin checks, with a body over 256 KiB that puts the id after a huge token (the comment at lines 14-18 acknowledges clients may write the id last); mainstream clients write id first and finish in the first piece. ADR-0009:273-285 accepts that local processes can connect, so this is a gate-bypass and CPU hardening gap, not a boundary breach.
- **Correction:** Timings on my re-run were larger than the reviewer's (31 s for 15 MiB versus 3.6 s), so the cost claim is conservative, though machine load affects it. 'About 30 MiB of churn' is the peak array size; total allocation churn is several GB. Priority P3 stands.

<a id="mtd-17"></a>

### MTD-17 — Every resource and tool result escapes non-ASCII text as \uXXXX, inflating non-English files several-fold

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpContracts.cs:35`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpResources.cs:470`
- **What:** NendoMcpJson.CreateOptions builds JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web) without an Encoder, so the default JavaScriptEncoder escapes every character outside Basic Latin. TranslateAsync serializes every resource with these options and ToolOptions derives from them. The inbound side already learned the cost (W-165: 'six bytes for one ø').
- **Failure:** A Danish planner record 'Smørrebrød på Nørrebro' reads as 'Sm\u00F8rrebr\u00F8d p\u00E5 N\u00F8rrebro'; a CJK file's text grows from 3 to 6 bytes per character. Pages and describe reach a client's size cut (Claude Code saves reads over about 30 KB to a file and shows only the head) sooner, and an agent copies escape sequences into labels it writes back.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: PowerShell 7.6.6 on .NET 10.0.12, [JsonSerializer]::Serialize('Smørrebrød på Nørrebro', [JsonSerializerOptions]::new([JsonSerializerDefaults]::Web)) -> "Sm\u00F8rrebr\u00F8d p\u00E5 N\u00F8rrebro"; '計画' -> "\u8A08\u753B". NendoMcpJson.CreateOptions (NendoMcpContracts.cs:35) sets no Encoder, and grep finds no Encoder or UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping in src/Nendo.LocalMcp.
- **Fix and guard:** Set Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping (the output is JSON-RPC text, not HTML) in CreateOptions. Guard: a resource test reading a record with 'ø' asserting the raw text contains 'ø' and no backslash-u escape.
- **Verifier:** NendoMcpJson.CreateOptions (NendoMcpContracts.cs:35-43) builds JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web) with no Encoder, and no Encoder or UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping appears anywhere under src/. NendoMcpResources.TranslateAsync (:470) serializes every resource with those options, GetVocabulary and describe use them via ToJsonString (:116, :130), and NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:735 passes ToolOptions (derived from Options) as the tools' SerializerOptions; nendo.read.resource returns the resource text byte for byte. I re-ran the probe in PowerShell on this machine: Serialize('Smørrebrød & <p>') gave "Sm\u00F8rrebr\u00F8d \u0026 \u003Cp\u003E". No contract or ADR documents the escaping as intended (the only mention, mcp-interface.md:215, is the inbound client-side escaping that W-165 already handles).
- **Correction:** The default encoder also escapes ASCII &, <, >, ' and +, which affects English text too (the probe shows \u0026 and \u003C), so the inflation is not limited to non-English files. The escapes are valid JSON and decode correctly, so the cost is size and readability, not corruption. P3 performance is right.

<a id="perf-02"></a>

### PERF-02 — Every filtered read wraps the column in a host function, so no index can serve it: the ADR-0003 covering index on reference columns is never used by the related-list read it exists for

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.HierarchyReads.cs:32`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:583`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:185`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:386`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/summary-tiles.ts:105`, `docs/decisions/0003-relational-user-data-and-protected-metadata.md:13`
- **What:** AddFilterPredicatesAsync registers `nendo_query_filter_N` with CreateFunction and emits `nendo_query_filter_N(CAST(col AS TEXT), @filterN)` for every comparison operator, eq on a reference included (HierarchyReads.cs:32-37). SQLite cannot use an index through a function call, so the page query (ReadQueries.cs:185-190), the count and every aggregate read scan the whole table and call into .NET once per row. relationQuery sends exactly `{viaFieldId eq recordId}` (plan-selection.ts:386-393), the read the ADR-0003 note created `nendo_ref_<table>_<column>(column, __nendo_record_id)` for (Operations.cs:583-603); relation-scoped tiles, group tiles, drills, quick filters and MCP `filter=` add the same kind of clause (summary-tiles.ts:105-122). ADR-0003 records that the index 'changed the plan into a covering search', which holds only for a plain `=`. For eq on Text, Reference, Uuid and Date, RecordQuerySemantics.Compare is StringComparer.Ordinal, whose equality is SQLite BINARY equality, so a sargable conjunct would not change any answer.
- **Failure:** A record page whose related list reads a 100,000-row child type: every read of the relation (on opening the page, on each refresh pass after any commit, on each relation page) scans 100,000 rows with 100,000 host callbacks instead of seeking the index; a page with three relations and a relation tile does it four times per pass.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_ref_index.py (the shipped reference index and the production SQL shape, 100,000 child rows) -> "production plan=['SCAN source_record USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_child_1'] rows=3 callbacks/read=100000 141.47 ms/read"; "plain = plan=['SEARCH source_record USING INDEX nendo_ref_child_parent (parent=?)'] rows=3 callbacks/read=0 0.06 ms/read"; "= AND fn plan=['SEARCH source_record USING INDEX nendo_ref_child_parent (parent=?)'] rows=3 callbacks/read=1 0.10 ms/read".
- **Fix and guard:** Keep the function as the authority but add an indexable conjunct beside it where SQLite's own comparison is identical: `col = @filterN AND nendo_query_filter_N(...)` for eq on Text/Reference/Uuid/Date, `col IS NULL` / `col IS NOT NULL` for isNull/isNotNull. Correct the ADR-0003 note to say which predicates the index serves. Guard: an Engine test that captures the SQL QueryRecordsAsync builds for a relation filter and asserts EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reports `SEARCH ... USING (COVERING )INDEX nendo_ref_`; falsify by removing the conjunct.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end: a related list is data.queryRecords with one eq filter on the reference (plan-selection.ts:386-393, reads.ts:177-188), QueryRecordsAsync (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:185) calls AddFilterPredicatesAsync, which emits nendo_query_filter_N(CAST(col AS TEXT), @filterN) for every comparison (HierarchyReads.cs:33-35). SQLite cannot seek an index through a function, so the ADR-0003 index (Operations.cs:597-600) that the note says 'changed the plan into a covering search' (ADR-0003 lines 30-43) is never used by the read it was accepted for. I re-ran the probe on the same SQL shape: production plan SCAN with 100,000 callbacks (31 ms/read) versus SEARCH on nendo_ref_child_parent (0.01-0.02 ms) for plain = or '= AND fn'. Real, but not P2: the cost is bounded by the file's row ceiling and the project qualifies reads only at 1,000 and 10,000 rows (tools/Review-Performance.ps1 ValidateSet), where this is a few ms; docs/contracts/queries.md also states filters may scan.
- **Correction:** The 100,000-row child type in the scenario is the whole-file ceiling (every entity table together is capped at 100,000 rows: Inspection.cs:53-84 and 149-159), so it is the worst case, not a typical one. The reported 141 ms/read did not reproduce (31 ms here with Python callbacks); a .NET callback would be of the same order, so roughly 30-140 ms per relation read at the ceiling and about 3-14 ms at 10,000 rows. The proposed fix (add 'col = @filterN' beside the function for eq on Text/Reference/Uuid/Date, 'IS NULL'/'IS NOT NULL' for the null checks) is sound and keeps the same answers. Priority P3.

<a id="perf-04"></a>

### PERF-04 — Unindexed revision lookups by proposal_id and compensation_of_revision_id scan __nendo_revision on every proposal prepare, promote, receipt check and undo: about 0.7 s each at 90,000 revisions

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Outcomes.cs:79`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:343`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:40`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:79`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:124`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:654`
- **What:** __nendo_revision has indexes only on revision_id and change_sequence (SqliteNendoStore.cs:654-671). ReadProposalReceiptAsync runs `... FROM __nendo_revision WHERE proposal_id = @proposalId ORDER BY change_sequence` (Outcomes.cs:79-87); SQLite walks the change_sequence index and fetches every row. It is called when a proposal is prepared (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:40), when it is promoted (Promotion.cs:50/79 and again inside the write transaction, SqliteNendoStore.cs:343), and for proposal.getReceipt (the save journal's retry check). CreateCompensationMutationAsync runs `... WHERE compensation_of_revision_id = @revisionId` (Compensation.cs:124-128), a full table scan, for every History compensation and every custom view undo/redo. The Engine keeps SQLite's default 2 MiB page cache, so a 30 MB revision table is read from the OS on each scan.
- **Failure:** Accepting an agent's proposal in a file with 90,000 revisions costs about 0.7 s at prepare and about 1.4 s at promote before any operation is applied; a native CSV import of 2,000 rows in 20 batches spends about 40 s on these lookups alone; each Undo in a custom view pays about 0.27 s.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_revision_predicates.py (shipped __nendo_revision DDL, 90,000 rows on disk, default cache) -> "by proposal_id (Outcomes.cs:86) 675.4 ms per lookup plan=['SCAN __nendo_revision USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex___nendo_revision_2']"; "by compensation_of_revision_id (Compensation.cs:126) 268.3 ms per lookup plan=['SCAN __nendo_revision']".
- **Fix and guard:** Add partial indexes `__nendo_revision(proposal_id, change_sequence) WHERE proposal_id IS NOT NULL` and `__nendo_revision(compensation_of_revision_id) WHERE compensation_of_revision_id IS NOT NULL` as a protected-layout rung (both columns are sparse, so the indexes are small). Guard: an Engine test asserting EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for both statements reports SEARCH ... USING INDEX, plus a timing bound on a 50,000-revision fixture; falsify by dropping the indexes.
- **Verifier:** The schema gives __nendo_revision only its primary key and the change_sequence UNIQUE index (SqliteNendoStore.cs:654-671); ReadProposalReceiptAsync filters on proposal_id (Outcomes.cs:83-87) and CreateCompensationMutationAsync on compensation_of_revision_id (Compensation.cs:125-128), so both scan. Callers are real: prepare (NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:40, and again inside the clone's ApplyChangeSetAsync), promote (Promotion.cs:50 and 79, then SqliteNendoStore.cs:343 inside the write transaction), proposal.getReceipt (MainPage.Csv.cs:134 on failure) and every History or custom-view undo. I re-ran the finder's probe at 90,000 revisions with the default cache and got the claimed plans (SCAN via sqlite_autoindex___nendo_revision_2, and a full SCAN) but only 29-31 ms and 24-28 ms per lookup, about 20x below the reported 675 and 268 ms. The defect exists; its cost is small, and qualification covers only 1,000 and 10,000 revisions (tools/Review-Performance.ps1), where a scan is about 3 ms. Fixing it needs a protected-layout rung (ProtectedSchemaSignatureAsync), a heavy change for a gain of tens of milliseconds at the 99,000-row ceiling.
- **Correction:** Replace the cost figures: about 25-30 ms per lookup at 90,000 revisions with a warm OS cache, so a promote adds roughly 60-120 ms and the 2,000-row CSV scenario about 2-3 s, not 0.7 s, 1.4 s and 40 s; a cold OS cache would cost more. Prepare and promote also copy and fully read the file, which dwarfs the scans. Priority P3.

<a id="perf-07"></a>

### PERF-07 — Proposal prepare and promote, and the MCP authoring calls, read every record with its calculations, and compile a digest over all of them, where only the manifest, touched versions or counts are used

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:92`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:311`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:421`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentProposals.cs:556`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:294`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:43`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Proposals.cs:104`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:109`
- **What:** application.GetSnapshotAsync reaches GetSessionSnapshotAsync(includeRecords: true): every row of every type becomes JsonElements, references are labelled and every calculation runs (Read.cs:259-301). The MCP authoring service calls it in BeginAsync (92), ValidateDraftAsync (311, validate and revalidate) and RevalidateAsync (421) and uses only snapshot.Manifest (RequireHostIdentity/RequireCapturedAuthority, 752-775); NendoAgentProposals.RequireMatchingFileAsync (556-570) does the same on every promote and reject; agent host start reads it only to test Health (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:294). PrepareProposalAsync reads the active file in full (Proposals.cs:43), the clone in full (104), and compiles the clone with all records, where each application plan carries every record and WithComposableDigest serialises them to JSON for a SHA-256 (ComposableSurfaces.cs:92, 914-917); it keeps diagnostics, per-type counts and a 50-per-type preview. CaptureTouchedRecords and TouchedRecordChanged call snapshot.Records.SingleOrDefault per touched record (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:548-576), O(touched x records), once at prepare and twice at promote (Promotion.cs:109-130) after another full read. This is the same waste as ESQ-04, on different paths.
- **Failure:** A native CSV import of 2,000 rows into a 40,000-record file runs 20 batches, and each batch reads all 40,000 records three times and serialises them into a digest before the Import button is answered; an agent's change_set.begin on that file pays a full read before it receives a changeSetId; a proposal that edits 2,000 records performs about 8 x 10^7 record comparisons at prepare.
- **Reproduction:** Source.
- **Fix and guard:** Use GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync (or a manifest read) for the identity and health checks; in proposals read touched records' versions by key, per-type counts with COUNT(*), and the 50-per-type preview with LIMIT; key any unavoidable snapshot by (entity, record) in a dictionary; compile without records when only diagnostics are kept. Guard: an AuthorityCacheTests-style assertion that FullRecordReadCount does not move across change_set.begin/validate or across PrepareProposalAsync for a schema-only proposal; falsify by restoring GetSnapshotAsync.
- **Verifier:** Traced: NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:92 (begin), 311 (validate and revalidate) and 421, NendoAgentProposals.cs:556-570 and NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:294 call application.GetSnapshotAsync, which is coordinator.GetSnapshotAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:190-210) and then store.GetSessionSnapshotAsync with includeRecords defaulting to true (SqliteNendoStore.Read.cs:11-45), i.e. ReadRecordsAsync with calculations (Read.cs:259-301, FullRecordReadCount++). Those callers use only Manifest, Health or FileName (RequireHostIdentity and RequireCapturedAuthority, AuthoringService.cs:752-775). GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:10-20, includeRecords: false, same manifest) already exists and the Desktop and CSV paths use it. PrepareProposalAsync reads the active file in full (Proposals.cs:43), PromoteProposalAsync again (Promotion.cs:109), and TouchedRecordChanged and CaptureTouchedRecords scan snapshot.Records per touched record (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:548-576). It is the same class as ESQ-04, which FIXES.md already lists as P3. Cost is unmeasured and small at the qualified 1,000-10,000 record scale.
- **Correction:** Part of the proposed fix is wrong: the prepare-time compile of the clone with all records (Proposals.cs:104-108) cannot simply drop the records, because ValidateRecords (NendoSemanticCompiler.cs:58-117) produces the NDATA001/010/011/012 record diagnostics that are kept in context.Diagnostics and shown to the reviewer, and the counts and 50-per-type preview come from the same snapshot. The solid part is replacing GetSnapshotAsync with GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync at the MCP call sites and keying the touched-record lookups by (entity, record). The 40,000-record and 8 x 10^7 comparison figures are estimates, not measurements. Priority P3.

<a id="perf-08"></a>

### PERF-08 — Every commit counts every table, entity tables twice, costing about 34 ms per single-field write in a file near the row bound

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:115`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:135`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:151`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:243`
- **What:** RequireRoomToGrowAsync runs `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM __nendo_operation` before staging (Inspection.cs:115-117). RequireInspectableCommitAsync then runs COUNT(*) over every non-search table listed in sqlite_schema, which already includes every entity table, and a second COUNT(*) over every entity table (Inspection.cs:135-159). Each COUNT(*) walks a whole b-tree, inside the write transaction, for every mutation including a one-field edit; only the tables the mutation touched can have changed.
- **Failure:** Each Studio cell edit or MCP set_field in a file with 90,000 rows per table spends about 34 ms counting before COMMIT, comparable to the commit's own fsyncs, and a burst of agent writes pays it per write.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_commit_counts.py 90000 (the same COUNT(*) sequence on disk, default cache) -> "rows per table=90000 file=353.4 MiB per-commit COUNT(*) checks: median 33.8 ms (min 30.6, max 39.6)".
- **Fix and guard:** Count only the tables the mutation wrote (the evidence names them) and keep cached counts for the rest, refreshed at open; drop the duplicate pass over entity tables. Guard: an Engine test with a counting seam asserting a single-field write issues COUNT(*) only for the touched tables; falsify by restoring the loop.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end: ApplyAsync calls RequireRoomToGrowAsync (SqliteNendoStore.cs:151, COUNT(*) of __nendo_operation, Inspection.cs:115) and RequireInspectableCommitAsync (cs:243) on every mutation, and the proposal path does the same (cs:368, 518). Inspection.cs:146-159 counts every non-search table from sqlite_schema, which already includes the entity tables, then counts each entity table again; __nendo_operation is also counted twice. I re-ran an adapted copy of the probe in verify/performance-cross-cutting-8: 30.1 ms median at 90,000 rows per table in an 87 MiB file, 21.2 ms at 57,000 rows in a 223.7 MiB file (the write ceiling). The duplication is real. It is a deliberate safety check (docs/architecture.md:767) and only costs tens of ms in files near the row bound, so P3.
- **Correction:** The reviewer's 34 ms figure came from a 353 MiB probe file, above the 224 MiB write ceiling (WriteCeilingFileBytes) where RequireRoomToGrowAsync would refuse the write before any COUNT ran, so that exact state is unreachable. The cost is driven by row count, not payload size, so it is still reproducible in reachable files: about 30 ms at 90k rows per table with light rows, about 21 ms at the byte ceiling with heavy rows, and under a few ms for a file of a few thousand rows. The fix and guard stand.

<a id="perf-09"></a>

### PERF-09 — Studio search sends one-letter prefix searches, which match most of the index and cost about 20 times a two-letter search; the palette and @ menu wait for two characters

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `performance-cross-cutting`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/studio-search.ts:71`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/command-palette.ts:53`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-mention.ts:36`
- **What:** schedule() searches whenever the trimmed text is non-empty (studio-search.ts:71-79), so typing the first letter of a word sends data.searchRecords with a one-character prefix term; the FTS5 table's prefix indexes are '2 3', so a one-character prefix walks the full term list. command-palette.ts and agent-mention.ts use searchMinimum = 2. Superseded answers are dropped in the renderer, but the host still runs every request, on the UI thread (DSH-04).
- **Failure:** In a 100,000-record type, typing 'a' then pausing for 200 ms runs a search matching 78% of the documents, about 266 ms of host work, before the second letter's 13 ms search.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python -I probe_search_prefix.py (FTS5 DDL and ranking query from SqliteNendoStore.Search.cs, 100,000 documents) -> "typed 'a' matching docs= 77927 first page=21 rows 266.1 ms"; "typed 'ab' matching docs= 4729 first page=21 rows 13.0 ms".
- **Fix and guard:** Apply the same two-character minimum in studio-search.ts (show a hint below it). Guard: a node test of wireStudioSearch with a stub client asserting no request for a one-letter input; falsify by removing the check.
- **Verifier:** Traced: studio-search.ts:71-79 sends data.searchRecords for any non-empty trimmed text after a 200 ms pause. SearchTerms.Parse (Search.cs:120-133) keeps a one-letter word and makes it a prefix term (`"a"*`), and the FTS5 table indexes only prefixes of 2 and 3 characters (Search.cs:26). command-palette.ts:53 and agent-mention.ts:36 do set searchMinimum = 2, so Studio is the odd one out. data.searchRecords is not in the OffUiThread list (WorkbenchCancellation.cs:33-82), so the host runs it on the UI thread. I re-ran the reviewer's probe: 161.4 ms for 'a' (77,927 matching docs) against 8.3 ms for 'ab' at 100,000 documents, which reproduces the roughly 20x ratio.
- **Correction:** The absolute cost scales with the number of search documents. The 160-266 ms applies only to a type near 100,000 text documents, and the debounce means it fires only when the person pauses 200 ms after the first letter. ADR-0028:133 deliberately specifies last-word prefix matching and records 0.8-2.7 ms median searches on the real workspace files, so at normal sizes this is a few ms. The UI-thread blocking is the already-recorded DSH-04, not new. Keep it P3.

<a id="site-11"></a>

### SITE-11 — The home page downloads the full 3.2 MB brand video on first load, even on a phone where it sits 8,000px below the fold

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/src/pages/index.astro:211`, `site/src/pages/index.astro:217`
- **What:** The <video> carries preload="metadata" but also autoplay (index.astro:216-217); autoplay overrides the preload hint, so the browser fetches the whole file at load. At 375x812 with cache disabled, 6 s after navigation: total 3,427,086 bytes, of which 3,225,456 are /nendo/brand/nendo.mp4, while the video's top was at 8018px and scrollY 0.
- **Failure:** A visitor on mobile data opening the home page spends 94% of the page's bytes on a decorative 10-second sting they may never scroll to.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: CDP net.mjs at 375x812, cache disabled -> 'total bytes 3427086', '3225456 /nendo/brand/nendo.mp4', 'scrollY 0 video top 8018'
- **Fix and guard:** Drop the autoplay attribute and start playback from an IntersectionObserver when the card enters the viewport (respecting reduced motion), or ship a smaller encode with a poster frame. Guard: the net probe as a lane asserting the home page's initial transfer stays under a budget (for example 600 KB) at 375px.
- **Verifier:** index.astro:211-219 sets preload="metadata" together with autoplay. The mp4 is 3,225,456 bytes, moov at the front, so metadata alone would need about 48 KB. I served site/dist with astro preview (Range supported, 206 responses) and loaded the home page in the browser pane at 375x812: scrollY 0, video top at 8019px, yet Resource Timing shows /nendo/brand/nendo.mp4 transferSize 3,225,756 and the element reports readyState 4, buffered 0-10.005 and paused false. The autoplay attribute overrides the preload hint, so a decorative sting below the fold is fetched in full at load, which the preload=metadata and the 'leave the first frame' comment show was not intended. Performance polish on the public site, P3.

<a id="site-22"></a>

### SITE-22 — Every internal link omits the trailing slash, so each navigation on GitHub Pages costs a 301 redirect

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/src/components/Nav.astro:9`, `site/src/docs-nav.ts:35`, `site/src/components/Footer.astro:19`, `site/astro.config.mjs:10`
- **What:** With the default directory build format, pages are dist/<page>/index.html, and the canonical URLs end in '/'. The header links (Nav.astro:9-15), the docs rail and cards (docs-nav.ts:35), the footer (Footer.astro:19-23) and the guides' markdown links all use /nendo/<page> without the slash, and trailingSlash is 'ignore' (astro.config.mjs:10), so nothing normalises them.
- **Failure:** Each click in the header, footer or docs rail on the live site makes an extra round trip (301 to the slash URL) before the page loads, which is noticeable on mobile latency.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: curl -sI https://thomasrohde.github.io/nendo/concept -> 'HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently' 'Location: https://thomasrohde.github.io/nendo/concept/'
- **Fix and guard:** Set trailingSlash: 'always' and emit hrefs with a trailing slash (in Nav, Footer, docs-nav, pages and the guide links), or set build.format: 'file'. Guard: check-links.mjs fails on an internal href to a directory page without the trailing slash.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. Nav.astro:9-15, Footer.astro:19-23 and docs-nav.ts:35 emit hrefs like /nendo/concept and /nendo/docs/<id> with no trailing slash, and the guides' markdown links do the same (agents.md:10, :136, :162). astro.config.mjs:10 sets trailingSlash 'ignore' and the default directory format emits dist/<page>/index.html (the built dist/index.html has href="/nendo/concept", /nendo/use, /nendo/status). I repeated the live probe: curl -sI https://thomasrohde.github.io/nendo/concept returns 301 Moved Permanently with Location .../nendo/concept/, and the slashed URL returns 200. No ADR or doc makes the slashless form deliberate. It is a real extra round trip per first navigation, but the redirect carries Cache-Control max-age=600 so repeats within ten minutes are cached; a latency nit, P3.
- **Correction:** 'Each click' overstates it: the 301 response is cacheable for 600 s, so only the first visit to each target per ten minutes pays the extra round trip.

<a id="tbi-10"></a>

### TBI-10 — Setup spends seconds on avoidable work: an O(n^2) identical-payload comparison and Uninstall hashing each tree twice

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:617`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:594`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:596`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:598`
- **What:** For each of the 687 next entries, line 620 pipes all old entries through Where-Object, which is quadratic in Windows PowerShell 5.1. Uninstall calls Assert-Bytes on $root (594) and then Remove-Owned, which runs Assert-Bytes again. The same happens for $previous (596). The script's own comment (lines 76-77) records that hashing cost was already worth optimising.
- **Failure:** Rerunning the same installer spends about 6.5 s in the comparison alone. Uninstall hashes about 1.2 GB instead of 600 MB.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: same-payload-cost.ps1 in Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 with 687 entries -> 'entries=687 same=True seconds=6.55'. The owner log shows '05:34:21 Checking the installed files.' followed by '05:34:27 This Nendo payload is already installed'.
- **Fix and guard:** Build a path->sha256 hashtable from $old once and compare by lookup. Drop the redundant Assert-Bytes calls before Remove-Owned, since Remove-Owned asserts itself. Guard: a timing assertion over 700 synthetic entries (under 0.5 s), or count hash calls in Test-NendoSetup via a log line.
- **Verifier:** tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:617-621 runs '@($old.files \| Where-Object {...}).Count' once per next entry, which is O(n*m). I reproduced it with 687 identical entries: 3.84 s in Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 and 2.58 s in pwsh 7.6.6 on this machine (the reviewer measured 6.55 s). Uninstall also hashes twice: line 594 Assert-Bytes then Remove-Owned (153) asserts again, and 596 does the same for $previous. It is wasted time, not wrong behaviour, on rare paths.
- **Correction:** The quadratic loop only runs when $old.files.Count equals $next.files.Count (line 617), so a normal upgrade that adds or drops a file skips it. The cost lands on same-payload reinstall and repair, plus equal-count upgrades. The 594 pre-check of the installed tree before the backup is removed has a purpose (it refuses before deleting the backup); only the 596 pre-check and the Remove-Owned duplicates are purely redundant. The owner-log gap between 'Checking the installed files' and 'already installed' also includes hashing the installed tree, so it does not isolate the comparison cost.

<a id="wau-05"></a>

### WAU-05 — Every read rebuilds the markup of every thread item, Markdown included, so one long agent line makes each later read cost close to a second

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:461`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent-chat.ts:463`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:264`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:108`
- **What:** patchChat calls itemMarkup for every item on every read (view-agent-chat.ts:461-462) and only then compares the result with the drawn string. itemMarkup runs markdownMarkup over each agent message every time (agent-chat-model.ts:264). Each item also costs a querySelector over the whole thread (463). In the inline formatter (markdown.ts:107-112), the strong, emphasis and strikethrough rules match lazily, (.+?), up to a closing delimiter that must follow a non-space. Each opener with no valid closer therefore scans to the end of the line, which is quadratic in line length. The host keeps entries of up to 200,000 characters.
- **Failure:** An agent lists matching files as one line of globs ('*.e0 *.e1 ...', 94,219 characters). From then on, every read of the conversation, including each streamed chunk of every later answer, spends about 0.8 s on markup before any DOM work, so typing in the composer stalls while the agent works. Even with ordinary text, a transcript at the host's bound of 1,000 entries costs 14 ms of markup (744 KB rebuilt) per read.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node perf-probe3.mjs -> {"longLineChars":94219,"msPerLaterRead":[798,792,832]}; node perf-probe2.mjs -> {"case":"long transcript, one patch","entries":1000,"items":600,"markupCharsRebuiltPerPatch":743915,"msPerPatch":14.08}; node inline-probe.mjs (one line of '**a ' repeated) -> {"chars":8000,"ms":25.5} {"chars":32000,"ms":398.5} {"chars":80000,"ms":2909.2}
- **Fix and guard:** Cache each item's markup by its key, the revisions of its entries, the expanded flag and live, or build markup only for the entry IDs that mergeChat returned. Find drawn items in a Map rather than with a querySelector per item. Make the emphasis rules linear: match delimiters in one pass, or skip inline emphasis on lines longer than a bound. Guard: a node test merges one chunk into a 1,000-entry chat and counts markdownMarkup calls (expect 1); a second test renders the 94,219-character glob line within a fixed operation count. Falsify by removing the cache.
- **Verifier:** The mechanism is real. patchChat calls itemMarkup for every item on every read before comparing with drawn (view-agent-chat.ts:461-464), including markdownMarkup for each agent message (agent-chat-model.ts:264), plus a querySelector per item. The strong and emphasis rules in markdown.ts:108-111 use lazy (.+?) with a closing delimiter that must follow a non-space, so an opener with no valid closer scans to the end of the line. I ran the two rules in node (verify/workbench-agent-ui-1/v5.mjs). A line of '*.eN ' globs took 18 ms at 8,002 chars and 90 ms at 16,002. 'char *p, *q; ' repeated took 29 ms at 8,008 chars and 517 ms at 32,006. Ordinary prose of 32,040 chars took 0.2 ms. The cost needs a single very long line with many unmatched openers, which agent prose rarely has. The always-rebuild cost on ordinary text is small (the reviewer measured 14 ms for a 1,000-entry transcript). Real as an inefficiency and a hazard on a pathological line, but not a material defect on a common path, so P3.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The 94,219-character glob line is a pathological input; for ordinary lines under about 8,000 characters the quadratic cost is under 30 ms, and a 1,000-entry transcript costs 14 ms per read. Memoising itemMarkup by key and entry revision is still a sound cleanup.

### WDV-20 — Surface tiles are still read while a drill narrows the list, though they are not drawn

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `workbench-data-views`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:456`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:462`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-markup.ts:114`
- **What:** surfaceTileMarkup hides surface tiles whenever narrowed() is true (a drill or a Filter pick). visibleTiles excludes them only for a Filter pick (quick), not for a drill, while visibleCharts uses narrowed(). tilePending therefore keeps the surface chase reading tiles nobody sees, and reads them again on every revision.
- **Failure:** On a list with three count/sum tiles, the person drills into a chart segment: each revision while drilled issues three exact aggregate reads whose results are never drawn.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Use narrowed(plan, surface) in visibleTiles as visibleCharts does. Guard: a plan-selection test asserting visibleTiles is empty for surface scope while a drill is active; falsify by restoring the quick-only check.
- **Verifier:** narrowed() is a drill OR a Filter pick (plan-selection.ts:365-367) and surfaceTileMarkup/columnTileMarkup draw nothing when it is true (surface-markup.ts:114,126), but visibleTiles excludes surface and group tiles only for a Filter pick (plan-selection.ts:456-462), not for a drill, whereas visibleCharts uses narrowed() (:486-494). With a drill active the surface tiles stay in visibleTiles; view-use.ts:270 sees tilePending once the changeSequence moves (readIsPending, plan-selection.ts:429-434) and starts surfaceChase, whose refreshVisibleTiles (panels.ts:283-288) issues data.countRecords/aggregateRecords for tiles that are hidden. git show df81c75 (W-172) shows the quick-only exclusion was added for the Filter pick and the drill case was never covered. Wasted reads per revision only, no wrong output, hence P3.
- **Correction:** Only surface-scoped tiles are affected in practice: a drill targets a list (activeDrill requires drill.listId === the selected surface), so the groupTiles part of the evidence applies to boards, which are not drilled.

### WMX-09 — Emphasis matching is quadratic, so a Markdown value or agent message with many unmatched delimiters freezes the Workbench

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `workbench-markup-xss`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:108`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:109`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:110`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts:111`
- **What:** For every unmatched opener, each lazy (.+?) with a lookbehind closer scans to the end of the paragraph. inline() runs again on every agent-chat patch while a message grows, and the Studio large-text editor accepts 1,000,000 characters (view-data.ts:83).
- **Failure:** A markdown field holding 128,000 characters of '**a ' takes 6.5 s to render, and the time grows quadratically, so a 1 MB value would take minutes. The WebView's main thread is frozen while the record is opened, or while an agent streams such a message.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-markdown-time.mjs -> `unclosed strong "**a " x32000 128000 chars 6516 ms`; `unclosed stars "*a " x32000 96000 chars 1487 ms`; plain prose of 216000 chars takes 1 ms.
- **Fix and guard:** Replace the regex passes with one pass that keeps a stack of delimiters (as CommonMark does), or skip emphasis processing for very long paragraphs. Guard: a markdown.test.mjs timing bound, such as 100k unmatched delimiters rendering in under 200 ms.
- **Verifier:** Reproduced with a copy of src/Nendo.Workbench/src/markdown.ts under node 25: '**a ' x32000 (128,000 chars on one line) took 7.0-7.3 s, x16000 took 1.5 s and x8000 0.47 s, which is quadratic. The cause is markdown.ts:108-111, where each unmatched opener's lazy (.+?) scans to the end of the text. Reachable by an agent or a package: agent-chat-model.ts:264 and view-help.ts:30 run it on agent and package text, and record-markup.ts:442 runs it on any Markdown field. It is not data loss, only a freeze of seconds, and only pathological text triggers it, so P3.
- **Correction:** The cost is bounded per line, because `.` in (.+?) does not match '\n' and paragraph lines are joined with '\n' (markdown.ts:79). The same 128,000 characters wrapped at 80 columns rendered in 7 ms, and 1 MB of prose with a few unmatched delimiters took 3 ms. Only one very long line with thousands of unmatched ** / * / _ / ~~ delimiters is slow, so it is adversarial or machine-generated input, not ordinary notes. The '1 MB would take minutes' claim holds only for a single 1 MB line.

### WST-12 — A 1391×1131, 1.3 MB brand PNG is decoded in every window to draw a 16 px mark, and a 1254×1254, 965 KB PNG is the favicon

**P3** · performance · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:20`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/index.html:11`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/21-native.css:55`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Nendo.Desktop.csproj:40`
- **What:** public/nendo-mark.png is 1391×1131 (1,343,821 bytes). It is shown at 16×16 in the title bar (21-native.css:55-58), at 28×24 in the collapsed rail, at 48×48 in the file look, and at most 92×76 on the empty screen. public/nendo.png is 1254×1254 (965,522 bytes) and serves only as the favicon. Both ship in payload/Workbench, and nendo-mark.png ships a second time as Assets\NendoMark.png.
- **Failure:** Each Nendo window, and each renderer restart, fetches and decodes about 6 MB of RGBA for a 16 px icon. Together with the duplicate copy, the installer carries about 3.6 MB of PNG for icons.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python struct read of the PNG headers -> 'nendo.png 1254 1254 965522', 'nendo-mark.png 1391 1131 1343821'
- **Fix and guard:** Ship right-sized assets, for example a 64 px and 192 px mark or an SVG, and a 32/48 px favicon. Keep the large master out of public/. Guard with a Test-BinaryAssets rule capping public/*.png dimensions or bytes.
- **Verifier:** Checked the PNG headers: public/nendo-mark.png is 1391x1131 (1,343,821 bytes) and public/nendo.png is 1254x1254 (965,522 bytes). index.html:20 and file-actions.ts:88/97, view-data.ts:348, file-look.ts:20 load /nendo-mark.png into boxes of 16 to 92 CSS px (21-native.css:55, 07-studio.css:167-169, 01-file-menu.css:34), and index.html:11 uses nendo.png only as the favicon. Nendo.Desktop.csproj:40 ships the same mark a second time as Assets\NendoMark.png (used for a XAML Image at MainPage.xaml.cs:420), so about 3.65 MB of PNG ships for small icons. Test-BinaryAssets.ps1:385-386 lists them as shipping assets with no size cap and nothing records a reason for the master resolution. Measured in headless Edge 154 (probe: scratchpad/review/verify/workbench-scripts-tests-7/png-decode-probe.mjs): fetch plus decode of nendo-mark.png takes about 26-32 ms and nendo.png about 19-27 ms each time. Decoded size 1391x1131x4 is about 6.3 MB. Nothing shows a consumer for the large size (92x76 CSS px at 200% DPI needs under 200 px).
- **Correction:** Impact is small: decode is asynchronous and off the main thread, the extra payload is about 1% of the 320 MB payload, and whether WebView2 even fetches the favicon was not established, so the favicon half may cost nothing at runtime. The 6 MB figure is arithmetic from the dimensions, not a measured memory number. P3 stands.

- **What:** The test copies workspace/BCM.nendo, replays tools/bcm-atlas/upgrade-operations.json through the MCP tools and, when validation reports NPROP010 'bcm.assessment already exists', calls Assert.Inconclusive. Its own comment says the committed file has carried the upgrade since ef0f13e, so every run takes this branch; everything after line 65 (promotion, required fields, the data-phase import) never executes.
- **Failure:** A regression in the upgrade operations, the 16-operation batching, or the import with ExpectedTargetVersions that Upgrade-BcmAtlas.mjs relies on ships unnoticed: the lane reports Skipped, which dotnet test counts as success, on every run.

The test's own comment says so. dotnet test counts Inconclusive as not-executed rather than failed, so the lane stays green.

The upgrade is finished and applied to the live file, and tools/bcm-atlas/upgrade.test.mjs:73-77 still guards that upgrade-operations.json equals what upgrade.mjs builds, so the operations cannot silently go stale. What nothing now guards is that they still validate and apply (including the 16-operation batching and the ExpectedTargetVersions import). The finding is a retired-test housekeeping item: delete it, or run it against a pre-upgrade fixture. extensions/bcm-atlas/README.md:231 still describes the test as applying the upgrade to a copy.

### SITE-18 — check-links.mjs claims to check anchors but skips every same-page '#' link, every relative href and every srcset

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `site`

- **Where:** `site/scripts/check-links.mjs:60`, `site/scripts/check-links.mjs:61`, `site/scripts/check-links.mjs:58`
- **What:** The header says every internal reference including 'an anchor that exists on the page it points at' must resolve, but line 60 skips any href starting with '#', line 61 skips anything not starting with '/', and the regex at line 58 only reads href= and src=, not srcset=. The guides' TOC links and in-guide links such as [Reference](#reference) and (#screens-for-the-whole-file) are therefore unchecked (they resolve today).
- **Failure:** Renaming the 'Reference' heading in concepts.md breaks the field table's '#reference' link and the TOC entry, and the build still prints 'Every internal reference resolves.'
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node site/scripts/check-links.mjs <scratch>/fakedist (a page with href="#nowhere", href="concepts", href="../nope" and srcset="/nendo/_astro/missing.webp 2x") -> 'Checked 1 internal reference(s) across 2 page(s). Every internal reference resolves.' exit 0
- **Fix and guard:** Resolve '#x' against the page's own ids, resolve relative hrefs against the page URL, and split srcset candidates. Guard: a node --test case in scripts/ that runs check-links over a fixture dist with each broken kind and expects exit code 1.
- **Verifier:** site/scripts/check-links.mjs:58 reads only href= and src= (no srcset), :60 skips any value starting with '#', :61 skips anything not starting with '/'. I ran the script against a task-owned fake dist containing href="#nowhere", href="concepts", href="../nope" and an srcset to a missing file: output 'Checked 1 internal reference(s)... Every internal reference resolves.' exit 0 (probe in verify/site-13). The build runs it as the last step (package.json build script), so a renamed heading breaks hand-written same-page links such as concepts.md:57 [Reference](#reference), files-and-data.md:17 (#copies), :32 (#history-and-undo) and screens.md:33 without failing the build. The header comment (check-links.mjs:1-2) says anchors on the page a link points at are checked, which holds only for absolute cross-page links (:72).
- **Correction:** Narrow the impact: the 'Reference' TOC entry cannot break because Doc.astro:60-64 generates the On-this-page list from the current headings, so only the hand-written in-body links are exposed (four in the guides). Relative hrefs are not used by convention (guides use absolute /nendo/ paths), and srcset values are emitted by astro:assets from imports, so they resolve by construction. In dist today all 126 same-page anchors resolve (my scan), so this is a latent guard gap, not a current break.

### TBI-04 — Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade writes a real HKCU Uninstall key, a real Start Menu shortcut and a folder in the real Programs\NendoPilot, aims setup at the owner's install root, fails whenever the owner's Nendo runs, and never cleans up

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:8`, `tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:43`, `tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:48`, `tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:53`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:511`, `docs/architecture.md:1198`, `docs/architecture.md:1212`
- **What:** The fixture installs into $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\NendoPilot\<id>, registers HKCU\...\Uninstall\NendoPilot-<id> and creates '$SMPROGRAMS\Nendo Pilot <id>.lnk'. The lane then throws at line 49. Cleanup exists only on the success path (lines 53-54), with no try/finally. docs/architecture.md says these three fast tests use 'no real payload and no NSIS' and that each lane removes its registrations in a finally block. This lane compiles NSIS and has no finally.
- **Failure:** A developer runs the documented 'pwsh ./tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1' while Nendo is open. The run fails, and each attempt leaves a 'Nendo Pilot <id>' entry in the person's Start Menu pointing at owned.txt, a hidden Uninstall key, and a folder. The next real installer's RetirePilots then executes the test fixture's Uninstall.exe as part of the owner's upgrade.

Both folders hold exactly 'Uninstall.exe owned.txt user.nendo', the fixture of lines 20-21 and 46. 'reg query HKCU\...\Uninstall' lists NendoPilot-7d914a37a6e745e4 and NendoPilot-e22c7b104a874d24, both with a blank DisplayName.
- **Fix and guard:** Pass a task-owned -InstallRoot under the evidence folder, which RetirePilots uses only for Assert-Tree, Assert-Closed and the mutex. Wrap everything after the fixture install in try/finally that runs the fixture's uninstaller, or removes its key, shortcut and folder. Correct docs/architecture.md about NSIS use and cleanup. Guard: after the lane, pass or fail, assert that no NendoPilot-<id> key, shortcut or folder for its id remains, and run it once with Nendo open.
- **Verifier:** Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1 compiles an NSIS fixture (41) that writes a real HKCU Uninstall\NendoPilot-<id> key and a real Start Menu shortcut (24-25) and installs into the real Programs\NendoPilot\<id> (8, 17). Setup is aimed at the owner's Programs\Nendo (48). Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:568 calls Assert-Closed before the RetirePilots branch, and 511 throws for any Nendo.Desktop whose path starts under $root, so the lane fails at line 49 whenever the owner's Nendo runs. Cleanup (53-54) is on the success path only, with no try/finally. I confirmed the leftovers on this machine, read-only: Start Menu 'Nendo Pilot 7d914a37a6e745e4.lnk' and 'Nendo Pilot e22c7b104a874d24.lnk' (23-09-2026 05:01), reg keys NendoPilot-7d914a37a6e745e4 and NendoPilot-e22c7b104a874d24, and each folder holds owned.txt, Uninstall.exe and user.nendo. The doc sentence that the three fast tests use 'no NSIS' is wrong for this lane.
- **Correction:** Downgrade to P3: a manually run developer lane, outside Test-Production (grep finds it only in docs); the damage is two junk Start Menu entries and keys, and the workaround is to close Nendo. 'The next installer executes the fixture's Uninstall.exe' is accurate but benign, since that cleans the fixture up; it only fires without /KEEPLEGACYPILOTS, which the owner's upgrades pass. The 'finally' sentence in architecture.md concerns the class-store lanes (Isolated, Installed journey, Setup-Tests), not this lane, so only the 'no NSIS' claim is drift. Setup uses the install root only for Assert-Tree/Assert-Closed/mutex in this mode, so the owner's install is not modified.

### TBI-07 — Test-NendoSetupIsolated passes setup arguments to Start-Process as an array, which is joined unquoted, so a checkout path with a space breaks the lane

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

Start-Process joins the elements with spaces and does not quote them. Test-NendoSetup.ps1:43 uses '& $powershell @arguments' instead, which quotes correctly.
- **Failure:** The repository lives at C:\Users\Some One\nendo or D:\My Projects\nendo. -File receives a truncated path, and the lane, documented as 'Always' runnable, fails with a parameter or file-not-found error unrelated to setup.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: argv-probe.ps1 (pwsh 7.6.6; Start-Process powershell.exe -ArgumentList @('-NoProfile','-File',<echo script>,'C:\Users\Some One\install')) -> 'argc=2 first=[C:\Users\Some]'.
- **Fix and guard:** Quote each element ('"' + $_ + '"') or invoke '& powershell.exe @arguments' with output redirection. Guard: run the lane once from a copy of tools/ under a scratch folder whose name contains a space.
- **Verifier:** tools/Test-NendoSetupIsolated.ps1:200-208 builds a string[] ($setup = $PSScriptRoot\Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1, $installRoot and the -PayloadRoot/-StartMenuRoot extras all under the checkout) and passes it to Start-Process -ArgumentList, which joins elements with spaces and adds no quotes. I reproduced it in the scratch folder under both Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 and pwsh 7.6.6: an element 'C:\Users\Some One\install' reaches the child script as 'C:\Users\Some' plus a stray argument. Test-NendoSetup.ps1:43 uses '& $powershell @arguments', which quotes correctly, so the two lanes disagree. Only trips when the checkout path contains a space (this machine's C:\Users\thoma\Projects\nendo does not), so it is a latent portability defect in a lane, not a product defect.
- **Correction:** The same unquoted-array pattern is at tools/Test-ExtensionInstalledJourney.ps1:42, so a fix and its guard should cover both lanes.

In tools/Put-NendoPackage.mjs:110-112 the extensions read then parses to an object with no 'packages', so (Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.packages ?? The Engine tests (ExtensionPackageTests.cs, ExtensionArchiveTests.cs) cover the operations' semantics, not this script's diff logic, and no other test invokes Put-NendoPackage. Package updates are the script's main use (every gantt, bcm-atlas and planner-skill revision), so the gap is real; it is a missing-coverage finding with no present misbehaviour, hence P3.
- **Correction:** None to locations. Note the test's three batching fixtures do assert the operation count (files + 1 + extra), which is only valid for the new-package path; an update fixture needs its own expected count.

### TST-08 — StopCancelsTheTurnAndAnyQuestionOpenInIt never has a question open, so answering a pending permission on Stop is untested

- **What:** The test prompts "wait", which in fake-acp-agent.mjs only streams "Working..." and waits for session/cancel. It never sends session/request_permission. That branch is what ACP requires so the agent's request does not hang. No test reaches it: grep shows CancelLaunchedAgentTurnAsync called only in this test, and "Cancelled" is never asserted on a permission entry.
- **Failure:** Someone removes or breaks the loop over open permissions. Stop then leaves the agent waiting on request_permission for ever: the transcript says "Stopped." while the agent process stays blocked. The suite stays green, and the test's name claims that behaviour is covered.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Add a case, or extend this test: prompt "permission", wait for the permission entry, call CancelLaunchedAgentTurnAsync, then assert that the entry's Answer is "Cancelled", that the fake agent's log has {permission: {outcome: {outcome: 'cancelled'}}}, and that the turn ends with Working = false. Falsify by deleting the foreach in CancelTurnAsync and quote the failure.
- **Verifier:** DesktopLaunchedAgentTests.cs:322-337 prompts 'wait', which fake-acp-agent.mjs:76-81 answers with one chunk and then waits for session/cancel. It never sends session/request_permission, so _permissions is empty when CancelTurnAsync runs (AgentConversation.cs:341-353). The loop `foreach (var permission in open) permission.Answer.TrySetResult(null)` is therefore never exercised by this test. Repo-wide grep finds CancelLaunchedAgentTurnAsync called only from this test, and 'Cancelled' is asserted nowhere. ARequestMeantForAReplacedConversationIsRefused leaves a question open, but it ends the conversation through End(), which has its own loop at line 380, not CancelTurnAsync. The test name promises 'any question open in it' and the code does not deliver. Test gap only, no product defect, so P3.
- **Correction:** Minor: the Answer='Cancelled' entry text and the cancelled outcome are produced by the shared permission handler (AgentConversation.cs:467,477), which the End() path reaches in other tests. Only CancelTurnAsync's own loop is untested, and the finding's fix (a 'permission' prompt, then Stop, then assert Answer == 'Cancelled' and the agent log's cancelled outcome) is the right one.

### TST-09 — The MCP perimeter's body bound for requests without Content-Length (chunked) has no test

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `dotnet-tests-quality`

- **Where:** `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/McpSecurityTests.cs:36`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:62`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:137`
- **What:** PerimeterRejectsOversizeAndDeepJsonBeforeDispatch only sets Request.ContentLength = MaximumRequestBodyBytes + 1 on an empty body, which exercises the header check at line 62. The streamed check inside AdmitAsync (`total += read; if (total > MaximumRequestBodyBytes) ...`) is the only bound on a chunked request or one with no declared length (F-182: unbounded buffers). No test sends such a body: grep across tests/ finds no Transfer-Encoding, chunked or `ContentLength = null`. AppBuilderReviewTests' oversize call goes through the SDK client, which sends a Content-Length.
- **Failure:** A refactor drops the in-loop total check or moves the buffering ahead of it. A local client can then send an unbounded chunked body that the host buffers whole in memory. Every test still passes.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Add a McpSecurityTests case: a DefaultHttpContext with ContentLength left null and a body stream yielding MaximumRequestBodyBytes + 16 KiB in 16 KiB reads. Assert 413 and NENDO_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE, assert no dispatch, and assert that the stream was not read far past the bound. Add a raw-TCP case with Transfer-Encoding: chunked against a real host. Falsify by commenting out the total check and quote the failure.
- **Verifier:** The streamed bound at NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:137 (`total > MaximumRequestBodyBytes`) is the only check for a request with no Content-Length. McpSecurityTests.cs:40 sets ContentLength = Max + 1 on an empty body and so hits only the header branch at line 62. Body() at lines 104-108 always sets ContentLength to the body length, and the default AssertRejectedAsync context has an empty body. Grepping tests/, tools/ and the Workbench scripts for Transfer-Encoding, chunked, StreamContent, HttpContent and 'ContentLength = null' finds nothing. AppBuilderReviewTests.cs:111 goes through the SDK client, which sends a length. The streamed branch and EnvelopeScanner's Feed-then-continue path (lines 137-143) therefore have no test.
- **Correction:** The failure scenario overstates 'unbounded'. NendoLocalMcp sets no Kestrel limit (grep MaxRequestBodySize in src/Nendo.LocalMcp finds none), so Kestrel's default 30 MB request-body cap would still stop a chunked body. Dropping the in-loop check would let up to about 30 MB be buffered instead of 256 KiB, which is a loopback-only host under ADR-0009. Still a real test gap on a security-perimeter branch, but P3.

### WAU-16 — The preview's scripted agent lets an old turn's timers write into the next conversation and run after Stop, and it launches while an agent runs, so the agent-chat gate exercises states production never reaches

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `workbench-agent-ui`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/preview-agent-session.ts:232`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/preview-agent-session.ts:139`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/preview-agent-session.ts:166`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/preview-agent-session.ts:102`
- **What:** later() runs a step unless the state is 'ended' (232-234). It records neither the launch nor the turn. sendPrompt schedules the tool calls and a permission request at 500-900 ms (139-145). answer() schedules the reply's chunks and then sets working = false (158-162). cancel() clears none of these timers (166-174). After New session (end, then launch, so the state is 'starting' or 'ready') or after Stop, the old timers add tool entries and an unasked permission request to the conversation on screen, and flip working. list() sets canLaunch from the mode alone (102), so launch() starts a second agent while one runs, where Desktop refuses with agent-already-running. tools/Review-AgentChat.ps1 drives the built Workbench against this script.
- **Failure:** In the preview, press Send and then New session within a second: the new conversation shows 'Add operations to a change set' asking permission, although nothing was asked of it. Press Stop right after Send: the permission request still appears after 'Stopped.'. A gate journey that runs inside that window reads the wrong state, and the refusal of a second launch is never exercised.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Capture the conversationId and a turn counter in later(), and skip steps from an older launch or a cancelled turn. Refuse a launch while an agent runs, as Desktop does. Guard: a node test of PreviewAgentSession with fake timers: after prompt, New session and 1 s, the new conversation has no entries; after prompt, cancel and 1 s, no permission request appears.
- **Verifier:** Reproduced against the real class with a fake clock (probe: scratchpad/review/verify/workbench-agent-ui-13/preview-probe.mjs). Send then Stop at 100 ms, wait 2 s: entries end 'notice:Stopped.', two tool entries, then an unanswered 'permission:Add operations to a change set'. Send then end+launch at 100 ms: the new conversation preview-2 holds the old turn's two tool entries and the permission request. launch() with an agent running returns preview-2 without refusing, where Desktop throws agent-already-running (DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:150-151). Cause: later() only checks state !== 'ended' (preview-agent-session.ts:232-234), launch() does not check this.agent (:111-117), and cancel() clears no timers (:166-174).
- **Correction:** This is a preview-fixture defect only, not a product one. The finding overstates the gate: Gate-AgentChat.mjs lets each turn finish (waits for Ready and the reply, lines 91-93 and 150-152) before pressing New session or opening a new tab, so no current journey reads the leaked state. It only bites a manual preview user, or a future journey that presses Stop or New session within 900 ms of Send.

### WST-04 — host-behavior's 'a host event never resolves a pending request' cannot fail: the fixture has already answered the request before the event is delivered

**P3** · test-gap · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/host-behavior.test.mjs:316`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/host-behavior.test.mjs:23`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:220`
- **What:** The fixture's postMessage answers session.getSnapshot synchronously (host-behavior.test.mjs:23). The test calls client.request('session.getSnapshot') and so gets an already-settled promise. Only then does it deliver the navigate event, then responds a second time. Any defect that lets an event resolve a pending request is invisible to it.
- **Failure:** A regression in DesktopWorkbenchClient.receive that routes a host event to the oldest pending request leaves this test green. A pending data write could then be resolved by an event payload, so the journal would be cleared and the save reported as committed without a receipt.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probes/host-event-falsify.mjs (src/host.ts built as shipped, and with a plant in receive() that resolves the oldest pending request on any host event; the test body run verbatim) -> 'as shipped answered before the event: 1 \| ... PASS' / 'planted defect answered before the event: 1 \| resolved fileName: fixture.nendo \| ... PASS'; with the fixture's automatic answer removed: 'unanswered, planted defect resolved fileName: resolved-by-event:agent \| FAIL'
- **Fix and guard:** In this test, use a bridge that records but does not answer session.getSnapshot, and preferably a journaled data.setFields as well. Deliver the event while the request is really pending, then respond. Keep the probe's planted defect as the falsification and quote its failure in the Finding.
- **Verifier:** host-behavior.test.mjs:23-24: the fixture bridge's postMessage answers session.getSnapshot synchronously with respond(...). host-desktop.ts:196-206 sets this.pending before bridge.postMessage, and receive() (host-desktop.ts:211-250) deletes the entry on that reply, so in the test at :316 the promise is already settled and the pending map is empty when deliver() sends the navigate event. The second f.respond(f.requests[0], ...) changes nothing. A regression that let an event resolve a pending request would find nothing to resolve, so the test cannot fail for the defect it names. The test is vacuous as written.
- **Correction:** The failure scenario is overstated. receive() routes responses strictly by requestId, and events are split off first by isHostEvent (host-desktop.ts:~221), so a data write being resolved by an event is not a realistic regression. Only the vacuity of the test is real.

### BL-05 — Test-Production's '--logger trx' writes a TestResults folder into each test project on every run and nothing removes it: 467 MB from 285 runs

### BL-07 — Eight tracked files carry a UTF-8 BOM although AGENTS.md says every tracked text file is UTF-8 without one, and the repository gate does not check it

**P3** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `baseline` · also reported as TGA-06

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Nendo.Engine.csproj:1`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/Nendo.LocalMcp.csproj:1`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests.csproj:1`, `tests/Nendo.Engine.Tests/MSTestSettings.cs:1`, `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests.csproj:1`, `tests/Nendo.LocalMcp.Tests/MSTestSettings.cs:1`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests.csproj:1`, `tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/MSTestSettings.cs:1`
- **What:** AGENTS.md 'Files and line endings': 'Every tracked text file is UTF-8 without a BOM and ends its lines with LF.' Test-Repository.ps1 refuses CRLF and mixed endings by file name but has no BOM check, so the template-generated csproj and MSTestSettings.cs files kept their EF BB BF prefix.
- **Failure:** A tool or check that relies on the stated rule (for example a byte comparison or a regex anchored at ^<Project) misreads these files; the rule in AGENTS.md is not what the tree holds.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: git ls-files \| python BOM scan -> 8 files starting with b'\xef\xbb\xbf': the three test csproj files, the three MSTestSettings.cs files, src/Nendo.Engine/Nendo.Engine.csproj and src/Nendo.LocalMcp/Nendo.LocalMcp.csproj.

AGENTS.md:105 and CONTRIBUTING.md:61 state 'UTF-8 without a BOM', and tools/Test-Repository.ps1:85-98 only inspects `git ls-files --eol` CRLF/mixed endings, so nothing checks a BOM. The drift between the written rule and the tree is real, but it is doc/tooling drift, not a defect: the rule sits under 'Files and line endings', not the enforced architecture invariants.
- **Correction:** The failure scenario is hypothetical. No consumer in the repo is BOM-sensitive: Test-Repository.ps1, Test-Production.ps1 and Test-BinaryAssets.ps1 read these files with .NET ReadAllText (which strips a BOM), MSBuild and the C# compiler accept the BOM, and no tool or regex anchors at '^<Project'. Practical impact is nil, so P3 is the ceiling. Test-Repository.ps1:85 is the line-ending section where a BOM check would go, so the fix location is right; the cheaper fix is to strip the three bytes from the eight files.

### DSH-18 — Release builds default to PublishTrimmed=True, which the shipped publish overrides; a plain 'dotnet publish -c Release' produces a host whose reflection-based bridge JSON is disabled

**P3** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Nendo.Desktop.csproj:69`, `tools/Publish-NendoPayload.ps1:47`
- **What:** The csproj sets PublishTrimmed True for every non-Debug configuration; Publish-NendoPayload.ps1 passes -p:PublishTrimmed=false. With trimming on, .NET disables reflection-based System.Text.Json by default, and WorkbenchProtocolHandler.Serialize (outside HandleAsync's try, inside the async void message handler) serialises anonymous types and records reflectively, as do every Desktop*Store and the [ComImport] interop.
- **Failure:** Someone publishes from Visual Studio or with 'dotnet publish -c Release': either the build fails on trim warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors) or, if it succeeds, the first bridge response throws in Serialize and ends the process.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Set PublishTrimmed false in the csproj for all configurations (matching the pipeline) or add a JsonSerializerContext and trim annotations. Guard: Test-Repository check that the csproj's PublishTrimmed agrees with Publish-NendoPayload.ps1.
- **Verifier:** Nendo.Desktop.csproj:72-73 sets PublishTrimmed=True for every non-Debug configuration, while tools/Publish-NendoPayload.ps1:47 overrides it with -p:PublishTrimmed=false; nothing else (no gate check) ties the two together. Microsoft.NET.ILLink.targets (microsoft.net.illink.tasks 10.0.8, lines 36-58) sets JsonSerializerIsReflectionEnabledByDefault=false and BuiltInComInteropSupport=false when PublishTrimmed=true. The host's bridge JSON and its [ComImport] taskbar and jump-list interop depend on both. Line 240 defaults ILLinkTreatWarningsAsErrors to TreatWarningsAsErrors, which Directory.Build.props sets true. A plain 'dotnet publish -c Release' therefore either fails on trim warnings or yields a host that breaks at runtime. I did not run it, as dotnet builds were off limits.
- **Correction:** The runtimeconfig switches key off PublishTrimmed at evaluation time, so even a Release build (not just publish) of the host would carry them. The sanctioned pipeline overrides the property, so only an unsanctioned publish is affected. Latent trap, not a shipped defect.

Meanwhile roadmap.md:23 hard-codes 'The current version is 0.19.0' and getting-started.md:16 hard-codes the SDK '10.0.204'. git show --stat 205be7a ('Cut 0.19.0') touched Directory.Build.props, README.md and site/src/content/docs/roadmap.md: the deploy only fired because the hard-coded copy was edited by hand.

- **Reproduction:** Executed: git show --stat 205be7a -> 'Directory.Build.props \| 2 +-', 'README.md \| 2 +-', 'site/src/content/docs/roadmap.md \| 2 +-'
- **Fix and guard:** Add Directory.Build.props (and global.json) to the pages.yml paths filter, and render the version in roadmap.md from version.ts (an MDX import or a remark substitution) instead of literal text. Guard: a check-links-style post-build assertion that every 'v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+' product version in dist equals version.ts.
- **Verifier:** site/src/version.ts:3 imports ../../Directory.Build.props?raw and index.astro:46 prints v{version}, but .github/workflows/pages.yml:9-13 triggers only on site/**, docs/assets/brand/**, AppIcon.ico and the workflow, so a push that changes only Directory.Build.props runs no deploy (GitHub paths filter semantics). The other two build inputs the site reads (brand assets, AppIcon.ico per scripts/sync-repo-assets.mjs) are in the filter; this one was added without widening it (commit 12d3bbb touched only site/ files). site/src/content/docs/roadmap.md:23 hard-codes 'The current version is 0.19.0' and getting-started.md:16 hard-codes 10.0.204 (matches global.json today). git show --stat 205be7a confirms the cut touched roadmap.md, which is the only reason that cut deployed.
- **Correction:** The failure needs a version bump with no site edit. Every recent 'Cut' commit (0.15 to 0.19) edits site/src/content/docs/roadmap.md in the same commit (git log), so the owner's routine currently prevents it; the defect is the deterministic filter gap plus a hand-copied version, not an observed stale site. No public release exists, so impact is a stale badge: P3.

<a id="tbi-06"></a>

### TBI-06 — nendo.nsi is written as UTF-8 without a BOM and makensis reads it as ACP, so the installer cannot be built from a path with any non-ASCII character

**P3** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:137`, `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:138`, `tools/Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:40`
- **What:** '$lines \| Set-Content -LiteralPath $script' under pwsh 7, which the docs prescribe, writes UTF-8 without a BOM. 'makensis $script' is called without /INPUTCHARSET, so it decodes the script in the ANSI code page. Absolute File paths that contain a character such as 'ø' turn into mojibake. The legacy fixture script is written the same way.
- **Failure:** A contributor whose profile or checkout path is, for example, C:\Users\Jørgen\Projects\nendo runs Build-NendoInstaller.ps1. Every 'File' line reports 'no files found' and the build fails with only 'Installer build failed. See .../installer-build.log'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: nsis-encoding-probe.ps1 (pwsh 7.6, Set-Content into a folder named 'Jørgen Ø'; first bytes '4f 75 74', no BOM) -> as built: makensis 'Processing script file ... (ACP)', 'File: "...\Jørgen Ø\payload.txt" -> no files found.', 'Error in script ... on line 7 -- aborting creation process'. With /INPUTCHARSET UTF8: '(UTF8)' ... 'Total size: 39324 / 44595 bytes (88.1%)'.
- **Fix and guard:** Call 'makensis /INPUTCHARSET UTF8 $script' in both scripts, or write the .nsi with -Encoding utf8BOM. Guard: a step in Build-NendoInstaller.ps1, or a repository check, that compiles a one-file script from a scratch folder with a non-ASCII name.
- **Verifier:** Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:137 does '$lines \| Set-Content -LiteralPath $script' with no -Encoding, and :138 runs 'makensis $script' with no /INPUTCHARSET. Under pwsh 7 (the documented shell) Set-Content writes UTF-8 without a BOM, and makensis 3.x decodes a BOM-less script as ACP; the generated absolute 'File' paths (66, 69, 70) and the MUI_ICON defines (57-58) therefore break on a non-ASCII character in the checkout path. The reviewer's probe logs (nsis-probe-as-built.log) show 'Processing script file ... (ACP)', 'File: ... -> no files found', 'Error in script', while /INPUTCHARSET UTF8 builds. The same pattern is at Test-NendoLegacyUpgrade.ps1:40. Under Windows PowerShell 5.1 Set-Content writes the ANSI code page and would work, so this is pwsh-7-specific. It is a latent portability defect: the owner's path (C:\Users\thoma\Projects\nendo) is ASCII and the project is a one-person repo, so it does not bite here.
- **Correction:** Low likelihood; P3 is right. Passing /INPUTCHARSET UTF8 to makensis (both scripts) or writing with -Encoding utf8BOM is a one-line fix.

<a id="tga-12"></a>

### TGA-12 — The node_modules and bin/obj path exclusions in two gate checks never match a Windows path

**P3** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `tools-gates`

- **Where:** `tools/Test-Production.ps1:353`, `tools/Test-Repository.ps1:142`
- **What:** Both use `'[\/](?:node_modules\|dist)[\/]'` and `'[\/](?:bin\|obj)[\/]'`. In .NET regex, `[\/]` is a class holding only '/', but Get-ChildItem returns backslash paths. The other filters in the same files use `[\\/]` correctly (for example Test-Production.ps1:111 and 233). The bug is latent today because neither tree holds such a folder.
- **Failure:** Once src/Nendo.LocalMcp gets an obj folder (a build with ArtifactsPath off, or an IDE design-time build), generated .cs files are counted in the MCP surface count. Once src/Nendo.Workbench/src gets a dist folder, the browser-dialog check scans bundled vendor code and fails on a third-party confirm(). Either way the gate fails for the wrong reason.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: "filter as written in Test-Production.ps1:353 excludes it? " + (-not ('C:\x\src\node_modules\y.ts' -notmatch '[\/](?:node_modules\|dist)[\/]')) -> "... excludes it? False". With `[\\/]` -> "True".
- **Fix and guard:** Write `[\\/]` in both filters. Guard: a self-check that feeds a synthetic backslash path through each filter and asserts it is excluded.
- **Verifier:** The filter defect is reproduced. tools/Test-Production.ps1:353 uses '[\/](?:node_modules\|dist)[\/]' and tools/Test-Repository.ps1:142 uses '[\/](?:bin\|obj)[\/]'. In .NET `[\/]` holds only '/', and I ran it: `'C:\x\src\node_modules\y.ts' -notmatch '[\/](?:node_modules\|dist)[\/]'` returned True (not excluded), and the obj path likewise, while `[\\/]` as used at Test-Production.ps1:111,233 returned False (excluded). So both exclusions are dead on Windows. It is a latent slip with no live effect, and the finding says so itself.
- **Correction:** The failure scenarios are unreachable under the current layout, so the finding overstates the risk. Directory.Build.props sets ArtifactsPath, which sends bin/obj to artifacts/ (no obj exists under src/Nendo.LocalMcp today, and design-time builds read the same props). The Workbench's node_modules and dist sit at src/Nendo.Workbench/, while the Test-Production.ps1:350-354 scan covers only src/Nendo.Workbench/src (vite.config.ts outDir is 'dist' at the Workbench root). Keep it as a one-character correctness fix, not as a way the gate can fail for the wrong reason today.
