### TGA-13 — The bundled-Workbench check passes on any Desktop output, including a stale one from another configuration

**P3** · build-tooling · Confirmed · area `tools-gates`

- **Where:** `tools/Test-Production.ps1:96`
- **What:** The check is `Get-ChildItem artifacts\bin\Nendo.Desktop -Recurse -Filter index.html \| Where-Object DirectoryName -match 'Workbench$'`, which passes when the count is above zero. artifacts/bin/Nendo.Desktop currently holds debug_win-x64, debug_win-arm64 and release_win-x64, and both x64 outputs carry Workbench/index.html. The gate only builds Debug.
- **Failure:** A change breaks the Workbench copy into the Debug output. The left-over release_win-x64/Workbench/index.html satisfies the check, which prints 'OK bundled Workbench entry point (1 output(s))', and the Debug app the tests ran against has no page.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Check the output this gate built (artifacts/bin/Nendo.Desktop/debug_win-x64/Workbench/index.html). Compare its hash with src/Nendo.Workbench/dist/index.html from the build step that just ran. Guard: delete the debug copy, leave the release one in place, and watch the check fail.
- **Verifier:** tools/Test-Production.ps1:96-103 searches all of artifacts\bin\Nendo.Desktop recursively for any index.html whose directory ends in Workbench and passes on a count above zero. artifacts/bin/Nendo.Desktop currently holds debug_win-x64, debug_win-arm64 and release_win-x64, and the debug_win-x64 and release_win-x64 outputs both carry Workbench/index.html. The gate builds only Debug (line 82 `dotnet build Nendo.slnx`). The Desktop csproj copies the bundle with `<Content Include="..\Nendo.Workbench\dist\**\*">` (Nendo.Desktop.csproj:62), which copies nothing without error if the glob or link breaks. No later step of Test-Production runs a native lane against the Debug exe (lines 389-399 are the browser preview lanes), and grep of tests/ finds no test of the output's Workbench folder. So this is the only gate check on that bundle, and a stale output from another configuration satisfies it.
- **Correction:** The check is weaker than described in one more way: MSBuild's PreserveNewest copy leaves old files in place, so a stale debug_win-x64/Workbench would also pass a check pointed at the Debug folder alone. The finding's hash comparison against src/Nendo.Workbench/dist/index.html is the part of the fix that catches that; pointing the check at the Debug folder is not enough on its own.

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `baseline`

- **What:** README.md:116-118: 'The Desktop project copies src/Nendo.Workbench/dist into its output but does not build it, so dotnet build on a fresh clone succeeds and produces a host with no interface to show.' Nendo.LocalMcp.csproj's RequireViewApiReference target errors before PrepareForBuild when ..\Nendo.Workbench\dist\_nendo\view-api.json does not exist, so the solution build fails on a fresh clone. README.md:134, AGENTS.md:254, CONTRIBUTING.md:43 and the getting-started guide say the gate takes about a minute; the .NET tests alone take several.
- **Failure:** A contributor follows the README's description, skips the Workbench step, and gets a build error the README told them would not happen; anyone budgeting for 'about a minute' sees a gate that takes five or more and assumes it hung.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: dotnet msbuild src/Nendo.LocalMcp/Nendo.LocalMcp.csproj -t:RequireViewApiReference -p:ViewApiReference=..\Nendo.Workbench\dist-missing\_nendo\view-api.json -> 'error : src/Nendo.Workbench/dist/_nendo/view-api.json is missing, and the local MCP serves it as nendo://application/view-api. - **Fix and guard:** Change README.md:116-118 to say dotnet build fails with the LocalMcp message until the Workbench is built, and replace 'about a minute' with the measured figure (or 'a few minutes') in README, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ADR-0018 and the getting-started guide. Guard: Test-Repository could fail when README carries 'fresh clone succeeds' while Nendo.LocalMcp.csproj declares RequireViewApiReference.

The timing claim holds too: README.md:134, AGENTS.md:254, CONTRIBUTING.md:43, ADR-0018:33, architecture.md:1064 and getting-started.md:33 all say 'about a minute', while the Engine tests alone ran 140.5 s in the baseline run.
- **Correction:** Practical harm is small. The very next sentence in README.md:114 says 'Do not skip the Workbench step', so a reader who follows it never hits the error. Only the stated consequence is wrong (the build fails rather than producing an interfaceless host). Documentation drift at P3.

- **What:** custom-views.md:107-109: 'Studio's History offers Compensate on such a revision, and one compensation reverses at most 128 operations.' - **Failure:** A contributor adding a new protected table (memory: 'Field metadata goes on the layout ladder ... as the last rung') reads relationships.md and inserts the rung after link_rule instead of after search, producing a layout signature no existing file matches.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: python drift_probe.py -> "longest layout: production-semantic-reference-deletion-choice-retirement-behaviour-tone-scale-purpose-extension-hierarchy-rule-look-fold-newfile-skill-linkrule-search-v1" and each cited line printed with 'the last rung'
- **Fix and guard:** Reword each to name its neighbour ('the rung after the extension rung', 'after the skill rung', etc.) as architecture.md does. Guard: a docs lint that refuses the phrase 'last rung' in docs/contracts outside history.
- **Verifier:** SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:820-842 builds the ladder through ...-hierarchy-rule-look-fold-newfile-skill-linkrule-search-v1, so the last rung is search. In present tense, docs/contracts/relationships.md:39 (`__nendo_hierarchy`), :87 (`__nendo_field_rule`) and :135 (`__nendo_link_rule`) call their tables 'the last rung of the layout ladder', and custom-views.md:49 and :298 say the same of the package tables and `__nendo_extension_kind`. Each was true when written and is now false; architecture.md:70 correctly says 'then-last rung'. The ADRs use 'new last rung' as a dated decision statement, which is fine.
- **Correction:** Impact is low: a contributor adding a rung is directed by AGENTS.md/memory to the ladder in Inspection.cs, which is the authority, so the 'inserts it after link_rule' scenario is unlikely. Pure wording drift; fix by naming the neighbour rung or saying 'added to the layout ladder' without 'last'.

- **What:** custom-view-authoring.md:333-334: 'A query cannot filter or sort by a calculated field.' The broker passes filters and sortFieldId straight to data.queryRecords (extension-broker.ts:529-531), and queries.md:19-26 (F-222, 2026-09-30) says the sort field and any predicate may name a calculated field, worked out over at most 10,000 records; custom-views.md:649-651 says the same for views.

### DOC-12 — Authoring guide says Put-NendoPackage sends each operation as its own mutation; it packs up to 16 per mutation

Put-NendoPackage.mjs:151-159 packs operations into mutations by size, up to OPERATIONS_PER_MUTATION = 16, and mcp-interface.md:492-493 says the uploader packs up to sixteen operations per call. Line 817-818 of the guide itself says one mutation becomes one revision.
- **Failure:** An author expects one History revision per file and per-file undo; they get a few revisions covering many files and compensate more than they meant to.

- **Fix and guard:** Say the script packs operations into mutations of up to 16 by size, each a revision. Guard: review only.

Lines 153-160 pack operations into a mutation until it holds 16 operations or exceeds CALL_CHARACTERS, so many small files share one mutation. The guide's own :817-818 says one mutation becomes one revision, so History shows one revision per packed mutation, not per file. The doc claim is wrong, and the consequence is only an author's expectation about per-file compensation.

The 16-per-mutation limit comes from the script constant at Put-NendoPackage.mjs:33 and the :102 check. The fix text should say operations are packed into mutations of up to 16 operations (also size-bounded), each mutation being one revision.

### DOC-14 — Semantic-surfaces says the host never fills in or enforces uniqueness of a Reference code; ADR-0020 numbered fields do both

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `docs-drift` · also reported as ESM-25

- **Where:** `docs/contracts/semantic-surfaces.md:1123`, `docs/contracts/relationships.md:107`, `docs/dogfooding.md:128`
- **What:** semantic-surfaces.md:1123-1126: 'Nothing here allocates the reference codes ... The host requires a Reference field to be non-empty. It does not fill the field in, enforce uniqueness or stop a change to it. So in a file whose records are named by hand, a person still decides which name is next.' Since ADR-0020 a unique Text field can carry a sequence the host writes on create when left empty, and duplicates are refused as value-not-unique (relationships.md:80-122; Studio shows 'Assigned when saved', studio.md:120-122); dogfooding.md:128-133 says the planner's Reference is unique and numbered.
- **Failure:** An author building a related-list Add flow adds a manual code-picking step or an action to number records, not knowing schema.setFieldSequence exists.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Replace the paragraph with: a Reference that is a numbered unique field is assigned by the host in the Add form's create; otherwise the person names it. Guard: review only.
- **Verifier:** semantic-surfaces.md:1123-1126 says the host 'does not fill the field in, enforce uniqueness or stop a change to it'. That paragraph dates from the initial release (2026-09-22) and predates ADR-0020 (accepted 2026-09-27), after which a unique Text field can carry a sequence that the host writes on any create that leaves it empty, and duplicates are refused as value-not-unique (relationships.md:80-122; studio.md:120-122; record-markup.ts:427 renders 'Assigned when saved'; dogfooding.md:128-133 documents the planner's numbered Reference). The paragraph was not updated when ADR-0020 landed. It is a documentation omission only.
- **Correction:** The paragraph is incomplete rather than flatly false. For a field not declared unique or numbered it is still right: the host does nothing. The sentence 'Nothing here allocates' can also be read as scoped to the Add flow, so the failure scenario (an author adds a manual numbering step) is speculative. The fix should add the opt-in: a Reference code that is a numbered unique field (schema.setFieldSequence) is assigned by the host inside the Add form's create, otherwise the person names it. Also 'Reference field' here is ambiguous: elsewhere in this file 'Reference' means the relation field type, whereas this paragraph means a code field named Reference.

### ECO-13 — Proposal retention is described as 'until explicit cleanup' and as surviving sessions, but every workspace is deleted when the file opens or closes

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/ProposalModel.cs:16`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ProposalWorkspace.cs:76`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ProposalWorkspace.cs:222`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:163`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:49`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:403`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentProposals.cs:140`
- **What:** Every preview reports NendoProposalRetention.RetainUntilExplicitCleanup (ProposalWorkspace.cs:76), which MCP describes as 'the proposal stays until it is accepted or rejected' (NendoAgentProposals.cs:140). ReadPlanAsync says 'A proposal outlives the session that made it' (ProposalWorkspace.cs:222-225), and promotion says 'a proposal reviewed in one session promotes the same way in the next one' (Promotion.cs:163-166). The constructor and DisposeAsync call CleanupAbandoned with no retained set (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:49, 403), and the Desktop warns that closing discards pending proposals (MainPage.FileActions.cs:139). ADR-0007 permits discarding, but the code and contract text say otherwise.
- **Failure:** An agent hands over a proposal by title, trusting 'retainUntilExplicitCleanup'. The owner upgrades Nendo or closes the file before accepting, and the proposal is gone with no record, which is what memory note 'Proposal lost across an upgrade' describes.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Rename the retention value to one meaning 'discarded when the file closes', correct the MCP description and the two code comments, and have the MCP instructions tell agents to ask for acceptance before the file is closed. Guard: a test asserting the preview's retention value, plus an MCP description lint for the new wording.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. The constructor calls ProposalWorkspace.CleanupAbandoned(_proposalRoot) with no retained set (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:49), so every proposal-* workspace is deleted when a file opens. DisposeAsync clears _proposals and sweeps again (cs:402-403). Nothing reloads a proposal from disk, and ProposalLifecycleTests.cs:248 (ReopenRemovesOnlyAbandonedProposalDirectoriesForTheApplication) pins the sweep. The Desktop confirm dialogs say pending proposals are discarded (MainPage.FileActions.cs:139,167,187), and ADR-0007:108,128 says there is no durable continuation of unaccepted proposals. Against that, the enum value and MCP description say 'retainUntilExplicitCleanup: the proposal stays until it is accepted or rejected' (ProposalWorkspace.cs:76, NendoAgentProposals.cs:140). The comments say 'A proposal outlives the session that made it ... closing the application' (ProposalWorkspace.cs:222-225), 'promotes the same way in the next one' (Promotion.cs:163-166) and 'lets a plan outlive the session that reviewed it' (Behaviour/OperationCodec.cs:14-15). They are false for a file close, or for a restart. This is documentation and agent-facing description drift only: behaviour matches the ADR, and the data-loss risk is bounded because an unaccepted proposal can be re-authored. P3 is right.
- **Correction:** Narrow the claim: no contract or doc states the retention, so 'code and contract text say otherwise' really means one MCP property description plus the enum name and three code comments (a fourth, OperationCodec.cs:14, is not cited). ADR-0007 already records the discard. NendoLeaseTools.cs:74 correctly scopes carry-over to 'this host run'. The memory note says the cause of the 2026-09-23 lost proposal was never investigated, so the upgrade scenario is consistent with the drift but is not evidence of it. Renaming the enum value changes a wire value that src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-preview.ts and NendoMcpResources.cs:364 also use, so correcting the description and the comments is the cheaper fix.

- **What:** ValidateDraftAsync returns NendoAgentProposalStore.ProjectPreview(preview), and PreviewAsync returns GetOwned -> TryGetOwned -> ProjectPreview(entry.Preview). ### MHS-10 — A call caught by the endpoint closing loses NENDO_HOST_CLOSED's remedy, and at the filter loses the code itself

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `mcp-host-security`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoToolErrors.cs:162`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpErrors.cs:29`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:482`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:519`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoHostAuthority.cs:24`, `docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md:581`
- **What:** NendoHostAuthority.RequireActive throws NendoAgentAuthorityException("HOST_CLOSED"), which is not an McpException. NendoToolErrors.AuthorityMessage has an arm for every authority code except HOST_CLOSED, so a tool answers with the default 'Agent authority rejected the request.', and NendoMcpErrors.Translate says the same for every authority code on a resource read. The CallToolFilter's own authority.RequireActive() (line 482) runs inside a try whose McpException arm does not match, so the generic catch rethrows and the SDK writes its bare "An error occurred invoking '<tool>'." with no code at all. The read filter (line 519), the list filters and skills/list and skills/get turn the same exception into a code-less -32603. The contract says that `NENDO_HOST_CLOSED` says why an endpoint closes and where the current one is shown. Only the middleware's 401, at the perimeter, does.
- **Failure:** An agent sends several writes. They queue behind one long call on NendoAgentAuthority._gate, and meanwhile the person switches file or changes the access level. Each queued write then gets `NENDO_HOST_CLOSED: Agent authority rejected the request.`, or a call that reaches the filter just after admission closed gets 'An error occurred invoking ...' with no code. Neither tells the agent that the file was closed or switched, or that the Agent page shows the current address, so it retries against a dead endpoint or reports an internal failure.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-host-closed.ps1 (NendoHostAuthority.CloseAdmission, then RequireActive, then both translators, by reflection) -> `RequireActive throws: Nendo.LocalMcp.NendoAgentAuthorityException (is McpException: False)` / `tool refusal: NENDO_HOST_CLOSED: Agent authority rejected the request.` / `resource refusal: NENDO_HOST_CLOSED: Agent authority rejected the request.`
- **Fix and guard:** Add a HOST_CLOSED arm to AuthorityMessage that reuses the middleware's sentence, and route NendoMcpErrors' authority arm through the same table. In the host's filters, catch NendoAgentAuthorityException and rethrow it through NendoToolErrors.Translate (tools) or NendoMcpErrors.Translate (reads, lists, skills). Guard: a StructuredRefusalTests case that closes admission while a write waits on the lease gate, and another that closes it between the middleware and the filter, each asserting the code and the remedy sentence in the text and in _meta.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. NendoHostAuthority.RequireActive (NendoHostAuthority.cs:22-25) throws NendoAgentAuthorityException("HOST_CLOSED", ...), and NendoToolErrors.AuthorityMessage (NendoToolErrors.cs:145-163) has no HOST_CLOSED arm, so it falls to "Agent authority rejected the request.". NendoMcpErrors.Translate (NendoMcpErrors.cs:27-29) gives that same text for every authority code. The queued-write path is reachable: DisposeAsync calls CloseAdmission first (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:679), and a write already waiting on _gate then runs host.RequireActive() at NendoAgentAuthority.cs:382. That throws inside NendoToolCall.RunAsync, which routes it to NendoToolErrors.Translate (NendoToolCall.cs:37). The agent gets the NENDO_HOST_CLOSED code with no remedy sentence. The filter claim also holds on the source: authority.RequireActive() at NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:482 throws a non-McpException that no catch arm there turns into a result. The comment at lines 488-490 says the SDK writes the error result above the filter, so the client sees only the SDK's generic text. The list, skills and read filters (412-459, 519) have the same gap.
- **Correction:** Minor overstatement. The filter-level loss of the code is a narrow race, because the middleware checks authority.IsActive at NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:173 just before next(context), so only a close landing in that window reaches the filter. The reachable case is the queued-write path, which keeps the NENDO_HOST_CLOSED code and loses only the remedy text. The contract line (mcp-interface.md:581) sits in the bullet about the perimeter's refusals, and the middleware's 401 does satisfy it, so the doc drift is partial: the sentence is accurate for the perimeter and not for inner paths. The impact is message quality only; the host is stopping, so a retry meets a refused connection or the middleware's full 401. P3 is right.

### MTD-15 — The records read's description points at vocabulary entries that do not say what it claims: 'the vocabulary's filterOperators' and 'limits.query'

- **What:** The description lists eq ... contains, isNull, isNotNull, descendantOf as '(the vocabulary's filterOperators)', but the vocabulary's FilterOperators are eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, isNull, isNotNull; contains and descendantOf are records-read only (the projection's own comment says so). The operator wording is also loose: the vocabulary's FilterOperators (SemanticVocabulary.cs:334) are eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, isNull, isNotNull, and NendoResourceProjection.cs:292 itself says the read adds two beyond the vocabulary.
- **Correction:** The operator half is weaker than stated: the same description lists all ten operators explicitly and the contract (mcp-interface.md:286) words it exactly ('the vocabulary's filterOperators ... plus contains and descendantOf'), so only the parenthetical in the attribute text is imprecise and an agent can still use contains. The limits.query half is the solid part. Pure doc drift, P3.

### R2AAV-10 — ADR-0001 still says a custom-view package is the one executable payload a file may carry; ADR-0024, ADR-0027 and ADR-0029 added skill and help packages and client-run skill scripts without touching it

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `r2-adr-and-vision-conformance`

- **Where:** `docs/decisions/0001-local-one-file-product-boundary.md:107`, `docs/decisions/0001-local-one-file-product-boundary.md:131`, `docs/decisions/0029-a-skill-may-carry-scripts-its-client-runs.md:17`
- **What:** ADR-0001 Consequences/Negative: 'A custom-view package, with its code and assets, is the one executable payload that a file may carry (ADR-0013).' Its History stops at 2026-09-25. ADR-0029 (Accepted 2026-10-08) lets a skill package carry scripts that the agent's client runs, and ADR-0024 and ADR-0027 add package kinds and uses. Each amends only ADR-0013 or ADR-0024, so ADR-0001, which AGENTS.md lists among the architecture authority, now misstates what executable content a .nendo file carries.
- **Failure:** A reviewer who checks a received file's risk against the product boundary reads that only view code can be executable. A skill package's .mjs scanner, which an agent may run on the person's machine, is then outside what the boundary document says can be there.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Add a dated History entry and amend the Negative bullet of ADR-0001: views run in Nendo; a skill may carry scripts that its client runs and Nendo never runs (ADR-0029); help pages are text (ADR-0027). Guard: none beyond review, because this changes documentation only.
- **Verifier:** ADR-0001:107-109 still says a custom-view package is 'the one executable payload that a file may carry (ADR-0013)'. Its History (lines 133-137) stops at the 2026-09-25 ADR-0013 entry. ADR-0029 (Accepted 2026-10-08) lets a skill package's supporting files include .js/.mjs/.ps1/.py/.sh/.cmd/.bat scripts that a connected agent's client runs. It says validation does not refuse them today (Context, lines 25-28). Its Amends line (17-18) lists ADR-0024 and the reading of ADR-0013, but not ADR-0001. ADR-0024 carries an 'Amended by ADR-0029' header (line 12), and ADR-0029 updated AGENTS.md and the vision, so ADR-0001 was the one boundary statement missed. The text is now inaccurate, and the ADR-0001 sentence is still read as boundary authority. The product boundary does not move, since Nendo never runs a skill script, so the harm is only a stale accepted ADR. Priority P3.
- **Correction:** ADR-0027 (help pages) is text-only and is not part of the drift, so only ADR-0029 matters. The failure scenario is hypothetical, but the stale-sentence defect is real. The fix is a dated History entry and a reworded Negative bullet in ADR-0001, with no code or guard.

### TBI-15 — Build-NendoInstaller's comment says installer rotation never happens on a development machine; it happens on every rebuild

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:140`, `tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:157`
- **What:** The NOTE at lines 140-144 says installer-status.json is written by Test-NendoInstaller.ps1 and that rotation therefore does not happen where Nendo is installed. The same script writes installer-status.json at line 177, so after any build the status hash matches Nendo-Setup.exe and the next build always moves it to Nendo-Setup.previous.exe. The 'only a checked binary becomes the rollback copy' reading of the comment is false: the previous copy is just the previous build, checked or not.
- **Failure:** A reader trusts that Nendo-Setup.previous.exe is a lane-checked rollback, or that it stays put on a development machine. Neither is true. Rebuilding twice from one payload makes 'previous' the same build, so Test-NendoInstaller's upgrade-from-previous step tests nothing.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: ls artifacts/installer -> Nendo-Setup.previous.exe (2026-10-10 10:09) and previous-installer-status.json with buildId 74e120c0a65af07c and nsisWrapper 'not run for this build', on this development machine where Test-NendoInstaller refuses to run.
- **Fix and guard:** Correct the comment to describe the actual rule. If the intent was to keep only a checked rollback, rotate only when lanes.nsisWrapper.status is 'passed'. Guard: none needed for a comment; for the behavioural variant, a Pester-style test of the rotation predicate.
- **Verifier:** tools/Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:140-144 says installer-status.json is written by Test-NendoInstaller.ps1 and that rotation therefore does not happen where Nendo is installed. The same script writes installer-status.json itself at lines 157-177, with sha256 = hash of the just-built Nendo-Setup.exe, so on the next build the check at lines 146-148 (hash of installer equals status.sha256) always passes and lines 149-150 move it to Nendo-Setup.previous.exe. Test-NendoInstaller.ps1:128 only updates its lane entry in a file Build already created. Observed in artifacts/installer: Nendo-Setup.exe 2026-10-10 15:06, Nendo-Setup.previous.exe 10:09, previous-installer-status.json 10:10, installer-status.json 15:07, on a machine where Test-NendoInstaller refuses to run. So the NOTE is false and the previous copy is simply the previous build. Pure comment drift, P3.
- **Correction:** The side claim that Test-NendoInstaller's upgrade-from-previous step 'tests nothing' when previous and current share a payload is overstated: Test-NendoInstaller.ps1:59-66 injects an obsolete owned file into the old inventory, so the upgrade path and obsolete-file removal still run. The comment text is the whole defect.

### WAU-15 — Open conversation opens a second conversation tab when the conversation's own tab has moved on, although the contract says one conversation never has two tabs

- **What:** openTabOn('agentChat') matches only a tab whose current place is the conversation (workspace-tabs.ts:161). The ACP-06 fix deliberately keeps a tab that went on to another page as the conversation's owner (trailHolds). From that state, Open conversation (view-agent.ts:226, agent-launch-model.ts:142) creates a new tab on the conversation, while the old tab still holds it and returns to it with Back. The contract says 'one conversation never has two tabs' (launched-agents.md:231).
- **Failure:** From the conversation's tab, the person goes to the Agent page and presses Open conversation. A second tab opens on the conversation, and Back in the first tab shows it again. Both tabs carry the activity mark, and both must be closed before the agent ends.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** For a one-of-a-kind view, have openTabOn prefer a tab whose trail holds it: switch to that tab and move it to the conversation. Otherwise, change the contract to say what happens. Guard: a navigation or gate test checks that conversation, then Agent, then Open conversation leaves exactly one tab holding agentChat.
- **Verifier:** Traced end to end. openTabOn matches only a tab whose current place has the view (workspace-tabs.ts:161, placeOf at :48-51 reads the trail cursor), so a conversation tab that went on to Data or the Agent page is not found and newTab(false) opens another tab on the conversation (workspace-tabs.ts:163-165). The ACP-06 fix keeps the old tab as an owner through trailHolds (tab-set.ts:76), so both tabs then hold agentChat, and the agent ends only when both close (view-agent-chat.ts:103-116). docs/contracts/launched-agents.md:228-231 says one conversation never has two tabs, and ADR-0030 says Open conversation reuses its tab. The route is natural: launch from the Agent page, look at Data in the conversation's tab, return to the Agent page's tab and press Open conversation. Minor, so P3.
- **Correction:** The activity mark appears on a tab only while its current place is the conversation (statusOf(place), workspace-tabs.ts:115), so the old tab carries it only after Back. tab-set.ts:81-82 words the invariant as two tabs never showing one conversation, which holds at any instant until Back; the contract's wording is the looser one.

### WSP-23 — Help names controls and screen behaviour that do not match the screen

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help.ts:139`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/help-concepts.ts:156`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-proposal.ts:29`
- **What:** The generated reference tells the person "Open Use and select X in Record type" for every type with a plan. The picker is labelled "Showing" when the file has a front page or file views (file-view-model.ts:67), and it leaves out types whose only roots are a record page and commands (plan-selection.ts:46). The 'lanes' topic describes a "What this builds" panel and says Accept "stays unavailable until [diagnostics] are gone". Studio's review heads that panel "Preview", and it keeps Accept enabled for a previewable proposal that shows warning diagnostics (view-proposal.ts:29-30).
- **Failure:** In a file with a front page, Help sends the person to a "Record type" picker that does not exist under that name. For a join type it names a place that is not offered at all.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Generate the label from showingLabel() and the place list from placePlans(). Match the lanes text to the review as built. Guard: help.test.mjs parity checks against those functions.
- **Verifier:** docs/contracts/help.md:41 requires help to say what the code does today, in the words the screen uses. help.ts:139 emits 'Open Use and select X in Record type' for every type that has a plan, but file-view-model.ts:67 showingLabel() returns 'Showing' when the file has a front page or file views, and plan-selection.ts:46 placePlans() leaves out types with no use surfaces, so a join type named by the help is not offered. help-concepts.ts:156 says the review has 'What this builds' and that Accept 'stays unavailable until they are gone'. view-proposal.ts:28 (Studio's review) heads the panel 'Preview', and Accept (line 29) is disabled only for a non-previewable state or a consent block, not for diagnostics. Previewable also holds when a file has no UI nodes even though compilation reports diagnostics (Proposals.cs:~140). The topic's last paragraph says Studio actions 'open the same review'.
- **Correction:** Two qualifications. The 'Showing' label is visually-hidden (file-views.ts:33, view-use.ts:167), so only screen-reader users meet that wording and the first sub-claim is weak. The agent review (view-agent.ts:360) does use 'What this builds' and disables Accept for error diagnostics, so help-concepts.ts:156 is accurate for that review. The drift is confined to Studio's review heading and the diagnostics-versus-Accept sentence. Pure doc drift, P3.

### WST-14 — README says verify:dependencies fails the build on licence keys, CDNs and host-object bridges; the script checks only the dependency names and two lockfile tokens

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `workbench-scripts-tests`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/README.md:168`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/scripts/verify-dependencies.mjs:9`
- **What:** README: 'React, AG Grid Enterprise, licence keys, CDNs and arbitrary host-object bridges are out of scope, and `verify:dependencies` fails the build if one appears.' verify-dependencies.mjs only requires Object.keys(dependencies) to equal ['ag-grid-community'] and the lockfile text to lack node_modules/ag-grid-enterprise, node_modules/react and node_modules/react-dom. Nothing in Test-Production.ps1 or Test-Repository.ps1 searches for LicenseManager/setLicenseKey, a CDN URL or AddHostObjectToScript. The script also does not check devDependencies or that versions are exact pins.
- **Failure:** A change adds AddHostObjectToScript in Nendo.Desktop, or a licence key string in src/. Every lane passes, while the README tells the reviewer the dependency gate would have refused it.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Either narrow the README to what the script checks, or extend verify-dependencies.mjs to scan src/ and index.html for LicenseManager/setLicenseKey and non-local http(s) script or style URLs, and Nendo.Desktop for AddHostObjectToScript, and to require exact versions in both dependency maps. Falsify each new check with a one-line plant.
- **Verifier:** src/Nendo.Workbench/README.md:38-41 says React, AG Grid Enterprise, licence keys, CDNs and host-object bridges are out of scope and that verify:dependencies fails the build if one appears. scripts/verify-dependencies.mjs:8-27 only requires Object.keys(dependencies) to equal ['ag-grid-community'] and the lockfile text to lack node_modules/ag-grid-enterprise, node_modules/react and node_modules/react-dom. I grepped tools/*.ps1, src, tests and scripts for AddHostObjectToScript, setLicenseKey, LicenseManager and CDN URL patterns and found no guard. Test-Production.ps1 runs verify:dependencies at line 74 and its other checks cover only SQLite escape, a catch-all resource filter, NCalc and similar. The only host-object control is a setting, AreHostObjectsAllowed = false at src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:192, with no test. A host-object bridge or licence key would pass every lane, so the README overstates the script. ADR-0015 and ADR-0017 do forbid these things, but they mandate the policy, not the claim that this script enforces it.
- **Correction:** The cited location README.md:168 does not exist; the file is 49 lines and the sentence is at lines 38-41. Partial cover exists for CDNs: scripts/csp.test.mjs pins index.html's CSP (script-src and connect-src 'self'), so a CDN script or fetch is also blocked at runtime. The CSP test does not scan src/ for URLs, so the README is still wrong for CDNs in the strict sense. The note that devDependencies and exact pins are unchecked is an extra observation, not something the README claims. This is documentation drift only, so P3 stands. The simplest fix is to narrow the README to what the script checks.

### WXS-19 — Custom-view docs disagree with the code: event lists, filter operators, filters on calculated fields, the toolbar's '128 in all' and the view-api context

**P3** · docs-drift · Confirmed · area `workbench-extension-sandbox`

- **Where:** `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:587`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:1127`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:646`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/reference.ts:331`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/reference.ts:290`, `docs/decisions/0013-custom-views-with-code-in-the-file.md:495`
- **What:** (1) The 'Messages on the port' row says events are `context`, `theme` or `changes`; the code also sends `command` and `place` (viewEventNames has five). (2) The refusals row for `unknown-event` names four events and omits `place`. (3) The filter operator list omits `descendantOf`, which reference.ts, queries.md and the host accept. (4) The view-api reference tells agents filters allow 'none on a calculated field', which contradicts its own records.query note and contract line 650 (calculated filters within 10,000 records since 1.40.0). (5) ADR-0013 bounds the toolbar to '128 in all', but readToolbar enforces no total, only 16 KiB, as the contract's Limits table says. (6) reference.ts's `context` table (lines 290-305), which agents read at nendo://application/view-api, has no `place` key, although viewContext sends it and the contract's context table lists it.
- **Failure:** An agent writing a view from nendo://application/view-api avoids a filter on a calculated field that the host supports, and does not know `context.place` exists. A reader of the ADR expects a 128-control bound that is not there, and a reader of the port table does not expect `command` or `place` events.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe.mjs toolbar -> F.items {"accepted":true,"controlsInAll":224,"bytes":6485} (readToolbar accepts 224 controls); the other items by Source
- **Fix and guard:** Update contract lines 587, 646-647 and 1127 to the five events and the full operator list. Drop 'and none on a calculated field' from reference.ts:331 and add `place` to its context table. Change ADR-0013:495 to the 16 KiB bound, or enforce 128 in readToolbar if that bound is still wanted. Guard: extend view-api-reference.test.mjs to assert that the events named in the contract tables equal viewEventNames and that the reference's context keys equal the keys viewContext returns.
- **Verifier:** All six drifts checked against the code. (1) custom-views.md:587 says events are context, theme or changes, but protocol.ts:355 viewEventNames has five: context, theme, changes, command, place. (2) The unknown-event row at custom-views.md:1127 lists four events and omits place. (3) The filter operator list at custom-views.md:646-647 stops at isNotNull, while reference.ts:326 and queries.md:13 accept descendantOf. (4) reference.ts:331 says 'none on a calculated field', which contradicts reference.ts:32 and queries.md:16-24 (calculated predicates work within 10,000 records). (5) ADR-0013:~495 says '128 in all', but view-toolbar-model.ts:244-247 enforces only 32 items and a 16 KiB total (protocol.ts:54, :60), and the contract Limits table (custom-views.md:1100) says 16 KiB. (6) extension-model.ts:304-319 viewContext plus the broker's place key (view-frames.ts:107) sends context.place, and the contract table (custom-views.md:992) lists it, but the reference.ts context table (:292-305) has no place key. The 224-control acceptance was a probe by the reviewer and I did not rerun it, but the missing total bound is plain in the source. Doc drift only; code is the authority and the fix is documentation.
- **Correction:** The wording in (1) understates the drift in the same table: custom-views.md:1069-1070 already lists command and place elsewhere, so only the port-messages row and the unknown-event row are stale.

### CSS-16 — Dead CSS: rules for classes no source emits, and 38 media-query declarations a later unconditional rule always overrides

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `workbench-css-design`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/11-agent-access.css:241`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/14-refinements-controls.css:146`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:250`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:272`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/22-agent-chat.css:742`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/16-command-palette.css:176`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/10-forms.css:292`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/05-help.css:63`
- **What:** `.permission-intro` (11:241-263, 14:146), `.chat-version` (22:250), `.chat-pill-key` (22:272) and `.chat-chip-sub` (22:742, 22:1174) are named by no .ts or .html source in the repository (git grep finds them only in styles/). Separately, the cascade probe found 38 declarations inside @media blocks that a later rule with the same selector and property always beats. They include 16:176's `.palette-trigger { width: 32px }`; all of 10's 840px rail and brand rules (10:292-322); 05:63's help-index padding; 10:476-477's status-bar rules; and nearly all of 12's compact rail block. 20-title-bar.css:517-524's `.workspace-header` reservation is also always beaten, by `html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header` (21:344). The slices still read as if these rules do something, which hid the defects reported above.
- **Failure:** A maintainer edits 10's or 12's narrow-window rules, or 20's title-bar reservation, and nothing changes on screen. The real layout is decided in 21-native, so fixes land in the wrong slice. This is how the compact-rail and recovery-layout defects survived.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-dead.cjs -> 'classes no source names: permission-intro, chat-version, chat-pill-key, chat-chip-sub' (diff-*, is-working/starting/thinking confirmed built dynamically). probe-shadow.cjs -> '38 conditional declarations always overridden' (full list in shadow.txt).
- **Fix and guard:** Delete the dead selectors and the overridden media declarations, keeping only what 21-native doesn't restate. Guard: add both probes (no unreferenced class selectors, no conditional declaration shadowed by a later unconditional one with the same selector and property) as a Workbench unit test over the parsed slices.
- **Verifier:** Both halves hold. (1) `git grep` over the whole repository, excluding .nendo files, finds `permission-intro`, `chat-version`, `chat-pill-key` and `chat-chip-sub` only in src/Nendo.Workbench/src/styles/ (11:241-263, 14:146, 22:250, 22:272, 22:742, 22:1175). No .ts or index.html names them, and no template string builds `permission-*`, `chat-pill-*` or `chat-chip-*` dynamically. (2) I reran probe-shadow.cjs, which uses postcss over the real @import order, and it again printed '38 conditional declarations always overridden'. I spot-checked these against the source: 01:79 `.recovery-layout` is beaten by 14:51; 05:63 `.help-index` by 13:637; 10:295-322 rail/brand/nav by 21:42-56 and 21:117-119; 12:298-306 compact rail by 21:40-163; 16:86 `.palette-trigger` width by 21:400-407. Each later rule has the same selector, no media wrapper and later order, so the earlier media declaration can never win. 20-title-bar.css:17-22 (`:root[data-title-bar=window] .workspace-header`, specificity 0,3,0) always loses to 21-native.css:344 `html:root .workspace-layer .workspace-header` (0,3,1), which sets min-height 0 and padding. The always-lose list includes dead recovery-layout (01:79 beaten by 14:51) and compact-rail rules, so it is a real maintenance trap. It is maintainability only, with no runtime effect, hence P3.
- **Correction:** Line numbers: `16:176` is really 16-command-palette.css:86 (the 1100px `.palette-trigger { width: 32px }`), and `20-title-bar.css:517-524` is really 20-title-bar.css:16-23, because the file has only 44 lines. 10-forms.css starts at 295, not 292. The citations 16:176, 20:517 and 20:513 in this finding and the next look like line numbers from a concatenated stylesheet. Note 16:86's width is shadowed but its padding and justify-content are redundant with 21:457 and 21:557 rather than shadowed by name. The count of 38 reproduces exactly.

### EBH-23 — The reviewed plan's read set records the wrong key for create-step reads and never records traversal targets

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `engine-behaviour`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:325`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourPlanner.cs:277`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.BehaviourSource.cs:231`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:130`
- **What:** For a CreateRecord step, EvaluateAssignmentAsync gets the created record type with the event record's ID and observes RecordKey(createdEntity, eventRecordId): usually no such record, or an unrelated one sharing the ID; the event record actually read is not observed. ReadFieldAsync and ReadReferenceAsync never call observe, so a traversal target (a task condition reading project.rate) is absent. The contract lists 'the records that a condition only read' among the promotion checks; only the global data-revision guard covers these today.
- **Failure:** When a created type has a record with the event record's ID, an edit to that unrelated record makes the proposal stale (NPROP003). If the conservative data-revision guard is ever narrowed, a plan whose condition read a project's rate promotes after the rate changed.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Observe inside ReadFieldAsync/ReadReferenceAsync with the (entity, record) actually read, and pass the event record's key to the CreateRecord observation. Guard: proposal test asserting the read set holds the traversal target and the event record.
- **Verifier:** The bookkeeping is wrong as stated. For a CreateRecord step, BehaviourPlanner.cs:277 passes entityId = step.EntityId (the created type) with raised.Key.RecordId, and EvaluateAssignmentAsync then calls ObserveAsync(new RecordKey(entityId, recordId)) at :325. That observes (created type, event record ID), so ReadVersionAsync finds nothing or an unrelated record, and the event record is never observed. BehaviourSource.cs ReadFieldAsync (:231) and ReadReferenceAsync never call observe; only the aggregate members (:465) and hierarchy ancestors (:427) do, so a traversal target such as project.rate is absent from ReadSet. This differs from the intent in the Promotion.cs:125-129 comment ('Records a condition merely read are checked too'). However the stale check at NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:131-133 also compares the global DataRevision whenever the plan is non-empty, which the finding concedes. No user-visible effect exists today, so this is latent maintainability and not a behaviour defect.
- **Correction:** Failure scenario (a) adds nothing, because any edit to the unrelated record bumps DataRevision and already makes the proposal stale (NPROP003) with or without the wrong key. Scenario (b) is hypothetical. The correct key for a CreateRecord assignment is (trigger.EntityId, raised.Key.RecordId), not the created type. Treat it as hardening, P3.

### ESM-26 — The Idea Garden service API is reachable only from tests and refuses its own output

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `engine-semantics`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/IdeaGardenDefinition.cs:39`, `src/Nendo.Engine/IdeaGardenDefinition.cs:358`, `src/Nendo.Engine/IdeaGardenCompatibility.cs:30`
- **What:** Nothing under src calls PrepareIdeaGardenProposalAsync, PrepareBoardTitleProposalAsync, CreateIdeaSchemaAsync, CreateIdeaRecordAsync, SetIdeaFieldAsync or ExecuteIdeaCommandAsync; only tests do. CreateInitialChangeSet creates Title with presentation 'singleLine', but ValidateExistingField accepts an existing Title only when its presentation is null, and that check runs before the semantic-definition-exists check. PrepareBoardTitleProposalAsync checks the title of the first boardSurface in the file but always writes node.idea.board.root.
- **Failure:** Running the Idea Garden proposal on a file it already set up refuses 'Existing field Title does not match the Idea Garden contract.' instead of saying the file already has surfaces, and after its surfaces are removed it can never be run again on that file.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Move the Idea Garden fixture into the test projects, or accept null or 'singleLine' for Title and check for existing UI nodes first. Guard: a test that runs the proposal twice and expects semantic-definition-exists.
- **Verifier:** A repo-wide search outside tests finds the six Idea Garden methods only at their definitions in IdeaGardenCompatibility.cs, so they are reached only from tests. The bridge methods that used them were retired on 2026-10-04 (architecture.md:536-541, ADR-0002:361-370). IdeaGardenDefinition.cs:39 creates Title with presentation 'singleLine', and AddFieldOperation stores it as given (Operations.cs:180-186, SqliteNendoStore.Operations.cs:151-157). ValidateExistingField (lines 358-363) accepts an existing Title only when its presentation is null, and it runs (lines 43-50) before the semantic-definition-exists check (lines 104-109). A second run on a file the first run set up therefore throws idea-field-conflict. PrepareBoardTitleProposalAsync (IdeaGardenCompatibility.cs:55-57) tests the first boardSurface but RenameBoardChangeSet always targets node.idea.board.root. No test covers a second run.
- **Correction:** Reach is test fixtures only (the tests seed the Title through CreateIdeaSchemaAsync, with null presentation), so there is no product impact. The real defect is the wrong error code and the non-rerunnable proposal in a compatibility API. The 'move it into the test projects' fix is a design choice.

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `site`

### TBI-08 — An upgrade removes obsolete owned files but leaves their now-empty directory tree in the install root

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:662`, `tools/Test-NendoSetup.ps1:57`
- **What:** Lines 662-664 delete each old entry that is not in the next inventory, but Remove-EmptyDirectories is called only from Remove-Owned (uninstall and backup rotation) and Restore-Pending. Test-NendoSetup asserts that 'stale/old.txt' is gone, not that 'stale' is gone.
- **Failure:** A release that drops a subtree, such as the ExtensionHost helper deleted in 44b7d5c, leaves its directory skeleton in Programs\Nendo for the life of the installation.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: find %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Nendo\ExtensionHost -> 16 directories (cs ... zh-Hant, runtimes\win-x64\native) and 0 files. The installed 0.18.0 inventory and Nendo.previous list no ExtensionHost path, and Nendo.previous, which was rotated through Remove-Owned, has no ExtensionHost directory.
- **Fix and guard:** After removing obsolete entries, delete each now-empty parent directory of a removed path, walking up to (not including) $root. Guard: extend the Test-NendoSetup v1->v2 case to assert that the 'stale' directory no longer exists.
- **Verifier:** tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:662-664 removes each old inventory entry that the next inventory drops, but Remove-EmptyDirectories (145-150) is only called from Remove-Owned (156, uninstall and backup rotation), Restore-Pending (557) and RetirePilots (583), never after a successful upgrade. tools/Test-NendoSetup.ps1:57 asserts 'stale/old.txt' is gone, not 'stale'. Read-only check of the owner install: Programs\Nendo\ExtensionHost holds 0 files and 17 directories (itself included), so the leftover skeleton is real. It is harmless and a later uninstall sweeps it through Remove-Owned, so it is polish.
- **Correction:** The skeleton does not live 'for the life of the installation': uninstall's Remove-Owned calls Remove-EmptyDirectories over the whole tree and removes it. The directory count is 17 including ExtensionHost itself (16 children).

### TGA-14 — Lanes leave scratch files behind on every run, including a .playwright-cli folder at the repository root

**P3** · maintainability · Confirmed · area `tools-gates`

- **Where:** `tools/Review-Garden.ps1:16`, `tools/Review-Swarm.ps1:14`, `tools/Review-AgentChat.ps1:22`, `tools/Test-SiteSearch.ps1:21`, `tools/Test-NendoBuildPruning.ps1:5`
- **What:** Review-Garden, Review-Swarm and Review-AgentChat run playwright-cli without Push-Location, so its snapshots land in the caller's directory, which is the repository root under Test-Production. They also leave a fixed-name probe.mjs in their output folders. Test-SiteSearch redirects the preview server to artifacts/site-search/server-<run>.log and .err and never deletes them. Test-NendoBuildPruning leaves artifacts/evidence/runs/prune-tests-<guid> on a pass. AGENTS.md asks lanes to clean up what they create.
- **Failure:** Measured now: 270 page-*.yml files in <repo>/.playwright-cli, dated from the 2026-10-10 gate run; 40 server logs in artifacts/site-search (20 runs); 133 snapshot files in artifacts/extension-runtime-results/.playwright-cli. They grow by one set per gate run. Two sessions running the gate at once also overwrite each other's fixed probe.mjs.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: `ls .playwright-cli \| wc -l` -> 270; `ls artifacts/site-search \| wc -l` -> 40; `ls artifacts/extension-runtime-results/.playwright-cli \| wc -l` -> 133
- **Fix and guard:** Push-Location into each lane's output folder as the other Review lanes do, and use run-unique probe names deleted in finally. Delete the site-search logs and the prune-tests root on success. Guard: snapshot the file lists of the repo root and the lane folders before and after a Test-Production run and assert nothing new remains.
- **Verifier:** The code and counts hold. Review-Garden.ps1, Review-Swarm.ps1 and Review-AgentChat.ps1 have no Push-Location (the six extension Review lanes do: e.g. Review-NendoGraph.ps1:20), and Test-Production.ps1:63 sets the repo root as cwd, so playwright-cli writes <repo>/.playwright-cli. I counted 270 files there (264 page-*.yml, 6 console logs), 133 in artifacts/extension-runtime-results/.playwright-cli and 40 in artifacts/site-search. Test-SiteSearch.ps1:21 redirects server-<run>.log/.err and never deletes them (only the probe, line 39). Review-Garden.ps1:28, Review-Swarm.ps1:26 and Review-AgentChat.ps1:31 write a fixed probe.mjs and leave it. It is a housekeeping gap only: .playwright-cli/ is git-ignored (.gitignore:14), artifacts/ is declared delete-freely scratch in AGENTS.md, and the page snapshots are 0-byte files.
- **Correction:** Weaken the framing. (1) The 270 root files are not 'from the 2026-10-10 gate run'; they accumulate across runs dated 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10 (16 of them from 10-10), and are 0-byte snapshots. (2) Test-NendoBuildPruning.ps1 is not in Test-Production (only listed as a manual command at docs/architecture.md:1224), it leaves three tiny files, and no prune-tests-* folder exists under artifacts/evidence/runs now. (3) The 'two sessions overwrite each other's probe.mjs' scenario is speculative: concurrent gate runs already collide on builds in artifacts/bin. (4) The proposed before/after file-list guard is the kind of retention scheme AGENTS.md ('Artifacts') tells agents not to build; Push-Location into the output folder plus deleting probe.mjs and the site-search logs in finally is the proportionate fix.

In the main checkout, git ls-files lists only HttpCanary.cs, and a grep for HttpCanary, MdnsObserver and FileOpenObserver outside the file finds hits only in stale .claude/worktrees copies. The SDK's default globbing still compiles it into Nendo.Desktop.Tests.
- **Failure:** The dead fixture adds P/Invoke surface (CreateFileW, DeviceIoControl with a hand-built NATIVE OVERLAPPED) and analyzer exposure to every Desktop test build. Readers take it as live boundary-test infrastructure. The canary tests it once fed no longer exist.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: git ls-files \| grep -i "HttpCanary\|BoundaryProbe\|OsBoundary" -> only tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/TestFixtures/HttpCanary.cs; git log -- tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/DesktopExtensionProcessTests.cs -> 44b7d5c deleted it.
- **Fix and guard:** Delete TestFixtures/HttpCanary.cs, or restore a test that uses it if the WebView2 egress canary is still wanted, now that views run inline. Guard: a Test-Repository check that every type under tests/*/TestFixtures/*.cs is referenced from at least one other file in the project.
- **Verifier:** tests/Nendo.Desktop.Tests/TestFixtures/HttpCanary.cs (315 lines) defines exactly three types: HttpCanary (line 12), MdnsObserver (207) and FileOpenObserver (253). A grep for all three names across tests/, src/, tools/ and docs/ finds only that file; the only other hits are stale .claude/worktrees copies and the untracked FIXES.md. Nendo.Desktop.Tests.csproj lists no explicit Compile items for it, so the SDK default glob compiles it. git ls-files shows it is the only tracked file of that family, and 44b7d5c ("Run custom views inline from the file, and delete the helper") touched DesktopExtensionProcessTests.cs, its former consumer. The fixture is dead code. It has no runtime effect because nothing instantiates it, so the UDP 5353 bind only happens if someone constructs it.
- **Correction:** The impact is compile-time only (dead P/Invoke surface and reader confusion); nothing binds a socket or opens a file unless instantiated, so the "failure scenario" is maintainability, not a test-run hazard.
