### BL-09 — npm audit reports a high-severity advisory in the Workbench's build toolchain (source-map-js 1.2.1 via vite -> postcss)

**P3** · security · Plausible · area `baseline`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/package-lock.json:1091`
- **What:** package-lock.json pins node_modules/source-map-js at 1.2.1 (dev, through vite@8.2.2 -> postcss@8.5.26). GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q (CVSS 7.5, range >=1.0.0 <1.2.2) is an event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets; fixAvailable is true. verify:dependencies only checks for React and AG Grid Enterprise, and no lane runs npm audit.
- **Failure:** A build that processes a crafted source map (for example from a compromised dependency) hangs the build; exposure is limited to build time on the developer machine, nothing ships.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: npm audit --json in src/Nendo.Workbench -> metadata.vulnerabilities {'high': 1, 'total': 1}, 'source-map-js allows event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets', range 1.0.0 - 1.2.1; npm ls source-map-js -> 'vite@8.2.2 -> postcss@8.5.26 -> source-map-js@1.2.1'.
- **Fix and guard:** Refresh the lock so source-map-js resolves to >=1.2.2 (npm update source-map-js, then npm ci and the gate). Guard: add 'npm audit --omit=optional --audit-level=high' to verify:dependencies or the Workbench step of Test-Production.
- **Verifier:** src/Nendo.Workbench/package-lock.json:1091-1095 pins node_modules/source-map-js at 1.2.1 with "dev": true, pulled by vite@8.2.2 -> postcss@8.5.26. I ran `npm audit --json` on a scratch copy of package.json and the lock: it reports 1 high (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q, CVSS 7.5, range >=1.0.0 <1.2.2, fixAvailable true) and nothing else, and verify-dependencies.mjs never audits. The advisory is real and the lock refresh is a one-line fix. Reachability is not established and is very likely nil: the flaw needs an attacker-crafted indexed source map to be parsed, and none of the Workbench's CSS inputs (src/styles.css, ag-grid-community/styles/*.css) carries a sourceMappingURL. It is also build-time only (dev dependency, not in the shipped payload), and a hostile dependency could already do more than hang the build.
- **Correction:** Exposure is lower than stated: no input in the repo's build supplies a source map to postcss, so the hang cannot be triggered from repo content, only by an already-compromised toolchain. Treat it as dependency hygiene (npm update source-map-js, then npm ci), not a security finding. Adding `npm audit --audit-level=high` to the gate would make every future advisory in a dev-only dependency block the gate, which is a policy decision for the owner.

<a id="dae-13"></a>

### DAE-13 — A view frame can launch any registered protocol handler: only pop-ups are limited to http, https and mailto

**P3** · security · Plausible · area `desktop-agents-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:130`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:117`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-frame-markup.ts:18`
- **What:** OnNewWindowRequested refuses every scheme but http, https and mailto, but OnFrameNavigationStarting cancels only the Workbench's host, and nothing handles CoreWebView2.LaunchingExternalUriScheme. The frame sandbox includes allow-popups, which lets a sandboxed frame navigate to a custom protocol, so a view's own navigation to search-ms:, ms-settings: or any registered app scheme reaches WebView2's default 'open this app?' dialog.
- **Failure:** A received file's view shows a button; the click navigates the frame to search-ms:query=invoice&crumb=location:\\attacker\share, and after the dialog Explorer opens a remote share dressed as a local search, the known phishing pattern the http/https/mailto rule was meant to keep out.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In OnFrameNavigationStarting cancel any view-frame navigation whose scheme is not https, http, data, blob or about, and route mailto through the same Launcher path as pop-ups; or handle LaunchingExternalUriScheme and cancel it for view frames. Guard: the extension-view journey navigates a view to a custom scheme and asserts no LaunchingExternalUriScheme dialog and the frame stays on its page; falsify by removing the scheme check.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: OnFrameNavigationStarting cancels only the Workbench host (ExtensionWebViewPolicy.cs:130-133), nothing handles LaunchingExternalUriScheme, and frameSandbox includes allow-popups (view-frame-markup.ts:18). The pop-up scheme limit at line 121 exists because Launcher.LaunchUriAsync starts a scheme with no prompt, whereas an engine-initiated launch goes through WebView2's own open-this-app dialog and needs a user gesture, so the asymmetry is explained. ADR-0013 ("The browser is open", lines 346-363) gives views most of what a web page may do and says anything else gets WebView2's default prompt. The finding's reproduction is "Source" only: nobody measured that a sandboxed view frame reaches the dialog, or what it shows. At most it is hardening against a user clicking Open on an OS dialog, with no P0 or P1 exposure.
- **Correction:** The reasoning that the http, https and mailto rule was meant to keep other schemes out is overstated: it guards the Launcher path, which has no dialog. The phishing scenario needs the person to accept WebView2's external-app prompt, unmeasured in this host. The fix is optional hardening beyond the current ADR.

<a id="ext-11"></a>

### EXT-11 — A compensation in a view's name skips the in-transaction actor check, reopening the R-014 race for records.undo and records.redo

**P3** · security · Plausible · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.cs:164`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionActor.cs:22`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:345`
- **What:** ApplyAsync runs RequireExtensionActorPackageAsync only when compensationOfRevisionId is null. A view's undo or redo is built by CreateCompensationMutationAsync with caller.Origin = `extension:<package>` and applied with the revision ID. It therefore commits without checking, in the transaction, that the package still exists and is not a skill. ExtensionActor.cs documents that check as the guard against a package removed between host admission and commit.
- **Failure:** An agent at Unattended accepts its own proposal removing package P while a P view's records.undo is queued behind it. The undo commits as `extension:P` for a package the file no longer carries, which is exactly what R-014's check exists to refuse.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Run RequireExtensionActorPackageAsync for every mutation whose origin starts with `extension:`, compensations included. A History compensation's origin is 'studio' and is unaffected. Guard: an Engine test that removes the package and then calls CompensateAsync with an extension caller, expecting `actor-not-allowed`.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. SqliteNendoStore.cs:164-165 runs RequireExtensionActorPackageAsync only when compensationOfRevisionId is null. A view's undo or redo goes DesktopSessionController.UndoRecordWritesAsync (line 315) -> MutateAsync -> service.UndoRecordWritesAsync -> coordinator.CompensateRevisionAsync (Promotion.cs:338) -> ApplyAsync with the revision ID, with origin extension:<package> from NendoCompensationCaller. So the in-transaction R-014 check is skipped. Tests cover the check only for ordinary writes (ExtensionActorWriteTests.cs), and none covers the undo path. Real exposure is a narrow race. The Desktop gate already refuses a stale undo at AdmitExtensionWriterAsync (DesktopSessionController.cs:538), so only an agent acceptance landing between that admission and the coordinator gate gets through. The committed undo only reverses the package's own earlier record writes, validated by record version, which the person can do from History anyway. It crosses no privilege boundary and only the attribution is odd. Real as a defense-in-depth gap in the R-014 invariant, but minor.
- **Correction:** Impact is overstated for 'security': the compensation reverses writes the same package already made, and an undo of a state write (extension.setState) is already refused by ExecuteSetExtensionStateAsync via ExtensionPackageExistsAsync. Only record undo and redo is unguarded. The fix (check every extension: origin, compensations included) looks safe, since a History compensation uses origin 'studio'. Priority is P3, closer to hardening than to a boundary breach.

<a id="r2sp-04"></a>

### R2SP-04 — The launched agent's 'Nendo' badge marks tools of any Nendo file's MCP server as going through this file's server

**P3** · security · Plausible · area `r2-several-processes` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.Options.cs:50`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.Options.cs:63`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/AgentConversation.cs:69`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/agent-chat-model.ts:216`
- **What:** Origin() returns 'nendo' when the unanchored pattern `nendo[-_.]+(?:nendo[-_.]+)?(?:read\|lease\|data\|change[-_.]?set\|health)` matches the tool name in the agent's metadata or its title. The host names its own session server 'nendo' (McpServerName) but never checks that name. originTag draws 'Nendo' for 'through this file's MCP server' and 'Its own tool' otherwise, on both tool steps and permission cards. docs/contracts/launched-agents.md says the badge is 'nendo' only when the name or title names this file's MCP tools.
- **Failure:** The person has registered Planner.nendo in their agent's own configuration as 'nendo-planner', as DesktopAgentPortStore's documentation invites. They launch Claude Code from BCM.nendo's Agent page. The agent calls mcp__nendo-planner__nendo_data_delete_record. The permission card reads 'Claude Code asks: … [Nendo]', so the person approves a delete in the Planner believing it acts on BCM through Nendo's own boundary. This is distinct from DAE-08, which is about the title being trusted over the metadata name.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-origin.mjs (the pattern copied verbatim) -> 'mcp__nendo__nendo_data_set_field origin "nendo"', 'mcp__nendo-planner__nendo_data_set_field origin "nendo"', 'mcp__nendo-bcm__nendo_change_set_accept origin "nendo"', 'nendo-planner-nendo-lease-acquire origin "nendo"'
- **Fix and guard:** Accept only the host's own server as Nendo: mcp__<McpServerName>__ or <McpServerName>- exactly. Name the session's server uniquely per file (for example nendo-<label>), so it cannot collide with a server the person registered themselves. Guard: an AgentConversation unit test asserting that mcp__nendo-planner__nendo_data_set_field yields origin 'agent' and mcp__nendo__nendo_data_set_field yields 'nendo'.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. AgentConversation.Options.cs:42-44 is an unanchored regex over the tool name, and AgentConversation.Options.cs:50-56 returns 'nendo' on any match; the host names its own server 'nendo' (AgentConversation.cs:69, 188) but Origin never checks the server part of `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Every Nendo file exposes the same nendo_data_/nendo_read_ tool family, so `mcp__nendo-planner__nendo_data_delete_record` matches via its tail. Not established: that a launched agent actually carries the person's own Nendo registrations (DesktopLaunchedAgent sets no config isolation, and docs/design/codemap.md:34 registers servers at Claude Code user scope, so it is possible but depends on the ACP adapter loading user config). Also the 'Nendo' tag (agent-chat-model.ts:216-217) carries no tooltip and the call does go through a Nendo MCP boundary (another file's, under that file's own level and leases), while launched-agents.md:138-141 words the rule as 'this file's MCP tools'. The permission card also shows the tool title, so the person can read nendo-planner. This is a label imprecision, not a boundary breach (the contract itself says the tab's gating is a convenience).
- **Correction:** Priority P3, category ux/label accuracy rather than security. The reproduction (regex match) is accurate but only proves the label, not that the person is misled about authority. Fix (match the exact `mcp__nendo__` / `nendo-` prefix of the host's own server name, or name the session server per file) is reasonable.

<a id="abs-11"></a>

### ABS-11 — Swarm marks an edit made while a save is in flight as saved, and the edit is lost

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/swarm/view.mjs:229`, `extensions/swarm/view.mjs:321`, `extensions/swarm/view.mjs:122`, `extensions/swarm/view.mjs:127`
- **What:** saveBehaviour sets saving=true but does not disable the parameter inputs; controls() is not called. The inspector's Name, Action, Steps and Path inputs were disabled only when they were drawn. Their change handlers call markDirty(), which does not check saving. When the batch and the five sequential queryAll reads finish, saveBehaviour sets dirty=false and calls keepDraft(), which removes the stored draft. A value typed during that window stays in the in-memory model while the view says 'Saved behaviour', Save behaviour is disabled, and the value was never written.
- **Failure:** A person presses Ctrl+S and at once changes Population from 240 to 300. The save completes, the field shows 300, and the line says 'Saved behaviour'. Leaving the screen or pressing Reload saved brings back 240.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Keep an edit counter. In saveBehaviour, note the counter before planning writes, and after success set dirty=false only if no edit happened since. Otherwise keep the draft and say so. Or disable the parameter and inspector inputs while saving. Guard: a Gate-Swarm step that changes a parameter between the batch request and its answer (fixture broker delay) and asserts dirty stays true and the draft is kept.
- **Verifier:** extensions/swarm/view.mjs:217 sets saving=true and the write plan is built from the model at :219 before the await at :221. controls() (:63-66) disables the parameter inputs only for replayMode/readOnly, so they stay editable; their change handlers (:322) set the model and call markDirty (:27-30), which does not check saving. After the batch, :229 sets dirty=false and keepDraft() removes the stored draft, so a value committed during that await stays in memory, is shown as 'Saved behaviour', and was never written. Diagram edits are blocked by SwarmRules (:143-144) while saving, and an edit made after dirty=false (during the read-back) correctly re-dirties, so the loss window is only the round trip of records.batch. The code reads as claimed, but I could not establish that a person commits a field edit inside that window in practice.
- **Correction:** The window is only the await on api.records.batch (:221), not the following readAll; an edit during the read-back sets dirty=true again. Diagram edits are already refused during a save. Inspector inputs and the parameter fields are the only unguarded paths.

<a id="dae-06"></a>

### DAE-06 — A view's origin is keyed by application ID, so a Duplicate (or a file claiming the same ID) shares its storage, drafts and unanswered saves with the original

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `desktop-agents-extensions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionOrigins.cs:43`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/ExtensionOrigins.cs:11`, `docs/decisions/0013-custom-views-with-code-in-the-file.md:416`, `src/Nendo.Engine/IdentityCopyModel.cs:45`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:302`
- **What:** ExtensionOrigins.Host derives the key from SHA-256(applicationId + "\n" + packageId) only. IdentityCopyModel refuses a non-Fork copy whose result application ID differs from the source's, so Duplicate keeps the application ID (a new instance ID only), as does a copy made in Explorer; a received file may also state any application ID. The class comment claims "two files carrying the same package keep separate storage, and a view left over from a closed file reaches nothing", and ADR-0013 says a view's drafts live in storage that "is per file and package". Garden keeps drafts and unanswered save batches in localStorage under garden.drafts.v1.<viewId> and garden.unanswered.v1.<viewId>, keyed further by record ID, and a Duplicate has the same view and record IDs.
- **Failure:** The person types a note in Garden in file A and the save goes unanswered, then works in A's Duplicate B: B's Garden restores A's draft over the same record and offers to send A's unanswered batch, which Save then writes into B. Separately, a file built with the application ID of a file the person got from a published template reads that file's view storage (drafts of private notes) and can plant an unanswered batch there.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Amend ADR-0013's key to include the instance ID (SHA-256(applicationId \n instanceId \n packageId)), accepting that a Duplicate starts with empty view storage, and update the class comment; the per-application settings and development links can stay keyed as they are. Guard: an ExtensionOrigins test that two snapshots with one application ID and different instance IDs get different hosts; falsify with the current formula.
- **Verifier:** The mechanics read as claimed: ExtensionOrigins.cs:43 hashes only applicationId + packageId; IdentityCopyModel.cs:45 requires a non-Fork copy to keep the source's application ID (ADR-0010 table: Duplicate preserves application ID, new instance ID), so a Duplicate, a New-file-of-this-application or any file stating that ID gets the same https://slug-key.example origin and therefore the same localStorage; Garden keys drafts/unanswered batches by viewId and record ID only (extensions/garden/workspace.js:302-303, drafts.mjs:37-95), which a Duplicate shares. However this is the formula ADR-0013 mandates in its Decision section (line 129: key = SHA-256(applicationId\npackageId)), and Duplicate-is-the-same-application is ADR-0010, so it is an accepted-design consequence rather than a coding slip; the test asserts only that different application IDs differ (DesktopExtensionServingTests.cs:24). The harm is bounded: cross-contamination of unsaved drafts between a file and its own Duplicate, or a forged-application-ID file (needs the victim's application ID, e.g. from a public template, and a victim with unsaved drafts) reading what a view chose to keep in browser storage. I could not establish a realistic high-impact path, and the received file's code already reads and writes all of its own file's records by design (ADR-0013 trust trade).
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. Reframe as an ADR-0013 amendment (the ADR text says storage is 'per file' and views cannot reach 'other files', which the application-ID key contradicts for same-ID files) rather than a defect in ExtensionOrigins.cs; the reviewer's evidence of shared-origin mechanics is accurate.

<a id="dsh-07"></a>

### DSH-07 — No WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION handling: Windows shutdown or sign-out kills a tray-resident Nendo without ShutdownAsync, mid agent write

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `desktop-shell` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:436`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopTrayIcon.cs:263`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopCloseAction.cs:16`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:252`
- **What:** The only orderly exit is AppWindow_Closing -> page.ShutdownAsync -> DesktopSessionController.DisposeAsync (stop admission, end the launched agent, dispose the coordinator). Session end does not raise AppWindow.Closing; neither the main window nor the tray window handles WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION (grep finds none; the tray WndProc passes them to DefWindowProcW), so after WM_ENDSESSION returns the process is terminated with agent requests still admitted. DesktopCloseAction's summary claims 'a Windows shutdown' is one of the two ways out, but nothing routes it there. The files use a rollback journal (inspection requires header bytes 18/19 = 1), and the Engine refuses any file with a -journal sidecar ('operational-sidecars: ... Close its writer before inspecting it').
- **Failure:** Nendo sits in the notification area with an agent at Unattended (the case the tray exists for); Windows Update restarts the machine overnight while the agent is writing. The kill leaves a hot journal; on the next start the file opens in recovery with 'Close its writer', there is no writer, and the obvious manual fix (deleting the journal) would corrupt the database.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Handle WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION in the tray window procedure (it is a top-level window and receives them): on ENDSESSION close agent admission and run the same shutdown synchronously with a bounded wait (ShutdownBlockReasonCreate while draining). Guard: a test that sends WM_ENDSESSION to the tray window of a controller with agent access on and asserts admission closed and the coordinator disposed; the Engine half (rolling back a hot journal) belongs to the Engine review.
- **Verifier:** Grep over src finds no WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION/SessionEnding/ProcessExit handling; the tray WindowProcedure (DesktopTrayIcon.cs:263) hands everything else to DefWindowProcW, and the only orderly exit is AppWindow_Closing -> ShutdownAsync (MainWindow.xaml.cs:436-490) whose DisposeAsync waits on _gate and disposes the coordinator (DesktopSessionController.cs:462-482). DesktopCloseAction.cs:17-19 does claim a Windows shutdown is an exit path, so the comment is wrong. Plain Win32 sends no WM_CLOSE at shutdown, so the gap is real, but I could not confirm WinUI's behaviour here, and the harm needs a write transaction in flight at that instant. The lockout itself comes from the Engine refusing any file with a -journal sidecar (SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:252-254), which is the Engine's separate hot-journal finding (ESC-01) and applies to any kill, task manager or crash alike; ADR-0011 cites 150 abrupt exits as accepted evidence. No database corruption is caused by Nendo itself.
- **Correction:** Lower to P3: SQLite keeps the main file atomic, so the damage is a refused open until the journal is rolled back, not corruption, and it needs shutdown to land inside a write. The remark that deleting the journal would corrupt the database is speculation about the person's reaction. The tray window is a top-level WS_OVERLAPPED window (DesktopTrayIcon.cs:140), so the proposed handler would receive the messages. The fix belongs mainly in the Engine (roll back a hot journal on open); the Desktop handler only narrows the window.

<a id="eco-10"></a>

### ECO-10 — The observed-open fast path skips the replacement-pending marker and read-only attribute that a fresh inspection refuses on

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:205`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:180`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ReplacementResolution.cs:64`
- **What:** When an observation carries a digest and the physical key matches, OpenCoreAsync trusts observation.Inspection (Open.cs:205-219) and re-checks only RequireUnchangedPhysicalFile (sidecars, size, header; Inspection.cs:180-183), the content digest and the integrity check. InspectAsync refuses write authority when <file>.recovery.json exists (Inspection.cs:355-357) or the file is marked read-only (line 368). The fast path checks neither. Once edits change the file under a pending marker, the recovery review offers no choice: KeepActive needs the original or result digest (ReplacementResolution.cs:64-66), and the occupied target rules out the other options.
- **Failure:** Window B observes Plan.nendo for the open dialog or recents. Window A, editing the same file, crashes during a restore after writing the marker but before moving anything. B then opens with the stale observation and gets a writable session on a file with a pending marker. After edits, the next normal open lands in recovery, and the review has no option to resolve it.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** In the confirming branch, refuse with file-changed-before-open when File.Exists(FileReplacementReceipt.PendingPath(fullPath)) or the read-only attribute is set (or add both checks to RequireUnchangedPhysicalFile). Restore and resolution handoffs stay valid, because their markers are deleted or archived before the reopen. Guard: a test that runs ObserveAsync, writes a marker, calls OpenObservedAsync and expects file-changed-before-open.
- **Verifier:** The code is as claimed. In OpenCoreAsync the 'confirming' branch (Open.cs:204-219) trusts observation.Inspection and runs only RequireUnchangedPhysicalFile (Inspection.cs:170-183: sidecars, size, header), the digest check and the integrity check. InspectAsync alone adds the replacement-pending finding (Inspection.cs:355-357) and the file-read-only finding (:366-369). No other code path checks PendingPath on a writable open (grep of PendingPath), and ReplacementResolution.PrepareAsync (:64-74) offers no choice once the active file's digest matches neither the original nor the result. But I could not establish a realistic route. A marker that existed at observation time already makes CanAcquireWriteAuthority false, so the fast path is not taken. A live restore in another window holds the Global instance lease for its whole run, so the second open fails at InstanceOwnershipLease.Acquire. So it needs the first process to crash in the narrow stage between writing the marker and moving the original, with a second window holding an observation taken before that. Observations are in-memory (Desktop _openCandidates, recents re-observe in ResolveAsync, DesktopFileHistory.cs:106-114). The read-only-attribute half only makes SQLite fail the writable open, with no integrity impact.
- **Correction:** Reachability is a multi-process crash race, not a normal workflow, so P3 at most. The cheap fix (File.Exists(PendingPath) check in the confirming branch) is still reasonable hardening.

<a id="esq-02"></a>

### ESQ-02 — The CSV code resolver folds case with OrdinalIgnoreCase, but uniqueness folds ASCII only, so a code can silently link to the wrong record

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `engine-service-queries` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:124`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:132`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:139`, `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:36`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:90`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:204`
- **What:** CsvCodeResolver builds _existing, _rows and _repeated with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase. It fills _existing with TryAdd, so the first record in record-ID order wins. The store defines Text uniqueness with a unique index and a check that use SQLite COLLATE NOCASE, which folds only A-Z. So two records with codes 'Æ1' and 'æ1' (or 'Ö-7' and 'ö-7') are both legal, yet the resolver treats them as one key.
- **Failure:** A Location type with a unique Code holds rec-a 'Æ1' and rec-b 'æ1'. A CSV row names parent 'æ1'. _existing kept only rec-a, so Resolve returns rec-a, and the row is committed pointing at the wrong record with no diagnostic. The contract requires a code that names two records to be refused. If the import itself carries both 'Æ1' and 'æ1', every row that names either one is refused with 'is on more than one CSV row', although the store would accept both rows.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe1.ps1 -> 'OrdinalIgnoreCase("Æ1","æ1") = True'. Executed: python sqlite3 with CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... (code COLLATE NOCASE) -> both 'Æ1' and 'æ1' inserted. The ASCII control 'a1'/'A1' -> 'UNIQUE constraint failed: t.code'.
- **Fix and guard:** Compare codes the way the store's uniqueness does: an ASCII-only case fold for Text, and exact for Integer. When building _existing, refuse a key that two existing records share instead of using TryAdd, so ambiguity is refused by the row and never decided by record-ID order. Guards in CsvTests: - target records 'Æ1' and 'æ1' exist, and importing a row that names 'æ1' links rec-b; - the resolver's comparer and the unique index agree on a set of non-ASCII pairs.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. CsvReferenceCodes.cs:124,139,140 use StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, which equates 'Æ1' and 'æ1', and line 132 fills _existing with TryAdd, so the first record wins. The store's uniqueness is SQLite COLLATE NOCASE (SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:90,170,204), which folds ASCII only. Two existing records with codes differing only by a non-ASCII case would therefore be legal but collapse to one key in the resolver. ADR-0020 (docs/decisions/0020-unique-and-generated-fields.md:321-322) states the ASCII-only fold as a known limitation, 'ASCII covers every code in use', and csv.md:26 and the site guide say a code is compared 'without regard to case'. The harm needs two existing records whose codes differ only by non-ASCII case and a CSV row naming one of them. That is contrived and the ADR accepts it, so I could not show it is reachable in real data. A wrong link would be silent if it happened.
- **Correction:** Downgrade P2 to P3. State that the ASCII-only store fold is the documented ADR-0020 trade-off, and the real defect is only that the resolver folds wider than the store. The cheap fix is an ASCII-only comparer for the resolver and a refusal of ambiguous existing keys instead of TryAdd. The false 'on more than one CSV row' refusal for an import carrying both 'Æ1' and 'æ1' is harmless.

### ESS-03 — A sequence's high-water mark is thrown away when the sequence is removed, and a (re)declaration seeds only from live rows, so numbers of deleted records are handed out again

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `engine-storage-schema` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldSequences.cs:94`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldSequences.cs:86`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldSequences.cs:50`, `docs/contracts/relationships.md:113`
- **What:** Removing a sequence (prefix null) writes sequence_prefix, sequence_width and sequence_next all NULL (FieldSequences.cs:94-101; the rung's CHECK forces the three together). Declaring a sequence again has previous == null, so next = max(NextFromDataAsync, MinimumNext ?? 1) (line 86); the 'same prefix keeps its high-water mark' branch (lines 88-89) applies only while a sequence still exists. NextFromDataAsync scans only the live table (lines 50-64), never __nendo_deleted_record.values_json, where every deleted record keeps its code. Only compensation passes MinimumNext. ADR-0020 item 4 and relationships.md:113-116 say the number 'is never lowered, so a deleted record's number stays spent'.
- **Failure:** Reference on Findings is numbered F- 3 and has reached F-169; F-169 is deleted. The owner chooses Stop numbering and later Number automatically with F- 3 (two proposals, not an undo). The next finding is assigned F-169 again, so a commit message or note that names F-169 now points at a different record, and undoing the old deletion is refused as value-not-unique because the restored code collides. The same reuse happens on a first declaration over a field whose highest code belonged to a deleted record.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Seed the counter from the tombstones as well: in NextFromDataAsync also read json_extract(values_json, '$."<fieldId>"') from __nendo_deleted_record rows of the entity and take the highest number of the shape; and on removal keep the previous high-water mark recoverable (for example read the latest removal's previousNext from history when re-declaring with the same prefix). Guard: a FieldSequenceTests case that numbers three records, deletes the last, stops and restarts numbering and asserts the next code is one past the deleted one and that compensating the deletion still restores it; falsify by scanning live rows only.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed. Removing a sequence writes NULL into prefix, width and next together (FieldSequences.cs:94-101; the CHECK in FieldRules.cs:21-22 forces them). A fresh declaration then has previous == null, so next = max(NextFromDataAsync, MinimumNext ?? 1) (FieldSequences.cs:86), and NextFromDataAsync scans only live rows (FieldSequences.cs:50-64), never __nendo_deleted_record. So stop-then-restart with the same prefix after deleting the highest-numbered record hands that number out again. Only compensation passes MinimumNext (test FieldSequenceTests.cs:116-135 covers just the undo). It is not clearly a defect, though. ADR-0020 item 4 says the mark is 'initialised on declaration from the largest existing value of that shape', and relationships.md:~113 says stored values 'set it on declaration'. The same ADR says a number 'is never reused, even after its record is deleted'. The two statements conflict only in the remove-then-redeclare case. The loss of the counter on removal follows from the fixed one-row layout, and ADR-0020 handles the undo path explicitly with minimumNext (lines 176-177). Reaching it takes two deliberate owner proposals (Stop numbering, then Number automatically) with the highest code deleted in between. The first-declaration variant is mandated by the spec as written, because deleted rows are not 'existing values'.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. Present it as a gap in ADR-0020 (a re-declaration should preserve the deleted high-water mark) rather than a deviation from it. The first-declaration case matches the stated spec.

### ESS-06 — Undoing a presentation change cannot restore a field that had no presentation; it writes 'singleLine' instead of NULL

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `engine-storage-schema`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldPresentation.cs:57`, `src/Nendo.Engine/FieldPresentationOperations.cs:22`, `src/Nendo.Engine/FieldPresentationOperations.cs:35`, `src/Nendo.Engine/IdeaGardenDefinition.cs:358`
- **What:** The evidence keeps previousPresentation = field.Presentation, which is null for a plain Text field, but CreateSetFieldPresentationInverse maps null to "singleLine" (FieldPresentation.cs:57) because SetFieldPresentationOperation only accepts singleLine/longText/markdown (FieldPresentationOperations.cs:22-24). The operation is still declared Reversible (line 35) although its inverse depends on retained evidence and does not reproduce the prior state. IdeaGardenDefinition.ValidateExistingField accepts the Idea title field only when its presentation is null (lines 358-362).
- **Failure:** A Text field added without a presentation is switched to Markdown and the change is undone: __nendo_field.presentation is now 'singleLine', not NULL. For the Idea Garden title field, ValidateExistingField then reports idea-field-conflict ('Existing field Title does not match the Idea Garden contract'), and describe/semantic diffs show a presentation the author never set.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Let the inverse carry 'no presentation' (an internal null-capable variant used only by compensation, or a dedicated flag in the payload) and write NULL when previousPresentation was null; declare the operation ReversibleWithRetainedState like its siblings. Guard: a test that adds a plain Text field, sets markdown, compensates, and asserts the field's Presentation is null again; falsify with the current mapping.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. ExecuteSetFieldPresentationAsync records previousPresentation = field.Presentation, which is null for a plain Text field (FieldPresentation.cs:38). CreateSetFieldPresentationInverse maps a null to 'singleLine' (FieldPresentation.cs:57), because SetFieldPresentationOperation accepts only singleLine, longText or markdown (FieldPresentationOperations.cs:14, 22-24). So after the undo __nendo_field.presentation is 'singleLine' where it was NULL, although the operation is declared Reversible (line 35). MarkdownPresentationTests.cs:73-74 undoes only a longText field and never the null case. The effect is almost purely cosmetic. Every Engine and Workbench check treats null and 'singleLine' alike for Text (FieldRules.cs:59, LinkRules.cs:159-164, view-structure.ts:85, write-failure.ts:56). The Idea Garden title conflict is real in the code (IdeaGardenDefinition.cs:358-362) but sits in a legacy fixture path: PrepareIdeaGardenProposalAsync has callers only in Desktop tests. The scenario also needs an Undo that the History UI does not offer for this operation (see finding 5: canCompensate is false for schema.setFieldPresentation). It is reachable only through a direct compensate call to the Engine API or the Workbench protocol (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:727).
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The Idea Garden consequence is fixture-only. The defect is reachable from the product UI only once finding 5 is fixed, because History does not currently offer this Undo. Otherwise it needs a direct compensate call.

### EXT-07 — Export then import is not the same package: valid paths that import skips are dropped, and a case-variant manifest is stored as a file

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:242`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:51`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionArchive.cs:157`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Extensions/ExtensionPackageModel.cs:333`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Extensions/WorkbenchProtocol.Extensions.cs:178`
- **What:** ValidPath, and so extension.putFile, accepts `.well-known/app.json`, `node_modules/lit/index.js` and a root `nendo-package.json`. Skipped() drops all three on every folder or zip import, and export overwrites a root `nendo-package.json` package file with the generated manifest. Separately, ReadFolder finds the manifest with File.Exists, which is case-insensitive on NTFS, but Skipped() compares `path == ManifestName` ordinally. A folder whose manifest is spelled `Nendo-Package.json` is therefore read as the manifest and also stored as a package file. Manifest()'s doc says export and import again gives the same package.
- **Failure:** An agent writes an unbundled view whose index.html loads node_modules/lit/index.js. The person exports it, edits a file and imports it, or uses Develop from folder then Save to file. The import change set proposes removing every node_modules file, and accepting it breaks the view. A Windows folder with Nendo-Package.json imports with the manifest as a served package file.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe7.ps1 -> 'folder with Nendo-Package.json -> package org.example.map, files: Nendo-Package.json, index.html'; 'ValidPath .well-known/app.json = True', 'ValidPath node_modules/lit/index.js = True', 'ValidPath nendo-package.json = True'.
- **Fix and guard:** Make the stored-path rule and the import rule one rule. Either refuse in ValidPath, or in the put, what Skipped() drops (a dot-leading segment, node_modules, a root nendo-package.json in any case), or stop skipping those paths when the target package already holds them. Compare the manifest name with OrdinalIgnoreCase in Skipped(). Guard: a round-trip test of Manifest() plus files through ReadFolder against ChangeSet(current) that expects `extension-unchanged`, and a test that the case-variant manifest is not among Files.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. ValidPath (ExtensionPackageModel.cs:333) accepts '.well-known/app.json', 'node_modules/x.js' and a root 'nendo-package.json', and no put-side guard rejects them (ExtensionPackageOperations.cs:121). Skipped() (ExtensionArchive.cs:242) drops all three on every folder and zip import, so ChangeSet() would propose removing such files from an existing package. ReadFolder finds the manifest with File.Exists (line 51, case-insensitive on NTFS), but Skipped() compares ordinally, so a 'Nendo-Package.json' folder stores the manifest as a file. The skip rule itself is documented and deliberate (docs/contracts/custom-views.md:1312-1316, docs/custom-view-authoring.md:229-231). The triggers are exotic: an agent has to put node_modules or dot-leading paths through raw ops, even though the shipped Put-NendoPackage.mjs applies the same skip, or someone has to name the manifest with odd casing. Only Manifest()'s round-trip is promised, not whole-package round-trip. Import removals show in the review diff, so nothing happens silently.
- **Correction:** The skip-on-import rule is documented behaviour, so the lead claim is a put-versus-import asymmetry, not a violated contract. The one clear undocumented defect is the case-variant manifest (File.Exists versus ordinal compare), and it needs a non-standard filename on Windows. Line 157 should be 158 for Manifest(). The 'Develop from folder then Save to file' scenario is loose: that path reads the folder through ReadFolder, which already skips these paths, so a folder never produces them.

### MAA-07 — Revalidate can lose a proposal's operations: it rejects before the new draft exists, and a revalidated draft is discarded at lease end

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `mcp-authoring-agent`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:419`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:438`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:696`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAuthoringTools.cs:20`
- **What:** RevalidateAsync runs proposals.RejectAsync(old), then _validated.Remove, then application.GetSnapshotAsync(cancellationToken) and RequireHostIdentity, and only then puts the new draft in _drafts at line 438. A cancellation or refusal in that window leaves neither the proposal nor its operations. A revalidate that does not validate at the new revision leaves an ordinary draft, and DiscardSessionAsync discards every draft of the handle at lease end. begin's description promises only that 'A draft never validated is discarded when the lease ends; a validated proposal stays'.
- **Failure:** (1) The client's request is cancelled just after the old proposal's clone is rejected. A retry of revalidate under the same key is NENDO_CHANGE_SET_NOT_FOUND, and the operations are gone. (2) Revalidate answers invalid at the new revision, and the agent releases its lease to come back later. The previously validated operations are dropped, though the agent had read that validated work survives the lease.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Build and register the new draft before rejecting the old proposal, and pass CancellationToken.None once the reject has started. Keep a draft that came from a validated proposal in _validated-style storage across lease end, or say in begin and revalidate that it is discarded. Guard: a test that cancels revalidate after the reject (through an internal fault hook like BeforeInvalidPreviewCleanup) and requires the change set still to be amendable or revalidatable.
- **Verifier:** Sub-claim (1) reads as stated: NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:419 awaits proposals.RejectAsync(old), :420 removes _validated, and only then :421 awaits application.GetSnapshotAsync(cancellationToken) (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:193 WaitAsync(token) throws if the request token is already cancelled). The new draft is not registered until :438, so a cancellation in that window leaves neither proposal nor kept operations, and a retry hits CHANGE_SET_NOT_FOUND. The window is narrow (a cancelled or timed-out request between the reject and the next coordinator-gate wait) and I could not establish it is hit in practice; the lost data is operations the agent itself sent. Sub-claim (2) is documented behaviour, not a defect: the revalidate tool description and mcp-interface.md:368 say a draft that no longer validates 'stays open to amend', RevalidateTests.cs:62 asserts exactly that, and the begin description says a never-validated draft is discarded at lease end.
- **Correction:** Drop scenario (2); only the reject-before-register ordering at NendoAgentAuthoringService.cs:419-438 stands, and it needs a cancellation race to trigger. Priority P3.

### R2SP-06 — The view-failure and agent-failure logs lose entries written at the same moment by several windows and leak stage files, on exactly the failure that reaches every window at once

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `r2-several-processes`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopCappedJsonlLog.cs:19`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopCappedJsonlLog.cs:31`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:159`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:267`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:332`
- **What:** Record reads every line, appends one, writes a stage and moves it over the log, with no cross-process lock. When the move fails, the catch returns false and never deletes the stage. Every Nendo process calls EnsureCoreWebView2Async() with the default environment, so all windows share one user-data folder and therefore one WebView2 browser process. Observed on this machine: the installed Nendo.Desktop.exe (PID 26128, started 12:19:19) runs on a msedgewebview2 browser process (PID 27164, user data Programs\Nendo\Nendo.Desktop.exe.WebView2) that started at 12:19:00 under a parent PID 18136 that no longer exists, so the browser process outlives the Nendo process that started it and serves the next one. BrowserProcessExited reaches every window's Workbench_ProcessFailed together, and each one runs ShowRecovery, RendererFailed and RecordViewFailure at the same instant. Agent failures from several files' hosts share agent-failures.jsonl in the same way.
- **Failure:** Three files are open and the shared msedgewebview2 browser process exits. All three windows go to recovery, and each writes its 'view failure' line at the same moment. One line survives, and the losers can leave *-<guid>.tmp files in the device-state folder that nothing removes. The ADR-0002 2026-09-15 amendment adds this record so that such a failure is written down, so losing these lines defeats its purpose.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-jsonl.ps1 (three pwsh processes running Record's exact read/append/stage/move sequence, released together) -> '3 processes recorded 1 entries each at the same moment: 1 of 3 lines kept, 0 stage files left behind' and, with 20 each, '21 of 60 lines kept, 21 stage files left behind'; Executed: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process for Nendo.Desktop.exe and msedgewebview2.exe (read-only) -> '27164 parent= 18136 browser C:\Users\thoma\AppData\Local\Programs\Nendo\Nendo.Desktop.exe.WebView2\EBWebView', parent 18136 not running, browser started 12:19:00 and Nendo.Desktop.exe 26128 started 12:19:19
- **Fix and guard:** Hold DesktopDeviceStateLock.Enter(stem) around the read-modify-write, delete the stage in a finally, and retry the move once on a sharing violation. Guard: a test that runs Record concurrently from several threads or processes and asserts N lines and no *.tmp left in the root.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. DesktopCappedJsonlLog.Record (DesktopCappedJsonlLog.cs:19-39) reads the whole log, appends, writes a GUID-named stage and File.Move(overwrite) over the log with no DesktopDeviceStateLock (callers DesktopViewFailureLog.cs:43-60 and DesktopAgentFailureLog.cs:30-33 use only an in-process lock), so concurrent processes lose entries (last move wins) and a failed move leaves the stage because the catch returns false without deleting it; nothing in Desktop sweeps *.tmp. Not established: the trigger. The 'every window fails at once' case is inferred from a shared WebView2 browser process and Workbench_ProcessFailed, which the reviewer says was not observed live. Impact is also small: the class is documented as fail-soft (DesktopCappedJsonlLog.cs summary; DesktopViewFailureLog.cs doc), simultaneous entries from one browser-process exit are near-identical so one surviving line carries the information, and orphan stages are rare and tiny. DesktopDeviceStateLock.cs docs show the authors lock shared state documents, so omitting it here looks like an oversight, but the consequence is a lossy diagnostic.
- **Correction:** Priority P3 (arguably polish). The 20-per-process probe numbers (21 of 60 lines kept) overstate real use; the three-simultaneous-failures case loses duplicate lines of the same event. Fix (DesktopDeviceStateLock.Enter around the read-modify-write, delete stage in a finally) is cheap and correct.

### WCS-03 — A pending save is keyed only by application and instance ID, so 'Check or retry save' replays it into a backup or raw copy of the file

**P3** · data-integrity · Plausible · area `workbench-core-state` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:60`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/pending-mutations.ts:99`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:258`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:206`
- **What:** The journal's storage key is 'nendo.pending-mutation.v1.' + encodeURIComponent(applicationId) + '.' + encodeURIComponent(instanceId). ADR-0010 states that a raw copy and a Backup preserve both IDs, and instance ownership only prevents two simultaneous writable opens. journal.retry reads the entry for that identity, looks up the receipt in whatever file is open now, and on 'not found' resends entry.method/entry.payload; entry.fileSessionId is stored but never compared. renderPendingMutation's notice does not say which file or when the save was made, and the only control it offers is the retry.
- **Failure:** A save to Planner.nendo times out (host-timeout while an agent holds the gate). The person later opens a backup of Planner.nendo to look something up. The backup shows 'A previous save has not been confirmed. Check or retry that saved request before making another change.' with every control disabled; pressing 'Check or retry save' writes the original file's record change into the backup (and, if the original save had in fact committed, the change now exists in both files).
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-journal-copy.mjs -> "original save: host-timeout" / "copy sees pending entry from session fs-original state pending" / "Check or retry save on the copy sent: data.getReceipt -> data.setFields \| applied as rev-in-copy"
- **Fix and guard:** Key the entry by something that distinguishes copies (the host's physical file key or a path digest returned in the snapshot), or refuse to replay when the open file is not the one the entry was written for, and name the file and time in the notice with an explicit 'Discard this unsent change' action. Guard: node test that an entry written under one file key is reported, not replayed, when retry runs under another key with the same application/instance IDs.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. The journal key is 'nendo.pending-mutation.v1.' + applicationId.instanceId (pending-mutations.ts:60, host-desktop.ts:258-259). entry.fileSessionId is only type-checked at read (pending-mutations.ts:74) and never compared, and retry() looks the receipt up and resends through fileSender() bound to whichever file is open now (:99-106, host-desktop.ts:173-181). ADR-0010 states that a raw copy and a Backup preserve both IDs. InstanceOwnership.cs:27-33 only blocks simultaneous writable opens, so a copy opens writable once the original is closed, and renderPendingMutation then shows the notice and the retry button for it (main.ts:188-223). I could not establish that this is reached in practice. It needs a save that left an unconfirmed entry (host-timeout), then the person opening a same-identity copy before resolving it, then an explicit click on 'Check or retry save'.
- **Correction:** Priority should be P3. Under ADR-0010 a raw copy or Backup is by design the same application instance, so keying by identity is consistent with the model rather than an oversight. The replay is also bounded: it carries the original idempotency key and expectedRecordVersion (a differing copy refuses with record-version-conflict, which is in the rejected set and clears the entry), so it only lands in a copy whose record is at the same version. The unconfirmed state is also reachable only after a timeout or lost response. The cheap fix is still worthwhile: compare entry.fileSessionId or a path digest, and name the file in the notice. The 'if the original save had in fact committed, the change now exists in both files' sentence is only true when the copy predates the commit; a copy taken after it carries the receipt and the retry just acknowledges.

### ABS-10 — Reads are silently cut at queryAll's max: the Atlas ignores assessments past 5,000, and Archi exports past 50,000 records per type

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:887`, `extensions/archi/view.js:48`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/nendo-api.ts:116`
- **What:** nendo.records.queryAll stops at max and returns items.slice(0, max) without error (nendo-api.ts:116-117). The Atlas reads every related type, assessments included, with { max: 5000 } and builds the latest-per-dimension index from what came back. Records come in record-ID order (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs:162), so a cut drops whichever IDs sort last. Northstar already ships about 2,500 assessments (assessments.mjs: migrated plus baseline, value and health per capability), and two more quarterly rounds over 635 capabilities x 3 dimensions pass 5,000. Archi reads each record type with { max: 50000 }; at that size Save as .archimate or Exchange, the validator and delete plans run on a partial model, with no warning.
- **Failure:** After a year of quarterly assessments a BCM file holds 6,300 assessments. The Atlas reads 5,000, so for capabilities whose newest assessments sort after the cut, the map shows the older maturity and a wrong 'Change since', and the inspector's 'Assessment history' misses rows. Nothing says data was left out. An Archi repository with more than 50,000 diagram items exports an .archimate missing the rest.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Read with a max larger than any bound the views accept and compare items.length with max; when the read hit the cap, say so in the notice line and refuse exports. For assessments, query per capability, or with a filter on date. A host aggregate (records.groupAggregate max(date) per capability and dimension) avoids reading every assessment. Guard: a fixture with 5,001 assessments where the newest sorts last, asserting the Atlas shows it as latest or names the cap.
- **Verifier:** The mechanism is as claimed: src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-api/nendo-api.ts:116-117 stops at max and returns items.slice(0,max) with no signal, records page in record-ID binary order (SqliteNendoStore.ReadQueries.cs, order = id COLLATE BINARY), and extensions/bcm-atlas/view.js:889 reads every related type with max 5000, assessments included, then derives 'latest' from them (:896). But the cap is the documented contract ('up to max', docs/contracts/custom-views.md:1043), the shipped data is about 2,500 assessments, so it needs several thousand more before anything is dropped, and the Archi 50,000-per-type cap (extensions/archi/view.js:49) is practically unreachable. I did not establish a realistic near-term path, only that the Atlas gives no notice when it is hit.
- **Correction:** The Atlas assessments read is the only plausible hit; the Archi 50,000 half is theoretical and should be dropped or noted as such. The behaviour is documented as 'up to max', so the defect is the missing truncation notice, not the cap.

### ESS-10 — A unique Integer field can be a hierarchy's order field, which makes ordinary moves fail as value-not-unique

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `engine-storage-schema`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Hierarchy.cs:85`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.FieldRules.cs:103`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:87`
- **What:** ExecuteDeclareHierarchyAsync checks only that the order field is an active Integer (Hierarchy.cs:85-92); ExecuteSetFieldUniqueAsync accepts any plain Integer (FieldRules.cs:103-111, CanBeUnique) without checking whether it orders a hierarchy. Sibling order values are per parent: MoveRecordAsync gives the first child of an empty parent OrderGap (NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:87) and renumbers windows in steps of the gap, so equal order values under different parents are the normal case, while uniqueness applies across the whole record type.
- **Failure:** Capabilities declares a hierarchy ordered by 'Position', which was earlier made unique. Moving a capability under a second, empty parent tries Position 1024, already held by the first parent's child, and is refused 'That Position is already used by c7 in Capabilities'; drag-and-drop in the outline fails for most moves.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Refuse declaring a hierarchy whose order field is unique, and refuse making a hierarchy's order field unique (hierarchy-field-in-use), naming the conflict. Guard: HierarchyTests cases for both directions asserting the refusal code.
- **Verifier:** The combination is accepted both ways: ExecuteDeclareHierarchyAsync only requires an active Integer order field (Hierarchy.cs:85-92) and ExecuteSetFieldUniqueAsync accepts any plain Integer (FieldRules.cs:58-60,103-105) without checking hierarchy use; HierarchyMetadataIsValidAsync does not check it either. MoveRecordAsync computes orders as lower+1024, upper-1024, midpoints and renumber windows (NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:86-109, 130-176) with no knowledge of other parents' values, so a record-type-wide unique index can refuse such a set-field as value-not-unique. It needs an owner to deliberately make a position field unique, and the refusal is explicit and reversible by un-uniquing, so P3.
- **Correction:** The stated failure scenario is wrong for a record that already has an order: moving it under an empty parent hits the 'keep the record's order' branch (NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:86: siblings.Count == 0 and at == 0 satisfy both guards, so placed = kept and no write is made), so it does not try 1024. Collisions come from records with no order (placed = OrderGap), last+1024 / first-1024 placement, midpoint placement and renumbered windows landing on another parent's value, so 'fails for most moves' is overstated. Fix suggestion (refuse in both directions with hierarchy-field-in-use) is sound.

### GDN-08 — Find takes at most 500 index hits, so a common word hides every further matching note in the tree and the graph

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/search.mjs:21`, `extensions/garden/search.mjs:40`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:152`, `extensions/garden/graph.js:217`
- **What:** createFinder() stops paging at max = 500 hits (21, 40) and reports them as the answer; drawTree()'s matches() (workspace.js:152) and the graph's search (graph.js:217) then treat a note as found only when it is among those hits, so the local match that found it a moment earlier is thrown away.
- **Failure:** In a garden of 2,000 notes, Find 'garden' first shows every match (local), then, once the index answers, only 500: notes that plainly contain the word vanish from the tree with no word that the list was cut.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** When the cursor is not exhausted, keep the local match for notes beyond the hits (hits rank, local fills), or page to the end within the file's bound and say when it stopped. Guard: a search.test with a stub search of 600 hits asserting every matching note stays matched (or that a cap notice is reported).
- **Verifier:** Code reads as claimed: createFinder pages records.search until hits.size reaches max=500 (search.mjs:21,36-40) and reports that Map as the answer; drawTree's matches() uses state.hits.has() whenever hits is non-null, discarding the local match (workspace.js:152), and graph.js:217 does the same with options.ids. ADR-0028 only bounds a page at 100 (line 136); no ADR, doc or test (tools/garden/search.test.mjs has no cap case) makes 500 a stated limit. But it needs more than 500 notes matching one query (loadIndex itself is bounded at 10,000, workspace.js:70), the survivors are the 500 best BM25 hits, and refining the query is the natural recovery, so I could not establish that it bites in practice. Not executed by the reviewer either (reproduction: Source).
- **Correction:** Only silent truncation for queries with more than 500 matches; a cap notice or keeping local matches would be a polish fix, not a data defect.

### GDN-14 — A save that links to a note changed elsewhere since the last index read is refused once: target versions come from the stale index

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `extensions/garden/workspace.js:892`, `extensions/garden/workspace.js:899`, `extensions/garden/sync.mjs:131`
- **What:** save() re-reads the note's related rows and the tags before planning (892), but passes state.index (899), read at the last change, to plan(); plan() writes each new Link's target version from that index (sync.mjs:129-131), and the host refuses a reference whose target changed since.
- **Failure:** An agent edits note B; within the 400 ms before the view re-reads the garden (or while that read is in flight), the person saves note A with a new [[B]]: the save is refused with a target-version conflict and the person must press Save again.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Read the targets' current versions (or the index) inside save() before plan(), as it does for tags, or let the batch name references by slug. Guard: a gate step that calls broker.touch on the target note, then saves a new link to it, and asserts one successful batch.
- **Verifier:** The path is as described: save() re-reads related rows and tags (workspace.js:892) but passes state.index to plan() (:899), and plan() writes each new Link's targetVersions from that index (sync.mjs:128-131, targetVersions helper at :46-49). The host does refuse a stale one: SqliteNendoStore.References.cs:151 throws target-version-conflict, and docs/custom-view-authoring.md:643-646 says so. The view refreshes the index only after a 400 ms debounce on 'changes' (workspace.js:1275-1288), and the Garden definition has no automatic actions (tools/garden/definition.mjs:105), so the only trigger is an outside edit to the link target landing inside that window. That is a narrow race, I did not reproduce it, and the recovery is a second Save with the draft kept (workspace.js:937), so it is a one-off friction rather than a defect people will meet often.
- **Correction:** The reviewer's fix (read target versions inside save()) only narrows the window, because a read-then-write race remains; the conflict message is also worded for a form ('Select it again'), which reads oddly here. Keep P3.

### GGV-06 — The graph views ignore loadGraph's hiddenEdges: links to records outside the view vanish silently, so Work dependencies calls blocked items unblocked and Systems Lens calls fed components sources

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `extensions-graph-gantt` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:684`, `extensions/work-dependencies/view.js:646`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:314`, `extensions/systems-lens/lens.js:288`, `extensions/dependency-graph/graph.js:80`
- **What:** nendo.view.loadGraph() leaves out every link whose source or target is not among the view's nodes (the view's authored filters) and counts them in hiddenEdges 'so a view can say how much it is not drawing' (custom-views contract). None of the three views reads hiddenEdges. Work dependencies counts items with no drawn incoming link as 'unblocked' and highlight() says 'nothing is blocking it'; Systems Lens takes every component with no drawn incoming feed as a declared source (seeds) and computes baseline and take-out verdicts from them.
- **Failure:** A planner view filtered to the Now horizon shows W-10, which is blocked by W-5 in Next: the summary counts W-10 among the unblocked items and selecting it says 'nothing is blocking it', inviting someone to start blocked work. In Systems Lens, a component whose only feeder is filtered out is reported as a declared source and never as 'no path'.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-elk.mjs with hiddenEdges=1 -> {"summary":"6 work items · 1 link · 5 unblocked","selection":"Item 2 · blocked by 0 · blocks 0 · nothing is blocking it"}; dependency-graph hiddenEdges=3 -> "6 records · 1 connection"; systems-lens hiddenEdges=3 -> "6 components · 1 feed · 5 declared sources".
- **Fix and guard:** Read graph.hiddenEdges in project(); add '· N links to items outside this view' to each summary, and in Work dependencies and Systems Lens qualify 'unblocked' / 'declared source' when hiddenEdges > 0 (or query the link type for the selected item's hidden incoming links with records.query before saying 'nothing is blocking it'). Guard: each Review fixture gets hiddenEdges > 0 and asserts the summary names it; falsify by dropping the clause.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: no extension file mentions hiddenEdges (grep covers all of extensions/), Work dependencies counts nodes with no drawn incoming link as unblocked and says 'nothing is blocking it' (view.js:684-688, 646-648), and Systems Lens takes every node with no drawn incoming feed as a declared source (lens.js:314). docs/custom-view-authoring.md:304-306 tells authors to say how many links are not drawn. loadGraph counts an edge in hiddenEdges only when an end is not among the nodes, either an authored filter on the node type (nendo-api.ts:154-163, 360) or a null end. Reachability is the weak point: the shipped definitions bind no filterClause (tools/planner-definition.mjs:685-690, tools/Build-NendoStation.mjs:930-936), and a link with a null end cannot make an item look unblocked wrongly. The misreport needs an author to add a node filter to such a view, which the definition supports (contract line 1443).
- **Correction:** Lower to P3: it breaks the authoring guide's advice but no shipped configuration triggers it. The Work dependencies in-view status chips (view.js:153-161) are a user choice reported as 'N hidden', and a Done blocker not blocking is defensible, so only authored filters are the real exposure. The scenario should be worded as 'if an author adds a node filter to the view'.

### GGV-15 — Kit fitBox mis-fits a one-dimensional drawing and returns a mirroring negative scale for a small or hidden viewport

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `extensions-graph-gantt`

- **Where:** `tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:137`, `tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:138`
- **What:** Any zero width or height returns {scale:1, x:padding, y:padding}, ignoring content.x/y and the other axis; the scale is (viewport - 2*padding)/content with no floor, so a viewport under 32 px gives a negative scale. kit.test.mjs covers only the all-zero box. No package calls fitBox yet, so this is latent.
- **Failure:** A view fitting a row of nodes (height 0) 800 units wide starting at x=100 into a 400x300 frame draws it from x=116 to 916, mostly off-screen; fitting while the frame is hidden (0x0) flips the drawing.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: node -e fitBox(...) -> row of nodes 100..900 at y=50, height 0, viewport 400x300: {"scale":1,"x":16,"y":16}; normal box in a 20x20 viewport: {"scale":-0.06,...}; hidden 0x0 viewport: {"scale":-0.16,...}.
- **Fix and guard:** Scale by the non-zero axis when one is zero and centre on content.x/y; clamp the available size to at least 1 and return null or scale 1 for an unsized viewport. Guard: add the three cases to kit.test.mjs; falsify against the current function.
- **Verifier:** tools/view-kit/nendo-view-kit.js:137 returns {scale:1,x:padding,y:padding} for any zero width or height, ignoring content.x/y and the other axis, and :138 computes (viewport - 2*padding)/content with no floor. I ran fitBox from the kit: a height-0 row 800 wide at x=100 in 400x300 gives {scale:1,x:16,y:16}; a 100x100 box in a 20x20 or 0x0 viewport gives scale -0.12 and -0.32. The code does what is claimed. But no package calls fitBox (grep finds it only in the three kit copies, the source, kit.test.mjs and the authoring guide), the dependency graph and Work dependencies each carry their own fit() that already skips a canvas under 1 px (graph.js:29, view.js:611), and real drawings are boxes with non-zero height, so the one-dimensional case is contrived. Reachability depends on a future caller.
- **Correction:** Latent only. The negative-scale case on an unsized frame is the realistic one (graph.js:27-29 documents that canvases do measure zero before layout); the one-dimensional example is unlikely with node boxes. Exact numbers differ from the reviewer's because content sizes differ.

### R2AP-08 — commands.run sends an entityId the host never reads, so a wrong one runs the command on the command's own record type and answers with a different type's record, or null as if deleted

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `r2-adapter-parity`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:600`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:292`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/WorkbenchProtocol.cs:174`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.cs:475`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:625`
- **What:** The method table takes commandId, entityId, recordId and version. ExecuteCommandPayload has no EntityId, so the host drops it; the Engine finds the command by ID across every application plan and writes the record of that command's own record type. The broker's write() then reads back {entityId: body.entityId, recordId} and answers that record. MCP's execute_command takes no entityId, so it cannot disagree with itself.
- **Failure:** A graph view showing Tasks and Dependencies calls commands.run('cmd.task.done', {entityId: 'entity.dependency', recordId: 'r1', version: 3}). The command marks Task r1 done; the view is answered with Dependency r1 (or null, which the contract defines as 'deleted'), and draws the wrong record or removes r1.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratchpad r2-adapter-parity/probe-broker.mjs -> 'commands.run host payload = {"method":"data.executeCommand","payload":{"commandId":"cmd.task.done","entityId":"entity.project","recordId":"r1",...}}' and 'commands.run read-back = {"entityId":"entity.project","recordId":"r1","limit":1} -> answered {"name":"from entity.project"}'; ExecuteCommandPayload's missing EntityId is source.
- **Fix and guard:** Carry entityId on data.executeCommand and refuse (command-unavailable naming the type) when it is not the command's record type, or have the host answer the command's entity and read back from that. Guard: a broker plus Desktop test with a mismatched entityId expecting a refusal and no write.
- **Verifier:** The mismatch is real in the code: the method table sends commandId, entityId, recordId and version (extension-broker.ts:600-602, custom-views.md:625), but ExecuteCommandPayload (WorkbenchProtocol.cs:174-178) has no EntityId, ExecuteGenericCommandAsync (:649-656) and DesktopSessionController.ExecuteCommandAsync (:348-363) never see it, and the Engine finds the command across all plans and writes plan.Entity.SemanticId with request.RecordId (NendoApplicationService.cs:455, 503-525). The broker's write() then reads back body.entityId (extension-broker.ts:292-300). So a stated param is silently ignored. But the harm needs a view to pass a record of one type with another type's command AND the command's own type to hold a record of the same ID at the same version: otherwise the Engine refuses with record-not-found or a version conflict, which is a correct refusal. schema.describe gives each command its entityId (custom-views.md:1032), nendo-api.ts:562 sends the passed record's real entityId, and Workbench-minted IDs are UUIDs, so a coincident ID and version is possible only in small hand-ID files. I could not establish a path that reaches the wrong write or wrong read-back without a view bug plus a collision. A hardening gap, P3.
- **Correction:** The failure scenario overstates: 'runs the command on the command's own record type' needs record ID and version to coincide in that type; otherwise it is refused. The 'null as if deleted' read-back case needs the command to have succeeded on a record whose same-ID twin does not exist in the view's named type. Fix (carry entityId on data.executeCommand and refuse a mismatch) is sound and cheap.

### R2LAT-06 — Two clocks decide 'today': the Engine's cached TimeZoneInfo.Local is never refreshed, so after a time-zone change command stamps and chart ranges disagree with the screen's filters and calendar

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.cs:532`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/record-window.ts:68`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/plan-selection.ts:133`
- **What:** Command steps resolve today with TimeZoneInfo.Local (NendoApplicationService.cs:532-533) and bucket ranges with DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Now) (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193). .NET caches the local zone for the life of the process until TimeZoneInfo.ClearCachedData() is called, and nothing in src/ calls it or handles WM_TIMECHANGE/SystemEvents.TimeChanged (grep finds none). The Workbench resolves filter clauses, the calendar's today and the timeline year in the renderer (record-window.ts:68-84, plan-selection.ts:133-135), whose V8/ICU clock follows the OS zone change through Chromium's time-zone monitor. The two layers also read different zone databases (Windows registry versus Chromium's bundled ICU), so a rule change one has and the other lacks splits them the same way.
- **Failure:** The owner flies Copenhagen to New York with automatic time zone on and Nendo keeps running in the tray. At 20:00 New York on 12 October (02:00 on the 13th in Copenhagen) they press a 'Done today' command: the Engine stamps 2026-10-13, while the 'Done today' screen filters on 2026-10-12, so the record just completed vanishes from it, the calendar puts it on tomorrow, and a 'last 30 days' trend counts it in a bucket the screen's own filters call the future. It stays wrong until Nendo is restarted.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Pick one source of 'today': either the host calls TimeZoneInfo.ClearCachedData() when Windows reports a time or zone change (WM_TIMECHANGE / SystemEvents.TimeChanged) and pushes its civil date to the Workbench, or the Workbench sends its resolved civil date with command and bucket requests and the Engine uses it. Guard: a Desktop test that raises the time-change notification and asserts ClearCachedData ran (or that the bucket query carries the client's date), and an Engine test that ResolveStepValue and DateBuckets take the same injected civil date the Workbench filter used.
- **Verifier:** The source reads as claimed: command steps resolve today from TimeZoneInfo.Local (NendoApplicationService.cs:532-544) and bucket ranges from DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Now) (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193), both of which use .NET's process-lifetime cached local zone, and grep over src/ finds no TimeZoneInfo.ClearCachedData, SystemEvents.TimeChanged or WM_TIMECHANGE handler. The Workbench resolves its own today with the renderer's JS Date (record-window.ts:68-84, plan-selection.ts:133-135), which Chromium updates on an OS zone change. So after a time-zone change with Nendo kept running, the Engine and the screen can name different days for a few hours. The two Engine call sites use the same cached zone, so they agree with each other; the split is only Engine versus renderer. I could not reproduce it (it needs the OS zone to change under a running host) and it rests on .NET and Chromium caching semantics I could not exercise without a live host. The trigger (travel across zones with Nendo resident, automatic zone on) is rare, the window of disagreement is hours around midnight, and a restart clears it.
- **Correction:** Keep at P3. The 'different zone databases' sentence is speculative and adds nothing; the single cause is the unrefreshed TimeZoneInfo.Local. A ClearCachedData call on time-change would fix the Engine side but not make the two layers share one clock; sending the Workbench's civil date with command and bucket requests would.
