### R2LAT-07 — The proposal preview resolves a trend or activity grid's range against the UTC date, while the running screen uses the local date, so the preview shows other months or days near midnight and on 29 February

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `r2-locale-and-time`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/charts.ts:470`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/surface-preview.ts:86`, `src/Nendo.Engine/DateBuckets.cs:54`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193`
- **What:** sampleBuckets (charts.ts:470-482), which surface-preview.ts:86 uses for a proposal's preview of a trendChart or activityGrid, reads today with getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate, while the host resolves the same words against the local civil date (DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Now)). Its comment says it is 'the preview's own resolution of the same closed words the host resolves'. Its lastTwelveMonths is Date.UTC(year-1, month, date+1), which on 29 February starts a day later than the Engine's today.AddYears(-1).AddDays(1).
- **Failure:** Reviewing an agent's proposal that adds a 'last 6 months' trend at 00:30 on 1 November in Copenhagen shows May to October, while the screen it installs shows June to November. In Apia (UTC+13) every review before 13:00 is a day behind, and at 00:30 on 1 January 'this year' previews 2026 while the screen shows 2027. On 2028-02-29 an activity grid previews 365 days while the screen draws 366.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-time.mjs on the bundled charts.ts with PROBE_TZ=Pacific/Apia at 2026-10-11T19:00Z (local 2026-10-12 08:00) -> todayDate "2026-10-12", previewLast30Days "2026-09-12..2026-10-11"; at local 2027-01-01 00:30 -> previewThisYear "2026-01-01..2026-12-31"; Europe/Copenhagen at local 2026-11-01 00:30 -> previewLast6Months "2026-05-01..2026-10-31". probe-leap.mjs -> 2028-02-29 preview lastTwelveMonths 2027-03-02 .. 2028-02-29 365 days; Engine arithmetic 2027-03-01 .. 2028-02-29 366 days
- **Fix and guard:** Resolve the civil today with the local getters (the same civilDate the filters use) and build the bounds with civil-date arithmetic that mirrors DateBuckets.Resolve, including AddYears' leap-day rule; or ask the host for the bounds. Guard: a charts test that runs sampleBucketed with TZ=Pacific/Apia and Pacific/Pago_Pago at hours either side of UTC midnight and on 2028-02-29 and compares start/end with DateBuckets.Resolve's documented results.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: command today uses TimeZoneInfo.Local (NendoApplicationService.cs:532-533, 544) and bucket ranges use DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Now) (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:193), while the Workbench resolves today with JS Date getters (record-window.ts:68-84, plan-selection.ts:133). A grep of src/ for ClearCachedData, TimeChanged and WM_TIMECHANGE finds nothing, and no doc or ADR states a decision on this. .NET caches TimeZoneInfo.Local for the process life until ClearCachedData, so the Engine side goes stale after a zone change while Chromium's renderer follows the OS. I could not change the system zone to reproduce it. It needs a zone change while the app stays running and a command or range near a day boundary, and a restart fixes it.

### TBI-12 — Assert-Tree refuses a reparse point on any ancestor of the install root, so a relocated profile or AppData can never install or uninstall

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:65`
- **What:** Lines 65-69 walk Split-Path -Parent from $root up to the drive root and throw 'Linked paths are not supported' if any ancestor is a reparse point. The same applies to $previous and the payload source under %TEMP%. A link above the install root cannot make an inventory path escape the root, because Resolve-Owned already checks containment.
- **Failure:** A person who moved C:\Users\<name> or AppData\Local to another drive with a junction runs the installer. Setup always fails, before doing anything, with 'Linked paths are not supported: C:\Users\<name>'.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Check for links only inside the install root, the backup and the payload tree, or resolve the final path once and check containment on the resolved path. Guard: a Test-NendoSetup case that installs into a root reached through a junction in the evidence folder.
- **Verifier:** tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:64-69 does walk Split-Path -Parent from the directory to the drive root and throws 'Linked paths are not supported' for any existing ancestor with the ReparsePoint attribute. It is applied to $root, $previous (566-567), the payload source under %TEMP% (605) and each legacy pilot folder. So a junctioned or symlinked profile, AppData\Local, Temp or Programs makes install and uninstall refuse up front, and the lanes fail the same way if the checkout sits under a link. A link above the root cannot escape Resolve-Owned's lexical containment, so the ancestor check adds little, and ancestor links are same-user controlled. The refusal is fail-closed, names the offending path, and matches the repo-wide 'Linked ... retained' stance (Remove-NendoBuildPayload.ps1:14, Runtime-SelectOwnedFile.ps1:37). It needs an unusual relocation, there is no reproduction beyond reading, and the owner log has no such refusal, so I could not establish that anyone is affected.
- **Correction:** This is a stated non-support rather than a bug. The change would be a policy relaxation: keep the inside-root recursive check and drop or limit the ancestor walk.

### TBI-13 — Assert-Closed refuses whenever any Nendo.Desktop process's path is unreadable, so another signed-in user's Nendo blocks this user's install and uninstall

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `tools-build-installer`

- **Where:** `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:509`, `tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:511`
- **What:** Get-Process -Name 'Nendo.Desktop' lists processes in every session. For another user's process, $process.Path is $null to a non-elevated caller, and '-not $exe' throws 'Close Nendo before installing or uninstalling'.
- **Failure:** On a shared PC with fast user switching, user B left Nendo open. User A cannot install, upgrade or uninstall their own per-user copy, and is told to close a process they cannot see.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Ignore processes whose SessionId differs from the current process's before treating an unreadable path as this install. Guard: extract the predicate and unit-test it with a fake process list (another session with a null path -> allowed; same session with a null path -> refused).
- **Verifier:** tools/Invoke-NendoSetup.ps1:508-516 does what is claimed: Assert-Closed lists every Nendo.Desktop process and throws when $process.Path is null ('-not $exe'), with no SessionId or owner filter. A probe under Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100 (the Sysnative shell NSIS uses; probe in verify/tools-build-installer-13/path-probe.ps1) shows Path is $null for processes the caller cannot open (lsass, csrss, services, winlogon), so another account's Nendo.Desktop would very likely read as null too and block this user's setup. I could not run a second signed-in account, so cross-user reachability is not reproduced. The null-means-refuse branch looks like a deliberate fail-closed choice (an unknown path could be this install), no test or doc covers it, and the scenario (shared PC, fast user switching) is niche for a per-user install, so P3.
- **Correction:** Reproduction is source-only plus the 5.1 null-Path probe above, not a cross-user run. The cheap fix (ignore processes whose SessionId differs from the current one before treating an unreadable path as this install) is sound; note same-session unreadable paths should still fail closed.

### WSP-11 — Complete Idea Garden never fills the Status of existing ideas in the desktop app

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/idea-garden-recipe.ts:139`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:205`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:642`
- **What:** The backfill reads session.records. The desktop client sends boundedRead: true on every request, so the host answers session.getSnapshot from GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync, whose Records is empty (NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:16-17). Only the browser preview host fills session.records.

- **Reproduction:** Executed: node probe-pure.mjs -> `recipe mutations with records -> ['Create the Idea Garden structure and surfaces','Place existing Ideas in the Idea group']` / `recipe mutations with bounded (empty) records -> ['Create the Idea Garden structure and surfaces']`
- **Fix and guard:** Build the backfill from a paged data.queryRecords read with an isNull filter on field.idea.status before preparing, or drop the mutation. Guard: a recipe test given records: [] and a stub query, asserting that the backfill mutation exists.
- **Verifier:** The data path reads as claimed: idea-garden-recipe.ts:139-151 builds the backfill from session.records. host-desktop.ts:205 sends boundedRead:true on every request, WorkbenchProtocol.cs:355-356 binds it, DesktopSessionController.cs:642-644 then calls GetDefinitionSnapshotAsync, and NendoWriteCoordinator.ReadQueries.cs:10-17 returns it with no records (includeRecords:false). Reachability is the weak part: the recipe only applies when the file has no screens at all (session.uiNodes.length > 0 returns null, line 32) yet already has entity.idea with status-less records, which Studio's own flows do not produce (Create record type makes entity.<uuid>). No test or doc exercises the 'Complete Idea Garden' branch. The outcome is mild, ideas sit in the board's ungrouped column.
- **Correction:** Reachability is narrow: needs entity.idea with records but no surfaces (hand-built or agent-built file, or one whose screens were all removed). Not a common path.

### WSP-22 — Make required can draw its dialog over whichever page the person moved to

**P3** · correctness · Plausible · area `workbench-studio-panels`

- **What:** After awaiting data.queryRecords, renderFieldRequirement checks only fileSessionId before writing content.innerHTML. It sets no actionInFlight and does not check that Structure is still on screen. renderReferenceConversion checks targetForm.isConnected; this path does not.

- **Reproduction:** Source

It does not check state.view or content.dataset.place, and it sets no actionInFlight. renderReferenceConversion (line 255) does check targetForm.isConnected. The trailing catch at line 419 would also call showError on whatever page is current. I could not establish practical reachability. <a id="r2sp-12"></a>

### R2SP-12 — The agent work signal announces busy and idle outside its lock, so an earlier call's idle can arrive after a later call's busy

**P3** · concurrency · Plausible · area `r2-several-processes`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentWorkSignal.cs:64`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentWorkSignal.cs:78`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoAgentWorkSignal.cs:94`
- **What:** Begin and End compute the announced state under _gate (_running++ / _running--), but Announce invokes the handler after the lock is released. The transport is stateless, so calls from several clients overlap on different request threads. Nothing orders the deliveries.
- **Failure:** Two clients overlap, for example an agent and the planner mod's poll. Call A's End computes busy=false and is preempted before announcing. Call B's Begin announces busy=true. Then A's stale false is delivered. The taskbar progress goes off, the 'is working' pill hides, and the busy bar falls back to 'Still working…' for the whole of B's long write, until B's own End.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Stamp each announcement with a sequence number taken under the lock and have the handler drop older ones, or deliver from one serialized queue. Guard: a test whose handler blocks the first End's delivery while a second Begin runs, asserting that the last delivered state is busy.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed. NendoAgentWorkSignal.Begin (:64-76) and End (:78-87) compute the announced state under _gate, but Announce (:94-101) takes the lock again and invokes the handler after releasing it, so nothing orders deliveries from different threads. The transport is stateless and Begin/End bracket each call on request threads (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:467, :513, :548), so two clients' calls can overlap. DesktopSessionSignals.cs:151-155 forwards the delivered value as-is and MainWindow.xaml.cs:231-235 enqueues it in arrival order, so a stale busy=false delivered after a newer busy=true leaves the taskbar progress and pill off until the second call's own End. I could not establish practical reachability: the window is a few hundred nanoseconds between lock release and the second lock/handler call, it needs End of one call and Begin of another to coincide in that window, and the effect is a brief cosmetic indicator error that the later End corrects.
- **Correction:** Priority P3 is generous: this is a latent ordering bug with a purely cosmetic, self-correcting effect. The sequence-number fix (stamp under the lock, drop older deliveries) is correct and cheap.

### ABS-03 — Archi Open writes a model in several revisions without first checking references, so a refusal part way leaves a half-imported model

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `extensions-archi-bcm-swarm` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:198`, `tools/archi/canvas/io.ts:390`, `extensions/archi/view.js:1518`
- **What:** planImport maps every sourceId, targetId, elementId, refViewId and folderId to a record ID blindly. importBatches gives a target version only to targets it knows, and a reference to something nobody creates goes out unchanged. openChosen then sends batches of 200, each its own revision, and stops at the first refusal with 'opened only in part ... To start again, make a new Archi model.' Nothing checks before the first write that every reference resolves, or that each relationship is one the file's link rule (Archi: refuse a relationship ArchiMate does not allow) accepts. Measured: Archisurance plus one AssociationRelationship whose target is 'id-nowhere' is accepted by the reader, and the plan goes into 4 batches with 'references to nothing planned: ar-id-dangling ar.concept.target -> ar-id-nowhere'.
- **Failure:** A file from another tool, or an older Archi model, holds one relationship to a missing element, or one the link rule refuses, near the end of the Relations folder. Batches 1-2 commit and batch 3 is refused. The new file is left with every element and half the relationships but no views. History cannot undo the import, so the person must make another new file.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: headless Edge over CDP, scratch truncated-open.html with one dangling AssociationRelationship -> '4 batches; references to nothing planned: ar-id-dangling ar.concept.target -> ar-id-nowhere' and 'opened; {"elements":120,"relationships":177,...}'
- **Fix and guard:** Add a preflight to planImport, or before readChosen enables Open. Every reference field must name a record in plan.creates, a root folder, the model record or an ar.type. Every relationship's (source type, target type, relationship type) must appear in the ar.rule records read. Refuse with the first offending ID before any write, or offer to leave those relationships out and count them in LeftOut. Guard: an io.test.mjs case with a dangling relationship and one with a disallowed relationship, each expecting a refusal or a count before importBatches runs.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: planImport (io.ts:198-323) maps source, target and folder IDs blindly, importBatches (io.ts:419-425) gives a target version only to targets it knows, and openChosen (view.js:1518-1541) sends batches of 200 and stops at the first refusal with 'opened only in part ... make a new Archi model'. No preflight of references or of the ar.rule link rule exists. But this outcome is documented and deliberate: docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:364-367 says 'A refusal part-way leaves the earlier batches, and the status line says how many went through', and extensions/archi/README.md:185-187 says History cannot undo them and to start again with a new model. ADR-0026 item 10 (:116-117) says an .archimate holding an invalid relationship 'is refused, naming it', and its Negative list accepts that an import from a tolerant tool is refused. A dangling relationship endpoint cannot come from Archi itself (archi-online checks only diagram connections, types.ts:371-411); the realistic trigger is an old Archi model with a relationship the 12,829-row table disallows, which I could not run against the host. This is a preflight enhancement with a workaround, not a new defect.
- **Correction:** Priority P3. The partial-import behaviour is already documented in docs/design/archi-in-nendo.md:364-367 and in the Archi README, and a dangling reference needs a file Archi itself would not write. The finding's measured evidence is the planner output, not a host refusal, and the link-rule scenario is the realistic one but was not exercised.

### DAE-07 — The Agent page requests agentSession.list every 3 seconds, and each one walks PATH under the request gate, so one unreachable PATH share stalls the whole window

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `desktop-agents-extensions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:87`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopSessionController.LaunchedAgent.cs:264`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/Agents/DesktopAgentCatalog.cs:148`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:770`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/view-agent.ts:648`
- **What:** ListLaunchableAgentsAsync enters the request gate and calls DescribeLaunchableCore, which runs DesktopAgentCatalog.List: for each of five known programs Resolve tries File.Exists on up to four extensions in every PATH folder, then reads npm shims. The Workbench's 3-second poll calls refreshAgentStatus, which requests agentSession.list, whenever the Agent page is shown. Every other gated request waits behind it.
- **Failure:** A laptop off its VPN has a mapped or UNC tools folder on PATH. With the Agent page open, each poll holds the request gate for about 20 seconds, so saving a record, opening a file or switching tabs waits behind it, and the next poll starts as the last one ends.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: pwsh -File scratchpad/review/desktop-agents-extensions/catalog-probe.ps1 (shipped DesktopAgentCatalog.List) -> "this machine: PATH has 62 folders; one list = 29,2 ms (mean of 10)" and "with one unreachable share first on PATH: one list = 21,1 s".
- **Fix and guard:** Resolve the catalogue outside the request gate (it reads no file state) and cache it for a short time, invalidated when the person sets a command or presses a refresh; skip or time-box UNC and unreachable PATH folders. Guard: a Desktop test with a PATH whose first folder blocks (an injected probe delegate) must answer a concurrent gated request without waiting for the list; falsify by moving the resolve back under the gate.
- **Verifier:** The code path is as claimed: main.ts:770-798 polls every 3 s while state.view === 'agent', refreshAgentStatus (view-agent.ts:644-649) requests agentSession.list each time, ListLaunchableAgentsAsync (LaunchedAgent.cs:85-98) holds the SemaphoreSlim request gate (DesktopRequestBinding.cs:38) while DescribeLaunchableCore -> DesktopAgentCatalog.List -> Resolve does File.Exists across every PATH folder and four extensions for five programs plus the custom command (DesktopAgentCatalog.cs:97-160); WorkbenchProtocol.Agents.cs:9-12 documents that list waits on the gate. The reviewer's probe measured 29 ms normally and 21 s for one list with an unreachable share first on PATH. What is not established is the repeated stall: only one list was timed, so 'each poll holds the gate about 20 seconds' is an extrapolation (the SMB client may fail fast on later attempts), and an unreachable UNC/mapped folder on PATH is an unusual environment. In a normal environment the cost is negligible. It is a latent robustness gap, not a common-path defect.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The refresh only matters with an unreachable PATH folder and the Agent page open. Note that the poll is not re-entrancy guarded (setInterval keeps firing), so a slow list could queue further gated requests behind it; that is plausible from the code but was not measured. Caching the catalogue off the gate, as proposed, is a sound fix.

### DSH-02 — A cancelled or superseded top-level navigation tears down a healthy Workbench (NavigationCompleted treats OperationCanceled as fatal); a URL drag or a file dropped while a dialog is open triggers it

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `desktop-shell` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:232`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:222`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:267`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/main.ts:584`
- **What:** Workbench_NavigationStarting cancels every top-level navigation whose URI is not https://app.nendo.local. Workbench_NavigationCompleted calls ShowRecovery for any !args.IsSuccess, without looking at WebErrorStatus or which navigation it was. WebView2 raises NavigationCompleted with IsSuccess=false / OperationCanceled for a navigation cancelled in NavigationStarting and for one superseded by another. The Workbench only calls preventDefault on dragenter/dragover/drop when a file is dragged and no dialog[open] exists (main.ts:584-617), so a dragged link, or a file dropped while a Workbench dialog is open, takes Chromium's default drop action: navigate the top document to the URL or file:/// path. ProcessFailed also treats RenderProcessUnresponsive (a busy, not dead, renderer) as fatal, contradicting the method's own summary that only processes 'going away' warrant recovery.
- **Failure:** A person drags a link from Edge onto a non-editable part of the Nendo window, or drops a .nendo file while the Ctrl K palette or a confirmation <dialog> is open: the navigation is cancelled, NavigationCompleted reports OperationCanceled, DetachWorkbench closes the WebView, unsaved typing in a record form is lost, and 'Studio recovery: The app view could not load (OperationCanceled).' replaces the app; a view-failure line and a 'needs attention' notification are recorded for a non-failure.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Only treat the host's own initial navigation as fatal: remember the NavigationId of core.Navigate(WorkbenchUri) (or the first allowed NavigationStarting) and ignore NavigationCompleted for other ids and for WebErrorStatus.OperationCanceled; for RenderProcessUnresponsive offer a wait/restart choice rather than tearing down. Also preventDefault dragover/drop for every drag in the Workbench. Guard: extract the decision into a pure function (isFatalNavigationFailure(navigationId, hostNavigationId, status)) with a test for OperationCanceled, and a journey that dispatches a URL drop and asserts the WebView survives.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: MainPage.xaml.cs:222-229 cancels any top-level navigation off https://app.nendo.local and :232-244 calls ShowRecovery for every !IsSuccess without looking at WebErrorStatus or the navigation id. main.ts:584-617 only preventDefaults dragenter/dragover/drop when a file is dragged (draggedFileCount>0) and no dialog[open] exists (dragover/drop also bail when dropTarget is hidden), so a dragged link, or a file dropped over an open dialog, takes the browser default. WebView2 documents OperationCanceled as the status when the app cancels in NavigationStarting, so recovery would follow. I could not run WebView2 to observe it, and the trigger needs an unusual gesture (dropping a link or file on the window while a dialog is open), the Restart view button recovers, and file data is not at risk, so P3 rather than P2. The RenderProcessUnresponsive part is NOT a defect: docs/contracts/custom-views.md ('When a view fails', ~line 1161) and ADR-0013 mandate that RenderProcessUnresponsive of the Workbench renderer sends the app to recovery.
- **Correction:** Drop the ProcessFailed/RenderProcessUnresponsive claim: the contract requires it (at most the method summary comment at MainPage.xaml.cs:245-249 is imprecise). Keep only the NavigationCompleted-on-cancel issue, rated P3, source-read only.

### DSH-03 — DeliverResponse posts to CoreWebView2 without the try/catch PostWorkbenchEvent has, so a response landing after the browser process died crashes the host instead of showing recovery

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `desktop-shell` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:304`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:276`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:272`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainPage.xaml.cs:395`
- **What:** Workbench_WebMessageReceived is async void. Its DeliverResponse checks only _webView is not null and the generation, then calls _webView.CoreWebView2?.PostWebMessageAsJson(responseJson) unguarded. PostWorkbenchEvent wraps the same call in catch (Exception) with the comment 'The renderer went away between the check and the post', i.e. the call is known to throw in that state. Workbench_ProcessFailed does not detach synchronously: it TryEnqueues ShowRecovery, so continuations already queued on the dispatcher (off-UI-thread request completions resuming on the UI thread) run first against a CoreWebView2 whose browser process has exited.
- **Failure:** The WebView2 browser process exits (memory pressure, GPU/driver reset) while the Workbench has reads in flight. ProcessFailed(BrowserProcessExited) queues ShowRecovery; a request completes first, DeliverResponse calls PostWebMessageAsJson on the dead browser, the COMException escapes the async void handler and the process terminates. The person loses the window, the tray icon and any agent connection, instead of getting the recovery panel this code path exists to show.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Wrap the post in DeliverResponse in try/catch(Exception) exactly like PostWorkbenchEvent (and still call ApplyFileName). Better, in Workbench_ProcessFailed set a 'browser gone' flag (or bump _workbenchGeneration) synchronously before enqueueing ShowRecovery so later deliveries skip. Guard: a test that injects a throwing post delegate into the delivery path and asserts no exception escapes; falsify by removing the catch.
- **Verifier:** MainPage.xaml.cs:300-306: DeliverResponse checks only _webView non-null and the generation, then calls _webView.CoreWebView2?.PostWebMessageAsJson(responseJson) with no try/catch, whereas PostWorkbenchEvent (:393-403) wraps the identical call in catch (Exception) because the post can fail when the renderer is gone. Workbench_ProcessFailed (:251-275) only TryEnqueues ShowRecovery, so DetachWorkbench/the generation bump run later; a continuation queued earlier (after Task.Run at :293-295 it resumes on the UI thread and calls DeliverResponse directly) can reach the dead CoreWebView2. Workbench_WebMessageReceived is async void and App.xaml.cs has no UnhandledException handler (grep finds none in src/Nendo.Desktop), so an exception there ends the process. Real asymmetry, but the window is narrow (browser process death with a response completing before ShowRecovery runs), a failure already in progress, and I could not confirm that PostWebMessageAsJson throws in that state, so P3.
- **Correction:** Fix is as stated (try/catch like PostWorkbenchEvent, still call ApplyFileName). Priority P3: it needs a browser-process death coinciding with an in-flight response.

### DSH-19 — An exception from session shutdown escapes the async void AppWindow_Closing after Exit() and ends the process with an unhandled-exception crash

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:476`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:466`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopSessionController.cs:490`
- **What:** AppWindow_Closing awaits page.ShutdownAsync() in try/finally with no catch; DisposeAsync -> CloseFileCoreAsync can throw from EndLaunchedAgentCoreAsync, the MCP host's DisposeAsync, the proposal store's CloseFileSessionAsync or coordinator.DisposeAsync. The finally calls Close() and Application.Current.Exit(), then the exception is rethrown on the dispatcher with no UnhandledException handler in App.
- **Failure:** Exit Nendo while the file has just lost write authority (proposal cleanup throws): the window closes, then Windows Error Reporting records a crash and the person may see a 'stopped working' dialog for a normal exit.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** catch (Exception) around ShutdownAsync in AppWindow_Closing (record it in the failure log when enabled) before the finally. Guard: a test whose controller's dispose throws and that asserts the closing handler completes without throwing.
- **Verifier:** MainWindow.xaml.cs:476-491 awaits page.ShutdownAsync() (MainPage.xaml.cs:374-379 -> DesktopSessionController.DisposeAsync -> CloseFileCoreAsync) in try/finally with no catch, and src has no UnhandledException handler (grep empty). The dispose chain does throw by design: NendoLocalMcpHost.DisposeAsync (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:711-716) rethrows an IOException when discovery-file delete or revoke fails (NendoDiscoveryStore.DeleteIfPresent, :151-167, only swallows not-found), and NendoAgentProposals.CloseFileSessionAsync (:489) rethrows the first reject failure. StopAgentAccessCoreAsync awaits the host dispose uncaught (DesktopAgentAccess.cs:419), while StopUnhealthyAgentAccessCoreAsync (:439-445) wraps the same call in a catch, showing the author knows it can throw. So the exception reaches the async void handler after Close()/Exit(); that the process then reports a crash (rather than just exiting) follows from normal async-void/WinUI behaviour but I could not run it. The trigger needs an exit-time cleanup failure, so it is rare and the effect is a crash report on an exit that was happening anyway.
- **Correction:** The cited trigger (proposal cleanup after losing write authority) is weak: CloseFileSessionAsync runs only when _service.Capabilities.Mutate is true (DesktopAgentAccess.cs:430), which is false once authority is lost. The more direct trigger is NendoLocalMcpHost.DisposeAsync throwing IOException when its discovery file cannot be deleted (locked by a reader or antivirus) or RevokeAllAsync/DiscardAllDraftsAsync fails, with agent access on. Fix is unchanged: catch around ShutdownAsync before the finally.

### DSH-23 — MainWindow's constructor calls AppWindow.SetIcon unguarded, unlike ApplyIcons, so a missing or unreadable icon ends the process before any window

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `desktop-shell`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:34`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:127`
- **What:** Line 34 calls AppWindow.SetIcon(Assets\AppIcon.ico) outside any try; ApplyIcons wraps the same call in catch (Exception) because it can throw. The constructor runs from OnLaunched, so an exception there exits before the recovery panel exists.
- **Failure:** An install where AppIcon.ico was removed or locked (antivirus quarantine, partial upgrade): Nendo exits at launch with no window instead of opening without its icon.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Route the constructor's icon through ApplyIcons(null) (which already catches). Guard: a test constructing the icon path to a missing file and asserting no throw from the helper.
- **Verifier:** MainWindow.xaml.cs:34 calls AppWindow.SetIcon on Assets\AppIcon.ico with no try, while ApplyIcons (:124-137) wraps the same API in catch (Exception) with the comment that nothing depends on the icon. The constructor runs from App.OnLaunched (App.xaml.cs:34) with no guard, and there is no UnhandledException handler, so a throw there ends the process before any window or recovery panel. The rest of the code treats a missing AppIcon.ico as tolerable: DesktopTrayIcon.LoadTrayIcon returns IntPtr.Zero on !File.Exists (DesktopTrayIcon.cs:189-190) and DesktopNotifier falls back to Register() (DesktopNotifier.cs:45-47). So the unguarded constructor call is the one inconsistent site. I could not confirm from the repository that AppWindow.SetIcon throws for a missing or unreadable file (it appears to, and ApplyIcons assumes so), and the trigger needs the shipped icon to be deleted or locked after install (the installer carries it: Build-NendoInstaller.ps1:57), a damaged install that would likely have other problems. Robustness hardening, not a common-path defect.
- **Correction:** The fix 'route the constructor's icon through ApplyIcons(null)' is slightly off: ApplyIcons also touches _tray and _notifier, which are not yet created at line 34 (null-safe, but they are set up later in AttachShell), so a try/catch around the single SetIcon call is the simpler equivalent. The suggested guard (test that a missing icon path does not throw) cannot run without a WinUI window, so the guard would need to be a gate lane or a small testable helper.

### ECO-01 — Restore/upgrade turns into an 'interrupted replacement' when any other handle on the active file lacks FILE_SHARE_DELETE, including a read-only Nendo session of the same file

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-coordinator` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Restore.cs:180`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Restore.cs:189`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Restore.cs:219`, `src/Nendo.Engine/VerifiedFileMove.cs:46`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:76`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:21`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Open.cs:44`, `src/Nendo.Engine/InstanceOwnership.cs:29`
- **What:** ExecuteReplacementCoreAsync sets _replacementRetired = true and calls NotifyAuthorityLost (Restore.cs:180-181) before it takes VerifiedFileMove.Acquire(_path, ...) (Restore.cs:189). OpenExclusive asks for GENERIC_READ\|DELETE with share READ (VerifiedFileMove.cs:46-47), so it fails while any other handle lacks FILE_SHARE_DELETE. OpenReadOnlyCoreAsync pins the file with FileShare.ReadWrite and no Delete (Open.cs:76), and ObserveAsync/IdentifyAsync do the same (Open.cs:21, 44). Any exception after retirement is rethrown as NendoReplacementInterruptedException (Restore.cs:219-221). In that state the finally keeps the .recovery.json marker, the receipt, the stage and the pre-change copy (Restore.cs:229-245), even though nothing was moved. The instance-in-use refusal tells the person to open the same file read-only in another session (InstanceOwnership.cs:29), which is exactly the handle that blocks the move.
- **Failure:** Window A has Plan.nendo open for editing. Window B opens the same file read-only, as the instance-in-use message suggests. In A the person restores a backup. Staging passes and the marker is written. Acquire then fails with a sharing violation (win32 32), and A's session closes with 'The replacement did not finish… Inspect the recovery record and retained original'. No retained original exists, because nothing moved. Plan.nendo now opens only in recovery (replacement-pending) until the person works through the recovery review, and two hidden full copies (.nendo-stage-restore-*, .nendo-stage-current-*) plus a receipt are left in the folder.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-share.ps1 (scratch) opening a file with FileShare.ReadWrite, then the same CreateFileW call OpenExclusive makes -> "exclusive with no other handle: OK" / "exclusive while a read-only pin (FileShare.ReadWrite) is open: FAILED win32=32"
- **Fix and guard:** Treat a failure to acquire the original's exclusive handle, before any namespace change, as a clean refusal. Delete the owned marker, receipt and stages (their identities are held) and throw a typed 'file-in-use' precondition. Alternatively, open the read-only and observe pins with FileShare.ReadWrite\|FileShare.Delete; the handle follows the renamed original, and later operations re-inspect _path and compare digests. Guard: an Engine test that holds OpenReadOnlyAsync on the target while a writable coordinator runs RestoreAsync. It asserts either success or a typed refusal, and that no <file>.recovery.json or .nendo-stage-* remains.
- **Verifier:** The mechanism is real: Restore.cs:180-189 sets _replacementRetired and writes the pending marker before VerifiedFileMove.Acquire, whose OpenExclusive (VerifiedFileMove.cs:46-47) requests DELETE with share READ only, and OpenReadOnlyCoreAsync pins with FileShare.ReadWrite (Open.cs:76), so a concurrent read-only holder gives a sharing violation. That IOException is rewrapped as NendoReplacementInterruptedException (Restore.cs:219) and the marker, receipt and stages are kept (229-245); the existing test TargetChangesDuringPinHandoff... shows this post-retirement policy is deliberate. Reachability is narrower than claimed: Desktop is one process per file and a second open of an owned file is handed to the owner window first (MainPage.FileActions.cs:164, DesktopWindowHandoff.cs), so a concurrent read-only session only arises when the reader opened first or the handoff failed. Nothing is lost: the original is untouched, and the recovery review offers KeepActive (ReplacementResolution.cs:64-66), though that path also uses VerifiedFileMove.Acquire and fails until the other handle closes. This is a rare-trigger polish issue (clean refusal before the marker), not a P2.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2. The 'Window B opens read-only as the instance-in-use message suggests' scenario is mostly pre-empted by DesktopWindowHandoff, and the 'instance-in-use' message is only reached when the handoff fails. Recovery is possible via KeepActive once the other handle is closed.

<a id="eco-02"></a>

### ECO-02 — FoldHistoryAsync reports a committed, destructive fold as failed when the post-commit VACUUM or re-inspection throws, and never raises Committed

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-coordinator` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:65`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:67`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:74`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.HistoryFold.cs:47`, `src/Nendo.Desktop/DesktopFileReplacement.cs:38`
- **What:** After store.FoldHistoryAsync commits and _authority = trusted (HistoryFold.cs:55-64), the method runs store.VacuumAsync(cancellationToken) and SqliteNendoStore.InspectAsync(_path, cancellationToken) (lines 65 and 67). AfterCommit and Committed are raised only after both succeed (lines 74-75). VACUUM needs free space about the size of the database for its temp copy and journal, and the Desktop has just written a full backup beside the file (DesktopFileReplacement.cs:38-42). A SqliteException (SQLITE_FULL) or an OperationCanceledException therefore leaves the method raw, after the history is already gone. The fold also minted a new session token, so backup.Authority != _authority on any retry (line 47).
- **Failure:** A 200 MB planner sits on a nearly full disk. History → Fold writes 'X before folding …nendo', and the fold transaction commits. VACUUM then fails with 'database or disk is full'. The person is shown an error for a fold that actually removed the history. The History view keeps listing the folded revisions, because Committed never fired. The file was not shrunk, and a retry reports there is nothing to fold.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Raise AfterCommit and Committed right after `_authority = trusted`. Run VACUUM with CancellationToken.None as best effort, catch SqliteException, and return the fold result with a 'space not reclaimed' flag. Keep the inspection-to-recovery rule, but surface it as a committed outcome rather than a raw exception. Guard: an Engine test that forces VACUUM to fail (a fault seam, or PRAGMA max_page_count on the connection) and asserts FoldHistoryAsync returns the result, Committed fires once, and the history is folded.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: store.FoldHistoryAsync commits (SqliteNendoStore.HistoryFold.cs:203-208) and _authority is updated (HistoryFold.cs:64), then store.VacuumAsync (HistoryFold.cs:65; store line 294, a plain VACUUM) and InspectAsync (line 67) run on the caller's token, and AfterCommit/Committed fire only at lines 74-75. A SQLITE_FULL from VACUUM would surface as a raw SqliteException after the history is gone, and a retry would hit preview.CanFold=false in DesktopFileReplacement.cs:34 ('history-fold-nothing'). Reachability is narrow: it needs a disk or temp volume full at the exact moment of the VACUUM, and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite only checks the token before starting a command, so cancellation matters only in the gap between commit and VACUUM. Impact is a misleading error and a missed Committed notification (MCP host and Desktop FileCommitted subscribers); the fold itself is correct and the backup exists, so there is no data loss and the session stays consistent.
- **Correction:** P3, not P2: the failure is confined to disk-full or cancel-in-a-small-window, nothing is lost, and the folded history shows on the next read. 'The History view keeps listing the folded revisions' is overstated since the view reads the store on load; only the push refresh (Committed) is missed.

<a id="eco-05"></a>

### ECO-05 — Proposal workspace deletion is fatal where cleanup should be best effort: a locked temp file turns a restore into an interrupted replacement, and makes Reject fail

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Restore.cs:182`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:55`, `src/Nendo.Engine/ProposalWorkspace.cs:236`
- **What:** After retirement, ExecuteReplacementCoreAsync calls the throwing ProposalWorkspace.Delete for each pending proposal (Restore.cs:182). That is Directory.Delete(recursive) (ProposalWorkspace.cs:236-242), which throws while any reader holds a file inside the workspace. The IOException is converted to NendoReplacementInterruptedException (Restore.cs:219-221) before the store is disposed or anything is moved. RejectProposalAsync persists Rejected and then calls the same Delete before _proposals.Remove (Promotion.cs:53-56), so a lock fails the reject and leaves the proposal listed. A TryDelete exists and CleanupAbandoned sweeps on dispose under the still-held instance lease.
- **Failure:** Two agent proposals are waiting, and a scanner or indexer is reading one proposal.nendo in %TEMP%. The person restores a backup and confirms that the proposals may be discarded. The restore stops with 'The replacement did not finish', the original file is untouched but flagged replacement-pending, and opening it requires the recovery review.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: probe-share.ps1 (scratch) holding a FileShare.ReadWrite reader on proposal.nendo, then Directory.Delete(workspace, recursive) -> "IOException: The process cannot access the file 'proposal.nendo' because it is being used by another process."
- **Fix and guard:** Use ProposalWorkspace.TryDelete in both places. Clear _proposals regardless, and set _proposalCleanupPending so the abandoned-workspace sweep finishes the job. Guard: a test that holds a FileStream on a proposal's proposal.nendo during RestoreAsync(confirmDiscardProposals: true) and during RejectProposalAsync. It asserts both complete and no .recovery.json remains.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: ProposalWorkspace.Delete (ProposalWorkspace.cs:236-242) is a throwing Directory.Delete(recursive). Restore.cs:182 calls it after _replacementRetired is set, so an IOException becomes NendoReplacementInterruptedException (Restore.cs:219) with the marker and receipt kept and nothing moved. RejectProposalAsync (Promotion.cs:54-56) persists Rejected and calls the same Delete before _proposals.Remove, so a lock leaves a Rejected proposal listed. The non-throwing TryDelete already exists and Proposals.cs:153-166 deliberately uses it for this reason. What I could not establish is a realistic holder of a handle without FILE_SHARE_DELETE inside %TEMP%/nendo-proposals-v1: the clone store is disposed before the workspace is deleted and common scanners open with delete sharing, so the trigger is an external lock, which is rare. Impact when it happens is a recoverable replacement-pending state or a failed Reject that can be retried.
- **Correction:** The probe only shows Directory.Delete fails under a FileShare.ReadWrite reader; it does not show any Nendo-side or common-scanner handle that does this. Treat as an inconsistency with the existing TryDelete/CleanupAbandoned convention, not a likely failure. P3.

<a id="eco-06"></a>

### ECO-06 — Post-commit work uses the caller's token and unisolated handlers, so a committed write can be reported as failed and skip the Committed events

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-coordinator`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:286`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:89`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:282`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoWriteCoordinator.Promotion.cs:362`
- **What:** After a definition-lane commit, ApplyAsync, PromoteProposalAsync and CompensateRevisionAsync await RefreshBehaviourRequirementAsync(cancellationToken) before RaiseCommitted (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:285-287; Promotion.cs:281-285 and 361-363). An OperationCanceledException there propagates although the store has committed. The comment at Promotion.cs:274-275 says derivative failures must never read as a failed transaction. RaiseCommitted also invokes Committed and CommittedChanges subscribers without the per-handler isolation NotifyAuthorityLost applies (lines 86-101 versus 458-464), so one throwing subscriber fails the caller and starves the rest.
- **Failure:** An agent's definition write commits. Its MCP request is cancelled during the brief refresh read. The agent receives an error, and the open screens are not told about the change (Committed never fired). For a promotion the proposal also stays in Applying until a retry finds the receipt. If the definition installed the file's first trigger, the cached requirement stays stale and Capabilities report Mutate=true while the store refuses edits.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Pass CancellationToken.None to every post-commit read. Wrap each Committed/CommittedChanges handler like NotifyAuthorityLost. Guard: an internal AfterStoreCommit seam that cancels the token. Assert the call returns the committed result, Committed fired once, and BehaviourTrust reflects the new definition.
- **Verifier:** The token half reads as claimed: after a definition-lane commit, ApplyAsync (NendoWriteCoordinator.cs:285-287), PromoteProposalAsync (Promotion.cs:281-284) and CompensateRevisionAsync (361-363) await RefreshBehaviourRequirementAsync(cancellationToken), which reads the store with that token (cs:156-163), before RaiseCommitted, so a cancel landing between commit and that read surfaces as OperationCanceledException with _authority already advanced and Committed not raised. The window is tiny and only applies to definition-lane writes. A retry with the same idempotency key replays the receipt and re-runs the refresh (cs:285 is not gated on IsIdempotentReplay), though a retried promotion goes through FinishCommittedProposalAsync and does not refresh. The stale requirement fails closed, since the store itself refuses edits. The unisolated-handler half is theoretical: RaiseCommitted (cs:86-102) invokes subscribers directly, but the only subscribers are DesktopAgentAccess.cs:390-397 (null-check plus an event) and NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:337-339 and NendoChangeFeed.Signal (TryWrite on a channel), none of which throws, and the documented contract (cs:70-74) says handlers must only marshal or queue.
- **Correction:** P3 and weaker than described: no current subscriber can throw, so 'one throwing subscriber starves the rest' is a hardening suggestion, not an observed defect. The cancel-after-commit window needs a client cancellation in microseconds after a definition commit, and a replay with the same key heals the cached requirement for ApplyAsync/Compensate.

<a id="esq-11"></a>

### ESQ-11 — Internal full scans page with change-bound cursors, so any unrelated commit fails an import, a move or an export with a paging message

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-service-queries`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/CsvReferenceCodes.cs:125`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:229`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Hierarchy.cs:214`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Csv.cs:134`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Csv.cs:180`, `src/Nendo.Engine/NendoApplicationService.Csv.cs:270`
- **What:** These loop over QueryRecordsAsync or QueryRevisionOperationsAsync with a cursor that binds the file-wide change sequence: - CsvCodeResolver.CreateAsync reads every record of the target type, 100 per page, with calculations; - SiblingsAsync reads all siblings; - ReplayMoveAsync reads a move's revision; - ReadRecordedTargetVersionsAsync reads a revision's operations; - ExportCsvAsync reads 50 records per page, computing calculations it never writes, and turns a stale page into 'stale-csv-export'. Any commit between pages makes the cursor stale. That includes an automatic action, another client, or a custom view's nendo.state write. In addition, CsvCodeResolver is rebuilt on every DecodeRowsAsync call, and the native importer calls it once per 100-row batch, so the whole target type is re-read for each batch.
- **Failure:** During a 10,000-row tree import, or a move among more than 100 siblings, a Garden view saving a draft (a Data revision) makes the next page throw 'The file changed during paging. Restart from the first page.' The import batch or the drag fails with a message about paging the person never did. A 10,000-record export is 200 pages, and one agent write during them fails it. A 10,000-row import with code matching re-reads the growing target type about 100 times, computing calculations for each page.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Do these scans in one read: an internal store method that returns the needed columns inside one deferred transaction. That keeps the export consistent without a change-bound cursor. Or look codes up per distinct value with an eq filter. Build the resolver once per import and pass it to each batch. Guard: a test that commits an unrelated write between the resolver's pages, between sibling pages, and between export pages must not fail the decode, the move or the export.
- **Verifier:** The mechanism is real: NendoQueryCursor.Decode (NendoQueryCursor.cs:32-33) throws 'stale-cursor' on any change-sequence difference, and CsvCodeResolver.CreateAsync (CsvReferenceCodes.cs:125-135) and SiblingsAsync (Hierarchy.cs:229-239) loop public QueryRecordsAsync pages with no retry, unlike the view API's queryAll (nendo-api.ts:120-123). So a commit between two pages of a target type or sibling set larger than 100 fails the decode or move with a paging message. Reachability is narrow, though: it needs more than 100 rows and a concurrent commit inside a window of milliseconds, a retry succeeds, and the two revision-operation loops (Hierarchy.cs:214, Csv.cs:137) need more than 100 or 200 operations in one revision, which import batches of 50 or 100 and ordinary moves do not reach.
- **Correction:** Two of the sub-claims are wrong. (1) Export: ExportCsvAsync (Csv.cs:270-272) compares the page change sequence on purpose, and NendoCsvExportPage's doc says a page read after somebody else committed does not belong in the same export, so 'stale-csv-export' is documented behaviour, not a defect. (2) Rebuilding CsvCodeResolver per batch is required: Resolve's 'a row an earlier batch committed is a record of the file by now' (CsvReferenceCodes.cs:180-181) relies on re-reading the target type, so the proposed 'build once and pass to each batch' would break parent resolution across batches. The agent importer already decodes all rows once (NendoImportService.cs:149), and the native flow has a human review dialog per batch, so the re-read cost is not the 100-fold blow-up described. Keep only the stale-cursor-without-retry point for resolver and sibling scans, at P3.

<a id="ext-10"></a>

### EXT-10 — State kept for a removed view is never deleted and keeps counting against the package's 1 MiB

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `engine-extensions`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:556`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs:491`
- **What:** Rows are keyed by the view definition's node ID. The only DELETE is the per-key forget, which the broker can send only for the mounted view's own ID. Nothing removes rows when the view node is removed. RequireStateBoundsAsync sums `length(CAST(value_json AS BLOB))` over every row of the package, live views or not, and MCP neither reads nor writes state.
- **Failure:** A view keeps about 300 KB of layout per view, and the person removes and re-adds it a few times (Studio's Add view form mints a new node ID each time). The orphaned rows fill the 1 MiB, and every state write by every view of the package is refused with state-too-large. No surface can free the space.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Exclude rows whose view_id names no current view node from the package byte sum, or delete a view's state in the same mutation that removes the view node, retained in evidence so compensation restores it. Guard: a test that removes a view with state and then writes 1 MiB for a new view of the same package, expecting success.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. A grep of src for __nendo_extension_state finds only the per-key DELETE in ExecuteSetExtensionStateAsync (SqliteNendoStore.ExtensionPackages.cs, about line 512) and the new-file wipe at NewFile.cs:374. Nothing removes rows when a view node is removed. RequireStateBoundsAsync sums length(value_json) over every row of the package (about line 556), so rows for views that no longer exist count toward the 1 MiB StatePackageBytes. The broker takes viewId from the mount, so a live view cannot free an old view's rows. Retention is partly deliberate: ADR-0013 (line 340) keeps a removed package's rows so compensation restores them, and contract line 1564 says a removed view root can be compensated. But the unbounded accumulation is not addressed anywhere. Reachability is thin: a single value is at most 64 KiB, the state is described as small JSON, and the person would have to remove and re-add a view with large state about 16 times or more, so P3 and unlikely.
- **Correction:** Note that retention of a removed view's state is consistent with the documented compensation story, so the fix should be more careful than deleting on removal. For example, exclude rows whose view_id names no live view from the byte sum, or delete them when the removal can no longer be compensated. The 'Add view mints a new node ID each time' premise was not checked; it is not needed for the defect.

### GDN-20 — The Garden lane measures moving layouts and held reads after fixed waits

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `extensions-garden`

- **Where:** `tools/Gate-Garden.mjs:581`, `tools/Gate-Garden.mjs:610`, `tools/Gate-Garden.mjs:945`, `tools/Gate-Garden.mjs:1085`, `tools/Gate-Garden.mjs:108`
- **What:** 66 waitForTimeout calls; for example 1,600 ms before measuring the spread of the force layout (581), 1,200 ms after Fit before clicking a note's centre (610), 1,100 ms after a 700 ms held records.get before asserting the last note won (945), and 1,600 ms before measuring the Overview hero (1085).
- **Failure:** On a busy or locked desktop the layout or the held read is still settling when the wait ends, and the lane fails at HEAD without a defect.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Wait for the condition: gardenGraph.state().alpha below alphaMin, the held request answered (broker.requests), or window.garden.note equal to the expected ID. Guard: run the lane with CPU throttling (CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and require it to pass.
- **Verifier:** The cited code reads as claimed: Gate-Garden.mjs has 66 waitForTimeout lines, and :581 (1600 ms before hover helpers that need nodes at rest), :610 (1200 ms after Fit, which runs a 450 ms d3 transition at extensions/garden/graph.js:309/328 before a real-pointer click on a node centre), :945 (1100 ms after a 700 ms held records.get, then asserts the last-opened note won) and :1085 (1600 ms before the Overview hero 'inside the box' check) all measure after a fixed wait. The owner's own memory (nendo-gate-fixed-waits-flake, 2026-10-06) records this lane failing at HEAD on a locked workstation for the same reason, so a late-settling layout is a credible failure mode. But I could not reproduce or trace a flake of these specific waits, and the margins are large (750 ms after Fit, 400 ms after the held read), so reachability only holds on a throttled or locked desktop; it is a hardening suggestion, not a demonstrated defect.
- **Correction:** Drop :108 from the locations: there the 2000 ms wait is the product requirement being measured ('still within two seconds'), so replacing it with a wait-for-condition would remove the check. The :581 spread assertion (laid.w > 120) is not settle-sensitive, because graph.js:176-179 runs the first-layout ticks before drawing; the wait there protects the later hover/centre measurements. :945's 700 ms hold is intentional. The real candidates are :610 (click after Fit) and :1085 (inside-box after remount), with waitForFunction on gardenGraph.state().alpha / transform settling as the fix.

<a id="mhs-07"></a>

### MHS-07 — Discovery entries are trusted on PID liveness alone, so a crashed Nendo's entry is listed, and never swept, once its PID is reused

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `mcp-host-security`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:238`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:269`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:243`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:114`
- **What:** ReadValidEntry admits an entry when Process.GetProcessById(ProcessId).HasExited is false. It never checks that the process is Nendo, or that it started before CreatedAt. The sweep (CleanupStaleEntries) uses the same rule and runs only when a host writes its own entry. Only DisposeAsync deletes an entry, so a killed or crashed process leaves its entry behind, and Windows reuses PIDs freely. The sweep also enumerates only *.json, so a `.{run}.{guid}.tmp` left by a crash between CreateNew and File.Move is never removed.
- **Failure:** Nendo is ended from Task Manager while BCM.nendo has access on, and another process later reuses its PID. nendo://host/instances then lists BCM.nendo at its old endpoint as a running Nendo. That breaks the contract's promise that 'a dead host is never offered as a place to work'. If a later host reuses that port, the agent sees two entries with one address and two files, and the sweep never removes the stale one.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Record the writer's process start time in the entry. Admit an entry only when the process's StartTime equals that value (or is at or before CreatedAt) and its process name matches the writer's. Sweep orphaned .tmp files older than a minute. Guard: a DiscoveryLifecycleTests case that writes an entry carrying a live but unrelated PID, with a CreatedAt earlier than that process's start, and asserts that ReadLiveEntries omits it and the next WriteAsync deletes it.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed: ReadValidEntry (NendoDiscoveryStore.cs:225-241) admits an entry on Process.GetProcessById(pid).HasExited alone (269-280), CleanupStaleEntries (243-267) applies the same rule and runs only from WriteAsync (line 102), and it enumerates only *.json, so a '.{run}.{guid}.tmp' left between CreateNew (118) and Move (131) is never removed. PID-liveness is the deliberate, tested definition of 'live' (DiscoveryLifecycleTests.cs:304-338; contract mcp-interface.md:282), but it does not cover Windows' fast PID reuse after a kill or crash, which skips DisposeAsync's DeleteIfPresent (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:691). I did not reproduce a reused-PID case. The consequence is a ghost row in nendo://host/instances; the contract says that resource 'does not make another endpoint reachable' and switching stays the person's action, so nothing is written, read or authorised through it.
- **Correction:** Keep at P3 (reliability/polish). The orphaned .tmp is a few hundred bytes after a crash in a millisecond window and is negligible. The suggested start-time check (record the writer's process start time) is a reasonable, small fix.

<a id="mhs-09"></a>

### MHS-09 — The listen timeout exemption trusts the client's Mcp-Method header rather than the parsed method

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `mcp-host-security`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:97`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:98`
- **What:** The five-minute CancelAfter is skipped whenever the Mcp-Method header equals "subscriptions/listen". The decision is made before the body is read, and the body's own method is never compared with it. The SDK enforces the Mcp-Method/body match only on the 2026-07-28 path (its 'Header mismatch: Mcp-Method' check), so a handshake-era request that carries the header is exempt whatever it calls. The exemption also covers the body-read phase, which the gate's comment relies on the timeout to bound.
- **Failure:** A client sends handshake-era tools/call requests with `Mcp-Method: subscriptions/listen`, or dribbles their bodies at Kestrel's minimum data rate (a 256 KiB body takes about 18 minutes). Each request holds a request-gate place with no timeout, and 16 of them leave every other client NENDO_BUSY for as long as they last.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Keep the timeout through the body read. Once AdmitAsync has parsed the body, lift it with CancelAfter(Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan) only when the parsed JSON-RPC method is subscriptions/listen. Guard: a perimeter test that sends a tools/call carrying the listen header and asserts it still meets NENDO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT under a shortened RequestTimeout.
- **Verifier:** The code does what is claimed: NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:97-98 skips timeout.CancelAfter(gate.Timeout) when the client-supplied Mcp-Method header equals subscriptions/listen, before any body is read, and AdmitAsync (lines 134-146) then reads the body under timeout.Token with no deadline while the request holds its gate place until gate.Exit() at line 110. The body's own method is never compared. The contract (mcp-interface.md:80-81, 226-227) exempts real listen streams and says every other request, body included, may take five minutes, so a spoofed header breaks that and also dodges the four-stream cap, which only the listen handler enforces (NendoChangeFeed.MaximumListeners). The weight is low. Only a hostile local process sets that header, and ADR-0009:273-285 says any process on the machine can connect and that this is not an anti-malware boundary. The gain over an unexempted request is small, about 5 minutes becoming at most roughly 18 minutes (Kestrel's default minimum body data rate), because a local client can re-open 16 requests every 5 minutes anyway. I did not reproduce NENDO_BUSY under load.
- **Correction:** The slow-body hold is bounded by Kestrel's default minimum request body data rate (about 18 minutes for 256 KiB), not unbounded. A tools/call carrying the header runs without the 5-minute cap but is still bounded by the Engine's own work. The scenario needs a deliberately crafted header, so it is a hardening note for a hostile local client, not a buggy-client defect. The proposed fix is sound: keep the timeout through the body read and lift it only when the parsed method is subscriptions/listen.

<a id="mtd-18"></a>

### MTD-18 — Change feed: each listen stream's queue is unbounded, and a records subscription for a record type that does not exist is acknowledged as honoured

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `mcp-tools-data`

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoChangeFeed.cs:140`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoChangeFeed.cs:39`, `src/Nendo.LocalMcp/NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:192`
- **What:** Listener uses Channel.CreateUnbounded and Signal/SignalChanges TryWrite three entries per commit (manifest, proposals, summary with its record IDs). When the client stops reading, SendNotificationAsync blocks on the stream and the queue grows for the life of the connection. RecordsEntity validates only the URI's shape, and ListenAsync acknowledges every such URI in resourceSubscriptions without checking the definition.
- **Failure:** A client that opened subscriptions/listen and stalled (paused debugger, wedged UI thread) holds a queue that grows with every commit the person and other agents make all day, each import batch adding its 50 record IDs. Separately, a client subscribing to nendo://application/entity/taks/records (typo) is told the subscription is honoured and waits for notifications that never come.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Use a bounded channel with DropOldest plus coalescing (a pending 'manifest changed' is idempotent; a records overflow can be sent as truncated=true), and acknowledge a records URI only for an entity the definition holds. Guard: a feed unit test that writes 10,000 commits to a non-reading listener and asserts a bounded count, and a listen test with an unknown entity asserting it is not acknowledged.
- **Verifier:** First half reads as claimed: Listener uses Channel.CreateUnbounded (NendoChangeFeed.cs:140) and Signal/SignalChanges only TryWrite (:95-111), while ListenAsync (NendoLocalMcpHost.cs:229-251) awaits SendNotificationAsync per change, so a connected-but-stalled client lets its queue grow (streams are exempt from the request timeout, NendoMcpSecurityMiddleware.cs:97). Reachability needs a client that holds the connection open and stops reading, a rare case; a dropped connection cancels and disposes the listener, at most 4 listeners exist (:74), and each entry is a small struct pointing at a shared commit summary, so growth is slow. 'Never blocks the caller' (:94) is the stated design goal of the unbounded choice. Second half is mostly by design (see corrections).
- **Correction:** Drop or soften the second half. docs/contracts/mcp-interface.md (W-171 paragraph) says a records subscription fires on every commit that changes a record of the type or changes the definition, and RecordsMeta (NendoChangeFeed.cs:55) emits on summary.DefinitionChanged, so a subscription made before the type exists is legitimate and will be told when it is created; the shape-only check in RecordsEntity (:39-44) is therefore deliberate. Only a typo'd ID is left waiting, a UX nit. The unbounded queue is a hardening idea with low real-world impact, P3 at most.

<a id="r2rm-03"></a>

### R2RM-03 — A view's records.undo and records.redo cannot survive a lost answer: each call sends a fresh idempotency key, so the retry is refused as already compensated, and redo needs the undo's revision, which the view never learns

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `r2-reversibility-matrix` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:361`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:356`, `src/Nendo.Workbench/src/host-desktop.ts:190`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Compensation.cs:133`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:692`, `docs/contracts/custom-views.md:749`
- **What:** undoWrites sends idempotencyKey `view-${crypto.randomUUID()}` on every call and accepts no writeKey, unlike records.batch (batchKey, extension-broker.ts:311-317). The compensation's revision enters ownRevisions only from a successful answer (writtenRecords, :327-333), and records.redo is refused 'not-this-view' for any revision not in that set (:356-357). host-desktop requestCore applies the 15 s host-timeout to data.undoRecordWrites, since only session.createFile/openFile and the file.* and extension.* methods are exempt, and it drops the late answer (:190-196). In the Engine, an existing compensation under a different scope or key is not an exact replay and is refused 'This revision already has a compensation revision.' (Compensation.cs:133-139), which the host answers as compensation-not-supported. History's own Compensate does not have this gap: it goes through pending-mutations with history.getCompensationReceipt. The contract tells a view whose answer is lost to read the record again or resend its batch under its writeKey (custom-views.md:692). The undo/redo section (:734-760) gives no lost-answer path.
- **Failure:** In the Archi view the person deletes 150 boxes with their connections in one batch and presses Ctrl+Z. The undo restores thousands of records, which is synchronous SQLite on the UI thread (DSH-04), or it waits behind an agent's write on the request gate, so it answers after 15 s. The view gets host-timeout while the host commits the restore. The view keeps the step on its stack, and the next Ctrl+Z is refused with compensation-not-supported. The records are back, but the view believes the undo failed. Ctrl+Y can never redo it, because the undo's revision is not in ownRevisions and the broker answers not-this-view. A frame reconnect during the request has the same effect.
- **Reproduction:** Source
- **Fix and guard:** Let records.undo and records.redo take a writeKey, or derive the key deterministically from the package, the revision and the redo flag (for example `view-${pkg}-undo-${revision}`), so a resend is the exact replay CreateCompensationMutationAsync already supports. Add the answered revision to ownRevisions on a replay, and document lost-answer handling in custom-views.md. Guard: a broker test that two records.undo calls for one revision send the same idempotencyKey, and a Desktop test that a repeated data.undoRecordWrites with that key returns isIdempotentReplay with the same revision. Falsify by restoring the random key.
- **Verifier:** The code reads as claimed. undoWrites (src/Nendo.Workbench/src/extension-broker.ts:348-366) sends `view-${crypto.randomUUID()}` on every call and accepts no writeKey, unlike batchKey (:311-317). The broker test even asserts a fresh `view-<uuid>` key (extension-broker.test.mjs:1077-1081). ownRevisions is filled only from a successful answer (:327-334), and a redo of a revision not in that set is refused not-this-view (:356-357). host-desktop requestCore applies a 15 s timeout to data.undoRecordWrites and drops the late answer (host-desktop.ts:191-196, 228-231). In the Engine a compensation that exists under a different scope or key is not an exact replay and throws 'already has a compensation revision' (Compensation.cs:131-140), which WorkbenchProtocol.cs:490 answers as compensation-not-supported. The custom-views.md lost-answer guidance (:692) covers writes only. Not established as reachable on a common path. It needs a lost answer: a more-than-15 s undo or a frame reconnect. An ordinary undo takes milliseconds. Impact is small: nothing is lost, the records are in fact restored, and custom-views.md:748 documents compensation-not-supported as 'already undone', so a view can treat it that way. The remaining gap is that redo cannot be reached, because the undo's revision is never learned. R-011 added writeKey for batches and left undo out.
- **Correction:** Priority P3, not P2: rare trigger, no data loss, and the retry refusal is a documented code meaning already undone. The Archi 150-box timeout scenario is speculative. Deriving a deterministic key from package, revision and redo flag (the proposed fix) would work with the Engine's existing exact-replay path.

<a id="r2sma-02"></a>

### R2SMA-02 — One blob cell or one missing record-type table rejects the whole file, while an extra table only puts it in recovery

**P3** · reliability · Plausible · area `r2-safe-mode-and-file-versions` (reported P2)

- **Where:** `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:610`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:634`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:645`, `src/Nendo.Engine/Storage/SqliteNendoStore.Inspection.cs:585`
- **What:** ValidateReadableMappingsAsync throws NendoValidationException for an entity whose physical table is not a table (610-613), a mapped column that is missing (634-637) and any blob value (645-648). None of these is caught where mapping drift is computed (Inspection.cs:395), so they fall to the outer catch and return Unreadable('unreadable-data') with NendoFileCapabilities.None. The same method already reports a table set that differs as drift (604), which leaves the file RecoveryRequired with 'Only the recognised data is shown'. ADR-0012 rejects complete rejection 'when bounded read-only access can be proven safe', and ADR-0003 routes drift to read-only or recovery-required.
- **Failure:** A file with Projects and Notes where one Notes cell holds a blob (or the notes table was renamed by a tool): Nendo refuses the whole file with 'The file could not be safely interpreted', so the person cannot read or export a single Project, and the message does not say which table is the problem. Adding an unrelated table instead gives a recovery open with all data readable.
- **Reproduction:** Executed: scratch probe9.ps1 -> 'two types, as written: classification=NormalReadOnly readData=True export=True backup=True findings=[]'; 'one blob cell in notes: classification=Rejected readData=False export=False backup=False findings=[unreadable-data: ...]'; 'an unrelated extra table: classification=RecoveryRequired readData=True export=True backup=False findings=[mapping-drift: ...]'; 'notes table renamed: classification=Rejected readData=False ...'.
- **Fix and guard:** Make these per-entity conditions drift: mark the entity or field unreadable (omit it from the snapshot, or project the field as Unsupported) and add a mapping-drift finding naming the record type, so the rest of the file opens in recovery with export. Guard: extend FileInspectionTests.DriftCannotBecomeWritableAlthoughKnownRecordsRemainReadable with rows for a blob cell, a dropped column and a renamed table in a second record type, asserting RecoveryRequired and that the first record type's records are readable.
- **Verifier:** Traced: Inspection.cs:608-613 (mapped table is not a table, e.g. renamed), :634-637 (mapped column missing) and :642-648 (blob cell) throw NendoValidationException from ValidateReadableMappingsAsync. The call at :395 has no catch, so the outer :585 handler (IsProjectionFailure :740 includes NendoException) returns Unreadable('unreadable-data') with NendoFileCapabilities.None, while an extra table is only drift (:604). That sits badly with ADR-0003:121 and ADR-0012:185. But the throws are deliberate fail-closed guards with explicit messages, no test pins either outcome, ReadRecordsAsync (Read.cs:268-272) SELECTs every mapped column so it cannot project a missing table/column or a blob, and the trigger needs an outside SQLite edit. This is a design gap in the projection, not a coding error.
- **Correction:** Priority P3 not P2: only reachable by editing the file outside Nendo, and a SQLite tool repairs it. The proposed fix is not a reclassification: the typed reader (Read.cs:259-300) would first need per-entity/per-field omission before such a file could open in recovery, so it is feature work (compare decisions/README.md:255-258 on the route back into files Unreadable results strand).
